# C Programming Mastery 5

<a id="v5-index"></a>
# C Mastery 5

56 domains · 429 projects · 1357 working units · 56 new executable units · 627 recall sets.

Start with [v5-guide](#v5-guide), use [v5-workflow](#v5-workflow), and follow [v5-route](#v5-route). Grow a shared toolbox, Linux telemetry/service, firmware gateway and VM/store kernel appliance.



<a id="v5-guide"></a>
# C Mastery 5: learn by growing useful systems

Start with a three-hour entry diagnostic, then grow a bounded record tool. The
curriculum assumes that you can already write elementary C; targeted remediation
is available when the diagnostic identifies a gap. A project is a coverage and
budget envelope. Your next action is a smaller working unit, usually one to three
hours, with a result you can explain and inspect before stopping.

The 56 domains and 429 projects remain the reference catalog. Their old numeric
order is not the v4 study order. Use the capability route and the CLI's readiness
explanations. A unit requires the capabilities and components it actually uses,
not every project in the domain where an earlier idea was taught.

## One session

1. Attempt two due recall sets, aiming for ten to fifteen minutes. Write or speak
   an answer before opening the prior implementation, notes or feedback.
2. Read the next unit's imported contracts, new boundary, assigned passages and
   stopping condition. Predict a normal, boundary and failure result.
3. At a designated design gate, compare the alternatives and seal the choice
   before the main implementation. A small comparison prototype is allowed.
4. Implement the narrow increment. Keep earlier regressions. Observe the first
   divergence before broad edits when a check fails.
5. Retain the actual source/trace and note assistance and active minutes. A unit
   completion is practice; component acceptance additionally needs its rubric,
   relevant contract recall and scoped execution evidence.

Do not write a new architectural dossier for every small unit. Carry forward an
unchanged decision and record the new assumption being tested. Setup, tool
discovery, wiring and capture are explicit tasks; equipment waiting is not
implementation time and does not block unrelated hosted study.

## Three systems and a shared toolbox

**Linux telemetry/service:** a record tool becomes a library consumer, then a
file/pipe service, then a bounded event-driven HTTP application. Slow peers,
malformed data, overload and shutdown repeatedly challenge the same ownership
rules. Numerical filters and measurements operate on its telemetry stream.

**Firmware acquisition gateway:** reuse record formats and portable algorithms
through reset/UART bring-up, MMIO drivers, interrupt/DMA handoff, layered serial
and Ethernet communication, original task scheduling, and H745 core ownership.
Model, emulator and physical observations are separate evidence.

**VM/store kernel appliance:** reuse byte access, allocation, generation handles,
algorithms and fault harnesses in a bytecode runtime and durable page store.
Bring up basic boot and exceptions before importing those finished services.
Later compose processes, channels, a single store owner and recovery.

The seven-layer educational stack, custom Ethernet-to-HTTP stack and HTTP server
over OS sockets remain distinct deliverables. Sharing a parser does not erase
their different physical, transport and lifecycle responsibilities.

## Progression without unnecessary waits

The nine capability phases overlap. The VM/store branch can proceed alongside
single-core task work. MCU and x86 branches require their own target knowledge
but need not wait for each other. Introductory SPSC publication follows the ring
and memory-model foundations; machine-level SMP/AMP revalidation comes later.

The route brings a working tool within twelve implementation/verification hours
after diagnosis and a real file or pipe boundary within forty-eight. These are
authoring targets, not guaranteed learner speeds. Each strand includes an
observable integration or adaptation within twenty-four assigned hours.

Advanced kernels, lock-free reclamation, real-time analysis and concurrent
services retain the required dispositions established in v3. All ten physical
communication-interface obligations and F439/H745 evidence remain in force.
Passing a host test, linking an image or completing recall cannot close them.
The final interface units register a manual `interface-bench` capture target;
it makes no compiler or simulator promise. Their reviewed raw captures identify
the actual interface, equipment and image. The MCU defense consumes those
accepted records and separate F439/H745 board records. SMP project milestones
require actual x86 guest receipts at one, two and four CPUs. You may continue
unrelated units while a physical project gate remains open.
The firmware capstone also requires its own current board captures at deployment,
fault/recovery and changed-condition defense. These are local observations of the
integrated application; the earlier interface and runtime portfolios remain
separate prerequisites. Integration stages consume the preceding stage's actual
component or design dossier, and the campaign preserves its learner workspace.
Run each SMP milestone with `--target x86-smp --cpus 1`, then repeat with two
and four CPUs. Selecting a target name does not itself establish guest execution;
the selected checks must include a real guest run. The archive milestone pairs
its host codec test with the earlier boot smoke test. The first Cortex-M
preemption gate likewise pairs its host scheduler check with the scoped image
and preemptive guest checks. Retain these receipts without requiring unfinished
later mechanisms to pass an entire family suite.

## Readings and references

Use the bounded passages on each unit card. Textbooks supply models and worked
reasoning; foundational publications explain the original mechanisms; standards,
architecture manuals and implementation documents establish applicable contracts.
The existing reference catalog records local library locators and source-inspection
limits. Read for the decision or experiment ahead, then retrieve the idea before
reopening a previous solution.

## What completion means

The CLI distinguishes practice, executable behavior, explanation, independence,
transfer, dependency closure and physical evidence. A self-assessment is visibly
self-assessed. Keep negative controls and the evidence a future reviewer would
need to challenge your claim. Historical success remains recorded when a changed
source, interface, target or recall failure reopens a particular claim.

<a id="v5-architecture"></a>
# Decisions before implementation, revision after evidence

An architecture decision is required when a component becomes reusable, an
execution/ownership/transport boundary changes, or two plausible designs make
different predictions under the assigned workload. Syntax drills and fixed ABI
facts need predictions and observation, not invented alternatives.

## A compact decision record

Record the requirement and capacity/failure assumptions; two plausible designs;
their predicted differences; the discriminating trace, model or prototype; your
choice; the rejected design; and the condition that would reverse the choice.
Seal this record before the main implementation. Record which experiment is an
exploratory spike so it is not confused with the final implementation.

Use the external behavioral contract to judge both designs. You cannot make an
incompatible design pass by changing a fixed wire format, ownership obligation,
test expectation or timing assumption after observing its failure.

| Progression | What is supplied | What you decide |
|---|---|---|
| Worked comparison, chiefly phases 1–2 | Constraints, alternatives and a comparison method | Complete the predictions, run the comparison, justify a choice |
| Bounded choice, chiefly phases 3–4 | Constraints and plausible alternatives | Design the comparison and explain the trade-off |
| Independent design, chiefly phases 5–7 | Workload, resource ceilings and acceptance boundary | Propose alternatives, interfaces and evidence |
| Architectural revision, chiefly phases 8–9 | A changed or competing requirement and your existing system | Clarify assumptions, revise ownership/boundaries, plan migration and revalidation |

Support fades per mechanism. Your first exception-frame or cache-maintenance
exercise can be guided even after independent design of a hosted service.

## Revisit the decision in code

| Earlier decision | Later pressure | Required reconsideration |
|---|---|---|
| Ring count versus monotonic positions | SPSC publication, non-power-of-two capacity | Which fields each participant owns; wrap bounds and publication order |
| Parser keeps bytes versus caller retains spans | Short transfers and cancellation | Retained lifetime, resumable state and atomic error handling |
| Timer list versus heap | Different task count or cancellation rate | Traversal bounds, measured cycles, code size and WCET assumptions |
| Copied messages versus transferred buffers | DMA completion or peer reset | Who can reuse memory, stale completion identity and recovery authority |
| Reactor versus worker pool | Slow clients and CPU-heavy requests | Fairness, backpressure, bounded queues, cancellation and shutdown |
| Shared store versus one store owner | Client death during commit | Serialization, durability, error propagation and restart state |

At a later handoff, reconstruct the old rationale without the record, predict
whether the new condition reverses it, then consult the original evidence. A
defensible decision to retain the design is valid when the evidence supports it.

Full milestone acceptance retains the six-dimension 0–3 rubric: mechanism,
correctness, memory ownership, resources/dependencies, failure diagnosis, and
communication/transfer. All dimensions must reach two and at least two must reach
three. Do not average away an ownership or correctness failure. Small units use
lightweight evidence until that boundary is ready for review.

<a id="v5-reuse"></a>
# Reuse source, contracts and evidence deliberately

The artifact registry identifies actual components. An import records a contract
version and immutable source snapshot, not merely the name of a previous project.
Export the library portion of the record tool; its command wrapper remains an
application. An ELF inspection, waveform or timing trace is evidence, not a
library that every later program must link.

## Handoff procedure

1. Before opening the old source, reconstruct the component's invariant and the
   assumptions the new consumer depends on.
2. Select its source revision and contract. Check allocation, blocking, callbacks,
   reentrancy, ISR use, retention, alignment, capacity and failure semantics.
3. Import the declared CMake target and actual source/include directories. Include
   the recursive pinned dependency closure so the handoff remains relocatable.
4. Write the adapter. Exercise partial progress, failure, exhaustion, cancellation
   or reset according to this new boundary; preserve the component regressions.
5. State which claims survive. Revalidate changed assumptions, then export only
   the claims and target scope that have evidence.

Do not rewrite the ring, codec or allocator because it is inconvenient to import.
A redesign is legitimate when a changed contract requires it; preserve the prior
revision and explain the migration. Never substitute assessor implementations
into ordinary learner imports. Assessor mode is explicit author validation.

## Example: one ring over several boundaries

First implement a caller-owned FIFO, including capacity 1, non-power-of-two wrap,
full/empty disambiguation and failure-preserving operations. A later threaded
consumer adds predicate-based blocking and shutdown. An SPSC variant changes the
publication argument. A DMA consumer introduces device completion and cache-line
ownership; an AMP consumer introduces peer epochs and independent reset.

FIFO ordering can be reused. Single-thread evidence does not establish atomic
publication, interrupt safety, cache visibility or DMA quiescence. Each handoff
names these separate claims so a new assumption cannot hide behind old tests.

## Compatibility boundaries

Preserve CVM1, the existing store format and kernel v1/v2 interfaces. A store
adapter must satisfy caller serialization, complete-page I/O and explicit
durability even when its underlying service is asynchronous. HTTP timeouts use
monotonic milliseconds; execution timers use their bounded modular tick contract.
Conversions must declare units and wrap limits. No universal runtime ABI is added.

Strict freestanding images still audit the entire link closure: no libc, libgcc,
compiler-rt, libatomic, HAL or existing OS implementation can supply the studied
original mechanism. Standard type headers and already-reviewed intrinsics retain
their existing policy. Hosted Linux and pinned FreeRTOS comparisons stay separate.

An accepted host-scoped component can be reused while its physical obligations
remain open. Editing source or a contract invalidates affected exported claims;
it does not erase historical learning or unrelated components.

<a id="v5-retrieval"></a>
# Recall, spacing and transfer during real project work

There is one scheduled set per micro-topic, with mechanism, trace/implementation
and changed-context variants. Projects reference those sets rather than creating
duplicate queues. The 627 sets cover the 1,881 objective facets, but each attempt
may score only what the response actually demonstrates.

## Attempt before feedback

Write the first prediction, draw a state/ownership diagram, trace a short input,
or reconstruct a small operation before looking at the old implementation. Record
assistance. After sealing the answer, inspect feedback and locate the first broken
assumption. A corrected answer is valuable practice; it is not a delayed test of
retention when produced in the same session.

Use the existing scale: zero is absent or materially wrong; one is partial or
cued; two is independently correct with the relevant boundary; three demonstrates
transfer under a changed condition with justified reasoning. A passing executable
test cannot grade the explanation or prove independent work.

## A bounded queue

Review approximately two due sets in ten to fifteen minutes at the start of an
actual study session. Prefer unresolved failures and prerequisite contracts, then
older material. The initial successful-review gaps are 1, 3, 7, 14 and 30 days
from the relevant preceding event. They are configurable engineering defaults.
Unstarted and elective material does not become due merely because it exists.

After the initial sequence, later consumption and cumulative milestones supply
maintenance practice. A missed session creates one overdue opportunity, not a
debt for every missed day. After a long gap, resume with a bounded diagnostic;
elapsed time alone is neither proof of forgetting nor reason to delete evidence.

At a component handoff, deduplicate the critical requirements of the imported
contracts. Each needs an unaided score of at least two in the relevant context
within fourteen days or a fresh preflight demonstration. This freshness window
is a policy, not a biological constant. Split a large preflight across sessions.
Do not quietly sample away a required ownership or synchronization assumption.

A failure reopens the affected objective/claim, supplies targeted corrective
practice and schedules a later independent attempt. Other study stays available.
Physical observations, dependency audits and implementation evidence retain their
own gates. The ledger keeps original and superseding evaluations.

## Useful interleaving

Compare already-studied mechanisms whose selection matters: semaphore versus
mutex versus notification; stack exhaustion versus corruption; asymptotic growth
versus measured cycles; ordinary accesses versus acquire/release publication.
Choose the mechanism before executing it. Interleaving is not random interruption
while the learner is still acquiring the first example.

Use changed-condition reconstruction already budgeted for assessment: capacity
8 to 7, new HTTP segmentation, a different allocator lifetime, an API invoked
from an ISR, or a peer reset during ownership transfer. Larger reconstruction
tasks are scheduled units, not invisible homework after the session.

## Evidence behind the design

[Karpicke and Blunt (2011)](https://learninglab.psych.purdue.edu/downloads/2011/2011_Karpicke_Blunt_Science.pdf)
studied conceptual retrieval with science texts. Applying reconstruction to C
mechanisms is a curriculum design inference.
[Karpicke and Bauernschmidt (2011)](https://learninglab.psych.purdue.edu/downloads/2011/2011_Karpicke_Bauernschmidt_JEPLMC.pdf)
support spacing while finding no inherently superior relative interval pattern
in their experiment. The selected schedule does not claim universal optimality.
[YeckehZaare and Resnick (2025)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41539-025-00322-5)
examined incentives to practice on separate days. These publications motivate
practice design; they do not establish this curriculum's effectiveness or duration.

<a id="v5-budgets"></a>
# Workload conservation and a sustainable rhythm

Keep the full catalog at 4,879 planned hours and the conservative core at 4,799.
Passing the entry diagnostic without its remaining remediation retains the
existing 4,777-hour personal-plan estimate. Time estimates remain provisional.

Every working unit owns an exact number of minutes within one original project.
All units together retain 3,599 implementation/verification hours. The 56 new
executable units replace or strengthen work already assigned in those envelopes.
Their tests and new family directories do not add another budget.

Across modules and integrations, 593 hours remain for reading, 368 for assessment
and 319 for consolidation. The conservation ledger assigns 160 assessment hours
formerly used for retrospective alternatives/dossier prose to prior design
comparisons and milestone reviews. It assigns 261.25 consolidation hours formerly
used for manual delayed reconstruction to 627 sets with five planned five-minute
reviews. The remaining 57.75 consolidation hours cover longer reconstructions and
other consolidation. The 32 integration assessment/consolidation hours are part
of these totals, not another allocation.

The integration slice remains 208 hours: 160 implementation/verification plus
48 reading/assessment/consolidation. Importing an existing codec, queue or VM pays
only for the new adapter and changed-boundary evidence. Earlier implementation is
charged once to its producer.

For a ten-hour week, the existing approximate split of two hours reading and
prediction, five implementation, two verification and one assessment/retrieval
remains useful. Short reviews occupy that last category; they are not added on
top. Use actual category budgets when a project requires more verification.
Twenty-hour weeks can complete more units, but delayed work still occurs on
separate days. Remediation and equipment waiting are recorded separately.

The session queue is a recommendation rather than a minimum daily debt. Record
active minutes and which activity a longer review replaces. A full six-score
review on every small unit would silently inflate the budget; perform it at the
reusable component or project boundary instead.

<a id="v5-workflow"></a>
# Offline learner workflow

Use one study profile for your progress and separate workspaces for implementations. All commands run locally. Python manages the learning records; execute the C laboratories in Linux or WSL with the tools described by their family.

The v4 records add working units to the existing projects. Existing `init`, `advance`, `check`, `report`, and schema-2 receipts remain usable. Practice and checks remain accessible when an acceptance requirement needs repair.

## Start a study session

From the curriculum directory, replace the example learner paths with your own separate directories:

```sh
python -m cmastery study init ../my-study
python -m cmastery study next ../my-study
python -m cmastery init PR-T01-01 ../prefix-lab --unit U-T01-01-01
python -m cmastery study sheet ../my-study ../session.md --unit U-T01-01-01 --assessment-template ../assessment.json
```

`study next` shows ready units and at most two due recall sets within a 15-minute review allowance. It does not mark work as learned. Read `UNIT.md`, make a prediction, implement or investigate the assigned mechanism, and retain the requested evidence. The generated assessment template starts with unaccepted values.

After studying a unit, explicitly record that event:

```sh
python -m cmastery study next ../my-study --studied U-T01-01-01
python -m cmastery check ../prefix-lab --unit U-T01-01-01
python -m cmastery study status ../my-study
```

Studying activates that unit's recall sets. It establishes neither implementation success nor mastery. A unit without an executable adapter uses its documented trace, analysis, observation, or design checks; the CLI reports an unavailable executable adapter rather than inventing a pass.

Use `advance WORKSPACE PROJECT --unit UNIT` to select another unit in the same family while preserving code. Advancing within the same project is allowed when its unit changes. The previous brief, source fingerprint, prediction record, and latest receipt are archived. A different family needs a separate workspace and explicit component imports.

## Attempt recall before feedback

```sh
python -m cmastery recall due ../my-study
python -m cmastery recall start ../my-study T01.01
python -m cmastery recall submit ../my-study ATTEMPT_ID ../original-answer.txt
python -m cmastery recall grade ../my-study ATTEMPT_ID ../grade.json
```

`start` returns an attempt ID, the selected prompt, and its objective IDs. Write the original answer, including an admission of uncertainty or inability to recall when appropriate. `submit` preserves it and then reveals the feedback checklist and resource references. An original submitted answer cannot be overwritten. Use `--assistance "consulted the old loop"` for disclosed help; multiple assistance entries are allowed.

A grade file uses the exact objective IDs returned for the attempt:

```json
{
  "scores": {"T01.01.a": 2, "T01.01.b": 1, "T01.01.c": 2},
  "feedback": "The loop invariant was correct. The recursive stack bound omitted one live frame; retained the corrected state table.",
  "assistance": []
}
```

Use the existing 0–3 rubric: absent/incorrect, nominal without sufficient explanation, correct under the declared contract, or independent transfer with a defended tradeoff. Score only what the attempt demonstrates. All prompted objectives receive their own score; an unattempted objective receives zero. Correcting a grade appends a superseding evaluation and keeps the earlier record.

The default successful-review gaps are 1, 3, 7, 14, and 30 days. The first review becomes due one day after study. An independent successful review advances the sequence only when its interval has elapsed. Early practice can satisfy an immediate preflight but cannot compress the spaced sequence. After the fifth spaced success, the set leaves the automatic queue; later consumption or cumulative work prompts another preflight as necessary.

An assisted or failed attempt schedules an independent retry for the following day. An immediate repaired answer remains corrective practice; it does not establish delayed retention. Missing a month produces one overdue opportunity per active set, not thirty daily entries. Reviews rotate among the authored variants. Already accepted historical implementation evidence is not revoked solely because recall becomes due.

The schedule is a curriculum policy, not a claim of a universal optimal interval. The profile stores configurable positive day gaps and the freshness window. Sessions remain bounded to at most two sets and 15 minutes; split larger preflights across sessions.

## Seal a consequential design choice

At a designated architecture boundary, the first unit tells you which final milestone's decision to seal. Comparison prototypes may precede the commitment; main implementation and its acceptance checks follow it.

```sh
python -m cmastery decision seal ../my-study ../component-lab FINAL_UNIT ../decision.json
```

The decision file contains:

```json
{
  "requirements": ["At most 64 queued records", "No allocation after startup"],
  "alternatives": ["caller-owned ring", "fixed linked pool"],
  "predictions": ["The ring uses less metadata; the pool makes cancellation cheaper"],
  "spike_evidence": ["evidence/ring-vs-pool.md"],
  "choice": "caller-owned ring",
  "rejected_reason": "Cancellation is rare and measured metadata cost exceeds the budget",
  "reversal_trigger": "If arbitrary cancellation dominates, repeat the comparison"
}
```

The CLI requires two distinct alternatives and local experiment evidence, pins the comparison files, and records the source state at commitment. Acceptance requires subsequent source changes and, where tests apply, a later check receipt. If `decision_before` names the first implementation unit, seal before accepting that unit. These local timestamps support an honest study process; they cannot independently prove when an idea was conceived.

## Accept the specific evidence demonstrated

Fill the generated assessment template using actual evidence. Each published check must be addressed in order. Each required claim names its scope: `host`, `model`, `emulator`, or `physical`.

```sh
python -m cmastery accept ../my-study ../prefix-lab --unit U-T01-01-01 --assessment ../assessment.json
```

The assessment has these fields:

| Field | Required content |
|---|---|
| `explanation` | Mechanism and invariants explained in your own words |
| `transfer` | What changed, your prediction, and the observed result |
| `independence` | `unaided: true` and disclosed assistance; assisted work remains practice |
| `evidence` | Relative paths to retained explanations, traces, or experimental results |
| `source_files` | Relevant source/header paths whose later changes reopen these component claims |
| `checks` | Published check text, in order, with a truthful `met` value |
| `claims` | Claim ID, scope, local evidence paths, and any required target, CPU counts, or interfaces |
| `dimensions` | Six scores, only for a milestone or exported component |

The six dimension keys are `mechanism`, `correctness`, `memory_ownership`, `resources_dependencies`, `failure_diagnosis`, and `communication_transfer`. A full milestone requires all six to score at least 2 and at least two to score 3. Ordinary working units do not require this full dossier.

Acceptance checks actual prerequisite records, required component imports, critical recall, the decision gate when designated, and current learner test results where the unit declares tests. Assessor runs never establish learner acceptance. A physical claim requires current registered physical captures; a target build or a host model does not become a physical observation. Explanations and trace interpretations remain explicit self-assessment rather than automatic certification.

Store evidence in distinct per-unit files instead of repeatedly overwriting one notebook. Each check retains an immutable receipt in `evidence/checks/` and updates the convenience `evidence/latest.json`. Acceptance copies source and evidence bytes into the profile's content-addressed object store. These accepted revisions preserve prerequisites when the next unit adds a function to the same C file. Current claim validity remains separate: changed claim files, listed component sources, or imports reopen the live claim and prevent reuse or export until revalidated. Changed unit contracts or damaged retained objects also invalidate historical prerequisites. Export additionally requires the entire producer workspace to match its accepted source fingerprint.

Required claim constraints cannot be weakened in the assessment. A `target` or `targets` declaration requires evidence for every listed target; `cpus: [1, 2, 4]` requires all three guest runs at each required target. An image build or audit is insufficient for emulator scope: the receipt must include an actual guest execution test. Unit-specific `target_tests` select the appropriate implemented guest stage without requiring later family mechanisms. Keep the ordinary host check and each required target/CPU run; their receipts can be recorded in any order.

## Retain physical interface and board evidence

Some units declare manual `capture_targets`, such as `interface-bench`, separately from executable family targets. These declarations authorize physical capture registration, not a simulated or automatic hardware test. Use `record-physical WORKSPACE MANIFEST` after performing and reviewing the actual measurement. The manifest identifies the target, observed interfaces, exact source hash, image files, raw captures, and measurement conditions:

```json
{
  "target": "interface-bench", "interfaces": ["UART"],
  "source_sha256": "SOURCE_HASH_FROM_CURRENT_REPORT",
  "images": ["uart-bench.elf"], "captures": ["uart-trace.csv"],
  "board_revision": "Recorded board and transceiver revision",
  "silicon_revision": "Recorded device revision", "clocks": "Measured clock configuration",
  "cache_mpu": "Recorded configuration or explicit not applicable",
  "instrument": "Instrument and probe configuration",
  "instrumentation_overhead": "Measured or bounded impact",
  "trace_overruns": "Observed loss or explicit none",
  "observations": "Interpret the raw capture against the required interface contract"
}
```

Image and capture paths are relative to the manifest directory. Only interfaces declared by the unit's manual target can be registered. Captures can be combined to cover the required interfaces. A build target named `stm32f439` cannot satisfy a required `stm32h745` observation, and a model cannot satisfy either physical claim.

Portfolio claims use canonical `source_units` to reuse accepted physical observations from earlier workspaces. They require a new interpretation dossier and verify each required target and interface against those retained observations. The portfolio pins the earlier acceptance identities; reassessing a source unit requires refreshing the live portfolio review. `study status` reports completed projects and core-route completion from accepted revisions, including every designated project completion gate. Missing physical or emulator obligations keep those gates incomplete. The report also lists current live acceptances separately, so historical course completion does not assert that subsequently edited code is still valid.

## Export your component and consume it elsewhere

An artifact is a portable implementation with a declared public contract, not a reference to an assessor solution. Finish and accept its producer unit before export. Keep application entry points outside a reusable library when the artifact contract describes a portable core.

An export declaration selects the actual relative files in your implementation:

```json
{
  "contract_version": "1",
  "cmake_target": "my_checked_bytes",
  "adapter_roles": ["foundations"],
  "profiles": ["C"],
  "targets": ["host"],
  "sources": ["src/checked_bytes.c"],
  "headers": ["include/checked_bytes.h"],
  "include_dirs": ["include"],
  "assets": [],
  "dependencies": []
}
```

Choose profiles and targets permitted by the catalog artifact. Declare every artifact imported by the producer in `dependencies`; the exporter copies their complete pinned closures. List required generated data or build-time inputs in `assets`. The exporter generates a relocatable CMake static-library target for the C/assembly sources and public include directories.

```sh
python -m cmastery artifact export ../my-study ../bytes-lab bytes.checked ../artifacts/bytes-v1 --manifest ../export.json
python -m cmastery artifact link ../my-study ../consumer-lab ../artifacts/bytes-v1 --profile C --target host
```

The bundle carries source, contract, acceptance and content identities, public headers, a CMake entry point, dependency closures, and the producer's scoped claims. Linking copies the pinned bundle into the consumer and generates `.cmastery/components.cmake`. Include it from the consumer's CMake file and link the returned target through your adapter:

```cmake
include(.cmastery/components.cmake)
target_link_libraries(my_service PRIVATE my_checked_bytes)
```

The learner owns that adapter and its integration tests. Exported profiles and targets describe declared compatibility; the retained evidence identifies which execution conditions were actually checked. Continue the required compiler, link-closure, freestanding, and hardware audits.

The supplied integration family also consumes these exports directly through `check --unit LAB-IN-01` (and its later integration units). Export `adapter_roles` defaults to the producer family; explicitly declare a compatible role when exporting a differently organized adapter. Its public headers must expose the integration API, and its target must contain the required implementation. For example, the supplied P1 integration expects the foundational cursor/parser interfaces and algorithm ring interface. Unfinished later functions may remain learner stubs in an early export. When a consumer combines multiple artifacts from one monolithic provider, revalidate and re-export the retained components from one coherent source revision, or split implementations into distinct source files with separate public symbol ownership. The runner rejects differing snapshots of the same source path within an adapter role before linking; it never silently chooses the first archive's stale stub.

For a controlled check, the runner verifies the pinned bundles, regenerates a CMake import file inside the fresh build directory, and passes its path plus validated `CMASTERY_COMPONENTS_FOUNDATIONS_TARGETS`, `CMASTERY_COMPONENTS_ALGORITHMS_TARGETS`, and other declared role targets. It does not execute the editable `.cmastery/components.cmake` convenience file. Artifact imports take precedence over manual source roots for their roles. Missing imports or tests cannot silently fall back to assessor code. `--all-tests` requires every test in the declared family or selected target scope; a P1-only dependency set cannot claim the firmware or VM/store integration scenarios.

The old explicit `--dependency FAMILY=WORKSPACE` route remains supported. Structured family declarations map implementation and include variables to the learner's actual `src` and `include` directories; existing runtime, storage, and kernel layouts retain their adapters. Every dependency fingerprint remains in the receipt.

Before accepting consumption, complete fresh independent recall for the artifact's critical objectives under its current contract:

```sh
python -m cmastery recall start ../my-study TOPIC_ID --contract bytes.checked@1
```

Use the artifact's actual critical-topic IDs, submit, and grade normally. Acceptance deduplicates objective requirements and defaults to a 14-day freshness window. A successful preflight under one artifact contract does not erase a different contract's evidence. Replacing a link or altering a pinned file makes dependent evidence stale; changing an unrelated component does not globally reset progress.

## Records, portability, and recovery

The profile is `PROFILE/.cmastery-study/profile.json`; the append-only ledger is `ledger.jsonl`; retained source and evidence objects live in `objects/` under their content hashes. Back up the whole profile and your workspaces. Corrections append records with `supersedes`; do not edit old ledger lines or retained objects. Hash chaining detects accidental edits, while clock checks reject future records or backwards appends. The profile is local self-reported evidence, not a secure examination system.

A short exclusive `ledger.lock` protects concurrent appends. After a crashed writer, inspect that no learning command is running before removing a leftover lock. The ledger is portable JSON, while its recorded workspace locations refer to the local evidence copies; preserve or deliberately restore those paths when moving a study installation.

Printable sheets use the same unit, set, variant, and objective identifiers. Write your answer on paper first, then enter it through the same start/submit/grade flow. Record the paper date in the answer if helpful; the CLI retains the actual entry time and does not backdate acceptance. Both workflows preserve the separation between practice, observed behavior, independent explanation, transfer, and physical evidence.

Bytes, containers, parsers, storage policies and algorithms shared by two consumers.

<a id="v5-recall-t01"></a>
# T01 recall sets

One queue entry per set; rotate variants. Attempt before feedback and score only the objectives actually demonstrated.

<a id="recall-t01-01"></a>
## T01.01 — Algorithmic reasoning

### mechanism

Without opening the old implementation, reconstruct Algorithmic reasoning. Trace loops and recursion using explicit state tables. State the precondition, state transition and one counterexample.

<details><summary>After the attempt: scoring facets</summary>

- Trace loops and recursion using explicit state tables.
- Derive time and auxiliary-space costs for simple implementations.
- State loop invariants and termination conditions before coding.

</details>

### trace-or-small-implementation

For Algorithmic reasoning: Trace a loop and recursive sum on [3, -1, 4]; count additions, iterations and maximum live calls, then state the invariant and decreasing measure. Reject a cancellation case whose intermediate prefix exceeds the declared bounds. Retain a state table, an induction argument, checked-prefix rejection evidence, and separate O(n) work / O(1) iterative / O(n) recursive stack claims. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T01.01.a (Trace loops and recursion using explicit state tables.); T01.01.b (Derive time and auxiliary-space costs for simple implementations.); T01.01.c (State loop invariants and termination conditions before coding.). Predict normal, boundary and failure outcomes before running the code. Reject a list longer than capacity, an out-of-range input, or an unrepresentable intermediate prefix without changing output storage. Do not dereference an empty range. Never compute an overflowing prefix first and inspect it afterward. A representable final mathematical sum is insufficient: retain the positive and negative cancellation failures as regressions.

<details><summary>After the attempt: scoring facets</summary>

- Derive time and auxiliary-space costs for simple implementations.
- Show the first divergent transition and justify the independent expectation.
- State loop invariants and termination conditions before coding.

</details>

### changed-condition

For Algorithmic reasoning, reconstruct the relevant interface or invariant before consulting earlier source. Replace summation with maximum selection, defining the empty case explicitly. Explain which part of the invariant and which storage bound change. Attempt the changed condition after a delay without copying the prior solution. Explain which invariant, lifetime, resource or dependency claims survive and which must be revised.

<details><summary>After the attempt: scoring facets</summary>

- Trace loops and recursion using explicit state tables.
- Derive time and auxiliary-space costs for simple implementations.
- Explain which assumptions survive and which evidence must be repeated.

</details>

**Objectives:** [T01.01.a](#t01-01-a), [T01.01.b](#t01-01-b), [T01.01.c](#t01-01-c).

### mechanism

Without opening the old implementation, reconstruct Basic C diagnostic. Predict array, pointer, function, and control-flow behavior. State the precondition, state transition and one counterexample.

<details><summary>After the attempt: scoring facets</summary>

- Locate uninitialized values and off-by-one errors in small examples.

### trace-or-small-implementation

For Basic C diagnostic: Write small examples of array traversal, a pointer parameter and nested calls; predict defined behavior, reject an uninitialized read, and rewrite a conflicting modification into separate statements. Retain a prediction ledger classified as defined, unspecified or undefined, with repaired examples and new boundary cases. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T01.03.a (Predict array, pointer, function, and control-flow behavior.); T01.03.b (Locate uninitialized values and off-by-one errors in small examples.); T01.03.c (Replace guesses about evaluation order with explicit reasoning.). Predict normal, boundary and failure outcomes before running the code. Do not run an undefined expression to discover its value. A missing warning is recorded as tool behavior, not semantic permission. Reject negative indices before unsigned conversion and ensure the empty-array policy does not manufacture a valid element.

<details><summary>After the attempt: scoring facets</summary>

| [lab-ex-11](#lab-ex-11) | foundations | PR-T44-10 | Before inspecting the test source, seal predictions and the first invalid state. Repair failure-atomic admission and retain a delayed changed-capacity variant. |

<a id="v5-research"></a>
# Search, reflection, and design decisions for C Mastery 4

Baseline: v3 commit `4f3e3a2`. The work starts from the existing source catalog and
local teaching documents, rather than replacing the curriculum's technical scope.

## What the audit found

- 56 domains, 627 micro-topics, 1,881 objectives, and 429 projects remain required or
  elective according to their existing dispositions. Project implementation and
  verification sum to 3,599 hours within the 4,879-hour full catalog.
- Nine executable families contain 261 memberships and 259 unique projects.
  Only 235 unique projects have a declared test selection. Shared anchor tests do
  not implement every project that cites them. There are 170 unmapped projects
  and 24 with recipes only.
- The legacy project ordering sorts largely by domain ID. Basic OS observation
  appears at step 338; basic boot waits for final VM and storage projects even
  though those components are consumed only in later kernel integrations.
- All 429 legacy graph outputs use the generic accepted-component-and-dossier
  suffix. This loses the identity and assumptions of the actual reusable code.
- Delayed retrieval and a 0–3 rubric already exist. The old CLI does not schedule
  retrieval, preserve an attempt ledger, or seal a design before implementation.
- Some generated working-card questions discuss mechanisms absent from their
  projects. V4 replaces those cards in its publication overlay while preserving
  the historical source bytes and migration contracts.

## Source search and limits

Technical reading continues to use the inspected 204-record reference library,
whose local locators point into `F:\Knowledge`. The SWE and data-structure graphs
are discovery indexes, not substitutes for the underlying documents. Each new
laboratory binds its mechanism to existing technical source passages; the v4
topic cards inherit bounded module readings and identify the relevant objectives.

A filename-oriented search of the local library did not find an obvious matching
learning-science collection. This is not evidence that no such works exist.
Primary publications were inspected online for the new retrieval design:

1. Karpicke and Blunt (2011), *Retrieval Practice Produces More Learning than
   Elaborative Studying with Concept Mapping*, Science 331:772–775,
   DOI 10.1126/science.1199327. Author-hosted paper:
   https://learninglab.psych.purdue.edu/downloads/2011/2011_Karpicke_Blunt_Science.pdf
2. Karpicke and Bauernschmidt (2011), *Spaced Retrieval: Absolute Spacing Enhances
   Learning Regardless of Relative Spacing*, JEP:LMC 37:1250–1257,
   DOI 10.1037/a0023436. Author-hosted paper:
   https://learninglab.psych.purdue.edu/downloads/2011/2011_Karpicke_Bauernschmidt_JEPLMC.pdf
3. YeckehZaare and Resnick (2025), *Counting Days Is a Spacing Incentive That
   Unlocks the Potential of Low GPA Students*, npj Science of Learning 10:35,
   DOI 10.1038/s41539-025-00322-5:
   https://www.nature.com/articles/s41539-025-00322-5

The first two studies support retrieval and spacing but do not establish an
optimal schedule for advanced C. The programming study concerns spacing
incentives; it does not justify promising a fixed improvement from this workflow.
The 1/3/7/14/30-day gaps and 14-day handoff freshness rule are adjustable design
defaults. We will calibrate workload with learner reports, not treat author tests
as evidence of learning effectiveness.

## Chosen response

Keep the existing budget and identity catalog. Add short units, concrete artifact
lineages, meaningful design gates, and a bounded recall queue. Practice remains
accessible while acceptance requires the relevant evidence. Build the CLI and
paper route from the same records. Preserve all required physical and strict
freestanding obligations; host tests cannot discharge them.

Start at [Entry](#guide-entry), follow the [Roadmap](#guide-roadmap), and use [Performance and debugging](#guide-performance-debugging), [Communication stack families](#guide-communication-stacks), [Assessment](#guide-assessment) and [Workload](#guide-workload). <a id="guide-third-edition"></a>

# C Mastery 3: operating systems and concurrent execution

This edition extends the accepted second edition through T49–T56. Follow the
[project route](#guide-project-route) and retain the earlier implementations. The
second-edition Git commit is `40bf1b2`; the immutable baseline and explicit third-
edition migration preserve its 1,605 objective and 337 project identities.

## What grows across the projects

Begin by observing a process, thread, mapping and descriptor on Linux. Write a
small scheduler model with a hand-derived trace. Next construct task contexts,
stacks, timers and wait queues, then the synchronization objects built upon them.
First make a blocked task wake correctly; only then add priorities, deadlines and
another CPU. A correct queue on one CPU is reusable evidence only after checking
the new ordering, ownership and reclamation assumptions.

The MCU and x86 branches can proceed independently after the common task and
synchronization mechanisms. The H745 uses an original runtime per core and
explicit messages between them. The x86 branch develops coherent SMP, process
address spaces and shared-kernel services. T56 brings completed components into
applications; VM/store completion does not gate an early context-switch exercise.

| Stage | Build on | New implementation |
|---|---|---|
| T49 | Earlier hosted C and architecture work | OS observations and finite scheduling models |
| T50 | Task/context observations | Original stacks, context switching and preemption |
| T51 | Original task runtime | Wait/wake, synchronization and IPC |
| T52 | Task and synchronization mechanisms | Real-time policies and analysis |
| T53 | Shared task and synchronization foundation | x86 SMP |
| T54 | Shared foundation, on a separate branch | Physical M7/M4 AMP |
| T55 | Atomics and shared-memory execution | Lock-free structures and reclamation |
| T56 | Completed mechanisms required by each project | Concurrent services and applications |

This table shows the conceptual route. Exact prerequisite project IDs in the
project route govern entry and allow the MCU and x86 branches to proceed separately.

## Required targets and boundaries

| Target | Actual responsibility | Completion evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Linux x86-64 | Observe hosted processes, scheduling, IPC, virtual memory and resource control | Commands, source, actual observations and controlled changes |
| STM32F439 | Original single-core preemptive tasks and peripheral/interrupt handoff | Strict image audit plus independent board timing and fault observations |
| x86-64 QEMU, 1/2/4 CPUs | AP startup, per-CPU state, IPIs, shared-kernel scheduling and OS services | Real guest traces and fault campaigns at each supported CPU count |
| NUCLEO-H745ZI-Q | Original M7/M4 runtimes, static ownership, shared SRAM, HSEM notification and cache/DMA visibility | Both image hashes, standalone boot and two-core physical trace |
| Pinned FreeRTOS | A separate comparison workload | Configuration, API/port inspection and actual run; does not replace the original runtime |

The H745 branch does not promise general cross-core task migration or cross-core
priority inheritance. The strict profile does not assume undocumented global
exclusive-monitor support; CAS-based MPMC/reclamation work executes on x86 SMP.
No observed overlap on a host or emulator replaces physical MCU observations.

## Work with target-specific evidence

```sh
python3 -m cmastery init PR-T49-03 ../my-os-observatory
python3 -m cmastery check ../my-os-observatory --target host
python3 -m cmastery report ../my-os-observatory
# Select a target and supported CPU count declared by a family:
python3 -m cmastery check ../my-smp-lab --target x86-smp --cpus 4
```

Use a family's manifest and executable-evidence directory to find exact tests.
Default tests are stage anchors. An assessor suite does not accept a learner's
explanation, independent implementation or physical claims. `--profile tsan`
selects a separate hosted diagnostic build; its runtime support must actually be
available. It neither instruments firmware nor proves all possible schedules.

`record-physical WORKSPACE MANIFEST` registers image/capture files with source
hashes, board/silicon revisions, clocks, cache/MPU state, instrument settings,
overhead and trace-overrun records. It preserves submitted evidence with status
`recorded`, requiring assessment of the raw observations. It never manufactures
an automatic physical pass from filenames or a successful firmware build.

## Deep diagnosis and performance

For every synchronization mechanism, deliberately construct a counterexample:
signal before wait, timeout racing grant, owner exit, event coalescing, queue full,
stale identity, premature reclaim, false sharing, interrupt arrival or peer stall.
Find the first incorrect state transition, repair its invariant and replay a
changed schedule. Reuse the T43–T45 reduction, disassembly and measurement methods.

Record ready-selection work versus task count, timer/wait-queue work, critical-
section duration, context-switch and wakeup latency, CPU time, wall time, cycles,
contention, throughput, stack/storage peaks and logical/device I/O separately.
For parallel speedup, retain the serial baseline, workload size, CPU placement and
instrumentation cost. An observed maximum is not a universal worst-case bound.

Complete the [concurrent-system contracts](#guide-concurrent-system-contracts), exact
project dossier and delayed transfer before accepting each capability. Hardware
waiting time and uncalibrated learner estimates remain visible in the workload.

<a id="guide-second-edition"></a>

# C Mastery 2: the implementation route

This edition retains the original assessable coverage and deepens it through a
single growing collection of components. The archived first edition is identified
by Git tag `curriculum-v1-2026-10-10`; `curriculum/migration.json` maps each prior
objective and project into active teaching. Active sources may be corrected and
reorganized without rewriting that historical record.

## A project route through the domains

Use the [project route](#guide-project-route), not numerical domain order. Start with
the diagnostic and precise C foundations. Introduce warnings, same-failure
reduction, debugger observations, bounds experiments and simple work counts as
soon as their named prerequisites are ready. Later diagnosis and measurement
projects reuse those habits under optimization, concurrency, devices and resource
pressure.

The sequence develops portable components, assembly/ABI evidence, Linux and MCU
adapters, physical communication, complete protocol families and advanced
reasoning. T46 then builds a bytecode runtime, T47 a persistent store and T48 an
educational operating system. Their final integration runs a VM and store in one
user process on the learner's kernel. Previously accepted parsers, containers,
allocators, queues and tests move forward with their contracts.

## Working with the supplied laboratory

Run the laboratory inside Linux x86-64; Windows hosts may use WSL. The Python
runner uses the standard library and is separate from the Sphinx publication
environment. From the source checkout:

```sh
python3 -m cmastery doctor
python3 -m cmastery list --module T46
python3 -m cmastery init PR-T46-01 ../my-runtime-lab
python3 -m cmastery check ../my-runtime-lab --compiler gcc --profile debug
python3 -m cmastery check ../my-runtime-lab --compiler clang --profile asan
python3 -m cmastery report ../my-runtime-lab
# Once its project evidence is complete:
python3 -m cmastery advance ../my-runtime-lab PR-T46-02
```

The first check of an unsolved scaffold is expected to fail its implementation
checks. Read the contract, seal predictions and implement the named mechanism.
The runner records commands, results, environment and source identity under the
learner workspace. A later source edit makes old evidence stale. Missing tools or
an unavailable adapter produce an explicit unavailable outcome.

Family suites can exercise more than one milestone. Passing a suite does not
automatically complete every objective linked to the family. The project-specific
explanation, failure campaign, independent variation and physical claims remain
separate. Assessor implementations are a distinct validation bundle; they are not
copied by the learner initialization command. Deliberately consulting them changes
the independence claim and calls for a fresh transfer exercise.

The [executable evidence directory](#guide-executable-evidence) lists exact test names,
scope and remaining work. The runner selects the current project's checks; use
`--all-tests` for cumulative family regression. For a second listed family, use
`cmastery init PROJECT EMPTY_PATH --family NAME`. Explicit completed dependencies
are selected with `--dependency runtime=PATH` or `--dependency storage=PATH`.
Use `advance WORKSPACE PROJECT` for the next supported project in that family.
It preserves implementation files and existing fixtures, archives the previous
brief, predictions and latest result in `evidence/history/`, and selects fresh
project evidence. Selection does not itself accept a prerequisite or a completed
project. Keep each independent transfer attempt in a separate workspace.

## Comprehensive completion

Complete every required objective, integration and delayed-transfer gate, including
physical UART, USART, I2C, SPI, RS-232, RS-422, RS-485, CAN, CAN FD and Ethernet
observations. Partial portfolios remain useful records of completed capabilities.
Software, emulator and physical evidence retain separate identities.

The full program is intentionally extensive. Project hours count new work once;
directories and reused artifacts add no duplicate budget. Reading, implementation,
verification, assessment and consolidation are recorded separately. Trial timings
from authors are not learner-time calibration; workload estimates retain that
uncertainty until actual learner observations exist.

## Closing the final system

First execute the runtime and store independently on Linux. Then establish kernel
boot, exceptions, paging, process isolation, scheduling and block ownership. Port
through explicit allocation, console and block adapters. Run a bytecode workload
that commits data, restart the guest and recover the committed result. Inspect
failure and resource evidence at each boundary before defending the whole system.

The required kernel has a deliberately bounded process/device contract. A working
guest is evidence for its pinned emulator and configuration. It does not establish
physical disk power-failure behavior, general OS compatibility or the MCU's
electrical/timing properties.

<a id="guide-entry"></a>

# Start here: evidence of mastery

This is an independent-study curriculum for someone who already writes basic C and understands elementary algorithms. The goal is to build small, explainable components, then carry them into a Linux process and a Cortex-M firmware image. Progress depends on evidence, rather than finishing a prescribed number of weeks.

A completed component has a contract, a working C implementation, a correctness argument, a resource model, adversarial tests, and a record of its dependencies. You must be able to explain a failed run and defend a design change. A passing test suite alone does not establish all of these abilities.

## Begin with the diagnostic

Complete the three-hour entry check in [T01](#t01) before choosing its remedial projects. Work without a solution or assistant-generated implementation. You may consult compiler and debugger manuals. Predict results before running them and save the prediction with the actual output. Identify which errors occur during compilation, linking, startup, or execution.

If the diagnostic passes its mandatory checks, retain its evidence and skip its remedial implementation work. Otherwise repair the specific gap and retest on changed inputs. There is no extended introductory course before the shared core.

Numerical work has additional entry checks. Before [T17](#t17), explain absolute versus relative error, powers of two, a finite geometric sum, vectors and matrix multiplication, and the meaning of a residual. Before filtering, distinguish sample rate from signal frequency and explain convolution of two short sequences. Before scheduling analysis, add rational utilizations and solve a small fixed-point recurrence. Use paper calculations, then independently check them in a hosted harness. Missing mathematics calls for targeted remediation before the relevant project; it does not require postponing all language study.

## Use a project as the unit of study

1. Read the module entry check and the project's contract. Record the selected standard, platform, dependency profile, capacity and failure policy.
2. Predict two normal cases and two boundary cases before opening the supplied expected results.
3. Study only the assigned passages. Write a short explanation in your own words. Mark any claim that depends on a compiler, libc, ABI, OS, or peripheral.
4. Implement the mechanism in C. Use the supplied fixtures and add at least one independent test that could reject your implementation.
5. Inspect failures and generated artifacts. Submit the evidence named in the project, including limitations.
6. Apply the mastery gate. When it fails, reduce the failing case, repair the underlying model, and repeat the gate on a new case.
7. After a delay, rebuild or adapt the component without consulting the prior implementation. Keep the new result and comparison.

Most implementation milestones fit a 4–12 hour working session budget, often spread over several sessions. Reading, assessment and later retrieval have separate budgets. An estimate is permission to narrow scope and diagnose an obstacle; it is not a time limit on learning.

## Independent study without a required mentor

Self-review is structured. Keep predictions dated, conceal fixture answers until the first attempt, and use the rubric in [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment). A week later, select a changed capacity, representation or failure point and defend the result from first principles. Record a short spoken explanation or a written review as if another programmer had to maintain the component.

An external reviewer is useful but optional. If a tool or assistant supplies a complete implementation, that implementation is study material. Reimplement the mechanism independently on a changed contract before claiming its objectives. Assistance with diagnosis is legitimate when the evidence records what was supplied and what you subsequently demonstrated.

## Equipment and boundaries

The shared core needs a Linux x86-64 environment, GCC, Clang and ordinary development tools. A Windows host may use WSL. The firmware branch uses a NUCLEO-F439ZI, its debugger connection, a serial connection and documented safe loopback or test devices. Analog and bus timing experiments need appropriate real instruments; they can be postponed while host and emulated work continues.

QEMU's MPS2 AN386 target is a separate Cortex-M learning platform. It cannot validate STM32F439 registers, pin routing, ADC behavior or board timing. A successful host, model or emulator test supports only its own contract. Hardware mastery gates remain pending until the physical evidence exists.

Advanced kernel work and modern lock-free reclamation retain their required v3 dispositions. Other elective subjects retain their explicitly recorded dispositions. Core awareness still requires explaining why their assumptions matter.

<a id="guide-roadmap"></a>

# Roadmap and prerequisite map

Domain numbering preserves coverage, not chronology. Begin with the diagnostic, build a shared portable core, then branch into Linux and firmware. Contracts, error handling and tests recur from the first project; their deeper modules consolidate practice.

For the recommended working sequence use the [project route](#guide-project-route). It brings introductory diagnosis, bounds experiments and measurement forward through selected prerequisites. The complete-domain order below is a reference traversal, not a demand to delay those projects.

## Phases and handoffs

| Phase | Main work | Handoff and gate |
|---|---|---|
| Entry | T01 plus targeted mathematical remediation | Predict, repair and explain a small multi-file program |
| Precise C | T02–T06, selected T12, early T18/T21/T32 habits | Object/representation/contract evidence on small components |
| Tools and reusable mechanisms | T07–T09, T12–T16, T18–T22 | Audited portable container/parser/allocator library; P1/P3 |
| Runtime boundary | T10–T11/T13, selected Linux interface foundations | Explain actual entry, linking and helper closure; P2 |
| Linux branch | T23–T25 plus testing/security refinements | Bounded telemetry, ownership/backpressure/shutdown; P5 |
| Firmware branch | T27–T31 plus selected T25 leaves | Reset, drivers, contexts, DMA and timing; P4 |
| Deeper reasoning | T17, T26 awareness, T32–T35 | Numerical, formal, performance and resilience evidence; P6 |
| Algorithms and architecture | T36–T37 after their named C/tool/ownership foundations | Handwritten assembly, invariant-backed algorithms, machine and MCU evidence |
| Communication foundations | T38–T39 after drivers and relevant architecture preludes | Measured serial/electrical channels and audited Ethernet frame ownership |
| Complete stack families | T40–T42 after their distinct prerequisites | Seven-layer telemetry, Ethernet-to-HTTP and socket-based HTTP server defenses |
| Measurement and diagnosis | T43–T45 after their named foundations; use introductory habits from the first component | Multi-axis cost evidence, causal diagnosis, repaired fault experiments and delayed transfer |
| Capstones | Shared core plus completed relevant branches | Independently defended Linux and firmware applications |
| Runtime, storage and kernel | T46–T48 after their explicit prerequisites | Portable VM, recoverable store, isolated kernel processes and an integrated persistent guest |
| OS, real-time and multicore | T49–T56 through stage-specific prerequisites | Original task runtime, synchronization, x86 SMP, physical MCU AMP and concurrent services |

T18 ownership and API foundations precede T14 container design. T29 requires selected race/atomic/ordering leaves from T25, rather than finishing all POSIX threading projects. Module front cards enumerate the precise preludes. Complete an explicitly named prelude before its dependent project even if the full domain is scheduled later. T26 preserves its awareness/elective route; T55 adds required advanced concurrency implementation.

## A valid full-domain order

The following order is computed from full prerequisites and the owning domains of selected module and project objective preludes. It supports full-domain completion. Early projects may begin after their own named entry/prelude gates; this serial traversal does not require postponing them until all later milestone foundations are complete:

[T01](#t01) → [T02](#t02) → [T03](#t03) → [T04](#t04) → [T05](#t05) → [T06](#t06) → [T07](#t07) → [T08](#t08) → [T09](#t09) → [T12](#t12) → [T18](#t18) → [T32](#t32) → [T14](#t14) → [T15](#t15) → [T16](#t16) → [T19](#t19) → [T20](#t20) → [T21](#t21) → [T22](#t22) → [T13](#t13) → [T11](#t11) → [T10](#t10) → [T17](#t17) → [T23](#t23) → [T24](#t24) → [T25](#t25) → [T26](#t26) → [T27](#t27) → [T28](#t28) → [T29](#t29) → [T30](#t30) → [T31](#t31) → [T33](#t33) → [T34](#t34) → [T35](#t35) → [T36](#t36) → [T37](#t37) → [T38](#t38) → [T39](#t39) → [T40](#t40) → [T42](#t42) → [T41](#t41) → [T43](#t43) → [T44](#t44) → [T45](#t45) → [T46](#t46) → [T47](#t47) → [T48](#t48) → [T49](#t49) → [T50](#t50) → [T51](#t51) → [T52](#t52) → [T53](#t53) → [T54](#t54) → [T55](#t55) → [T56](#t56)

## Parallel progress

After the portable foundations, a Linux learner can advance processes/events while a firmware learner completes reset/driver work. Both retain a common protocol and data-structure core. To complete the full core curriculum, return to the other branch and defend both capstones. A branch-only portfolio is useful but is not full-core completion.

Source reading and proof/measurement techniques recur at progressively deeper gates. Where a selected prelude introduces a mechanism early, mark those exact objectives complete with evidence and reuse them later; do not double-count the work. Use the complete objective map to identify unassessed leaves before final review.

<a id="guide-component-contracts"></a>

# Shared component contracts and evidence cards

Apply these cards to the boundary named by a project. The project brief supplies
its specific inputs, allowed operations, limits and observations. A reusable
record may support several objectives; link the exact claim instead of copying
the entire dossier into every assignment.

## Card 1: representation before mutation

Write an abstraction function: what logical value does the concrete state mean?
Then state the representation invariant and every admitted state, including empty,
full, failed, destroyed and partially constructed states where applicable.
For a ring with capacity C and count n, the live sequence has n elements and
0 <= n <= C; equal cursors do not determine empty versus full by themselves.
At each mutator, establish its precondition before forming an invalid pointer or
executing arithmetic whose result is not representable.

The useful proof boundary is a state transition. If adding a node needs both a
free slot and a link update, acquire the slot first or provide an explicit rollback
path. An allocation failure must not leave the old logical value ambiguous.

## Card 2: storage, ownership and dependency profile

Record live objects, their extents, owners, borrowers and mutation rights. A
numerically unchanged pointer after resize does not establish that a previous
alias remains valid. A cancellation request does not establish completion or
device quiescence. Name the event that permits each buffer to be reclaimed.

Under the C17 baseline, alignment alone does not turn a declared character array
into arbitrary typed allocated storage. Use actual typed objects, byte operations
and value copies, or genuinely allocated storage according to the selected
contract. A target-specific mapping or firmware storage convention needs its own
implementation assumptions. Check alignment, type, lifetime and bounds separately.

Use [profiles A–F](#guide-profiles). A hosted test harness can call a mature oracle;
the studied target mechanism must be implemented locally. Audit source effects,
undefined symbols and the final image. Compiler helpers, callbacks, startup,
libraries and transitive allocation belong in the declared closure. Source spelling
alone does not establish an allocation-free or no-library property.

## Card 3: failure policy and progress

State whether a failing operation leaves the old state, publishes a partial result,
or enters an explicit recovery-required state. For transfers, record requested
length, positive returned counts, cursor movement, zero progress, retry and error.
For persistence, distinguish return, completion, synchronization and the actual
durability assumptions. An uncertain commit outcome must not be relabeled as a
definite abort merely because the caller saw an error.

Exercise empty and singleton cases, exact capacity, one beyond capacity and every
acquisition-failure prefix that can occur. Use invalid-input tests only through
interfaces that admit the invalid representation. Deliberate native undefined
behavior belongs in a bounded supervised fault exercise, never in a supposedly
portable functional oracle.

## Card 4: independent evidence

Begin with a handwritten prediction and a small independent model. Then add a
boundary input, a generated sequence, a metamorphic relation or a deliberately
wrong implementation that the check rejects. Merely translating the target code
into Python is weak independence. State the distinct reasoning used by the oracle.

Keep four identities: the source revision, built artifact, input and environment.
An observation belongs to that combination. A fixture replay establishes a finite
model result; a compiler run establishes a build observation; a board trace
establishes a physical observation under its recorded setup.

## Card 5: resources and explanation

Name the question and unit before collecting numbers. Keep algorithmic work,
instruction count, CPU cycles, elapsed time, CPU time, stack/heap peaks, allocation
counts and I/O traffic separate. Explain inclusive/exclusive accounting and
overlapping asynchronous spans. Compare instrumented and ordinary builds before
attributing a change to the studied algorithm.

Give a bound with its assumptions, a measurement with its uncertainty, and a
counterexample that would reject your interpretation. Measured high-water marks
and observed maximum latency are not universal worst-case bounds.

## Progressive dossier sizes

| Stage | Minimum record | Reused evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Early mechanism | Prediction, small program, observed result, one boundary and explanation | Toolchain identity and common build commands |
| Reusable component | Interface/invariant, implementation, independent tests, failure history, resource/dependency ledger | Accepted prerequisite component revisions |
| Systems integration | Ownership/timing trace across boundaries, adverse campaign, platform records and defense | Portable-core evidence whose assumptions still hold |
| Delayed transfer | Changed capacity/representation/failure schedule; explanation without the old solution | Prior record as a comparison after the new attempt |

A failed delayed gate reopens the affected claims. A stronger performance score
does not compensate for incorrect lifetime, arithmetic, authority or failure
semantics. See [assessment](#guide-assessment) for the common rubric.

<a id="guide-concurrent-system-contracts"></a>

# Concurrent-system implementation and evidence contracts

These contracts extend the shared component cards. Each project names the stage
and supported target; a later feature is not an unstated early prerequisite.

Declare the numerical priority convention in every trace. The finite inheritance
and ceiling fixtures use larger numbers for higher urgency; the original
`execution` runtime uses smaller numbers for higher urgency. Translate urgency
when moving an example between them. Numerical order alone is not a portable
scheduling contract.

## State, lifetime and authority

Keep process address spaces/handles separate from thread context, stack, wait and
join state; keep CPU-local current-task and interrupt state separate from both.
Every ready/wait/timer-list membership has one owner. Task states have explicit
transitions among NEW, READY, RUNNING, BLOCKED and EXITED. Reaping requires that
no CPU, wait object or callback can still use the task's state or stack.

The advanced OS uses bounded admission: eight process slots, thirty-two total
thread slots and four threads per process. Treat these as tested limits and reject
one beyond each. Retain the original six-slot T48 compatibility workload. Static
ELF spawn selects a validated boot-archive image; it is not a general exec/dynamic-
linking API. COW clone admits exactly one thread and no outstanding operation,
gives the child only explicitly permitted handles, and rolls back partial failure.

Use generation identities for revocable handles. Shared-memory messages carry
validated offsets/lengths, not pointers meaningful only in another address space.
Pin a mapping/frame while copying or using it across a blocking operation; a
successful earlier range check does not protect against a concurrent unmap.
TLB invalidation acknowledgments precede frame reuse. A failed acknowledgment
quarantines affected state; it must not be treated as a successful remote flush.

## Waiting and synchronization

Wait registration, protected-state release and blocking form one serialized
transition. Grant and timeout race for one result. A timeout cannot consume a
permit or message that the caller was not told it acquired. Absolute monotonic
deadlines avoid extending waits after every notification. State rollover bounds
explicitly and use a half-range argument only within its valid interval.

| Primitive | Required contract and failure experiment |
|---|---|
| Semaphore | Checked maximum/count; permits have no mutex ownership; reject overflow |
| Mutex | Nonrecursive, owner checked; ISR acquisition forbidden; test inversion and nested donation withdrawal |
| Condition | Predicate loop under the matching mutex; atomic release/wait; reacquire before returning |
| Message channel | Fixed capacity and explicit copy/borrow ownership; normal close drains accepted messages; abort discards and wakes waiters |
| Events | Wait-any/all and clear-on-consume defined; bits coalesce rather than count occurrences |
| Notifications | Count accumulated occurrences with explicit overflow policy |
| Barrier/once | Generation and initialization failure/lifetime defined; no early reuse while old participants remain |
| Reader/writer lock | Declared fairness policy; exercise writer starvation and interrupted acquisition |

Cancellation is cooperative. Owner failure poisons affected mutexes and wakes
waiters with failure; protected state is not silently declared consistent. A
recursive lock attempt, stale handle and wrong-owner unlock must produce an
explicit result. In fixed-priority variants, donation follows dependency chains
and is removed on timeout, cancellation and unlock. A ceiling protocol states its
task/resource assumptions; it is not interchangeable with ordinary inheritance.

ISR-safe APIs are separate bounded entry points: no blocking, allocation, remote-
core waiting or arbitrary callbacks. They report whether deferred scheduling is
needed. Interrupt masking only excludes the relevant local contexts. A spinlock
must account for local interrupts and cannot be held across blocking operations.

## Machine and compiler boundary

Use the strict E/F variant: original reset/entry/vector/trap/context code and
required runtime helpers; no linked libc, libgcc, compiler-rt, libatomic, HAL,
OpenAMP or existing scheduler. Compiler headers and inspected inline intrinsics
are permitted. Audit final link inputs and instructions as well as undefined
symbols: static linkage can hide a dependency from `nm -u`.

Save the context required by the ABI and architecture, including alignment,
exception-return metadata and any enabled FP state. Begin with integer-only
contexts, then test FP preservation and the selected lazy-stacking policy.
Distinguish compiler ordering, C synchronization, hardware barriers, MMIO and
cache/DMA ownership. `volatile` does not establish a happens-before relation.

## SMP, AMP and progress

The x86 SMP route starts with a coarse kernel-entry lock and deferred rescheduling,
then separates locks after correctness. Timer preemption, concurrent kernel entry
and a fully preemptible kernel are different claims. Per-CPU ownership, remote
wakeup, migration and shootdown protocols each need independent adversarial tests.

The H745 route has separately linked M7/M4 images and static peripheral/task
ownership. Both linker scripts reserve identical common SRAM, excluded from
ordinary `.bss` clearing. M7 initializes shared state before publishing an epoch-
qualified ready handshake. Shared queue state is authoritative; HSEM doorbells
may coalesce, requiring drain/recheck before sleeping. A peer timeout does not
authorize reusing state it may still own.

Start with noncacheable shared control and SPSC rings using aligned 32-bit indices
and inspected acquire/release publication. Cacheable payloads use cache-line-
exclusive ownership: clean/complete before publication, invalidate/complete before
consumption. Include unrelated dirty-byte loss and late-DMA counterexamples.
Do not assume generic inter-core CAS support on this target.

Specify lock-free progress for the whole admitted operation, including allocation,
reclamation and callbacks. Identify a linearization point and record overlapping
operation histories. Stalling one participant is an essential test, not proof of
all schedules. Hazard protect/validate/retire and epoch quiescence are lifetime
protocols; neither follows merely from making a pointer atomic.

## Real-time and physical observations

Separate task WCET assumptions, release jitter, blocking, interrupt interference,
scheduler overhead and communication-server interference. Derive response-time or
demand bounds for the declared model; compare model traces with actual traces.
Keep fixed-priority ceilings and EDF resource rules distinct. A utilization bound
for independent uniprocessor tasks does not certify a shared-resource multicore
application. Overload handling must name drop, defer, coalesce or fail behavior.

Physical H745 records include both image hashes/boot epochs, overlapping work
pulses on one analyzer timebase, a shared peripheral timer for common timestamps,
per-core DWT deltas, fixed clock settings, silicon revision, cache/MPU regions,
trace overflow and instrument overhead. Never subtract unrelated M7/M4 cycle
counters as if they shared a synchronized origin. Run cold-reset trials detached
from the debugger. Mark simulated, emulated, instrumented and physical records
separately, preserving missing observations as not-run.
