<a id="guide-enhancement"></a>

# Algorithms, architecture and interfaces: the extension route

T36–T42 extend the preserved T01–T35 curriculum. They deepen existing implementations and connect them to machine execution, electrical interfaces and complete communication services. Complete the named prerequisite or selected prelude before its dependent milestone. A project family is a view of module work, not an additional budget.

## From mathematical mechanism to reusable C

Use this progression for each selected algorithm. The complete vector, list, heap, hash, AVL and graph work from T14/T15 remains the reusable base.

| Level | Question to answer | Artifact and failure evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Mathematical relation | Which outputs are correct for which inputs? | Input/output relation, invariant, termination measure and counterexample |
| Finite representation | Where do values, links and states live? | Index/offset/ownership diagram, checked arithmetic, capacity and unreachable-state case |
| Handwritten assembly | Which instruction/register transitions implement that relation? | Original x86-64 or Thumb source, liveness table, ABI harness, bounded accesses and disassembly |
| Typed C | Which C object and lifetime rules permit the representation? | Actual typed storage or representation-safe byte interface, failure-atomic operations and differential evidence |
| Higher abstraction | Which representation details can a client ignore? | Typed wrapper, opaque/context/callback interface, comparator/ownership/invalidation contract and replacement implementation |
| Measured execution | What determines actual work and elapsed time? | Operation counts, cycle/model assumptions, repeated measurements and disclosed uncertainty |

An abstraction preserves a promised relation while permitting a different representation. It does not remove lifetime, error or resource obligations. A generic pointer collection and a byte-copy value container have different contracts. An assembly kernel has the chosen platform ABI; its arithmetic does not grant permission for C signed overflow.

For lower-bound search, derive a half-open search interval before writing instructions. In a sorted array, all positions below `lo` contain values less than the key, and all positions at or above `hi` contain values at least the key. Every update preserves those statements and shrinks `[lo, hi)`. At `lo == hi`, return that boundary; it can equal the array length. Duplicate keys make the difference between “some matching position” and “the first position whose value is at least the key” observable. Compare the C and handwritten kernels on the same relation, then expose the typed wrapper. Compiler output is useful comparison evidence but does not replace writing the required assembly.

T36 applies this progression to search, stable sorting, heap repair, AVL certificates, collision probing, byte matching and graph frontiers. T37 explains why equivalent operation counts can produce different machine behavior: finite ALU flags, clocked state, instruction encoding, hazards, locality, memory reachability and exception boundaries.

## Three architecture levels

| Level | Authority and scope | Curriculum experiment |
|---|---|---|
| ISA and ABI | Exact Intel/Arm instruction semantics and selected call convention | Decode actual bytes, handwrite callable kernels, prove register/stack obligations |
| CPU implementation or declared model | Pipeline/cache structure and quantitative assumptions | Four-bit ALU, clocked toy datapath, hazard schedule, tag/index/replacement traces, CPI and Amdahl calculations |
| Microcontroller and board system | Selected STM32 bus masters, memory targets, clock/peripheral integration and fitted board components | CPU/DMA reachability, reset/exception artifacts, driver ownership and physical measurements |

The toy datapath, pipeline and cache are deliberately small models with explicit inputs and outputs. Their predictions are not observations of an x86 implementation or a Cortex-M4. F439 CCM is CPU-only for the selected DMA use, and F439 does not have the data-cache behavior of a Cortex-M7. Interrupt entry has an architectural saved frame and separate compiler/handler obligations; it is not an ordinary function call with another name.

The source spine includes [R-clrs-4](#r-clrs-4) (fourth-edition *Introduction to Algorithms*) and [R-hanson-cii](#r-hanson-cii) (*C Interfaces and Implementations*), alongside the exact Knuth and Hennessy/Patterson editions assigned in [T36](#t36) and [T37](#t37). The historical publications include Dijkstra's 1959 graph paper, Hoare's axiomatic basis and Dijkstra's refinement notes. Native contracts come from pinned Intel/Arm manuals and ABI documents. Follow exact module reading locators and their limits: a contents page, graph-origin badge or old textbook example is not an inspected current contract.

## Communication progression

T38 separates peripheral behavior from voltage conversion, medium access and application meaning. T39 separates PHY/media, MAC frame service, descriptor ownership and upper-layer protocols. Use `Communication stack families` for the complete projects.

| Interface | First-principles implementation/measurement focus | Main teaching |
|---|---|---|
| UART | Start/data/parity/stop timing, divisor error, RX faults, TXE versus final TC | `T38.02` |
| USART synchronous mode | Peripheral-generated clock, polarity/phase and last pulse; compare with asynchronous UART and SPI | `T38.03` |
| I2C | Wired-AND, pull-up feasibility, arbitration/stretching, combined transactions, terminal NACK and conditional recovery | `T38.04–05` |
| SPI | All four sampling modes, target-defined chip-select framing, receive draining and buffer/completion ownership | `T38.06` |
| RS-232 | Logic/wire voltage and polarity conversion, DTE/DCE and connector/pin contract | `T38.07` |
| RS-422 | One-driver differential multidrop, pair polarity, termination and receiver observations | `T38.08` |
| RS-485 | Differential multidriver medium, part-specific enable timing, final-stop-bit release, grant schedule and byte-channel events | `T38.09` |
| Classic CAN | Actual transmitted-bit arbitration, frame/error states, timing encodings and bxCAN mailbox/filter/FIFO ownership | `T38.10–11` |
| CAN FD | ISO DLC, FDF/BRS/ESI, CRC/stuffing changes, nominal/data timing and external-controller capabilities | `T38.12` |
| Ethernet | Physical media and link, MAC frame/FCS/padding, addressing/switching, RMII/MDIO and DMA handoff | `T39` |

The F439 has classic bxCAN. A transceiver alone cannot add CAN FD. The FD topic includes an original software format/capability project and a documented external-controller route; physical FD closure is conditional on exact additional controller/adapter setup inspection and hardware evidence. The inspected TCAN4550 has separate VSUP and VIO supplies. Its full device supply cannot be replaced by the Nucleo's 3.3 V rail.

## Reuse and assessment

Reuse the earlier container/parser/ownership library, Linux adapters, startup/linker artifacts and MMIO/ISR/DMA mechanisms. Add the new invariant certificate, assembly kernel, interface or protocol boundary specified by each milestone. Mark reused artifacts by their original project IDs; carry actual prior evidence rather than assuming a component still meets its contract after a change.

For each new objective retain a distinct evidence item: derivation, state trace, original implementation, negative case, tool result or physical observation as appropriate. A synthetic verifier establishes only its static calculation. Actual machine code, OS socket behavior and electrical/PHY results need their own execution records. After a delay, reconstruct a mechanism and change one capacity, representation, target or fault assumption.

Read [guide-roadmap](#guide-roadmap) for the full dependency order, [guide-communication-stacks](#guide-communication-stacks) for the three families, [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles) for implementation boundaries and [guide-workload](#guide-workload) for reconciled effort.

<!-- performance-debugging guide extension -->

## Continue into cost and causal diagnosis

The assembly, architecture and communication artifacts become experimental subjects in [T43](#t43)–[T45](#t45). Follow [guide-performance-debugging](#guide-performance-debugging) for complexity models, hosted/bare-metal profiling, progressive debugger practice and controlled memory/lifetime experiments. Earlier implementations and evidence are reused rather than charged twice.

<a id="guide-communication-stacks"></a>

# Three complete communication project families

The three families teach different ownership boundaries. Each consists of small module milestones with exact contracts, fixtures, failure cases and evidence gates. The family view adds no hours to the workload table: every milestone is already charged in its owning module.

| Family | Owned implementation | Supplied mechanisms | Completion evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| [T40](#t40): EDU7-v1 | Original seven-layer protocol, routing relay, message transport, dialogue/session, codec and application | MCU UART engine and declared RS-485 transceivers/media | Independent layer faults plus actual two-segment electrical and end-to-end routed exchange |
| [T41](#t41): Ethernet through HTTP | Custom PHY-management/MAC-DMA adapter, Ethernet/ARP/IPv4/ICMP/TCP subset and HTTP integration | F439 MAC hardware, LAN8742A analog PHY, magnetics and cable; previously authored T42 HTTP core | Real PHY/MAC/DMA records and independent ARP/ping/TCP/HTTP captures, loss/flow/close/cable-reset campaigns |
| [T42](#t42): HTTP server | Original HTTP octet parser, router, serializer, socket lifecycle, queues and deadlines | OS TCP/IP/link/physical stack | Original C inspection and independent curl/raw-client results with fragmentation, framing, partial I/O and bounded resources |

X.200 supplies a conceptual service/peer model, not a wire implementation specification. EDU7-v1 is an original educational protocol designed to make all seven responsibilities observable. Internet protocols use their own normative contracts; TCP/IP and HTTP do not form seven matching OSI protocols. See [R-NET-X200-1994](#r-net-x200-1994) and the exact assigned RFC/device passages.

## Family 1: a real seven-layer exchange

Use endpoint A, router R and endpoint B across two distinct RS-485 segments. R has two independent UART/transceiver channels and relays at the network layer. Each segment has its own master/grant schedule and local link addresses. The source/target IDs at different layers are separate namespaces.

| Layer | Original responsibility and public service | State/identity owned here | Fault that must stop here |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 physical | Declared UART/transceiver configuration exposes ordered octets and explicit UART/link faults | Bit timing, DE/receiver state, medium and local transmit ownership | Bad voltage/wiring, contention, framing/overrun and premature DE release |
| L2 data link | Delimit/escape/CRC bounded frames and grant access on one segment | Segment-local source/destination, frame parser and grant state | Bad CRC/length/escape, foreign local address or invalid grant |
| L3 network | Deliver bounded end-to-end datagrams through a static relay | Node IDs, route/interface/next hop and hop limit | Unknown route, invalid protocol/length or exhausted hop limit |
| L4 transport | Segment/reassemble complete messages with matching ACKs, credit, probes and bounded retry | Ports, transfer IDs, fragment index/count and reassembly | Missing/duplicate/wrong ACK, out-of-order fragment and blocked credit |
| L5 session | Negotiate the schema/units, control dialogue token, checkpoints and retained-state resume | Session ID, epoch, token holder and committed checkpoint | Token violation, incompatible OPEN, conflicting duplicate or lost-state resume |
| L6 presentation | Convert original typed records to canonical bounded TLVs | Schema, tag ordering, integer byte order, units and UTF-8 validity | Malformed/noncanonical representation or unrepresentable typed value |
| L7 application | Execute bounded GET/SET fixture-plant operations and correlate responses | Request ID, setpoint and permitted value range | Unknown verb, missing semantic fields or out-of-range SET; old state survives |

Adjacent-layer services use owned spans or complete events with explicit consumed/retained storage. Peer headers travel as lower-layer payload. The router copies the datagram before returning an RX buffer; it does not decode or apply the application's SET. A CRC is integrity evidence, not authentication. A successful transport ACK is separate from session commitment and successful application execution.

Work a SET of 2500 centidegrees with request ID 0x1234. Its presentation PDU without label is 15 octets: schema 1, verb TLV, request-ID TLV, signed value TLV and unit TLV. A seven-octet session DATA header makes 22 octets. One transport fragment fits the 24-octet fragment payload; its eight-octet header makes 30. The six-octet network header makes 36, within the 40-octet link payload. Five link header octets plus CRC make 43 unescaped body octets. Compute CRC before delimiter escaping; actual wire length depends on escaped values.

R preserves network source 17/destination 51 and every transport/session/presentation/application octet, decreases hop 4 to 3, selects the other segment and rebuilds that segment's link frame/CRC. The local address numbers 1/2 may recur on both segments; their meanings belong to their segment, not a global node namespace. Verify both ingress and egress capture points. A direct A–B loopback cannot close the relay objective.

Complete PR-T40-01 through 08 in order, reusing T38's byte-channel interface and earlier parser/queue/timer work. The physical milestone measures the actual declared transceiver, guards, final-stop-bit release and cable setup; porting the same API to another transceiver requires part-specific timing evidence. Host traces may close higher-layer tests while physical gates remain pending. Checkpoint/resume retains RAM state only. Peer reboot refuses resume; no durable exactly-once or authenticated-session claim follows.

## Family 2: Ethernet layer 1 through HTTP

The selected physical route is the NUCLEO-F439ZI/MB1137 with LAN8742A. Verify the actual board marking, revision, fitted bridges/jumpers and inspected manual boundary. The PHY and magnetics implement analog cable signaling. Learner C configures and observes the digital PHY-management/MAC/DMA route and constructs the higher protocols. A byte array or host TAP interface cannot close physical layer 1.

| Boundary | Contract and ownership | Required evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Cable/PHY | Actual media, reset/identity, reference clock, link and negotiated mode | Board/part identity, RMII clock/status and cable removal/recovery |
| MAC/DMA | Reachable buffers, normal descriptors, complete publication before OWN and completion before reuse | Map/ordering ledger, descriptor/status traces, backpressure and reset handling |
| Ethernet | Untagged Ethernet II, local/broadcast filtering, type, FCS and padding policy | Validated frame spans; exclude preamble/SFD and subtract retained FCS exactly once |
| ARP/IPv4/ICMP | Bounded configured-peer resolution, fixed IPv4 header/checksum/length and unicast echo | Cache/timer, corrupt length/checksum, exact echo and explicit options/fragment rejection |
| TCP | Passive-open tuple, checksums, modular sequence/ACK/window, retransmission, flow and close | Loss/duplicate/prefix/zero-window/timer/FIN/RST/TIME-WAIT traces |
| HTTP | Reused portable T42 parser/serializer on preserved stream bytes | GET/HEAD/binary echo and error response through actual custom transport |

The precise controlled profile is in the T41 contracts. Static addresses, one configured peer, one connection, a small MSS and one outstanding segment make state inspectable. Omitted IPv4 options/reassembly and general TCP event/congestion coverage mean this is a restricted interoperability laboratory. A cooperative client exchange does not certify a general Internet host.

Use virtual monotonic time for deterministic TCP timer tests; actual firmware keeps its declared physical linger/deadline behavior. Distinguish congestion allowance from advertised receive window and from local storage. ACK-only, SYN and FIN consume different sequence space. IP total length excludes Ethernet padding; TCP checksum includes its IPv4 pseudo-header. PHY link, MAC completion, TCP acceptance and HTTP application success are different evidence.

T39 supplies the architecture and validated frame-channel mechanisms. PR-T41-01 through 08 add finite protocol state, exact controller work and end-to-end closure. Reuse the T39 adapter and its artifacts when compatible; charge only the changed controller/protocol/integration work specified in T41. A solved vendor Ethernet driver or lwIP/OS TCP stack cannot perform the custom work being assessed.

## Family 3: an HTTP server from scratch

Begin this family on Linux loopback using the previous event/descriptor adapters. PR-T42-02 through 05 build the portable grammar, framing, chunk decoder, router and serializer. PR-T42-01/06/07 attach the owned socket lifecycle, partial-output persistence and deadlines. PR-T42-08 requires independent clients and a scope defense.

GET and HEAD /health select exactly three representation octets, hex `6f6b0a`. HEAD sends the GET-equivalent length and no body. POST /echo returns the bounded original octets. The profile supports bounded origin-form and absolute-form authority, separate trailers, immediate 100-continue or header-determined error, FIFO responses, strict ambiguous-framing rejection and staged close. Root fixtures include exact one-request close-mode headers for reuse by T41.

Test every selected byte split, multiple coalesced requests, duplicate Content-Length, TE+CL, chunk extensions/trailers, premature EOF, short sends, EAGAIN/EINTR, slow progress and request-total deadlines. Following optimistic CONNECT/Upgrade bytes and requests after close never receive another application dispatch. RFC 9112 plus the inspected March 2026 RFC 9931 update inform the limits; the project's unsupported-transition rejection policy remains explicitly an origin-server policy.

No HTTP library implements the target. OS sockets supply the lower stack; curl and an independent raw-octet peer are verification tools. Completion requires actual original learner C and peer results, rather than the supplied static fixture verifier alone.

## A practical shared route and equipment

1. Preserve the accepted T14/T15/T18 library and T23/T24 adapters. Complete the relevant machine/startup/driver/ISR/DMA prerequisites.
2. Develop T36/T37 alongside the appropriate earlier foundations. Complete T38 serial/electrical and T39 frame-channel gates.
3. Build the portable T42 parser/serializer milestones before the final T41 HTTP milestone. They are charged once in T42. Hosted-server work can progress while physical equipment is unavailable.
4. Complete the original T40 seven-layer family and the T41 custom Internet subset as separate contracts. Reuse mechanisms and evidence by original project ID.
5. Defend each family's layer ownership, source scope, limits, resource bounds and physical-versus-synthetic closure independently.

| Route | Declared equipment and evidence boundary |
|---|---|
| Hosted algorithms/HTTP | Linux x86-64/WSL toolchain, debugger, independent clients and injected test clocks |
| Thumb/MCU | Exact Cortex-M4/F439 toolchain/ABI, startup/map artifacts and selected board |
| Serial electrical labs | Declared matching UART/USART/SPI/I2C targets, logic analyzer/appropriate voltage measurement, transceiver/connector/power documentation |
| EDU7 physical | Three declared MCU nodes, router with two UARTs, four THVD1400 adapters, two short terminated bench segments and common-reference measurement |
| Ethernet physical | Declared F439ZI/LAN8742A board, dedicated host Ethernet adapter/cable and independent packet capture; isolated same-link configuration |
| Required physical CAN FD | Supported external controller/adapter or alternate native-FD board, correct separate supplies, exact additional setup readings and an independent peer |

Equipment identity and physical measurements belong to the learner's evidence. The curriculum supplies contracts and static/reference oracles; it does not report these future hardware runs as completed. See [guide-workload](#guide-workload) for totals and [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for mastery records.

<a id="guide-performance-debugging"></a>

# Performance, debugging and failure experiments

Use [T43](#t43) to explain and measure cost, [T44](#t44) to move from symptoms to causal evidence, and [T45](#t45) to investigate memory and lifetime failures. Each track adapts earlier small C components. An algorithm, allocator, parser, driver or event loop already built in its owning module becomes the experimental subject; the new project pays for the additional measurement, diagnosis or repair.

## Start the habits early, deepen them in stages

From the first component, state its input sizes, capacities, ownership and failure policy. Predict a boundary result before running it. Keep the exact build command, input, result and unanswered question. In T03/T05, practice object bounds and warnings; in T21/T32, preserve first-cause context, minimize a failure and retain a regression. These are early habits within the existing budgets, rather than a requirement to finish three advanced domains before writing C.

After the named foundations, follow the full project contracts. T43 deepens the T13/T15/T30/T34/T37 cost and timing work. T44 begins with warnings, logs and a small reproducer, then adds stepping, watches, optimized images, I/O, concurrency and firmware diagnosis. T45 deepens the T03/T16/T21/T27/T29/T31/T32/T35 ownership, storage and failure work. Later system and firmware projects name their selected preludes. A cross-reference supplies a route, not automatic credit for an objective.

## Give every complexity claim a cost contract

Record the operation, successful and rejected outcomes, input/output parameters, representation, case and primitive cost. For a graph, both vertices and edges may matter. For a parser, input bytes and produced records may matter. Distinguish worst case, a specified expected-input distribution, and an amortized sequence guarantee. State any bound on key length, comparator cost, recursion or allocation separately.

An exact abstract count such as

$$
C(n)=3n^2+5n+7
$$

has a tight quadratic bound: for integer $n\ge1$, $3n^2\le C(n)\le15n^2$. This supplies constants and a threshold; a finite timing plot does not supply the same proof. A loose upper bound also does not establish a tight bound or a universal speed ordering. Amortized analysis accounts for expensive operations across a sequence; it does not require random inputs. Use the bounded formal and amortized passages in [R-clrs-4](#r-clrs-4) and the original certificates in T43.

“Cycles” needs an explicit meaning. Executed processor cycles depend on instructions, memory behavior, clock and execution conditions. They are not the cycles of a control-flow graph. Cyclomatic complexity is a static graph metric used in design and testing; it is not a time complexity class. The quantitative architecture reading [R-ENH-HENNESSY-PATTERSON-6](#r-enh-hennessy-patterson-6) and the control-flow reading [R-PERF-NIST-SP500-235](#r-perf-nist-sp500-235) support different claims.

| Measure | State the boundary and unit | Useful evidence and remaining question |
|---|---|---|
| Abstract work | Comparisons, moves, probes, visited edges, or another declared primitive | Exact counters and a proof for the input family; primitive costs may differ |
| Time complexity | Function of named sizes and case, with model assumptions | Upper/lower/tight or sequence argument; finite samples do not prove asymptotics |
| Instructions and cycles | Executed instructions/events or identified processor-counter cycles | Matching image, event definition and observation; stalls and frequency affect interpretation |
| Elapsed and CPU time | Clock, process/thread scope and start/end events, in time units | Raw timestamps and scope; parallel process CPU can exceed elapsed time |
| Space | Logical live bytes, capacity, retained storage, simultaneous scratch, stack or static sections | Lifetime ledger, map, conditional frame bound and qualified observations; categories are not interchangeable |
| Code and control flow | Linked/object code bytes or a declared connected-function graph | Matching build and graph; neither determines runtime alone |
| Traffic and I/O | Useful, read, written and transferred bytes at a named layer; calls, blocks or I/O operations | Model and actual counts kept separate; amplification is undefined when useful bytes are zero |
| Latency and throughput | Particular completion interval versus completed items in a stated window | Per-request events and window counts; queueing and overlapping stages matter |
| Deadline and jitter | Release/start/finish definitions, deadline and variation statistic | Observed misses and distribution; sampled tails are not a WCET proof |
| Energy | Instrument/counter, units, measurement boundary and integration method | Actual qualified energy observation; elapsed time alone cannot establish energy |

A space ledger counts shared storage once and takes the peak over simultaneous lifetimes. Sum of all allocations over a run is not peak live space. A freed allocation may remain reserved by an allocator. Stack-frame estimates need call paths, indirect calls, recursion, callbacks and permitted exception nesting. Keep sampled high water and an analytical bound as separate entries.

## Measure a component through its complete operation

Draw the events before choosing timers: accepted request, submit, function return, completion, buffer release, and any requested persistence or peer-observation boundary. An asynchronous submit can return while a borrowed buffer is still in use. Overlapping spans cannot be added blindly to obtain end-to-end latency. Inclusive and exclusive function attribution require a stated nesting model. Subtracting process CPU time from elapsed time does not universally measure waiting.

For read/write work, record requested bytes, each returned positive count, cursor advancement, EOF and retry/error history. Measure setup, read, processing, write, requested synchronization and cleanup separately when useful. Label the filesystem/device, buffering, file lifetime and warm/cold assumption. A successful write, complete transfer, requested synchronization and experimentally established crash durability are different claims. Use the exact Linux interface and synchronization readings assigned in T43/T44; reuse the existing partial-I/O adapters.

The abstract block model in [R-PERF-VITTER-2001](#r-perf-vitter-2001) names item count, fast-memory capacity and block size. A block transfer in that model is not automatically one system call, cache miss, DMA transaction or physical media operation. Compare these layers to explain a discrepancy, preserving their units.

## Profiling routes and experimental controls

| Route | New investigation on a reused component | Evidence limits and practical alternative |
|---|---|---|
| Portable/hosted harness | Paired, repeated consumed-result trials; exact work and lifetime counters; clock/read-overhead controls | Preserve raw samples, workload, build identity and ordering. Inspect generated code when work may have disappeared. Reuse T34's harness |
| Linux PMU | Identified per-process events, grouped counts, enabled/running times and permitted sampling evidence | Availability and event meaning vary. Multiplex scaling is an estimate and requires positive running time. Denied/unsupported events remain explicit; clock/work measurements close narrower claims |
| Linux cgroup v2 | Read permitted CPU, memory, per-device I/O and pressure accounting; compare a prepared delegated quota when available | Configuration is distinct from accounting. Ancestor limits, membership, controller and writeback scope matter. Read-only observations and supplied finite snapshots support a no-root route |
| Compiler instrumentation | Matching baseline versus bounded entry/exit hooks, coverage/arc counts and a supported single-threaded gprof comparison | Instrumentation changes code, stack and timing. Counted calls, sampled self time, estimated child time and off-CPU waits are separate. Record dropped or incomplete traces |
| Bare metal | Identified counter or timer around a reused kernel; empty-bracket and interrupt variants | Verify presence/access/enable/clock/wrap/debug conditions and shared trace ownership. An ambiguous multi-wrap interval cannot yield a unique delta. Timer/GPIO alternatives need their own actual setup |

The route contracts are bounded by [R-PERF-LINUX-CLOCK-6-19](#r-perf-linux-clock-6-19), [R-PERF-LINUX-PERF-EVENT-6-19](#r-perf-linux-perf-event-6-19), [R-PERF-LINUX-CGROUP-V2-6-18](#r-perf-linux-cgroup-v2-6-18), [R-PERF-GCC-INSTRUMENT-16-2](#r-perf-gcc-instrument-16-2), [R-PERF-GPROF-2-47](#r-perf-gprof-2-47) and [R-ENH-ARMV7M-DDI0403EE](#r-enh-armv7m-ddi0403ee). Record the installed versions rather than assuming the inspected versions are installed. Use already permitted per-process capabilities or a prepared delegated environment. Each project distinguishes an actual run, a supplied-data analysis and unavailable evidence.

Before comparing speed, keep correctness, ownership and failure gates fixed. Separate setup from the measured operation, declare warmup and workload families, vary execution order, preserve outliers and state the sample/quantile convention. Compare instrumented and uninstrumented artifacts; measure observer cost rather than subtracting an assumed constant indiscriminately. A debugger stop, allocation interceptor, log call or sanitizer can change the behavior being measured. Repeat only when the changed condition or unresolved uncertainty justifies it.

## Debugging progression: from a symptom to a repair

Begin with a defined-state wrong-result defect. Predict the first invariant that should fail, then use warnings, an assertion or bounded log to locate it. Assertions support internal diagnostics; externally required validation must survive a build that disables them. Preserve the first useful cause before later cleanup or logging changes its context.

Next, make a bounded same-failure reproducer. The reducer distinguishes PASS, the same FAIL, and UNRESOLVED, such as malformed input or a different failure. A 1-minimal result can still be larger than another trigger. Reduction localizes an input; the causal explanation still needs the invalid state transition. See [R-PD-DDMIN-ISSTA2000](#r-pd-ddmin-issta2000).

Use source and instruction stepping, selected frames, pure conditional breakpoints and valid-object watches to discriminate competing explanations. Keep the exact image and debug information. Watchpoints have target resources, lifetime, thread and stopping-granularity limits. In optimized code, a source variable or statement may have been removed or moved. A core or fault snapshot is a stopped state, with missing-history and missing-memory limits. The precise command readings are in [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009).

Advance to partial I/O, descriptor reuse, race/deadlock/predicate histories and reset/HardFault/ISR/DMA diagnosis. Reconstruct cursor, ownership and happens-before transitions rather than patching the last visible crash. Avoid treating stale errno after success, a longer sleep, a larger buffer, or a cleared single pointer as causal proof of a repair. Compare debug, optimized and suitable instrumented builds after fixing the invariant.

## Bug laboratory: mechanism, observation and mitigation

The same visible crash or corrupt output can have different causes. Each T45 brief asks for a pre-run prediction, a controlled negative case, an observation, a discriminating experiment, the first supported invalid transition, a causal repair and delayed transfer. Tool diagnostics and native undefined-behavior symptoms are not fixed portable output strings.

| Failure family | Mechanism and useful experiment | Repair and mitigation limits |
|---|---|---|
| Buffer over/underflow, off-by-one, missing NUL | Separate capacity, initialized length and terminator space; probe lower/upper/exact boundaries and preserve sentinels | Validate before invalid arithmetic/access, maintain length/capacity invariants and rejection policy. A legal-address wrong-cell write still needs a logical invariant |
| Wrapped or truncated size | Trace checked count×stride plus headers/terminator, signed conversion and narrowing | Check before each operation and preserve ownership on rejection. Unsigned wrap is defined arithmetic but may violate the size contract |
| Stack exhaustion | Bound depth, frame size, callbacks, reentrancy and permitted nesting; compare compiler records, samples and isolated child-process exhaustion | Reduce/bound depth or frames and reserve justified space. Per-function reports, fill scans and canaries do not prove every execution fits |
| Stack-local buffer corruption | Observe a bad extent/initialization transition within an existing frame | Repair that object's contract. More total stack capacity does not repair an out-of-bounds access |
| Fixed `.bss`/RAM placement or startup error | Inspect link-region capacity, alignment, load/run sections and copy/zero/retained ranges | Repair placement or startup ranges. Link success does not bound dynamic use or establish correct initialization |
| Heap/stack collision | Use an explicitly declared shared interval and dynamic-region guard; distinguish it from stray writes | Enforce allocator/stack boundaries for that map. Hosted heaps do not universally follow this model |
| Leak or forgotten release | Trace every acquisition and partial-failure prefix, owning/borrowed edges, cleanup order and live/retained bytes | Restore exactly-once release and bounded retention. Reachable retained storage differs from a lost-owner leak; RSS alone is not the oracle |
| Failed resize, UAF, double/invalid free, escaped alias | Trace generations and extents; preserve old owner on failed nonzero resize; invalidate prior aliases on success, including reused address tokens | Fix ownership and publication. `free(NULL)` is valid; clearing one owner does not clear other aliases. Diagnostic quarantine cannot establish correct lifetime |
| Uninitialized state | Distinguish addressability from field initialization and track propagation to a consuming branch/output | Initialize complete semantic state before publication. Zero bytes are not a universal pointer/value initialization rule; padding is not semantic field state |
| DMA/callback/ISR lifetime and reentrancy | Trace submit, timeout, cancel request, confirmed completion/quiescence and reuse; introduce late/stale completion and shared-scratch cases | Keep borrowing until the declared completion/reclaim condition. A timeout or cancellation request alone does not establish device quiescence |

`.bss` is a fixed linked section: it does not grow during execution. “BSS overflow” can mean a linker region-capacity failure, incorrect startup ranges, corruption of a global object, or dynamic regions colliding under a custom layout. Write the exact mechanism in the dossier; each needs different evidence. T45 supplies separate models and actual map/startup observation tasks.

The held explanation [R-effective-c-2](#r-effective-c-2), historical detector mechanism [R-MEM-ASAN-PAPER-2012](#r-mem-asan-paper-2012) and current bounded tool/linker readings complement one another. Use ASan/UBSan for their selected checks, separate unsanitized Memcheck for supported comparison, and LSan for the declared leak phase. MSan is a conditional experiment with its own platform and external-code instrumentation requirements. A detector's silence is not a complete ownership or correctness proof. Actual board observations remain separate from hosted tools and finite histories.

## Experiment dossier and delayed transfer

Keep contract and units; predicted symptoms and competing causes; source/image/input/tool/environment identities; finite timeout and capacities; raw observed events; first invalid transition and discriminating evidence; reduced trigger; causal repair; regression/measurement matrix; and remaining claims. Retain the original failing case and a nearby case that rejects a symptom-only patch.

Practice with guidance first, then receive a symptom-only variant whose cause and oracle are withheld until the dossier is complete. A reviewer or peer can prepare an unseen case. For solo work, delay and use an unopened seeded variant, then disclose what the generator or prior work already revealed; self-authored known faults have weaker independence. A public supplied oracle replay is regression practice, rather than an unseen diagnosis gate.

After roughly one to two weeks, change capacity, failure point, build configuration, nesting or completion order and repeat the reasoning. A delayed failure reopens that claim. A repaired defect passes only when the invariant, regression and changed-condition evidence agree. Static fixture checks accept the supplied finite contracts; learner C, actual debugger/profiler/tool records and physical measurements remain separate activities.

<a id="guide-standards"></a>

# Standards, dialects and measured support

Use explicit `-std=c17` for the portable baseline and keep C23 experiments in a separate build configuration. A compiler's default dialect can change. A GNU dialect permits extensions beyond the corresponding ISO mode. `-pedantic-errors` is useful diagnostic evidence, but acceptance is not a proof of conformance.

## Edition comparison

| Edition | Teaching comparison | Curriculum use |
|---|---|---|
| C89 / C90 | ANSI 1989 and ISO 1990 origins; prototypes, portable declarations and hosted/freestanding distinction | Read historical code; repair implicit assumptions and old declaration style |
| C95 | Amendment to C90, including wider character-library support and alternative tokens | Recognize legacy interfaces and internationalization limits |
| C99 | Mixed declarations, designated initializers, compound literals, `restrict`, integer-width facilities and revised inline rules | Explain which familiar facilities are later than C90 |
| C11 | Atomics, thread storage, alignment, generic selection and static assertions; some facilities are conditional | Separate language memory rules from runtime/library support |
| C17 | Technical corrections to the C11 line; ISO publication is 2018 | Default portable implementation contracts |
| C23 | ISO publication is 2024; type inference, `typeof`, `nullptr`, bit-precise integers, attributes and checked arithmetic among major teaching comparisons | Parallel feature probes and carefully scoped migration |

Publication identities and the committee's draft links are recorded by [WG14](https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg14/www/projects). Its N3220 link is labeled an early C2y draft and N2310 an early C23 draft. The inspected N3096 is a pre-publication C23 draft. Use its recorded locators with that label; do not cite it as an exact copy of ISO/IEC 9899:2024. Defect reports, proposed corrections and later working drafts can describe different wording.

## Compiler and library matrix

Checked 2026-10-04. These documentation entries are bounded support reports, separate from local experiments. [GCC status](https://gcc.gnu.org/projects/c-status.html) and [Clang status](https://clang.llvm.org/c_status.html) are live pages; revisit them when selecting an installed release.

| Facility | GCC documented introduction | Clang documented introduction | Runtime/library question |
|---|---|---|---|
| Explicit C17 mode | `-std=c17`; default GNU17 in GCC 8–14 | C17 mode from Clang 6; status page retains partial qualifications | Hosted libc and optional features are separate |
| Explicit C23 mode | C23/GNU23 modes; default GNU23 from GCC 15 | `-std=c23` from Clang 18; partial support | Do not equate a dialect flag with whole-edition support |
| `nullptr` | 13 | 17 | Pointer use is a compiler feature |
| `typeof` / `typeof_unqual` | 13 | 16 | Distinguish older extensions from ISO semantics |
| Object `auto` inference | 13 | 18 | Not C++ object deduction semantics |
| Object `constexpr` | 13 | 19 | Does not provide general C++ constexpr functions |
| `_BitInt` | 14, target-qualified | Check the selected target/release | Arithmetic lowering, ABI and maximum width need probes |
| `#embed` | 15 | 19 | Inputs and build dependencies must be explicit |
| `<stdckdint.h>` | 14 | Verify selected headers | Header implementation and overflow behavior need tests |
| `<stdbit.h>` | Verify compiler/libc pair | Verify compiler/libc pair | Availability cannot be inferred from language parsing |
| Non-native atomics | Target-dependent | Target-dependent | May require an atomic runtime; lock-free is a separate property |

GCC's floating-point qualifications and Clang's partial/unknown entries prohibit claiming full conformance from this table. C++ library availability says nothing about the C library selected by the C driver.

## Executed local probes

The recorded environment is WSL Ubuntu Linux x86-64, GCC 15.2.0 (Ubuntu 15.2.0-16ubuntu1), glibc 2.43. Seven exact snippets compiled with warnings, `-Werror` and `-pedantic-errors`, then exited successfully: a C17 width assertion; C23 `nullptr`; `auto` plus `typeof`; object `constexpr`; unsigned `_BitInt(17)`; `ckd_add`; and `stdc_count_ones`. Sources and results are preserved in `reviews/compiler_probes.json`.

This establishes only those snippets in that installation. Clang was not installed for execution, the embedded compiler was not exercised, and no complete standard/library test suite was run. Learners repeat feature probes for their environment before relying on a facility. Record language acceptance, header availability, successful linking and runtime behavior in separate columns. Include a negative or overflow case where relevant; a nominal call alone is a small capability probe.

## Claim classification

Label each reasoning statement as ISO guarantee, implementation-defined choice, unspecified outcome, undefined behavior, extension, ABI convention, libc behavior, POSIX/Linux contract or hardware constraint. Save the authority and configuration. For example, a C pointer does not gain a valid lifetime from an integer address that looks plausible; x86 behavior is not a portable object-model rule. A `volatile` access does not establish an ISO interthread happens-before edge. A device barrier is not a mutex.

Old-source porting is an investigation rather than a global C89 restriction. Keep the baseline modern and portable, compare edition-sensitive mechanisms in [T05](#t05), and document deliberate extensions at the interface boundary.

<a id="guide-profiles"></a>

# Dependency and allocation contracts

Select a profile for each component and executable before implementation. The profile defines a boundary to audit. A hosted harness may have different dependencies from the reusable component it tests.

| Profile | Boundary and permitted headers | Startup and linked support | Allocation and services | Required audit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: hosted C | Whole hosted program; standard headers permitted, POSIX only when declared | Platform CRT, libc and declared libraries; compiler helpers permitted | Explicit allocation allowed; record ownership, failure handling and OS use | Link command, dynamic dependencies, undefined symbols, allocator entry points |
| B: allocation-free component | Named component and declared callees; `<stddef.h>`, `<stdint.h>`, `<limits.h>` and selected interface headers; explicitly allow individual library calls | Hosted CRT normally belongs to harness; list libc/helper calls reachable from component | Caller storage only in component; separately investigate transitive allocation, TLS, lazy initialization and callbacks | Source call graph plus binary evidence and failure instrumentation; disclose opaque callees |
| C: portable component with no external C-library calls | Component only; declaration/type headers permitted; no calls to external C-library functions | Hosted harness supplies testing/printing; compiler support routines require an explicit allowlist, or must be removed | Caller storage or explicit allocator callback; no direct OS service | Component object undefined-symbol allowlist, generated code, callback contract and target build |
| D: custom-entry Linux executable | Whole executable; selected types/constants and ABI declarations, no assumed hosted services | Own entry assembly, linker choices, syscall adapter; any compiler helper must be named and supplied or deliberately linked | OS services only through enumerated Linux syscalls; kernel allocation is separate from application allocation | Final ELF, program headers, entry address, relocation/dependency closure and syscall trace |
| E: bare-metal image | Whole firmware; standard type/limit headers and target declarations, own MMIO interfaces | Own reset/vector code and linker script; enumerated memory/arithmetic/ABI helpers; no hidden hosted CRT | Caller storage, fixed pools or declared arena; MMIO/interrupts/DMA, no implicit OS | Map, disassembly, undefined symbols, memory regions, stack budget and reset-to-main trace |
| F: educational kernel and custom user ABI | Named kernel or static user image; explicit boot/ISA/ABI/device contract | Declared bootloader handoff, own entry and exception machinery; named compiler helpers; no assumed hosted CRT | Kernel page/pool policy and explicit user syscall adapters; bounded device capabilities | Boot/ELF/map audit, isolation and scheduler tests, user-copy bounds, device ownership and reset/recovery traces |

Profile C does not promise that the compiler emits no calls. A structure assignment may become a memory helper. Division on a target lacking suitable instructions may require an arithmetic helper. Non-native atomics may invoke a runtime. Audit the actual object and final image, including link-time optimization and libraries selected by the driver.

Caller storage still has an object-model contract. Under the C17 baseline, an aligned declared `unsigned char` array is not automatically typeless allocated storage for arbitrary typed lvalue access. A portable byte arena can expose byte operations and copy values into actual typed objects; a typed pool can use an array of its real element type. A hosted harness can supply genuine allocated storage through an explicit allocator interface. Firmware casts into a byte arena need a documented implementation contract as well as alignment, lifetime and bounds reasoning.

## Make the boundary executable

Keep `dependency-contract.md` beside the component. List allowed headers, external symbols, compiler support, startup objects, allocation sources, OS services and target assumptions. For callbacks, list whether they can allocate, block, retain pointers or reenter the component. Write down whether the promise covers only your code, the reachable call graph, or the entire executable.

Use `nm -u`, `readelf -Ws`, `readelf -d`, the link map and disassembly as complementary evidence. Undefined symbols in an object show requirements before linking; a statically resolved helper will no longer be undefined in the final executable. Search the final symbol table and inspect the relevant code as well. `ldd` belongs only to trusted executable inspection and is not a substitute for static ELF inspection. Profile D projects use `readelf` first.

An allocation-free claim needs more than finding no spelling of `malloc`. Sorting may allocate temporary storage; formatted output and locale initialization may have implementation-dependent costs; a callback may allocate. An allocation interceptor detects selected paths in the tested configuration. It does not prove that every path through an opaque library is allocation-free. Where a hard bound is required, use inspected local mechanisms with explicit storage instead.

## Distinguish six different restrictions

Removing `<stdlib.h>` removes declarations from that translation unit. It does not remove linked code. Removing `malloc` prohibits a particular allocation interface, rather than all storage acquisition. Freestanding compilation changes the implementation environment and compiler assumptions. Suppressing startup files removes the driver's usual entry objects. Suppressing default libraries removes the usual libraries. Suppressing compiler-runtime support is an additional target-dependent obligation.

Under the C17 baseline, freestanding facilities include the selected standard's required minimal headers; do not infer that a complete hosted libc exists. C23 extends freestanding library provisions. Consult the bounded standard-draft material in [guide-standards](#guide-standards) and verify availability on the chosen compiler/library pair. A header's existence does not establish its runtime implementation.

No-library projects may use a hosted oracle that calls the equivalent mature function. The learner's component must implement the studied mechanism itself. Document the oracle's preconditions and disagreements; do not silently choose the result that makes the test pass.

## Resource ledger

For every substantial component, record persistent bytes, worst-case temporary bytes, maximum recursion/stack depth, allocation count and failure behavior. Separate measured high-water marks from analytical bounds. Include interrupts, nested contexts, alignment padding and callback costs where applicable. Profiles are constraints to investigate, not evidence that a custom replacement is safer or faster than a production library.

## Extension boundaries

Handwritten assembly in [T36](#t36) has a chosen ISA/call convention and remains subject to its surrounding C interface contract. Protocol cores in [T40](#t40)–[T42](#t42) use profile C; their hosted/firmware adapters use the separately declared profile A or E. The full Ethernet-to-HTTP family owns its driver and higher protocols while physical MAC/PHY hardware supplies the declared lower mechanisms. The hosted HTTP family owns HTTP and socket lifecycle while the OS supplies TCP/IP and the lower layers. Follow [guide-communication-stacks](#guide-communication-stacks) for the complete ownership map.

<!-- performance-debugging guide extension -->

## Diagnostic and measurement boundaries

An instrumented investigative variant has its own dependency contract. Sanitizers, profiling hooks and logs can add calls, allocation, code, stack and timing effects. Retain the uninstrumented profile-B/C component or profile-E image audit separately; a diagnostic variant cannot silently stand in for its original dependency or resource promise.

Add named cost units, simultaneous lifetime peaks, completion/reclamation events and observer overhead to the resource ledger. Fixed link sections, whole-path conditional stack estimates, sampled high water, allocator retention, process resident bytes and cgroup accounting are distinct entries. Reuse these ledgers in [T43](#t43)–[T45](#t45); the directory does not add another implementation budget.

## Strict third-edition E/F variant

T50–T56 custom images select the strict E/F variant in their dependency ledger.
They retain the existing profile letters for compatibility and add the explicit
restriction: no linked libc, libgcc, compiler-rt, libatomic, HAL, OpenAMP or existing
RTOS. Original memory/arithmetic helpers are allowed and need ABI tests. Compiler
type/limit headers, register definitions and inspected inline intrinsics are
permitted. The x86 bootloader handoff remains an explicit pre-runtime boundary.

Inspect the final link inputs, symbol ownership, memory map and disassembly.
An entirely resolved ELF can still contain an unintended statically linked
library. Ensure memory helpers cannot be optimized into recursive calls to
themselves; prove supported atomic widths/alignment and reject unsupported helper
calls. Diagnostic hosted builds and FreeRTOS/Linux comparison applications have
separate dependency profiles and cannot substitute for a strict-image audit.

See [concurrent-system contracts](#guide-concurrent-system-contracts) for task/ISR
legality, wait outcomes, reclamation and the physical evidence requirements.

<a id="guide-inventory"></a>

# Required implementation inventory

Build a reusable component library gradually. Implement the studied mechanisms in C rather than forwarding to an equivalent library routine. Caller-provided storage or an explicit allocator interface makes the portable core usable in both hosted and firmware harnesses. Apply profiles C/B as appropriate and audit the actual generated dependencies.

| Family | Required core mechanisms | Ownership and acceptance evidence | Principal modules |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sequences | Fixed array, bounded/growable vector, stack, FIFO ring and linked list | Capacity arithmetic, empty/full/wrap states, iterator invalidation and allocation failure | T14, T18 |
| Associative structures | Linear-probing hash table, binary search tree, one balanced-tree family and trie/prefix index | Collision/deletion/tombstone behavior, ordering, prefix and balancing invariants, adversarial capacities | T14, T15 |
| Priority and graph structures | Binary heap/priority queue, bitset/sparse set, disjoint set, graph representation and traversal | Heap order, union/find invariants, disconnected/cyclic graph handling, explicit frontier capacity | T14, T15 |
| Algorithms | Search/partition, insertion sort, quicksort, heap sort, stable merge, counting/radix method, selection, graph traversal/ordering/path, one greedy and one dynamic-programming problem | Stability where promised, comparator contract, overflow-safe indexing, time/space argument | T15 |
| Byte and text processing | Byte copy/move/search, bounded string operations, UTF-8 validation, numeric parse/format, framing, incremental parser and small lexer/grammar processor | Overlap policy, embedded zeroes, truncation, malformed sequences, endian-independent serialization and explicit grammar | T12, T15, P3 |
| Allocation | Arena with marks, fixed-slot pool, stack discipline, bounded variable-size allocator with splitting/coalescing, segregated-class/slab comparison mechanism | Alignment, overflow, fragmentation, exhaustion, lifetime/rollback and metadata corruption tests | T16, P1 |
| Numerical mechanisms | Stable accumulation, fixed-point saturating kernel, matrix layout, interpolation, FIR filter and a small linear solve/iteration | Error contract, residual, conditioning, exact/reference comparison and bounded storage | T17, P6 |
| Abstractions | Callback/context, iterator, tagged union, opaque handle, allocator/backend interface and state machine | Signature compatibility, ownership, invalid states, reentrancy and replacement backend | T18, T19, T20 |
| Runtime and binary | Own entry adapter, minimal memory helpers, linker placement and Cortex-M reset/vector/data/bss initialization | Symbol/dependency closure, ABI alignment, section/segment map and return/fault policy | T08–T11, T27, P2/P4 |
| Systems services | Partial-I/O adapters, event loop, bounded work queue, shutdown/backpressure and portable protocol reuse | Error injection, readiness states, race/lifetime reasoning and resource ceilings | T21, T23–T25, P5 |
| Firmware services | GPIO/UART/timer/SPI/I2C and supported ADC/DMA driver milestones, ISR communication and cooperative scheduling | Register contracts, timeout/recovery, DMA ownership, overflow, timing limits and physical evidence | T28–T31, P4 |
| Verification tooling | Contract tests, property/differential cases, failure injector and reproducible benchmark | Independent oracle, minimized regressions, model assumptions and measurement variability | T32–T35 |

The default balanced-tree choice is AVL; a red-black tree is an acceptable substitution when its invariant and deletion contract are implemented and reviewed. Implementing both is elective. A project may offer a smaller preliminary representation, but it must culminate in the mechanism named in its core contract. If the supplied module chooses another balanced family, use that module's gate and record the substitution in the dossier.

## Component interfaces before code

Define element ownership, copy/move policy, comparator ordering and invalidation rules before choosing representation. A generic byte container cannot infer the lifetime or destruction needs of pointer members. Allocator callbacks need alignment, failure and free/reset contracts. A queue's capacity convention must be explicit: storage of size N is not always usable capacity N.

Core allocators manage a declared backing region. Avoid ordering unrelated allocated-object pointers as if ISO C guaranteed a global numeric address order. Store validated offsets into one backing array when that is the design. Historical allocator readings are critique material; their assumptions are not silently inherited.

Specify the backing region's object type as well as its alignment. For C17, distinguish genuine allocated storage, actual typed pool elements and declared byte arrays. Byte-array bookkeeping and byte payload operations do not grant unrestricted typed access to that storage. Use a representation-safe byte interface or an explicitly documented target contract; retain the T03 effective-type argument in the allocator dossier.

## Worked boundary reasoning

For a vector with `count` elements, require `element_size > 0` before dividing by it. Then prove `count <= SIZE_MAX / element_size` before multiplication. Growing capacity is another checked operation. If growth fails, the original buffer, count and ownership must still satisfy the invariant. A nominal successful append cannot validate that failure rule.

For a circular queue with capacity four and separate count, enqueueing four values fills it; the fifth returns `FULL` without modifying indices, data or count. After two dequeues and two enqueues, iteration follows logical order across the physical wrap. The integration fixtures test this representation-independent contract rather than prescribing your internal index strategy.

For a numerical kernel, choose an error measure before optimizing. Near a zero exact result, a relative-only tolerance is ill-defined or misleading. Use an absolute bound as well and explain conditioning. SIMD and compiler transformations must preserve the chosen contract, including tail elements and exceptional inputs.

One explicit comparison rule is

$$
|y_{\mathrm{computed}}-y_{\mathrm{reference}}|
\le \tau_{\mathrm{abs}}+\tau_{\mathrm{rel}}|y_{\mathrm{reference}}|.
$$

Choose both nonnegative tolerances from the numerical contract, rather than adjusting them after a failed run. The absolute tolerance has the output's units; the relative tolerance is dimensionless. With an exact reference of zero, an output of `1e-8` passes an absolute tolerance of `1e-7`. With reference `1000`, output `1000.002`, absolute tolerance `1e-7` and relative tolerance `1e-6`, the error `0.002` exceeds the allowed `0.0010001`. Account separately for uncertainty in a reference approximation. This rule checks a declared error criterion; it does not establish conditioning or stability by itself.

## Extensions

Additional tree/allocator families, lock-free reclamation, bytecode interpreter, shell, ELF loading, storage engine, RTOS context switching, kernel driver, signal transforms and specialized numerical kernels remain optional. Each extension needs its own inspected evidence, dependencies and gate. Awareness of their tradeoffs is retained even when their implementation is omitted.

<!-- performance-debugging guide extension -->

## Investigation adapters on existing components

Add exact work/lifetime counters, bounded event/timestamp adapters, a tri-state reducer, bounded compiler hooks and fault-dossier replay only where the new project asks for them. Reuse the earlier benchmark runner, parser, allocator, algorithm, event loop and driver. The new implementation is the experimental adapter or repair, not a duplicate mechanism library.

Defend cost units and model bounds, identify the first invalid state, preserve cleanup and ownership, and show regression plus delayed transfer. The project directory in [guide-performance-debugging](#guide-performance-debugging) maps these additional milestones and their owning budgets.

<a id="guide-laboratory"></a>

# Reproducible laboratory and repository

Use Linux x86-64 for hosted experiments, GCC and Clang as complementary compilers, and C17 as the default dialect. WSL is a suitable host arrangement. Record distribution, compiler, libc, linker and kernel versions. The curriculum's publishing environment is separate from the learner's C toolchain.

## Learner repository

```text
c-lab/
  contracts/           # dependency and interface contracts
  include/             # self-contained public headers
  src/core/            # portable mechanisms written in C
  src/linux/           # syscall/POSIX adapters and application
  src/firmware/        # MMIO adapters, vectors, startup and application
  tests/unit/
  tests/integration/
  tests/negative/      # expected compile/link failures
  fixtures/            # inputs plus separately stored oracle results
  platform/            # linker scripts, startup assembly, target descriptions
  evidence/PROJECT-ID/ # commands, versions, reports, review and limitations
  cmake/               # optional toolchain files and presets
  CMakeLists.txt
  Makefile
```

Choose Make or CMake for the first implementation, then reproduce one component with the other to investigate dependency semantics. The build files are learner work. Keep target objects in separate output directories; never reuse a hosted object in a cross build. Header dependencies must rebuild affected objects. Generated headers need explicit producing rules and dependencies.

## Build/test profiles

| Profile | Suggested investigation | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Debug hosted | C17, `-O0 -g -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic`; add focused warnings as supported | Command, diagnostics, debugger record, tests |
| Optimized hosted | `-O2 -g`, then selected `-O3`/LTO experiments | Results, assembly differences, unchanged contracts |
| Sanitized hosted | Address/undefined sanitizers together where supported; thread sanitizer separately | Instrumented paths, tool limitations and minimized defects |
| Portable component | Two compilers, no external library calls in the component | Object symbol audit, harness tests, target comparison |
| Custom Linux entry | Own entry/adapter and explicitly selected link suppression flags | ELF and syscall dossier; no accidental CRT/libc assumptions |
| Cortex-M | `arm-none-eabi` toolchain, exact core/FPU/float ABI flags and linker script | Map, symbol/section/segment audit and reset trace |
| C23 companion | Explicit supported C23 dialect and feature-specific probes | Compile results separated from library/runtime availability |

Suggested warning flags are starting points, not portable assertions. Do not impose `-Werror` on third-party headers indiscriminately. Negative tests should check that a diagnostic occurs for the intended constraint; exact wording changes by version. Preserve literal commands and full exit status.

CMake presets should name a generator, output directory and toolchain, with separate debug/release/sanitized/cross configurations. Export compile commands for inspection. Investigate installation/exported usage requirements with a second consuming repository: an in-tree successful build is not proof that a library package is usable. Do not copy the curriculum's Python publishing dependencies into a learner C project.

## Continuous verification

Run a small matrix on every meaningful change: GCC/Clang C17 unit tests, one sanitizer job, fixture regression, header self-containment and component symbol allowlists. Run cross compilation without hardware. Run actual-board tests separately when connected. Cache build tools deliberately and record resolved versions. Retain a failing case and logs as artifacts. A clean rebuild is necessary after changing toolchains, ABI or compile-time configuration.

Add Valgrind where the chosen host and program are supported; explain its overlap with and differences from compiler sanitizers. Use GDB or LLDB for minimized failures. Collect coverage and targeted mutation evidence after defining useful tests, rather than optimizing a percentage alone. Concurrency tests must identify synchronization assumptions and instrumentation effects.

## Firmware and emulation

Record the board marking/revision, schematic revision, MCU marking, flash/SRAM placement, ST-LINK firmware and bridge configuration. The default USART3 virtual-COM and ST-LINK MCO arrangements are document-revision-dependent; verify the actual board. Keep DMA buffers out of F439 CCM: the CPU-only memory path is unsuitable for the selected DMA contracts.

Use QEMU MPS2 AN386 for a separate reset/vector/memory experiment with its own linker map and UART model. Query the installed QEMU machine list and record the version before using it. The research inspected the published MPS2 documentation, not an installed emulator. Do not reuse a STM32 register driver against an MPS2 peripheral.

For first power-up and flashing, preserve the known image and record reset/boot assumptions. Host tests establish portable logic; emulation establishes only modeled behavior; real-board traces establish observations for the tested setup. Timing and electrical conclusions require suitable physical measurements.

## Rebuilding this handbook

The extension adds handwritten x86-64/Thumb assembly, small architecture models, serial/electrical measurements and two physical stack routes. Follow [guide-enhancement](#guide-enhancement) and the equipment table in [guide-communication-stacks](#guide-communication-stacks) before acquiring parts. Record exact interface voltage, connector, transceiver supply and timing contracts. F439 classic bxCAN and an external analog transceiver do not supply a CAN FD controller; the required physical FD route requires its own supported controller and additional inspected setup.

The editable sources are under `curriculum/`, `references/`, `research/`, `fixtures/`, `site/` and `tools/`. Create a Python virtual environment and install `requirements-lock.txt`, then run `build.ps1`. This validates canonical metadata, recomputes fixture expectations, builds Sphinx with warnings as errors and checks local links and source fidelity. `serve.ps1` serves the generated HTML on loopback port 8766. Normal rebuilding does not query the Knowledge library or resource graphs and needs none of their document payloads.

<!-- performance-debugging guide extension -->

## Measurement and fault-experiment builds

Keep native, debug, optimized, sanitized, coverage, profiling and firmware outputs in distinct build directories. A diagnostic runtime or compiler hook changes the binary and its dependencies; compare against the matching uninstrumented artifact. Record source/image hashes, compiler/linker/tool versions, input and clock/counter identities, actual returned statuses and raw reports.

Store controlled fault cases under a separate learner test target, with finite capacities/timeouts and paired repaired controls. Native exhaustion runs in a learner-owned child process with verified child-only limits and supervisor evidence. Undefined behavior has no promised native crash value or diagnostic string. ASan/UBSan and unsanitized Memcheck runs are separate; conditional MSan needs its own supported instrumented environment.

Use permitted per-process profiling and read-only cgroup observations first. A prepared delegated subtree supports the optional quota experiment. Hardware profiling and fault work reuse the recorded target map, drivers, clock and trace ownership. Static/captured-data analysis is available when a capability is missing, but it leaves the corresponding runtime or physical claim open. Follow [guide-performance-debugging](#guide-performance-debugging) and the exact project limits.


Edition 2 requires physical closure for every named interface; see [guide-physical-evidence](#guide-physical-evidence). Run the learner CLI and retain its scoped receipts as described in [guide-second-edition](#guide-second-edition).

<a id="guide-assessment"></a>

# Mastery gates and the component dossier

Every linked objective needs evidence that could expose an incorrect implementation or explanation. The original objective definitions are retained, and separately versioned extensions append new claims. Use the complete objective map for the current counts. These are separate evidence claims rather than independent assignments: one well-designed experiment may support several objectives, provided its record identifies each claim and its limits.

## Common rubric

Score each dimension 0–3: **0** absent or materially wrong; **1** succeeds on the nominal case with unexplained gaps; **2** satisfies the declared contract and explains boundary behavior; **3** transfers the reasoning to a changed condition and defends the tradeoff.

| Dimension | Evidence for level 2 | Transfer for level 3 |
|---|---|---|
| Mechanism | Predict state transitions and explain generated or observed behavior | Explain a contrasting representation or target |
| Correctness | Contract, invariant, termination and independent checks agree | Adapt the argument after a contract perturbation |
| Memory and ownership | Lifetimes, aliasing, bounds and cleanup are accounted for | Change capacity or ownership policy without losing guarantees |
| Resources and dependencies | Bounds and permitted dependency closure are recorded | Remove a dependency or tighten a resource limit |
| Failure and diagnosis | Invalid input/exhaustion follows an explicit policy; failure is minimized | Recover after a new injected failure without corrupting state |
| Communication and transfer | Another reader can rebuild and assess the result | Defend architecture alternatives and reproduce it after a delay |

Core mastery requires all six dimensions at least 2 and at least two at 3. Correctness, memory/ownership, declared dependencies and failure handling are mandatory: a higher performance or documentation score cannot compensate for a failure there. Awareness projects need accurate explanation, one inspected example and a clear limit; they do not claim implementation mastery. Electives have their own declared gates.

## Growing demands

For T01–T06, evidence may be a compact prediction table, small C program, negative compilation test and explanation. For reusable algorithms and abstractions, require a full component dossier. Systems and firmware gates add binary inspection, environment-sensitive behavior and failure injection. Integration and capstone gates require cross-component traceability, architecture alternatives and a perturbation that changes a real boundary.

Submit a dossier containing:

1. Problem, inputs, outputs, capacities and failure policy.
2. Public API, representation and invariants.
3. Ownership, lifetime and execution-context model.
4. Correctness argument, termination and complexity/resource bounds.
5. Test strategy, supplied and independent cases, oracle assumptions and failure minimization.
6. Build commands, tool versions, binary/dependency evidence and measurements.
7. Alternatives considered, selected tradeoffs and limitations.
8. Objective IDs supported by specific evidence files.

Code comments explain local decisions. The dossier explains why the architecture and contract fit the problem. Do not substitute a function listing for the argument.

## Remediation and delayed retrieval

On failure, name the violated contract and smallest reproducer before editing. Classify the cause: misunderstood semantics, wrong representation, incorrect algorithm, incomplete failure policy, unsuitable tool/environment or invalid oracle. Repair the model, add the reproducer to regression tests, then retest on at least one new case.

Delay retrieval by roughly one to two weeks. Without the old implementation, reproduce a key invariant or rebuild a small variant. Change one parameter: capacity, signedness, allocator, backend, ABI, concurrency strategy or dependency policy. Compare evidence and record which conclusions survive. A delayed failure reopens that gate; it does not erase evidence for unrelated objectives.

## Capstone review

Review the Linux and firmware capstones independently, then compare their shared portable core. Demonstrate malformed input, overload, shutdown/reset and one backend failure. Explain resource ceilings and what happens at each ceiling. Show a complete provenance chain from contract through source and build to artifact and observed result. Record a review defense and answer a counterproposal with evidence.

Accept a capstone only when all mandatory dimensions pass and every required objective has a credible artifact. A sanitizer pass, bounded proof, coverage number, stress run or benchmark is a particular kind of evidence, with particular assumptions. None is a universal substitute for the others.

## Debugging practice and feedback

For [T44](#t44), submit the contract, pre-run predictions, matching source/image/input/environment identities, actual observations, earliest supported invalid transition, competing hypotheses and discriminating test, reduced trigger, invariant-based repair, regression matrix and delayed variant. Mark a supplied finite history as a model. Mark an actual debugger/tool record as an observation of its particular build and execution. A stopped state or smaller input does not by itself establish the complete causal history.

Begin with a guided, defined-state defect and an explicit invariant. Then receive only a symptom and input. The independent gate withholds the planted cause, solution and oracle until the learner seals and submits a dated diagnosis dossier; the learner chooses observations before editing. A visible public fixture or self-authored fault is guided or lower-independence practice. After a repair, challenge it with an adjacent boundary or a competing cause. One to two weeks later, change the capacity, build configuration, failure point or completion order and repeat the diagnosis without the old solution.

Feedback names the missing inference or violated contract before providing a command or solution. A diagnostic-string match earns no causal credit. A clean run retains its executed-path and tool limits. If a required observation is unavailable, record the narrower evidence and leave that claim open. The reduction reading [R-PD-DDMIN-ISSTA2000](#r-pd-ddmin-issta2000) and debugger contract [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009) support this practice; the project supplies the exact bounded scope.

<a id="guide-integrations"></a>

# Integration families and the two capstones

Integration adds new boundary work to already completed components. Do not rewrite or charge the same implementation twice. P1–P6 each have two 8-hour milestones; each capstone has four 8-hour milestones. Additional reading, review and delayed transfer are budgeted separately in the workload guide. Complete the listed module foundations before the corresponding family, then retain reusable evidence.

The enhancement adds three complete [communication stack families](#guide-communication-stacks): an original seven-layer exchange, Ethernet through HTTP, and a hosted HTTP server. Their small milestones belong to T40/T41/T42 and are already charged in those modules. They complement the integration work below; they do not add a second family budget or replace its existing objectives.

## Shared educational wire contract

P3 and both capstones use this deliberately small protocol unless a dossier documents a compatible alternative:

| Field | Encoding |
|---|---|
| Sync | One byte `A5` |
| Version | One byte `01` |
| Sequence | Two unsigned bytes, little endian |
| Payload length | Two unsigned bytes, little endian, 0–32 |
| Payload | Exactly length bytes, including zero bytes |
| Check | Four little-endian CRC-32 bytes |

The CRC covers version, sequence, length and payload, excluding sync and the CRC itself. Use the reflected IEEE polynomial `EDB88320`, initial value `FFFFFFFF` and final XOR `FFFFFFFF`. The supplied fixture oracle uses Python's independently maintained `zlib.crc32`; the learner writes the C mechanism. CRC detects selected transmission corruption, not intentional tampering or authenticity.

A valid empty payload is a complete frame. An incomplete frame reports `NEED_MORE` and retains only bounded state. Length above 32 or unsupported version reports rejection before payload storage. A bad CRC emits no application message. The streaming decoder scans for sync and, after rejecting a candidate, resumes searching one byte after that candidate's starting sync. Sequence numbers wrap modulo 65536; sequence policy belongs to the application, not the framing parser. Declare duplicate/gap handling separately.

The maximum frame is 42 bytes. This bound follows from 1+1+2+2+32+4. Avoid overlaying a C structure on wire bytes: padding, alignment, endianness and object lifetime would introduce unrelated assumptions. Decode integers explicitly and validate size before computing or advancing offsets.

## Integration dossier and perturbations

Link existing component dossiers rather than duplicating their contents. Add a boundary diagram, ownership transfer table, end-to-end error paths, resource ceiling and objective-to-artifact map. For each family change one boundary: allocator policy, capacity, backend, ABI, concurrency strategy or runtime dependency. Explain which invariants survive and which evidence must be regenerated.

The final capstones share the portable protocol core and its tests. They may use different adapters and scheduling policies. A Linux mutex or file descriptor must not leak into the firmware core. A register address must not leak into the Linux core. Prove separation with builds and dependencies as well as architecture prose.

Accept both capstones only under the common noncompensable gate in [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment). Host/model fixtures are reproducible starting cases. Physical firmware timing, bus behavior and recovery need actual board evidence and remain pending for the learner until measured.
