<a id="t04"></a>

# T04 — Integer, bit-level, and floating-point semantics

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| shared | core | 54 | A, C |

**Prerequisites:** [T02](#t02).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 9 | 22 | 12 | 6 | 5 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Make numerical contracts explicit from type selection through serialization and tolerances. Mathematical formulas do not automatically survive finite width, promotions, rounding or compiler transformations. The projects implement checked integers and fixed-point mechanisms, then investigate floating behavior under stated formats and modes.

## Entry check and remediation

Revisit T01 finite patterns and T02 typed expression trees. Derive one mixed signed/unsigned conversion before coding. If rounding-error reasoning is unfamiliar, work with a small synthetic decimal precision model before using host floating-point measurements.

## Component progression

**Checked machine arithmetic.** Derive representable preconditions before addition, multiplication, conversion or shifting. Compare a mathematical reference with the actual C operation and its promoted operand types.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **A size product that wraps to a small apparently valid allocation, followed by a narrowing conversion.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t04-01"></a>

### T04.01 — Integer type selection

Choose a type by required range and role. size_t represents sizes, ptrdiff_t represents certain pointer differences, and intmax_t is a widest signed integer type. Exact-width families are optional; a byte has CHAR_BIT bits rather than an assumed eight. A wire octet and a C byte may need an explicit portability condition.

Investigation: Inventory limits and optional typedefs on both target builds, then justify types for counts, differences and wire fields.

Misconception to resolve: int is not a portable 32-bit synonym and fixed-width typedef availability must be checked.

Observable evidence: A role/range table and compile-time assertions for deliberate target restrictions. Evidence is developed in [PR-T04-01](#pr-t04-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t04-01-a"></a>


- **T04.01.a** Use limits instead of assuming widths for fundamental types. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-01](#pr-t04-01).


<a id="t04-01-b"></a>


- **T04.01.b** Compare size_t, ptrdiff_t, intmax_t, and fixed-width families. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-01](#pr-t04-01).


<a id="t04-01-c"></a>


- **T04.01.c** Account for optional exact-width types and non-eight-bit bytes. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-01](#pr-t04-01).


<a id="t04-02"></a>

### T04.02 — Promotions and mixed arithmetic

Small integer operands promote before arithmetic and bitwise operations. Usual arithmetic conversions then reconcile mixed operand types. For signed -1 compared with an equal-rank unsigned type, conversion can produce the maximum unsigned value. Validate the source value before casting at a boundary.

Investigation: Annotate operand/result types and implement a signed-input-to-size conversion that rejects negatives and excess magnitude.

Misconception to resolve: Casting after a mixed comparison cannot undo the earlier conversion.

Observable evidence: Typed traces and accepted/rejected boundary cases, including a negative source. Evidence is developed in [PR-T04-01](#pr-t04-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t04-02-a"></a>


- **T04.02.a** Trace small-integer promotion before bitwise and arithmetic operations. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-01](#pr-t04-01).


<a id="t04-02-b"></a>


- **T04.02.b** Diagnose signed/unsigned comparison surprises. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-01](#pr-t04-01).


<a id="t04-02-c"></a>


- **T04.02.c** Design conversion boundaries that reject out-of-range values. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-01](#pr-t04-01).


<a id="t04-03"></a>

### T04.03 — Overflow and checked arithmetic

Unsigned arithmetic is modular; signed overflow is undefined in the baseline. A checked operation asks whether the mathematical result is representable before publishing it. For sizes, check multiplication and addition separately. Compiler builtins and C23 checked arithmetic have their own support and result contracts.

Investigation: Implement checked add/subtract/multiply and allocation sizing, then compare them with a supported builtin or C23 probe.

Misconception to resolve: Unsigned wrap is defined but may still violate the application size contract.

Observable evidence: Independent mathematical results, unchanged outputs on failure and minimum/maximum operand tests. Evidence is developed in [PR-T04-01](#pr-t04-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t04-03-a"></a>


- **T04.03.a** Separate mathematical overflow from the selected language semantics. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-01](#pr-t04-01).


<a id="t04-03-b"></a>


- **T04.03.b** Implement checked addition, subtraction, multiplication, and size calculations. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-01](#pr-t04-01).


<a id="t04-03-c"></a>


- **T04.03.c** Compare manual checks, compiler builtins, and C23 checked arithmetic. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-01](#pr-t04-01).


<a id="t04-04"></a>

### T04.04 — Division and remainder

Modern C integer division truncates toward zero, with a remainder satisfying a = q*b + r and a remainder sign matching the dividend when nonzero. Floor division is a different operation. Zero divisors and an unrepresentable minimum/-1 quotient must be rejected before evaluation.

Investigation: Implement a truncating division wrapper and a separate positive-modulus normalization policy; check all sign combinations.

Misconception to resolve: Remainder is not always a nonnegative mathematical modulo.

Observable evidence: Quotient/remainder identities, sign tables and explicit rejection of exceptional operands. Evidence is developed in [PR-T04-01](#pr-t04-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t04-04-a"></a>


- **T04.04.a** Analyze quotient and remainder signs for supported editions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-01](#pr-t04-01).


<a id="t04-04-b"></a>


- **T04.04.b** Handle zero divisors and minimum-integer edge cases. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-01](#pr-t04-01).


<a id="t04-04-c"></a>


- **T04.04.c** Distinguish truncating division from floor division and modular arithmetic. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-01](#pr-t04-01).


<a id="t04-05"></a>

### T04.05 — Shifts and masks

Shift counts must be nonnegative and less than the promoted operand width. Prefer unsigned values for bit construction, then mask to the declared field width. Rotations need a zero-count path to avoid a shift by the width. Leading-zero operations may need a specified zero-input convention.

Investigation: Implement extract/insert/rotate and population/bit-width routines for a declared width, validating count and field boundaries.

Misconception to resolve: Masking a count does not automatically define the intended rotation or make signed left shifts safe.

Observable evidence: Exhaustive small-width checks and edge cases for zero, full width and highest set bit. Evidence is developed in [PR-T04-02](#pr-t04-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t04-05-a"></a>


- **T04.05.a** Validate shift counts and operand types before shifting. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-02](#pr-t04-02).


<a id="t04-05-b"></a>


- **T04.05.b** Construct field insertion, extraction, and rotation operations. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-02](#pr-t04-02).


<a id="t04-05-c"></a>


- **T04.05.c** Compare population count, leading zeros, and bit-width calculations. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-02](#pr-t04-02).


<a id="t04-06"></a>

### T04.06 — Byte order and serialization

A wire format defines byte sequence independently of host endian order, padding and alignment. Decode octets with unsigned shifts into a suitably wide type rather than dereferencing a cast buffer. Packed structures remain implementation/ABI artifacts, not a universal interchange specification.

Investigation: Encode and decode a 32-bit field in network order under an explicit eight-bit-octet condition.

Misconception to resolve: The host structure layout is not the protocol, even when a nominal packet happens to match.

Observable evidence: Known wire bytes, round trips, malformed-length rejection and an unaligned-input test without cast access. Evidence is developed in [PR-T04-02](#pr-t04-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t04-06-a"></a>


- **T04.06.a** Encode integers independently of native byte order. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-02](#pr-t04-02).


<a id="t04-06-b"></a>


- **T04.06.b** Avoid alignment and aliasing assumptions when decoding byte buffers. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-02](#pr-t04-02).


<a id="t04-06-c"></a>


- **T04.06.c** Separate wire formats from packed in-memory structure layouts. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-02](#pr-t04-02).


<a id="t04-07"></a>

### T04.07 — Bit-fields and representation control

Bit-field allocation units, ordering and some type behavior are implementation-defined. They may be useful inside an ABI-controlled representation but should not define a portable wire format or unconstrained device register access. Explicit masks make field positions part of the specification.

Investigation: Compare a measured bit-field layout with a mask-based register model and document read-modify-write implications separately from hardware semantics.

Misconception to resolve: A field declaration does not guarantee one bus access or a particular register bit position.

Observable evidence: An ABI-tagged layout report and explicit mask operations checked against the synthetic register specification. Evidence is developed in [PR-T04-02](#pr-t04-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t04-07-a"></a>


- **T04.07.a** Evaluate bit-field allocation and ordering assumptions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-02](#pr-t04-02).


<a id="t04-07-b"></a>


- **T04.07.b** Compare language bit-fields with explicit masks for register access. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-02](#pr-t04-02).


<a id="t04-07-c"></a>


- **T04.07.c** Document ABI dependence in externally shared binary layouts. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-02](#pr-t04-02).


<a id="t04-08"></a>

### T04.08 — Fixed-point arithmetic

A fixed-point integer represents value q/scale. Select range and resolution together; multiply in a sufficiently wide intermediate, then apply a named rounding and saturation rule. With nearest rounding, one conversion error is at most half a quantum, but subsequent operations require their own propagation bound.

Investigation: Implement a scaled multiply with ties-away-from-zero rounding and saturation; derive intermediate and quantization bounds.

Misconception to resolve: Changing scale is not a free precision improvement when it reduces range or overflows intermediates.

Observable evidence: Exact integer oracle checks, tie cases, saturation endpoints and an error-bound derivation. Evidence is developed in [PR-T04-03](#pr-t04-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t04-08-a"></a>


- **T04.08.a** Choose scale, signedness, range, and precision explicitly. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-03](#pr-t04-03).


<a id="t04-08-b"></a>


- **T04.08.b** Implement widening intermediates, rounding, and saturation policies. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-03](#pr-t04-03).


<a id="t04-08-c"></a>


- **T04.08.c** Derive overflow and quantization-error bounds for a calculation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-03](#pr-t04-03).


<a id="t04-09"></a>

### T04.09 — Floating-point representations

The floating type’s characteristics come from implementation macros and documented formats. IEEE-style NaNs, infinities, signed zero and subnormals need conditional investigation rather than universal assumptions. A finite binary fraction need not exactly represent a finite decimal fraction.

Investigation: Record radix/precision/exponent limits and classify conditional exceptional values on the chosen target.

Misconception to resolve: More printed digits do not make an inexact value mathematically exact.

Observable evidence: A format report, adjacent-value observations and clearly bounded assumptions for exceptional cases. Evidence is developed in [PR-T04-04](#pr-t04-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t04-09-a"></a>


- **T04.09.a** Identify target formats and relevant implementation characteristics. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-04](#pr-t04-04).


<a id="t04-09-b"></a>


- **T04.09.b** Examine NaNs, infinities, signed zero, and subnormal handling. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-04](#pr-t04-04).


<a id="t04-09-c"></a>


- **T04.09.c** Compare floating-point representation with real-number arithmetic. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-04](#pr-t04-04).


<a id="t04-10"></a>

### T04.10 — Floating-point computation

Rounding accumulates, cancellation magnifies relative error near a small result, and fused multiply-add rounds differently from separate multiplication/addition. Choose absolute tolerance near zero, relative tolerance away from it and ULP-oriented checks only under a stated format. Tolerance follows analysis, not a failing test.

Investigation: Compare naive and compensated summation on cancellation-prone data and a fused/separate expression where supported.

Misconception to resolve: Reordering equivalent real arithmetic can change the floating result.

Observable evidence: Higher-precision or exact references, error tables and a justified criterion for each workload. Evidence is developed in [PR-T04-04](#pr-t04-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t04-10-a"></a>


- **T04.10.a** Quantify rounding, cancellation, and accumulation error. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-04](#pr-t04-04).


<a id="t04-10-b"></a>


- **T04.10.b** Compare fused operations and separated arithmetic under stated assumptions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-04](#pr-t04-04).


<a id="t04-10-c"></a>


- **T04.10.c** Choose absolute, relative, and ULP-oriented test criteria. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-04](#pr-t04-04).


<a id="t04-11"></a>

### T04.11 — Environment and compiler modes

Rounding mode, exception handling, evaluation precision and contraction policy are part of the environment. Fast-math can relax assumptions concerning NaNs, signed zero or reassociation. A benchmark comparing modes must first state whether both satisfy the same required contract.

Investigation: Build a strict and documented relaxed configuration, inspect supported environment operations and record semantic changes before timings.

Misconception to resolve: A faster numerical build is not interchangeable if it changes required exceptional behavior.

Observable evidence: Compiler flags, environment-support probes, exception observations and a contract comparison. Evidence is developed in [PR-T04-04](#pr-t04-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t04-11-a"></a>


- **T04.11.a** Inspect rounding modes and floating-point exception behavior. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-04](#pr-t04-04).


<a id="t04-11-b"></a>


- **T04.11.b** Analyze evaluation precision and floating-point contraction policies. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-04](#pr-t04-04).


<a id="t04-11-c"></a>


- **T04.11.c** Compare strict and fast-math builds without silently changing the specification. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-04](#pr-t04-04).


<a id="t04-12"></a>

### T04.12 — Numerical boundary testing

Numerical tests should target adjacent values, extremes, underflow/overflow, ties and cancellation, not just random middle values. An independent reference can use exact rational arithmetic for integers/fixed-point and higher precision for floating calculations. Explain why a tolerance is appropriate at each boundary.

Investigation: Generate boundary partitions and minimize one numerical disagreement without loosening tolerance first.

Misconception to resolve: A relative tolerance alone is unreliable at zero and near cancellation.

Observable evidence: A test partition, independent references, minimized disagreement and recorded acceptance rationale. Evidence is developed in [PR-T04-04](#pr-t04-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t04-12-a"></a>


- **T04.12.a** Generate exceptional, adjacent, extreme, and cancellation-prone inputs. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-04](#pr-t04-04).


<a id="t04-12-b"></a>


- **T04.12.b** Use higher-precision or independently derived reference results. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-04](#pr-t04-04).


<a id="t04-12-c"></a>


- **T04.12.c** Separate tolerance selection from unexplained test relaxation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T04-04](#pr-t04-04).

## Reading guidance

- **R-goldberg-floating-1991**, **Cancellation** (2 h): Distinguish cancellation from simplistic relative-error expectations.

- **R-goldberg-floating-1991**, **Relative Error and Ulps** (2 h): Choose error criteria with explicit magnitude/format assumptions.

- **R-GCC-OPT-152**, **-ffast-math** (1 h): Treat optimization mode as part of the numerical contract.

Read only these inspected locators as the essential spine. Additional reading time covers comparison, notes and retrieval, not an unstated whole-book assignment. Historical examples require the modern contract review stated here; draft and live-document limits remain in [guide-reading](#guide-reading).

## Implementation projects

- [PR-T04-01](#pr-t04-01) — Checked arithmetic and signed division kernel (10 h, profile C, core).

- [PR-T04-02](#pr-t04-02) — Bit operations and explicit wire layout (8 h, profile C, core).

- [PR-T04-03](#pr-t04-03) — Fixed-point rounding and saturation (6 h, profile C, core).

- [PR-T04-04](#pr-t04-04) — Floating contract and boundary laboratory (10 h, profile A, core).

The project-hour total is 34 h and is already included in implementation plus verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation are separate. Follow [guide-workload](#guide-workload) for conditional diagnostic and elective accounting.

## Mastery gate and feedback

Derive checked-operation boundaries and fixed-point error bounds without executing overflow. Defend one serialization contract and one floating tolerance. Reproduce strict/relaxed build differences while naming the assumptions each result requires.

For independent study, make predictions before execution, compare an independent oracle, inspect one counterexample and defend the result aloud or in a short recorded review. Link each original objective to a specific artifact; use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) to score it. A failed gate requires a minimized cause, a corrected model and a fresh regression, not repeated nominal runs.

## Consolidation and transfer

Change width, scale or rounding rule after a delay and revise the proofs before the code. Transfer integer checks to a size calculation and numerical criteria to a new accumulation workload.

## Environment and limits

Use the recorded hosted laboratory in [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and the per-project boundary in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). C17 is the baseline; edition/extension experiments are isolated and capability checked. Supplied fixture oracles validate mathematical or declared synthetic expectations. They do not execute the learner’s C, prove all language behavior or certify target hardware. Record actual commands, versions, observations and unresolved limits separately.

<a id="t05"></a>

# T05 — Standards evolution, dialects, and portability

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| shared | core | 43 | A |

**Prerequisites:** [T02](#t02).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6 | 20 | 10 | 4 | 3 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Treat an edition or dialect as a versioned contract. Learn how C changed, how legacy code can be migrated, and how implementation capability is measured without claiming whole-edition conformance. The elective survey keeps proposals and extensions visible while preserving the portable baseline.

## Entry check and remediation

Use T02 declaration and diagnostic reasoning. Read [guide-standards](#guide-standards) before experiments. If draft and publication identities are confused, write a short authority table before proceeding. C23 projects need support probes, not an assumption that a mode flag implements every library facility.

## Component progression

**A feature claim with a compiler witness.** Keep language, library, ABI and extension claims in separate columns. Implement a fallback and compile the same bounded behavior under the chosen standards modes.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **A compiler accepting syntax while the required header or runtime operation remains unavailable.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t05-01"></a>

### T05.01 — Standards and authority

Published editions, drafts, corrigenda and proposals answer different questions. A normative shall imposes a requirement in its applicable document; a note or rationale explains rather than automatically extending it. N3096 is a pre-publication C23 draft, while later working drafts can include changes beyond the published edition.

Investigation: Build an authority ledger for three claims, recording document identity, wording category, edition and implementation evidence.

Misconception to resolve: A recent committee PDF is not necessarily the published edition named by a compiler flag.

Observable evidence: Traceable claims with separate normative, explanatory and measured columns. Evidence is developed in [PR-T05-01](#pr-t05-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t05-01-a"></a>

<a id="t05-01-b"></a>


- **T05.01.b** Read normative requirements separately from notes and rationale. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T05-01](#pr-t05-01).

<a id="t05-02"></a>

### T05.02 — C89 and C90 baseline

Legacy C89/C90 code often reflects earlier declaration placement, prototype habits and historical implicit declarations. Port the intended defined behavior, not accidental effects of an old compiler. Replace old-style definitions and incompatible callback casts with complete prototypes and real adapters.

Investigation: Modernize a small historical callback/declarator example and build both a declared legacy configuration and the portable baseline.

Misconception to resolve: Compiling an old example today does not prove its old assumptions remain valid.

Observable evidence: A before/after semantic ledger, explicit prototype changes and regression cases for intended behavior. Evidence is developed in [PR-T05-01](#pr-t05-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t05-03"></a>

### T05.03 — C95 and internationalization

C95 internationalization facilities address wide characters, multibyte conversion and alternative tokens within implementation locales. They do not specify a portable UTF-8 interchange format or grapheme processing. Historical compatibility and modern Unicode requirements therefore need different contracts.

Investigation: Locate the amendment-era facility names through the standards guide and compare a locale-dependent wide-character conversion with a strict UTF-8 byte grammar.

Misconception to resolve: wchar_t is not universally a Unicode code point or a fixed-width interchange unit.

Observable evidence: A facility/context table and an explicit boundary between locale state and protocol bytes. Evidence is developed in [PR-T05-01](#pr-t05-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t05-04"></a>

### T05.04 — C99 language and library changes

C99 brought familiar mechanisms such as mixed declarations, designated initialization, compound literals, restrict and variadic macros. VLA and inline details need edition/implementation context; integer and formatting facilities also have header/library obligations. A migration suite should isolate each change.

Investigation: Port a tiny C90-style record initializer and formatter to C99, adding cases for lifetime, integer formatting and macro invocation.

Misconception to resolve: New syntax availability does not remove object-lifetime or call-type obligations.

Observable evidence: Separate compile/link/run evidence for each feature and regressions that preserve the old intended behavior. Evidence is developed in [PR-T05-02](#pr-t05-02).

<a id="t05-05"></a>

### T05.05 — C11 changes

C11 added atomics, thread facilities, alignment, generic selection and static assertions, while some facilities depend on implementation support. Parsing an atomic declaration, linking a helper and executing a thread are distinct capabilities. Concurrency semantics are developed in the systems route, not inferred from one accepted snippet.

Investigation: Probe alignment, _Generic and _Static_assert; inventory thread/atomic support and any runtime dependency without claiming a race proof.

Misconception to resolve: A compiler feature and a complete runtime library are separate layers.

Observable evidence: A capability matrix with language acceptance, headers, linking, runtime and declared limits. Evidence is developed in [PR-T05-02](#pr-t05-02).

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

- **T05.05.a** Study atomics, thread facilities, alignment, generic selection, and assertions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T05-02](#pr-t05-02).


<a id="t05-05-b"></a>

<a id="t05-05-c"></a>


- **T05.05.c** Distinguish language acceptance from linked-library availability. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T05-02](#pr-t05-02).


<a id="t05-06"></a>

### T05.06 — C17 and corrections

C17 follows the C11 line with corrections rather than a large new feature set. DR400 documents conflicting zero-size realloc practices and a C17-labeled resolution: the zero-size ownership outcome needs implementation documentation, while nonzero failure preserves the old allocation. The record also makes zero-size use obsolescent. Avoid this ambiguity in the component by defining empty-buffer release separately; C23 rules are a distinct edition question.

Investigation: Compare DR400’s original wording, final proposed corrigendum and C17 status, then revise a resize contract to require nonzero requests.

Misconception to resolve: Renaming C11 syntax as a C17 innovation obscures the reason for the corrective edition; a null zero-size result is not a portable nonzero-failure ownership rule.

Observable evidence: A precise correction analysis, ownership decision table and a limit on what the committee record establishes. Evidence is developed in [PR-T05-03](#pr-t05-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t05-06-b"></a>


- **T05.06.b** Compare C11 and C17 behavior using authoritative change records. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T05-03](#pr-t05-03).


<a id="t05-06-c"></a>


- **T05.06.c** Avoid inventing a large new feature set for a corrective edition. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T05-03](#pr-t05-03).


<a id="t05-07"></a>

### T05.07 — C23 declaration and expression facilities

C23 adds facilities including nullptr, typeof forms, object type inference, object constexpr and bit-precise integers. Similar names in C++ do not import C++ semantics. Some familiar spellings also change their authority: in C17, bool comes from <stdbool.h>, alignas from <stdalign.h> and static_assert from <assert.h>, as macros for _Bool, _Alignas and _Static_assert. C23 makes bool, alignas and static_assert language keywords and retains the underscored alternate spellings. Test their language/header boundaries separately. Bit-precise widths, enum changes and constant-expression rules need explicit probes and ABI constraints.

Investigation: Create isolated positive/negative probes for each selected facility, including old/new keyword spellings, a width boundary and a misuse of object constexpr as if it were a constexpr function.

Misconception to resolve: A successful nominal snippet is not whole-C23 conformance and a header-defined macro in C17 is not evidence of a C23 keyword.

Observable evidence: Per-facility source, configuration, header/spelling distinction, expected constraints and actual compile/link/run results. Evidence is developed in [PR-T05-04](#pr-t05-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t05-07-b"></a>

<a id="t05-08"></a>

### T05.08 — C23 preprocessing and library facilities

C23 preprocessing and library changes cross several layers: __VA_OPT__ changes token construction, #embed introduces input dependencies, attributes have support semantics, and checked/bit-operation headers require the chosen implementation. Expanded freestanding provisions do not mean every target ships a complete hosted libc.

Investigation: Probe empty variadics, an embedded byte file and checked/bit operations; list build inputs and distinguish header existence from successful calls.

Misconception to resolve: A C23 dialect flag does not certify #embed, every attribute or the entire runtime.

Observable evidence: A feature/dependency matrix and repeatable unsupported-feature responses. Evidence is developed in [PR-T05-04](#pr-t05-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t05-08-b"></a>


- **T05.08.b** Exercise checked arithmetic and bit-operation headers where implemented. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T05-04](#pr-t05-04).


<a id="t05-08-c"></a>

<a id="t05-09"></a>

### T05.09 — Feature detection and migration

Edition macros are useful gates but cannot substitute for documented capability tests on partial implementations. Keep portability boundaries narrow: a baseline mechanism, a separately selected enhancement and a regression suite shared by both. Strict and extension dialects expose different assumptions.

Investigation: Build baseline and feature configurations in GCC and Clang when available, recording unavailable compilers rather than fabricating results.

Misconception to resolve: A compiler version number alone does not identify the selected target’s headers or ABI.

Observable evidence: Versioned capability tests, fallback behavior and a migration comparison with explicit extension use. Evidence is developed in [PR-T05-04](#pr-t05-04).

<a id="t05-10"></a>

### T05.10 — Beyond-base-standard mechanisms

Technical reports, provenance specifications and cleanup proposals can illuminate future design, but their status is part of the claim. Extensions need a replacement strategy and versioned implementation evidence. The elective survey is bounded reading and experiment design, not an assertion that unadopted mechanisms are C23.

Investigation: Select one non-base mechanism, identify its exact authority/status, and describe a portable alternative before any extension experiment.

Misconception to resolve: A widely implemented extension is not automatically an adopted ISO facility.

Observable evidence: An authority/status record, isolated experiment or documented non-execution and a replacement plan. Evidence is developed in [PR-T05-05](#pr-t05-05).

This is an elective topic with a separate project gate.

## Mastery gate and feedback

Defend a feature claim by edition, document status and actual implementation layer. Port one legacy construct without a signature cast, and show baseline/feature configurations with honest unavailable entries. Core mastery excludes the elective implementation survey, which has its own evidence gate.

For independent study, make predictions before execution, compare an independent oracle, inspect one counterexample and defend the result aloud or in a short recorded review. Link each original objective to a specific artifact; use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) to score it. A failed gate requires a minimized cause, a corrected model and a fresh regression, not repeated nominal runs.

## Consolidation and transfer

Re-run the capability matrix after a toolchain upgrade. Revise only claims invalidated by evidence; keep published-edition identities and proposal statuses distinct.

## Environment and limits

Use the recorded hosted laboratory in [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and the per-project boundary in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). C17 is the baseline; edition/extension experiments are isolated and capability checked. Supplied fixture oracles validate mathematical or declared synthetic expectations. They do not execute the learner’s C, prove all language behavior or certify target hardware. Record actual commands, versions, observations and unresolved limits separately.

<a id="t06"></a>

# T06 — Preprocessing and metaprogramming

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| shared | core | 36 | A, C |

**Prerequisites:** [T02](#t02).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5 | 16 | 8 | 4 | 3 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Use preprocessing as token transformation with a verifiable evaluation contract. Debug expansion directly, keep registries authoritative, and choose between macros, typed functions and external generation based on diagnostics and maintenance rather than cleverness.

## Entry check and remediation

Read function declarations and sequencing from T02. If macro output is surprising, inspect -E output before editing types. Complete the T05 __VA_OPT__ support prelude before the optional C23 form; the portable baseline must have a deliberate empty-argument policy.

## Component progression

**A single registry, several generated views.** Follow tokens through preprocessing; compare expansion with evaluation. Generate declarations and dispatch from one small registry and test bad configuration values.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **A side-effect argument used twice by a superficially type-correct macro.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t06-01"></a>

### T06.01 — Translation phases

Translation phases explain why line splicing, comment replacement and tokenization affect later expansion. A backslash-newline can join physical lines before a comment is recognized; comment text is not a reliable macro separator after tokenization. Preprocessed output reveals tokens, while later semantic analysis still belongs to the compiler.

Investigation: Create line-splice/comment/literal examples and compare physical source, logical tokens and -E output.

Misconception to resolve: Macro expansion is not arbitrary string replacement over the original file bytes.

Observable evidence: A phase timeline and minimal sources that explain each surprising token result. Evidence is developed in [PR-T06-01](#pr-t06-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t06-01-a"></a>


- **T06.01.a** Trace source-character handling, line splicing, tokenization, and preprocessing. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T06-01](#pr-t06-01).


<a id="t06-01-b"></a>


- **T06.01.b** Analyze comments and literals at the correct translation stage. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T06-01](#pr-t06-01).


<a id="t06-01-c"></a>


- **T06.01.c** Inspect preprocessed output to explain unexpected compilation results. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T06-01](#pr-t06-01).


<a id="t06-02"></a>

### T06.02 — Macro expansion

Function-like macros expand when followed by the invocation parentheses; object-like macros replace tokens directly. Arguments generally undergo prescan, substitution and rescanning, with special handling around # and ## and recursion suppression. Track tokens at each stage rather than guessing the final spelling.

Investigation: Trace nested replacement lists and a macro name used without parentheses, then check the preprocessor output.

Misconception to resolve: A macro that expands to its own name does not recurse forever under normal suppression rules.

Observable evidence: A token-stage table and actual -E observations with no semantic inference from text alone. Evidence is developed in [PR-T06-01](#pr-t06-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t06-02-a"></a>


- **T06.02.a** Follow argument prescan, substitution, rescanning, and suppression rules. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T06-01](#pr-t06-01).


<a id="t06-02-b"></a>


- **T06.02.b** Distinguish object-like and function-like macro invocation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T06-01](#pr-t06-01).


<a id="t06-02-c"></a>


- **T06.02.c** Diagnose surprising expansion caused by nested replacement lists. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T06-01](#pr-t06-01).


<a id="t06-03"></a>

### T06.03 — Stringification and token construction

Stringification preserves an argument’s token spelling at that step; an extra macro layer is needed when prior expansion is intended. Token pasting must produce valid preprocessing tokens. Generating a plausible identifier does not guarantee that its eventual declaration or type is valid.

Investigation: Build two-level stringify/paste helpers and one intentionally invalid token combination as a negative preprocessing case.

Misconception to resolve: Pasting is not a way to create arbitrary punctuation or bypass type checking.

Observable evidence: Exact token/string results and a separated preprocessing-versus-semantic diagnostic ledger. Evidence is developed in [PR-T06-01](#pr-t06-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t06-03-a"></a>


- **T06.03.a** Apply stringification and token pasting with controlled expansion. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T06-01](#pr-t06-01).


<a id="t06-03-b"></a>


- **T06.03.b** Generate identifiers without accidentally creating invalid tokens. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T06-01](#pr-t06-01).


<a id="t06-03-c"></a>


- **T06.03.c** Separate textual assembly from semantic type checking. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T06-01](#pr-t06-01).


<a id="t06-04"></a>

### T06.04 — Variadic preprocessing

Variadic macros need a stated empty-argument policy. C23 __VA_OPT__ conditionally contributes tokens when variadic arguments are present; older comma-swallowing forms are implementation extensions. Evaluation obligations belong to the resulting C expression, so count each argument occurrence after expansion.

Investigation: Implement a trace wrapper with baseline and supported C23 forms, testing empty/nonempty arguments and side-effect counts.

Misconception to resolve: A convenient variadic spelling does not guarantee single evaluation.

Observable evidence: Expansion vectors, capability checks and observed evaluation counts for defined calls. Evidence is developed in [PR-T06-01](#pr-t06-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t06-04-a"></a>


- **T06.04.a** Handle empty and nonempty variadic argument cases deliberately. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T06-01](#pr-t06-01).


<a id="t06-04-b"></a>


- **T06.04.b** Compare C23 __VA_OPT__ with documented older extensions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T06-01](#pr-t06-01).


<a id="t06-04-c"></a>


- **T06.04.c** Design macros that preserve argument evaluation contracts. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T06-01](#pr-t06-01).


<a id="t06-05"></a>

### T06.05 — Macro safety

Parenthesizing operands and the result handles precedence, but cannot prevent duplicated effects. Statement macros commonly use do/while(0) to behave as one statement; internal names can still collide and reserved identifiers remain off limits. Prefer static inline when types and single evaluation fit.

Investigation: Repair a minimum macro and a dangling-else statement macro; compare a typed function alternative.

Misconception to resolve: A fully parenthesized macro can still evaluate an argument twice.

Observable evidence: A side-effect counter test, scope/collision review and a documented remaining contract. Evidence is developed in [PR-T06-01](#pr-t06-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t06-05-a"></a>


- **T06.05.a** Prevent unintended repeated evaluation and precedence changes. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T06-01](#pr-t06-01).


<a id="t06-05-b"></a>


- **T06.05.b** Analyze statement macros, dangling else, and scope interactions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T06-01](#pr-t06-01).


<a id="t06-05-c"></a>


- **T06.05.c** Avoid reserved names and collisions with caller identifiers. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T06-01](#pr-t06-01).


<a id="t06-06"></a>

### T06.06 — X-macros and registries

An X-macro registry stores one row per authoritative item and derives enums, names and tables by redefining the row macro. Completeness includes duplicate identifiers, missing mappings and value constraints. Generated artifacts should be checkable against the registry rather than manually synchronized.

Investigation: Generate command IDs, names and dispatch metadata from one list and test round-trip name/ID consistency.

Misconception to resolve: One source list reduces duplication but does not automatically validate its contents.

Observable evidence: Duplicate/unknown checks and a complete generated table comparison. Evidence is developed in [PR-T06-02](#pr-t06-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t06-06-a"></a>


- **T06.06.a** Generate enums, names, dispatch tables, and validation tables. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T06-02](#pr-t06-02).


<a id="t06-06-b"></a>


- **T06.06.b** Maintain one authoritative input representation for related artifacts. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T06-02](#pr-t06-02).


<a id="t06-06-c"></a>


- **T06.06.c** Check completeness and consistency with compilation tests. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T06-02](#pr-t06-02).


<a id="t06-07"></a>

### T06.07 — Type-directed interfaces

_Generic selects by compatible type without runtime dispatch, but association expressions still need valid syntax and constraints. Selecting function designators and calling the result often avoids invalid type-specific expressions in unselected branches. Array conversions and qualifiers need deliberate interface tests.

Investigation: Implement two typed operations with generic dispatch and compare a static-inline-only interface; add unselected-association negative tests.

Misconception to resolve: Generic selection is not a lazy parser for arbitrary invalid branches.

Observable evidence: Type-selection tests, diagnostics and generated-code evidence for the selected call. Evidence is developed in [PR-T06-02](#pr-t06-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t06-07-a"></a>


- **T06.07.a** Implement _Generic dispatch with documented compatible-type rules. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T06-02](#pr-t06-02).


<a id="t06-07-b"></a>


- **T06.07.b** Compare generic selection with static inline specialization. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T06-02](#pr-t06-02).


<a id="t06-07-c"></a>

<a id="t06-08"></a>

### T06.08 — Configuration architecture

Build configuration determines compilation choices; public contracts describe supported behavior. Validate incompatible features early and include configuration identity in artifacts. A generated config header needs input provenance and stable ordering so rebuilds can be explained.

Investigation: Create a small feature matrix with required and forbidden combinations and a reproducible config manifest.

Misconception to resolve: An undocumented -D option can change ABI or semantics even if every source still compiles.

Observable evidence: Positive/negative configuration builds and artifact identities linked to inputs. Evidence is developed in [PR-T06-03](#pr-t06-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t06-08-a"></a>


- **T06.08.a** Separate build configuration from public API contracts. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T06-03](#pr-t06-03).


<a id="t06-08-b"></a>


- **T06.08.b** Validate incompatible feature combinations at compilation time. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T06-03](#pr-t06-03).


<a id="t06-08-c"></a>


- **T06.08.c** Preserve generated configuration provenance and reproducibility. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T06-03](#pr-t06-03).


<a id="t06-09"></a>

### T06.09 — External code generation

External generation suits structured schemas whose validation exceeds preprocessing. The generator’s contract includes accepted schema, deterministic output and failure behavior. Compare debugging, dependency tracking and review cost with macros; neither method is inherently more maintainable.

Investigation: Generate a protocol/register description from a validated JSON schema and compare generated constants with the schema oracle.

Misconception to resolve: Generated code is not correct merely because the generator ran successfully.

Observable evidence: Schema rejection tests, deterministic regeneration and artifact-to-input traceability. Evidence is developed in [PR-T06-03](#pr-t06-03).

# T07 — Compilation and build engineering

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| shared | core | 66 | A, C |

**Prerequisites:** [T02](#t02), [T03](#t03).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |

| 8 | 36 | 14 | 4 | 4 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Make the build an inspectable dependency computation. Leave with reproducible commands, deliberate target/runtime selection, portable exported library boundaries and failure evidence that another repository can reproduce. The intended result is a mechanism you can explain, a bounded artifact you can inspect and an evidence trail someone else can reproduce.

## Entry check and remediation

Given two source files and one generated header, predict which stage fails for an undeclared identifier, an unresolved reference and a stale object. If those are conflated, revisit T02 translation and compile a single-file example before the first graph project. Use [guide-entry](#guide-entry) for diagnostic evidence and [guide-roadmap](#guide-roadmap) for route choices. Domain numbers are coverage IDs, not an instruction to study them numerically.

## Component progression

**A build graph with observable edges.** Touch a header, generated configuration and source separately; predict which artifacts must change. Reproduce one component with Make and CMake before trusting cached outputs.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **A clean build that passes while an incremental build reuses an incompatible object.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching

Work through the mechanism notes in order within each project, alternating hand prediction with observation. Preserve the first counterexample rather than only a final green test. Full implementations belong to the projects; these notes explain what they must establish.


<a id="t07-01"></a>

### T07.01 — Build pipeline

A translation pipeline transforms a token stream into machine instructions and then resolves references between objects. The driver orchestrates those stages; an object file is not an executable merely because it contains code.

Investigate: Stop a two-file example at .i, .s and .o, then reconstruct the final link command. A common mistake is: Compilation success implies link success. Evidence: A diagram names the producer and consumer of each artifact, and the reconstructed binary agrees with the driver build. Develop that evidence in [PR-T07-01](#pr-t07-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t07-01-b"></a>

### T07.02 — Compiler driver and target selection

A target triple selects a toolchain family; CPU tuning, enabled instructions and calling convention are additional choices. The machine running the compiler need not be the machine running its output.

Investigate: Inventory driver include paths, sysroot, startup objects and target libraries; classify every discovered tool as host or target. A common mistake is: Changing -march alone creates a correct cross-toolchain. Evidence: A manifest explains each implicit input and rejects an incompatible object before execution. Develop that evidence in [PR-T07-01](#pr-t07-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t07-02-a"></a>

<a id="t07-02-b"></a>

### T07.03 — Diagnostics policy

Diagnostics are part of the build contract: a warning depends on language edition, compiler version and what the compiler can establish. Suppression moves an obligation to review rather than repairing behavior.

Investigate: Create one positive, one expected-warning and one expected-failure translation unit; justify one narrow suppression. A common mistake is: Warning-free means defined behavior. Evidence: Versioned logs distinguish the expected diagnostic class from brittle exact wording. Develop that evidence in [PR-T07-01](#pr-t07-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t07-03-b"></a>

<a id="t07-03-c"></a>


- **T07.03.c** Scope suppressions narrowly and document their justification. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T07-01](#pr-t07-01).


<a id="t07-04"></a>

### T07.04 — Optimization and debug profiles

Debug information, optimization and instrumentation are independent settings. Inlining changes frames; instrumentation adds runtime support; size optimization need not minimize every function.

Investigate: Build debug, sanitizer, release and size configurations of the same defined program and compare symbols and disassembly. A common mistake is: A debug dependency audit also covers release or LTO. Evidence: A table separates stable semantic output from configuration-dependent code and runtime dependencies. Develop that evidence in [PR-T07-02](#pr-t07-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t07-04-a"></a>


- **T07.04.a** Compare optimization levels through behavior and generated code. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T07-02](#pr-t07-02).


<a id="t07-04-b"></a>


- **T07.04.b** Configure separate debug, sanitizer, release, and size-oriented builds. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T07-02](#pr-t07-02).


<a id="t07-04-c"></a>


- **T07.04.c** Avoid assuming debug and release profiles have identical dependencies. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T07-02](#pr-t07-02).


<a id="t07-05"></a>

### T07.05 — Make fundamentals

A Make rule is a dependency assertion. File prerequisites trigger rebuilding; order-only edges establish sequencing without making their timestamps a reason to rebuild. Phony names represent actions.

Investigate: Break a generated-header edge deliberately, then repair it with compiler-generated dependency files. A common mistake is: Listing a directory as an ordinary prerequisite expresses only creation order. Evidence: Touch and delete inputs in a controlled matrix and predict every rebuild before observing it. Develop that evidence in [PR-T07-02](#pr-t07-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t07-05-a"></a>


- **T07.05.a** Model explicit targets, prerequisites, recipes, and generated dependencies. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T07-02](#pr-t07-02).


<a id="t07-05-b"></a>


- **T07.05.b** Distinguish ordinary files, phony targets, and order-only prerequisites. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T07-02](#pr-t07-02).


<a id="t07-05-c"></a>


- **T07.05.c** Diagnose stale, missing, and unnecessarily rebuilt outputs. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T07-02](#pr-t07-02).


<a id="t07-06"></a>

### T07.06 — CMake target model

A target has requirements for its own compilation and requirements for consumers. PUBLIC participates in both; PRIVATE affects the implementation; INTERFACE describes consumers. Exported paths must survive relocation.

Worked dependency transfer: a producer exports Tiny::tiny with install-relative include/tiny and its public compile definition. A consumer links that imported target in a different source root. If hiding the producer breaks configuration, inspect the exported paths before adding a consumer include flag: that flag can conceal a defective package.

Investigate: Package a two-library component, install it to a temporary prefix and consume it from a separate tree. A common mistake is: Global include directories are a substitute for interface requirements. Evidence: The consumer builds after moving the install prefix, without references to the original build directory. Develop that evidence in [PR-T07-03](#pr-t07-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t07-06-a"></a>


- **T07.06.a** Distinguish sources, usage requirements, and transitive link requirements. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T07-03](#pr-t07-03).


<a id="t07-06-b"></a>


- **T07.06.b** Apply PRIVATE, PUBLIC, and INTERFACE at correct boundaries. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T07-03](#pr-t07-03).


<a id="t07-06-c"></a>


- **T07.06.c** Export and consume a library without leaking build-tree assumptions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T07-03](#pr-t07-03).


<a id="t07-07"></a>

### T07.07 — Generated inputs and configuration

Generated inputs belong in the graph just like handwritten inputs. Configuration probes can compile target code without running it; cross-build checks must not accidentally execute target binaries on the host.

Investigate: Generate a header from a small schema and provide explicit configuration answers for a non-runnable target. A common mistake is: A file produced once during configuration cannot become stale. Evidence: Clean and incremental builds record generation order and do not invoke the target during host configuration. Develop that evidence in [PR-T07-02](#pr-t07-02).

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

### T07.08 — Ninja and compilation databases

Ninja consumes an explicit graph and tracks compiler-discovered header edges. A compilation database records translation commands, not necessarily the full link or generation workflow.

Investigate: Replay one database command outside the front end, then inspect why a header change rebuilds only its dependents. A common mistake is: compile_commands.json is a complete reproduction recipe. Evidence: The replay uses the same directory, defines and include paths, and its object provenance is recorded. Develop that evidence in [PR-T07-03](#pr-t07-03).

### T07.09 — Cross-toolchain configuration

A cross build has two search universes: utilities that run now and headers/libraries for the target. A sysroot does not by itself choose the correct multilib or floating-point convention.

Investigate: Write a toolchain manifest and classify compiler, generator, target archives and linker script separately. A common mistake is: Successful linking proves that all ABI choices agree. Evidence: Compile/link probes plus object attributes expose a deliberately mismatched library. Develop that evidence in [PR-T07-04](#pr-t07-04).

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

### T07.11 — Testing and CI integration

Tests exercise configurations as well as functions. A negative-build test passes only when a prohibited construct fails for the intended reason; a target test needs an execution environment.

Investigate: Register semantic, expected-failure and target-only tests with explicit skip reasons. A common mistake is: A skipped on-target test is a successful hardware result. Evidence: CI artifacts retain the compiler identity, command, failure log and binary for a deliberately broken case. Develop that evidence in [PR-T07-05](#pr-t07-05).

### T07.12 — Reproducible artifacts

Reproduction requires control over embedded paths, timestamps, ordering and generated IDs. A hash mismatch is a starting point for locating differences, not automatic evidence of semantic divergence.

Investigate: Build in two clean directories and classify every byte difference before introducing path/timestamp controls. A common mistake is: The same source revision necessarily produces the same binary. Evidence: A provenance record and a byte-difference report explain both eliminated and retained variability. Develop that evidence in [PR-T07-06](#pr-t07-06).

## Reading guidance

The essential spine below is deliberately narrow. Assign only the exact inspected registry locators shown; no whole book, standard or implementation is implied. Historical rationale does not replace a current contract, and one implementation does not create a portable guarantee. Keep a short discrepancy log linking each source claim to the target/configuration where it applies.

- **Using the GNU Compiler Collection (GCC 15.2.0)** — `R-SYS-GCC-15-2`, exactly **§3.2 Options Controlling the Kind of Output, opening stage description** (1 h). Recover the four driver stages and locate the artifact each produces. Compare the source claim with your project assumptions. The registry classifies this as oracle; its inspection limits remain part of the assignment.

- **GNU make manual (GNU make 4.4.1)** — `R-SYS-MAKE-4-4-1`, exactly **doc/make.texi — Generating Prerequisites Automatically** (1 h). Explain generated-header prerequisite edges and stale-build failures. Compare the source claim with your project assumptions. The registry classifies this as primary; its inspection limits remain part of the assignment.

- **cmake-buildsystem(7) (CMake 3.31.12 documentation)** — `R-SYS-CMAKE-3-31-12`, exactly **Target Usage Requirements** (1 h). Distinguish target-local usage requirements from accidental global settings. Compare the source claim with your project assumptions. The registry classifies this as primary; its inspection limits remain part of the assignment.

- **The Ninja build system (v1.13.1, July 2025)** — `R-SYS-NINJA-1-13-1`, exactly **C/C++ header dependencies — depfile and deps** (1 h). Read depfile discovery and compare generated graph edges. Compare the source claim with your project assumptions. The registry classifies this as supplement; its inspection limits remain part of the assignment.

- **cmake-toolchains(7) (CMake 3.31.12 documentation)** — `R-SYS-CMAKE-TOOLCHAINS-3-31-12`, exactly **Cross Compiling for Linux** (1 h). Separate host tools from target includes/libraries and identify the sysroot boundary. Compare the source claim with your project assumptions. The registry classifies this as oracle; its inspection limits remain part of the assignment.

- **cmake-presets(7) (CMake 3.31.12 documentation)** — `R-SYS-CMAKE-PRESETS-3-31-12`, exactly **Configure Preset — name, hidden, inherits, toolchainFile, binaryDir, installDir, cacheVariables, environment** (1 h). Predict preset inheritance and toolchain/build/install path resolution. Compare the source claim with your project assumptions. The registry classifies this as oracle; its inspection limits remain part of the assignment.

- **cmake-packages(7) (CMake 3.31.12 documentation)** — `R-SYS-CMAKE-PACKAGES-3-31-12`, exactly **Creating Relocatable Packages** (2 h). Explain why install-relative imported target properties survive second-repository relocation. Compare the source claim with your project assumptions. The registry classifies this as oracle; its inspection limits remain part of the assignment.

See [guide-reading](#guide-reading) and [guide-standards](#guide-standards) for edition and evidence distinctions. Additional elective/API investigations require inspecting their precise version-specific passages before treating them as assigned authority.

## Mastery gate and feedback

Explain one positive path and one failure/counterexample for every subtopic without reading your implementation. Submit each project’s leaf-objective checklist with a distinct evidence item; shared runs may support several items only when the relation is explained. Re-run the saved independent fixture verifier, then reproduce at least one artifact from a clean environment. Passing those checks is evidence within their scope, not full-domain certification.

If an invariant, lifetime or environment claim cannot be defended, return to its project’s smallest trace and remediate the named entry knowledge. If a tool result disagrees with reasoning, minimize before changing expected results. A module passes when all core projects and awareness duties are accepted; elective implementation gaps remain visible. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) and [guide-audit](#guide-audit) for review records.

## Consolidation and transfer

After at least one day, reconstruct a selected contract and failing trace from memory, then apply one changed capacity/backend/target assumption. Explain which evidence survives and which must be regenerated. Transfer the dependency, ownership, representation or ordering ledger into the next project rather than copying an unexplained implementation. Record the delayed correction in the consolidation budget; see [guide-integrations](#guide-integrations) and [guide-workload](#guide-workload).

## Environment and limits

Use the declared Linux x86-64 environment for hosted observations and profile-specific adapters for portable components. Record compiler, linker, OS/library, architecture and configuration. Synthetic fixtures certify their declared static/reference calculations only. Unavailable target runs, unsupported instrumentation and hardware-dependent results are reported explicitly; emulator results do not prove STM32 electrical/peripheral behavior. No privileged host operation is required by a core project. See [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory), [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles) and [guide-inventory](#guide-inventory) before changing a boundary.

# T08 — Machine architecture, assembly, and ABIs

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cross-track | core | 49 | A, C |

**Prerequisites:** [T07](#t07), [T03](#t03), [T04](#t04).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3 | 27 | 11 | 4 | 4 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Connect C semantics to one declared machine/ABI without importing platform observations into portable C. Read instructions and encoded bytes, uphold call boundaries and test assembly against an adversarial harness. The intended result is a mechanism you can explain, a bounded artifact you can inspect and an evidence trail someone else can reproduce.

## Entry check and remediation

Explain a pointer/length array loop and signed versus unsigned comparison in C, then identify load/store/call instructions in one short disassembly. Remediate pointer arithmetic in T03, integer semantics in T04 and driver staging in T07 before writing assembly. Use [guide-entry](#guide-entry) for diagnostic evidence and [guide-roadmap](#guide-roadmap) for route choices. Domain numbers are coverage IDs, not an instruction to study them numerically.

## Component progression

**A hostile caller around an assembly kernel.** Name argument/result locations, preserved registers, stack alignment and permitted accesses. Test adversarial surrounding register values and inspect actual instruction bytes.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **A routine returning the right answer while corrupting a callee-saved register.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching

Work through the mechanism notes in order within each project, alternating hand prediction with observation. Preserve the first counterexample rather than only a final green test. Full implementations belong to the projects; these notes explain what they must establish.


<a id="t08-01"></a>

### T08.01 — Instruction-set fundamentals

Disassembly exposes an instruction-set computation: loads and stores use effective addresses, branches test a selected condition, and calls transfer control according to a convention. Cache latency is a different layer.

Investigate: Trace an indexed structure access instruction by instruction and calculate its effective addresses. A common mistake is: One measured cycle count is an ISA guarantee. Evidence: A register/memory trace predicts the result and states which timing claims remain microarchitecture-specific. Develop that evidence in [PR-T08-01](#pr-t08-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

- **T08.01.a** Read arithmetic, branches, calls, loads, and stores in disassembly. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T08-01](#pr-t08-01).


<a id="t08-01-b"></a>


- **T08.01.b** Relate addressing modes to C array and structure accesses. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T08-01](#pr-t08-01).


<a id="t08-01-c"></a>


- **T08.01.c** Distinguish instruction-set guarantees from microarchitectural behavior. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T08-01](#pr-t08-01).


<a id="t08-02"></a>

### T08.02 — Registers and flags

Caller-saved registers may be destroyed by a call; callee-saved registers must be restored. Arithmetic flags describe a particular instruction result, including signed versus unsigned comparisons.

Investigate: Track a signed and unsigned branch over the same bit pattern, and poison preserved registers before a call. A common mistake is: A register that happened to survive one call is preserved by contract. Evidence: A mechanical harness detects a missing restore and an annotated trace distinguishes the comparison conditions. Develop that evidence in [PR-T08-01](#pr-t08-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t08-02-a"></a>


- **T08.02.a** Track general, stack, status, and floating-point registers. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T08-01](#pr-t08-01).


<a id="t08-02-b"></a>

<a id="t08-03"></a>

### T08.03 — Call boundaries

An ABI classifies arguments before assigning registers or stack storage. A large return value can introduce a hidden storage pointer; that shifts apparent parameter positions.

Investigate: Compare scalar, small-aggregate and large-aggregate call sites on the declared x86-64 target. A common mistake is: C source parameter order completely describes the machine call. Evidence: Call-site and callee annotations agree on registers, spill slots, result storage and alignment. Develop that evidence in [PR-T08-02](#pr-t08-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t08-03-c"></a>

<a id="t08-04"></a>

### T08.04 — Stack frames

A frame contains more than source locals: saved state, spilled temporaries, padding and sometimes outgoing arguments. Optimization can remove the frame pointer or replace a tail call with a jump.

Investigate: Compare recursive and iterative routines under two optimizations and account for every observed stack adjustment. A common mistake is: Source-level local sizes equal total frame size. Evidence: A stack diagram distinguishes observed frames from a conservative bound and names any red-zone assumption. Develop that evidence in [PR-T08-02](#pr-t08-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t08-05"></a>

### T08.05 — Data layout and ABI compatibility

LP64 and ILP32 differ in integer and pointer widths; padding separates member offsets from payload sizes. Binary compatibility is a promise about layout and calling conventions, not only matching declarations.

Investigate: Generate a layout manifest and compare a packed or differently configured object against it. A common mistake is: Equal sizeof values prove compatible layout. Evidence: Offsets, alignment, widths and symbol-level interface checks identify the intentionally incompatible pair. Develop that evidence in [PR-T08-02](#pr-t08-02).

<a id="t08-06"></a>

### T08.06 — Floating-point ABI

Floating-point instructions and floating-point parameter passing are separate decisions. On Arm, soft, softfp and hard-float choices can differ even when arithmetic instructions are available.

Investigate: Inspect target attributes for one compatible and one incompatible floating-point library pairing; diagram who preserves FP registers. A common mistake is: A hardware FPU makes every library ABI compatible. Evidence: The audit rejects mismatched call conventions and keeps x86-64 observations separate from Arm examples. Develop that evidence in [PR-T08-03](#pr-t08-03).

### T08.07 — Standalone assembly

Standalone assembly owns the full call boundary: exported symbol, section placement, preserved registers and stack alignment. Unwind annotations describe recovery state; they do not execute the restore.

Investigate: Write a short callable integer routine and an intentionally broken preserved-register variant. A common mistake is: Returning the correct value is enough to satisfy the ABI. Evidence: Repeated calls with register sentinels and a debugger/unwind inspection expose the broken variant. Develop that evidence in [PR-T08-03](#pr-t08-03).

<a id="t08-08"></a>

### T08.08 — Inline assembly

Inline assembly describes both an instruction and a contract with the optimizer. Tied operands share storage; early-clobber prevents overlap with inputs; a memory clobber constrains compiler motion rather than ordering a CPU.

Investigate: Compare a correct operand specification with one missing a clobber at multiple optimization levels. A common mistake is: volatile asm or a memory clobber automatically acts as a hardware fence. Evidence: A constraints explanation and generated-code comparison identify the compiler and hardware obligations separately. Develop that evidence in [PR-T08-04](#pr-t08-04).

### T08.09 — Exceptions and privileged execution

A trap crosses an architectural exception boundary, with privilege and saved-state rules unlike a normal call. Kernel entry does not follow the portable C abstract machine.

Investigate: Classify ordinary calls, syscalls, interrupts and privileged instructions in a table; inspect a documented trap boundary. A common mistake is: Every instruction visible in disassembly is legal in userspace. Evidence: The table states privilege, return mechanism and saved-state owner without attempting privileged operations on the host. Develop that evidence in [PR-T08-04](#pr-t08-04).

<a id="t08-10"></a>

### T08.10 — Compiler-to-machine reasoning

The compiler may transform a defined computation while preserving observable behavior. Source, intermediate representation and final instructions answer different questions; undefined behavior removes the premise of the comparison.

Worked encoding anchor: in the declared 64-bit mode with no prefixes and default 32-bit operand size, B8 78 56 34 12 selects the MOV-immediate form for EAX. Its immediate is 0x12345678 because the least significant byte comes first; the encoding is five bytes. This one form is not a general x86 decoder, and changing operand size or prefixes changes the investigation.

Investigate: Compare a defined strength-reduction example with a separately diagnosed overflow-invalid variant. A common mistake is: An unexpected instruction sequence proves an optimizer bug. Evidence: A minimized case first states its language preconditions, then explains one eliminated branch, inline call or spill. Develop that evidence in [PR-T08-01](#pr-t08-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t08-10-b"></a>

## Reading guidance

The essential spine below is deliberately narrow. Assign only the exact inspected registry locators shown; no whole book, standard or implementation is implied. Historical rationale does not replace a current contract, and one implementation does not create a portable guarantee. Keep a short discrepancy log linking each source claim to the target/configuration where it applies.

- **System V Application Binary Interface: AMD64 Architecture Processor Supplement (Draft 0.99.6, 2 July 2012)** — `R-SYS-AMD64-ABI-0-99-6`, exactly **§3.2.3 Parameter Passing, opening classification rules, pp. 17–19** (2 h). Trace integer/aggregate parameter classification and the caller/callee boundary. Compare the source claim with your project assumptions. The registry classifies this as supplement; its inspection limits remain part of the assignment.

- **LLVM X86 MOV-immediate instruction definitions (llvmorg-21.1.0)** — `R-SYS-LLVM-X86-MOV-21-1`, exactly **llvm/lib/Target/X86/X86InstrMisc.td — MOV16ri, MOV32ri and MOV64ri32 declarations** (1 h). Correlate opcode 0xB8, register/immediate operands and declared operand width with the five-byte MOV anchor. Compare the source claim with your project assumptions. The registry classifies this as source; its inspection limits remain part of the assignment.

See [guide-reading](#guide-reading) and [guide-standards](#guide-standards) for edition and evidence distinctions. Additional elective/API investigations require inspecting their precise version-specific passages before treating them as assigned authority.

## Implementation projects

Project hours combine implementation with the verification described in each contract. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation are budgeted separately; do not add project hours again to the module total.

- [PR-T08-02: ABI boundary and frame laboratory](#pr-t08-02) — 10 h; core.
