## Mastery gate and feedback

Explain one positive path and one failure/counterexample for every subtopic without reading your implementation. Submit each project’s leaf-objective checklist with a distinct evidence item; shared runs may support several items only when the relation is explained. Re-run the saved independent fixture verifier, then reproduce at least one artifact from a clean environment. Passing those checks is evidence within their scope, not full-domain certification.

If an invariant, lifetime or environment claim cannot be defended, return to its project’s smallest trace and remediate the named entry knowledge. If a tool result disagrees with reasoning, minimize before changing expected results. A module passes when all core projects and awareness duties are accepted; elective implementation gaps remain visible. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) and [guide-audit](#guide-audit) for review records.

## Consolidation and transfer

After at least one day, reconstruct a selected contract and failing trace from memory, then apply one changed capacity/backend/target assumption. Explain which evidence survives and which must be regenerated. Transfer the dependency, ownership, representation or ordering ledger into the next project rather than copying an unexplained implementation. Record the delayed correction in the consolidation budget; see [guide-integrations](#guide-integrations) and [guide-workload](#guide-workload).

<!-- enhancement handoff -->

Transfer the same object/disassembly/ABI dossier to [T36](#t36) handwritten kernels and [T37](#t37) instruction decoding. Identify the chosen machine ABI before comparing compiler output with original assembly.

## Environment and limits

Use the declared Linux x86-64 environment for hosted observations and profile-specific adapters for portable components. Record compiler, linker, OS/library, architecture and configuration. Synthetic fixtures certify their declared static/reference calculations only. Unavailable target runs, unsupported instrumentation and hardware-dependent results are reported explicitly; emulator results do not prove STM32 electrical/peripheral behavior. No privileged host operation is required by a core project. See [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory), [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles) and [guide-inventory](#guide-inventory) before changing a boundary.

# T09 — Linkers, ELF, and binary inspection

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cross-track | core | 61 | A, C |

**Prerequisites:** [T07](#t07), [T08](#t08).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 7 | 32 | 14 | 4 | 4 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Read a binary as a set of linking/loading promises. Trace symbols, relocations, dynamic/TLS metadata and layout into a declared dependency and memory budget before converting or deploying an image. The intended result is a mechanism you can explain, a bounded artifact you can inspect and an evidence trail someone else can reproduce.

## Entry check and remediation

Distinguish an object from an executable and identify a symbol reference in disassembly. If code addresses and file offsets are confused, redo the T08 address trace and the T07 explicit link. Use [guide-entry](#guide-entry) for diagnostic evidence and [guide-roadmap](#guide-roadmap) for route choices. Domain numbers are coverage IDs, not an instruction to study them numerically.

## Component progression

**A symbol through compilation, linking and loading.** Trace a reference through relocation, archive selection and final placement. Separate source visibility, symbol binding, section reachability and runtime mapping.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **An archive order change or garbage-collected section that alters the executable despite unchanged C.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching

Work through the mechanism notes in order within each project, alternating hand prediction with observation. Preserve the first counterexample rather than only a final green test. Full implementations belong to the projects; these notes explain what they must establish.


<a id="t09-01"></a>

### T09.01 — ELF structure

ELF sections organize link-time information; program headers organize loading. A zero-fill segment can require RAM without storing those zero bytes in the file.

Investigate: Decode a synthetic header table and then compare a relocatable object, executable and shared object. A common mistake is: The section table alone specifies the runtime mappings. Evidence: The report separately totals file bytes, load-image bytes and memory bytes. Develop that evidence in [PR-T09-01](#pr-t09-01).

Binding determines which definitions can satisfy references. Local names stay within an object; weak definitions have lower precedence; undefined references need resolution. Common symbols depend on compiler conventions.

Investigate: Link two objects and an archive with controlled duplicate and weak symbols. A common mistake is: Identical C names always denote one link-time entity. Evidence: A symbol-resolution ledger explains every chosen definition and every diagnosed conflict. Develop that evidence in [PR-T09-01](#pr-t09-01).

An archive is searched for members needed by unresolved references at the relevant point in the link. Its existence on the command line does not force every member into the result.

<a id="t09-04"></a>

### T09.04 — Relocations

Relocation records identify unfinished address computations. For a simplified PC-relative field, the linker applies S+A−P; the result must fit the relocation width.

Worked relocation: for S=4096, A=-4 and P=4112, S+A-P=-20. That fits signed eight bits (-128 through 127) and is represented by low byte 0xEC. With S=4352 the displacement is 236: low byte 0xEC still appears, but the relocation must reject it because 236 exceeds the signed range. Byte matching alone would accept the wrong result.

Investigate: Calculate a positive, negative and overflowing relocation, then locate one real relocation and its final bytes. A common mistake is: A relocation contains only an absolute address. Evidence: Hand arithmetic, width checks and the binary report agree; overflow is rejected rather than truncated silently. Develop that evidence in [PR-T09-02](#pr-t09-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

The interpreter loads dependencies and resolves symbols using an implementation-defined policy documented for the chosen loader. GOT/PLT mechanisms can defer some bindings, but not every environment uses lazy binding.

TLS and initializer arrays are metadata that require runtime code. Merely placing a pointer in an init section does not call it; each thread requires an appropriate TLS instance.

A linker script maps input sections into output addresses and can distinguish load address from execution address. A RAM-resident initialized object may have bytes stored in a flash load image.

### T09.09 — Retention and garbage collection

Garbage collection follows linker reachability, which can miss tables consumed indirectly. KEEP preserves selected sections but archive extraction remains a separate decision.

Investigate: Create a registration table and observe its disappearance, then justify the smallest retention rule. A common mistake is: KEEP automatically pulls every archive member into the image. Evidence: The map shows the expected retained table and excludes a deliberately unused function. Develop that evidence in [PR-T09-04](#pr-t09-04).

<a id="t09-10"></a>

### T09.10 — Memory and image budgets

Image budgets count different resources: text/constant bytes, stored initial data, RAM data and zero-fill. Alignment holes and metadata may dominate a tiny example.

Investigate: Calculate budgets from a declared map and add linker assertions for one region limit. A common mistake is: Small file size proves low runtime RAM use. Evidence: A failing over-budget case is caught at link time and each byte category is attributed. Develop that evidence in [PR-T09-04](#pr-t09-04).

<a id="t09-11"></a>

### T09.11 — ABI evolution

Source compatibility allows recompilation; binary compatibility must preserve the machine-visible interface. Visibility and symbol versioning constrain what clients can depend on.

Investigate: Change a public structure or function contract in a toy library and classify old-client outcomes. A common mistake is: An unchanged function name guarantees old binaries work. Evidence: A compatibility matrix distinguishes source rebuild success, binary linkage and semantic agreement. Develop that evidence in [PR-T09-03](#pr-t09-03).

<a id="t09-12"></a>

### T09.12 — Binary transformations

Converting ELF to a raw image discards structure and often debug information. Address correlation, build IDs and checksum placement must be preserved in separate artifacts or declared transforms.

Investigate: Inspect a synthetic sparse image and define raw/HEX outputs plus a retained debug companion. A common mistake is: Stripping is a harmless final cleanup with no traceability effect. Evidence: An address-to-source and checksum ledger explains every post-link transformation. Develop that evidence in [PR-T09-05](#pr-t09-05).

## Reading guidance

The essential spine below is deliberately narrow. Assign only the exact inspected registry locators shown; no whole book, standard or implementation is implied. Historical rationale does not replace a current contract, and one implementation does not create a portable guarantee. Keep a short discrepancy log linking each source claim to the target/configuration where it applies.

- **Computer Systems: A Programmer’s Perspective (Third Edition, GLOBAL EDITION)** — `R-SYS-CSAPP-GLOBAL-3E`, exactly **§7.7 Relocation, pp. 725–730** (2 h). Compute symbolic relocation values before field-width validation. Compare the source claim with your project assumptions. The registry classifies this as primary; its inspection limits remain part of the assignment.

- **Using LD, the GNU linker (GNU binutils 2.45)** — `R-SYS-LD-2-45`, exactly **§3.6 SECTIONS Command** (1 h). Explain how input sections become output sections in a declared layout. Compare the source claim with your project assumptions. The registry classifies this as oracle; its inspection limits remain part of the assignment.

- **System V Application Binary Interface, Generic ABI (Draft, 24 April 2001)** — `R-SYS-GABI-2001`, exactly **Chapter 5 — Program Header, entry fields and Segment Types** (1 h). Separate stored file extent from the runtime PT_LOAD memory extent. Compare the source claim with your project assumptions. The registry classifies this as supplement; its inspection limits remain part of the assignment.

- **dlopen(3) (Linux man-pages 6.19; captured 2026-10-04)** — `R-SYS-LINUX-DLOPEN-6-19`, exactly **dlopen(3) — DESCRIPTION: dlopen() and dlclose()** (1 h). State loader policy, binding timing and handle reference-count ownership. Compare the source claim with your project assumptions. The registry classifies this as oracle; its inspection limits remain part of the assignment.

- **Using LD — VERSION Command (GNU binutils 2.45)** — `R-SYS-LD-VERSION-2-45`, exactly **§3.9 VERSION Command — version nodes, symbol visibility, requirements and default .symver binding** (1 h). Distinguish hidden exports, named symbol versions and the one default symbol binding. Compare the source claim with your project assumptions. The registry classifies this as oracle; its inspection limits remain part of the assignment.

- **Using GCC — Thread-Local Storage (GCC 15.2.0)** — `R-SYS-GCC-TLS-15-2`, exactly **§6.6 Thread-Local Storage — mechanism, __thread declarations and address lifetime** (1 h). Explain per-thread instances, runtime cooperation and address lifetime for the GNU TLS extension. Compare the source claim with your project assumptions. The registry classifies this as oracle; its inspection limits remain part of the assignment.

See [guide-reading](#guide-reading) and [guide-standards](#guide-standards) for edition and evidence distinctions. Additional elective/API investigations require inspecting their precise version-specific passages before treating them as assigned authority.

## Implementation projects

Project hours combine implementation with the verification described in each contract. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation are budgeted separately; do not add project hours again to the module total.

- [PR-T09-01: ELF symbols and archive resolution](#pr-t09-01) — 10 h; core.

- [PR-T09-02: Relocation and position independence](#pr-t09-02) — 8 h; core.

- [PR-T09-03: Loader, TLS and versioned exports](#pr-t09-03) — 12 h; core.

- [PR-T09-04: Linker layout, retention and budgets](#pr-t09-04) — 10 h; core.

- [PR-T09-05: Raw image with a debug companion](#pr-t09-05) — 6 h; core.

## Mastery gate and feedback

Explain one positive path and one failure/counterexample for every subtopic without reading your implementation. Submit each project’s leaf-objective checklist with a distinct evidence item; shared runs may support several items only when the relation is explained. Re-run the saved independent fixture verifier, then reproduce at least one artifact from a clean environment. Passing those checks is evidence within their scope, not full-domain certification.

If an invariant, lifetime or environment claim cannot be defended, return to its project’s smallest trace and remediate the named entry knowledge. If a tool result disagrees with reasoning, minimize before changing expected results. A module passes when all core projects and awareness duties are accepted; elective implementation gaps remain visible. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) and [guide-audit](#guide-audit) for review records.

## Consolidation and transfer

After at least one day, reconstruct a selected contract and failing trace from memory, then apply one changed capacity/backend/target assumption. Explain which evidence survives and which must be regenerated. Transfer the dependency, ownership, representation or ordering ledger into the next project rather than copying an unexplained implementation. Record the delayed correction in the consolidation budget; see [guide-integrations](#guide-integrations) and [guide-workload](#guide-workload).

## Environment and limits

Use the declared Linux x86-64 environment for hosted observations and profile-specific adapters for portable components. Record compiler, linker, OS/library, architecture and configuration. Synthetic fixtures certify their declared static/reference calculations only. Unavailable target runs, unsupported instrumentation and hardware-dependent results are reported explicitly; emulator results do not prove STM32 electrical/peripheral behavior. No privileged host operation is required by a core project. See [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory), [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles) and [guide-inventory](#guide-inventory) before changing a boundary.

<a id="t12"></a>

# T12 — Standard-library semantics and implementation literacy

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| shared | core | 77 | A, B |

**Prerequisites:** [T03](#t03), [T04](#t04), [T06](#t06).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 12 | 34 | 18 | 7 | 6 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Learn library families by contract and implementation boundary. stdlib.h is one header, not the whole standard library. The breadth is organized into five laboratories: header/format inventory, bytes/text, allocation/conversion, streams/environment, and algorithm/source literacy. Selected routines receive deep implementation work; the remaining families receive explicit contract comparison and bounded probes.

## Entry check and remediation

Pass T03 memory/lifetime reasoning and T04 checked-size/conversion boundaries. Read the allocation/dependency profiles first. Before a library call, write valid argument domains, ownership, error result and effects; if those cannot be stated, inspect that contract before executing a speculative test.

## Component progression

**Library contracts as implementation experiments.** Separate the public contract, local implementation policy and your independent oracle. Exercise zero length, overlap, locale, failure and execution-environment assumptions only where admitted.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **Two implementations disagree because the supposed test input violates one interface's precondition.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t12-01"></a>

### T12.01 — Library and header taxonomy

Inventory headers by facility and edition: declarations/types/macros can be compiler-provided while calls require linked support. ISO, POSIX, optional annex and implementation extensions are separate authorities. A freestanding build has a different promised environment from a hosted program, even if both can include a header.

Investigation: Create an edition-tagged header/family matrix and classify a deliberate mix of ISO, POSIX and extension interfaces.

Misconception to resolve: Removing stdlib.h does not remove the standard library or its linked implementation.

Observable evidence: A facility/authority/dependency inventory with compile-only versus linked evidence. Evidence is developed in [PR-T12-01](#pr-t12-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t12-01-a"></a>


- **T12.01.a** Separate the complete standard library from the single stdlib.h header. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-01](#pr-t12-01).


<a id="t12-01-b"></a>


- **T12.01.b** Inventory headers and function families by language edition. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-01](#pr-t12-01).


<a id="t12-01-c"></a>


- **T12.01.c** Distinguish ISO, POSIX, optional annex, and implementation-specific interfaces. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-01](#pr-t12-01).


<a id="t12-02"></a>

### T12.02 — Types, limits, and feature interfaces

Limits and format macros connect abstract types to actual ranges and variadic types. Use %zu for size_t and the appropriate inttypes macros for available fixed-width families. Feature macros describe a selected environment; optional typedefs and headers need detection. Declarations alone do not demonstrate runtime support.

Investigation: Build a limit/format report and compile negative mismatched-format examples separately.

Misconception to resolve: A type with the right measured width may still have a different required variadic format.

Observable evidence: Type/range/format mapping and compiler/header/library layer records. Evidence is developed in [PR-T12-01](#pr-t12-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t12-02-a"></a>


- **T12.02.a** Use standard limit, type, format, and feature macros correctly. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-01](#pr-t12-01).


<a id="t12-02-b"></a>


- **T12.02.b** Audit fixed-width integer formatting and size-dependent conversions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-01](#pr-t12-01).


<a id="t12-02-c"></a>


- **T12.02.c** Separate compiler-provided headers from external linked facilities. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-01](#pr-t12-01).


<a id="t12-03"></a>

### T12.03 — Memory operations

memcpy requires nonoverlap; memmove gives overlap-safe copy semantics as if through temporary storage. Both still require valid object/range arguments. Copying representations is not arbitrary typed construction. A zero count does not invent a universal permission to pass null to every library function.

Investigation: Write checked copy/move wrappers with explicit zero-length policy and compare overlapping ranges through a byte-array oracle.

Misconception to resolve: The size argument alone cannot rescue invalid pointer arguments or incompatible typed use.

Observable evidence: Range/overlap proofs, exact moved bytes and separately analyzed invalid calls. Evidence is developed in [PR-T12-02](#pr-t12-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t12-03-a"></a>


- **T12.03.a** Specify overlap, object validity, size, and return-value contracts. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-02](#pr-t12-02).


<a id="t12-03-b"></a>


- **T12.03.b** Compare copying representations with constructing typed values. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-02](#pr-t12-02).


<a id="t12-03-c"></a>


- **T12.03.c** Test boundary cases without inventing universally valid null-pointer exceptions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-02](#pr-t12-02).


<a id="t12-04"></a>

### T12.04 — Byte strings and bounded buffers

A byte array, a null-terminated string and a pointer/length view have distinct invariants. Track capacity, logical length and termination separately. strncpy may pad and may fail to terminate; snprintf reports required output length. A wrapper should choose reject, truncate or grow explicitly instead of blending their policies.

Investigation: Implement bounded append and conversion from a view to a terminated string, including embedded-zero input.

Misconception to resolve: A buffer capacity is not its current string length, and bounded spelling does not guarantee safe semantics.

Observable evidence: Exact content/length/termination results for empty, exact-fit, truncated and embedded-zero cases. Evidence is developed in [PR-T12-02](#pr-t12-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t12-04-a"></a>


- **T12.04.a** Distinguish byte arrays, terminated strings, and pointer/length views. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-02](#pr-t12-02).


<a id="t12-04-b"></a>


- **T12.04.b** Track capacity, logical length, termination, and truncation policies. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-02](#pr-t12-02).


<a id="t12-04-c"></a>


- **T12.04.c** Compare strcpy, strncpy, snprintf, and explicit-length interfaces by contract. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-02](#pr-t12-02).


<a id="t12-05"></a>

### T12.05 — Character and locale handling

ctype inputs must be EOF or values representable as unsigned char. Convert a potentially negative plain char before classification, without confusing it with EOF. Locale affects byte classification and case conversion; neither supplies Unicode character properties for arbitrary multibyte text.

Investigation: Classify byte inputs under a named locale and demonstrate the safe unsigned-char boundary.

Misconception to resolve: A UTF-8 byte is not independently a Unicode character for ctype.

Observable evidence: Domain checks, locale identity and a byte-versus-code-point explanation. Evidence is developed in [PR-T12-02](#pr-t12-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t12-05-a"></a>


- **T12.05.a** Check valid domains for ctype functions and macros. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-02](#pr-t12-02).


<a id="t12-05-b"></a>


- **T12.05.b** Distinguish byte classification from Unicode character properties. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-02](#pr-t12-02).


<a id="t12-05-c"></a>


- **T12.05.c** Identify global and per-operation locale assumptions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-02](#pr-t12-02).


<a id="t12-06"></a>

### T12.06 — Multibyte and wide-character conversion

Restartable conversion carries mbstate_t across chunks. mbrtowc distinguishes completed null, completed character, incomplete input and encoding failure; after failure the state needs a deliberate recovery policy. wchar_t representation and locale encoding are implementation choices, whereas RFC UTF-8 defines interchange bytes.

Investigation: Feed a character across chunk boundaries, handle invalid bytes and bounded output, then compare with a strict UTF-8 validator.

Misconception to resolve: Each input chunk is not automatically a complete independently decodable string.

Observable evidence: State/result traces, invalid recovery and a locale/UTF-8 boundary table. Evidence is developed in [PR-T12-02](#pr-t12-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t12-06-a"></a>


- **T12.06.a** Track conversion state and incomplete input across calls. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-02](#pr-t12-02).


<a id="t12-06-b"></a>


- **T12.06.b** Handle invalid sequences and output-capacity limits. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-02](#pr-t12-02).


<a id="t12-06-c"></a>


- **T12.06.c** Separate wchar_t representation from a portable Unicode interchange format. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-02](#pr-t12-02).


<a id="t12-07"></a>

### T12.07 — Allocation API semantics

malloc acquires uninitialized storage, calloc initializes representation bytes, and realloc has distinct success/failure lifetime transitions. free releases owned allocated storage. Alignment APIs and zero-size behavior need edition-specific contracts; define empty logical objects without relying on ambiguous resize behavior.

Investigation: Write an allocation adapter with failure injection, nonzero resize and explicit empty release; compare aligned storage obligations.

Misconception to resolve: All-zero bytes do not universally initialize every typed value, and failed nonzero resize must not lose its owner.

Observable evidence: Allocation/lifetime ledger, checked sizes and exactly-once cleanup under each failure. Evidence is developed in [PR-T12-03](#pr-t12-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t12-07-a"></a>


- **T12.07.a** Compare malloc, calloc, realloc, free, and aligned allocation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-03](#pr-t12-03).


<a id="t12-07-b"></a>


- **T12.07.b** Analyze failure, zero-size, alignment, and lifetime rules by edition. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-03](#pr-t12-03).


<a id="t12-07-c"></a>


- **T12.07.c** Preserve ownership correctly when resizing operations fail. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-03](#pr-t12-03).


<a id="t12-08"></a>

### T12.08 — Integer and floating conversion

strto functions expose conversion progress and range failure; a zero result alone is ambiguous. Clear/check errno for the documented range condition, inspect endptr, validate signs/bases and apply the application’s trailing-data policy. Locale affects floating parsing. C23 binary-prefix behavior must not be silently assumed in a C17 suite.

Investigation: Build strict decimal-integer and C-locale floating parsers around explicit token boundaries.

Misconception to resolve: atoi-style conversion cannot provide the same error/progress contract as a checked strto wrapper.

Observable evidence: No-conversion, trailing-junk, range, sign and locale tests with unchanged outputs on failure. Evidence is developed in [PR-T12-03](#pr-t12-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t12-08-a"></a>


- **T12.08.a** Compare strto-family APIs with weaker conversion interfaces. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-03](#pr-t12-03).


<a id="t12-08-b"></a>


- **T12.08.b** Validate end pointers, range errors, signs, bases, and trailing data. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-03](#pr-t12-03).


<a id="t12-08-c"></a>


- **T12.08.c** Specify locale and rounding assumptions for numeric conversions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-03](#pr-t12-03).


<a id="t12-09"></a>

### T12.09 — Formatted output

Formatted output is a variadic protocol: argument types and length modifiers must match exactly. Width and precision alter presentation, not the source type. snprintf returns required characters excluding the terminator, or a negative encoding error; check negativity before converting to size_t, then compare with capacity.

Investigation: Implement bounded diagnostic formatting with a required-size result and a declared truncation policy.

Misconception to resolve: A nonnegative snprintf return does not necessarily mean the full output fit.

Observable evidence: Format/type audit, zero-capacity sizing, exact-fit/truncation and encoding-error policy. Evidence is developed in [PR-T12-01](#pr-t12-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t12-09-a"></a>


- **T12.09.a** Match variadic argument types to format specifications. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-01](#pr-t12-01).


<a id="t12-09-b"></a>


- **T12.09.b** Handle precision, width, length modifiers, and required output size. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-01](#pr-t12-01).


<a id="t12-09-c"></a>


- **T12.09.c** Design bounded formatting with explicit truncation and error reporting. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-01](#pr-t12-01).


<a id="t12-10"></a>

### T12.10 — Formatted input

scanf reports successful assignments, not a complete parse proof. Field widths limit selected conversions but must account for destination storage and termination. Matching failure, input failure/EOF and leftover characters are different states. A line-plus-token-plus-strto design often gives clearer boundaries.

Investigation: Compare a width-bounded scanf example with an explicit parser on malformed, ambiguous and leftover input.

Misconception to resolve: A conversion count of one does not prove the entire record was accepted.

Observable evidence: Destination-size audit, count/EOF distinctions and exact remaining-input observations. Evidence is developed in [PR-T12-03](#pr-t12-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t12-10-a"></a>


- **T12.10.a** Analyze conversion counts, field widths, and destination storage. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-03](#pr-t12-03).


<a id="t12-10-b"></a>


- **T12.10.b** Compare scanf-family parsing with explicit tokenization and conversion. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-03](#pr-t12-03).


<a id="t12-10-c"></a>


- **T12.10.c** Handle ambiguous input, leftover characters, and EOF distinctly. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-03](#pr-t12-03).


<a id="t12-11"></a>

### T12.11 — Streams and buffering

FILE owns a stream state with orientation, buffering, position and indicators. EOF is a failed read condition to inspect afterward, not a prediction that the next read will fail. Update streams have required transitions between reading and writing. Closing ends FILE lifetime; fflush is not a universal storage-durability guarantee.

Investigation: Build a small stream copier and update-stream experiment with explicit transitions, then contrast FILE with an OS descriptor.

Misconception to resolve: while(!feof(f)) is not a correct read loop, and a descriptor is not interchangeable with FILE.

Observable evidence: Read-result/error/EOF traces, cleanup and documented flush/position limitations. Evidence is developed in [PR-T12-04](#pr-t12-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t12-11-a"></a>


- **T12.11.a** Model FILE ownership, orientation, buffering, and error indicators. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-04](#pr-t12-04).


<a id="t12-11-b"></a>


- **T12.11.b** Distinguish EOF, failure, flushing, positioning, and update-stream transitions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-04](#pr-t12-04).


<a id="t12-11-c"></a>


- **T12.11.c** Relate standard streams to lower-level OS descriptors without conflating them. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-04](#pr-t12-04).


<a id="t12-12"></a>

### T12.12 — Searching, sorting, and random numbers

A comparator must define consistent ordering without subtraction overflow. qsort specifies sorted results, not a universal stable algorithm or allocation profile; bsearch needs the compatible sorted order. rand supplies a reproducible pseudorandom facility under a chosen implementation, not security-sensitive entropy.

Investigation: Use a relational comparator, test duplicates/extremes, and compare pinned sorting sources plus a deterministic nonsecurity generator.

Misconception to resolve: The same qsort signature does not imply the same algorithm, stability or hidden effects.

Observable evidence: Comparator properties, sorted/search checks and a randomness-purpose classification. Evidence is developed in [PR-T12-05](#pr-t12-05).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t12-12-a"></a>


- **T12.12.a** Specify comparator consistency and avoid arithmetic-overflow comparisons. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-05](#pr-t12-05).

<a id="t12-13"></a>

### T12.13 — Mathematics and floating environment

math, complex, type-generic math and fenv cover different layers. Domain/range signaling and accuracy depend on facility and target assumptions; math_errhandling identifies supported reporting mechanisms. Complex and type-generic calls still need typed expectations and numerical criteria from T04.

Investigation: Map one scalar, complex and generic operation, probe a domain/range case and record observed errno/exceptions where supported.

Misconception to resolve: A returned finite value or nominal accuracy observation does not establish every exceptional contract.

Observable evidence: Facility map, supported reporting probes and justified independent reference tolerances. Evidence is developed in [PR-T12-05](#pr-t12-05).

<a id="t12-14"></a>

### T12.14 — Time and execution environment

Calendar time, process CPU time and elapsed monotonic time measure different quantities. ISO time representations and precision are implementation-dependent; a Linux elapsed-time adapter is a separate contract. Environment strings have ownership/lifetime hazards, termination handlers have ordering rules and system executes an implementation-defined command interface.

Investigation: Compare time measurements, copy an environment value under a documented protocol and inventory termination/system effects.

Misconception to resolve: clock is not universally elapsed wall time, and getenv results are not caller-owned heap allocations.

Observable evidence: Measurement-role table, environment lifetime notes and a declared effects/dependency ledger. Evidence is developed in [PR-T12-04](#pr-t12-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t12-14-b"></a>


- **T12.14.b** Audit environment variables, termination handlers, and system interaction. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-04](#pr-t12-04).


<a id="t12-14-c"></a>


- **T12.14.c** Identify implementation-dependent time representations and concurrency hazards. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-04](#pr-t12-04).


<a id="t12-15"></a>

### T12.15 — Signals, nonlocal jumps, and thread facilities

ISO signals offer a restricted handler environment distinct from POSIX signal contracts. setjmp/longjmp transfers control without automatic resource cleanup and can leave modified nonvolatile local state indeterminate. Thread and atomic interfaces must be located before assuming Linux behavior; language order is not the same as a platform API.

Investigation: Analyze a nonlocal-jump cleanup defect, design a restricted signal flag policy and inventory selected thread/atomic contracts.

Misconception to resolve: A jump is not exception unwinding, and a signal handler is not an ordinary callback.

Observable evidence: Control/lifetime trace, allowed-handler operations and bounded thread/runtime capability evidence. Evidence is developed in [PR-T12-04](#pr-t12-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

- **T12.15.a** Separate ISO signals from richer operating-system signal interfaces. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-04](#pr-t12-04).


<a id="t12-15-b"></a>


- **T12.15.b** Analyze setjmp/longjmp lifetime, local-state, and cleanup consequences. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-04](#pr-t12-04).


<a id="t12-15-c"></a>


- **T12.15.c** Locate thread and atomic contracts before applying platform assumptions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-04](#pr-t12-04).


<a id="t12-16"></a>

### T12.16 — Implementation source literacy

Source reading begins at a pinned public entry point, then follows helpers and configuration. Compare glibc 2.41 and musl 1.2.5 qsort entries with their public sorting contract; an internal algorithm is not an API guarantee. Picolibc 1.8.10 supplies a concrete embedded comparison: tinystdio console streams use application-defined FILE objects and getc/putc callbacks, with an optional flush callback. Enabling POSIX-backed fopen/fdopen adds malloc/free and open, close, read, write and lseek requirements. Disabling posix-io narrows this file-I/O boundary; it does not prove the entire library allocation-free. Static inspection supports hypotheses, while runtime allocation or stack claims need separate evidence.

Investigation: Navigate the specified pinned qsort entries and compare the two specified Picolibc console/file-I/O configurations, distinguishing public guarantees from internal choices.

Misconception to resolve: Finding no malloc spelling in one function does not prove the reachable call graph allocation-free, and a library configuration option is not evidence that its target backend has been implemented.

Observable evidence: Pinned source/call-flow map, two-row Picolibc configuration/backend inventory and explicitly limited effect claims. Evidence is developed in [PR-T12-05](#pr-t12-05).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t12-16-b"></a>


- **T12.16.b** Compare an embedded-oriented library's configuration and backend requirements. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-05](#pr-t12-05).


<a id="t12-16-c"></a>


- **T12.16.c** Separate public contracts, internal optimization, and application-visible extensions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T12-05](#pr-t12-05).

## Mastery gate and feedback

Given a library call, state argument domains, ownership, error and effects before using it. Demonstrate bounded parsing/text behavior, distinguish EOF from failure, and compare sorting implementation choices without promoting them to API guarantees. The five dossiers cover all families, while implementation depth remains explicit.

For independent study, make predictions before execution, compare an independent oracle, inspect one counterexample and defend the result aloud or in a short recorded review. Link each original objective to a specific artifact; use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) to score it. A failed gate requires a minimized cause, a corrected model and a fresh regression, not repeated nominal runs.

## Consolidation and transfer

Tighten one reusable component from profile A to B or C after a delay. Replace only the needed mechanism and audit transitive effects; do not equate avoiding a header with avoiding linked support.

## Environment and limits

Use the recorded hosted laboratory in [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and the per-project boundary in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). C17 is the baseline; edition/extension experiments are isolated and capability checked. Supplied fixture oracles validate mathematical or declared synthetic expectations. They do not execute the learner’s C, prove all language behavior or certify target hardware. Record actual commands, versions, observations and unresolved limits separately.

<a id="t18"></a>

# T18 — Contracts, ownership, and API design

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| shared | core | 47 | B, C |

**Prerequisites:** [T03](#t03), [T12](#t12).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | 20 | 10 | 5 | 4 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Design interfaces as contracts over values, resources, lifetimes and execution contexts. This module should precede serious container design: ownership vocabulary and failure guarantees prevent representation convenience from silently dictating caller obligations.

## Entry check and remediation

Use T03 lifetime diagrams and T12 bounded-buffer/error reasoning. Given a pointer parameter, name owner, capacity and invalidation before writing code. If the interface promises “safe” without a specific failure/alias contract, narrow it until the promise can be tested.

## Component progression

**An API whose failures preserve a state.** Write success and failure postconditions, ownership transfer points and callback effects. Compile a second consumer that attempts every documented boundary.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **A capacity error leaving a caller unable to determine which object it owns.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t18-01"></a>

### T18.01 — Domain and representation contracts

Representable states are broader than permitted domain states. An integer may encode milliseconds, a sentinel or an invalid negative duration; a structure can be initialized yet violate its invariant. Specify units, ranges and sentinel meanings at the boundary, including deliberate target-width assumptions.

Investigation: Write a bounded byte-view and timeout domain contract, then list representable but forbidden states.

Misconception to resolve: A C type alone rarely expresses the entire domain contract.

Observable evidence: Value partitions, unit-aware names and explicit acceptance/rejection tests. Evidence is developed in [PR-T18-01](#pr-t18-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t18-01-a"></a>


- **T18.01.a** Specify valid values, ranges, units, and sentinel meanings. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T18-01](#pr-t18-01).


<a id="t18-01-b"></a>


- **T18.01.b** Distinguish representable states from permitted states. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T18-01](#pr-t18-01).

<a id="t18-02"></a>

### T18.02 — Function contracts

A function contract separates caller preconditions from promised postconditions and preserved invariants. Capacity, overlap, mutation and failure effects need independent clauses. For append, success changes length/content; failure can promise unchanged state only if validation or staging precedes mutation.

Investigation: Define append pre/postconditions and prove the capacity check before writing.

Misconception to resolve: A return code does not by itself say whether partial mutation occurred.

Observable evidence: A contract table and state snapshots proving the declared success/failure guarantee. Evidence is developed in [PR-T18-01](#pr-t18-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t18-02-a"></a>


- **T18.02.a** Define preconditions, postconditions, and preserved invariants. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T18-01](#pr-t18-01).


<a id="t18-02-b"></a>


- **T18.02.b** Specify capacity, aliasing, mutation, and failure effects. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T18-01](#pr-t18-01).


<a id="t18-02-c"></a>


- **T18.02.c** Separate caller obligations from implementation checks. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T18-01](#pr-t18-01).


<a id="t18-03"></a>

### T18.03 — Ownership vocabulary

Ownership names who must release a resource, borrowing names temporary use without release authority, transfer changes the release obligation, and weak access does not keep the owner alive. Apply the same vocabulary to memory, descriptors, locks and device sessions. Copying an address does not copy ownership.

Investigation: Create creation/release/transfer ledgers for a buffer and a non-memory resource, contrasting shared and weak access.

Misconception to resolve: Every pointer holder is not an independent owner entitled to release it.

Observable evidence: Resource ledgers with exactly one release obligation or an explicit shared-count protocol. Evidence is developed in [PR-T18-02](#pr-t18-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t18-03-a"></a>


- **T18.03.a** Distinguish owned, borrowed, shared, transferred, and weak references. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T18-02](#pr-t18-02).


<a id="t18-03-b"></a>


- **T18.03.b** Document which operation creates and releases each resource. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T18-02](#pr-t18-02).


<a id="t18-03-c"></a>


- **T18.03.c** Model ownership consistently for memory, descriptors, locks, and devices. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T18-02](#pr-t18-02).


<a id="t18-04"></a>

### T18.04 — Lifetime relationships

Views depend on owner lifetimes and may additionally depend on mutation epochs. Callbacks depend on the lifetime of their context and registration. SQLite’s result pointers illustrate invalidation by conversion, stepping, reset and finalization, so “borrowed until close” may still be too weak a description.

Investigation: Design an owner/view/callback timeline and replace one fragile direct pointer with a generation handle.

Misconception to resolve: An owner still being alive does not guarantee a view survives every owner mutation.

Observable evidence: An invalidation table and stale-view tests tied to exact operations. Evidence is developed in [PR-T18-02](#pr-t18-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t18-04-a"></a>


- **T18.04.a** Express parent/child, view/owner, and callback/context lifetimes. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T18-02](#pr-t18-02).


<a id="t18-04-b"></a>


- **T18.04.b** Identify references invalidated by mutation or reset. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T18-02](#pr-t18-02).


<a id="t18-04-c"></a>


- **T18.04.c** Replace ambiguous lifetime rules with handles or explicit protocols. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T18-02](#pr-t18-02).


<a id="t18-05"></a>

### T18.05 — Object lifecycle

An object lifecycle defines legal operations in uninitialized, active, failed, stopped and destroyed states. Partial initialization acquires only a prefix of resources; shutdown should release exactly that prefix. Repeated stop/destroy behavior must be specified rather than guessed from a null field.

Investigation: Implement a lifecycle machine with injected init failure and a deliberate repeated-shutdown policy.

Misconception to resolve: A failed initialization is not automatically equivalent to a fully constructed object.

Observable evidence: State/operation table, failure-point tests and release counts. Evidence is developed in [PR-T18-03](#pr-t18-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t18-05-b"></a>

<a id="t18-06"></a>

### T18.06 — Opaque and exposed representations

Opaque pointers hide layout but often require allocation or a factory; exposed structs enable embedding and direct layout dependence. Caller-owned opaque storage needs an actual size/alignment contract, not guessed byte arrays. Choose by ABI, allocation policy, debugging and embedding needs.

Investigation: Compare all three representations for one object and implement a version with explicit caller-storage requirements.

Misconception to resolve: Opaque does not mean allocation-free, and hidden layout does not remove ABI obligations.

Observable evidence: Representation alternatives, size/alignment evidence and an independently compiled consumer. Evidence is developed in [PR-T18-03](#pr-t18-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t18-07"></a>

### T18.07 — Errors and result types

Status returns, tagged results and output parameters trade clarity, size and compatibility. A sentinel can collide with a valid result; separate status from payload when that ambiguity exists. Define whether outputs are initialized, unchanged or partially valid on each failure.

Investigation: Design a lookup that permits zero as a valid value and a parse operation with explicit output-state rules.

Misconception to resolve: A null or zero result is not necessarily an error without a contract.

Observable evidence: Result tables, sentinel-collision cases and output-state checks. Evidence is developed in [PR-T18-01](#pr-t18-01).

<a id="t18-08"></a>

### T18.08 — Execution-context contracts

Execution-context properties belong to a boundary and its reachable callees: allocation, blocking, reentrancy, thread access and ISR suitability are different claims. State whether callbacks are synchronous or asynchronous, what they may retain, and when cancellation completes ownership transfer.

Investigation: Write context contracts for a synchronous transform and deferred completion adapter.

Misconception to resolve: A function containing no allocation spelling is not automatically bounded or ISR-safe.

Observable evidence: Call/effect ledger, callback lifetime/retention rules and cancellation traces. Evidence is developed in [PR-T18-04](#pr-t18-04).

<a id="t18-09"></a>

### T18.09 — Contract enforcement

Compile-time checks reject configuration/type violations; runtime validation handles untrusted/environmental inputs; assertions express internal obligations under a chosen fault policy. Disabled assertions must not remove required validation or side effects. Tests expose counterexamples within their scope.

Investigation: Build enabled/disabled assertion configurations and compare externally invalid input behavior.

Misconception to resolve: An assertion is not a reliable user-input error path when it can disappear.

Observable evidence: Checks classified by purpose and identical required validation across build modes. Evidence is developed in [PR-T18-01](#pr-t18-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

- **T18.09.b** Define behavior when assertions or diagnostics are disabled. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T18-01](#pr-t18-01).


<a id="t18-09-c"></a>


- **T18.09.c** Keep contract violations distinguishable from ordinary environmental failures. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T18-01](#pr-t18-01).


<a id="t18-10"></a>

### T18.10 — API evolution

Evolution can change source, ABI, ownership or behavior independently. A new layout or a transferred result changes caller obligations even if a function name survives. Version a boundary, deprecate deliberately and test a consumer outside the implementation tree.

Investigation: Add a versioned operation while keeping an old consumer usable, with a migration note for changed constraints.

Misconception to resolve: A library version number does not itself ensure compatibility.

Observable evidence: Independent-consumer builds, compatibility matrix and an ownership-aware migration example. Evidence is developed in [PR-T18-04](#pr-t18-04).

The project-hour total is 30 h and is already included in implementation plus verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation are separate. Follow [guide-workload](#guide-workload) for conditional diagnostic and elective accounting.

## Mastery gate and feedback

Defend an API against hostile-but-valid caller cases, invalid input and resource failure. Show lifetime/invalidation and output-state guarantees explicitly. An independent consumer must compile and reproduce the documented behavior without inspecting private source.

For independent study, make predictions before execution, compare an independent oracle, inspect one counterexample and defend the result aloud or in a short recorded review. Link each original objective to a specific artifact; use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) to score it. A failed gate requires a minimized cause, a corrected model and a fresh regression, not repeated nominal runs.

## Consolidation and transfer

After a delay, change the allocator, storage representation or callback timing. Revise the contract first, then test the migration against the earlier consumer.

<!-- enhancement handoff -->

Use these ownership and compatibility contracts at the assembly/C boundary in [T36](#t36) and at every communication service in [T38](#t38)–[T42](#t42). Specify whether an adjacent layer consumes, borrows or retains a span before implementing its adapter.

## Environment and limits

Use the recorded hosted laboratory in [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and the per-project boundary in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). C17 is the baseline; edition/extension experiments are isolated and capability checked. Supplied fixture oracles validate mathematical or declared synthetic expectations. They do not execute the learner’s C, prove all language behavior or certify target hardware. Record actual commands, versions, observations and unresolved limits separately.

# T32 — Systematic testing and debugging

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cross-track | core | 69 | A, B, C |

**Prerequisites:** [T07](#t07), [T12](#t12), [T18](#t18).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10 | 30 | 16 | 8 | 5 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Build evidence that survives changes to implementation and environment. Testing progresses from independent contract oracles to model histories, fuzz/failure campaigns, supported instrumentation and reproducible diagnosis.

## Entry check and remediation

Write normal/boundary/invalid cases for a caller-storage component and explain output ownership after failure. Repair T07/T12/T18 interface/lifetime skills selectively. Confirm a supported Linux environment for Valgrind and GCC condition coverage; tool absence must be resolved for the dependent activity rather than treated as a pass.

Use [guide-entry](#guide-entry) for the diagnostic policy and [guide-roadmap](#guide-roadmap) for route order. Only the stated prelude leaves must precede a dependent project.

## Component progression

**Tests that reject plausible wrong mechanisms.** Start from a contract, then combine boundary examples, stateful generation, metamorphic relations, mutation and reduced reproducers. Keep oracle independence visible.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **A high-coverage suite accepting a deliberately corrupted invariant because it asserts only nominal outputs.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t32-01"></a>

### T32.01 — Test architecture

A test architecture separates a portable contract from adapters and the harness that observes it. The harness may allocate and print even when the component is profile B/C. Build a caller-owned bounded queue/parser with a scripted adapter and a genuinely independent list/grammar oracle. A mock's deterministic convenience can hide physical side effects. Evidence is the dependency boundary, fixture manifest and a map of which properties need real OS/target execution.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T32-01](#pr-t32-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t32-01-a"></a>


- **T32.01.a** Separate production components from test harness and platform adapters. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-01](#pr-t32-01).


<a id="t32-01-b"></a>


- **T32.01.b** Define fixtures, deterministic inputs, and independent oracles. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-01](#pr-t32-01).


<a id="t32-01-c"></a>


- **T32.01.c** Audit dependencies introduced solely by verification tooling. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-01](#pr-t32-01).


<a id="t32-02"></a>

### T32.02 — Unit testing

Unit tests should observe contracts rather than struct layout. Partition empty, full, normal, invalid and failure cases; sentinel storage detects unintended writes outside the declared extent. Implement table-driven tests for a component's public API and critical invariants. Merely obtaining the expected return value does not establish preserved ownership or unchanged output on failure. Evidence includes both result checks and state/effect checks, with the smallest reproducer retained.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T32-01](#pr-t32-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t32-02-a"></a>


- **T32.02.a** Test public contracts and critical internal invariants. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-01](#pr-t32-01).


<a id="t32-02-b"></a>


- **T32.02.b** Cover boundaries, invalid input, empty states, and failure returns. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-01](#pr-t32-01).


<a id="t32-02-c"></a>


- **T32.02.c** Avoid tests coupled unnecessarily to one implementation layout. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-01](#pr-t32-01).


<a id="t32-03"></a>

### T32.03 — Integration and system testing

An integration test crosses an actual boundary: framing to partial I/O, driver to adapter, or application to shutdown logic. Reuse vectors while substituting scripted and real backends, but retain backend-specific expectations. A simulated successful write is not evidence of Linux short-I/O or physical UART behavior. Evidence is a complete acquisition-to-release workflow with partial progress, one failure and deterministic cleanup, plus a declared environment scope.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T32-01](#pr-t32-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t32-03-a"></a>


- **T32.03.a** Verify contracts across real component boundaries. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-01](#pr-t32-01).


<a id="t32-03-b"></a>


- **T32.03.b** Exercise backend substitution and complete operational workflows. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-01](#pr-t32-01).


<a id="t32-03-c"></a>


- **T32.03.c** Distinguish mocked behavior from target or OS behavior. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-01](#pr-t32-01).


<a id="t32-04"></a>

### T32.04 — Property and model-based testing

Model-based testing generates operation sequences and compares implementation state to a simpler model after every operation. For a bounded queue, the list oracle is intentionally unlike a ring's index arithmetic. Enumerate short push/pop sequences and add seeded longer runs; minimize the first failing prefix. Random volume does not replace a stated invariant. Retain the seed, sequence and model/implementation disagreement, including a wraparound and full-queue case.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T32-02](#pr-t32-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t32-04-a"></a>


- **T32.04.a** Generate operation sequences against a simpler reference model. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-02](#pr-t32-02).


<a id="t32-04-b"></a>


- **T32.04.b** State invariants independently of implementation code. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-02](#pr-t32-02).


<a id="t32-04-c"></a>


- **T32.04.c** Preserve seeds and minimize failing sequences. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-02](#pr-t32-02).


<a id="t32-05"></a>

### T32.05 — Differential and metamorphic testing

Differential testing is useful only when both implementations share the same contract; two copies of the same algorithm are weak independence. Metamorphic relations can supply checks without a complete expected output: scaling a linear FIR input scales its output, and splitting a stream into chunks preserves stateful results. Apply relations to the supplied filter/queue data and include a transformation that is intentionally invalid for saturation. Evidence explains why each relation holds and the assumptions it needs.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T32-02](#pr-t32-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t32-05-b"></a>


- **T32.05.b** Define transformations with predictable relationships between outputs. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-02](#pr-t32-02).


<a id="t32-05-c"></a>


- **T32.05.c** Detect shared assumptions that invalidate apparent oracle independence. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-02](#pr-t32-02).


<a id="t32-06"></a>

### T32.06 — Fuzzing

A fuzz harness takes bytes, bounds memory/work, resets state and avoids nondeterministic external effects. Start with valid short packets and malformed length/truncation seeds, then mutate deterministic bytes and persist the smallest failing case. Code coverage feedback is optional machinery, not the oracle. Evidence includes maximum input/work limits, timeouts, corpus identities and crash-versus-contract-failure triage; a clean campaign establishes only its explored execution scope.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T32-03](#pr-t32-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t32-06-a"></a>


- **T32.06.a** Build bounded, deterministic parser or component harnesses. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-03](#pr-t32-03).


<a id="t32-06-b"></a>


- **T32.06.b** Seed corpora with meaningful valid and malformed cases. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-03](#pr-t32-03).


<a id="t32-06-c"></a>


- **T32.06.c** Triage crashes and maintain minimized regression inputs. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-03](#pr-t32-03).


<a id="t32-07"></a>

### T32.07 — Fault injection

Failure injection turns hidden cleanup paths into controlled contracts. Number acquisition points and fail each in turn; for I/O also inject zero progress, partial progress and timeout. A callback returning an invalid count must be contained before pointer arithmetic uses it. Implement rollback with an observable live-resource ledger. Evidence requires every prefix to release only acquired resources and leave the caller's output in the declared failure state.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T32-04](#pr-t32-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

- **T32.07.a** Inject allocation, I/O, timeout, and partial-progress failures. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-04](#pr-t32-04).


<a id="t32-07-b"></a>


- **T32.07.b** Exercise every acquisition and rollback boundary. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-04](#pr-t32-04).


<a id="t32-07-c"></a>


- **T32.07.c** Test misbehaving adapters while stating actual isolation limits. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-04](#pr-t32-04).


<a id="t32-08"></a>

### T32.08 — Dynamic instrumentation

Dynamic tools have different detection mechanisms and environments. Compare a native ASan/UBSan build with an unsanitized debug binary under Valgrind Memcheck on a supported Linux setup; include heap overrun, use-after-free and an uninitialized value used in a branch. ASan alone is not an initialized-value detector. Also scope separate thread instrumentation where supported. Record reports, runtime/stack dependencies and slowdowns; an unsupported host is a route-to-supported-environment issue, not a passing test.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T32-05](#pr-t32-05).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

- **T32.08.a** Apply address, undefined-behavior, thread, and memory-initialization checks where supported. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-05](#pr-t32-05).


<a id="t32-08-b"></a>


- **T32.08.b** Understand added runtime, memory, and execution costs. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-05](#pr-t32-05).

<a id="t32-09"></a>

### T32.09 — Static analysis

Warnings and static analysis inspect executions through models and approximations. Run high-value compiler diagnostics and Eva or another supported path-sensitive analyzer on a bounded routine, then classify alarms by actual preconditions and configuration. Suppress only with a written contract argument and a regression test. Removing an alarm by assuming the failing input away changes the claim. Evidence includes the before/after code, analyzer configuration and the remaining uncertainty.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T32-05](#pr-t32-05).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t32-09-a"></a>


- **T32.09.a** Combine compiler warnings with path-sensitive or abstract analysis. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-05](#pr-t32-05).


<a id="t32-09-b"></a>


- **T32.09.b** Review findings against contracts and configuration assumptions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-05](#pr-t32-05).


<a id="t32-09-c"></a>


- **T32.09.c** Track justified suppressions and analysis regressions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-05](#pr-t32-05).


<a id="t32-10"></a>

### T32.10 — Coverage

Coverage counts execution events, not correctness. For decision allow=length_ok && authorized, use TT, FT and TF to show each condition independently changes the decision while the other is fixed. Build a targeted MC/DC evidence table and compare statement, branch and condition-tool reports; short-circuit evaluation may leave a condition unevaluated. Evidence includes the independent-effect pairs and unreachable/excluded rationale. A 100% branch report alone is not this MC/DC argument.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T32-06](#pr-t32-06).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t32-10-a"></a>


- **T32.10.a** Distinguish statement, branch, condition, path, and MC/DC objectives. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-06](#pr-t32-06).


<a id="t32-10-b"></a>


- **T32.10.b** Verify tool support and explain unreachable or excluded code. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-06](#pr-t32-06).


<a id="t32-10-c"></a>


- **T32.10.c** Avoid equating executed code with tested correctness. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-06](#pr-t32-06).


<a id="t32-11"></a>

### T32.11 — Mutation testing

Mutation testing asks whether an oracle notices meaningful wrong behavior. Change <= to < at a capacity boundary, omit a cleanup and invert authorization; run retained tests and explain survivors. Some mutations are equivalent under the declared domain and require reasoning rather than arbitrary new cases. Evidence distinguishes equivalent, killed, surviving and unexecuted mutations, and strengthens one previously weak oracle without coupling it to internal implementation details.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T32-06](#pr-t32-06).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t32-11-a"></a>


- **T32.11.a** Select meaningful fault models and surviving mutations. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-06](#pr-t32-06).


<a id="t32-11-b"></a>


- **T32.11.b** Diagnose weak oracles and untested error paths. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-06](#pr-t32-06).


<a id="t32-11-c"></a>


- **T32.11.c** Separate equivalent mutations from actual testing deficiencies. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-06](#pr-t32-06).


<a id="t32-12"></a>

### T32.12 — Interactive debugging

Interactive debugging should discriminate hypotheses. Reduce the input, state a predicted register/memory observation, set a breakpoint/watchpoint and test it before changing several variables. Compare debug and optimized builds with matching symbols; concurrent stepping changes timing. Evidence is a short hypothesis log with one rejected explanation and the minimal repaired defect. A debugger can show a particular state without proving all paths reach that state safely.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T32-07](#pr-t32-07).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t32-12-a"></a>


- **T32.12.a** Use debugger state, watchpoints, and backtraces to test hypotheses. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-07](#pr-t32-07).


<a id="t32-12-b"></a>


- **T32.12.b** Minimize examples before changing multiple variables. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-07](#pr-t32-07).


<a id="t32-12-c"></a>


- **T32.12.c** Diagnose optimized and concurrent failures with appropriate caution. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T32-07](#pr-t32-07).


<a id="t32-13"></a>

### T32.13 — Host, simulator, and target evidence

Allocate evidence by modeled behavior: host logic for grammar/ownership, an identified emulator for its implemented core/board behavior, and real hardware for physical bus, analog and timing properties. The same bytes can be reused across these environments while the expected observation differs. Build an evidence matrix and deliberately reject a simulated ADC-accuracy claim. Passing all host fixtures does not close the board-specific obligations.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T32-07](#pr-t32-07).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t32-14"></a>

### T32.14 — Regression and reproducibility

Regression artifacts are a replay package: exact input, expected relation, binary/symbol identity, versions, flags, command, seed and limitations. Automate a representative debug/release/instrumented matrix and preserve failures before repairing code. Logs from a different image can mislead diagnosis. Evidence must link each claimed property to its test/proof/measurement artifact and show that a fresh replay reproduces both an injected failure and its repaired result.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T32-07](#pr-t32-07).

## Reading guidance

Read the bounded selections before the corresponding project, then annotate one contract or assumption you will test. The assigned reading table is generated from the exact inspected locators. Spend the remaining reading budget on original teaching, worked traces and target documentation comparisons, not whole uninspected chapters.

**Test-Driven Development for Embedded C — 5.4 The Embedded TDD Cycle (1 h):** Separate harness/target evidence.

**GCC program instrumentation options, selected verification and hardening contracts — -fsanitize=address (1 h):** Scope exercised memory checks.

**GCC program instrumentation options, selected verification and hardening contracts — -fsanitize=undefined (1 h):** Select arithmetic/semantic diagnostics.

**Valgrind Memcheck manual, selected detection contracts — 4.2.2. Use of uninitialised values (1 h):** Compare initialized-value detection.

**GCC program instrumentation options, selected verification and hardening contracts — -fcondition-coverage (1 h):** Build a targeted independent-effect exercise.

**The Eva plug-in — 1.2 Run-time errors and the absence thereof (1 h):** Interpret static/runtime claims.

**Shared scope limit — Test-Driven Development for Embedded C:** Host tests and simulator runs do not establish actual peripheral behavior. Historical tooling references require current commands. This inspection supports the strategy passages, not all mock-driver chapters.

**Shared scope limit — GCC program instrumentation options, selected verification and hardening contracts:** Selected options only, not every instrumentation feature. Flag availability and effective dependencies vary with installed compiler/target. GNU/Linux hardening aggregate is not a bare-metal recipe; instrumentation changes resource/timing behavior.

**Shared scope limit — Valgrind Memcheck manual, selected detection contracts:** Moving manual snapshot; installed version/platform must be recorded. No tool executed during research. Tool detection does not establish full correctness or prevent the underlying invalid access.

**Shared scope limit — The Eva plug-in:** False alarms can result from approximation. Soundness is relative to the specified context and supported semantics. Current manual states asynchronous interrupts are not directly modeled; do not claim full firmware proof from sequential analysis.

See [guide-reading](#guide-reading) for access/provenance and [guide-standards](#guide-standards) for the language baseline.

Project hours are the implementation plus verification budget, counted once. The optional-project-hour metadata identifies extensions included in this complete-module ledger; consult [guide-workload](#guide-workload) when selecting a core-only route.

## Mastery gate and feedback

Demonstrate an independent oracle, minimized failure, rollback coverage, supported instrumentation comparison and targeted MC/DC pairs. Kill one meaningful mutation and justify one equivalent case. If a failure survives, improve the property/oracle rather than merely increasing random iterations.

For every linked objective, retain a separately labeled explanation, implementation/analysis artifact and check. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the rubric; one passing fixture does not establish all three objectives of a topic.

## Consolidation and transfer

After a delay, substitute a different adapter and replay the retained corpus/matrix. Predict which evidence remains portable and which must be recollected on the OS or physical board.

<!-- enhancement handoff -->

Apply the existing length, arithmetic, ownership and failure reasoning to [T40](#t40)–[T42](#t42). Preserve malformed-input and resource-exhaustion cases at each layer; CRC success and a cooperative peer do not establish authentication or general protocol conformance.

## Environment and limits

Use [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles) to declare the dependency boundary, [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory) for installed tools and hardware, and [guide-audit](#guide-audit) for image/call-graph evidence. Fixtures are original deterministic mathematical or synthetic-protocol data. Run `python tools/verify_embedded_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to recompute their expectations. This oracle checks fixtures, not learner code.

Record host/tool/ISA identities and all mathematical/environment assumptions. Instrumented timings are not production timings; numerical references have stated domains; proof results hold only for reported obligations/models.

Use [guide-inventory](#guide-inventory) to find supplied data and [guide-integrations](#guide-integrations) for later cross-module work.

## Performance and debugging handoff

Reuse regression, minimization and separate dynamic/static tool builds in [T44](#t44) and [T45](#t45). Add prediction/observation/repair dossiers and delayed unseen variants; tool silence retains its configuration and executed-path limits.

Follow [guide-performance-debugging](#guide-performance-debugging) for the full route. The new project briefs budget only the additional experiment, diagnosis and repair; earlier implementation evidence stays in its original module.
