<a id="t21"></a>

# T21 — Error handling, resource management, and observability

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| shared | core | 53 | A, C |

**Prerequisites:** [T18](#t18), [T20](#t20).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6 | 24 | 12 | 6 | 5 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Make failure behavior part of correctness. Errors carry causes, acquisition can stop partway, mutation has a guarantee, cancellation has an in-flight owner, and diagnostics consume resources. The projects connect resource rollback to bounded observability and distinguish crash evidence from validated recovery.

## Entry check and remediation

Use T18 output/lifetime contracts and T20 effect boundaries. Before coding an error path, name acquired resources and externally visible state. If cleanup is duplicated in several branches, draw the acquisition stack and verify exactly-once release before choosing a control-flow style.

## Component progression

**A failure-complete state machine.** Enumerate acquisition prefixes and commit points. Preserve the original cause while cleanup runs, and distinguish cancellation request from confirmed quiescence.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **Cleanup itself failing after a partially published operation.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t21-01"></a>

### T21.01 — Error taxonomy

Invalid external input, internal contract violation, resource exhaustion and hardware fault need different policies. Recoverable, retryable, terminal and degraded describe application outcomes, not merely numeric codes. Preserve the original operation/resource context so diagnosis can distinguish symptom from cause.

Investigation: Define an error table for parser, allocator and transport failures with recovery class and context.

Misconception to resolve: Every nonzero result should not trigger the same retry or panic policy.

Observable evidence: Error/class/action matrix and tests for at least one outcome in each category. Evidence is developed in [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t21-01-a"></a>


- **T21.01.a** Separate invalid input, contract violations, resource failures, and hardware faults. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-01-b"></a>


- **T21.01.b** Define recoverable, retryable, terminal, and degraded outcomes. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-01-c"></a>


- **T21.01.c** Preserve enough context to identify the original cause. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-02"></a>

### T21.02 — Propagation and translation

Translation maps unstable backend errors into a stable public taxonomy while retaining causal context. A component can expose a portable timeout status and store a backend detail for diagnostics. Success must not be ambiguous with partial failure, and overwriting the first cause can destroy useful evidence.

Investigation: Implement a bounded error record and backend-to-public mapping with an explicit unknown-error policy.

Misconception to resolve: Abstraction does not require discarding all cause information.

Observable evidence: Mapping tests, stable public codes and original-cause preservation across propagation. Evidence is developed in [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t21-02-a"></a>


- **T21.02.a** Map backend errors into stable component-level results. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-02-b"></a>


- **T21.02.b** Retain causal context without exposing unstable implementation details. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-02-c"></a>


- **T21.02.c** Avoid silent information loss and ambiguous success codes. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-03"></a>

### T21.03 — Partial initialization

Partial initialization acquires a prefix of resources. Track completed stages and roll back in reverse dependency order. Repeated init/cleanup requires a state policy; a failed object may permit cleanup without permitting active operations.

Investigation: Inject failure after each of three acquisitions and check remaining ownership after rollback.

Misconception to resolve: A final “initialized” flag is insufficient to describe every intermediate owner.

Observable evidence: Acquisition/rollback traces and repeated-init/cleanup tests. Evidence is developed in [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t21-03-a"></a>


- **T21.03.a** Track resource acquisition order and completed initialization stages. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-03-b"></a>


- **T21.03.b** Roll back safely after every possible failure point. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-03-c"></a>


- **T21.03.c** Test repeated initialization and cleanup under injected failures. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-04"></a>

### T21.04 — Cleanup control flow

Early returns, nested cleanup and narrowly scoped cleanup labels are tools for proving release exactly once. Choose the structure that makes resource state visible and minimizes duplicated obligations. A forward jump to cleanup can be clearer than deeply nested success paths; it is not arbitrary control flow.

Investigation: Implement the same small acquisition sequence with two cleanup structures and compare reviewability.

Misconception to resolve: A blanket goto ban or blanket goto preference does not establish correctness.

Observable evidence: Exactly-once release proof, failure-point tests and a justified style choice. Evidence is developed in [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t21-04-a"></a>


- **T21.04.a** Compare early returns, nested cleanup, and narrowly scoped cleanup labels. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-04-b"></a>


- **T21.04.b** Establish exactly-once release for each acquired resource. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-04-c"></a>


- **T21.04.c** Choose structure by correctness and readability rather than blanket style rules. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-05"></a>

### T21.05 — Transactional mutation

The strong guarantee leaves observable state unchanged on failure; the basic guarantee keeps invariants while allowing changes. Stage allocations/copies before commit where strong behavior is required. Retry is idempotent only if repeated requests cannot duplicate externally visible effects.

Investigation: Implement a staged configuration update and compare strong/basic failure contracts.

Misconception to resolve: Returning an error does not imply rollback happened.

Observable evidence: Before/after snapshots, commit-point proof and repeated-request checks. Evidence is developed in [PR-T21-02](#pr-t21-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t21-05-a"></a>


- **T21.05.a** Define strong, basic, and explicitly weaker failure guarantees. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-02](#pr-t21-02).


<a id="t21-05-b"></a>


- **T21.05.b** Stage changes before committing externally visible state. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-02](#pr-t21-02).


<a id="t21-05-c"></a>


- **T21.05.c** Verify rollback and idempotent retries where promised. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-02](#pr-t21-02).


<a id="t21-06"></a>

### T21.06 — Cancellation and timeouts

Timeout says a deadline expired; cancellation completion says the operation will no longer use retained resources. An in-flight callback can arrive after a timeout, so identify requests and define one completion owner. Context cannot be reclaimed merely because the caller stopped waiting.

Investigation: Model timeout, cancel request, late callback and cancel acknowledgment, rejecting stale/duplicate completion.

Misconception to resolve: Timeout and successful cancellation are not interchangeable.

Observable evidence: Ownership/timing traces, exactly-once completion and no stale-context access. Evidence is developed in [PR-T21-02](#pr-t21-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t21-06-a"></a>


- **T21.06.a** Distinguish timeout expiry from successful cancellation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-02](#pr-t21-02).


<a id="t21-06-b"></a>


- **T21.06.b** Specify ownership of operations still in flight. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-02](#pr-t21-02).


<a id="t21-06-c"></a>


- **T21.06.c** Prevent stale callbacks and duplicate completion reporting. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-02](#pr-t21-02).


<a id="t21-07"></a>

### T21.07 — Assertions and fault policy

Assertions check developer invariants under a fault policy; required validation must remain when assertions disappear. Decide whether a fault returns, panics, enters safe state or resets, with target-specific implications. Expressions inside removable checks must not carry required side effects.

Investigation: Build assertions on/off and inject an invalid input plus an internal invariant defect under distinct policies.

Misconception to resolve: An assert is not a durable external-input validator.

Observable evidence: Equivalent required validation, explicit fault behavior and disabled-side-effect audit. Evidence is developed in [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t21-07-a"></a>


- **T21.07.a** Separate development assertions from required runtime validation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


<a id="t21-07-b"></a>


- **T21.07.b** Define panic, safe-state, reset, or error-return policies explicitly. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


<a id="t21-07-c"></a>


- **T21.07.c** Audit behavior when assertion code is absent. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


<a id="t21-08"></a>

### T21.08 — Logging and trace design

Logging uses storage, time and transport. Bounded records need severity, timestamp units, operation identity and an overflow/backpressure policy. Error reporting must not recursively allocate or fail through the same broken backend without a bounded fallback.

Investigation: Implement a fixed ring of event records with a stated drop policy and rate limit.

Misconception to resolve: More logs do not automatically improve diagnosis if they can destroy timing or recurse on failure.

Observable evidence: Exact overflow/rate traces, resource bounds and reporter-failure tests. Evidence is developed in [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t21-08-a"></a>


- **T21.08.a** Use bounded records with severity, timestamps, and context. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


<a id="t21-08-b"></a>


- **T21.08.b** Specify overflow, rate limiting, and transport backpressure. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


<a id="t21-08-c"></a>


- **T21.08.c** Avoid recursive failures inside error-reporting code. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


<a id="t21-09"></a>

### T21.09 — Developer and integrator diagnostics

White-box developer instrumentation and stable integrator diagnostics serve different audiences. Give them independent switches and supported contracts. Disabled instrumentation that promises no evaluation/storage cost needs preprocessor/code/binary evidence; a runtime if may preserve argument evaluation.

Investigation: Build four switch combinations and inspect expression counts, symbols and record storage.

Misconception to resolve: A disabled sink does not necessarily mean disabled call arguments or static buffers.

Observable evidence: Independent toggle matrix, no-evaluation checks and stable black-box output contract. Evidence is developed in [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t21-09-a"></a>


- **T21.09.a** Separate white-box introspection from stable black-box diagnostics. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


<a id="t21-09-b"></a>


- **T21.09.b** Define independently togglable interfaces and supported contracts. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


<a id="t21-09-c"></a>


- **T21.09.c** Verify disabled instrumentation removes promised evaluation and storage costs. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


<a id="t21-10"></a>

### T21.10 — Crash evidence and recovery

Crash evidence needs minimal bounded context and a build identity that resolves against matching symbols. Persistence has its own atomicity/reset/lifetime assumptions. A captured symptom supports diagnosis; recovery requires restoring validated state and testing the resumed behavior under the fault model.

Investigation: Encode/decode a small checksummed fault record and test corrupt/stale-build rejection plus a separate recovery policy.

Misconception to resolve: A readable crash record is not proof that continuing execution is safe.

Observable evidence: Corruption/build-correlation tests and recovery evidence explicitly separated from collection. Evidence is developed in [PR-T21-04](#pr-t21-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t21-10-a"></a>


- **T21.10.a** Preserve minimal fault context in suitable storage. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-04](#pr-t21-04).


<a id="t21-10-b"></a>


- **T21.10.b** Correlate records with build identifiers and symbol files. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-04](#pr-t21-04).


<a id="t21-10-c"></a>


- **T21.10.c** Distinguish symptom collection from validated fault recovery. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-04](#pr-t21-04).

<a id="t22"></a>

# T22 — Production-quality libraries and repositories

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| shared | core | 58 | A |

**Prerequisites:** [T18](#t18), [T21](#t21).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 7 | 26 | 14 | 6 | 5 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Turn a working component into a reviewable, consumable library. Organize source and contracts, trace requirements, test installation and FFI boundaries, pin dependencies, and release with reproducible evidence. Packaging and documentation are correctness work when they define what an independent consumer can safely assume.

## Entry check and remediation

Use T18 API contracts and T21 error/diagnostic evidence. Start from a small component already built in earlier modules, not an unrelated large repository. If an independent consumer cannot identify the public header, minimal build and ownership rules, repair those before adding release automation.

## Component progression

**A library consumed outside its own tree.** Install the interface and rebuild an independent client. Carry compiler options, dependency provenance, compatibility claims and reproducible release evidence with the package.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **A consumer that succeeds only because it accidentally includes a private build-tree header.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t22-01"></a>

### T22.01 — Repository organization

Separate public headers, private source, tests, examples, tools and target backends by their consumption role. A minimal supported build should not accidentally depend on the developer’s source tree or optional examples. Layout is useful when it makes boundaries obvious, not when it adds empty directories.

Investigation: Organize an earlier component and rebuild its smallest supported configuration from a clean checkout.

Misconception to resolve: A neat directory tree alone does not establish a usable library boundary.

Observable evidence: Clean-build instructions, public/private inventory and target-backend separation. Evidence is developed in [PR-T22-01](#pr-t22-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t22-01-a"></a>


- **T22.01.a** Separate public headers, private code, tests, examples, and tools. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T22-01](#pr-t22-01).


<a id="t22-01-b"></a>


- **T22.01.b** Keep target-specific backends identifiable. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T22-01](#pr-t22-01).


<a id="t22-01-c"></a>


- **T22.01.c** Make the minimal supported build easy to reproduce. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T22-01](#pr-t22-01).


<a id="t22-02"></a>

### T22.02 — Naming and readability

Names can encode units, roles and ownership, while small explicit control flow reduces hidden state. Complexity metrics highlight review candidates rather than dictate automatic rewrites. Prefer a name that explains a domain constraint over a short ambiguous name that needs repeated comments.

Investigation: Review one interface and one failure-heavy function, rename unclear units/ownership and simplify only with preserved contracts.

Misconception to resolve: A lower branch count is not automatically clearer or safer code.

Observable evidence: Before/after review examples and behavior-preserving regression evidence. Evidence is developed in [PR-T22-01](#pr-t22-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t22-02-a"></a>


- **T22.02.a** Encode role, units, ownership, and domain meaning in names. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T22-01](#pr-t22-01).


<a id="t22-02-b"></a>


- **T22.02.b** Reduce unnecessary branching and hidden state. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T22-01](#pr-t22-01).


<a id="t22-02-c"></a>


- **T22.02.c** Use complexity metrics to investigate code rather than replace judgment. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T22-01](#pr-t22-01).


<a id="t22-03"></a>

### T22.03 — Documentation

Doxygen comments document preconditions, postconditions and resource/lifetime rules; usage examples test the public story. Rationale comments explain nonobvious invariants. Generated API references show interface details, while architecture narratives explain why boundaries and policies exist.

Investigation: Document an API, compile its usage example and write a short architecture note.

Misconception to resolve: Generated documentation does not enforce a contract or replace design rationale.

Observable evidence: Rendered references, executable examples and a consumer-readable ownership/failure narrative. Evidence is developed in [PR-T22-01](#pr-t22-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t22-03-a"></a>

<a id="t22-03-b"></a>

Packaging installs public headers and artifacts with consumable build targets or explicit commands. Static/shared choices affect dependency closure, symbol visibility and runtime lookup. Test consumption outside both source and build trees, including a clean installation prefix.

### T22.06 — Compatibility and FFI

FFI crosses calling convention, layout, string/buffer and ownership boundaries. Define length units, encoding, allocator/release pairing and version-skew behavior. A foreign runtime cannot safely guess private structure layout or release memory with a different allocator.

Investigation: Expose a minimal C ABI and call it from a small independent Python ctypes consumer with explicit signatures.

Misconception to resolve: A function name being visible does not make arbitrary foreign signatures compatible.

Observable evidence: Layout/calling-contract evidence, buffer ownership tests and version-skew rejection. Evidence is developed in [PR-T22-03](#pr-t22-03).

Review follows invariants, ownership, failure and generated code, using call/data flow to navigate unfamiliar source. Form a hypothesis before modifying a legacy path and test it against evidence. Review findings should name a contract and reproducer rather than only style preference.

### T22.09 — Refactoring and regression analysis

Characterization tests preserve current behavior before a structural change, while intentionally changed contracts need new expectations. Bisection narrows a regression to a change; minimized inputs reveal its mechanism. Refactoring is successful when improved structure and preserved behavior are both demonstrated.

Investigation: Refactor one failure path after characterization, insert a regression and locate/minimize it through version history.

Misconception to resolve: Passing only new tests cannot demonstrate old consumers retained their behavior.

Observable evidence: Before/after consumer checks, bisection evidence and a retained minimized regression. Evidence is developed in [PR-T22-04](#pr-t22-04).

<a id="t22-10"></a>

### T22.10 — Release engineering

A release includes versioned binaries, matching symbols, build/configuration provenance, changes and known limits. Reproducibility can mean identical bytes under controlled inputs or explainable differences under declared toolchains; state the claim. Clean installation and rollback/replacement tests establish deployment behavior.

Investigation: Create two small releases, install each into isolated prefixes and test replacement plus migration.

Misconception to resolve: An archive filename and successful local build are not a release evidence chain.

Observable evidence: Artifact hashes, matching debug identifiers, clean-consumer runs and rollback/migration results. Evidence is developed in [PR-T22-04](#pr-t22-04).

## Reading guidance

- **R-doxygen-contract-docs**, **Documenting the code** (1 h): Produce API references while retaining separate architecture rationale.

- **R-doxygen-contract-docs**, **\pre { description of the precondition }** (1 h): Write caller obligations explicitly; documentation does not enforce them.

- **R-modern-c-3**, **10.1 Interface documentation** (1 h): Review the public contract from a consumer perspective.

- **R-hanson-cii**, **3.2 Implementation** (1 h): Practice unfamiliar-source navigation and representation/invariant review.

Read only these inspected locators as the essential spine. Additional reading time covers comparison, notes and retrieval, not an unstated whole-book assignment. Historical examples require the modern contract review stated here; draft and live-document limits remain in [guide-reading](#guide-reading).

## Implementation projects

- [PR-T22-01](#pr-t22-01) — Readable repository and executable API documentation (8 h, profile A, core).

- [PR-T22-02](#pr-t22-02) — Traceable package consumed outside the tree (10 h, profile A, core).

- [PR-T22-03](#pr-t22-03) — Foreign consumer and dependency provenance (10 h, profile A, core).

- [PR-T22-04](#pr-t22-04) — Review, minimized regression and two reproducible releases (12 h, profile A, core).

The project-hour total is 40 h and is already included in implementation plus verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation are separate. Follow [guide-workload](#guide-workload) for conditional diagnostic and elective accounting.

## Mastery gate and feedback

Consume the installed library from an independent project and foreign-language harness, then review/refactor/release it without losing contracts. Detect traceability gaps and explain all dependency/license provenance. The release dossier must make a known limitation visible rather than quietly burying it in source.

For independent study, make predictions before execution, compare an independent oracle, inspect one counterexample and defend the result aloud or in a short recorded review. Link each original objective to a specific artifact; use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) to score it. A failed gate requires a minimized cause, a corrected model and a fresh regression, not repeated nominal runs.

## Consolidation and transfer

After a delay, rebuild from a clean clone with pinned inputs, replace one dependency or package mode and repeat the independent-consumer and migration tests.

## Environment and limits

Use the recorded hosted laboratory in [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and the per-project boundary in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). C17 is the baseline; edition/extension experiments are isolated and capability checked. Supplied fixture oracles validate mathematical or declared synthetic expectations. They do not execute the learner’s C, prove all language behavior or certify target hardware. Record actual commands, versions, observations and unresolved limits separately.

<a id="t13"></a>

# T13 — Implicit resource use and hidden costs

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cross-track | core | 45 | A, B, C |

**Prerequisites:** [T07](#t07), [T12](#t12).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3 | 24 | 10 | 4 | 4 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Treat resource effects as observable contracts. Measure with stated coverage, characterize cold/warm and contended paths, and choose restricted replacements only after defining what is actually required. The intended result is a mechanism you can explain, a bounded artifact you can inspect and an evidence trail someone else can reproduce.

## Entry check and remediation

Given a callback, name possible allocation/blocking/state effects even when its return value is deterministic. If output correctness is the only criterion, redo a T12 interface contract and the profile guide. Use [guide-entry](#guide-entry) for diagnostic evidence and [guide-roadmap](#guide-roadmap) for route choices. Domain numbers are coverage IDs, not an instruction to study them numerically.

## Component progression

**An effect ledger that includes hidden work.** Measure first-use and steady-state paths separately; identify allocation, locks, stack, callbacks and global state. Explain the boundaries of interception and opaque dependencies.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **A no-malloc spelling audit missing allocation in a callback or lazy initialization.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching

Work through the mechanism notes in order within each project, alternating hand prediction with observation. Preserve the first counterexample rather than only a final green test. Full implementations belong to the projects; these notes explain what they must establish.


<a id="t13-01"></a>

### T13.01 — Effects contract

An effects contract includes allocation, stack, synchronization, OS work, persistent state and blocking, including callback effects. Correct return values alone do not characterize suitability.

Investigate: Draw a reachable call graph and annotate effects and unknown nodes before measuring. A common mistake is: A pure-looking API name implies no environmental effects. Evidence: A component and a transitive ledger distinguish proven restrictions, observed paths and unresolved callees. Develop that evidence in [PR-T13-01](#pr-t13-01).

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

### T13.02 — Heap allocation census

An allocation interceptor sees only the interfaces it hooks. A library can use an internal allocator, a pool or mapping path outside that hook; reuse can hide storage activity on later calls.

Investigate: Compare source inspection, wrapper interception and a process-level observation on fresh and warm executions. A common mistake is: No observed malloc call proves no storage acquisition. Evidence: The report states interception coverage and includes a deliberate bypass path. Develop that evidence in [PR-T13-01](#pr-t13-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t13-03"></a>

### T13.03 — Stack consumption

Stack use depends on call depth, alignment, spills and dynamic storage, not merely local declarations. Whole-system bounds must add nested contexts that measurements may never trigger.

Investigate: Combine a static synthetic call graph with compiler frame estimates and an observed high-water experiment. A common mistake is: The largest single frame is the whole-program maximum. Evidence: A conservative path/nesting bound is separated from measured high water and unknown callback frames. Develop that evidence in [PR-T13-02](#pr-t13-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t13-04"></a>

### T13.04 — Locking and contention

Lock acquisition is not the same observation as contention. Stream, allocator and once initialization locks can be hidden behind simple APIs, and reentrant entry adds a different failure mode.

Investigate: Compare uncontended, contended and reentrant scenarios in a small annotated call graph. A common mistake is: An uncontended benchmark proves a routine never blocks. Evidence: Each scenario records synchronization assumptions and distinguishes lock presence from measured waiting. Develop that evidence in [PR-T13-02](#pr-t13-02).

First-call paths can initialize state or acquire resources that steady-state timing misses. A reset must genuinely restore the relevant process/library state.

<a id="t13-06"></a>

### T13.06 — System interaction

Syscalls expose kernel interaction, but user-space work and already-reserved storage may occur without a syscall. Conversely, an OS mapping acquires address space without necessarily making every page resident.

Investigate: Attribute a controlled operation to user computation, syscalls and storage ledgers separately. A common mistake is: Absence of syscalls proves absence of allocation or blocking. Evidence: A trace interpretation states what the observation excludes and what it cannot see. Develop that evidence in [PR-T13-01](#pr-t13-01).

errno is thread-local state in the relevant implementation; locale, streams and caches may have broader sharing. Independent instances need state separation or explicit reset rules.

<a id="t13-08"></a>

### T13.08 — Execution-context suitability

Thread safety, reentrancy and signal safety answer different questions. Fixed storage does not bound execution time, and an ISR cannot safely inherit arbitrary userspace blocking assumptions.

Investigate: Classify a fixed-buffer operation, a mutex-protected operation and a signal-handler callback. A common mistake is: Allocation-free means safe in every execution context. Evidence: A context suitability matrix separates memory bounds, time bounds, interruption and allowed services. Develop that evidence in [PR-T13-03](#pr-t13-03).

<a id="t13-09"></a>

### T13.09 — Implementation comparison

Implementation observations belong to a version and configuration. The inspected glibc 2.41 qsort path selects stack or acquired temporary storage and has an allocation-failure heapsort fallback; inspected musl 1.2.5 uses a different smoothsort path. A common signature does not imply common effects.

Worked source branch: the inspected glibc 2.41 source reserves a 1024-byte temporary stack buffer. Sorting 64 four-byte elements needs 256 temporary bytes and selects it; 300 four-byte elements need 1200 and reach the acquisition branch, which falls back to heapsort if acquisition fails. For ten 64-byte elements and eight-byte pointers, indirect storage is 2*10*8+64=224 bytes. These are source-selected temporary requirements, not total-stack bounds; helper and comparator frames/effects remain separate. The restricted local replacement accepts at most sixteen ints, so its workload and API exclusions are explicit.

Investigate: Audit the two pinned qsort source paths, annotate comparator/transitive-helper unknowns and separate source branches from runtime measurements. A common mistake is: One libc result is a portable C guarantee, or qsort necessarily implements quicksort. Evidence: The conclusion labels API guarantees, inspected temporary-buffer/fallback paths and separately measured behavior; equivalent-key order is not presumed stable. Develop that evidence in [PR-T13-04](#pr-t13-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t13-10"></a>

### T13.10 — Replacement decisions

Replacement begins with a restricted requirement, not a general claim to improve a mature routine. An at-most-sixteen-int sorter can reject unsupported capacity visibly and use an explicit local insertion invariant without supplying general qsort semantics.

Investigate: Implement that narrow insertion-sort replacement with actual caller-owned int storage and no external sorting/byte calls; compare sortedness and multiplicities using a hosted oracle. A common mistake is: A shorter implementation is necessarily safer or faster. Evidence: Empty, duplicate, endpoint, exact-capacity and over-capacity cases plus dependency/effect audit support a bounded decision; a rejected input remains unchanged. Develop that evidence in [PR-T13-04](#pr-t13-04).


#### Evidence checklist

## Reading guidance

The essential spine below is deliberately narrow. Assign only the exact inspected registry locators shown; no whole book, standard or implementation is implied. Historical rationale does not replace a current contract, and one implementation does not create a portable guarantee. # T11 — Freestanding and minimal-runtime construction

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cross-track | core | 55 | C |

**Prerequisites:** [T07](#t07), [T08](#t08), [T09](#t09).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |

| 3 | 32 | 12 | 4 | 4 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Construct small portable components and runtime support under precise dependency restrictions. Separate freestanding compilation from no-library, no-allocation and whole-image claims, then audit actual emitted support. The intended result is a mechanism you can explain, a bounded artifact you can inspect and an evidence trail someone else can reproduce.

## Entry check and remediation

List what the compiler and linker add to a source file. Recover one unresolved helper from an object. Revisit T07/T09 until component and executable dependency boundaries are distinguishable. Use [guide-entry](#guide-entry) for diagnostic evidence and [guide-roadmap](#guide-roadmap) for route choices. Domain numbers are coverage IDs, not an instruction to study them numerically.

## Component progression

**The complete dependency closure.** Audit both object requirements and the linked image. Supply selected support routines and explain where structure copies, division or atomics can introduce helpers.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **An optimized build introducing a helper that was absent at debug optimization.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching

Work through the mechanism notes in order within each project, alternating hand prediction with observation. Preserve the first counterexample rather than only a final green test. Full implementations belong to the projects; these notes explain what they must establish.


<a id="t11-01"></a>

### T11.01 — Dependency profiles

Hosted, freestanding, libc-free, allocation-free and custom-startup claims restrict different dimensions. A component promise is weaker than a whole-executable promise because the harness and callbacks have their own effects.

Investigate: Write an allowlist for headers, symbols, callbacks, storage and OS services at two boundaries. A common mistake is: Omitting stdlib.h removes runtime dependencies. Evidence: The contract labels every requirement by its exact scope and makes unknown transitive callees explicit. Develop that evidence in [PR-T11-01](#pr-t11-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t11-01-a"></a>


- **T11.01.a** Separate hosted, freestanding, libc-free, allocation-free, and custom-startup requirements. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T11-01](#pr-t11-01).


<a id="t11-01-b"></a>


- **T11.01.b** State whether restrictions apply to component or entire executable. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T11-01](#pr-t11-01).


<a id="t11-01-c"></a>


- **T11.01.c** Enumerate headers, libraries, runtime helpers, syscalls, and allocation sources. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T11-01](#pr-t11-01).


<a id="t11-02"></a>

### T11.02 — Compiler and linker controls

Freestanding flags change compilation assumptions; startup and default-library exclusions act during linking. Header search paths form a third independent axis.

Investigate: Build a controlled option matrix and compare unresolved symbols, selected startup inputs and final dependencies. A common mistake is: -ffreestanding is equivalent to -nostdlib. Evidence: A matrix explains which stage each control affects and retains the actual driver commands. Develop that evidence in [PR-T11-01](#pr-t11-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t11-02-a"></a>


- **T11.02.a** Compare -ffreestanding and -fno-builtin with link-stage exclusions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T11-01](#pr-t11-01).


<a id="t11-02-b"></a>


- **T11.02.b** Distinguish -nostdlib, -nodefaultlibs, and -nostartfiles experimentally. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T11-01](#pr-t11-01).


<a id="t11-02-c"></a>


- **T11.02.c** Treat header-search restrictions as a separate build dimension. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T11-01](#pr-t11-01).


<a id="t11-03"></a>

### T11.03 — Compiler-generated memory operations

Aggregate copy and initialization may be lowered into memory-helper calls even without a source call. The generated form depends on size, optimization and target.

Investigate: Compile several fixed-size aggregate operations and inspect objects and LTO images for helper requirements. A common mistake is: A source-level call census is a complete binary dependency audit. Evidence: An emitted-call ledger names the support implementation or a documented compiler configuration that avoids it. Develop that evidence in [PR-T11-02](#pr-t11-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t11-03-a"></a>


- **T11.03.a** Detect emitted memcpy, memmove, memset, and comparison operations. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T11-02](#pr-t11-02).


<a id="t11-03-b"></a>


- **T11.03.b** Exercise aggregate copies and initialization at different optimization levels. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T11-02](#pr-t11-02).


<a id="t11-03-c"></a>


- **T11.03.c** Supply documented support routines where required by the toolchain. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T11-02](#pr-t11-02).


<a id="t11-04"></a>

### T11.04 — Arithmetic support

Integer division and soft-float operations can require compiler-runtime routines. Avoiding a source library function does not provide the missing instruction or helper contract.

Investigate: Inspect a wide division and conversion on one instruction-rich and one constrained target. A common mistake is: Arithmetic expressions are always dependency-free. Evidence: Each helper is classified as deliberately linked, implemented under an explicit contract, or excluded from supported operations. Develop that evidence in [PR-T11-02](#pr-t11-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t11-04-a"></a>


- **T11.04.a** Identify division, multiplication, conversion, and soft-float helpers. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T11-02](#pr-t11-02).


<a id="t11-04-b"></a>


- **T11.04.b** Inspect libgcc or compiler-rt symbol contracts for the target. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T11-02](#pr-t11-02).


<a id="t11-04-c"></a>


- **T11.04.c** Decide whether to link, implement, or avoid each helper. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T11-02](#pr-t11-02).


<a id="t11-05"></a>

### T11.05 — Atomic and instrumentation support

Atomics, stack protection and instrumentation can introduce state and out-of-line calls. Verification builds may intentionally carry support absent from production, but those differences need evidence.

Investigate: Compare atomic and instrumented objects against production allowlists. A common mistake is: Passing an instrumented build proves the production image has identical dependencies. Evidence: Separate audit reports name helper symbols, alignment and actual lock-free observations without inferring universal support. Develop that evidence in [PR-T11-02](#pr-t11-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t11-05-a"></a>


- **T11.05.a** Detect out-of-line atomic operations and support-library calls. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T11-02](#pr-t11-02).


<a id="t11-05-b"></a>


- **T11.05.b** Audit stack-protection, sanitizer, profiling, and coverage runtime requirements. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T11-02](#pr-t11-02).


<a id="t11-05-c"></a>


- **T11.05.c** Keep verification-only dependencies separate from production dependency claims. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T11-02](#pr-t11-02).


<a id="t11-06"></a>

### T11.06 — Minimal memory primitives

A byte-copy contract excludes overlap, while move must preserve the original source bytes when ranges overlap. Zero length must be decided before any access. Compiler recognition can turn a helper implementation into its own external call.

Investigate: Implement copy, move, set and lexicographic byte compare without external C-library calls. A common mistake is: A forward copy works for every overlapping range. Evidence: Snapshot-based oracle cases cover both overlap directions; object inspection excludes accidental self-recursive helper calls. Develop that evidence in [PR-T11-03](#pr-t11-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t11-06-a"></a>


- **T11.06.a** Implement byte-copy, overlap-safe move, set, and comparison operations. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T11-03](#pr-t11-03).


<a id="t11-06-b"></a>


- **T11.06.b** Test boundaries, overlap contracts, alignment, and zero-length conditions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T11-03](#pr-t11-03).


<a id="t11-06-c"></a>


- **T11.06.c** Prevent optimizer transformations from creating unintended self-recursive support calls. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T11-03](#pr-t11-03).


<a id="t11-07"></a>

### T11.07 — Environment adaptation

An embedded library asks the environment for services such as stream output or storage extension. Semihosting redirects requests through a debugger and therefore changes standalone behavior.

Investigate: Specify a small service adapter with a refusing heap policy and a transport stub; classify debugger-dependent paths. A common mistake is: Successful output under a debugger proves the board can print independently. Evidence: The adapter reports unsupported operations explicitly and its dependency table distinguishes test backend from board service. Develop that evidence in [PR-T11-04](#pr-t11-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t11-07-a"></a>

<a id="t11-07-c"></a>


- **T11.07.c** Distinguish semihosting dependencies from standalone board operation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T11-04](#pr-t11-04).


<a id="t11-08"></a>

### T11.08 — Runtime entry contracts

Entry establishes a contract for stack, initialized storage, exception state and any retained TLS/hooks. A reusable component should consume this contract rather than silently repairing the whole environment.

Investigate: Write a platform entry checklist and test the component with one intentionally uninitialized service excluded. A common mistake is: Link success establishes a valid runtime entry state. Evidence: The checklist names each initializer and every hosted facility deliberately unavailable. Develop that evidence in [PR-T11-04](#pr-t11-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t11-08-b"></a>

<a id="t11-08-c"></a>


- **T11.08.c** Make unsupported hosted services fail visibly rather than accidentally work. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T11-04](#pr-t11-04).


<a id="t11-09"></a>

### T11.09 — Automated dependency audit

An object exposes unresolved requirements before linking, whereas final linking can hide them by supplying code. Audits therefore need both undefined symbols and final maps/disassembly.

Investigate: Automate allowlist checks over debug/release and GCC/Clang outputs, including one deliberate forbidden call. A common mistake is: No undefined symbols in an executable means no forbidden dependency. Evidence: The failing fixture is rejected and statically resolved support is still visible in the final closure report. Develop that evidence in [PR-T11-05](#pr-t11-05).

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t11-09-c"></a>


- **T11.09.c** Compare audits across optimization, compiler, and configuration changes. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T11-05](#pr-t11-05).


<a id="t11-10"></a>

### T11.10 — Runtime validation

A hosted reference is useful for checking semantics while the tested component remains under its stricter profile. Boundary tests and failures need a backend that does not rely on the component being verified.

Investigate: Run differential byte-operation tests plus failure injection and then rerun selected cases in the restricted environment. A common mistake is: Using libc in the test oracle violates the component boundary. Evidence: The component/harness boundary is documented, disagreement is minimized and unsupported targets are listed rather than silently skipped. Develop that evidence in [PR-T11-03](#pr-t11-03).

# T10 — Hosted startup and minimal Linux executables

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| linux | core | 48 | D |

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |

## Purpose and outcomes

Understand where Linux process entry becomes a C program. Build a deliberately restricted custom-entry executable and make every retained runtime/syscall service explicit. The intended result is a mechanism you can explain, a bounded artifact you can inspect and an evidence trail someone else can reproduce.

## Entry check and remediation

Explain program headers versus sections and the chosen call ABI. Decode a pointer table with explicit bounds. If that fails, repeat T09 ELF structure and T08 alignment; do not guess at entry stack addresses. Use [guide-entry](#guide-entry) for diagnostic evidence and [guide-roadmap](#guide-roadmap) for route choices. Domain numbers are coverage IDs, not an instruction to study them numerically.

## Component progression

**A Linux executable owning its entry.** Decode the real initial stack, establish the ABI before entering C and wrap only declared syscalls. Record partial progress and exit behavior without importing hosted startup assumptions.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **A short write followed by interruption, where resending the original span duplicates bytes.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching

Work through the mechanism notes in order within each project, alternating hand prediction with observation. Preserve the first counterexample rather than only a final green test. Full implementations belong to the projects; these notes explain what they must establish.


<a id="t10-01"></a>

### T10.01 — Kernel-to-userspace handoff

exec replaces a process image; the kernel chooses mappings and an entry address, possibly first entering the dynamic loader. No caller has pushed a normal C return address for the executable entry point.

Investigate: Trace kernel loader source and inspect PT_INTERP and e_entry in three variants. A common mistake is: _start is called exactly like main. Evidence: A handoff diagram assigns mappings, relocations, stack setup and language startup to their actual owners. Develop that evidence in [PR-T10-01](#pr-t10-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t10-01-a"></a>


- **T10.01.a** Trace exec loading, mappings, and initial entry selection. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T10-01](#pr-t10-01).


<a id="t10-01-b"></a>


- **T10.01.b** Identify which responsibilities belong to kernel and dynamic loader. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T10-01](#pr-t10-01).


<a id="t10-01-c"></a>


- **T10.01.c** Distinguish an executable entry point from a C function call. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T10-01](#pr-t10-01).


<a id="t10-02"></a>

### T10.02 — Initial process stack

The initial stack encodes argc, pointer arrays, terminators and an auxiliary vector according to the selected ABI. Pointer values refer to separately placed strings rather than an assumed packed layout.

Investigate: Decode the declared synthetic stack and inspect a debugger snapshot at entry. A common mistake is: argv strings must immediately follow their pointer table. Evidence: Decoded counts, terminators, alignment and auxv entries agree without reading beyond declared bounds. Develop that evidence in [PR-T10-01](#pr-t10-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t10-02-a"></a>

### T10.03 — Startup object families

CRT filenames describe toolchain conventions rather than one universal runtime interface. Startup fragments and compiler CRT support can change with static, PIE and shared configurations.

Investigate: Use driver output to inventory entry and initialization objects for each chosen build mode. A common mistake is: crt1.o always has the same role and content on every target. Evidence: A manifest associates each object with its provider, mode and observed symbol contribution. Develop that evidence in [PR-T10-01](#pr-t10-01).

### T10.04 — C runtime initialization

Runtime startup prepares facilities that retained library calls may assume: TLS, canaries, environment, initialization hooks and loader state. Omitting one service narrows the supported application contract.

Investigate: Compare the inspected glibc and musl startup paths and name the services a custom entry will retain. A common mistake is: Calling a libc symbol from custom startup is safe because it links. Evidence: A dependency ledger follows every retained service to an initialization obligation or explicit exclusion. Develop that evidence in [PR-T10-02](#pr-t10-02).

<a id="t10-05"></a>

### T10.05 — Process termination

Returning from main lets the runtime choose process termination and cleanup; a raw Linux syscall follows kernel semantics. Thread exit and process-wide exit are distinct. A custom entry must not fall through into unknown bytes.

Investigate: Compare buffered output and handlers under hosted exit paths, then define a non-returning custom-entry finish path. A common mistake is: Every exit mechanism flushes streams and runs handlers. Evidence: The report distinguishes observed cleanup, declared syscall use and behavior of the impossible return path. Develop that evidence in [PR-T10-02](#pr-t10-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t10-06"></a>

### T10.06 — Syscall ABI

The x86-64 syscall convention changes the fourth argument register to r10 and destroys rcx/r11. Raw negative error values must be translated explicitly if a wrapper promises errno-style results.

Investigate: Map a six-argument synthetic call and check both success and negative-error decoding. A common mistake is: C-call register assignments can be reused unchanged for syscalls. Evidence: A register/clobber diagram and error table match the declared ABI, not an accidental successful run. Develop that evidence in [PR-T10-03](#pr-t10-03).

<a id="t10-07"></a>

### T10.07 — Minimal output and input

A byte operation reports progress, not a promise to transfer its full request. A wrapper must keep a cursor, recognize EOF and choose an operation-specific EINTR/would-block policy.

Investigate: Implement a write-all adapter and a bounded read loop over a scripted transfer backend. A common mistake is: Retrying every error from the beginning is safe. Evidence: Transferred bytes occur exactly once, and zero progress terminates visibly rather than spinning. Develop that evidence in [PR-T10-03](#pr-t10-03).

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

Dynamic, static and static-PIE images select different relocation and startup mechanisms. Minimality is a supported-service claim plus a dependency audit, not a competition for smallest file.

Adding parsing or formatting expands the dependency and failure surface. Keeping service layers separate makes each new effect observable.

### T10.10 — Startup failure diagnosis

Before-main faults often belong to entry alignment, relocations or omitted initialization, not application logic. An entry breakpoint and minimal image reduce the number of possible owners.

Investigate: Inject one malformed stack/alignment assumption into a controlled variant and repair it with a recorded trace. A common mistake is: A missing main breakpoint proves main itself is defective. Evidence: The minimized reproduction identifies the earliest violated startup contract and the corrected handoff. ## Reading guidance

The essential spine below is deliberately narrow. Assign only the exact inspected registry locators shown; no whole book, standard or implementation is implied. Historical rationale does not replace a current contract, and one implementation does not create a portable guarantee. Keep a short discrepancy log linking each source claim to the target/configuration where it applies.

- **System V Application Binary Interface: AMD64 Architecture Processor Supplement (Draft 0.99.6, 2 July 2012)** — `R-SYS-AMD64-ABI-0-99-6`, exactly **§3.4.1 Initial Stack and Register State — Stack State, pp. 28–30** (1 h). Decode argc, argument/environment pointer tables and auxiliary-vector boundaries. Compare the source claim with your project assumptions. The registry classifies this as supplement; its inspection limits remain part of the assignment.

- **GNU C Library startup source (glibc 2.41 release)** — `R-SYS-GLIBC-START-2-41`, exactly **sysdeps/x86_64/start.S — ENTRY (_start)** (1 h). Trace where the x86-64 startup stub transfers ownership to libc startup. Compare the source claim with your project assumptions. The registry classifies this as source; its inspection limits remain part of the assignment.

- **musl libc startup source (musl 1.2.5 release)** — `R-SYS-MUSL-START-1-2-5`, exactly **src/env/__libc_start_main.c — __init_libc and __libc_start_main** (1 h). Identify initialization and main/exit ownership in the musl startup path. Compare the source claim with your project assumptions. The registry classifies this as source; its inspection limits remain part of the assignment.

- **Linux ELF binary loader source (Linux v6.12 tag)** — `R-SYS-LINUX-ELF-6-12`, exactly **fs/binfmt_elf.c — create_elf_tables** (1 h). Inspect the kernel-side construction of entry metadata without treating it as C-call state. Compare the source claim with your project assumptions. The registry classifies this as source; its inspection limits remain part of the assignment.

See [guide-reading](#guide-reading) and [guide-standards](#guide-standards) for edition and evidence distinctions. Additional elective/API investigations require inspecting their precise version-specific passages before treating them as assigned authority.

## Implementation projects

Project hours combine implementation with the verification described in each contract. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation are budgeted separately; do not add project hours again to the module total.

- [PR-T10-01: Entry stack and startup ownership](#pr-t10-01) — 8 h; core.

- [PR-T10-02: Runtime initialization and exit choices](#pr-t10-02) — 8 h; core.

- [PR-T10-03: Raw syscall transfer adapter](#pr-t10-03) — 10 h; core.

- [PR-T10-04: Grow and debug a minimal image](#pr-t10-04) — 10 h; core.

## Mastery gate and feedback

Explain one positive path and one failure/counterexample for every subtopic without reading your implementation. Submit each project’s leaf-objective checklist with a distinct evidence item; shared runs may support several items only when the relation is explained. Re-run the saved independent fixture verifier, then reproduce at least one artifact from a clean environment. Passing those checks is evidence within their scope, not full-domain certification.

If an invariant, lifetime or environment claim cannot be defended, return to its project’s smallest trace and remediate the named entry knowledge. If a tool result disagrees with reasoning, minimize before changing expected results. A module passes when all core projects and awareness duties are accepted; elective implementation gaps remain visible. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) and [guide-audit](#guide-audit) for review records.

## Consolidation and transfer

After at least one day, reconstruct a selected contract and failing trace from memory, then apply one changed capacity/backend/target assumption. Explain which evidence survives and which must be regenerated. Transfer the dependency, ownership, representation or ordering ledger into the next project rather than copying an unexplained implementation. Record the delayed correction in the consolidation budget; see [guide-integrations](#guide-integrations) and [guide-workload](#guide-workload).

## Environment and limits

Use the declared Linux x86-64 environment for hosted observations and profile-specific adapters for portable components. Record compiler, linker, OS/library, architecture and configuration. Synthetic fixtures certify their declared static/reference calculations only. Unavailable target runs, unsupported instrumentation and hardware-dependent results are reported explicitly; emulator results do not prove STM32 electrical/peripheral behavior. No privileged host operation is required by a core project. See [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory), [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles) and [guide-inventory](#guide-inventory) before changing a boundary.

<a id="t17"></a>

# T17 — Numerical and data-oriented C

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cross-track | core | 61 | B, C |

**Prerequisites:** [T04](#t04), [T14](#t14).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | 28 | 15 | 6 | 4 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Build small numeric kernels whose units, finite representations and error contracts can be defended. The result is a reusable caller-storage kernel library, not an assumption that more floating-point digits guarantee a better model.

## Entry check and remediation

Without coding, convert 0.5 to Q7, multiply a 2x3 shape by a 3x2 shape, distinguish absolute from relative error at zero, and trace a three-value sum. Repair only the failed skill: binary scaling in T04, loop/index invariants in T14, or a one-page units/algebra exercise. For filters, practice geometric decay; for the elective ODE, review a derivative as rate and Euler as a tangent step. Neither calculus nor advanced linear algebra blocks the accumulation/fixed-point projects.

Use [guide-entry](#guide-entry) for the diagnostic policy and [guide-roadmap](#guide-roadmap) for route order. Only the stated prelude leaves must precede a dependent project.

## Component progression

**A numerical result with an error model.** State units, ranges, conditioning and rounding before choosing a layout. Compare residuals and convergence rather than treating one floating result as exact.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **A small residual masking a large forward error in an ill-conditioned problem.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t17-01"></a>

### T17.01 — Numerical problem formulation

Start with the quantity, not its C type. A sensor reading in millivolts and a normalized controller input are different domains even if both are doubles. For a reference value r, use absolute error near zero and relative error only where |r| is bounded away from zero. Write a units/domain/error ledger for the supplied accumulation cases. The misconception is that extra precision repairs an inaccurate physical model. Evidence is a separately justified model, representation and algorithm error allowance.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T17-01](#pr-t17-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t17-01-a"></a>


- **T17.01.a** State units, domains, tolerances, and conditioning assumptions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T17-01](#pr-t17-01).


<a id="t17-01-b"></a>


- **T17.01.b** Separate physical-model error from numerical and representation errors. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T17-01](#pr-t17-01).


<a id="t17-01-c"></a>


- **T17.01.c** Define independently checkable invariants and reference cases. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T17-01](#pr-t17-01).


<a id="t17-02"></a>

### T17.02 — Stable accumulation

Accumulation loses information when an addend is too small to change a rounded partial sum. With binary64 round-to-nearest, the ordered values 2^53, 1, -2^53 can produce zero although the exact sum is one. Pairwise grouping and compensation change the rounding history; neither removes poor conditioning. Implement three accumulators, permute inputs and compare to exact integer/rational references. Preserve the algorithm, order and compiler flags with each result rather than declaring one tolerance pass universally stable.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T17-01](#pr-t17-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t17-02-a"></a>


- **T17.02.a** Compare naive, pairwise, and compensated summation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T17-01](#pr-t17-01).


<a id="t17-02-b"></a>


- **T17.02.b** Test cancellation and changing accumulation order. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T17-01](#pr-t17-01).


<a id="t17-02-c"></a>


- **T17.02.c** Relate reproducibility requirements to parallel and vectorized implementations. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T17-01](#pr-t17-01).


<a id="t17-03"></a>

### T17.03 — Fixed-point kernels

Fixed point stores an integer q representing q/2^F. Multiplying two such values doubles the fractional-bit count, so widen before multiplication, round at the declared shift and saturate only after rounding. For Q7, 64 times 64 represents 0.25 and returns 32; a half-way negative result requires an explicit rule rather than a signed-shift guess. Implement a scaled multiply-accumulate with ties away from zero, test positive/negative saturation, and show that the intermediate bound fits the widened type.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T17-02](#pr-t17-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t17-03-a"></a>


- **T17.03.a** Implement scaled multiply-accumulate with explicit widening. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T17-02](#pr-t17-02).


<a id="t17-03-b"></a>

<a id="t17-03-c"></a>

<a id="t17-04"></a>

### T17.04 — Vector and matrix representations

A matrix interface needs rows, columns, stride, extent and overlap rules. Row-major address i*stride+j is valid only after dimensions and multiplication/addition bounds are checked. Multiply a 2x3 by a 3x2 matrix using a simple reference order, then add transposed and blocked traversals. A contiguous allocation does not imply stride equals the logical width. Evidence includes sentinel-preserving padded rows, rejected incompatible shapes and a dependency argument for any in-place operation.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T17-03](#pr-t17-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t17-04-a"></a>

<a id="t17-04-b"></a>


- **T17.04.b** Implement core vector operations and small matrix products. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T17-03](#pr-t17-03).


<a id="t17-04-c"></a>


- **T17.04.c** Compare row-major, transposed, and blocked traversal. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T17-03](#pr-t17-03).


<a id="t17-05"></a>

### T17.05 — Interpolation and approximation

Linear interpolation joins two neighboring samples: y0+(x-x0)*(y1-y0)/(x1-x0). Sorted distinct knots are a precondition; clamping, rejection and extrapolation are different APIs. Implement clamped lookup interpolation, then compare a sampled quadratic table with a degree-two polynomial on a dense grid. The misconception is that passing the knots bounds the error between them. Report the maximum observed error, its location, evaluation cost and the limited grid scope.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T17-04](#pr-t17-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t17-05-b"></a>

<a id="t17-05-c"></a>

<a id="t17-06"></a>

### T17.06 — Digital filters

A FIR output is a finite weighted history; an IIR also feeds prior outputs back into future state. For the teaching recurrence y[n]=0.5*x[n]+0.5*y[n-1], zero initial state and a unit step give 1-2^-(n+1). Implement caller-owned FIR and first-order IIR state with sample and block interfaces. Changing block size must not reset state. Test impulse/step responses, chunk equivalence and quantized coefficients; use |a|<1 only for this first-order pole, not as a general filter-stability rule.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T17-05](#pr-t17-05).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t17-06-b"></a>


- **T17.06.b** Specify state initialization, coefficient representation, and stability checks. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T17-05](#pr-t17-05).


<a id="t17-06-c"></a>


- **T17.06.c** Compare sample-wise and block-oriented interfaces. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T17-05](#pr-t17-05).


<a id="t17-07"></a>

### T17.07 — Linear systems and iterative methods

Gaussian elimination transforms equations but dividing by a tiny pivot magnifies perturbations. Partial pivoting chooses the largest available magnitude in a column; it is a strategy, not proof that a system is well-conditioned. Solve the supplied 2x2 systems, detect singular pivots with a scale-aware rule, and report residual ||Ax-b|| and a perturbed-input comparison. A small residual alone does not imply small solution error. Count arithmetic and bytes touched for your representation.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T17-06](#pr-t17-06).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t17-07-b"></a>


- **T17.07.b** Define convergence, failure, and ill-conditioning diagnostics. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T17-06](#pr-t17-06).


<a id="t17-07-c"></a>


- **T17.07.c** Compare mathematical operation counts with actual storage traffic. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T17-06](#pr-t17-06).


<a id="t17-08"></a>

### T17.08 — Signal transforms and simulation

**Elective extension.** The elective Euler experiment separates the differential model from its integrator. For y'=-y and step h, forward Euler gives y[k+1]=(1-h)y[k]; stability for this equation requires |1-h|<1, while accuracy still depends on h. Implement a finite-step solver with explicit initial/time units and compare step halving against exp(-t). An accurate implementation of an unsuitable model remains unsuitable. Preserve both convergence evidence and the model assumptions; do not require calculus fluency for the rest of T17.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T17-07](#pr-t17-07).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t17-08-b"></a>


- **T17.08.b** Validate scaling, normalization, conservation, or convergence properties. **Disposition:** elective. **Activity:** [PR-T17-07](#pr-t17-07).


<a id="t17-08-c"></a>


- **T17.08.c** Separate mathematical model validation from implementation validation. **Disposition:** elective. **Activity:** [PR-T17-07](#pr-t17-07).


<a id="t17-09"></a>

### T17.09 — Data-oriented representations

Array-of-structures interleaves fields; structure-of-arrays groups values used together. If a loop needs only x, interleaved cold labels enlarge its accessed footprint even when object count is unchanged. Implement both layouts for the matrix/vector workload and calculate useful versus touched bytes under a stated synthetic cache-line model. Alignment alone does not guarantee locality or speed. Evidence includes padding/stride diagrams, identical semantic outputs and separately observed timing on the selected host.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T17-03](#pr-t17-03).

### T17.10 — Reproducibility and reference testing

Reference testing needs a stronger independent computation, not the same loop at a different optimization level. Use rational/integer cases, analytic filter responses and a higher-precision hosted oracle; record rounding mode, contraction/fast-math settings and exceptional-input policy. Test reproducibility separately from accuracy: changed reduction order can be accurate yet bitwise different. Retain a distribution of errors and a failing-input replay, with explicit limits of the reference precision.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T17-01](#pr-t17-01).

## Reading guidance

Read the bounded selections before the corresponding project, then annotate one contract or assumption you will test. The assigned reading table is generated from the exact inspected locators. Spend the remaining reading budget on original teaching, worked traces and target documentation comparisons, not whole uninspected chapters.

**Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms — 4.1. Summation Methods (2 h):** Compare accumulation strategies.

**Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms — 4.3. Compensated Summation (1 h):** Understand compensation limits.

**What Every Computer Scientist Should Know About Floating-Point Arithmetic — Cancellation (1 h):** Separate conditioning from arithmetic error.

**Using the GNU Compiler Collection: Options That Control Optimization — -ffast-math (1 h):** Keep compiler numeric assumptions visible.

**Shared scope limit — Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms:** Text extraction damages equations. Exact bounds need visual inspection before formula-level teaching. Compensated summation does not guarantee small relative error for severely cancelling sums.

**Shared scope limit — What Every Computer Scientist Should Know About Floating-Point Arithmetic:** An edited historical reprint, not the current IEEE 754 specification or a guarantee about the selected compiler flags. Formula-heavy material needs original rendering when used quantitatively.

**Shared scope limit — Using the GNU Compiler Collection: Options That Control Optimization:** The reference version is deliberately fixed; installed compiler identity and target-dependent behavior require separate evidence. Enabling fast-math changes admissible numeric semantics and needs a documented error/exception contract.

See [guide-reading](#guide-reading) for access/provenance and [guide-standards](#guide-standards) for the language baseline.

## Implementation projects

- [PR-T17-01 — Accumulation and error ledger](#pr-t17-01), 7 h, core, profile B. Implement naive, pairwise and compensated binary64 accumulation over caller storage.

- [PR-T17-02 — Saturating Q7 multiply-accumulate](#pr-t17-02), 6 h, core, profile C. Implement Q7 multiplication with an explicitly widened intermediate, nearest rounding with ties away from zero, and final saturation to [-128,127].

- [PR-T17-03 — Strided matrix and layout kernel](#pr-t17-03), 7 h, core, profile C. Implement caller-storage small matrix multiplication with explicit dimensions/row strides and nonoverlap.

- [PR-T17-04 — Clamped interpolation and approximation](#pr-t17-04), 5 h, core, profile B. Implement piecewise-linear interpolation over strictly increasing knots with endpoint clamping.

- [PR-T17-05 — Streaming FIR and first-order IIR](#pr-t17-05), 8 h, core, profile C. Implement a three-tap FIR and a stable first-order IIR with caller-owned histories and chunk-invariant state.

- [PR-T17-06 — Pivoted 2x2 solver](#pr-t17-06), 6 h, core, profile B. Implement elimination with partial pivoting for a 2x2 linear system.

- [PR-T17-07 — Euler convergence experiment](#pr-t17-07), 4 h, elective, profile B. Electively implement forward Euler for y'=-y with exact step count and caller storage.

Project hours are the implementation plus verification budget, counted once. The optional-project-hour metadata identifies extensions included in this complete-module ledger; consult [guide-workload](#guide-workload) when selecting a core-only route.

## Mastery gate and feedback

Reimplement one numeric kernel from its contract, then explain a cancellation case and a rejected shape/range. Pass exact integer cases, stated numeric tolerances, ownership/dependency audits and perturbed-input analysis. If result error is acceptable but conditioning is unexplained, redo the reference/error ledger; if bounds fail, return to the indexing or widening derivation before optimizing.

For every linked objective, retain a separately labeled explanation, implementation/analysis artifact and check. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the rubric; one passing fixture does not establish all three objectives of a topic.

## Consolidation and transfer

After a delayed closed-book replay, change input scale, accumulation order and layout independently. Predict which exact values, error margins and costs should change before measuring. Explain one case where a numerically smaller error does not improve physical-model accuracy.
