<a id="t28-08"></a>

### T28.08 — I2C

I2C has bus phases and application meaning. For the bounded seven-bit write-then-single-byte-read, send address/write, register byte, repeated START and address/read; configure ACK off before clearing ADDR for the single-byte receive and request STOP after that event. Bound every wait and distinguish NACK, arbitration loss and timeout from retry policy. A timeout is not permission to force the bus while another master owns it. Preserve a phase trace and hardware SDA/SCL evidence when available.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T28-04](#pr-t28-04).

<a id="t28-09"></a>

### T28.09 — ADC and analog interfaces

An ADC result combines conversion settings with an analog source and reference. The bounded task uses one regular channel, explicit sample cycles, single conversion, trigger policy and a result/error record. For the documented twelve-bit path, conversion duration includes sampling plus twelve ADC cycles; that arithmetic excludes stabilization and analog settling. Derive an RC settling allowance from the supplied synthetic front-end, inspect the actual device/board electrical limits before wiring, and distinguish quantization from reference/source error. Simulated codes do not establish physical accuracy.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T28-05](#pr-t28-05).

<a id="t28-10"></a>

### T28.10 — DMA driver interface

A DMA API transfers ownership, not merely an address and count. Validate accessible SRAM, width/alignment and capacity, then move CPU-owned to device-owned until completion or confirmed cancellation. CCM on this F439 is CPU D-bus-only and cannot be treated as a generic DMA destination. Return partial completion and errors explicitly. Evidence includes rejected buffers, no reuse-before-stop interleavings, and final ownership/byte-count traces across polling, interrupt and DMA adapters.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T28-06](#pr-t28-06).

## Implementation projects

- [PR-T28-01 — Side-effect MMIO and GPIO](#pr-t28-01), 6 h, core, profile C. Implement a logged synthetic MMIO adapter with explicit W1C and consuming-read behavior, then a GPIO update/debounce service.

- [PR-T28-02 — Clock-aware bounded UART](#pr-t28-02), 8 h, core, profile E. Implement a clock-aware 8N1 polling UART adapter plus a capacity-two receive service with drop-newest/count policy.

- [PR-T28-03 — Timer and PWM configuration](#pr-t28-03), 6 h, core, profile E. Implement a validated timer configuration calculator and preload/update protocol for a known up-counting timer clock.

- [PR-T28-04 — Bounded SPI and one-byte I2C transaction](#pr-t28-04), 10 h, core, profile E. Implement an eight-bit full-duplex SPI transfer with GPIO CS and a seven-bit I2C write-register/repeated-start/single-byte-read adapter.

- [PR-T28-05 — Single-channel ADC acquisition](#pr-t28-05), 6 h, core, profile E. Implement one regular-channel single-conversion adapter with declared sampling/trigger/result policy.

- [PR-T28-06 — DMA buffer and portable service boundary](#pr-t28-06), 8 h, core, profile C. Implement a caller-storage DMA/service API with explicit CPU/device ownership, accessible-bank validation, width/alignment and partial-completion/cancellation outcomes.

- [PR-T28-07 — Elective Ethernet diagnostic service](#pr-t28-07), 6 h, elective, profile A. Implement a bounded application datagram above a declared Ethernet/IP/UDP adapter:16-bit big-endian sequence,16-bit payload length, then at most 32 payload bytes.

## Purpose and outcomes

Construct bounded communication protocols between foreground, interrupts and DMA. A correct queue or buffer lifecycle needs an ownership/order argument as well as observed latency.

## Entry check and remediation

Complete the selected T25 race, atomic-support and memory-order leaves below before projects. Draw a release/acquire publication and explain why volatile alone is insufficient; inspect target helper/lock-free support. Complete T27/T28 bring-up/driver contracts, then decode a basic frame and numeric priority. The full pthread, mutex and condition-variable laboratory route is not a prerequisite.

Use [guide-entry](#guide-entry) for the diagnostic policy and [guide-roadmap](#guide-roadmap) for route order. Only the stated prelude leaves must precede a dependent project.

## Component progression

**Interrupt and DMA ownership histories.** Follow CPU, ISR and device access rights through submit, completion, timeout and reset. State which memory masters can reach the region and which ordering operation is required.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **A late DMA completion touching storage already reused after an unconfirmed cancellation.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t29-01"></a>

### T29.01 — Exception entry and return

Exception entry saves an architectural frame before the handler's compiled prologue creates its own stack use. Decode the teaching eight-word basic frame as r0–r3, r12, lr, pc and xPSR, and inspect EXC_RETURN to decide which stack/frame variant applies. A backtrace that ignores an extended floating-point frame can read the wrong PC. Compare nested event/frame fixtures with an actual core trace and label which state hardware saved versus software preserved.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T29-01](#pr-t29-01).

<a id="t29-02"></a>

### T29.02 — Interrupt routing and priorities

Routing and priority must be reasoned about in the target's convention: lower numeric Cortex-M priority values mean higher urgency, and only implemented priority bits matter. Enable/pending/mask states are separate. Build a nesting timeline and inspect the FreeRTOS CM4F priority validation before selecting ISR APIs. Giving every interrupt priority zero defeats threshold masking assumptions. Evidence includes the configured grouping, implemented-bit readback and the ordered handler trace.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T29-01](#pr-t29-01).

<a id="t29-03"></a>

### T29.03 — ISR design

An ISR should acknowledge the hardware cause, capture bounded information and defer expensive work. A burst of interrupts can exhaust a queue even when each handler is short. Implement a handler that captures one event and increments a dropped-event counter when full, with formatting/processing in foreground. Reentrant callbacks or a printf in a handler can import hidden blocking and stack costs. Retain worst-path disassembly/call graph and a burst/overflow trace, with measured latency identified as measured.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T29-02](#pr-t29-02).

<a id="t29-04"></a>

### T29.04 — Critical sections

Critical sections protect a stated invariant against particular participants. Save and restore the prior interrupt-mask state; unconditionally enabling interrupts on exit breaks a caller's outer critical section. A BASEPRI threshold can leave higher-urgency interrupts active and does not stop DMA. Model nested masking and an interrupt update, then audit the target primitive and generated instructions. Evidence names which accesses are excluded, which remain possible and why the region is bounded.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T29-02](#pr-t29-02).

<a id="t29-05"></a>

### T29.05 — Shared foreground/ISR data

Foreground/ISR communication needs an ownership protocol and target-specific atomic support. Release publication followed by an acquiring observation is a useful hosted model, but embedded interrupt semantics and lock-free instruction/runtime behavior require the selected compiler/core contract. Check width/alignment and helper symbols before using atomics in an ISR. Volatile alone is not this argument. Draw the publication relation and test a deliberately premature publish that exposes uninitialized payload.

<a id="t29-06"></a>

### T29.06 — ISR-safe queues

For a one-producer/one-consumer queue, each context owns one index and publishes payload before exposing the new head. Use N slots with one deliberately unused slot, so usable capacity is N-1; choose drop-newest and count drops. Exercise wraparound and consumer pauses against a simpler sequence model. A modulo index equality cannot distinguish full from empty without a policy. Evidence includes no partially published elements, exact FIFO order and tested overflow behavior.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T29-03](#pr-t29-03).

<a id="t29-07"></a>

### T29.07 — DMA ownership

DMA and CPU are different participants: prepare data/descriptors, publish only when the device can see them, then withhold CPU reuse until device completion or confirmed stop. A cancellation request is not cancellation completion. Implement generation-tagged buffer ownership and inject completion after cancellation request. Evidence must demonstrate one terminal outcome per generation, preserved partial byte counts and no new transfer reusing a still-owned buffer.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T29-04](#pr-t29-04).

<a id="t29-08"></a>

### T29.08 — Ordering and coherency

Compiler ordering, CPU barriers, cache maintenance and mutual exclusion solve different problems. This selected F439 Cortex-M4 path has no CPU data cache to flush; that does not eliminate bus ordering or DMA-accessible-memory requirements. Compare its contract to a declared synthetic cache-equipped target without issuing fictitious cache operations on the F439. Evidence separates each visibility edge and documents barrier purpose; 'add DSB everywhere' is neither a protocol nor a performance argument.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T29-04](#pr-t29-04).

### T29.09 — Timestamp and event consistency

A multiword timestamp can tear if an interrupt updates one half between foreground reads. The fixture's hi-lo-hi method retries when high words differ; rollover interval bounds and event sequence numbers expose missed samples. Implement coherent snapshots and mark events whose relative order remains uncertain within the acquisition window. A stable number is not necessarily the exact physical event time. Retain counter-wrap, torn-read and missing-event traces with stated uncertainty.

ADC sampling/trigger/single conversion are inspected, but analog electrical accuracy and Stop/Standby recipes are not. Physical timings, package pins and device electrical conditions need DS/board evidence and measurement.

## Implementation projects

- [PR-T29-01 — Exception frame and nesting decoder](#pr-t29-01), 6 h, core, profile E. Implement an offline basic-frame/EXC_RETURN decoder and a target exception/nesting demonstration.

- [PR-T29-02 — Bounded ISR and nested masking](#pr-t29-02), 6 h, core, profile E. Implement a bounded acknowledge/capture/defer handler and a save/restore mask primitive.

- [PR-T29-03 — Foreground/ISR bounded queue](#pr-t29-03), 8 h, core, profile C. Implement an N-slot single-producer/single-consumer queue using N-1 usable slots and drop-newest accounting.

- [PR-T29-05 — Coherent time and delayed-service validation](#pr-t29-05), 6 h, core, profile E. Implement coherent multiword snapshots and event-sequence consistency, then validate delayed-service/cancellation races in a logical harness and physically scoped trace.

# T30 — Scheduling, timing, and constrained execution

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| bare-metal | core | 56 | C, E |

**Prerequisites:** [T20](#t20), [T21](#t21), [T29](#t29).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | 24 | 12 | 7 | 5 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Make scheduling, rollover, resources and supervision explicit in a constrained application. Preserve the difference between a mathematical task model, a logical trace and a measured physical response.

## Entry check and remediation

Derive unsigned elapsed time across one rollover and label release/start/finish on a trace. Repair only integer modular arithmetic or ceiling/utilization algebra before analysis. Verify T29's bounded ownership/priority argument, and understand one FSM/service interface from T20 before adding releases or preemption.

Use [guide-entry](#guide-entry) for the diagnostic policy and [guide-roadmap](#guide-roadmap) for route order. Only the stated prelude leaves must precede a dependent project.

## Component progression

**An execution budget with interference.** Separate algorithmic work, release jitter, blocking, interrupt interference and deadline. Compare a recurrence with measured traces under stated scheduling assumptions.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **A watchdog feed succeeding while a required task no longer makes useful progress.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t30-01"></a>

### T30.01 — Superloop design

A superloop is a scheduler even without a task API. Its longest non-yielding activity delays every later service. Calculate a service bound from ordered activities, then split a long parse/send into bounded slices and retain periodic releases separately from event work. Implement a tick-driven superloop with a quota per iteration. 'No threads' does not mean 'no starvation'. Evidence is a release/start/finish trace and a counterexample from the unsliced version.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T30-01](#pr-t30-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t30-01-a"></a>


- **T30.01.a** Bound each foreground activity and service interval. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-01](#pr-t30-01).


<a id="t30-01-b"></a>


- **T30.01.b** Separate periodic work from event-driven work. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-01](#pr-t30-01).


<a id="t30-01-c"></a>


- **T30.01.c** Identify starvation caused by long-running operations. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-01](#pr-t30-01).


<a id="t30-02"></a>

### T30.02 — Cooperative scheduling

Cooperative work progresses only where tasks explicitly return/yield. Use ready records with period, deadline and per-dispatch work quota; release jobs from elapsed ticks and prevent unbounded catch-up after overload. Implement fair round-robin among equal-priority runnable work and a declared drop/coalesce policy for stale releases. Fairness is not a deadline guarantee. Trace queue depth and release counts under the supplied overloaded input.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T30-01](#pr-t30-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t30-02-a"></a>


- **T30.02.a** Represent runnable tasks and explicit yield points. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-01](#pr-t30-01).


<a id="t30-02-b"></a>


- **T30.02.b** Implement timer-driven release and bounded work queues. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-01](#pr-t30-01).


<a id="t30-02-c"></a>


- **T30.02.c** Define fairness, priorities, and overload policy. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-01](#pr-t30-01).


<a id="t30-03"></a>

### T30.03 — Preemption and RTOS integration

An RTOS task boundary changes blocking, ownership and context assumptions; it does not automatically fix them. Read the selected CM4F port's PendSV/priority assertions and map which application operations may block. Implement a two-task producer/consumer integration using caller-owned bounded storage and the appropriate ISR API only where priority permits. The original scheduler implementation is assessed separately in T50; it is not required to pass this integration milestone. Evidence includes configuration, context/stack ledger and shutdown/error ownership paths.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T30-02](#pr-t30-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t30-03-a"></a>


- **T30.03.a** Map application ownership and blocking rules to RTOS services. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-02](#pr-t30-02).


<a id="t30-03-b"></a>


- **T30.03.b** Understand context switching before relying on task abstractions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-02](#pr-t30-02).


<a id="t30-03-c"></a>


- **T30.03.c** Treat writing a scheduler kernel as a separate elective project. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-02](#pr-t30-02).


<a id="t30-04"></a>

### T30.04 — Clock and deadline arithmetic

Unsigned counter subtraction gives elapsed time modulo 2^W; ordering absolute deadlines requires all compared distances to stay below half the range. With an eight-bit fixture, elapsed from 250 to 4 is ten ticks. Derive a future/due predicate without converting an out-of-range unsigned value to signed C. Implement explicit bound checks and test equality, wrap and half-range ambiguity. The misconception is that ordinary numeric less-than preserves time order across rollover.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T30-03](#pr-t30-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t30-04-a"></a>


- **T30.04.a** Select time units and a monotonic counter representation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-03](#pr-t30-03).


<a id="t30-04-b"></a>


- **T30.04.b** Prove rollover-safe comparison under explicit interval bounds. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-03](#pr-t30-03).


<a id="t30-04-c"></a>


- **T30.04.c** Distinguish elapsed intervals from absolute timestamps. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-03](#pr-t30-03).


<a id="t30-05"></a>

### T30.05 — Latency and jitter

Release latency is start minus release; execution is finish minus start; response is finish minus release; jitter concerns variation around a stated reference. The fixture has response equal to latency plus execution, which makes inconsistent logs detectable. Instrument these separately, budget interrupt/queueing interference and report distributions. A maximum from a finite test is an observed maximum, not a proved upper bound. Include timer resolution and trace disturbance in the result.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T30-03](#pr-t30-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t30-05-a"></a>


- **T30.05.a** Define release latency, execution time, response time, and jitter. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-03](#pr-t30-03).


<a id="t30-05-b"></a>


- **T30.05.b** Budget interrupt interference and queueing delays. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-03](#pr-t30-03).


<a id="t30-05-c"></a>


- **T30.05.c** Measure distributions without labeling observed maxima as proven bounds. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-03](#pr-t30-03).


<a id="t30-06"></a>

### T30.06 — Scheduling analysis

Under fixed priorities, response-time iteration includes own cost, blocking and higher-priority interference: R=C+B+sum(ceil(R/Tj)*Cj). State independent periodic-task and deadline assumptions before using it. Compute the supplied model by hand and with an independent checker; explain why its result ceases to apply when a service can block without bound. Utilization alone cannot certify every task set. Evidence names each assumption and one deliberately violated scenario.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T30-04](#pr-t30-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t30-06-a"></a>


- **T30.06.a** Derive utilization and response-time checks for stated task models. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-04](#pr-t30-04).


<a id="t30-06-b"></a>


- **T30.06.b** Identify blocking and priority-inversion contributions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-04](#pr-t30-04).


<a id="t30-06-c"></a>


- **T30.06.c** Document assumptions violated by asynchronous hardware or unbounded services. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-04](#pr-t30-04).


<a id="t30-07"></a>

### T30.07 — Memory and resource budgets

A resource budget is a worst-path composition, not the sum of observed averages. Reserve queue storage, persistent state, task stacks and nested interrupt frames, plus alignment and runtime helpers. Implement an admission check that fails before publishing a job whose budget cannot fit. A watermark only describes exercised paths. Evidence includes symbolic maximum depth and tested exhaustion behavior, with opaque library costs reported as unknown rather than zero.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T30-02](#pr-t30-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t30-07-a"></a>


- **T30.07.a** Bound queue capacity, stack depth, and persistent storage. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-02](#pr-t30-02).


<a id="t30-07-b"></a>


- **T30.07.b** Include interrupt nesting and library/runtime contributions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-02](#pr-t30-02).


<a id="t30-07-c"></a>


- **T30.07.c** Define predictable behavior on exhaustion. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-02](#pr-t30-02).


<a id="t30-08"></a>

### T30.08 — Watchdogs and progress

A watchdog should witness meaningful progress, not a timer callback that keeps running while the application is stuck. Require every supervised task to advance its epoch before feeding once per window; missing progress leads to a bounded fault/recovery decision. The F439 IWDG has its own low-speed clock, whose variation matters to timeout selection. Inject a hung task and a repeatedly failing reboot. Evidence demonstrates withheld refresh and a finite recovery limit, not an exact timeout from simulation.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T30-05](#pr-t30-05).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t30-08-a"></a>


- **T30.08.a** Define meaningful progress conditions rather than periodic blind refresh. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-05](#pr-t30-05).


<a id="t30-08-b"></a>


- **T30.08.b** Coordinate supervision across tasks and execution contexts. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-05](#pr-t30-05).


<a id="t30-08-c"></a>


- **T30.08.c** Test hangs, overload, and recovery loops. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-05](#pr-t30-05).


<a id="t30-09"></a>

### T30.09 — Low-power execution

Sleep entry has a lost-event window if the foreground tests 'no work' and then sleeps after an interrupt publishes work. Treat pending work, wake source and entry instruction as one architecture-specific protocol; use the inspected sleep rules, not a generic C lock. Build a logical interleaving counterexample and an actual board sleep/wake trial. Clock restoration and Stop/Standby are separate unassigned extensions. Energy claims require measured voltage/current and timing on the real setup.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T30-05](#pr-t30-05).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t30-09-a"></a>


- **T30.09.a** Design sleep entry and wakeup without lost-event windows. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-05](#pr-t30-05).


<a id="t30-09-b"></a>


- **T30.09.b** Account for clock restoration and peripheral state. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-05](#pr-t30-05).


<a id="t30-09-c"></a>


- **T30.09.c** Measure energy and timing on actual hardware when making physical claims. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T30-05](#pr-t30-05).


<a id="t30-10"></a>

### T30.10 — Real-time evidence

Real-time evidence combines a cost model, generated-code inspection and bounded measurements. Record optimization settings, task priorities, timer frequency and uncertainty with each trace; inspect helper calls on the critical path. Compare analytical model bounds, observed maxima and requirements in separate columns. The misconception is that a long successful run proves WCET. The mastery artifact must state exactly which requirement is supported and which environmental interference remains unbounded.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T30-04](#pr-t30-04).

# T31 — Embedded debugging, fault handling, and deployment

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| bare-metal | core | 55 | E |

**Prerequisites:** [T27](#t27), [T28](#t28), [T29](#t29).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |

| 7 | 24 | 12 | 7 | 5 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Diagnose a bare-metal failure from image identity through machine state, then preserve deployment and recovery evidence. A useful crash record should make a causal claim checkable with matching symbols.

## Entry check and remediation

Read an ELF/map/vector address, identify a basic exception frame and explain UART/DMA ownership. Repair those selected T27–T29 mechanisms first. Establish probe/server/board identities from the laboratory guide rather than guessing a target configuration.

Use [guide-entry](#guide-entry) for the diagnostic policy and [guide-roadmap](#guide-roadmap) for route order. Only the stated prelude leaves must precede a dependent project.

## Component progression

**An image-bound fault record.** Decode the captured frame against the exact map and build. Bound trace overhead and retained records; reproduce startup and deployment failures with a known recovery image.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **A debugger session changing timing or reset state enough to conceal the original defect.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t31-01"></a>

### T31.01 — Debug connection

Debug connection depends on probe firmware, physical SWD/reset wiring, target identity and server configuration before it depends on application C. Record these separately and progress from device-ID read to halt/reset to programming. A flash failure and an application reset loop demand different diagnosis. Capture exact tool versions and commands from the laboratory setup; never infer that a generic Cortex-M4 configuration selects F439 Flash. Evidence is a classified connection log and repeatable reset strategy.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T31-01](#pr-t31-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t31-01-a"></a>


- **T31.01.a** Configure SWD/JTAG, reset strategy, and supported debug server. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T31-01](#pr-t31-01).


<a id="t31-01-b"></a>


- **T31.01.b** Distinguish connection, flash, reset, and application failures. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T31-01](#pr-t31-01).


<a id="t31-01-c"></a>


- **T31.01.c** Record probe firmware and target/debug configuration. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T31-01](#pr-t31-01).


<a id="t31-02"></a>

### T31.02 — Source and machine debugging

Optimized machine code can combine, move or remove source operations, so source stepping is a hypothesis aid rather than a source-order trace. Inspect registers, instruction addresses and memory for one simple numerical/driver routine at debug and release optimization. Hardware breakpoints/watchpoints have finite supported resources. Evidence links the actual ELF to disassembly and explains one optimized-out local; disabling all optimization is not the final diagnosis.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T31-01](#pr-t31-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t31-02-a"></a>


- **T31.02.a** Correlate source, disassembly, registers, and memory. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T31-01](#pr-t31-01).


<a id="t31-02-b"></a>


- **T31.02.b** Use hardware breakpoints and watchpoints within target limits. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T31-01](#pr-t31-01).


<a id="t31-02-c"></a>


- **T31.02.c** Diagnose optimized-out variables and misleading source stepping. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T31-01](#pr-t31-01).


<a id="t31-03"></a>

### T31.03 — Fault decoding

A fault report needs fault status, saved frame interpretation and the offending instruction/address. Decode synthetic CFSR bits before trying a target injection, then capture the core's applicable status registers and EXC_RETURN in a minimal handler. Avoid printing through a failing peripheral or using a corrupt stack in recovery. A secondary handler fault can obscure the first. Evidence distinguishes captured valid fields, unavailable fields and the causal access reconstructed from the matching ELF.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T31-02](#pr-t31-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t31-03-a"></a>


- **T31.03.a** Read exception status and saved execution context. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T31-02](#pr-t31-02).


<a id="t31-03-b"></a>


- **T31.03.b** Reconstruct the failing instruction and access. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T31-02](#pr-t31-02).


<a id="t31-03-c"></a>


- **T31.03.c** Separate primary faults from secondary faults in the handler. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T31-02](#pr-t31-02).


<a id="t31-04"></a>

### T31.04 — Stack integrity

Stack corruption may arise from overflow, misalignment, bad returns or nested handlers. Reserve a region, establish ABI alignment and use canary/watermark observations alongside a static depth budget; use guards/MPU only if verified supported/configured. The fixture shows a valid watermark coexisting with a possible unexercised deeper call. Evidence includes a controlled overwrite detection and a quantified tested high-water mark without labeling it a universal bound.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T31-02](#pr-t31-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t31-04-a"></a>


- **T31.04.a** Detect overflow, bad alignment, corrupted returns, and nested-handler growth. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T31-02](#pr-t31-02).


<a id="t31-04-b"></a>


- **T31.04.b** Compare canaries, watermarks, guards, and MPU protection where supported. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T31-02](#pr-t31-02).


<a id="t31-04-c"></a>


- **T31.04.c** Avoid treating one observed watermark as a universal bound. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T31-02](#pr-t31-02).


<a id="t31-05"></a>

### T31.05 — Peripheral and bus faults

A peripheral that stays silent may have the wrong clock, mode, pin route or sequencing even when software reads plausible values. Inject one synthetic configuration defect at a time and classify status versus external-signal expectations. For USART, TXE alone does not establish final wire completion; for SPI, paired receive handling matters. Evidence ties an ordered register trace to a board signal capture where available. Do not 'fix' a bus by changing unrelated timeouts together.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T31-03](#pr-t31-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t31-05-a"></a>


- **T31.05.a** Debug wrong clocks, wrong modes, and erroneous register sequencing. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T31-03](#pr-t31-03).


<a id="t31-05-b"></a>


- **T31.05.b** Use device documentation to interpret status and error flags. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T31-03](#pr-t31-03).


<a id="t31-05-c"></a>


- **T31.05.c** Correlate software access with observable external signals. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T31-03](#pr-t31-03).


<a id="t31-06"></a>

### T31.06 — DMA and concurrency diagnosis

DMA diagnosis starts with ownership epochs and memory placement. Trace submit, enable, partial progress, complete, cancel request and confirmed stop, then locate a stale-buffer or premature-reuse defect. Debugger halts may stop a core while peripherals continue, changing the interleaving. Evidence includes reproducible logical schedules and a target run with the probe's freeze policy recorded; a debugger-only success cannot settle a physical race.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T31-03](#pr-t31-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t31-06-a"></a>


- **T31.06.a** Trace buffer ownership and completion events. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T31-03](#pr-t31-03).


<a id="t31-06-b"></a>


- **T31.06.b** Reproduce stale data, premature reuse, and missing coherency operations. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T31-03](#pr-t31-03).


<a id="t31-06-c"></a>


- **T31.06.c** Account for debugger effects on timing and peripheral progress. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T31-03](#pr-t31-03).


<a id="t31-07"></a>

### T31.07 — Trace and timing tools

Trace has capacity, timestamps and a cost. Design fixed-size records with sequence numbers and a drop counter, then correlate samples against a known counter frequency. Use a verified target cycle counter only after recording enable/configuration/wrap rules; do not assume every emulator models it. Evidence measures tracing-on versus tracing-off disturbance and accounts for missing records. The trace itself must not block the critical path it measures.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T31-04](#pr-t31-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t31-07-a"></a>


- **T31.07.a** Use cycle counters and trace facilities verified for the exact target. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T31-04](#pr-t31-04).


<a id="t31-07-b"></a>


- **T31.07.b** Design bounded trace output and timestamp correlation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T31-04](#pr-t31-04).


<a id="t31-07-c"></a>


- **T31.07.c** Quantify measurement disturbance and missing-event behavior. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T31-04](#pr-t31-04).


<a id="t31-08"></a>

### T31.08 — Image deployment

Deployment identifies the bytes, address map and matching symbols before flashing. Produce a release manifest with image hash, vector address, sizes, compiler/link settings, ELF and map identity; verify programmed bytes where the selected probe supports it. Repeat standalone power-on operation. A file named release.bin is not evidence of the deployed image. Keep the synthetic fixture's offset checks separate from actual target flash verification.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T31-04](#pr-t31-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t31-09"></a>

### T31.09 — Boot and update interfaces

An update protocol needs image length/version/address compatibility and an interruption policy before transfer of control. Use two logical slots with a commit marker written last; a partially written candidate must leave the previous committed image selectable. The checksum fixture detects accidental corruption but supplies no authenticity. Evidence includes every power-loss boundary and the stack/vector/interrupt responsibilities at handoff; do not implement a security-sensitive production bootloader from this small exercise.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T31-05](#pr-t31-05).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t31-09-b"></a>


- **T31.09.b** Model interrupted update and invalid-image cases. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T31-05](#pr-t31-05).


<a id="t31-09-c"></a>


- **T31.09.c** Separate integrity checking from cryptographic authenticity. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T31-05](#pr-t31-05).


<a id="t31-10"></a>

### T31.10 — Fault injection and recovery

Fault injection tests containment, not just detection. Corrupt a retained record, freeze progress, return a timeout and inject an invalid adapter response in isolated trials. Preserve a bounded crash record and stop after the declared recovery count, keeping outputs in the specified safe state. A reboot that repeats the hazardous action is not recovery. Evidence records the initial fault, detection latency where measured, recovery transition and residual consequences.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T31-05](#pr-t31-05).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t31-10-b"></a>

## Reading guidance

Read the bounded selections before the corresponding project, then annotate one contract or assumption you will test. The assigned reading table is generated from the exact inspected locators. Spend the remaining reading budget on original teaching, worked traces and target documentation comparisons, not whole uninspected chapters.

**Cortex-M4 Devices Generic User Guide — 2.4.2 Fault escalation and hard faults (1 h):** Separate primary and escalated faults.

**Cortex-M4 Devices Generic User Guide — 2.4.3 Fault status registers and fault address registers (1 h):** Plan valid captured fields.

**STM32F427/437 and STM32F429/439 device errata — Applicability (1 h):** Scope silicon limitations.

**STM32 Nucleo-144 boards (MB1137) — 6.9 USART communication (1 h):** Check board diagnostic routing.

**Shared scope limit — Cortex-M4 Devices Generic User Guide:** Generic core document; optional features and device integration require ST evidence. Publication year is not inferred from copyright or identifier. Read barrier instruction definitions before using the overview as a complete ordering specification.

**Shared scope limit — STM32F427/437 and STM32F429/439 device errata:** An erratum applies only under its listed conditions and revision applicability. No physical board revision was read. DSB and dummy-read remedies must not be generalized to unrelated devices.

**Shared scope limit — STM32 Nucleo-144 boards (MB1137):** Inspected Rev 8, not current Rev 11. Board revision, actual solder bridges and clock population must be recorded on physical hardware; described defaults are not a measurement of the learner's board.

See [guide-reading](#guide-reading) for access/provenance and [guide-standards](#guide-standards) for the language baseline.

## Implementation projects

- [PR-T31-01 — Debug connection and optimized-state notebook](#pr-t31-01), 6 h, core, profile E. Create a repeatable probe/server/reset connection notebook, then correlate one routine's source, instructions, registers and memory in debug/release builds.

- [PR-T31-02 — Fault and stack capture](#pr-t31-02), 8 h, core, profile E. Implement a bounded crash record and offline decoder for declared fault masks/basic-frame fields, then inject one controlled target fault.

- [PR-T31-03 — Peripheral/DMA diagnosis](#pr-t31-03), 6 h, core, profile E. Implement a deterministic defect-injection harness for one selected peripheral and its DMA ownership; reproduce and classify wrong-clock, premature reuse and stale-generation outcomes.

- [PR-T31-04 — Bounded trace and release deployment](#pr-t31-04), 8 h, core, profile E. Implement fixed-size sequence-numbered trace records and a release-image manifest, then program/verify the identified image and run standalone power-on.

- [PR-T31-05 — Interrupted update and bounded recovery](#pr-t31-05), 8 h, core, profile E. Implement a logical two-slot image/update model with commit-last and compatible-version selection, plus bounded recovery/crash-record handling.

Project hours are the implementation plus verification budget, counted once. The optional-project-hour metadata identifies extensions included in this complete-module ledger; consult [guide-workload](#guide-workload) when selecting a core-only route.

## Mastery gate and feedback

Decode a controlled fault with matching ELF, diagnose one bus/ownership defect, audit a deployed release and demonstrate bounded recovery. A physical release gate includes standalone power-on and programmed-byte verification where supported. If a handler obscures the first fault, shrink the handler before adding diagnostics.

For every linked objective, retain a separately labeled explanation, implementation/analysis artifact and check. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the rubric; one passing fixture does not establish all three objectives of a topic.

## Consolidation and transfer

Investigate the same defect in optimized firmware, then with tracing enabled/disabled. Predict debugger and trace disturbance, preserve artifact identities and explain any unreproduced physical consequence.

## Environment and limits

Use [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles) to declare the dependency boundary, [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory) for installed tools and hardware, and [guide-audit](#guide-audit) for image/call-graph evidence. Fixtures are original deterministic mathematical or synthetic-protocol data. Run `python tools/verify_embedded_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to recompute their expectations. This oracle checks fixtures, not learner code.

Host adapters establish only their declared state-machine semantics. QEMU mps2-an386 establishes its Arm FPGA machine behavior; it does not implement STM32F439 registers. Physical-board completion requires the exact board/revision/pin/clock evidence. RM0090 Rev 21 and UM1974 Rev 8 are the inspected revisions; newer portal revisions require delta review before adopting changed procedures. No simulated timing or analog result is a physical measurement.

Use [guide-inventory](#guide-inventory) to find supplied data and [guide-integrations](#guide-integrations) for later cross-module work.

# T33 — Formal reasoning and verification

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |

| cross-track | core | 63 | B, C |

**Prerequisites:** [T03](#t03), [T04](#t04), [T14](#t14), [T18](#t18), [T32](#t32).

## Purpose and outcomes

State properties precisely and connect them to concrete C semantics, bounded environments and reported verifier obligations. A proof artifact must make its assumptions and skipped/unproved goals visible.

## Entry check and remediation

Derive a prefix-sum invariant, trace one bounded pointer extent and distinguish mathematical versus unsigned/signed C arithmetic. Repair T03/T04/T14 reasoning selectively. Review T32 independent-oracle and reproducibility work before installing the selected CBMC/Frama-C/solver environment.

Use [guide-entry](#guide-entry) for the diagnostic policy and [guide-roadmap](#guide-roadmap) for route order. Only the stated prelude leaves must precede a dependent project.

## Component progression

**A bounded proof with visible assumptions.** Translate the C arithmetic and environment into the verifier's model. Preserve counterexamples, unwinding checks, unproved obligations and assumptions as separate outputs.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **An overstrong precondition or insufficient unwinding bound making a false claim appear verified.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t33-01"></a>

### T33.01 — Specifications and invariants

A specification relates concrete state to mathematical meaning. For a bounded prefix sum, require a valid extent, define the accepted integer range and state which bytes may change. Safety, functional result and eventual termination are separate properties. Write pre/postconditions and an abstraction mapping for the fixture before choosing a verifier. The misconception is that a precise English return-value sentence also specifies lifetime, ownership and side effects.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T33-01](#pr-t33-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t33-01-a"></a>


- **T33.01.a** Express preconditions, postconditions, and representation invariants precisely. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-01](#pr-t33-01).


<a id="t33-01-b"></a>


- **T33.01.b** Separate safety, functional correctness, and liveness properties. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-01](#pr-t33-01).


<a id="t33-01-c"></a>


- **T33.01.c** Match mathematical state to concrete C representations. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-01](#pr-t33-01).


<a id="t33-02"></a>

### T33.02 — Loop reasoning

A useful loop invariant carries what is already processed and what remains valid. For summing n elements, i<=n and accumulator=sum of elements before i support the exit result; an overflow bound must also be preserved. Prove initialization, one iteration and exit, then give n-i as the termination variant. Testing all small n is not an inductive proof for arbitrary n. Evidence is a proof outline plus a broken-invariant counterexample.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T33-01](#pr-t33-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t33-02-a"></a>


- **T33.02.a** Derive invariants strong enough to establish postconditions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-01](#pr-t33-01).


<a id="t33-02-b"></a>


- **T33.02.b** Prove initialization, preservation, and exit consequences. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-01](#pr-t33-01).


<a id="t33-02-c"></a>


- **T33.02.c** State termination variants and resource bounds. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-01](#pr-t33-01).


<a id="t33-03"></a>

### T33.03 — Arithmetic and memory models

Mathematical integers do not wrap, while unsigned C arithmetic is modular and signed overflow is not a valid arithmetic step. Pointer validity also needs extent, lifetime and aliasing assumptions. Compare the fixture's unbounded result with an explicitly eight-bit modular result, then write the stronger precondition needed for equality. Evidence includes the promoted intermediate type and every memory bound; silently replacing C expressions with ideal arithmetic proves a different program.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T33-02](#pr-t33-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t33-03-a"></a>

<a id="t33-03-b"></a>


- **T33.03.b** Distinguish mathematical abstractions from executable C semantics. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-02](#pr-t33-02).


<a id="t33-03-c"></a>


- **T33.03.c** Prevent proofs from silently assuming away implementation defects. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-02](#pr-t33-02).


<a id="t33-04"></a>

### T33.04 — Contracts and annotations

Annotations belong to the API: requires describe caller obligations, ensures describe results and assigns describe the frame. ACSL's logical integers need explicit connections to machine values. Annotate a caller-storage prefix-sum or maximum routine and test that its documented failure behavior matches the contract. An omitted frame condition can leave a functional proof compatible with unwanted writes. Evidence includes a side-effect counterexample and repaired frame.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T33-02](#pr-t33-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t33-05"></a>

### T33.05 — Bounded model checking

A bounded model checker explores a finite encoding of input, loops and environment. Build a CBMC harness with nondeterministic n/data under the public contract, assert the result/bounds, and require unwinding assertions. The loop guard may need one more unwinding evaluation than body iterations. A too-small bound can hide a reachable defect. Preserve successful obligations, failed counterexamples, tool defaults and an intentionally insufficient-bound run.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T33-03](#pr-t33-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t33-06"></a>

### T33.06 — Deductive verification

Deductive proof generates obligations under contracts and models. With WP, inspect initialization/preservation/postcondition and runtime-error goals separately, including selected arithmetic and memory models. Start with a small integer routine whose range fits; do not use the Real model to claim C floating-point correctness. Evidence lists proved, assumed, unproved and unsupported obligations. 'No reported failures' is inadequate if goals were skipped or a precondition excluded every call.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T33-04](#pr-t33-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t33-06-b"></a>

<a id="t33-07"></a>

### T33.07 — Abstract interpretation

Abstract interpretation computes an over-approximation of reachable values. An interval containing zero can warn about division even if a richer relation would rule zero out. Inspect an Eva alarm, justify an invariant or partition, and rerun without suppressing actual behavior. Evidence separates a real defect from an imprecision alarm and records soundness/context assumptions. Sequential Eva does not directly establish asynchronous interrupt correctness.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T33-05](#pr-t33-05).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t33-08"></a>

### T33.08 — Environment models

An environment model determines what the proof can see. If an adapter always returns full success, the harness cannot prove cleanup after partial progress, invalid counts or allocation failure. Make nondeterministic outcomes range over the real documented contract, with explicit exclusion of unsupported asynchronous hardware. Evidence includes one counterexample admitted only after repairing an overly helpful stub. More assumptions can make a proof easier while making its claim weaker.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T33-03](#pr-t33-03).

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t33-09"></a>

### T33.09 — Concurrency reasoning

**Elective extension.** The elective finite queue model can test abstract linearization and FIFO histories under a declared sequentially consistent event model. Enumerate interleavings while preserving each participant's order and identify publication/removal points. This is not proof that a C acquire/release implementation realizes the abstract history, nor that an interrupt/compiler extension has ISO-thread semantics. Evidence includes accepted/rejected histories and a separate memory-order argument with its unsupported cases disclosed.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T33-06](#pr-t33-06).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t33-10"></a>

### T33.10 — Evidence composition

Compose evidence by property: a proof may establish bounds under preconditions, instrumentation may find exercised lifetime defects, tests may establish vectors, and a scope may measure a physical pulse. Maintain a claim/assumption/artifact table with trusted compiler, runtime, solver and hardware entries. Do not add coverage percentages to proof percentages. The final argument states which properties are unproved and which counterexamples would invalidate the environment model.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T33-05](#pr-t33-05).

## Reading guidance

Read the bounded selections before the corresponding project, then annotate one contract or assumption you will test. The assigned reading table is generated from the exact inspected locators. Spend the remaining reading budget on original teaching, worked traces and target documentation comparisons, not whole uninspected chapters.

**An Axiomatic Basis for Computer Programming — 3.1. Axiom of Assignment (1 h):** Connect state transformations to contracts.

**CBMC training: What is loop unwinding? — Loop unwinding assertions (1 h):** Expose bounded completeness.

**ANSI/ISO C Specification Language — 2.2.4 Integer arithmetic and machine integers (1 h):** Connect logical and C arithmetic.

**WP Plug-in Manual — 1.2 Tutorial (1 h):** Generate selected obligations.

**WP Plug-in Manual — 1.6 Limitations & Roadmap (1 h):** Report unsupported cases.

**The Eva plug-in — 2.1 Introduction (1 h):** Interpret value approximation.

**The Eva plug-in — 5.4.5 Applications relying on software interrupts (1 h):** Keep interrupt scope honest.

**Shared scope limit — An Axiomatic Basis for Computer Programming:** A small illustrative language and historical formalism, not modern C semantics. Signed overflow, aliasing, memory safety and termination need current C/tool evidence. Remaining paper pages were not visually inspected.

**Shared scope limit — CBMC training: What is loop unwinding?:** Training examples do not select a release or prove a hardware environment. Pin tool version, check defaults and report assumptions, reachability and every unwinding result. The old CPROVER manual routes returned navigation only.

**Shared scope limit — ANSI/ISO C Specification Language:** Logical arithmetic has no machine overflow by default. Language expressiveness does not imply every clause is supported by each plug-in; WP limitations must accompany assignments.

**Shared scope limit — WP Plug-in Manual:** Proof is conditional on contracts, runtime-error obligations and models. Tutorial reports skipped unaligned-pointer/function-pointer guards. The Real Model explicitly does not establish C/IEEE floating-point correctness. Selected passages only; no solver execution.

**Shared scope limit — The Eva plug-in:** False alarms can result from approximation. Soundness is relative to the specified context and supported semantics. Current manual states asynchronous interrupts are not directly modeled; do not claim full firmware proof from sequential analysis.

See [guide-reading](#guide-reading) for access/provenance and [guide-standards](#guide-standards) for the language baseline.

## Implementation projects

- [PR-T33-01 — Prefix invariant and termination](#pr-t33-01), 6 h, core, profile C. Specify and implement a bounded prefix sum for at most 4valuesin[0,10], caller-provided extent and unchanged output on invalid input.

- [PR-T33-02 — Machine arithmetic and ACSL frame](#pr-t33-02), 6 h, core, profile C. Annotate one small caller-storage routine with pre/post/frame conditions and explicit logical-to-machine arithmetic.

- [PR-T33-03 — CBMC harness and demanding environment](#pr-t33-03), 8 h, core, profile C. Build a CBMC harness for the bounded prefix routine and an adapter with partial/zero/error/invalid progress outcomes.

- [PR-T33-04 — WP obligations and explicit assumptions](#pr-t33-04), 8 h, core, profile C. Use Frama-C WP on a small integer routine with a finite admitted range, explicit memory/frame contracts and runtime-error obligations.

- [PR-T33-05 — Eva precision and composed claims](#pr-t33-05), 6 h, core, profile C. Analyze a bounded routine with Eva, classify real versus imprecision alarms and compose property-specific proof/test/measurement evidence.

- [PR-T33-06 — Elective finite publication model](#pr-t33-06), 6 h, elective, profile C. Enumerate a two-event producer/two-event consumer under a declared sequentially consistent event model.

Project hours are the implementation plus verification budget, counted once. The optional-project-hour metadata identifies extensions included in this complete-module ledger; consult [guide-workload](#guide-workload) when selecting a core-only route.

## Mastery gate and feedback

Present one successful small CBMC claim with complete unwinding checks and one WP/Eva analysis with explicit runtime/model assumptions. Preserve a real counterexample and an unproved/imprecise obligation. If success required an unjustified assumption, repair the harness rather than announcing verification.

For every linked objective, retain a separately labeled explanation, implementation/analysis artifact and check. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the rubric; one passing fixture does not establish all three objectives of a topic.

## Consolidation and transfer

Revisit the routine with changed bounds, aliasing or partial-I/O behavior. Predict which obligations/models must change and retain one failing case that exposes an overly helpful environment stub.

## Environment and limits

Use [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles) to declare the dependency boundary, [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory) for installed tools and hardware, and [guide-audit](#guide-audit) for image/call-graph evidence. Fixtures are original deterministic mathematical or synthetic-protocol data. Run `python tools/verify_embedded_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to recompute their expectations. This oracle checks fixtures, not learner code.

Record host/tool/ISA identities and all mathematical/environment assumptions. Instrumented timings are not production timings; numerical references have stated domains; proof results hold only for reported obligations/models.

Use [guide-inventory](#guide-inventory) to find supplied data and [guide-integrations](#guide-integrations) for later cross-module work.

# T34 — Optimization, vectorization, and measurement

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cross-track | core | 71 | A, B, C, E |

**Prerequisites:** [T08](#t08), [T17](#t17), [T32](#t32).

## Purpose and outcomes

Optimize one verified kernel by forming cost hypotheses, inspecting generated code and measuring representative work. Preserve exact/approximate semantic contracts while changing layout, vectorization and build strategy.

## Entry check and remediation

Pass T17's independent-reference/error checks and T32's reproducible test habit. Draw nonoverlapping array extents and a publication/race argument using the selected T25 leaves; the full pthread route is unnecessary for the scalar/SIMD kernel. Repair only ratio/units, stride arithmetic or sampling/distribution vocabulary before measurements.

Use [guide-entry](#guide-entry) for the diagnostic policy and [guide-roadmap](#guide-roadmap) for route order. Only the stated prelude leaves must precede a dependent project.

## Component progression

**Optimization after a fixed correctness gate.** Measure the workload before transforming layout, branches, alias information or vector code. Compare generated code and consumed results under matched builds.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **An apparently faster kernel whose observable work was optimized away or whose input contract changed.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t34-01"></a>

### T34.01 — Optimization specification

Optimization starts with a contract: representative sizes/data, allowed numeric error, latency/throughput targets and memory/energy limits. Reuse the scalar correctness oracle before changing code. A faster result on one favorable input can fail the deployed workload or its error allowance. Define pass/fail gates independently of timing and include both tiny and large cases. Evidence is a workload ledger whose correctness gates cannot be relaxed to rescue a speed claim.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T34-01](#pr-t34-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t34-01-a"></a>


- **T34.01.a** Define workload, latency, throughput, memory, and energy objectives. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-01](#pr-t34-01).


<a id="t34-01-b"></a>


- **T34.01.b** Preserve correctness and numerical constraints as acceptance gates. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-01](#pr-t34-01).


<a id="t34-01-c"></a>


- **T34.01.c** Select representative inputs rather than only favorable microbenchmarks. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-01](#pr-t34-01).


<a id="t34-02"></a>

### T34.02 — Cost models

Work, instruction count and memory traffic are different cost models. A vector add has about one arithmetic operation per element but reads two arrays and writes one; define the measured boundary before calculating bytes or intensity. Use a simple roofline-style ceiling to form a bottleneck hypothesis, then revise it using actual evidence. A theoretical ceiling is not a measured rate or a Cortex-M WCET bound. Preserve the model and its counterexample.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T34-01](#pr-t34-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t34-02-a"></a>

<a id="t34-02-b"></a>


- **T34.02.b** Identify compute-bound, bandwidth-bound, and latency-bound regions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-01](#pr-t34-01).


<a id="t34-02-c"></a>


- **T34.02.c** Use measurements to revise initial bottleneck hypotheses. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-01](#pr-t34-01).


<a id="t34-03"></a>

### T34.03 — Memory hierarchy

Stride and working set determine which memory hierarchy is stressed. A blocked traversal can reuse a tile, while a transposed or hot/cold layout changes touched bytes without changing the algorithmic result. Implement variants of the T17 matrix/data kernel and calculate a declared synthetic cache-line footprint. Real TLB/cache observations require actual host counters and sizes. Alignment alone does not guarantee a gain; evidence includes semantic equality and generated access patterns.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T34-02](#pr-t34-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t34-03-b"></a>


- **T34.03.b** Compare data layout, blocking, and hot/cold field separation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-02](#pr-t34-02).


<a id="t34-03-c"></a>


- **T34.03.c** Account for alignment without assuming alignment alone improves speed. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-02](#pr-t34-02).


<a id="t34-04"></a>

### T34.04 — Control and instruction effects

Branches, dependencies and code size trade against one another. A branchless selection may execute extra work or extend a dependence chain, while an unrolled loop may increase instruction-cache pressure and spills. Compare branchy and branchless bounded clamp/count kernels under predictable and mixed inputs. 'Fewer branches' is not an acceptance criterion. Evidence links measured distributions to disassembly, including spills/code bytes and a workload where the anticipated gain disappears.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T34-02](#pr-t34-02).

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

### T34.05 — Compiler optimization evidence

Compiler reports are explanations to check against final code. Compile the scalar loop at fixed settings, retain vectorization diagnostics, inspect intermediate/final instructions and identify one justified missed optimization. If aliasing prevents transformation, inspect the interface before adding restrict. A report that says vectorized does not establish correctness or actual speed. Evidence preserves flags, object identity, report text and the corresponding machine-code loop.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T34-03](#pr-t34-03).

<a id="t34-06"></a>

### T34.06 — Auto-vectorization

Auto-vectorization can change iteration order, reduction grouping and alias assumptions. Permit restrict only for demonstrably nonoverlapping extents; a forbidden overlap must be rejected by the API or excluded explicitly, not accidentally benchmarked. Use unsigned elementwise arithmetic for the initial kernel to avoid floating-reduction ambiguity, then revisit a sum under its numeric tolerance. Evidence includes alias/tail cases, scalar comparison and a valid contract supporting each hint.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T34-03](#pr-t34-03).

<a id="t34-07"></a>

### T34.07 — Explicit SIMD

Explicit SIMD works on lanes with an extent contract. The core x86 teaching kernel uses SSE2 four-lane uint32 addition modulo 2^32, unaligned full-vector loads/stores, and a scalar tail. For nine elements, process two groups of four and one tail; an unaligned load still needs sixteen valid bytes. Implement a scalar fallback and forbid partial overlap. Evidence includes wrap values, lengths 0–9, offset alignments and final instructions on a verified supported host.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T34-04](#pr-t34-04).

<a id="t34-08"></a>

### T34.08 — ISA dispatch

Dispatch must not execute specialized instructions while checking whether they are supported. Put the baseline selector and SSE2 implementation in separate translation units with recorded flags; use the documented positive/zero feature result and a force-scalar test option. On the selected x86-64 Linux environment also record applicable OS/ABI support. AVX dispatch is an unassigned extension requiring OS-state checks. Evidence is selector tests, baseline disassembly and a specialized path that is unreachable under the unsupported-feature fixture.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T34-04](#pr-t34-04).

### T34.09 — Benchmark construction

A benchmark must retain its result, exclude unrelated setup and state how warmup/cache state/affinity/clock changes are handled. Record repeated samples and report median plus spread; preserve raw samples rather than a single rounded speedup. The supplied times are synthetic oracle data, not measurements. Implement a harness with a consumed checksum and paired baseline/variant runs. Evidence includes empty-loop overhead and one source of uncertainty the setup cannot eliminate.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T34-05](#pr-t34-05).

<a id="t34-10"></a>

### T34.10 — Profiling and counters

Sampling and counters estimate where cost occurs under their own limits. Correlate hot addresses with matching code; record counter availability, multiplexing scale and permission failures. A scaled event count is not exact when workloads change during multiplexing. Use sampling plus one supported counter when available, otherwise report the missing evidence and rely on a narrower timing claim. Evidence includes raw enabled/running times, scaling arithmetic and a revised bottleneck hypothesis.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T34-05](#pr-t34-05).

<a id="t34-11"></a>

### T34.11 — Whole-program optimization

LTO and PGO alter whole-program decisions and introduce build/profile assumptions. Compare plain, LTO and representative-profile builds, inspect code/dependencies and retest the correctness gate. A training workload biased toward one branch may regress a different input distribution. Evidence includes build cost, executable size, profile identity/mismatch diagnostics and a held-out workload. A flag alone does not prove the linker performed the intended transformation.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T34-06](#pr-t34-06).

### T34.12 — Embedded optimization

Embedded optimization trades latency, Flash, RAM/stack and energy; the fastest version can be unacceptable in another budget. Deploy two semantically equivalent variants only after the target startup/dependency audit, measure actual execution and optionally current with recorded equipment, and keep error limits fixed. Emulator cycle counts do not establish F439 physical energy or WCET. Evidence distinguishes measured speed/size/stack from inferred models and retains regression thresholds with configuration.

Read the bounded selections before the corresponding project, then annotate one contract or assumption you will test. The assigned reading table is generated from the exact inspected locators. **Using the GNU Compiler Collection: Options That Control Optimization — -O2 (1 h):** Compare fixed optimization settings.

**Using the GNU Compiler Collection: Options That Control Optimization — -fstrict-aliasing (1 h):** Audit optimization preconditions.

**Clang SSE2 intrinsic header, selected definitions — _mm_add_epi32 (1 h):** Select modulo lane semantics.

**Clang SSE2 intrinsic header, selected definitions — _mm_loadu_si128 (1 h):** Respect full-vector extent.

**GCC x86 built-in CPU detection contract — __builtin_cpu_supports (1 h):** Build positive/zero feature dispatch.

**Using the GNU Compiler Collection: Options That Control Optimization — -flto (1 h):** Inspect whole-program compile/link behavior.

**GCC program instrumentation options, selected verification and hardening contracts — -fprofile-generate (1 h):** Collect a representative training profile.

**Using the GNU Compiler Collection: Options That Control Optimization — -fprofile-use (1 h):** Reject mismatched profiles.

**Shared scope limit — Roofline: An Insightful Visual Performance Model for Multicore Architectures:** Original examples are multicore floating-point kernels with DRAM traffic. It is a reasoning model, not a universal prediction or proof of Cortex-M4 latency, WCET or energy. State the measured memory boundary and ceilings.

**Shared scope limit — Using the GNU Compiler Collection: Options That Control Optimization:** The reference version is deliberately fixed; installed compiler identity and target-dependent behavior require separate evidence. Enabling fast-math changes admissible numeric semantics and needs a documented error/exception contract.

**Shared scope limit — Clang SSE2 intrinsic header, selected definitions:** These functions specify four-lane modulo integer addition and full 16-byte unaligned access; unaligned access still requires the complete valid extent. Intrinsic header/source version is fixed, installed compiler is not verified. No other intrinsic or ISA dispatch mechanism was inspected.

**Shared scope limit — GCC x86 built-in CPU detection contract:** Does not verify installed GCC internals or OS support for arbitrary AVX state. Teaching core specialization uses SSE2 on an identified supported x86 host; AVX/ifunc expansion requires additional OS-state and loader research.

**Shared scope limit — GCC program instrumentation options, selected verification and hardening contracts:** Selected options only, not every instrumentation feature. Flag availability and effective dependencies vary with installed compiler/target. GNU/Linux hardening aggregate is not a bare-metal recipe; instrumentation changes resource/timing behavior.

See [guide-reading](#guide-reading) for access/provenance and [guide-standards](#guide-standards) for the language baseline.

## Implementation projects

- [PR-T34-01 — Workload gate and traffic hypothesis](#pr-t34-01), 6 h, core, profile B. Specify and implement a scalar uint32 vector-add reference with representative sizes, modulo results and immutable correctness limits.

- [PR-T34-02 — Layout and branch experiment](#pr-t34-02), 8 h, core, profile B. Implement layout/traversal and branch-based/branchless variants of one bounded clamp/data kernel.

- [PR-T34-03 — Auto-vectorization and alias evidence](#pr-t34-03), 8 h, core, profile C. Implement unsigned elementwise addition with a documented nonoverlap contract and compare scalar/compiler-vectorized builds.

- [PR-T34-04 — SSE2 kernel and safe dispatch](#pr-t34-04), 8 h, core, profile A. Implement four-lane SSE2 uint32 modulo addition with full16-byte unaligned loads/stores and scalar tail/fallback.

- [PR-T34-05 — Benchmark, sampling and counter record](#pr-t34-05), 8 h, core, profile A. Implement a paired repeated benchmark with consumed results and separate setup.

- [PR-T34-06 — Whole-program and embedded trade-off](#pr-t34-06), 8 h, core, profile E. Compare hosted plain/LTO/PGO builds, then separately audit uninstrumented Profile E firmware against Flash, stack and latency budgets.

Present a correct scalar/auto/SIMD kernel, safe dispatch, generated-code explanation and reproducible benchmark/counter evidence. Show a held-out workload and a rejected faster-but-invalid budget variant. Embedded physical completion needs an actual target comparison; observed maxima remain measured values.

For every linked objective, retain a separately labeled explanation, implementation/analysis artifact and check. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the rubric; one passing fixture does not establish all three objectives of a topic.

Change size distribution, alignment, compiler version and profile-training data independently. Predict invalidated assumptions and keep correctness thresholds fixed. Retain a performance regression whose cause was a mistaken cost hypothesis.

This oracle checks fixtures, not learner code.
