<a id="t38-10"></a>

### T38.10 — Classic CAN framing, arbitration and error confinement

Classic CAN combines an identifier/content-oriented frame with nondestructive bitwise arbitration. Dominant 0 overrides recessive 1. A transmitter that releases 1 but observes 0 during arbitration becomes a receiver; losing arbitration is not a transmission corruption. For a shared 11-bit base identifier, a standard data frame's dominant RTR defeats a standard remote frame and an extended frame's recessive SRR. A standard remote frame and an extended frame proceed to the format distinction, where standard IDE is dominant. Sorting complete numeric 11/29-bit IDs without these bits gives the wrong argument.

Classic data payloads are 0–8 bytes in the declared lab subset. The actual standard's DLC values 9–15 can represent 8 bytes; the local strict encoder rejects those values deliberately, without calling them universally invalid CAN. The classic CRC covers destuffed SOF through data, while dynamic stuffing spans the selected encoded region and the CRC delimiter/ACK/EOF have separate fixed-form boundaries. A receiver's link ACK acknowledges valid reception, not application consumption or identity-based delivery.

Build a bounded standard-data codec and arbitration analyzer, then interpret supplied retry/error-state traces. Error-active, error-passive and bus-off constrain participation differently; do not turn a handful of fixtures into a complete fault-confinement implementation. The misconception is that no application listener means no ACK, or that every arbitration loser must send an error flag. Evidence includes mixed-format arbitration, CRC/stuff-boundary reasoning, ACK/application separation and a stated limit on unsupported error/recovery states.

Apply and verify this mechanism in [PR-T38-09](#pr-t38-09).

<a id="t38-11"></a>

### T38.11 — F439 bxCAN timing, filters, mailboxes and receive ownership

bxCAN handles classic frame timing/arbitration autonomously, while software manages finite mailboxes, filter banks and receive FIFO ownership. An identifier is content used for acceptance, not a destination address. A mask filter compares `(id & mask)` with `(filter_id & mask)`;0x120 with 0x7F0 accepts 0x123 and 0x12F but rejects 0x130. Configure a filter bank while deactivated, then expose only the selected identifier/format contract.

Timing registers encode values minus one. For a 42 MHz APB clock, prescaler 6 and 1+11+2 time quanta give 500 kbit/s. The sample point is 12/14=6/7 of the bit; BRP, TS1, TS2 and SJW fields are 5,10,1,0 for SJW1. This arithmetic does not prove the real cable/transceiver/oscillator tolerances. Check legal segment ranges and measure the physical result separately. Use the inspected ISO edge rule rather than the suspicious Rev 21 direction sentence.

The two three-entry receive FIFOs have distinct full policies. In the declared sequence 10,20,30,40, locked mode retains 10,20,30 and discards 40; unlocked mode overwrites the last entry, leaving 10,20,40. Release a consumed FIFO entry exactly once, and inspect mailbox status for success, arbitration loss or transmit error before returning ownership. Implement one TX mailbox, one acceptance rule and FIFO0 first. The misconception is that a pending request is completion or that FIFO full means the oldest entry is always overwritten. Evidence includes both modeled policies, timing/encoding checks and one documented classic two-node exchange.

Apply and verify this mechanism in [PR-T38-09](#pr-t38-09).

<a id="t38-12"></a>

### T38.12 — CAN FD ISO format, dual bitrate and external-controller boundary

CAN FD changes more than the maximum payload. The DLC map is 0–8 bytes for codes 0–8, then 12,16,20,24,32,48,64. Code 9 therefore does not mean nine bytes. FDF identifies FD format, BRS permits a separate data-phase bitrate, and ESI exposes error-state information. FD has data frames rather than classic remote frames. The selected ISO format uses 17-bit CRC through 16 bytes and 21-bit CRC for longer payloads, with protected stuff count and fixed CRC-field stuffing; a pre-ISO frame description is not interchangeable.

Propagation and transmitter loop delay impose timing constraints even when software can calculate two divisors. The controller performs the selected CRC/stuffing and transmitter-delay-compensation mechanisms. This project implements metadata/DLC and capability validation, not a whole conformant bit-level FD engine. Preserve that boundary in the evidence ledger.

F439's bxCAN lacks FD. A compatible external SPI controller can add the frame engine; the inspected TCAN4550 also integrates a transceiver, but its VSUP6–24 V supply is separate from VIO3.135–5.25 V. Its SPI transactions use 32-bit units and held select, and MRAM initialization has explicit ECC/data obligations. Model that boundary and reject an FD request directed to bxCAN even when the connected transceiver advertises FD. The misconception is that a larger byte array or faster transceiver is enough. Evidence includes every DLC transition, remote/length/capability/power failures and a conditional physical route requiring a separately inspected exact setup.

Apply and verify this mechanism in [PR-T38-10](#pr-t38-10).

## Reading guidance

Read just the exact assigned locator for the upcoming milestone and build a small responsibility/timing table. Previous T28 fundamentals are reused. Inspect device truth/operating tables together with the actual selected circuit; record every maximum that depends on supply/load/enable mode. The ISO held standard is a bounded normative oracle with licensed access, while the Bosch explanation and TI design guides have their narrower purposes. Do not assign whole manual chapters or infer all-mode conformance from these passages. All source identities and access limitations are in [guide-reading](#guide-reading); retain current-versus-historical distinctions and the primary corrections to rejected textbook descriptions.

The physical FD continuation reuses T38.12 in [PR-T38-11](#pr-t38-11) and [PR-T38-12](#pr-t38-12). Consult [guide-physical-evidence](#guide-physical-evidence) for the completion contract.

## Implementation projects

Work in the stated order, reusing one prepared target image and portable test harness. Projects 3/4/10 study portable profile C components; target adapters/images have their own E dependency receipts. Physical milestones reuse already-established startup and interface hardware, so the project budget covers bounded mechanisms and verification. Total 80 project hours reconcile to 52 implementation plus 28 verification, without being added again to the module total.

- [PR-T38-02](#pr-t38-02): Synchronous USART clock and sampling laboratory (6 hours; profile E).

- [PR-T38-03](#pr-t38-03): I2C pull-up and wired-AND investigation (6 hours; profile C).

## Mastery gate and feedback

Use an independent evaluator or the delayed blind checks in [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment). Given a fresh waveform and clock, decode framing and locate the first failed contract; distinguish I2C NACK/loss/stretch, SPI sampling/ownership, RS-232 polarity, RS-422 topology, RS-485 driver turnaround and CAN arbitration/capability. Run your code against new capacity, rounding, simultaneous-prefix and cancellation cases, then explain the mechanism without reading the implementation. Every linked objective needs its own evidence, including source-analysis objectives. A software pass, target observation and physical receipt close different claims. FD core mastery is the implemented metadata/capability boundary; physical FD is required in edition 2 through PR-T38-11 and PR-T38-12. Completion of metadata tests alone leaves the FD physical gate open.

## Consolidation and transfer

After a delay, reconstruct one UART divisor, one I2C pull-up interval, one SPI edge diagram and one CAN arbitration comparison. Change a clock, capacitance, target mode or driver-enable state and predict the first contract requiring revision. Bind the unchanged `rs485_byte_channel_v1` to T40 framing, separating record semantics from electrical timing. Preserve failed prefixes and explain why the fix changes the correct layer.

## Environment and limits

Exact baseline is the declared F439 board/clock/package route plus source-backed external interfaces, fixed storage and bounded operations. Generic Cortex-M/QEMU behavior does not replace board/wire evidence. F439 bxCAN is classic-only and its MAC requires an external PHY; neither larger buffers nor a different transceiver supplies a missing controller. Required external FD has separately budgeted bring-up and physical exchange milestones. No complete TIA/ISO-CAN, electrical, automotive or safety conformance claim follows from these laboratories. See [guide-standards](#guide-standards), [guide-inventory](#guide-inventory) and [guide-workload](#guide-workload) for common audit and accounting rules.

# T39 — Ethernet, OSI and MCU frame-channel foundations

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| bare-metal | core | 96 | C, E |

**Prerequisites:** [T04](#t04), [T18](#t18), [T27](#t27), [T28](#t28), [T29](#t29), [T31](#t31), [T38](#t38).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 18 | 42 | 24 | 7 | 5 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Connect physical Ethernet and OSI responsibilities to a checked MCU frame channel. Derive actual frame/buffer boundaries, PHY management and DMA ownership before the finite Internet implementation in T41. The portable mechanisms use profile C and caller storage; target adapters/images use the prepared E route. This is a core foundation beyond the older optional T28 network-awareness exercise.

## Entry check and remediation

This route follows completed core prerequisites, including T38 architecture/communication timing and the T27/T28/T29/T31 target, MMIO, interrupt and ownership work. Diagnose byte-order/unaligned parsing, checked address ranges, bounded state machines and exactly-once token release. Use targeted prior remediation for a failed item. Before physical milestones, verify matching board/PHY/revision/clock/pins, prepared cable/peer and instrument capability. Incomplete equipment permits synthetic progress but leaves the physical receipt open. Use [guide-entry](#guide-entry) and [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory).

## Component progression

**Ethernet frames with owned descriptors.** Trace PHY readiness, MAC framing and DMA ownership independently. Validate every length and descriptor transition before exposing a frame to upper layers.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **A link reset followed by completion from an earlier descriptor incarnation.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t39-01"></a>

### T39.01 — OSI services, peer protocols and Internet layer mapping

A layer provides a service to its local user and follows a protocol with its peer. These are different relationships. An application can call a local send service without knowing a remote implementation's function names; the peer still must understand the transmitted PDU. A service data unit becomes payload inside a protocol data unit, which becomes the next lower service's input. In the original fixture,12 application bytes plus 8 transport,20 network and 14 link header bytes produce 20,40,54-byte PDUs. Those invented wrappers illustrate encapsulation; they are not a claim that the trace is valid UDP/IP/Ethernet.

OSI organizes responsibilities into seven conceptual layers. Physical moves signals/bits; data link supplies local frame/link functions; network deals with network paths; transport supplies end-to-end transport services. Session/dialogue and representation tasks may live inside an Internet application's libraries rather than as separate wire protocols. L2 bridges also relay frames, so saying that every kind of forwarding is IP routing is too broad. Likewise, a local socket call is a service interface above substantial work already performed by the OS, not a complete implementation of those lower layers.

Build a responsibility table and an original peer/service trace, then test matching and mismatching interfaces. The misconception is that equal layer numbers guarantee compatible protocols, or that seven OSI layers demand seven C libraries. Evidence includes the SDU/PDU boundaries, actual peer agreement, local service shape and a mapping of the later finite MCU Internet endpoint to the conceptual purposes.

Apply and verify this mechanism in [PR-T39-01](#pr-t39-01).

<a id="t39-02"></a>

### T39.02 — Ethernet physical media and PHY responsibilities

The F439 Ethernet block includes MAC and DMA, but the external PHY handles the selected media/signaling boundary. In a 100BASE-TX copper route, show MAC→RMII→PHY→magnetics→connector→cable→peer rather than drawing the MCU GPIO directly into the cable. The IEEE layer diagram separates reconciliation/xMII, coding and physical-medium functions; our assignment uses only the declared 10/100 foundation. Detailed PHY coding/analog internals and modern multi-gigabit modes are outside this scope.

RMII supplies two data bits on a shared 50 MHz reference clock, corresponding to 100Mbit/s at the digital interface. A10Mbit/s link still has the required reference-clock contract; link operation is not inferred by counting CPU loops. Preamble, framing, FCS, negotiation and application throughput occur at different boundaries. A byte copied into a DMA buffer does not prove that the PHY has established a link or that the cable peer received the frame.

Shared half-duplex Ethernet has collision/deference behavior; the selected switched full-duplex baseline uses independent directional links without that collision algorithm. A100 m media example in a historical workshop is not a guarantee for an arbitrary cable, board layout or connector. Record the exact PHY, board revision, clock source and prepared media. The misconception is that a MAC peripheral, virtual NIC or emulator supplies physical evidence. Evidence needs actual clock/link/cable observations and a declared topology; this prepares the frame and PHY-management milestones without hiding a full board bring-up campaign.

Apply and verify this mechanism in [PR-T39-02](#pr-t39-02).

<a id="t39-03"></a>

### T39.03 — Ethernet frame, padding, FCS and buffer boundaries

An untagged basic Ethernet frame begins with destination and source 6-byte addresses, then a 2-byte length/type field, payload/padding and 4-byte FCS. Preamble 7 bytes plus SFD1 byte precede the frame and are outside our frame buffer. A minimum frame is 14+46+4=64 bytes from destination through FCS. A3-byte payload needs 43 pad bytes. A basic 1500-byte payload gives 1518 bytes including FCS. The interpacket gap is timing, equivalent to 12 byte times for the declared basic accounting; it is not another 12 bytes to place in the buffer.

The length/type boundary is also a parsing rule. Values≤1500 are lengths, values≥1536 are types, and the intervening range is excluded by this local parser. VLAN-tagged frames are valid Ethernet but deliberately unsupported here. For a length interpretation, application data length differs from padding; for an EtherType packet, the upper protocol must determine its own true packet length. Do not pass Ethernet padding blindly into an HTTP parser.

FCS covers destination through padding, excluding preamble/SFD and FCS itself. The original arithmetic fixture declares reflected CRC32 parameters and checks an independent recurrence against zlib; the RFC appendix is an algorithm source, not normative Ethernet conformance. The physical MAC may generate/strip CRC or padding according to configuration. Build a checked parser/builder and record the exact driver buffer policy. The misconception is that every capture includes FCS or that 64 bytes means 64 application bytes. Evidence includes minimum/maximum/gap/tagged cases and a capture-point ledger.

Apply and verify this mechanism in [PR-T39-02](#pr-t39-02).

<a id="t39-04"></a>

### T39.04 — MAC addressing, filtering and switching boundaries

MAC address bits are interpreted in the first octet: I/G is its least-significant bit and U/L the next bit. Thus 02:00:00:00:00:01 is local individual,01:00:5E:00:00:01 is a group address, and all-FF is broadcast. Byte representation is not the same as the LSB-first order in which each octet is sent. A locally administered address must still be unique on the selected link; a source address, destination MAC, IP endpoint and CAN content identifier are different namespaces.

A small learning bridge learns the ingress port of each individual source, then uses the destination to choose forwarding. Unknown unicast and group/broadcast traffic flood the selected other ports. Known unicast goes to the learned port; if it is the ingress port, no forwarding is needed. Our fixture's 10-tick expiry is a declared educational policy, not a universal bridge standard. Expire entries before each lookup and refresh a valid source observation. A port is not an IP route, and learning source addresses does not establish an endpoint's IP identity.

Implement a three-port/four-entry table and an endpoint address classifier. Keep loops, spanning tree and VLAN outside this model rather than accidentally promising a production switch. The misconception is that promiscuous mode on one switched port exposes every network packet, or that the first bit printed in a hexadecimal octet is I/G. Evidence includes known/unknown/group forwarding, same-port filtering, expiry and the exact endpoint receive-filter/capture-point assumptions.

Apply and verify this mechanism in [PR-T39-03](#pr-t39-03).

<a id="t39-05"></a>

### T39.05 — MII/RMII, MDIO and PHY link negotiation

RMII data signals and MDIO/MDC management solve different problems. RMII moves the MAC's digital frame stream with a shared 50 MHz clock. SMI/MDIO addresses one PHY register at a time; MDC is limited to the inspected 2.5 MHz maximum with its own pulse/period conditions. At HCLK168 MHz, RM0090's CR100 selects divide 102, yielding about 1.647 MHz MDC. For PHY address 0/register 2, a read-start word is 0x91: address 0, register 2 shifted 6, CR4 shifted 2, MW0 and MB1. First check MB0 and never rewrite address/data while an access is busy; read data become valid only after MB clears.

PHY status has temporal semantics. LAN8742A register 1 link bit 2 is read-only/latch-low: two reads separate accumulated history from the current observation. A first 0x20 then 0x24 means historical link-low and current link-high with autonegotiation complete. It does not promise the link will remain up afterward. ID registers must match 0x0007 and masked 0xC130; silicon revision is the low nibble. Register 31 done bit 12 plus speed bits 4:2 code 110 describes 100/full; code 010 is 100/half. The selected route rejects half duplex rather than silently programming full duplex.

Implement bounded identity/status/negotiation queries and configure MAC mode only from an accepted current result. The misconception is that one old link bit or configured PHY preference proves negotiated speed. Evidence includes identity masking, latched/current reads, incomplete/unsupported results, actual RMII/MDC clocks and a pin/clock/bridge ledger tied to the inspected board revision.

Apply and verify this mechanism in [PR-T39-04](#pr-t39-04).

<a id="t39-06"></a>

### T39.06 — F439 MAC/DMA initialization and reachable memory

DMA accesses memory as a different bus master. A C pointer valid for the CPU is insufficient: F439 Ethernet DMA cannot reach CPU-only CCM. In the selected SRAM range,0x20000100 plus 64 bytes is reachable;0x10000100 is not. A region starting 0x2002FFF0 with 32 bytes crosses the declared end and fails even though its first address is in SRAM. The fixture additionally requires 4-byte alignment as a local descriptor/buffer policy; do not generalize that local policy into every silicon transfer-width requirement.

Initialization has dependencies, not just a list of writes. Set MII/RMII selection under Ethernet reset or before enabling its clocks. The selected recipe asserts reset, chooses RMII, enables the required clocks, completes reset, prepares descriptors/buffers, installs bases and accepted PHY speed/duplex, then starts the separately controlled MAC/DMA engines. A reset that fails to finish is an explicit bounded error, not permission to keep writing the rest of the recipe. Distinguish peripheral reset, DMA software reset and later reset/recovery ownership.

Publish ordinary descriptor/buffer stores before giving ownership to DMA, and use the declared compiler plus hardware ordering contract. Volatile MMIO alone does not order all ordinary memory or make shared ownership atomic. This Cortex-M4 route does not need an invented M7 data-cache cleaning sequence. Build a dependency checker and reachable-memory validator, then bind the minimal existing board image. The misconception is that correct descriptor values imply a correct sequence or that a DMB makes unreachable memory reachable. Evidence includes first violated dependency, address-end checks and actual map/order observations.

Apply and verify this mechanism in [PR-T39-05](#pr-t39-05).

<a id="t39-07"></a>

### T39.07 — Ethernet receive descriptors, validation and recycling

A receive descriptor is a handoff record. OWN1 means DMA owns it; CPU must not interpret unfinished status or recycle that buffer. After OWN clears, FS and LS identify frame boundaries, the final descriptor's FL is meaningful under its stated validity conditions, and ES/DE report errors/truncation. With CSTF=APCS=0 in the selected MAC configuration, retain FCS and validate FL before exposing FL−4 bytes beginning at destination address. FL64 therefore exposes 60 bytes, not 64 and not 56. Padding still remains for the upper protocol to interpret.

For a bounded chain, require its first FS and last LS, all descriptors returned, no error summary/descriptor error, and length 64..1518 within actual combined capacity. Partial chains, errors and oversized values must not yield a pointer/length pair to the consumer. The original fixture's two-descriptor frame uses only the last descriptor's length. A consumer borrowing accepted storage prevents recycling; returning a token once permits it. A second release or stale generation is an ownership error even when the address looks valid.

Implement a small validator and the `ethernet_frame_channel_v1` receive contract in PR-T39-06. A full receive ring can suspend DMA; backpressure must become a counted result or a declared drop, not silent overwrite of consumer-owned data. The misconception is that OWN clearing alone proves a usable frame or that every capture/driver has the same FCS policy. Evidence includes first failed validation, retained/recycled ownership, incomplete-chain handling and an actual descriptor/wire correlation when closing the target route.

Apply and verify this mechanism in [PR-T39-06](#pr-t39-06).

<a id="t39-08"></a>

### T39.08 — Ethernet transmit descriptors, completion and recovery

Transmit begins with CPU ownership of the buffer and descriptors, not with a wire delivery promise. Prepare byte counts, buffer addresses, FS/LS and the selected padding/CRC policy before publishing. With a multi-descriptor frame, prepare all descriptors and give the tail its ownership before publishing the first descriptor's OWN; otherwise DMA can consume an incomplete chain. An ordering barrier and compiler contract cover the publication point. A queued request or OWN1 means in flight, not completion.

The normal path is CPU-prepared→DMA-owned→completed→reusable. The fixture deliberately publishes a head before its tail and reuses a buffer before completion; both fail. An error completion can return local ownership if the descriptor/DMA state establishes it, but does not mean the peer accepted the frame. Reset returns ownership only after the engine is confirmed stopped; stale completion from the previous generation must not complete the next request. Full-ring backpressure is a normal bounded result.

Implement the fixed two-descriptor publication model, then use the selected bare-metal adapter without rebuilding the whole network stack. For a 3-byte payload, MAC padding supplies 43 bytes under the declared policy; a software frame that already contains pad/FCS needs a different policy and is outside this baseline. The misconception is that a request function returning or an interrupt count proves delivery. Evidence includes publication order, completion/error/reset timelines, no premature reuse and the actual frame/descriptor observation points.

Apply and verify this mechanism in [PR-T39-07](#pr-t39-07).

<a id="t39-09"></a>

### T39.09 — From Ethernet to IPv4, TCP and HTTP responsibility contracts

An HTTP exchange crosses several endpoint namespaces and checks. HTTP supplies a request/status/body framing contract. TCP supplies ordered byte sequence and connection/port state; its segment boundaries are not HTTP message boundaries. IPv4 supplies addresses, packet length, header checksum and a next-hop responsibility. On a local Ethernet route, ARP resolves the selected next-hop IP to a destination MAC; that MAC is not automatically the final IP destination on a routed path. Ethernet validates local frame/address/FCS properties before an IP parser sees bytes.

Walk one request from application bytes through TCP, IP and the frame channel, then back through receive demultiplexing. In the later finite T41 route, these headers/state/timers belong to the learner's MCU implementation above a real MAC/PHY adapter. An OS socket may serve as a peer/client or comparison oracle; using it inside the claimed lower-layer path would delegate the mechanism under study. The finite endpoint intentionally excludes mandatory general-host features such as IP reassembly, so it is an educational subset rather than a complete Internet host.

Specify frame/time/event interfaces with bounded capacity, checksum/length ownership and error propagation before adding protocol code. Reuse the T39 receive/transmit token contract; do not rebuild a second incompatible driver in T41. The misconception is that one successful GET proves a complete stack or that payload/frame/stream sizes are interchangeable. Evidence is a responsibility trace, exact handoff ledger and declared accepted/excluded inputs; T41 supplies the concrete finite protocol implementation.

Apply and verify this mechanism in [PR-T39-08](#pr-t39-08).

<a id="t39-10"></a>

### T39.10 — Cross-layer timing, fault localization and evidence

Cross-layer evidence has capture points and clocks. A host fixture describes a deterministic logical sequence; a target log records descriptor/control events; a PHY status read samples a physical link; an external capture records packets visible at its own point. Additive clock offsets can align timestamps only under a declared synchronization/uncertainty model. Equal-looking timestamps or a decoded packet do not prove that all layers used the same buffer or ownership generation.

For 32 application bytes, simple 20-byte TCP and 20-byte IPv4 headers yield 72IP bytes. Ethernet adds 14 header and 4FCS to make 90 frame bytes;8 preamble/SFD and 12 gap-equivalent byte times make 110 for the declared serialization accounting. At 100Mbit/s this is 8.8 µs, excluding processing, queueing, propagation and peer response. TCP ACKs and extra ARP/connection/HTTP packets are additional events, not silently included in that one-frame estimate. A minimum frame consumes 84 byte times including preamble/gap under the same model.

Localize the first failed contract: lost link, descriptor unavailable, invalid frame, unavailable next hop, transport timeout or malformed HTTP. Several later symptoms may follow one early failure. Implement budget/capture correlation and a minimal failure ledger, then exercise the frame-channel handoff with a synthetic upper-layer consumer. The misconception is that every timeout belongs to TCP or that raw line rate equals application throughput. Evidence includes units, first-failure priority, capture uncertainty and separate software, target and physical receipts.

Apply and verify this mechanism in [PR-T39-08](#pr-t39-08).

## Reading guidance

Read each exact locator before its dependent milestone. The book and ITU model explain boundaries; ST/PHY documents define the selected hardware contract. The CRC appendix supplies declared arithmetic only, not Ethernet normative framing. Reuse previously inspected memory/barrier knowledge, and keep the exact normal-descriptor/stripping policy beside the implementation. No whole current IEEE 802.3 standard or Rev 11 board chapter is assigned from a lead/contents page. The merged [guide-reading](#guide-reading) registry supplies edition/access/scope limitations and the complementary T41 primary RFC spine.

## Implementation projects

The eight milestones build one reusable frame service and prepared image, rather than eight independent board/network stacks. The total 66 project hours are 42 implementation plus 24 verification. Reading 18, assessment 7 and delayed consolidation 5 remain separate; total module 96 hours. Reuse prior token/ring/bounds code and the T38 clock/ownership ledger, but implement the new studied frame/descriptor/PHY mechanisms yourself.

- [PR-T39-01](#pr-t39-01): OSI service and encapsulation ledger (6 hours; profile C).

- [PR-T39-02](#pr-t39-02): Ethernet media and checked frame boundary (8 hours; profile C).

- [PR-T39-03](#pr-t39-03): MAC addressing and bounded learning bridge (6 hours; profile C).

- [PR-T39-04](#pr-t39-04): RMII clock and bounded PHY management (10 hours; profile E).

- [PR-T39-05](#pr-t39-05): MAC/DMA reachability and initialization dependencies (8 hours; profile E).

- [PR-T39-06](#pr-t39-06): Checked Ethernet receive frame channel (10 hours; profile C).

- [PR-T39-07](#pr-t39-07): Ethernet transmit publication and bounded recovery (10 hours; profile C).

- [PR-T39-08](#pr-t39-08): Cross-layer frame handoff and failure evidence (8 hours; profile C).

## Mastery gate and feedback

Given a fresh frame/descriptor/PHY trace, identify the buffer boundary, owner, first failed status/length condition and allowed next action. Explain exactly when FL includes CRC and which configured policy lets the consumer use FL−4. Derive a fresh MDIO word/divider and negotiated mode, then diagnose missing link versus descriptor backpressure versus an upper-layer failure. Show no premature reuse or duplicate release across complete/error/reset generations. Apply [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment): independent review or delayed blind replay, per-objective receipts and targeted repair. Host/C checks close arithmetic/state claims; board and external captures close their separately declared physical claims.

## Consolidation and transfer

After a delay, redraw MAC/RMII/PHY and OSI service/peer paths; reconstruct a minimum frame, an address-bit decision and a DMA publication order. Change FCS policy, PHY mode or consumer lifetime and identify the first interface requiring revision. Pass the unchanged `ethernet_frame_channel_v1` plus monotonic time/error events into T41, and compare actual multi-packet exchange accounting with the one-frame fixture.

## Environment and limits

Baseline is untagged ordinary 10/100 Ethernet with the selected full-duplex MCU/PHY route, normal descriptors, fixed storage and bounded failures. VLAN/jumbo, advanced timestamp/offload, general bridging/loop control and complete Internet-host conformance are excluded. Root T41 owns the finite ARP/IPv4/TCP/HTTP implementation; a socket is a peer/oracle, not a replacement for its claimed lower layers. The actual F439 needs an external PHY and DMA-reachable SRAM; QEMU and virtual NICs do not certify board clocks/media. Follow [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles), [guide-standards](#guide-standards), [guide-inventory](#guide-inventory) and [guide-workload](#guide-workload) for dependency, source and workload audit.

## Purpose and outcomes

Build **EDU7-v1**, an original seven-layer exchange with each responsibility visible in code, wire records and evidence. A and B communicate through router R on two separate RS-485 segments. It is deliberately a small educational suite rather than a claim to implement an ISO OSI protocol suite. The reference model explains where responsibilities belong; our versioned [wire contract](research/enhancement/networking_contracts.json) supplies the concrete fields and policies that a model alone cannot supply.

Successful work distinguishes local frame delivery, unreliable routed delivery, reliable message transfer, negotiated dialogue, canonical representation and application effects. A valid CRC establishes one check over a received frame. It cannot establish that a transfer reached B, that a session remains valid or that a setpoint operation is authorized. Conversely, a session checkpoint can suppress a repeated effect while saying nothing about voltage or physical timing.

The eight projects form one family and contribute **58 implementation and verification hours** once. Reading, the oral/reconstruction assessment and delayed transfer work have separate budgets. Complete host contracts first, then the declared bench; an absent bench leaves the physical and final whole-stack gates open.

## Entry check and remediation

Decode a big-endian signed 16-bit value, compute a maximum nested length without overflow, and explain the difference between a borrowed span and a retained buffer. Trace TXE versus TC on a UART and show why releasing DE at TXE can truncate the final byte. Implement only the deficient T15 serialization/framing leaves or T18 ownership exercises before continuing; existing UART evidence from T28 can be reused.

Mathematics is targeted: powers of two and masks for fields, polynomial XOR for CRC, division for baud timing, and bounded integer comparisons for clocks/checkpoints. If the CRC recurrence is unfamiliar, manually divide a two-byte bit string by a short polynomial and check a remainder before working with 0x1021. For timing, first solve ten bits divided by 115200 bits/s with units. This module requires neither a general algebra course nor probability theory.

Use [guide-entry](#guide-entry), [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles) and [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory) to record the actual host, board, adapter and measurement setup. The initial diagnostic is short; it selects remediation, not a replacement for the eight implementations.

## Component progression

**Seven explicit service boundaries.** Give each layer an input contract, peer identity and failure responsibility. Test routing across two physical segments while preventing the relay from acquiring application responsibility.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **A valid lower-layer frame carrying an invalid session or application operation.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t40-01"></a>

### T40.01 — Model, service boundaries and ownership

A service interface joins adjacent layers locally; a peer protocol relates entities at the same layer across nodes. At A, an application record is encoded by L6, wrapped by L5, segmented by L4, addressed by L3 and framed by L2. L1 moves electrical symbols. At R, L1/L2 terminate on each segment and L3 forwards; R need not decode the application record. At B, the inverse operations validate before publishing upward. This explains why R changes link addresses and CRC while preserving end-to-end node IDs and transport ports.

Use a span `{bytes,length}` with a precise lifetime at every boundary. Receive callbacks borrow an immutable span until return. A layer that waits after return copies into its own bounded slot. A lower asynchronous send retains an immutable owned span until completion; BUSY consumes nothing. Router queues, transport reassembly and session replay records therefore have different owners. Document `submit`, `receive`, `tick` and `completion` contracts without making all layers share one global mutable buffer.

A worked capacity proof starts with the conservative L6 service envelope of 80 octets. L5 adds seven, giving 87; L4 capacity is sufficient for fragments 24, 24, 24, 15. This is a storage envelope, not a valid 80-octet schema-1 record. The actual canonical maximum is 1 schema octet plus five two-octet TLV headers plus values 1+2+2+1+16 = 33 octets. Its session SDU is 40 and fragments are 24, 16. Both proofs give a largest L4 PDU of 32 octets, L3 packet 38 and L2 unescaped body 45; the independent general L2 maximum remains 47 for any legal 40-octet link payload. Confusing capacity with accepted syntax can create an overflow or an invalid acceptance. Build this two-part boundary ledger in [PR-T40-01](#pr-t40-01); retain an encapsulation trace and a rejected lifetime violation.

<a id="t40-02"></a>

### T40.02 — RS-485 physical adapter and medium access

RS-485 supplies differential electrical behavior; it does not supply node addresses, frame delimiters or a collision-free application protocol. Wire A—R.left and R.right—B as two separate segments, with four THVD1400 adapters at 3.3 V, a common reference and a 120-ohm termination at each end. Read the actual adapter schematic and identify D, R, active-high DE and active-low RE. RE stays low, so an enabled transmitter can receive local echo; tag and filter that echo by local transmit ownership rather than feeding it into an apparent peer frame.

For 8N1, one octet occupies ten bit times: about 86.806 microseconds at 115200 baud. A worst-case 96-octet escaped frame occupies at most 8334 microseconds when the integer timing budget rounds upward. Assert DE 200 microseconds before data; keep it asserted through TC, then impose a 200-microsecond peer guard. TXE only permits another register write. A logic trace must establish which event occurs after the final stop bit.

Link address 1 is master on each segment. Every 25-ms turn it may send one DATA and then POLL; address 2 sends one DATA or EMPTY only after that grant. The reply starts within 2 ms after the complete POLL and guard and finishes within 10 ms of its first octet. The master distinguishes a start deadline from a completion deadline. Dropping a legal 8-ms reply at a 2-ms start deadline would be an arbitration bug. [PR-T40-02](#pr-t40-02) combines synthetic event checks with actual voltage, termination, timing and disconnect captures; host octets cannot establish L1 success.

<a id="t40-03"></a>

### T40.03 — Link framing and error detection

L2 uses 0x7e delimiters and escapes body bytes 0x7e/0x7d as 0x7d followed by XOR 0x20. The unescaped body is version, kind, link source, link destination, payload length, payload and big-endian CRC. CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE covers all bytes before the CRC with polynomial 0x1021, initial 0xffff, no reflection and xorout zero. The independent check vector `123456789` has remainder 0x29b1. Compute the CRC before escaping and validate after unescaping; a CRC over the escaped byte stream is a different protocol.

An incremental decoder has SEARCH, BODY, ESCAPE and DISCARD behavior. Empty delimiters yield no packet. A delimiter after an unfinished escape drops the candidate and begins resynchronization; overlong input stays in DISCARD until a delimiter. Version, actual length, legal kind, link destination and grant ownership are checked before upper delivery. A foreign frame still occupies the wire, but it must not mutate upper state.

Exercise every split of an escaped frame, truncated escape, 48-octet body, incorrect CRC and a valid frame after noise. The misconception is that CRC provides retransmission or security. Here L2 reports validated local SDUs and counters only; L4 recovers loss. [PR-T40-03](#pr-t40-03) requires identical results for byte-at-a-time and coalesced input and no callback for a rejected candidate.

<a id="t40-04"></a>

### T40.04 — Network addressing, routing and hop limits

Node IDs A=17, R=34 and B=51 persist across both segments. Link addresses are local: A=1/R.left=2, R.right=1/B=2. Ports 7 and 8 select endpoint services and never choose a route. A datagram for B starts with node source 17, destination 51, hop limit 4 and next protocol 4. R accepts the left frame, copies the packet, decreases hop limit to 3, and creates a right frame from link 1 to link 2. B consumes a positive-hop packet addressed to 51. It does not decrement the packet merely to deliver it.

The six-octet network header contains version, source, destination, hop limit, next protocol and payload length. The only routes are the four versioned entries in the contract. At R, hop limit at most one, unknown destination, an own-origin loop, invalid protocol or a length mismatch produces a counted drop. This is a fixed educational routing rule, not a dynamic discovery protocol.

A router's copy must outlive the input callback, particularly while waiting for its other segment's grant. Poison a released input span and verify the queued output remains correct. The common mistake is to store a pointer into a reusable receive buffer or to carry left link address 2 unchanged onto the right link. [PR-T40-04](#pr-t40-04) requires exact preserved and changed fields, a rebuilt CRC and a private-buffer ownership trace.

<a id="t40-05"></a>

### T40.05 — Reliable bounded transport and flow state

L4 turns unreliable datagrams into complete bounded messages, not a TCP-like byte stream. Its eight-octet header carries DATA/ACK/PROBE, two ports, a transfer ID, fragment index/count and credit. DATA contains 1–24 octets; all non-final fragments contain exactly 24. A message of 25 octets becomes two fragments of 24 and 1, while 120 becomes five of 24. One outstanding fragment and one reassembly tuple per direction keep both memory and protocol state inspectable.

An ACK matches nodes, ports, transfer ID and index before advancing the sender. The receiver remembers an accepted fragment and re-ACKs a duplicate without appending it again. Only the complete message is published. Retain one last completed receipt and a highest-completed ID; ACK an identical repeated last fragment, drop earlier IDs, and replace the receipt only on the next completion. IDs strictly increase within a session and never wrap. A completed SDU awaiting upper consumption holds credit zero. An index/count mismatch fails the candidate instead of stitching bytes from different transfers.

Start the 100-ms retransmission clock after the lower layer actually accepts the fragment for transmission, not while it is still BUSY waiting for a grant. At most three retransmissions use identical bytes and index. Credit zero pauses new DATA; a 100-ms PROBE asks for credit, and an independent 500-ms blocked deadline frees state with a failure event. Duplicate ACKs and probes cannot postpone that deadline indefinitely. ID wrap forces session reopen. In [PR-T40-05](#pr-t40-05), show a dropped ACK, duplicate fragment, credit pause and timeout with no partial publication. A plausible retry count without an exact buffer/state trace is insufficient.

<a id="t40-06"></a>

### T40.06 — Session dialogue and resynchronization

L5 adds schema/unit negotiation, dialogue ownership and checkpoints; these are distinct from transport delivery. OPEN and OPEN_ACK agree on nonzero session/epoch, schema 1, unit 1 and initial token A. Their checkpoint is zero, as are TOKEN/CLOSE/ERROR control records. DATA carries the next positive checkpoint for its direction. A cannot send another application DATA while B holds the token, even though transport buffers may be available.

Transferring the token is itself uncertain until transport completion. The sender enters TOKEN_PENDING and sends no new DATA. The receiver changes holder when the complete TOKEN arrives. If its ACK is lost, the former holder remains blocked and a repeated TOKEN changes nothing again. This may pause progress, but never gives both endpoints permission. After A's request and token transfer, B sends the reply and returns the token.

Retained RAM remembers the last committed per-direction checkpoint and payload/response. Same checkpoint plus identical bytes causes no new effect; same checkpoint plus changed bytes is an error. A transport reset can use RESUME only when both peers retain matching session/epoch/checkpoint state. A rebooted peer with no state refuses. Checkpoint wrap requires close/reopen. This is neither authenticated identity nor durable exactly-once processing. [PR-T40-06](#pr-t40-06) asks for a state diagram and effect count that distinguish lost ACK, stale epoch, incompatible negotiation, retained resume and reboot refusal.

<a id="t40-07"></a>

### T40.07 — Presentation syntax and typed representation

L6 begins with schema 1 and ascending unique TLVs. Tags encode verb, request ID, signed value, unit and optional UTF-8 label. Two octets `f0 60` mean signed -4000 in the declared two's-complement 16-bit representation; they do not depend on the host's native byte order or struct padding. Decode through unsigned arithmetic, then convert within a representable signed range. A 16-byte label limit counts UTF-8 octets, not displayed characters.

Stage a decoded record until all TLV syntax, lengths, required fields, units and canonical UTF-8 have passed. Reject duplicate/out-of-order tags, truncated values, overlong encodings, surrogates and unknown schema. A label is display data, never a format string. Presentation validation proves that a typed record can be represented; only L7 decides whether a SET value is allowed for this application.

Implement encode/decode without copying a native struct. Compare a boundary SET, reordered tags and a UTF-8 label split inside a multibyte code point. [PR-T40-07](#pr-t40-07) requires unchanged output sentinels on failure and a round trip with a separately derived wire record. A decoder that silently replaces malformed UTF-8 would violate this canonical contract.

<a id="t40-08"></a>

### T40.08 — Application exchange and seven-layer acceptance

GET returns a declared fixture plant value. SET changes the fixture setpoint only within -4000 through 12500 centidegrees Celsius; ERROR leaves it unchanged. Unit 1 is mandatory for SET and REPLY, and every response correlates the request ID. These are explicit original application semantics; no physical sensor is implied. An otherwise valid session cannot make an out-of-range setpoint acceptable.

Trace SET from A to B through representation, session checkpoint, transport fragments, routed packets and two link frames, then the reply in the reverse direction. Correlate address scopes without expecting identical wire bytes at R. Apply the effect once before replying and keep the recorded response for a valid duplicate checkpoint. The invalid-SET ERROR includes the retained setpoint and a state witness demonstrates unchanged state independently of the error text. GET still returns the separate fixture plant value, not the setpoint.

[PR-T40-08](#pr-t40-08) integrates all eight milestones. Its host fixture deliberately lacks physical evidence, so a correct protocol transcript still reports an open physical gate. Actual acceptance adds two-segment relay captures, corrupt/noisy/truncated frames, dropped ACKs, blocked credit, dialogue violation, retained resume, reboot refusal and cable interruption. Each fault is attributed to the responsible boundary, rather than described vaguely as a network failure.

## Reading guidance

The JSON reading list supplies exact inspected locator strings. X.200 assigns responsibilities; Peterson/Davie explains encapsulation; the TI documents constrain the actual declared wiring and driver enables. Read them against the boundary ledger, not as an implementation recipe. The whole wire format, retry policy and fixture application are original EDU7-v1 decisions. No textbook C solution is supplied. The TI application note is guidance, not complete TIA conformance evidence; component specifications also do not verify an adapter PCB or bench installation.

Allocate the remaining reading hour to the original contract and your layer/API ledger. For current edition, access and inspection limits use [guide-reading](#guide-reading) and [guide-inventory](#guide-inventory). Advanced OSI service definitions outside these selected passages are further study, not required uninspected reading.

## Implementation projects

Complete [boundary ledger](#pr-t40-01) (4 h), [physical adapter and grant scheduler](#pr-t40-02) (8 h), [framer](#pr-t40-03) (6 h), [router](#pr-t40-04) (6 h), [message transport](#pr-t40-05) (10 h), [session](#pr-t40-06) (8 h), [presentation](#pr-t40-07) (8 h), and [whole-stack exchange](#pr-t40-08) (8 h). Keep a host adapter for injected faults and clocks while replacing the physical adapter with target UART/DE operations.

Run `python tools/verify_networking_fixtures.py` in the declared host Python environment to check supplied expected values. It checks finite independent calculations/traces, not your C implementation. Your own tests exercise every listed transition, capacity and publication contract and compare against these oracles. Retain a fixture-to-evidence index using [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) and [guide-audit](#guide-audit).

## Mastery gate and feedback

For each topic submit the three project evidence items and explain one changed condition without running code. Reconstruct the 87-octet message budget; redraw the lost-token-ACK trace; predict the next-hop rewrite; decode a negative value; and identify which observations establish TC and physical driver release. The reviewer selects at least one unseen split, corruption, route and session reset, then checks unchanged state or exact accepted bytes.

Feedback names the failed boundary and observable invariant. Repair framing by a minimal noise/resynchronization trace, transport by a matching tuple/index ledger, session by effect/token state, and hardware timing by a measured waveform. Repeat the failed gate and one adjacent interaction only. A host-only route can close portable protocol objectives while marking physical objectives pending; it cannot receive a whole-family completion claim.

## Consolidation and transfer

After at least several days, rebuild one frame and one lost-ACK/session-resume trace from the versioned contract. Replace the UTF-8 label with a longer legal multibyte label and explain why the byte budget changes while routing does not. Add an optional second application verb by first changing L7/L6 contracts and tests, not by making R interpret it. A second session or dynamic routing is a new design with fresh ownership/state bounds.

Use [guide-workload](#guide-workload), [guide-integrations](#guide-integrations) and [guide-standards](#guide-standards) to record the family hours and scope. The extension teaches mechanisms deeply while preserving the original curriculum's foundational ownership and verification work.

## Environment and limits

Profile C executes deterministic host octet/event tests. Profile E uses the three declared boards and two bounded bench segments, with actual MCU clocks/pins and adapter schematics recorded. Firmware evidence must include original layer/state work; supplied solved stack code cannot fulfill it. Wire captures, voltage and termination measurements retain uncertainty and equipment settings. No host model, emulator, replayed capture or synthetic register log establishes electrical safety, timing or a connected physical sensor. There is no encrypted/authenticated session, durable recovery, automatic route discovery or ISO protocol-suite conformance claim.

# T42 — From-scratch HTTP server over OS sockets

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HTTP application and Linux systems | core | 96 | A, C |

**Prerequisites:** [T15](#t15), [T18](#t18), [T23](#t23), [T24](#t24), [T32](#t32).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 20 | 46 | 18 | 6 | 6 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Build an original bounded HTTP/1.1 origin server in C. It owns incremental octet parsing, framing, routes, serialization, descriptor/buffer lifetime, bounded queues and deadlines. It listens on loopback 127.0.0.1:8080. The OS supplies TCP/IP and lower layers. This is the third communication family; the first is the original seven-layer protocol and the second supplies its own Ethernet-to-TCP implementation. The portable HTTP core developed here is reused by the second family.

## Entry check and remediation

Demonstrate span bounds and retained-pointer lifetimes; predict short read/write/EINTR/EAGAIN behavior; trace an event-loop resource acquisition and cleanup; derive checked integer accumulation. Reuse T15/T18 parsing/ownership and T23/T24 Linux adapters. A failed prediction returns to those exact mechanisms before implementing a larger server. Inspect the shared contract and distinguish octets, TCP stream, HTTP message and application representation. Do not assume that one read contains a request.

## Component progression

**One HTTP core across transport adapters.** Implement octet grammar, authority and framing before routing. Preserve parser/output cursors across fragmentation, short writes, persistence and bounded deadlines.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **Two interpretations of the same request framing or a partially emitted response followed by buffer reuse.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t42-01"></a>

### T42.01 — Socket lifecycle and layer ownership

A socket delivers an ordered stream whose chunk boundaries belong to the current call, not to HTTP. OS TCP performs sequence/retransmission work. The application owns descriptor lifecycle, byte retention and message interpretation. Reuse the earlier Linux accept/event adapter, then attach four explicitly owned connection records. Accept readiness is only a hint: another action can consume the pending connection, so EAGAIN returns to the event loop. On Linux an accepted descriptor does not inherit the listener's nonblocking status; set and verify flags explicitly. A failed initialization must close the descriptor exactly once before publishing a record.

Trace accepted descriptors 11,12,13,14 into four slots. Descriptor 15 cannot acquire a slot and is closed. Releasing 12 allows 16 to enter; no reference to 12 may survive in a queued event. Add a generation number to distinguish a recycled descriptor number from the old connection. Record this invariant: every live descriptor has one owner and every published record has a valid descriptor. A readable listener does not guarantee a successful accept, and an open socket does not establish an HTTP session. Evidence includes flag inspection, an accept-race trace, injected exhaustion, resource counters and an explicit layer-ownership map.

<a id="t42-02"></a>

### T42.02 — Incremental request grammar and target authority

Treat input as bounded octets. A recv call may stop between CR and LF, between a field name and colon, or inside a request target. Save state and the precise consumed offset; never append a NUL then assume all octets are text. The strict project grammar uses one SP between request-line elements and CRLF delimiters. Field names use the HTTP token alphabet and case-insensitive matching; whitespace before the colon, folding, NUL and invalid controls cause rejection before publication. Strict recipient policy is allowed here but is not a claim that the RFC has no tolerant parsing provisions.

For a GET header ending at offset 46, feed prefixes of lengths 0 through 46. Every proper prefix reports NEED_MORE with no complete request; the final LF completes the header once. Feeding two headers in one span completes only the first and returns its consumed length, leaving the second unchanged. Absolute-form http://localhost:8080/health selects authority localhost:8080, even if the syntactically valid single Host says other.example. Origin-form uses the single Host. Validate bounded configured host/port authorities; do not implement filesystem normalization. Missing/duplicate/malformed HTTP/1.1 Host returns 400 and close. A complete header is not yet a complete body. Retain split/coalescing, target-authority and smallest malformed-octet evidence.


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t42-02-a"></a>


- **T42.02.a** Parse request lines and headers incrementally as octets across every selected split and coalescing boundary. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T42-02](#pr-t42-02).


<a id="t42-02-b"></a>


- **T42.02.b** Validate the declared origin-form and bounded absolute-form targets and the single HTTP1.1 Host contract. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T42-02](#pr-t42-02).


<a id="t42-02-c"></a>


- **T42.02.c** Reject ambiguous whitespace, control bytes and obsolete folding before publishing a request. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T42-02](#pr-t42-02).


<a id="t42-03"></a>

### T42.03 — Header normalization and unambiguous message framing

After headers, select exactly one body mode. The method name does not define the wire boundary: a GET can carry framed content, while a POST without length fields has zero request-body length. This project consumes a framed body before routing even when a route later rejects it. NONE means zero body; LENGTH requires exact unsigned decimal syntax; CHUNKED means the decoder owns termination. Header lookup must retain duplicate occurrence counts rather than overwriting one field with another.

Derive a checked decimal accumulation condition before each multiply/add using the declared maximum 4294967295. Then apply the 1024-byte body cap. An overflowing numeral is 400; a representable declared body above the cap is 413. Identical duplicate Content-Length is conservatively400+close. TE+CL is always400+close, rather than choosing whichever parser seems convenient. Check syntax and framing before unsupported decoding: a request whose final coding is not chunked is 400+close. Thus gzip alone and chunked,gzip are 400. Repeated chunked, malformed token lists and chunked parameters are 400. A valid gzip,chunked list is framed but requires an unsupported decoder, so it is 501+close. The declared strict profile rejects other parameterized coding lists with 400; this is a syntax-subset policy. For LENGTH 5 and input abcdeGET..., consume exactly five body octets; GET belongs to the next message. Premature EOF after four bytes is incomplete and cannot dispatch a successful echo. Produce the framing-decision table, byte-conservation ledger and overflow counterexamples.

<a id="t42-04"></a>

### T42.04 — Chunked decoding, extensions and trailers

Chunked transfer encoding is a framing grammar. Maintain SIZE_LINE, DATA, DATA_CRLF, TRAILERS and COMPLETE states with independent counters. Hex accumulation and aggregate size are checked before accepting bytes. A valid bounded unknown extension is syntactically parsed and ignored; rejecting every unknown extension would evade the receiver contract. Trailer fields are validated in separate bounded storage and discarded. They never replace Host, Content-Length or routing decisions.

Trace 3;x=y CRLF abc CRLF 2 CRLF de CRLF 0 CRLF X-Debug: ignored CRLF CRLF. The representation is the five octets abcde. The zero-size chunk ends data but does not finish the message until the trailer section's final empty line. A CR split across reads is still pending state, not an optional delimiter. The supplied invalid trace puts X where the data-ending CR belongs and returns 400+close; the incomplete trace has no terminal empty line and publishes no body. Check every byte split, extension/trailer capacities and EOF in every state. Keep decoded content separate from wire byte counts; the wire overhead is not echoed.

<a id="t42-04-b"></a>


- **T42.04.b** Keep trailer fields separate from original routing/framing headers and discard them under the declared policy. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T42-04](#pr-t42-04).

<a id="t42-05"></a>

### T42.05 — HTTP semantics, routing and response serialization

Routing begins only after a complete admissible request, except that header-determined errors and 100-continue need early handling. GET and HEAD /health select the representation hex `6f6b0a`: three octets, including LF. HEAD sends its GET-equivalent Content-Length: 3 with no representation body. POST /echo returns identical bounded octets, including NUL and non-UTF8 values. Unknown route returns 404. A recognized method disallowed on the selected route returns 405 and route-specific Allow; an unknown method returns 501. Declare bounded supported methods GET, HEAD, POST and distinguish recognition from permission.

Every HEAD response suppresses content, including error responses. HEAD /unknown therefore reports the selected ten-octet error representation length and sends zero body octets. HEAD /echo reports 405 with Allow: POST and the selected nineteen-octet error length, again with no body. Preserve representation metadata separately from actual serialized content.

For an admissible POST with Expect: 100-continue and body not yet received, enqueue the interim 100 immediately, then wait for the framed body. If headers already establish an error, enqueue that final error instead. Waiting for the body before 100 can deadlock a cooperative client. Emit Date using a reasonable UTC clock; fixture epoch 1672531200 yields Sun, 01 Jan 2023 00:00:00 GMT in the required fixed-date format. Use a separate monotonic clock for deadlines. Length is an octet count, not Unicode character count. User data never becomes unchecked header syntax or a format string. Evidence includes exact serialization, binary echo, HEAD boundary, Allow and expectation traces.

<a id="t42-06"></a>

### T42.06 — Partial output, persistence and pipelining

Keep immutable response storage until every queued byte is locally accepted or the connection aborts. A send of four bytes advances the offset by four; EINTR and EAGAIN advance it by zero. Sending again from offset 0 duplicates output. POLLOUT interest is needed only while pending bytes remain; a permanent writable interest can spin an otherwise idle event loop. Local send success is not evidence that the peer application consumed the response.

For nine output octets and results 4, EINTR, 2, EAGAIN, 3, the retained offsets are 4, 4, 6, 6, 9. A two-entry request queue holds requests 1, 2 and pauses parsing 3. Persistent responses remain FIFO even if their computation costs differ. The default maximum is four requests per connection; the fourth response announces close. If request 2 requests Connection:close, 3 is never dispatched. Drain the final response, shutdown the write direction, then receive/discard remaining bytes only until EOF or the 1000 ms drain deadline, and close. The discarded bytes are not new requests. Record read backpressure, output retention, FIFO and close-state transitions with tiny-send and coalesced-input tests.

Interim responses preserve association too. If a pipelined second request expects 100-continue, queue its interim response after the first request's final response and before its own final response. Decide on 100 as soon as the admissible headers are complete; that decision cannot preempt an earlier response's bytes. Apply bounded output backpressure while the client waits for the ordered interim response.

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t42-06-c"></a>

<a id="t42-07"></a>

### T42.07 — Deadlines, resource limits and transport failure

Resource limits are part of the state machine. Idle activity and total elapsed request time are independent. A byte every four seconds can keep a five-second idle timer fresh while violating a fifteen-second total request deadline. Do not renew the total deadline on every byte. Bound headers at 8192 octets, 32 fields, target 1024 octets, body 1024 octets, extension 128 octets per chunk and trailer 1024 octets/eight fields; apply limits before storing. Track four connections, two complete queued requests and four requests per connection. Derive actual memory from chosen representations, including retained spans, output, queues and error paths.

With request start 0, progress at 4000, 8000, 12000, 14900 ms and now 15000 ms, idle has not expired but the total deadline has. A request timeout returns bounded 408+close where output remains usable; output timeout aborts and makes no completed-response claim. POLLHUP may arrive with readable buffered bytes: consume those before treating recv 0 as EOF. A half-close after a complete request can still allow its response; one inside a declared body remains incomplete. EPIPE/reset aborts output and releases ownership. Retain monotonic-clock traces, failure-state distinctions and allocator/descriptor high-water evidence rather than calling every close successful.

<a id="t42-08"></a>

### T42.08 — Parsing security and independent interoperability

A parser boundary is a security boundary because two participants can disagree on where a request ends. Compare your exact framing decisions with an independent raw client and the current RFC contract. A mature client is an oracle peer, not permission to import an HTTP parser/server library. Reject unsupported CONNECT or Upgrade with a final error and close; optimistic following bytes never become another dispatched request. RFC 9931's inspected CONNECT proxy requirements are background authority, while this origin-server rejection policy is an original declared policy.

Run curl for GET, HEAD, binary POST and expected 100-continue behavior, and a separate raw-octet peer for duplicate lengths, TE+CL, invalid controls, chunks, pipelines and half-close. Packet segmentation, socket read chunks and HTTP messages are three different units. Save normalized status/header/body results and exact byte traces where framing matters. Test that the same request under all partitions produces one result and that a close/error prevents any second application effect. Publish component/source/dependency ownership, unresolved deviations and limits. Plain loopback HTTP has no TLS, proxy or production deployment claim. Static fixture checks cannot replace executing and inspecting the learner's original C.

## Reading guidance

Read UNP for the short-I/O mechanism, then extract the current Linux return/error and readiness rules. Its blocking helpers are explanation rather than event-loop code to copy. Read RFC 9112 in the order grammar → framing → chunking → persistence/teardown, constructing a decision table for the project instead of reading the entire protocol at once. RFC 9110 supplies method/expectation/Date semantics; it cannot replace wire-framing rules. RFC 9931 updates HTTP/1.1 transition security with explicitly scoped CONNECT proxy requirements.

The assigned table contains exact inspected passages. Adjacent RFC sections may be consulted as reference; assigning new obligatory passages requires inspection and registry extension. Distinguish the RFC obligation, a stricter original resource/syntax policy and an excluded capability in the evidence ledger. Current primary contracts take precedence over old textbook behavior.

## Mastery gate and feedback

Every topic needs separate a,b,c evidence. Defend one successful path and one minimized failure without reading the implementation. Publish a byte-conservation ledger and demonstrate identical semantic results under every selected partition/coalescing of the input. Show one output backpressure trace, one deadline that survives slow progress, and one close/error followed by apparent request bytes with no second dispatch. The complete gate includes actual original C execution with independent curl/raw peers, current source contracts, memory/descriptor limits, symbol/dependency inspection and delayed reconstruction.

A fixture verifier checks static oracles only. Parser bugs, send success, coverage percentages and cooperative-client success do not establish every HTTP receiver requirement. Minimize disagreement before changing the contract. A body/framing defect returns to the portable parser; an event/lifetime defect returns to the adapter. Record excluded features and unresolved actual execution explicitly.

## Consolidation and transfer

After at least one day reconstruct framing precedence, HEAD length and the partial-send invariant from memory. Change a split, duplicate header, EOF point or timeout boundary and predict the new result. Carry the accepted portable parser/serializer into T41 through a span/event adapter. Keep its original project IDs and hours; the new adapter must demonstrate preservation of bytes and ownership over custom TCP rather than charge for rewriting HTTP again. See the communication-family guide for the cross-domain route.

## Environment and limits

The hosted executable uses profile A; parser/router/serializer components use profile C with caller storage, allowed type headers and explicit time/config callbacks. Audit compiler helpers and callbacks separately; no external HTTP library implements the studied mechanisms. Linux-specific MSG_NOSIGNAL, descriptor flags and poll behavior are declared platform contracts. curl and raw clients are verification peers only. The server is plain loopback HTTP with bounded routes, not TLS, a proxy, a filesystem server, a tunnel or a production deployment. Hardware lower-layer closure belongs to T40/T41 and cannot be claimed from these sockets.

## Purpose and outcomes

Implement the packet and state work of a **custom minimal Ethernet-to-HTTP stack** on NUCLEO-F439ZI. The MCU provides an Ethernet MAC/DMA controller; the fitted LAN8742A, magnetics and cable provide actual physical signaling. Your original C owns the selected driver, Ethernet/ARP, IPv4/ICMP, passive TCP and HTTP adapter. Register definitions are permissible aids, while a vendor Ethernet driver, lwIP or an OS TCP/IP stack cannot perform the owned mechanism work.

This is a controlled, same-link interoperability profile, with board 192.0.2.2/24, peer 192.0.2.1/24 and server port 8080. The [original contract](research/enhancement/networking_contracts.json) excludes DHCP, DNS, routing, IP reassembly/options, general congestion growth and several TCP services. Successful exchanges with a declared cooperative client do not establish general RFC host or IEEE conformance. The Internet suite also does not map one-for-one onto OSI's seven layers: HTTP can include several upper-layer concerns, TCP supplies transport, and the PHY/MAC boundary still requires explicit physical evidence.

Eight milestones contribute **72 implementation and verification hours** once. The portable HTTP parser/serializer projects in T42 are prerequisite work reused here; their hours belong to T42 and are not added again. Physical bring-up and protocol logic remain independently reviewable.

## Entry check and remediation

Before driver work, reconstruct a T29 DMA ownership transition and show which SRAM regions are Ethernet-DMA accessible on the recorded F439 target. Before packet work, safely decode a bounded big-endian integer and prove every nested length lies within its enclosing span. Before final HTTP integration, complete T42.02–T42.05's portable grammar/framing/chunk/serializer evidence; the hosted multi-connection event-loop milestones need not precede this board's one-connection adapter.

Targeted mathematics covers unsigned modular subtraction with live intervals below 2^31, one's-complement end-around carry, powers/masks, and weighted means for SRTT/RTTVAR. If sequence wrap is unclear, first draw a 16-value ring and compare intervals shorter than eight; then apply the same reasoning to 32 bits. If checksum carry is unclear, add three 16-bit words on paper and repeatedly fold high carries before complementing. These are local repairs, not a prerequisite general mathematics course.

Pin the exact board marking, RM0090 Rev 21, UM1974 Rev 8, inspected LAN8742A datasheet revision, compiler/linker and host adapter settings using [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles), [guide-inventory](#guide-inventory) and [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory). Verify clock and board pin configuration from earlier T27/T28 work rather than guessing from another STM32 board.

## Component progression

**A minimal Internet endpoint with actual interoperability.** Separate sequence arithmetic, stream delivery, timers, flow pressure and HTTP framing. Verify each substate with virtual time and an independent peer before closing physical gates.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **A delayed duplicate, sequence wrap or half-close exposing a disagreement between transport and application completion.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t41-01"></a>

### T41.01 — Protocol subset, interfaces and bounded resources

Each input span has a local interpretation. Ethernet supplies an entire frame beginning with DA. IPv4 supplies a datagram whose total length excludes Ethernet padding. TCP supplies a sequence-space segment, but the HTTP consumer receives an ordered byte stream with no preserved packet boundaries. Do not cast all three into one native struct or use Ethernet receive length as an HTTP body length.

Declare immutable borrowed spans for synchronous receive; owned slots for queued transmit data; and explicit consume counts for the HTTP stream adapter. Packet validation publishes nothing on failure. A TX DMA completion permits reuse of that DMA buffer but does not acknowledge the TCP bytes: their immutable retransmission copy remains until valid ACK. A full queue returns BUSY without consuming caller bytes. Link-down invalidates the transport incarnation and reports an abort rather than pretending all queued data reached the application.

For a TCP payload of 3 octets with fixed IPv4/TCP headers, 20+20+3=43 IPv4 octets, plus 14 Ethernet octets gives 57. MAC padding brings the frame from DA through padding to 60, then FCS yields 64. Preamble/SFD and interframe gap are physical/MAC behavior outside the driver's DA-starting span. [PR-T41-01](#pr-t41-01) produces the scope/API/length ledger and a bounded memory budget. The trap is labeling all exclusions as optional standards features instead of acknowledging that a full IPv4 host must do more.

<a id="t41-02"></a>

### T41.02 — Ethernet PHY, RMII and physical readiness

The F439 Ethernet block speaks RMII to an external PHY. LAN8742A converts that digital interface to actual cable signaling through magnetics. Its 50-MHz reference and the selected board pins/bridges are functional dependencies, not observations proven by a packet fixture. Configure RMII during the documented reset/clock sequence, confirm actual reference operation, then use MDIO to read the fitted PHY's identity and status.

The inspected identity is register 2 = 0x0007 and register 3 masked by 0xfff0 = 0xc130; the low nibble records silicon revision. Reset bit 15 of control register 0 self-clears. Use a recorded finite reset/MDIO deadline rather than an infinite busy loop. Basic Status link bit 2 is latch-low: reading 0x0020 then 0x0024 means a down condition was latched and the current link is up, not that the second value erased the event. Negotiation completion also requires the selected status fields.

Register 31 has negotiation-done bit 12 and speed bits 4:2. Codes 001/101 mean 10 half/full, 010/110 mean 100 half/full. Thus 0x1018 indicates completed 100-Mbit full duplex. Only supported full-duplex results enable this profile; MAC DM/FES must match the actual outcome. [PR-T41-02](#pr-t41-02) checks numeric decoding and actual clock/link/reset/cable captures. PHY IDs do not prove a clock exists, and a TAP or mocked status register cannot close this topic's physical gate.

<a id="t41-03"></a>

### T41.03 — MAC and Ethernet DMA descriptor lifecycle

Use four RX and two TX normal, 16-byte descriptors, each paired with one 2048-byte buffer in DMA-accessible SRAM, not CCM. Disable enhanced descriptors and timestamps; DSL=0 gives contiguous descriptors. The final RX uses RER, the final TX TER; chained mode is off. Buffer 1 has the exact RX size or TX byte count, and buffer 2 is unused. This costs 6×2048+6×16=12384 bytes before higher-layer queues.

Initialize complete buffers/descriptor controls, apply the target's required ordering, then publish OWN. CPU may inspect payload/status only after DMA clears OWN. For TX, normal TDES0 holds OWN31, IC30, LS29, FS28 and TER21; DC27=0 and DP26=0 request MAC CRC/padding and CIC23:22=0 disables transmit checksum offload. DMA writeback resets transmit control fields, so reconstruct them on every reuse. The earlier generic operation paragraph's IC reference conflicts with the normal-descriptor detail; use the inspected normal description, not the generic reference.

For RX, require OWN clear, FS+LS, no error summary/descriptor error and FL in 64..1518. CSTF=APCS=0 retains FCS, so expose FL-4 bytes beginning DA. A minimum FL=64 exposes 60; do not subtract the four bytes again in Ethernet. Store-and-forward is enabled for RX/TX; bad/undersized forwarding and checksum offload are disabled. Configure list bases only while stopped. Poll status with defined W1C masks, refill a suspended ring before poll demand and stop service on fatal bus error. [PR-T41-03](#pr-t41-03) combines the finite ownership oracle with actual ring wrap and descriptor reuse. Volatile alone does not order ordinary packet stores or grant CPU ownership.
