<a id="t41-04"></a>

### T41.04 — Ethernet demultiplexing and ARP neighbor state

Untagged Ethernet II carries DA, SA and a big-endian type. This profile accepts local unicast and ARP broadcast, types 0x0800/0x0806, and drops VLAN/foreign traffic. Hardware perfect filtering is an aid; the software contract still validates its inputs. The board's locally administered fixture MAC is 02:00:00:00:00:02; actual peer MAC is observed and recorded, not assumed from the fixture.

ARP does not use an IPv4 wrapper. Its 28-octet Ethernet/IPv4 payload declares hardware type 1, protocol 0x0800, lengths 6/4 and opcode 1 or 2. Check those and enclosing length before reading variable fields; require ARP sender MAC to equal Ethernet SA. Only the configured peer IP can enter the one-entry cache. Reply to requests for the local IP, expire learned state after 30 seconds, retain at most one queued datagram, and issue at most three resolution requests one second apart.

An unresolved neighbor is a bounded resolution failure rather than permission to overwrite the only queue. Learning a tuple establishes a local address association, not authentication. A poisoned source field must never silently redirect the queued TCP packet. [PR-T41-04](#pr-t41-04) checks exact ARP wire bytes, mismatch/expiry/drop outcomes and an actual request/reply capture on the isolated link.

<a id="t41-05"></a>

### T41.05 — IPv4, ICMP echo and Internet checksum

Accept version 4, IHL 5, total length 20..1500 within the received span, TTL positive, valid header checksum, local destination and configured peer source. Protocol is ICMP or TCP. Emit DF=1, MF=0, offset=0, ID=0, TTL=64. Dropping options and all fragments is an explicit restricted-profile omission: full-host reassembly requirements do not disappear merely because the lab avoids fragments.

The Internet checksum adds big-endian 16-bit words with end-around carry and then complements the folded sum. An odd final octet is the high byte of a zero-padded word. Byte `61` contributes 0x6100, not 0x0061. Bound accumulation or fold periodically so the host integer cannot overflow. TCP's checksum covers its IPv4 pseudo-header, TCP header/options and payload; IPv4 header checksum alone says nothing about transport integrity.

Echo accepts ICMP type 8, code 0 and at most 64 payload bytes with valid checksum. Reply type 0 preserves identifier, sequence and every payload octet, then recomputes the checksum. With five echoed bytes, IP length is 33; Ethernet length before padding is 47, requiring 13 zero pad bytes to reach 60. [PR-T41-05](#pr-t41-05) independently derives those checksum/length expectations and adds default 56-byte real ping. A successful ping proves neither TCP nor HTTP framing.

<a id="t41-06"></a>

### T41.06 — TCP handshake, sequence and close state

Listen passively on 8080 for one connection. Validate tuple, checksum, header/data offset and options before state mutation. Advertise MSS 256 and use min(256, peer MSS or default 536) for sending. Parse EOL/NOP/MSS and skip well-formed unknown length-coded options; malformed lengths drop. Do not negotiate scaling/SACK/timestamps/ECN. Unsupported urgent data or SYN payload has a recorded restricted-profile outcome rather than a false full-TCP claim.

Sequence numbers lie on a 2^32 ring; all live spans stay below 2^31. SYN and FIN each consume one, pure ACK consumes zero. Starting peer SYN at 0xfffffff0 gives RCV.NXT=0xfffffff1. Sixteen accepted bytes move it to 1. A repeated segment contributes zero new bytes; an overlapping segment starting at 0xfffffff9 with twelve bytes has eight old bytes and four new, moving it to 5. Ordinary unsigned less-than fails across this wrap. Use explicit modular interval predicates whose preconditions are checked.

Reject an ACK beyond SND.NXT before freeing output. Update the peer window only with the inspected SND.WL1/WL2 guards; stale ACKs cannot roll it backward. Trim to an admissible in-order span and ACK gaps without retaining an out-of-order queue. Exact-RCV.NXT RST aborts; an in-window unequal RST sends a challenge ACK and no effect, outside-window RST drops. This is not authentication.

Trace LISTEN→SYN-RECEIVED→ESTABLISHED and active/passive close, FIN-WAIT-1/2, CLOSE-WAIT, LAST-ACK, CLOSING and TIME-WAIT. A peer FIN is a half-close, not successful completion of an incomplete HTTP body. Hold active-close TIME-WAIT for 240 seconds using MSL=120; a repeated remote FIN restarts it. [PR-T41-06](#pr-t41-06) requires a transition ledger, overlap bytes and separate reset/half-close observations, including actual packet captures after host state tests.

<a id="t41-07"></a>

### T41.07 — TCP timers, flow pressure and conservative sending

Retransmission and flow state are separate. RTO begins at 1000 ms, estimates from unambiguous RTT samples and backs off after timeout; receiver window expresses storage, while cwnd expresses a sending restriction. The profile keeps at most one outstanding segment and fixed conservative cwnd of one effective MSS. This bounded policy is intentionally slower than a full Internet implementation and does not demonstrate congestion growth, fast recovery or all event obligations.

For the first 80-ms sample, SRTT=80 and RTTVAR=40. With the next sample 120, update RTTVAR first: 0.75×40+0.25×|80-120|=40; then SRTT=0.875×80+0.125×120=85. Raw RTO 85+4×40=245 becomes 1000 under the minimum. No ambiguous retransmitted sample enters this calculation. Timeout events after an initial send occur at 1000, 3000, 7000 ms with three retransmissions, then the explicit finite resource abort at 15000. Cap RTO at 60000; a SYN retransmission keeps post-handshake initial data RTO at least 3000.

Keep the unacknowledged byte copy until ACK, even after TX DMA completes. Zero peer window pauses new data; a probe on the current RTO/backoff schedule requests an update without consuming another application byte. Local advertised window follows actual retained RX capacity and reopens when the parser consumes it. [PR-T41-07](#pr-t41-07) verifies clocked samples, ignored ambiguous samples, zero-window/reopen and no duplicate delivery. It also compares the omitted general behavior explicitly rather than calling a one-segment sender a complete congestion controller.

<a id="t41-08"></a>

### T41.08 — HTTP reuse, independent interoperability and physical closure

Attach the existing T42 portable parser/serializer through a stream adapter. Its byte grammar, Content-Length/chunked rules, Host/target validation, trailer limits and error-close policy stay the same. Configure one connection, queue depth one, one request and Connection: close. GET/HEAD /health uses the three-octet representation hex 6f6b0a; POST /echo preserves bounded binary octets. The shared fixed-order response fixture is an original serializer policy, not a universal RFC field-order rule.

Set the adapter's configured authority to `192.0.2.2:8080`; the hosted profile uses its separately declared loopback authority. This changes configuration and I/O callbacks, not parser grammar or Host validation. The fixed epoch 1672531200 belongs only to deterministic fixtures. Actual cable responses use a recorded reasonable UTC callback or initialized clock for Date, separate from the monotonic TCP clock. If no reasonable UTC is available, omit Date as allowed by the inspected RFC 9110 Date rule and record that response variant; do not call the fixture's historical date current.

TCP can ACK bytes retained for the parser before an HTTP request is complete. A callback passes arbitrary accepted prefixes; preserve each consume count and leftover octet. Serialize once, retain immutable response bytes while segmenting at effective MSS/window, and free them only under the declared acknowledgment/completion rules. Send FIN after all response bytes are acknowledged. Error requests close without interpreting optimistic trailing bytes as a second request.

[PR-T41-08](#pr-t41-08) correlates independent captures for ARP, echo, handshake, exact HTTP semantics, loss/retry, zero window and close. Remove/reconnect the cable and reset the board; show link down aborts the old incarnation and new requests belong to a recorded new one. A replayed pcap or hosted TAP closes finite protocol tests only. The full family closes only with actual fitted PHY/clock, cable operation, original driver/state work and independent client evidence.

## Reading guidance

The exact reading locators are in the front matter. Board/manual/PHY readings constrain the chosen physical and driver setup; RFC readings constrain packet/state mathematics. Allocate the remaining reading hour to the original contract and omitted-requirements matrix. RM0090 is the actually inspected English Rev 21 and UM1974 the actually inspected English Rev 8; later catalog revisions have uninspected deltas. Register scopes cover only the normal polled, untimestamped, software-checksum profile. No whole Ethernet chapter, analog PHY certification or complete TCP event/congestion algorithm is implied.

Use [guide-reading](#guide-reading) and [guide-standards](#guide-standards) for source access and version records. T42's exact HTTP readings remain attached to the reused parser work; this module does not pretend to inspect or assign an entire HTTP RFC again.

## Implementation projects

Complete [scope and API ledger](#pr-t41-01) (4 h), [physical readiness](#pr-t41-02) (8 h), [custom MAC/DMA driver](#pr-t41-03) (10 h), [Ethernet/ARP](#pr-t41-04) (8 h), [IPv4/ICMP](#pr-t41-05) (8 h), [TCP state](#pr-t41-06) (12 h), [timers and flow](#pr-t41-07) (12 h), and [HTTP/cable closure](#pr-t41-08) (10 h). Stage every 12-hour milestone into a first host checkpoint and a second integration checkpoint without adding hours.

Run `python tools/verify_networking_fixtures.py` for the supplied finite arithmetic and trace expectations. Independently execute your C against packet/event adapters and the board. Reuse T42's wire fixture without copying its hours or delegating custom TCP to the OS. Keep captures and failure attribution alongside the evidence index from [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) and [guide-audit](#guide-audit).

## Mastery gate and feedback

Explain an unseen retained-FCS receive length, rebuild a reused TDES0, decode two latch-low status reads, checksum an odd payload and predict a modular overlap. Then reconstruct a close and RTO trace from state, not from remembered packet pictures. A reviewer injects a malformed option, ACK beyond SND.NXT, zero window and incomplete HTTP half-close; rejected inputs must neither free unacknowledged bytes nor publish partial application requests.

Repair the smallest failed invariant: a hardware-mode ledger for negotiation, a descriptor ownership log for reuse, a nested-length/checksum witness for parsing, or a state/sequence/clock table for TCP. Retest that invariant and one adjacent layer interaction. Require the per-topic three evidence items; an HTTP 200 alone cannot replace physical, ownership or failure evidence. Host-only progress records its pending physical objectives clearly.

## Consolidation and transfer

After a delay, recompute the wrap and second RTT example, then change one MSS and one odd payload length. Explain why packet boundaries and MAC padding change while HTTP semantics do not. Port the HTTP core to the board adapter without changing parser contracts. An optional second connection or IP fragmentation adds state/resource obligations and requires a new specification and source scope, rather than silently removing declared limits.

Use [guide-roadmap](#guide-roadmap), [guide-workload](#guide-workload) and [guide-integrations](#guide-integrations) to schedule T42 portable leaves before this family's final adapter. Keep the 72 project hours here, the existing parser hours there, and observed integration evidence in both cross-references.

## Environment and limits

Use a dedicated isolated Ethernet adapter and short cable, with no default route, Internet bridge, DHCP or DNS. Record actual peer MAC, adapter offload settings and capture point; offloads can alter what a host capture shows, so do not label a missing displayed checksum as a wire failure without checking that environment. Plain HTTP has no TLS or authentication claim. Fixture ISNs are deterministic; physical isolated-lab incarnation policy is documented separately and is no production security guarantee.

Profile C supplies packets/register mocks and virtual clocks. Profile E supplies actual PHY/RMII/MAC/DMA/cable measurements. Neither host mocks, QEMU, TAP, replayed captures nor a loopback client establishes physical L1 completion. Exact subset interoperability and full-host conformance are separate claims; the omitted-requirements matrix remains part of acceptance even when all cooperative-client tests pass.

## Purpose and outcomes

Explain an algorithm's cost and measure a component without turning one kind of evidence into another. This module deepens accepted C containers/algorithms, paired assembly kernels and hosted/firmware adapters with explicit analysis certificates and bounded observation protocols. Fourteen topics produce forty-two separate mastery claims; twelve small projects add 102 hours of new implementation/verification. With reading 18, assessment 8 and consolidation 6, total workload is 134 hours. Prior builds remain credited to their original modules.

The target result is a reproducible decision dossier: proved model bounds, independently checked finite traces, actual runtime observations and conditional hardware evidence each carry their own scope. Profiles C, A and optional E describe different implementation/harness/firmware boundaries, not interchangeable results.

## Entry check and remediation

Bring accepted T13/T15/T18/T23/T34 artifacts and the selected assembly/cache/quantitative and counter/deadline preludes in the front card. Before projects, explain a valid span/lifetime, one accepted short transfer, one potential initial state, the units of cycles/frequency and the difference between all-thread CPU and elapsed time. Calculate 64 cycles at 16 MHz and identify why a historical memory peak cannot identify a new run.

If an answer fails, return to that exact accepted contract, write a six-row trace and repair the missing owner-domain evidence. Do not rebuild a sorting suite or file layer inside T43. The conditional firmware work has additional exact project gates; the captured/static core route remains explicitly non-silicon evidence. No T44/T45 completion is a prerequisite.

## Component progression

**A measurement that answers a named question.** Specify workload, unit, boundary and uncertainty before choosing a counter. Distinguish asymptotic work, machine cycles, CPU time, waiting, completion and durable effects.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **A counter wrap, multiplexed event or asynchronous return producing a plausible but invalid measurement.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching

Begin with cost models and prefix reasoning, then add space/traffic/component boundaries, clock protocols and tool observations. Keep a running evidence ledger. Reserve PR-T43-03's final verification for the concluding multi-measure decision rather than spending another project budget.


<a id="t43-01"></a>

### T43.01 — Cost contracts and observable work

A complexity statement needs a cost contract. The same sort can have n records, four-byte keys and a variable-size comparator payload: those are different size measures. “One comparison” is constant only in a model that fixes its cost. Declare successful and failed operations, output size and the case quantifier before counting. Then choose a work vector instead of prematurely collapsing comparisons, moves and probes into a time estimate.

For [4,2,5,2,1,4], each earlier key greater than a later key must cross it under insertion sorting. Eight inverted pairs explain eight shifts. The scan also makes stopping comparisons, giving eleven comparisons; five final placements add to thirteen destination writes. Equal keys illustrate why comparisons can occur with no shift. Trace these events on the accepted T15 kernel in [PR-T43-01](#pr-t43-01), preserving stability.

The misconception is that a profiler number supplies the omitted model. It does not: instrumented event counts, retired instructions, target cycles and a static CFG measure have different definitions. Mastery evidence names all boundaries and predicts the count vector before running C.

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t43-02"></a>

### T43.02 — Asymptotic bounds and finite scaling evidence

Big-O says there exist a positive constant c and threshold n₀ bounding the named function above thereafter. Big-Ω supplies a lower bound; a tight Θ statement needs both. For f(n)=3n²+5n+7 and n≥1, n≤n² and 1≤n² give 3n²≤f(n)≤15n². The constants are witnesses; deleting lower terms without the quantifier is not a proof. The worst-case function is the maximum cost over valid inputs of a given size, so a lower bound on that maximum does not assert every input costs as much.

Output matters: a traversal contract 3V+2E+Z yields O(V+E+Z) under fixed record/edge work. If output generation emits Z records, an expression that erases Z may miss the dominant cost. Use [PR-T43-01](#pr-t43-01) for the quantified proof and multi-parameter worksheet.

Measured slopes are finite evidence. A function equal to n through 128 and n² afterwards looks linear at 2,4,8,16, yet costs 16900 at 130. Construct that counterexample and explain why an upper bound is neither necessarily tight nor a universal finite-size speed ranking.


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t43-02-b"></a>

<a id="t43-03"></a>

### T43.03 — Aggregate, accounting and potential analysis

Amortized analysis bounds a sequence without a probability distribution. A table growth may cost Θ(m) once while total cost over many appends is linear. Aggregate analysis adds actual costs; accounting precharges operations and keeps nonnegative credit; potential records stored work in state. Each method must name its initial state and cost primitive.

Twelve appends from an empty doubling table cost 27 unit insert/copy operations, with the ninth append alone costing 9. Charging 3 per append gives 9 credits left after twelve and no negative prefix. For Φ=2·live−capacity, Φ₀=0 and Φ₁₂=8, so Σĉ=Σc+Φ₁₂−Φ₀=35. The initial append costs amortized 2; later ones cost 3. This is a deterministic expansion certificate, not an expected average over workloads.

In [PR-T43-02](#pr-t43-02), extend the accepted T14 table with prefix rows and a nonempty-initial-state variant. Preserve allocation-failure behavior separately. Unit copies exclude allocator latency, cache stalls and arbitrary destructor work. Show actual rows, the telescoping identity and the 96-byte transient old/new payload capacity before claiming mastery.


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t43-03-b"></a>


- **T43.03.b** Build a nonnegative-credit or potential certificate and check the telescoping total at every prefix, including the declared initial state. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T43-02](#pr-t43-02).

<a id="t43-04"></a>

### T43.04 — From work to instructions, cycles and bottlenecks

An executed instruction count depends on the selected path and generated code. A cycle model additionally depends on the target's instruction/stall assumptions; elapsed time depends on clock and observation boundary. The processor equation IC×CPI/f helps separate these terms. A linear primitive count can cross cache/branch thresholds or run under different clocks, so it need not produce a universal linear-cycle relation.

The original mix 100×1+40×2+20×4 gives 260 cycles for 160 instructions: CPI 1.625. At 100 MHz, that is 2.6 µs, not 260 ns. Under a separate affected-fraction model, improving 40% of work by a factor two bounds total speedup to 1/(0.6+0.4/2)=1.25; untouched work remains. These are model calculations, not timings for either ISA.

Reuse the T36 callable kernel and T37 quantitative artifact in [PR-T43-03](#pr-t43-03). Count an executed path, compare with identified measurements, and explain a residual. Include code bytes, branches and connected-function cyclomatic e−n+2 as distinct measures. Equal static graph complexity says nothing automatic about repeated loop work or processor cycles.

<a id="t43-05"></a>

### T43.05 — Storage boundaries and lifetime peaks

Space is also a model with boundaries. Live payload, reserved capacity, retained inactive storage and scratch may overlap in time. A shared owned object is counted once, even if two views point into it. Peaks must be calculated on simultaneous states, not by adding independently occurring maxima. Static sections and measured resident/charged memory are other categories.

At time 3 the fixture has 64 live work bytes plus 80 scratch bytes: live peak 144. At time 7 work/result capacity is 128+96=224, while their payload is only 88. At time 10 work's 128 bytes remain retained although its live interval has ended. Summing 144+224+128 would count overlapping storage repeatedly and combine different times.

For stack, a .su record describes a function frame and qualifier. A feasible main/work/leaf chain is 32+48+16=96; main/other is 112. A stipulated 24-byte nonnested interrupt allowance makes 136 only for the declared known paths. Unknown callbacks, recursion or unbounded dynamic records remain unresolved. [PR-T43-04](#pr-t43-04) pairs the original ledger with actual compiler/section evidence; a sampled watermark or .bss total cannot certify a whole-program stack maximum.

<a id="t43-06"></a>

### T43.06 — Block transfers, locality and amplification

An external-memory model counts transfers of B fixed-size items between main memory M and a larger sequence N. The bounded activity fixes one disk/processor and a stated replacement/write policy. It is useful because locality can change transfer counts while comparison counts remain similar. It does not prescribe disk service latency or every bus transaction.

With four-byte items, B=2 and M=4, reading items 0..7 needs four eight-byte blocks: 32 bytes transferred for 32 useful bytes. A mixed read/write stream transfers 48 for 28 useful bytes, amplification 12/7. Dirty eviction and the final flush both matter. No-reference input has denominator zero and an undefined amplification ratio, including 0/0.

In [PR-T43-05](#pr-t43-05), add a bounded traffic adapter to existing T37 reference reasoning. Show residents, recency and dirty status at each reference. Contrast model transfers with file/syscall/device observations: warm pages, buffering, readahead and shared writeback can change the mapping. A cache miss, syscall and physical block I/O are not interchangeable events. Mastery retains item/byte units and a named layer for every ratio.

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t43-07"></a>

### T43.07 — Component runtime, overlap and completion

Component runtime needs events rather than one undifferentiated duration. A blocking return can include completion. Asynchronous submission returns acceptance, while completion and safe buffer release have separate boundaries. A fast operation can complete before its submission function returns; event semantics, not a preferred diagram shape, decide validity. POSIX AIO is the bounded concrete comparison here, with one result collection after completion and valid borrowed request/buffer storage while pending.

Submission 0, return 2 and completion 12 yield call span 2 and latency 12. Overlapping phases [0,2],[1,11],[10,12] sum to 14 but cover a union of 12. Two threads can consume 15 CPU units in that 12-unit elapsed window. Wall-minus-process-CPU then becomes −3; it is not a universal waiting estimate. Serial nested attribution can calculate exclusive time under a complete call model, but that rule cannot blindly subtract concurrent phases.

[PR-T43-06](#pr-t43-06) adds an event adapter to accepted components. Define throughput's completed-item numerator and observation window. Submit separate serial/overlap and CPU/elapsed evidence, including completion-before-return, rather than inferring hidden work from one timestamp.


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t43-07-b"></a>


- **T43.07.b** Compute end-to-end latency, throughput and scoped inclusive/exclusive serial attribution while accounting for overlapping phases rather than summing spans blindly. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T43-06](#pr-t43-06).


<a id="t43-07-c"></a>

<a id="t43-08"></a>

### T43.08 — Read/write performance and persistence

A request count is not an accepted-byte count. Positive read/write results advance by exactly that many bytes; interruptions or nonblocking unavailability need explicit bounded policy. A zero read means EOF, while the chosen bounded write adapter stops on zero progress. Terminal errors preserve the already accepted prefix instead of replaying it or concealing it.

Writing eight bytes through returns 3,EINTR,2,EAGAIN,3 accepts eight in five attempts. Buffered write completion at 8 followed by successful requested fsync at 13 has a five-unit synchronization phase. A separate device-byte observation can exceed the logical file size; the synthetic 4096/8 ratio is 512. The file, buffered transfer and media/accounting layers answer different questions.

Extend T23 in [PR-T43-07](#pr-t43-07). Preserve native file-byte verification, requested synchronization results and warm-state/file lifetime. Successful write alone does not establish durable storage; a delayed fsync error remains significant. Directory-entry synchronization is separate where creation/rename matters. No timing sample demonstrates survival under all crashes or power failures. Mastery reconciles these boundaries without an unbounded retry loop or a global cache flush.

<a id="t43-09"></a>

### T43.09 — Experimental protocol, clocks and uncertainty

Choose a clock contract before collecting numbers. CLOCK_MONOTONIC can be frequency adjusted and excludes suspend; RAW avoids that adjustment and also excludes suspend; BOOTTIME includes suspend. Process CPU counts all threads, thread CPU one thread. Resolution is a stated granularity, not accuracy or bracket overhead, and consecutive valid timestamps can be equal. Integer conversion and return errors belong in the harness contract.

For paired A/B samples, analyze each pair before summarizing. The fixture medians 102 and 98 differ by 4, while the median paired improvement is 3. Nearest-rank p95 at N=5 selects the largest sample. An empty-bracket median 11 yields a 91-unit subtraction sensitivity; it does not prove a removable constant overhead. Small signals require a changed bracket or an inconclusive conclusion.

[PR-T43-08](#pr-t43-08) adds one controlled condition and at least 31 raw pairs to existing harness work. Retain warmup, order, checksum, outliers and clock identity. Report observed deadline misses/reference jitter and confounders. Sample quantiles and maxima describe the recorded trials; they are not WCET or a universal deadline guarantee.

<a id="t43-10"></a>

### T43.10 — Linux PMU counting and sampling boundaries

PMU counters observe selected events under hardware, kernel, privilege and scheduling constraints. Identify target, event meaning, binary and permitted user/kernel scope. Generalized cache references are not universally load counts; unsupported or denied events are unavailable rather than zero. The source baseline does not promise access on a stricter distribution/container.

When raw instructions=1200 and cycles=3000 with enabled=20/running=10, extrapolated values are 2400 and 6000. A co-scheduled matching group gives CPI 2.5. Positive running time is necessary; zero supplies no finite scaling. Matching numeric intervals on unrelated groups do not make their ratio trustworthy. Scaling assumes the observed partial interval represents the rest; a nonstationary workload can defeat that assumption.

In [PR-T43-09](#pr-t43-09), extend the accepted T34 raw ledger and preserve permitted or denied actual output. Relate a usable event to the work contract, and compare grouped count/sampling evidence without treating attribution as ownership. The finite certificate checks result semantics. It does not prove PMU availability, target cache behavior or reconstructed unobserved counts.

<a id="t43-10-c"></a>

<a id="t43-11"></a>

### T43.11 — cgroup CPU, memory and I/O accounting

cgroup v2 supplies resource policy and scoped accounting. cpu.max configures temporal fair-class bandwidth; cpu.stat observes usage/throttling. memory.current is a charged-memory gauge; high/max are different control boundaries. io.stat reports keyed major:minor counters, whereas io.max configures limits. Delegation and ancestor constraints decide who can change what. A useful read-only investigation needs no new privileges.

The original snapshot adds 800 µs CPU in a 2000-µs window, fraction 0.4; a configured 500/1000 quota ratio is 0.5. They need not coincide. memory.current can decrease while historical memory.peak is 12288. Reset semantics apply to subsequent reads on the same open descriptor; without that reset no fresh-window peak is established. Per-device byte deltas and PSI totals have their own units; pressure is not exclusive component waiting.

[PR-T43-10](#pr-t43-10) parses by key and distinguishes absent controllers from zero. Core route reads permitted files or records denial plus captured analysis. A prepared delegated experiment is optional and preserves/restores authorized state. Filesystem writeback support/shared-inode attribution, descendants and counter reset remain limits. Show policy versus observation and avoid a false isolated-memory claim.


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t43-11-a"></a>


- **T43.11.a** Inspect a permitted cgroupv2 hierarchy/controller/delegation snapshot and distinguish observation files from configuration and inherited restrictions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T43-10](#pr-t43-10).


<a id="t43-11-b"></a>


- **T43.11.b** Interpret keyed CPU-time/throttle, current/peak memory, per-device byte/IO and pressure deltas with units and scope, retaining per-FD peak-reset and writeback-attribution limits. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T43-10](#pr-t43-10).


<a id="t43-11-c"></a>


- **T43.11.c** Compare a bounded workload with unchanged observations or a prepared delegated quota experiment, explaining quota/pressure effects while preserving an explicit no-root unavailable-controller route. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T43-10](#pr-t43-10).


<a id="t43-12"></a>

### T43.12 — Compiler-based profiling and its perturbation

Compiler instrumentation observes a changed program. -pg needs matching compile/link boundaries and a supported runtime; --coverage counts selected execution arcs, not elapsed time. Entry/exit hooks can give a bounded serial call ledger, but must exclude themselves and avoid recursion/allocation/I/O hazards. Conceptual inline calls, code growth, dropped records and nonlocal exits limit completeness.

For complete work [0,9] containing child [1,4] and [5,7], inclusive work is 9 and exclusive work 4. A truncated buffer with open frames cannot supply exact durations. gprof samples self CPU time and propagates child time using an average-per-call assumption: two cheap/expensive caller populations can invalidate it. The original 20-ms child with two A/eight B calls predicts 4/16 ms, but declared actual 16/4 gives ±12-ms error. Off-CPU I/O delay is absent from that self-time estimate.

[PR-T43-11](#pr-t43-11) uses a reused single-threaded component, matched baseline, bounded hooks and a supported/unavailable gprof comparison. Record measured perturbation and code/.su changes. Mastery separates counts, samples, inferred children and elapsed waiting boundaries rather than calling instrumentation transparent.


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t43-12-a"></a>


- **T43.12.a** Build matching uninstrumented and instrumented variants of a reused single-threaded component and verify -pg/coverage or entry/exit hook build/runtime boundaries. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T43-11](#pr-t43-11).


<a id="t43-12-b"></a>


- **T43.12.b** Record bounded hook/arc/call or gprof samples and explain inline, recursion/exclusion, dropped-record and caller-dependent attribution limitations. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T43-11](#pr-t43-11).


<a id="t43-12-c"></a>


- **T43.12.c** Compare measured overhead and code/stack effects against the baseline, separating counted execution, sampled self time, estimated children time and off-CPU waiting. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T43-11](#pr-t43-11).


<a id="t43-13"></a>

### T43.13 — Bare-metal cycle and timer measurement

CYCCNT is an optional 32-bit processor-clock counter. Exact Armv7-M architecture addresses/fields are the start of an access contract, not proof that every board has an available counter. DEMCR.TRCENA must make trace reads meaningful; with it clear, DWT reads are UNKNOWN. Counter presence, access, enable, clock, device errata, interrupt/debug conditions and setup ownership must be checked before a claim.

Endpoints 4294967280→48 have a modulo delta 64. Only an independent interval bound below 2³² rules out additional wraps. At 16 MHz that is 4000 ns; removing an eight-cycle empty bracket yields a sensitivity 3500 ns. Debug state stops the counter, so halt-spanning active cycles cannot simply represent wall time. An unknown/absent counter is not a zero-cycle result.

[PR-T43-12](#pr-t43-12) requires the captured/static certificate. Optional silicon execution follows its firmware-specific gates and reuses existing setup/kernel/timer work. Preserve other debug bits and users; never reset a shared counter merely for a tidy sample. Timer/GPIO alternatives name their own clock/resolution observer. Emulators support correctness evidence, not measured silicon cycles, energy or sampled-tail WCET.


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t43-13-a"></a>


- **T43.13.a** Check the selected core/device counter presence, access, enable, processor clock and debug/interrupt conditions before claiming a cycle observation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T43-12](#pr-t43-12).


<a id="t43-13-b"></a>


- **T43.13.b** Compute a bounded modular cycle delta and clock-unit conversion, reject ambiguous multi-wrap intervals and compare empty-bracket overhead with a reused kernel. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T43-12](#pr-t43-12).


<a id="t43-13-c"></a>


- **T43.13.c** Produce silicon measurements or a clearly labeled captured/static certificate, documenting timer/GPIO alternatives and refusing emulator timing, energy or sampled-tail WCET claims. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T43-12](#pr-t43-12).


<a id="t43-14"></a>

### T43.14 — Choosing useful measures and making a performance decision

Choose measures from requirements. Useful work units, cycles/time, completed-item throughput, per-item latency, peak/retained space, code size, branches/traffic and deadline jitter form a vector. A single score can conceal an unacceptable resource. Energy needs a documented observable/instrument or declared physical model; elapsed time alone is insufficient. Cyclomatic complexity is a static design/test aid, not either Big-O or runtime cycles; feasible paths and fault freedom remain separate.

Variant B is faster in the fixture's model (240 versus 260 cycles) but exceeds both code and retained-storage limits. A is the accepted candidate. Equal cyclomatic v=3 graphs have sequential 2n versus nested n² body work; that shared static number cannot settle a speed decision. A different traffic/jitter constraint could change the accepted choice again.

Complete [PR-T43-03](#pr-t43-03)'s reserved decision dossier after the observation projects. It must cite the requirement, each accepted/rejected candidate, omitted measures and revision/build/workload. Label algebraic proof, finite fixture arithmetic, actual learner runtime and optional silicon/energy separately. A rigorous inconclusive or baseline-retention decision can pass; a fast number with missing boundaries cannot.


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t43-14-a"></a>


- **T43.14.a** Select a justified vector of time, latency/throughput, space, work, traffic and code/control-flow measures for an original requirement and explain the omitted observables. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T43-03](#pr-t43-03).


<a id="t43-14-b"></a>


- **T43.14.b** Resolve a case where a faster measured variant increases retained storage, traffic, static test complexity or jitter, using stated acceptance limits rather than a single score. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T43-03](#pr-t43-03).


<a id="t43-14-c"></a>


- **T43.14.c** Submit a reproducible evidence and limitations ledger distinguishing proved model bounds, finite fixture checks, learner runtime observations and conditional energy/hardware evidence. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T43-03](#pr-t43-03).

## Reading guidance

Use the front-card locators as bounded assignments. CLRS supplies formal quantifiers and deterministic prefix proofs; it does not predict allocator or target time. The architecture equation is a declared model; recompute its units and exclude the known inconsistent copied numerical examples. Vitter defines fixed-item block parameters; its historical device numbers are not today's measurements. NIST supplies the connected-function static CFG convention and its feasible-path limits.

Read Linux interfaces alongside the specific observation adapter: clocks/AIO/read/write/fsync before phase logs; PMU/security before permitted counts; cgroup/PSI before interpreting keyed snapshots. GCC/gprof scopes govern matching builds, stack qualifiers and perturbation. The exact Arm scopes govern only the optional counter certificate and ownership/presence/halt boundaries. Assigned reading cards total 15 hours; use the remaining 3 reading hours to recompute formulas, compare actual tool records and annotate the accepted source scopes. Wider chapters, additional PMU tables or board-specific setup recipes require fresh inspection before becoming an assigned authority.

## Mastery gate and feedback

Spend the 8 assessment hours on a cold explanation plus evidence audit. For every topic, point to three separate evidence items matching its objective claims. An assessor changes one input/case/clock/scope and asks for a prediction before execution. Require all twelve finite certificates, their rejection controls, actual demanded C/tool observations and honest unavailable/conditional routes; static fixture success cannot replace a required C count adapter or native clock trial.

Explain a formal bound with constants, a nonempty-state potential correction, unequal simultaneous space peaks, zero useful-byte amplification, completion-before-return, process CPU greater than wall, historical cgroup peak, zero-running PMU estimate and ambiguous wrap. Explain why equal cyclomatic v does not imply equal work. Repair a failed claim at its mechanism: missing prefix credit needs a corrected state proof, not more timing runs; missing observation needs a correctly scoped experiment, not a stronger asymptotic label. Reassess the exact leaf with a fresh input. The final decision dossier records justified acceptance, rejection or inconclusive evidence.

## Consolidation and transfer

Use 6 delayed hours for two transfer reviews. After a week, choose an already accepted different kernel/component and rebuild its cost/event contract on paper before instrumenting; after a second interval, examine one deliberately misleading performance claim and identify missing size, clock, layer, attribution or evidence. Credit prior owner-domain work once. Keep one frozen dossier with source locator/build/raw samples and limitations so a second reader can reproduce the bounded result.

Connect the work to [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory), [guide-reading](#guide-reading), [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles), [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment), [guide-workload](#guide-workload) and [guide-performance-debugging](#guide-performance-debugging). Integration reuse organizes these completed artifacts; it adds no duplicated implementation hours.

## Environment and limits

Core hosted observations use permitted interfaces and disposable files. Controller/PMU/gprof access can be absent; record an actual attempt and explicit unavailable result rather than changing global policy or claiming zero work. A prepared delegated cgroup or exclusive board trace session is optional. CPU clock/event meaning, compiler/runtime, filesystem writeback, shared descendants/inodes, asynchronous phases and device/debug/interrupt state remain named limitations.

The Arm route's static/captured evidence is mandatory and its actual silicon implementation is optional, with additional firmware gates in PR-T43-12. Emulation demonstrates functional execution, not silicon timing. No project claims energy without an instrument/source, experimental crash durability, whole-program stack proof from .su alone, or WCET from sampled maxima. tools/verify_performance_fixtures.py independently verifies finite arithmetic/semantic certificates and strict owned file correspondence; it does not compile or solve the learner's C, mutate host controls or certify hardware.

# T44 — Debugging from symptoms to causal evidence

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cross-track | core | 114 | A, B |

**Prerequisites:** [T03](#t03), [T07](#t07).

**Required selected foundations:** [T21.07.a](#t21-07-a), [T21.08.a](#t21-08-a), [T32.01.b](#t32-01-b), [T32.14.a](#t32-14-a). Complete those leaves before the dependent project; the rest of the referenced domain need not be finished.

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 18 | 56 | 26 | 8 | 6 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Develop a diagnosis that survives a changed input, build or environment. T44 turns symptoms into replayable evidence, locates the first violated contract, tests competing causes and verifies a causal repair. It reuses existing components and tool practices; new hours cover the intentional defect, dossier and transfer. Ten projects of 4–12 hours total 82 hours; with reading 18 hours, assessment 8 hours and consolidation 6 hours, the module totals 114 hours. The 82 hours are implementation 56+verification 26, not an additional allocation.

## Entry check and remediation

After T03/T07, explain a valid object/lifetime, compile a two-function C program and test a boundary without executing UB. Complete only the named T21 assertion/logging and T32 fixture/replay leaves for the first milestone. If a learner cannot distinguish observed output from a hypothesis, use the defined assignment/counter faults in PR-T44-01/03 and repeat one discriminating test. The first three milestones need no completed T24/T25/T27/T31/T33 or T45 module. Later briefs list their exact selected preludes and reused artifacts; prerequisite time belongs to those existing exercises. A full-program order may place T44 later, while this novice diagnostic route selects only its entry leaves.

Use [guide-entry](#guide-entry), [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles) and [guide-roadmap](#guide-roadmap) for entry/dependency policy. Every project keeps predicted, observed, inferred and open claims distinct. A tool absence has a supported alternate environment or a narrower model task, with the dependent runtime claim left open.

## Component progression

**A diagnosis that discriminates competing causes.** Seal the prediction, establish a same-failure reproducer and choose an observation before editing. Preserve the earliest supported invalid transition and an adjacent case rejecting a symptom-only patch.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **A delayed variant with a different root cause but the same visible crash.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t44-01"></a>

### T44.01 — Observation, contracts and replay identity

A symptom is an observation; a cause is an explanation that survives discriminating tests. Record the expected contract before the first run: input range, state/effect limits, output on failure and finite completion policy. Preserve source revision, compiler/flags, image hash, input hash, configuration, platform and timeout. A log paired with the wrong image is not the same experiment. PR-T44-01's image A / input abc record matches, whereas image B with image A symbols does not. Its digest identifies bytes, not their authenticity.

Predict two causes before editing: for an accepted out-of-range request, either validation was removed or validation changed the input. Observe the parameter immediately before/after validation to separate them. Keep expected, observed, inferred and open claims in separate fields. An isolated deterministic harness makes hypotheses cheap to test; a synthetic expected history remains a model. A build that happened to print the expected value says little about an untested boundary. Retain the first useful cause separately from secondary cleanup/logging failures and reduce one diagnostic variable at a time.

Apply in [PR-T44-01](#pr-t44-01). Evidence must separately address these objective checks:

- `T44.01.a`: Write an observation record that separates actual output, expected contract, inference and an untested hypothesis.

- `T44.01.b`: Reproduce a bounded failure with input, source/image/configuration/environment identities and a finite timeout.

- `T44.01.c`: Predict two competing causes and select a discriminating observation before changing the program.

<a id="t44-02"></a>

### T44.02 — Build diagnostics, assertions and bounded logs

Use an explicit dialect and a warning build such as cc -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -Wformat=2 -g -Og on a supported GCC environment. Record the actual version and accepted options; GCC 15.2 is the inspected contract, not an installed-tool claim. -Wall enables a selected set, not every warning. The faulty admissible function in PR-T44-01 assigns n=0 in its condition, then accepts every supplied value. This is a defined logic error, so its source transition is suitable for a first novice investigation. A warning is a lead: parenthesizing the assignment may silence it while preserving the defect. Repair the intended 1..4 relation and test 0, 1, 4, 5.

External validation must survive NDEBUG. Assertions express internal promises, and their expressions must not perform a required operation. Reuse T21's three-record ring with overflow policy and an independent first-cause field: four events retain the last three while the first cause stays E_INPUT. Disable each diagnostic channel independently, then verify no diagnostic-only side effect is evaluated and required validation still runs. Bounded logs can drop events and change timing; retain those limits and compare a release build. A clean warning build or debug-only repair is not a correctness certificate.

Apply in [PR-T44-01](#pr-t44-01). Evidence must separately address these objective checks:

- `T44.02.a`: Interpret warnings and generate a matching debug-information build while retaining the production optimization comparison.

- `T44.02.b`: Separate internal assertions from durable external validation and make a bounded diagnostic log preserve the first useful cause.

- `T44.02.c`: Demonstrate that disabled assertions or logs do not erase required validation or evaluate diagnostic-only side effects.

<a id="t44-03"></a>

### T44.03 — Minimal reproducers and input reduction

Specify one same-failure predicate before reducing input. PASS means the selected contract holds; FAIL means the selected failure persists; UNRESOLVED means a malformed candidate, another symptom, or an unclassified replay. Treating UNRESOLVED as PASS can produce an invalid alleged minimality result. The inspected ddmin algorithm tries subsets and complements, keeps a failing smaller configuration and increases partition granularity when no reduction works. Use at most 16 chunks, bounded work/time, a stable configuration identity and cached test outcomes. Reuse the T32 replay harness; write only the new reducer and small original input grammar.

The eight-chunk fixture fails when it contains 1, 7, 8 together or 2, 3 together; a partial 1/7/8 group without either complete trigger is unresolved. The candidate 1, 7, 8 fails and all three single deletions are unresolved, so it is 1-minimal. Yet 2, 3 is a smaller failing input. Exhaustive finite enumeration is the independent fixture oracle, distinct from the learner reducer. Check every remaining single deletion and retain the actual replay classification. The reduced input localizes a trigger; inspect the first invalid code transition separately to explain the repair.

Apply in [PR-T44-02](#pr-t44-02). Evidence must separately address these objective checks:

- `T44.03.a`: Define PASS, same-failure FAIL and UNRESOLVED outcomes with a stable finite replay contract.

- `T44.03.b`: Implement a bounded original token reducer using subset/complement trials and preserve the failing input grammar.

- `T44.03.c`: Check every single remaining deletion to certify 1-minimality and explain why it does not prove global minimality or causal code repair.

<a id="t44-04"></a>

### T44.04 — Stepping, scopes and call stacks

Begin with initialized valid storage and a defined logic defect. A counter used represents admitted records with invariant 0<=used<=capacity. The faulty condition used>capacity admits a fifth record at capacity 4; the counter reaches 5 without requiring an invalid memory access. `break try_acquire if *used == cap` can stop before this transition when symbols permit it. Use step to enter, next to stay at the current source level, finish to return and stepi/nexti for machine instructions. State which transition each command observes; source stepping is not an instruction-by-instruction history.

Frames and scopes select different objects. In the supplied synthetic two-frame example, probe's status 7 differs from caller's status 2. Use bt full, frame 0 and frame 1, then inspect the appropriate name/argument. A selected frame's locals may be incomplete in a machine prologue or absent after optimization. Save the command transcript and exact image/symbol identities; an unavailable value is not evidence that its source variable was zero. Reuse the prior minimization/backtrace practice, add this new counter defect and explain why the final count 4 after a release hides the earlier violation 5.

Apply in [PR-T44-03](#pr-t44-03). Evidence must separately address these objective checks:

- `T44.04.a`: Use source and instruction stepping to stop before the first contract-violating transition in a learner-owned C program.

- `T44.04.b`: Select frames and scopes to distinguish the current local, a shadowed name and the caller’s arguments.

- `T44.04.c`: Record a backtrace with matching symbols and state what optimized-out or unavailable values prevent it from proving.

<a id="t44-05"></a>

### T44.05 — Conditional breakpoints and watchpoints

Choose a stopping mechanism from a hypothesis. A pure breakpoint condition used==capacity tests the admission boundary without calling code that changes inferior state. A watch on a live, initialized object tests a particular value change. Avoid dereferencing a guessed address or an expired local. Hardware watches typically stop at the responsible instruction, while software watches can stop at the next statement and are much slower. GDB's current manual states that software watches observe only the current thread; they do not establish another thread's writes.

The fixture requests an eight-byte watch on a four-byte-width target and three watches with only two slots. Both exceed its declared geometry; those numbers are a model, not F439 capabilities. Actual hardware availability and insertion/resume errors must be collected. Narrow the watched valid object, use a pure breakpoint, or add a bounded replay log when unsupported. This changes the claim's granularity and perturbation. A watchpoint shows a change, which may occur after the first invalid state; compare it with the contract transition and retain the earliest corroborated violation. Document object lifetime, scope expiry, thread focus, width and slot limits.

Apply in [PR-T44-03](#pr-t44-03). Evidence must separately address these objective checks:

- `T44.05.a`: Choose a pure conditional breakpoint or valid-object watchpoint from a falsifiable hypothesis.

- `T44.05.b`: Compare the first observed changed value with the earliest invalid state and account for hardware/software stopping granularity.

- `T44.05.c`: Document target width/slot, thread and lifetime limits and choose a bounded alternative when the watch cannot be installed.


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

### T44.06 — Optimized images, ABI, disassembly and cores

Debug symbols describe generated code; they do not require every source variable or source ordering to survive optimization. GCC permits -g with optimization and explains why -Og can collect useful debug information. Compare matched -Og and production-optimized images, but diagnose the production failure itself. Use info line and disassemble /s or /r to map a stopped PC to a range and inspect the actual branch/call. PR-T44-04 maps synthetic PC 4098 into half-open 4096..4100, source line 42. This teaching map is not a real compiler output.

Reuse a selected ABI probe. Under the inspected historical SysV AMD64 scope, the example entry stack 4104 has the expected 16-byte relation; a changed preserved register 11 → 12 violates the chosen boundary even though the stack returns unchanged. Confirm the actual ABI/build variant before generalizing. A core or saved state needs the matching executable and symbols and can omit memory. The fixture contains registers/text but no heap; unavailable heap state stays open. A core is a stopped snapshot, not the preceding history. If cores are unavailable, compare a valid bounded saved-state record and collect an actual live stop; do not rename the synthetic record a core.

<a id="t44-07"></a>

### T44.07 — Memory fault diagnosis through reused invariants

Reuse object extents, allocator ownership and T32's isolated faulty/repaired memory variants. The finite model marks an offset 4 write into extent 4 invalid, a read after free invalid, an uninitialized value use invalid and an old alias after successful nonzero resize invalid. Failed resize preserves the old allocation and valid aliases under the declared contract. Even a successful in-place realloc ends the old allocation lifetime; old aliases must be re-derived from the returned pointer. Deep stack, fixed-region and asynchronous memory practice belongs in T45 rather than a duplicate allocator implementation here.

Keep the language violation distinct from its observed symptom. A tool might report a later visible use, the process might continue, and a clean run may miss the path. Run separate supported ASan/UBSan and unsanitized Memcheck tracks; use origins where available. ASan alone is not an initialization detector. Record the first invalid source/lifetime transition, each actual tool report or silence, flags and environment. Repair before the invalid transition, verify ownership/failure state, then transfer to a different extent or failure point. An oracle's invalid-event index cannot certify an actual diagnostic or prescribed UB output.

Apply in [PR-T44-05](#pr-t44-05). Evidence must separately address these objective checks:

- `T44.07.a`: Locate a bounds, lifetime or initialization contract violation in an isolated learner-owned program using existing T03/T16/T21/T32 artifacts.

- `T44.07.b`: Reconcile sanitizer, unsanitized Memcheck and source-level evidence while retaining unsupported or clean-run uncertainty.

- `T44.07.c`: Repair the first invalid access or ownership transition and transfer the diagnosis to a changed input without prescribing a UB symptom.

<a id="t44-08"></a>

### T44.08 — I/O, errno and descriptor failure histories

A stream cursor advances by each positive byte count, not by the requested count or the last count alone. For seven bytes and results 2, EINTR, 2, EAGAIN, 3 the retained offsets are 2, 2, 4, 4, 7. EINTR before progress and EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK leave the cursor unchanged; a successful short result already accounts for progress. A positive-count stream read 0 means EOF, while a zero write requires the declared zero-progress policy and a finite bound. Reuse T24's cursors and event state rather than write another event loop. Reject impossible adapter counts before arithmetic.

Capture errno immediately after the operation indicates failure, before logging can overwrite it. ENOSPC followed by logging EIO still has original cause ENOSPC. Pthread functions return direct statuses, so that layer does not use this errno rule. EPIPE with default SIGPIPE may terminate before the return is observed; an explicitly handled/ignored signal disposition makes a different experiment. Positive write means local acceptance, not durable storage or peer consumption. On Linux, close releases the descriptor early, so retry after an error can close a reused number/generation. The inspected POSIX.1-2024 EINTR rule differs; label this exercise Linux. Use an injected/capped EMFILE ledger first; any actual exhaustion test is limited to the isolated learner process, at most eight owned records, with cleanup and no system-wide ENFILE campaign.

Apply in [PR-T44-06](#pr-t44-06). Evidence must separately address these objective checks:

- `T44.08.a`: Trace positive partial progress, zero/EOF, EINTR and EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK without discarding or duplicating bytes.

- `T44.08.b`: Capture errno only after the relevant failure and diagnose EPIPE/SIGPIPE and bounded per-process descriptor exhaustion.

- `T44.08.c`: Repair cursor/ownership cleanup under the declared Linux close contract and explain its POSIX.1-2024 portability limit.

<a id="t44-09"></a>

### T44.09 — Concurrency, deadlock and lost events

Reproduce a schedule before drawing a timing conclusion. If A holds lock L and waits for B's lock R while B holds lock R and waits for A's lock L, the finite wait-for graph has a cycle. Whole-thread backtraces can corroborate a stopped instance; the graph and one run are not every future schedule. A non-atomic write and read to the same object on different threads, without a happens-before edge, are an unordered conflict in the fixture. Its repaired ownership/mutex argument must supply the edge; volatile and longer sleeps do not supply it. A data race has no promised final value.

The lost-wakeup fixture has consumer check false, producer set true/signal, consumer waits. Fixing only the sleep length leaves that window. Reuse T25's predicate-under-the-same-mutex protocol: the wait releases atomically, the producer changes state while holding the mutex, and the consumer rechecks after reacquisition and every wakeup. Save forced schedules, thread identities, direct API statuses and a written ordering/lifetime argument. Supported detector runs and stress add exercised evidence. Halting or logging can hide a race; a detector's silence and one deterministic history do not close all schedules or establish fairness.

Apply in [PR-T44-07](#pr-t44-07). Evidence must separately address these objective checks:

- `T44.09.a`: Reconstruct a forced event schedule, happens-before obligations and a wait-for graph while separating mutex correctness from timing observations.

- `T44.09.b`: Diagnose a race, deadlock or predicate/wakeup defect using reused T24/T25 programs and whole-thread observations.

- `T44.09.c`: Test a causal synchronization repair with controlled schedules and detector runs while leaving unobserved schedules open.

<a id="t44-10"></a>

### T44.10 — Bare-metal startup, faults and asynchronous state

Reuse the selected F439 startup/image and basic exception decoder. The fixture reset word 0x08000101 denotes Thumb entry 0x08000100. IRQ 3 corresponds to exception 19 and vector 0x0800004C. EXC_RETURN 0xFFFFFFFD selects the scoped basic PSP/Thread return; with aligned pre-PSP 0x20001000 and no padding, eight words start 0x20000FE0. Optional extended FP frames, padding and nested-handler details need their own supported interpretation rather than this simplified model.

CFSR 0x8200 indicates precise BusFault plus BFAR valid; HFSR 0x40000000 records forced escalation. The imprecise 0x400 case has no valid BFAR, so the stale address is not usable evidence and stacked PC is not promised to identify the responsible access. Compare bad startup, peripheral clock/pin sequencing and invalid ownership as competing hypotheses. Do not inspect arbitrary side-effecting MMIO in the debugger. The policy model's configure-before-enable violates its stage invariant; actual peripheral effects require device evidence/measurement. DMA cancellation request leaves ownership with DMA until stop acknowledgment; the third CPU write is invalid even if the core is halted. The selected F439 SRAM/DMA path has no core data-cache maintenance requirement. Static arithmetic, emulator observations and physical fault/electrical observations remain separately labelled.

Apply in [PR-T44-08](#pr-t44-08). Evidence must separately address these objective checks:

- `T44.10.b`: Discriminate a bad peripheral setup, invalid stacked state and ISR/DMA ownership defect without blindly reading side-effecting MMIO.

- `T44.10.c`: Repair a documented initialization or completion invariant and keep static, emulator and physical-target claims separate.

<a id="t44-11"></a>

### T44.11 — Sanitizer, static, fuzz and differential evidence

Choose a tool by the defect class and supported environment. Reuse T32's separate dynamic tracks, bounded fuzz seeds, independent differential reference and static review; do not build another fuzz framework. Static over-approximation can produce alarms that are not demonstrated executions. Eva's inspected scope does not directly model asynchronous interrupts. ASan, UBSan, thread instrumentation and Memcheck have distinct contracts and incompatible/unsupported combinations; record actual versions/options and instrumented versus release behavior. Unsupported capability is an open tool claim, not a clean run.

The original u8 contract is saturating addition. For 100+50, 250+10, 255+1 the mathematical reference returns 150, 255, 255 while a defined uint8_t narrowing defect returns 150, 4, 0. A differentially failing sum begins at 256; the candidate 255, 1 is one boundary example, not the unique smallest operand pair. Build a bounded original C implementation and test harness, then preserve a minimized failing pair and an independent arithmetic oracle. Each clean run covers only its executed scope; a static model/fixture does not establish a sanitizer message. Triangulate the source transition with actual supported evidence, explain disagreement and retain unsupported observations honestly.

<a id="t44-12"></a>

### T44.12 — Causal repair, regression and delayed blind transfer

A causal repair prevents the first invalid transition. A symptom patch may only hide its final effect. At used 4/capacity 4, reject-before-commit keeps state valid and reports full; clamp-after-commit temporarily reaches 5 before restoring 4. The identical final count does not make the histories equivalent. Test the minimized trigger, normal/boundary/invalid neighbors, failure cleanup and matched debug/release/instrumented images. A fix whose check only exists in an assertion fails the release contract. Save raw observations and remaining scope limits instead of matching diagnostic wording.

Progress through guided investigation, symptom-only investigation, then delayed transfer. The supplied public fixture/oracle is visible, so it is guided practice, not a blind assessment. A peer/reviewer supplies a genuinely withheld new variant, or a solo learner commits to an unopened seeded variant and reveals its oracle only after submitting the predictions, first-invalid-state evidence and repair. Revisit after at least seven days. Self-authored faults retain limited independence even when delayed; state this and use an independent reviewer when possible. Remediate the mistaken inference or invariant, then retry a different withheld variant rather than rereading every module.

- `T44.12.b`: Replay the minimized trigger, adjacent boundary cases and matched debug/release/instrumented builds with explicit observation categories.

- `T44.12.c`: Diagnose a delayed unseen variant from an evidence dossier and record remaining claims instead of reusing memorized diagnostic strings.

## Reading guidance

The metadata assigns 18 bounded one-hour passages, including the original ISSTA 2000 reduction argument, GDB's captured development snapshot, GCC 15.2 and exact Linux/POSIX/Arm contracts. Read the named locator and limits rather than an entire manual. Further accepted ABI, POSIX memory, ST DMA/boot and Eva passages remain available through the reused T08/T25/T27/T29/T31/T33 lessons. A prior source acceptance supports only its inspected scope. The held Vidović book supplies a layered crash example on its own SEGGER platform; compare it with the official contract rather than importing a proprietary setup or promised C-UB trap. Grenning's host-to-target cycle explains which evidence must be recollected for each boundary.

## Implementation projects

Complete PR-T44-01..03 as the novice diagnosis spine, then PR-T44-04/05 for image/memory evidence. Enter PR-T44-06/07 only with the stated hosted I/O/concurrency leaves, and PR-T44-08 with the selected firmware artifacts. PR-T44-09 compares tool/reference evidence; PR-T44-10 assesses delayed transfer. Adapt PR-T21-03, PR-T24-04, PR-T25-05, PR-T31-01/02 and PR-T32-05/07 instead of rebuilding logs, event loops, queues, allocators or fuzzers. T45 is optional deep memory practice with no mandatory dependency in this module.

The supplied fixtures are finite model histories with independent static certificates. The learner owns original C and its fault/repaired variants. Run the static oracle separately from actual C/debugger/tool/hardware collection. Strict fixture/catalog checks reject missing, unexpected nested, duplicate, mistyped or wrongly bound artifacts. Model outcomes are not runtime observations.

## Mastery gate and feedback

For every a/b/c objective, supply its explanation, evidence and scope. A complete dossier includes expected contract; pre-run competing predictions; source/image/configuration/environment identities; finite replay/actual observation; earliest invalid transition; discriminating hypothesis test; minimized tri-state trigger; invariant repair/limits; regression matrix and changed variant. The novice gate requires one warning/validation investigation and one counter / watch investigation. The later gate requires a systems/firmware dossier with its selected preludes, a tool-disagreement explanation and a causal-repair counterexample. Missing runtime capability leaves that claim open instead of passing a different property silently.

Use guided→symptom-only→delayed assessment. Visible public fixtures/oracles are guided, not blind. A reviewer/peer withholds a new variant, or a solo learner commits to an unopened seeded variant and reveals its oracle only after the submitted dossier. Separate this from self-authored fault practice, whose independence is limited. Feedback names the faulty inference, state transition or contract; the retry uses another variant.

## Consolidation and transfer

After at least seven days, diagnose a withheld new boundary, cleanup, schedule or stale-generation variant without reopening the old answer. Predict which image/input/tool/target evidence must be recollected. Retain rejected hypotheses and an example symptom patch that final-state checks would miss. Summarize the actual remaining claims rather than treating one successful transfer as every-case correctness.

## Environment and limits

GDB's inspected 19.0.50.20261009-git manual is a current development snapshot. Installed compiler/debugger, target watch resources, permissions, core generation and tool platforms must be recorded. Watchpoints can expire or miss other threads; optimization can erase variables; logs/stops/instrumentation perturb timing. Dynamic tools observe supported executed paths, static tools require context and may alarm conservatively, and cores omit history/memory. Undefined behavior and data races have no prescribed symptom. Linux close/EINTR policy is not a portable generic POSIX rule. The F439/basic-frame/static model excludes unsupported FP/padding/board effects; the selected F439 SRAM/DMA path has no core data-cache maintenance requirement. No fixture or emulator certifies physical timing, peripheral effects or electrical behavior.

## Third-edition implementation handoff

T50–T56 extend controlled diagnosis to context corruption, missed wakeups, priority inversion, remote scheduling, cache visibility and late completion. A longer stress run is not a causal explanation.

## Purpose and outcomes

Learn to diagnose and repair memory and resource failures with evidence that distinguishes object bounds, initialization, lifetime and capacity. The result is ten small original experiments and repair dossiers, built on earlier APIs and harnesses. Each gives a prediction, controlled negative observation, first-invalid-state argument, repair and new regression/transfer cases.

## Entry check and remediation

Before PR-T45-01 explain ownership after failed nonzero resize, a bounded NUL scan, a three-stage cleanup prefix and the difference between a model and actual tool evidence. Revisit selected T03/T21/T32 leaves when needed. PR-T45-04 adds T13 stack analysis and T23 checked process/limit setup; PR-T45-05 adds T27 layout/startup. PR-T45-09 adds the T29 DMA/ordering leaves. The front card records these selected imports; early hosted milestones do not require completing every firmware laboratory first.

Use [guide-entry](#guide-entry) and [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted feedback. Repair integer interval/multiplication reasoning in PR-T45-02/03, maximum path sums in 04, aligned interval placement in 05 and root reachability in 06. State the equation and one counterexample before returning to C; no unrelated mathematics restart is required.

## Component progression

**A memory defect with a paired repaired control.** Distinguish extent, initialization, lifetime, placement and capacity failures. Compare native, diagnostic and abstract histories without promising deterministic undefined-behavior symptoms.

Before implementation, predict this discriminating case: **A global-object overwrite mislabeled as a dynamically growing .bss, or clearing one pointer presented as repair of every stale alias.** Carry its evidence into the projects below. Reuse one accepted component revision; new projects charge their new mechanism or experiment, not a second implementation of the old one.

Follow the [project route](#guide-project-route) for ordering. Domain numbers are reference categories. The [laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts) separate automatic execution from reasoning, transfer and physical observations.

## Study sequence and teaching

Reuse a prior implementation or write a small owned example; do not consume a supplied solved C program. Run one deliberately faulty mechanism per supervised hosted process. Preserve input, build identity and observation before repair, then repeat with identical controls. Native undefined behavior does not have a prescribed output, crash signal or address.


<a id="t45-01"></a>

### T45.01 — Controlled observation and detection contracts

An experiment starts with a claim and its detection contract. An extent monitor checks permitted addresses; an initialization monitor follows valid values; a resource ledger checks acquired and retained objects. Each can miss a different kind of defect. Name the exercised path, monitored boundary, runtime dependencies and observations before running the faulty version. An unavailable tool is an unresolved observation; a setup failure is not evidence about the target.

Worked trace: a negative control produces a report, a repaired trial produces no report, and another negative trial is silent. These results establish detection for the first exercised trial and support the repaired trial's selected checks. The silent faulty trial remains inconclusive. They do not establish a universal memory-safety property. A report also needs a matching binary and an explanation of the first invalid state; later runs after corruption can obscure that state.

Reuse the T32 harness in PR-T45-01. Record exact compile/link commands, sanitizer options, symbols, supervisor limits and tool versions for native, ASan/UBSan and separate unsanitized Memcheck builds. Predict which checked invariant should fail, then record actual output and termination without imposing a portable crash value or diagnostic string. The misconception is that a clean dynamic report proves all paths or that an unsupported invocation counts as a pass. Evidence is a coverage matrix plus a negative/repaired pair and an explicit open-claim list.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T45-01](#pr-t45-01).

<a id="t45-02"></a>

### T45.02 — Object extents, underflow, off-by-one and NUL boundaries

Capacity describes storage; initialized length describes valid payload; a string adds a terminating NUL within the object's extent. A signed external index must be checked before conversion or pointer formation. One-past permits a position used for a zero-length operation under this API's explicit contract, never a dereference. Check lower bounds, remaining extent and NUL space before touching the destination, so rejected input preserves sentinels and observable length.

For capacity 8, indices 0 through 7 name bytes. Index −1 is below the lower bound and index 8 with count 1 is beyond it. Index 8 with count 0 is accepted without access. Seven data octets plus one NUL fit; eight data octets plus NUL require nine bytes. A scan bounded to eight bytes can return missing-terminator without reading byte 8. Do not use strlen to discover the length of an untrusted unterminated array.

In PR-T45-02 build these checked operations and contrast them with separate faulty learner-owned copies in the hosted process. Add a legal C array access that writes the wrong logical field: it can violate an application invariant while staying inside addressable storage. The misconception is that any array-shaped or zero-filled data is a valid string, or that an addressability tool checks the application meaning of every write. Evidence includes preserved failure snapshots, explicit terminator bytes, exact-capacity success, lower/upper cases and an independent logical-field assertion.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T45-02](#pr-t45-02).

<a id="t45-03"></a>

### T45.03 — Checked allocation sizes and integer conversions

A correct allocation extent comes from a checked expression, not the wrapped result. Validate nonnegative external counts before converting them, constrain representable inputs, check multiplication, then check the header or terminator addition. Do not compute an overflowing intermediate and attempt to validate it afterwards. Conversion to a narrower size can lose information before the allocator is called.

The supplied model uses a maximum of 65535, header 12 and stride 7. Count 9360 gives 65520 payload bytes and 65532 total. Count 9361 has a representable product, 65527, but its total 65539 fails addition. Count 9363 has product 65541, so multiplication fails first. Count zero with header 12 still requests twelve bytes; total zero is rejected by this lab contract. These numbers model a declared width; the learner's C uses its actual SIZE_MAX and selected interface limits.

PR-T45-03 repairs a count-to-storage helper and a caller that narrows a length too early. The API returns a status and publishes the size only on success; no allocation occurs on rejection. The misconception is that defined unsigned wrapping makes the requested storage sufficient, or that UBSan's default group detects every unsigned size wrap. Evidence is the first rejected arithmetic stage, unchanged output/owner, independent wide arithmetic and native boundary tests. Remediate division inequalities and representability before adding complexity.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T45-03](#pr-t45-03).
