<a id="t45-04"></a>

### T45.04 — Stack exhaustion, frames and nested execution

Stack-capacity exhaustion consumes the reserved stack through calls, recursion, dynamic storage and nested contexts. A buffer write outside a local object's bounds is a different failure, even if it corrupts the stack. Frames depend on actual compilation, alignment, spills and callees. A GCC dynamic entry without bounded cannot close the whole-path bound. Unknown recursive depth or indirect callees keep that claim open.

The synthetic single descending stack has frames 32 + 48 + 64 = 144 bytes. Its two permitted nested contexts contribute (32 + 48) + (32 + 40) = 152, for 296 total. A 320-byte reservation leaves 24. Replacing one 32-byte saved frame with a declared 104-byte extended frame makes 368, exceeding the reservation. Real MSP/PSP selection and floating-point/lazy-frame configuration must be recorded separately; this is not a universal frame formula.

Changed-pattern scanning measures bytes that no longer match the fill. In the fixture, 32 unchanged bytes become eight four-byte words; the recorded minimum SP reserves 48 bytes even though only 32 changed. Unwritten local space or a restored pattern can hide reservation. Reentrant logging and interrupt nesting can add paths absent from the trial. PR-T45-04 combines closed-path calculations, actual .su/object inspection, a bounded high-water experiment and child-only native exhaustion. The misconception is that the largest single frame, watermark or canary proves a maximum. Evidence separates conditional bound, tested observation, guard behavior and unresolved paths.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T45-04](#pr-t45-04).

<a id="t45-05"></a>

### T45.05 — Fixed RAM sections, startup and collision failures

A .bss output section occupies a fixed linked interval. Startup initializes selected zeroed storage; it does not grow .bss as the program allocates. Four failures need different evidence: fixed sections exceeding a linker region; an incorrect copy/zero range; a custom heap violating its reserved interval; and a stray runtime write into another object. Link success cannot rule out the latter three.

In the synthetic 1024-byte region, aligned data 96, bss 400 and retained storage 64 end at offset 560. The declared descending 256-byte stack begins at 768. A 160-byte heap ends at 720, leaving 48; a 32-byte guard fits. A 192-byte heap ends at 752, leaving 16, so the reservation contract fails despite all fixed sections fitting. Changing bss to 900 also aligns the retained start to 1000 and ends fixed placement at 1064, a 40-byte region overflow. Those are distinct verdicts.

PR-T45-05 reuses startup and map work from T27 and checks boundaries before initialization. A wrong zero range ending at byte 13 would touch retained byte 12; the checked adapter rejects it before mutation. In a separate defined reserved-cell experiment, change a logical value with an incorrect legal-address write and show that section size remains unchanged. The misconception is that corruption means .bss grew, or that hosted heaps necessarily collide with a descending contiguous stack. Evidence includes the exact map/allocator policy, nonoverlap, retained sentinels and separate link versus runtime observations.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T45-05](#pr-t45-05).

<a id="t45-06"></a>

### T45.06 — Leaks, retained storage and failure cleanup

A resource leak can come from a missing release, a lost owning handle, a failed acquisition prefix or a retained object whose lifetime is too broad. Build an ownership ledger with acquisition, transfer, borrow and exactly-once release. Report live payload, retained bytes and peak bytes separately. RSS includes effects beyond the application's live allocation count.

Three resources of 32, 48 and 16 bytes produce peak prefixes 0, 32, 80 and 96. Failure before resource 2 acquires resources 0 and 1 and releases 1 then 0. Publication occurs only after all acquisitions; cleanup errors preserve the first cause. In the finite graph, lost A retains child B, rooted C remains reachable and D has only an interior root. These are declared graph categories, not promised native Memcheck output. C's 24 reachable bytes exceed a retention budget of 16 even though reachability prevents a lost-root classification.

In PR-T45-06 reproduce forgotten free, direct owner overwrite on failed resize and cleanup failure in separate owned processes. The repair stages publication, retains owners until release, and exercises every failure prefix. Native leak tools use conservative roots and selected error policies; state those settings. The misconception is that reachable means acceptable retention, that every RSS increase is a leak or that process exit substitutes for bounded repeated-use cleanup. Evidence includes the ledger before and after every acquisition/failure, repeated cycles, separate leak observations and a resource budget.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T45-06](#pr-t45-06).

<a id="t45-06-b"></a>


- **T45.06.b** Distinguish forgotten release, lost owner, indirect lost children and reachable retained storage using a declared finite graph and a separate native leak observation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T45-06](#pr-t45-06).


<a id="t45-06-c"></a>

<a id="t45-07"></a>

### T45.07 — Resize, invalid release and stale aliases

The resize protocol has two branches. Failed nonzero resize retains the original allocation and its owner. Successful resize ends the old allocation's lifetime and supplies a new owner; every old derived alias is invalid even if the allocator reuses the numeric address. Compute and save required lengths/contents before the call, retain the result temporarily, and publish it only under the chosen failure contract. Do not compare, dereference or release the old C pointer after success.

The finite history gives generation 1 eight initialized bytes. Refusal preserves generation 1 and size 8. Success supplies generation 2 and size 12, retains the first eight bytes and leaves four additional bytes uninitialized. Its address token can be 1000 again, yet the generation-1 alias is stale. Integer tokens are safe model data; they are not permission to examine an invalid C pointer.

PR-T45-07 repairs a resize wrapper and alias publication. It separately studies double release, interior/foreign release and use-after-free with own-program negative controls, never as expected production behavior. free(NULL) is valid and has no effect; clearing one owner does not clear another alias. Zero-size resize is excluded. The misconception is that a same-address return preserves old aliases, or that a null assignment repairs ownership everywhere. Evidence is failure preservation, success invalidation, initialized-tail handling and exactly-once release, followed by new relocation and alias tests.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T45-07](#pr-t45-07).

- **T45.07.a** Preserve old ownership on failed nonzero resize and invalidate all prior aliases after successful resize even if an address token is reused. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T45-07](#pr-t45-07).

<a id="t45-07-c"></a>


- **T45.07.c** Repair ownership and alias publication, test forced failure/movement/address reuse, and explain why free(NULL) or clearing one owner does not repair other aliases. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T45-07](#pr-t45-07).


<a id="t45-08"></a>

### T45.08 — Initialization state and delayed invalid use

Addressability and initialization are independent. Storage can be accessible while a field lacks an initialized value. A field or byte-state model tracks intended writes; a publication contract requires every semantically required field. A zero-byte fill is not a universal typed-object initializer for every pointer or floating representation. Use typed initialization and explicit field assignments where the object contract requires them.

The supplied record has length and mode. Writing only length leaves mode uninitialized, so consuming mode fails and publication is denied even though the address is accessible. Writing both permits publication; making their storage inaccessible still fails. The two supplied synthetic representations differ in nonsemantic bytes while length 7 and mode 1 compare equal. They model a reason to compare fields, without defining a real C struct layout or promising initialized padding.

PR-T45-08 repairs partial initialization and adds branch/output consumption controls. Memcheck can propagate invalid-value metadata before reporting an externally significant use; that reporting policy is not permission to evaluate an indeterminate C value. ASan alone is not a general initialization-use detector. Optional MSan needs a supported OS and correctly instrumented dependencies. The misconception is that malloc supplies valid values, a silent copy is legal C, or whole-struct memcmp expresses semantic equality. Evidence is the write/consume history, field-wise regression, fill-pattern variation and a declared coverage limit.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T45-08](#pr-t45-08).

<a id="t45-08-b"></a>


- **T45.08.b** Trace the first consumed uninitialized field through propagation to a branch or output and compare supported Memcheck with declared optional MemorySanitizer coverage. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T45-08](#pr-t45-08).


<a id="t45-08-c"></a>


- **T45.08.c** Repair complete initialization and publication, then test different fill patterns, partial failure and field-wise equality without treating padding as semantic state. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T45-08](#pr-t45-08).


<a id="t45-09"></a>

### T45.09 — Asynchronous borrowing, DMA and reentrancy

An asynchronous borrower can retain a buffer or callback context after the caller stops waiting. A timeout changes waiting policy; a cancellation request changes intent. Reclamation requires confirmed quiescence under the adapter's contract. A request identity and generation prevent a late callback from accessing a new object at a reused address. Protecting allocation metadata does not establish this application lifetime.

In the fixture, request 7 times out and requests cancellation. Reclaim is busy until its completion confirms no further access. Reclaim advances generation 1 to 2; a later generation-1 completion is stale. Request 8 instead confirms cancellation, yielding exactly one cancellation completion before generation 3 reuse. Two simultaneous users of scratch buffer 1 conflict; buffers 1 and 2 do not under the declared nonoverlap contract.

PR-T45-09 reuses the T21 operation model and T29 adapter. Add reentrant callbacks, duplicate completion and expired callback borrows. Hosted atomics or TSan observations do not model independent DMA. F439 SRAM/CCM reachability, ordering, interrupts and actual device quiescence require qualified target evidence. Halting the core may leave a peripheral active. The misconception is that disabling interrupts, a mutex, timeout or debugger stop authorizes reuse. Evidence is the ownership interval, exactly-once completion, denied early reclaim and explicit physical claims left open until measured.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T45-09](#pr-t45-09).

<a id="t45-10"></a>

### T45.10 — Causal repair, prevention and transfer

A crash site is where a symptom becomes visible, not necessarily where the contract first failed. Work backwards using a competing-hypothesis table: extent, initialization, lifetime, resource boundary and observation setup. Use the smallest reproducing prefix to find the first invalid state, then design a distinguishing experiment rather than changing several conditions at once.

The extent history fails at event 2 but exhibits its symptom at event 5; the lifetime history fails at 1 and exhibits a symptom at 4. Reporting event 5 or 4 as the cause loses the repair boundary. A watchpoint should target a live, bounded object and be re-established when its scope or allocation changes. Hardware slot/width limits and software stepping affect observation. Arm watchpoint events are asynchronous; a recorded PC alone is not a universal offending-store proof. Fault frames and addresses must be validated before interpreting them.

PR-T45-10 requires an unseen repair dossier, semantic regression and delayed transfer. Separate prevention by a checked extent/owner protocol from mitigation by canaries, guard regions or hardening. A mitigation may reduce damage without restoring the invariant. The misconception is that the first reported symptom, a new allocation layout or disappearance under debug proves the repair. Evidence connects prediction, minimum trigger, first invalid state, mechanism, repair and remaining limits. Transfer changes capacity, failure position, nesting or completion order after a delay.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T45-10](#pr-t45-10).

## Reading guidance

Use only the exact front-card locator scopes and their registry limits. The book's inspected second edition uses some C23 examples; this laboratory's portable drills retain the selected C17 contracts and exclude zero-size resize. Tool manuals pin documents, not installed executables. Record actual versions, target support, symbols and enabled options for every run. GDB's shared manual is a dated development snapshot. The ASan paper is historical mechanism evidence, with no transplanted overhead prediction.

For initialization, the inspected Memcheck valid-value/address subsections explain the model; MSan is a supplemental supported-environment comparison. For stack mitigation, the inspected GCC guard/check/probe entries show narrower contracts. For a watched Cortex-M object, use the two inspected Arm DWT pages and accepted fault/status passages; broader optional register programming requires new inspection. Read full runtime or peripheral chapters only after extending source scope through the research process.

Reused code is charged for the new experiment and evidence, not a second full implementation.

## Mastery gate and feedback

For each topic submit a prediction, original negative control, earliest-invalid-state argument, repaired invariant, semantic regression and explicit observation limits. A quiet tool run cannot replace the repaired contract. An unavailable environment leaves its observation open; move to a supported host or keep a clearly limited static result. Apply [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) to the smallest failed criterion and rerun the relevant boundary/failure case. Explain allocation/lifetime and resource budgets even when a detector reports the symptom.

The final dossier must distinguish prevention from mitigation and survive new capacity, failure-prefix, address-token, initialization and completion-order cases. For independent unseen assessment, keep the selected variant's defect identity and semantic oracle withheld until the dossier is submitted. Self-authored delayed practice has weaker independence and does not close that criterion. Keep exact C-language and target assumptions in the report. Source declarations, finite fixtures, actual C execution and physical evidence have separate claims.

## Consolidation and transfer

After a delay, diagnose a changed mechanism with the same outward symptom, then the same mechanism with a different symptom. Vary count widths, retained roots, permitted nesting and cancellation order. Transfer to one existing container/parser/request pipeline and predict the first invalid state before enabling the tool. Compare the earlier and later evidence without editing original expected results to match a broken target.

## Environment and limits

The finite oracle verifies arithmetic and supplied identity/history contracts. It executes no learner C, sanitizer, debugger or board test. Hosted negative controls belong to disposable learner-owned processes with verified limits, bounded input and supervisor deadlines. Separate native and diagnostic builds; do not run Memcheck on an ASan binary. Disable core dumps for routine fault trials and record any evidence-retention variant explicitly.

Core hosted observation requires a supported Linux setup for the Memcheck comparison. The optional MSan experiment needs supported instrumented dependencies and is not a Windows claim. Native exhaustion uses child-only checked limits and a supervisor; it does not attempt recovery on the exhausted stack. Embedded extensions use qualified existing adapters after the named preludes. No undefined-pointer/double-free failure is required on a board. Host histories do not establish DMA, electrical or real-time behavior. F439 results do not generalize to cached Cortex-M7 targets.

Follow [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory), [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles), [guide-standards](#guide-standards), [guide-integrations](#guide-integrations) and [guide-audit](#guide-audit) for environment, boundary and evidence records.

<a id="t46"></a>

# T46 — A bounded language runtime from representation to execution

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| runtime specialization | core | 124 | C, A, E |

**Prerequisites:** [T03](#t03), [T04](#t04), [T07](#t07), [T14](#t14), [T15](#t15), [T18](#t18), [T32](#t32).

**Required selected foundations:** [T16.01.a](#t16-01-a). Complete those leaves before the dependent project; the rest of the referenced domain need not be finished.

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 12 | 64 | 34 | 8 | 6 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Build a small compiler and virtual machine to make representation, machine state, verification, recursion and lifetime policies observable in original C. The same VM core executes on Linux, an emulated Cortex-M4 and the own-kernel route. The compiler remains hosted. Twelve milestones add 98 implementation/verification hours; reading, assessment and consolidation bring this family to 124 hours. Existing parsers, allocation reasoning and tests retain their original credit. This is a runtime specialization with deliberate limits, not a production language implementation.

## Entry check and remediation

Explain a typed value versus object bytes; trace a checked addition and a bounded stack; draw an owning/borrowed edge and an iterative graph traversal. Repair exactly the failed T03/T04/T14/T16/T18 gate. Hosted language work can proceed before firmware or kernel integration; PR-T46-11 requires the relevant startup/build foundations and keeps unavailable target evidence pending.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t46-01"></a>

### T46.01 — Values and a portable bytecode image

The first deliverable is a portable program image and value contract. Write the magic, function descriptors and code bytes individually; a C structure dump would inherit host padding and byte order. Decode a negative int32 via its mathematical unsigned representation before converting a representable result. Implement `cvm_encode` and `cvm_decode` for the bounded container first: check count, region lengths, contiguous descriptors and arity/local bounds, then publish the complete output. These raw codec functions deliberately do not accept instructions for execution. An unknown opcode can round-trip as bytes; the next checkpoint rejects it through the instruction verifier. Keep every output byte and reported length unchanged on failure. Value tags belong to the educational language: Boolean true is not an integer accepted by addition. Object references carry a slot and generation rather than exposing a native address.

Investigate: Hand-encode the bytes for a program returning 42, round-trip them without running the VM, then encode the INT32_MIN immediate as 00 00 00 80. Predict every truncation verdict. Keep a canary program as the destination and prove rejection does not publish a partially decoded image. Develop the artifact in [PR-T46-01](#pr-t46-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

- **T46.01.b** Encode and decode a bounded CVM1 image using explicit little-endian fields and failure-atomic loading. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T46-01](#pr-t46-01).


<a id="t46-01-c"></a>


- **T46.01.c** Reject truncated, unsupported and oversized images and explain which checks belong before execution. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T46-01](#pr-t46-01).


<a id="t46-02"></a>

### T46.02 — Structural and stack-height verification

First scan each function interval to discover instruction boundaries and validate operand widths. Then validate all branch targets, including unreachable instructions. A bounded worklist propagates the operand-stack height from each function entry; every incoming edge at a join must agree. A return requires exactly one value relative to its frame. Direct-call arity is checked against the descriptor. Infinite loops with a balanced stack can verify: verification establishes this representation discipline, not termination. Locals initialization and tags remain runtime checks. Add `cvm_load` and `cvm_save` as verified wrappers around the earlier raw codec; publish only after `cvm_verify` succeeds. This milestone has no dispatch or compiler dependency.

Investigate: Break one valid image at a time: truncate an immediate, branch into an immediate, change a call arity, add a mismatched join or allow fallthrough beyond the function. Retain the first rejecting phase. Derive the finite worklist bound from code bytes rather than relying on unbounded recursion. Develop the artifact in [PR-T46-02](#pr-t46-02).

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t46-02-c"></a>

<a id="t46-03"></a>

### T46.03 — Checked dispatch and operand stack

A dispatch iteration consumes exactly one unit of guest fuel and updates explicit machine state. Addition, subtraction and multiplication use a representable int64 intermediate; division rejects zero and INT32_MIN divided by -1 before the C operation. Integer division truncates toward zero. The operand stack is a caller-owned array with a checked push; verified per-function heights do not bound the sum of live caller temporaries and a callee. Results are written only on a successful return. A failed run can leave diagnostic VM state and must be reinitialized before independent replay.

Investigate: Trace two integer constants and ADD by hand. Compare nominal, extreme, wrong-tag and divide-by-zero cases. Keep a nearby valid boundary beside every rejection. Explain why changing overflow to wrapping would change the language rather than repair this implementation. Develop the artifact in [PR-T46-03](#pr-t46-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t46-03-a"></a>


- **T46.03.a** Implement a bounded opcode dispatch loop with explicit stack effects and checked int32 operations. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T46-03](#pr-t46-03).


<a id="t46-03-b"></a>


- **T46.03.b** Distinguish type, range, stack-capacity and bytecode-format errors using deliberate counterexamples. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T46-03](#pr-t46-03).


<a id="t46-03-c"></a>


- **T46.03.c** Preserve a declared result/error boundary and explain why VM arithmetic cannot inherit C signed-overflow behavior. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T46-03](#pr-t46-03).


<a id="t46-04"></a>

### T46.04 — Explicit call frames and recursion

A function is a descriptor; an invocation is a live frame. Arguments move from the caller operand stack into initialized callee locals. The callee has its own instruction position and saves the operand-stack base to restore on return. Repeated calls to the same function therefore have distinct local values and return histories. The VM loop itself never recursively invokes cvm_run. The sixteen-frame bound produces FRAME_LIMIT before constructing a seventeenth frame; this is a VM resource condition, not a claim about exhausting the C stack.

Investigate: Compile or hand-encode sum(5) and draw its six nested sum calls plus entry frame. Compare a finite result with unbounded self-calls stopped at the frame limit. Reject the same function invoked with the wrong number of arguments before running any instruction. Develop the artifact in [PR-T46-04](#pr-t46-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t46-04-a"></a>


- **T46.04.a** Represent each invocation with an independent instruction position, local slots, initialization state and operand-stack base. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T46-04](#pr-t46-04).


<a id="t46-04-b"></a>


- **T46.04.b** Implement direct calls and returns with checked arity and frame capacity without recursing through the C interpreter. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T46-04](#pr-t46-04).


<a id="t46-04-c"></a>


- **T46.04.c** Explain recursive execution and demonstrate bounded exhaustion distinct from native stack exhaustion. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T46-04](#pr-t46-04).


<a id="t46-05"></a>

### T46.05 — A bounded hosted expression compiler

The hosted compiler uses a deliberately small prefix grammar to keep representation and semantic work visible. It collects top-level function signatures before compiling bodies, so direct forward calls have known arity. Within a function, lexical let bindings map names to bounded slots; the initializer sees the outer environment and the body sees the new binding. Shadowing is allowed, but a self-reference without an outer binding is rejected. Compiler recursion is limited to 64 expression levels and source spans to 4096 bytes. Neither the syntax nor checked numeric semantics claims C or Lox compatibility.

Investigate: Begin with literals and binary expressions, then introduce one lexical binding and shadow it. Predict (+ (let x 40 x) x) inside outer x=2. Preserve an existing program on unknown-name, extra-token, excessive-depth and out-of-range-literal failures. Test emitted bytecode separately from parser acceptance. Develop the artifact in [PR-T46-05](#pr-t46-05).

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t46-05-b"></a>


- **T46.05.b** Compile literals, lexical bindings and arithmetic into the declared bytecode and validate the emitted program. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T46-05](#pr-t46-05).


<a id="t46-05-c"></a>


- **T46.05.c** Separate hosted compiler limits and source errors from runtime errors and preserve output on failed compilation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T46-05](#pr-t46-05).


<a id="t46-06"></a>

### T46.06 — Conditionals, mutation and bounded loops

Every expression leaves one value. An if consumes a Boolean condition and leaves exactly the chosen arm value; its two joins must agree. set updates an existing local and leaves the assigned value. do evaluates and discards its first expression before returning its second. while repeatedly checks a Boolean condition, discards each body value and returns nil when false. Emitted branch offsets are absolute offsets into the code region. These policies make stack equations simple enough to prove. A source loop is not trusted to terminate merely because it was compiled.

Investigate: Lower a local counter from zero to five and annotate each branch target and stack height. Change the condition to true and retain the fuel-stop evidence. Try an integer condition, unknown assignment target and branch into an immediate. Explain why equal output on one path cannot validate both arms. Develop the artifact in [PR-T46-06](#pr-t46-06).

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t46-06-a"></a>


- **T46.06.a** Lower Boolean conditionals and loops into patched instruction-boundary branches with compatible stack joins. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T46-06](#pr-t46-06).


<a id="t46-06-b"></a>


- **T46.06.b** Define mutable local assignment, sequencing and loop-result semantics without accidental host-language control behavior. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T46-06](#pr-t46-06).


<a id="t46-06-c"></a>


- **T46.06.c** Demonstrate both a terminating source loop and an infinite guest loop bounded by fuel. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T46-06](#pr-t46-06).


<a id="t46-07"></a>

### T46.07 — Arena phase and object handles

Start with sixteen fixed pair slots and arena mode. Each successful allocation owns a new generation; the seventeenth allocation fails even if previous objects are unreachable. A pair holds two tagged values, enabling a small object graph without a string subsystem or external allocation. A reference is valid only when its slot is occupied and its generation matches. Generation values never wrap: an exhausted-generation slot is retired. Reset destroys the entire VM lifetime; callers must discard all prior references, because generation checks do not provide identity across separate VM initializations.

Investigate: Allocate all sixteen pairs and retain the exact failure of the seventeenth request. Read both fields of a valid handle, then distinguish wrong-tag and stale-generation errors. Draw which handles a caller must release or re-root before enabling collection. Develop the artifact in [PR-T46-07](#pr-t46-07).

<a id="t46-08"></a>

### T46.08 — Nonmoving mark-sweep and temporary roots

The root set consists of live operand-stack values, initialized locals in live frames and an explicit host/temporary-root stack. Marking visits each object at most once, so cycles do not require recursive C calls. Sweep begins only after complete marking and a reserved sweep budget; a budget failure cannot free an object that marking did not finish examining. The critical allocation experiment fills the heap, keeps a child only in a C temporary, then constructs its parent. cvm_pair must temporarily root both operands before collection. A returned object held outside the VM must be pushed as a root before a subsequent allocation can collect it.

Investigate: Compare rooted and unrooted cycles; retain slot/generation traces. Fill the heap with garbage and allocate a parent around a temporary child. Kill the supplied missing-root mutant with this case. Force GC budget exhaustion and prove that failed collection did not sweep existing objects. The collector is nonmoving and stop-the-world, not a real-time collector. Develop the artifact in [PR-T46-08](#pr-t46-08).

<a id="t46-09"></a>

### T46.09 — Guest, collection and host budgets

Guest fuel counts dispatched instructions, GC budget counts root/edge inspections and the fixed sweep pass, and host budget counts callback invocations. The ledgers are independent: an infinite loop consumes fuel while leaving host and GC budgets unchanged if it performs neither activity. These units are educational accounting, not CPU cycles or wall-clock deadlines. Verification and compilation have their own finite size bounds. The embedding adapter must bound blocking work separately and cannot reenter the same VM from a callback. Resource refusal is a supported result and does not demonstrate application correctness.

Investigate: Measure all three counters before and after a finite run, infinite loop, collection and callback. Exhaust one budget at a time. Present a callback that could block as a counterexample to claiming a time guarantee from fuel. Keep the actual host deadline policy in the adapter contract. Develop the artifact in [PR-T46-09](#pr-t46-09).

<a id="t46-10"></a>

### T46.10 — Embedding and bounded store services

The embedding boundary accepts a numeric service ID and int32 argument, returning an int32 or error. It is intentionally narrower than a native FFI. The store adapter owns a pre-opened store and supports two fixed services: commit vm-result and read it. It encodes the integer as four explicit little-endian bytes. A failed commit may be indeterminate; the VM reports HOST_ERROR and the caller must recover the store rather than blindly replay a write. The host budget is charged before invocation. Store correctness belongs to its own tested contract and is not inferred from a successful VM response.

Investigate: First use the deterministic echo callback and test denied budget, absent service and adapter failure. Then run the separate store integration with an accepted store implementation. Record which layer owns transaction recovery and what HOST_ERROR can and cannot establish about durable bytes. Develop the artifact in [PR-T46-10](#pr-t46-10).

## Mastery gate and feedback

Require all mandatory contract, ownership, failure and dependency dimensions. Explain the verifier/runtime division, one recursive frame trace, one temporary-root collection, and why fuel is not a wall-time bound. Actual C tests and mutants are regression evidence; learner reasoning and changed-condition performance remain separate gates. Source/type/format/resource/host errors must be distinguishable. Use the actual stage artifacts to identify the first incorrect inference before offering another hint.

## Consolidation and transfer

Use six delayed hours for two changed-condition defenses. First shrink one bounded resource and predict the exact rejection boundary; later reuse the same bytecode with a different bounded host service. Record source, image, tool and target identities. Kernel and Thumb emulation support only their stated execution models; physical MCU evidence remains separate.

## Environment and limits

CVM1 has eight functions, 1024 code bytes, 64 operand slots, sixteen frames, eight locals per frame, sixteen pair objects and eight explicit roots. The compiler accepts at most 4096 source bytes and 64 nested expression levels. No required closures, JIT, moving/generational collector, native FFI, floating point, arbitrary object mutation or production sandbox is claimed. Native callback correctness and bounded I/O remain embedding obligations. The compiler uses hosted string operations; the core requires no libc calls in source, while actual compiler helpers are audited per target.

# T47 — Persistent storage engine and crash consistency

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| systems | core | 138 | C |

**Prerequisites:** [T03](#t03), [T15](#t15), [T21](#t21), [T32](#t32), [T36](#t36), [T43](#t43), [T45](#t45).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 18 | 64 | 38 | 10 | 8 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Build a bounded B+tree store whose success and failure semantics survive a declared crash model. Derive byte encoding, ordered index invariants, memory/page bounds and persistence ordering before optimizing. This is one engine grown through small projects, not twelve independent database implementations. All values are length-delimited bytes; the C core has no SQL or external storage-engine dependency.

## Entry check and remediation

Implement a bounds-checked byte decoder, an ordered search invariant and a partial-I/O loop from memory. Explain object lifetime, unsigned conversion, stale cache data and why write return is not a persistence barrier. If these fail, return to T03/T15/T21 and reproduce the exact missing mechanism. T32/T43/T45 supply fault isolation, measurements and causal diagnosis. No prior database product experience is assumed.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t47-01"></a>

### T47.01 — A byte-exact page codec

Define the file before casting a pointer. Encode integer fields byte by byte into a 4096-byte page; a C struct is an in-memory representation whose padding and alignment are not a portable file format. Validate magic, kind, generation, page identity, count, key/value extents and CRC before interpreting references. CRC-32 detects the exercised tears but is not a cryptographic authenticity guarantee. The corruption model explicitly excludes checksum collisions. A fresh format and reopening an established image are separate operations: corrupted existing data must not silently become an empty database.

Complete [PR-T47-01](#pr-t47-01). Keep three separate evidence items: derivation, executed implementation and repaired/transfer case.

<a id="t47-02"></a>

### T47.02 — A bounded clean page cache

A cache hit means the requested physical page and the cached identity agree, not merely that two logical IDs collide in a slot. The four-entry direct-mapped cache retains only clean bytes. Transaction scratch owns dirty nodes separately. Publication switches reads from home to redo images; checkpoint switches them back. Both transitions invalidate cache entries. Count backend reads and hits rather than calling a warm run evidence of faster storage hardware. Bound cache memory as four full pages plus tags, independently of the transaction workspace.

Complete [PR-T47-02](#pr-t47-02). Keep three separate evidence items: derivation, executed implementation and repaired/transfer case.

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t47-03"></a>

### T47.03 — B+tree lookup and ordered scan

All values reside in leaves. Internal separator i duplicates the smallest key in child i+1, so equality descends to the right child. Keys are length-delimited unsigned bytes: embedded zeros are ordinary data and shorter equal prefixes sort first. Tree descent and linked-leaf traversal are two independently checkable descriptions of the same ordered records. A cycle, dangling page or unreachable allocated node violates the representation even when one lookup succeeds. Bound descent and scan steps by the finite page count before following disk references.

Complete [PR-T47-03](#pr-t47-03). Keep three separate evidence items: derivation, executed implementation and repaired/transfer case.

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t47-03-b"></a>


- **T47.03.b** Implement bounded lookup and linked-leaf lower-bound scans with early-stop callbacks and unchanged outputs on missing or undersized results. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T47-03](#pr-t47-03).

<a id="t47-04"></a>

### T47.04 — Insertion, splits and root growth

Insertion maintains sorted keys within a leaf and increases height only when a root splits. With maximum seven keys, the eighth exists only in private split scratch. A leaf split yields four records on each side and copies the right minimum upward; an internal split promotes a separator and partitions child intervals. These are different operations. Reserve or recover capacity for propagation: a failed allocation cannot leave a half-published tree. This first implementation aborts the entire transaction on page exhaustion and refreshes separator minima over allocated nodes, explicitly adding O(P) work.

Complete [PR-T47-04](#pr-t47-04). Keep three separate evidence items: derivation, executed implementation and repaired/transfer case.

<a id="t47-05"></a>

### T47.05 — Deletion, redistribution and page reuse

Deletion may change an ancestor minimum even when no node underflows. Non-root leaves require four records and internal nodes require three separators. Borrow from a sibling with spare occupancy; otherwise merge, remove the corresponding parent separator/child and propagate the underflow. If an internal root loses its last separator, replace it with its only child. A freed page becomes reusable only after no tree or leaf-chain reference names it. The allocation bitmap and reachable-node set must agree after every transition.

Complete [PR-T47-05](#pr-t47-05). Keep three separate evidence items: derivation, executed implementation and repaired/transfer case.

<a id="t47-06"></a>

### T47.06 — Bounded no-steal transactions

Atomicity begins before logging: uncommitted nodes must never reach their home pages. store_begin loads live nodes into bounded typed scratch, records the prior root/allocation map and admits one writer. Input rejection leaves staged earlier work intact; capacity failure aborts the complete transaction. This explicit difference belongs in the API contract. The caller serializes all access, including readers; there is no hidden locking or snapshot mechanism. Scratch, clean cache, I/O buffers and C call stack have separate memory bounds.

Complete [PR-T47-06](#pr-t47-06). Keep three separate evidence items: derivation, executed implementation and repaired/transfer case.

<a id="t47-07"></a>

### T47.07 — Full-page redo and commit outcomes

A successful write callback reports transfer acceptance; only a successful flush establishes the declared persistence barrier. Invalidate and flush the prior marker before reusing redo space, write and flush every after-image, then write and flush the new commit marker. Before marker publication an error is a definite abort in this model; after attempting publication it is indeterminate. The caller may not infer absence from a lost acknowledgment. The live handle reads committed redo images until checkpoint. Full-image logging has a simple bounded recovery argument and deliberately high write amplification.

Complete [PR-T47-07](#pr-t47-07). Keep three separate evidence items: derivation, executed implementation and repaired/transfer case.

<a id="t47-08"></a>

### T47.08 — Checkpoint generations and reclamation

Checkpoint moves already committed state; it does not decide whether a transaction committed. Validate the complete redo batch before changing home pages, copy and flush all home images, write and flush the alternate generation record, then invalidate and flush the log marker. The old generation survives a torn replacement; retained WAL repairs incomplete home writes. Reclaiming the log earlier destroys the only complete explanation of a mixed home image. Two slots are sufficient for this serialized bounded design, not a general concurrent checkpoint algorithm.

Complete [PR-T47-08](#pr-t47-08). Keep three separate evidence items: derivation, executed implementation and repaired/transfer case.

<a id="t47-08-c"></a>


- **T47.08.c** Recover from an interrupted checkpoint and explain why early marker reclamation can destroy the only authoritative committed generation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T47-08](#pr-t47-08).


<a id="t47-09"></a>

### T47.09 — Recovery and repeated interruption

Recovery is a state machine that may itself fail. A valid newer marker names a complete after-image batch; every image is checked before the first home write. Full-page replacement is idempotent, so a second crash during replay can restart from intact log evidence. Generation mismatches, corrupted committed images and I/O failure are errors. Invalid incomplete marker bytes before any home writes can be ignored under the declared ordering model. Corruption after acknowledged persistence is a different fault class and must not be turned into an old-or-new success claim.

Complete [PR-T47-09](#pr-t47-09). Keep three separate evidence items: derivation, executed implementation and repaired/transfer case.


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t47-09-b"></a>


- **T47.09.b** Implement idempotent full-page redo that can itself be interrupted and repeated without changing the recovered application map. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T47-09](#pr-t47-09).


<a id="t47-09-c"></a>


- **T47.09.c** Reject corrupt committed input and failed recovery I/O while preserving the failure image; distinguish corruption from an admissible old-or-new crash result. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T47-09](#pr-t47-09).


<a id="t47-10"></a>

### T47.10 — Crash schedules and adversarial oracles

A crash test needs a semantic oracle and a persistence model. The model maintains stable and pending pages, permits reordering unsynchronized writes and can return an error after partial or complete persistence. The suite walks every write/flush boundary of selected transactions and applies five representative patterns. Its independent key/value oracle checks old/new state, not merely whether opening succeeds. These finite schedules do not enumerate every possible tear offset or pending subset; the ordering proof and measured test coverage have different roles.

Complete [PR-T47-10](#pr-t47-10). Keep three separate evidence items: derivation, executed implementation and repaired/transfer case.

<a id="t47-11"></a>

### T47.11 — Linux file I/O and amplification

The POSIX adapter translates one logical page operation into a loop of byte transfers. Positive short transfers advance progress; EINTR retries the interrupted operation; zero progress or an error terminates with failure. A successful fsync is the adapter persistence promise, conditional on the underlying stack honoring it. An existing preallocated file avoids mixing transaction recovery with file creation and directory persistence. Compare requested bytes, accepted bytes, synchronization count and useful changed payload; whole-image WAL naturally amplifies a tiny value update.

Complete [PR-T47-11](#pr-t47-11). Keep three separate evidence items: derivation, executed implementation and repaired/transfer case.

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t47-11-b"></a>


- **T47.11.b** Implement the existing-file fsync contract and demonstrate commit-close-reopen on a disposable preallocated image with platform failures reported explicitly. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T47-11](#pr-t47-11).


<a id="t47-11-c"></a>

<a id="t47-12"></a>

### T47.12 — VM and kernel storage boundaries

The VM may invoke two narrow host services: encode an integer under vm-result and read it back. Host-call budget, storage capacity and persistence outcome are independent contracts. No arbitrary pointer or path crosses the bytecode interface. The kernel adapter exposes complete page read/write and flush operations for an exclusive image slice; it validates user buffers and device completion. Reusing the store core preserves its invariants only when the new adapter satisfies the same durability model. Component success does not automatically certify the VM or device integration.

Complete [PR-T47-12](#pr-t47-12). Keep three separate evidence items: derivation, executed implementation and repaired/transfer case.

<a id="t47-12-b"></a>


- **T47.12.b** Adapt kernel whole-page read/write/flush capabilities to an exclusive store image slice, preserving user-buffer validation and durability responsibilities. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T47-12](#pr-t47-12).

## Reading guidance

The held OSPP second-edition persistent-storage volume supplies the inspected redo, repeatable replay and reclamation arguments. Public SQLite pages supply bounded alternative explanations of persistence assumptions and crash tests. Bayer/McCreight supplies the original B-tree balancing argument; the leaf-only values and separator convention here are an original B+tree contract. ARIES is listed as an unassigned foundational lead: only its IBM bibliographic record/abstract was inspected. No full ARIES implementation is implied. Assigned passages total 16 hours; use two additional hours to reconcile diagrams, assumptions and your own format.

Named tests are mapped per project; passing them supplies bounded runtime evidence, not all objective credit.

## Mastery gate and feedback

Spend ten hours on cold review and an unseen fault schedule. Explain right-child equality, internal versus leaf split, minimum-key repair, free-page ownership, no-steal scratch, commit indeterminacy, checkpoint order and repeated recovery. Demonstrate the complete old/new semantic oracle and three killed wrong implementations. Minimize a failed schedule to the first invalid persistence transition. A setup failure or skipped POSIX case remains unavailable. Remediate the actual violated invariant, then repeat the trigger and one new variation.

## Consolidation and transfer

Use eight delayed hours to compare a new trace, optimize separator refresh without changing the API, and integrate a narrow VM host service or educational-kernel block backend. Existing implementation hours are charged once; new adapter evidence belongs to the integration milestone. Predict write amplification before counting it. Preserve old accepted evidence when making a format change; a new wire format needs a migration/rejection policy rather than silently reinterpreting old bytes.

## Environment and limits

One exclusive caller serializes all accesses. Fixed capacities, seven-key nodes and full-image redo favor observable mechanisms over production throughput. Successful flush persists all preceding writes; tears affect only addressed pages; checksum collisions, lying flushes and later media corruption lie outside the atomicity argument. The harness samples five admitted persistence patterns at each selected write/flush boundary. It is not exhaustive over arbitrary subsets or tear positions and does not cut physical power. The preallocated-file route tests Linux API/reopen behavior; initial pathname durability and concurrent-process locking are separate. A complete runtime receipt records compiler/options/source hashes and actual results. Python contract checks do not replace those runs.

# T48 — A small isolated x86-64 operating system

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |

| kernel | core | 186 | C, F |

**Prerequisites:** [T08](#t08), [T09](#t09), [T16](#t16), [T23](#t23), [T27](#t27), [T32](#t32), [T37](#t37), [T46](#t46), [T47](#t47).

## Purpose and outcomes

Build an original bounded kernel that runs isolated user programs, preempts them, provides checked services and persists a VM/store result through its own block driver. The supplied bootloader, emulator and packaging are explicit infrastructure. Fourteen small milestones contribute 138 implementation/verification hours; 26 reading, 10 assessment and 12 consolidation hours make a 186-hour module estimate. Actual time and remediation must be recorded, not hidden behind this estimate.

## Entry check and remediation

Before entering, derive a callable assembly ABI, inspect an ELF/map, implement checked span parsing, and account for fixed/stack storage. Complete the named foundations; T46/T47 are additionally required before projects 12/13. Earlier boot, interrupt, ownership, algorithms and debugger artifacts are reused by original ID and not charged as new implementations.

## Component progression

Boot and inspect first; validate boot data; establish traps and frames; construct isolated process memory; regain control through a timer; load bounded images; expose checked services; then add a real queue/block driver. The shell, VM and durable store are clients. The OS route is x86-64 with its necessary small 32-bit transition; Thumb remains the separate microcontroller/runtime target.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t48-01"></a>

### T48.01 — Boot contracts and the long-mode transition

GRUB supplies a 32-bit protected-mode entry, not a ready C environment. Preserve EAX/EBX, make the initial stack and page tables, load a GDT, enable PAE and long mode, then enter the 64-bit code segment. Our four-GiB supervisor identity map uses 2048 two-MiB entries; it includes the fixed PC MMIO window without exposing it to user mode.

Write the Multiboot2 header, original transition assembly and link layout. Inspect entry address, header checksum and map before stepping the transition. Audit undefined symbols and distinguish bootloader service from learner-owned entry code.

A discriminating failure campaign includes: wrong header checksum, lost EBX, malformed CR3 alignment, absent far jump, wrong C stack alignment and accidentally linked hosted startup. The gate is concrete: Boot the selected QEMU guest to the first serial marker and retain disassembly, register trace and ELF/map identities. Explain every supplied and owned operation.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T48-01](#pr-t48-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t48-02"></a>

### T48.02 — Bounded boot information and memory reservations

A boot tag carries a byte size; the following tag starts at its eight-byte-rounded end. Check the raw extent before rounding or reading fields. Preserve the module, boot structure and kernel physical ranges before giving any page to a process. Reserved overlapping map entries win over usable entries in this teaching allocator.

Decode tags by explicit field widths, accepting larger compatible memory-map entry strides. Require one bounded module and one map. Generate truncated headers, invalid strides and overflowing physical ranges before using actual GRUB input.

A discriminating failure campaign includes: size below eight, rounded tag beyond total size, overflowing base plus length, missing terminator, duplicate required tag and reserving only kernel .text. The gate is concrete: Pass kernel_boot and retain an actual boot reservation ledger. A synthetic tag at offset 8 with size 21 must advance to offset 32.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T48-02](#pr-t48-02).

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t48-02-c"></a>

<a id="t48-03"></a>

### T48.03 — Serial diagnosis and normalized exception frames

A trap enters asynchronously, so ordinary function-call preservation is insufficient. Normalize the hardware error/no-error cases, save all general registers and retain the interrupted CS/RIP/flags/stack. The kernel uses a separate double-fault stack and does not execute floating-point/SIMD instructions.

Implement bounded serial output, GDT/TSS/IDT setup and original assembly save/restore. Draw the 15 saved general registers, vector/error pair and five-word hardware frame before writing the C frame declaration.

A discriminating failure campaign includes: wrong pushed-word order, missing error placeholder, insufficient stack alignment at a C call, invalid TSS descriptor and returning with the wrong operand size. The gate is concrete: Retain a real saved-frame trace and successful return. In the declared frame there are 22 eight-byte words; the software declaration must agree with assembly.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T48-03](#pr-t48-03).


#### Evidence checklist

<a id="t48-04"></a>

### T48.04 — Physical frames and explicit page-table ownership

A frame belongs to exactly one allocation state: reserved, free or allocated. Alignment is necessary but not sufficient for release. Address translation is a separate structure: every process owns its user mappings while supervisor mappings remain inaccessible from ring 3.

Build the bitmap/state allocator from boot memory, then create per-process tables. Zero newly exposed frames. Roll back a partly fulfilled allocation and delay reclaiming an exited process until another address space is active.

A discriminating failure campaign includes: reserved-page release, double free, allocation of boot data, partial-allocation leak, stale mapping and exposure of nonzero reclaimed bytes. The gate is concrete: Exhaust a finite hosted map, show exactly 256 pages from [3 MiB,4 MiB), and execute zero-filled user allocation and process teardown in the guest.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T48-04](#pr-t48-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t48-04-a"></a>


- **T48.04.a** Derive and implement frame ownership and exhaustion invariants. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T48-04](#pr-t48-04).


<a id="t48-04-b"></a>


- **T48.04.b** Construct explicit process mappings with zero-fill and bounded allocation rollback. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T48-04](#pr-t48-04).


<a id="t48-04-c"></a>


- **T48.04.c** Explain when page-table and frame storage may be reclaimed after a context switch. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T48-04](#pr-t48-04).


<a id="t48-05"></a>

### T48.05 — Ring-3 isolation and guarded user storage

A user-capable upper table does not grant access through a supervisor leaf. The selected process window is two MiB; static image, heap and guarded 128-KiB stack have separate regions. Kernel identity mappings remain supervisor-only. Writable user data is non-executable and executable text is not writable.

Construct the first privilege-return frame and enforce permissions at every mapping level. Run two instances that write different values at the same virtual address. Add a separate process that attempts to write the kernel load address.

A discriminating failure campaign includes: user bit propagated to a supervisor region, writable executable segment, wrapping extent, a cross-page buffer entering a guard and incorrect initial privilege flags. The gate is concrete: Show actual peer progress and a protection page fault at 0x100000 with present/write/user bits set, while both independent virtual data values survive preemption.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T48-05](#pr-t48-05).

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t48-06"></a>

### T48.06 — Timer preemption with a nonpreemptible kernel

The timer regains control even when a user program never yields. Saving context and choosing the next runnable process are different mechanisms. The first scheduler is round-robin, one CPU and one thread per process; interrupts remain disabled inside the kernel. A long synchronous device operation therefore adds scheduler latency.

Configure the pinned PC timer/PIC, issue end-of-interrupt, retain each process frame, switch CR3 and kernel-stack ownership, then return to the next user. Separate explicit yield from timer-caused switches.

A discriminating failure campaign includes: no EOI, switching to a dead process, using another process kernel stack, dropping a register, confusing syscall frequency with cooperative yield and claiming hard real-time behavior from QEMU ticks. The gate is concrete: Two CPU-consuming workers that never call yield complete after observed timer ticks; their private memory values survive. Record timer-driven switches and nonpreemptible sections.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T48-06](#pr-t48-06).

<a id="t48-07"></a>

### T48.07 — Static ELF64 and a read-only boot archive

The loader consumes program headers, not section names. File bytes are copied into a checked virtual span and the remaining memory bytes start at zero. CMKA1 maps bounded unique names to non-overlapping image spans; it is a boot container, not a general filesystem.

Decode ELF64 little-endian x86-64 ET_EXEC images with at most eight load segments, fixed 4096-byte alignment and no interpreter, dynamic linking or TLS. Validate all segments before mapping. Package init, workers, fault control and shell.

A discriminating failure campaign includes: truncated header or payload, filesz greater than memsz, overlapping page mappings, entry outside executable storage, writable executable segment, duplicate archive names and payload/table overlap. The gate is concrete: Pass hosted truncation/extent cases and boot real independently linked ELF programs. Preserve zero-fill and rejected-image evidence separately.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T48-07](#pr-t48-07).

<a id="t48-08"></a>

### T48.08 — Bounded syscalls and revocable process handles

The syscall number selects a service; user data never selects an arbitrary kernel entry point. CMK uses int 0x80 with RAX number/result and three argument registers. Validate arithmetic and every page crossed before copying. A handle combines a slot and generation and becomes invalid after close.

Implement console, exit, yield, ticks/PID, page allocation, archive and block calls using the public header. Make the disk handle exclusive to init. Enforce read/write direction and reject high bits rather than silently truncating caller values.

A discriminating failure campaign includes: unknown call, foreign/stale handle, pointer into kernel memory, huge/wrapping byte count, read output into text and handle use after close. The gate is concrete: Actual user programs receive errors for kernel pointers, oversized allocation, unknown syscall and a closed handle; hosted generation checks reject stale tokens.

<a id="t48-09"></a>

### T48.09 — Modern PCI virtio discovery and split queues

A device capability describes a register window, not permission to dereference arbitrary offsets. Discover the modern block device and required capabilities, negotiate VERSION_1 and FLUSH, then publish a split queue. One outstanding request makes descriptor and bounce-buffer ownership visible.

Inspect PCI capabilities with bounded traversal, reject unsupported transport/feature/extent cases, initialize an eight-descriptor queue and derive its DMA addresses from the declared identity mapping. Publish descriptors before advancing availability.

A discriminating failure campaign includes: treating a PCI access capability as a MMIO window, wrong feature bank, absent required feature, wrapped notification offset, premature buffer reuse and a completion naming the wrong descriptor. The gate is concrete: Retain actual negotiated status, queue addresses, descriptor identities and successful guest requests. A 16-bit index wraps from 65535 to 0 while the corresponding eight-slot position wraps from 7 to 0.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T48-09](#pr-t48-09).

<a id="t48-10"></a>

### T48.10 — Block completion, flush and persistence boundaries

The kernel block service moves exactly one 4096-byte page or reports failure. A virtio sector is a separate 512-byte unit. Successful completion of a write does not by itself close the declared durable-storage boundary; the store must request and observe flush.

Implement bounded read/write/flush requests with a static DMA bounce page. Validate capacity before multiplying a page index by eight. Poison the device on timeout and retain in-flight storage. Reboot with the same ordinary raw image.

A discriminating failure campaign includes: page beyond capacity, writable destination in kernel space, wrong sector units, missing flush feature, error status interpreted as completion and retry after losing DMA ownership. The gate is concrete: Write a patterned page, flush, read it, then boot a new guest and compare all bytes. Keep backend cache configuration and exact image identity; do not claim a physical power-loss test.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T48-10](#pr-t48-10).

<a id="t48-11"></a>

### T48.11 — Init, bounded console shell and teardown

Init and the shell are ordinary isolated ELF programs. The small shell owns a 64-byte command buffer, reads nonblocking console bytes and yields when no byte is available. The command set is help, echo and exit; overflow follows an explicit reset-and-report policy.

Package named init/shell images in the archive, implement a bounded line parser and exercise input through the real serial channel. Exit revokes capabilities and releases user frames after scheduling away.

A discriminating failure campaign includes: unterminated command, overlong input, duplicate image name, command-buffer reuse across an outstanding operation and freeing the currently active kernel stack. The gate is concrete: An automated interactive guest receives help and exit and produces the expected bounded response; hosted archive tests reject malformed tables.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T48-11](#pr-t48-11).

<a id="t48-12"></a>

### T48.12 — One portable VM core inside a user process

Porting means changing adapters while retaining the VM relation and bytecode. The kernel never interprets VM object references or accepts native addresses from bytecode. Its user process owns Cvm and program storage, supplies a bounded numeric callback and preserves separate instruction and host-call budgets.

Link the original T46 core into a freestanding ELF, audit compiler helpers and user stack usage, then execute a hand-encoded CVM1 program. Keep the hosted compiler outside this guest milestone.

A discriminating failure campaign includes: duplicated interpreter, silently linked libc, missing stack budget, arbitrary FFI pointer, failed callback returned as successful VM execution and an exhausted host budget ignored. The gate is concrete: Actual ring-3 execution computes 42 through a bounded callback and independently returns CVM_HOST_BUDGET with zero callback allowance. Record the shared source identity.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T48-12](#pr-t48-12).

<a id="t48-13"></a>

### T48.13 — VM, durable store and kernel reboot integration

The store owns B+tree pages, WAL and recovery; the kernel owns the block transfer/flush service. An exclusive adapter maps the 67-page store image to raw pages starting at 16. VM bytecode may request named store services but cannot choose a device page or kernel pointer.

Link T46/T47 cores in init with caller-owned static workspace. Execute bytecode that commits value 42, deliberately lose the callback success reply, restart the guest on the same disk, recover and read the value through bytecode.

A discriminating failure campaign includes: double-charged copied implementation, write without flush, bytecode raw-device access, unknown transaction outcome treated as definitely absent, wrong store-slice arithmetic and stack exhaustion from nested workspace. The gate is concrete: Preserve first-boot CVM_HOST_ERROR after the known committed callback, second-boot VM GET42, WAL recovery/store-check evidence and actual syscall/virtio image identities. This is a lost-reply experiment, separate from the store simulator crash matrix.

A green image is one experiment. Diagnose entry failures, bad page permissions, malformed images, lost context and queue ownership at their first violated boundary. Keep host and guest results separate so a correct model cannot conceal broken assembly or an unexecuted device path.

Run the dual-compiler hosted matrix and real guest campaign, then introduce one controlled mutation at a time in a separate learner copy. Use GDB saved state and serial evidence to minimize the first causal divergence. Rebuild from a new directory.

A discriminating failure campaign includes: synthetic log substituted for guest output, source/image mismatch, timeout reported as pass, changed expected marker hiding a defect and a known fault reported as blind diagnosis. The gate is concrete: Reject learner stubs and corrupted ELF/handle variants; pass repaired host and guest gates. Complete a reviewer-held perturbation after seven days and annotate unresolved physical/SMP/general-OS claims.

## Mastery gate and feedback

Preserve original learner code, contract/ABI map, source/image identities, hosted cases, actual boot/device/peer traces, resource ledger, first-cause repair and delayed changed-condition result. Read `labs/kernel/README.md` for exact commands and unimplemented-stub behavior. The integrated gate must show actual bytecode to store to syscall to virtio, a committed/lost-response distinction, and a fresh boot that recovers the value. Reusing assessor evidence is infrastructure review, not learner mastery.

## Consolidation and transfer

After at least seven days, diagnose one unseen page, ELF, handle or queue perturbation and change one resource limit. Explain which claims survive and which need new observations. Reconcile source version, adapter semantics and available capabilities before comparing runs.

## Environment and limits

The selected kernel is single-core, uses static ELF admission at boot and a nonpreemptible kernel. Synchronous bounded device polling may delay peers. There is no required SMP, general POSIX/filesystem/network stack, JIT, dynamic linker or physical-device conformance. User faults terminate the process; unexpected kernel exceptions stop the diagnostic image. QEMU-backed persistence and supplied crash models remain separately scoped.

<!-- third-edition handoff -->

## Third-edition implementation handoff

Preserve this bounded single-core route and ABI regression. T53 adds a separate SMP profile; T56 introduces thread/process separation, blocking IPC, memory faults and concurrent services.

# T49 — Operating-system mechanisms and the Linux observatory

## Purpose and outcomes

Treat a process as an ownership and protection boundary, a thread as an execution context, and scheduling as a policy over runnable contexts. Build models before comparing their predictions with observed Linux behavior.

The 10 projects contribute 86 implementation/verification hours. Together with reading (12), assessment (8) and consolidation (8), the provisional module budget is 114 hours. These are planning estimates, not measured learner calibration.

## Entry check and remediation

Reuse the process launcher, descriptor ledger and thread join exercises. Before the observatory, distinguish a return value from errno and explain which process owns a descriptor. Assembly context switching is taught later and is not an entry requirement here. Where a prerequisite is missing, repair its smallest failing experiment first. Use prior projects by ID rather than duplicating their implementation hours. Explicit project dependencies govern the implementation route; module prerequisites describe the complete study background.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t49-01"></a>

### T49.01 — Privilege, traps and a syscall observatory

Trace one write from a C call through the syscall ABI to kernel work and return. A library function, syscall, trap and device interrupt are different boundaries. An address meaningful in user mode is not automatically a valid kernel copy source; errno is a wrapper convention rather than the machine return ABI.

Build a bounded syscall tracer experiment and an original raw-syscall assembly wrapper for one write. Compare its return with the libc wrapper on success and an invalid descriptor; inspect arguments and clobbers in disassembly.

A discriminating experiment exposes: negative return confused with positive byte count; missing register clobber; invalid pointer; interrupted call; partial transfer. Required evidence: Retain a source-to-disassembly-to-trace correspondence, correct byte counts and a checked error conversion. Identify precisely which behavior belongs to ISO C, the chosen ABI and Linux.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T49-01](#pr-t49-01).

<a id="t49-02"></a>

### T49.02 — Processes, threads and lifetime ownership

A process owns an address-space and descriptor context; multiple threads can execute within it. A child process initially sharing physical pages is not permission to share later ordinary writes. Exiting a thread, exiting a process, waiting for a child and joining a thread have distinct reclamation obligations.

Build a process/thread tree that reports identities, shared and private counters, exit states and reaping. Use explicit synchronization and wait for every owned child or thread.

A discriminating experiment exposes: unreaped child; joining twice; thread using a returned stack address; duplicated buffered output after fork; process exit mistaken for thread exit. Required evidence: Observe thread-shared state and process-private state, account for all created entities, and explain termination when one worker fails before publishing its result.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T49-02](#pr-t49-02).

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t49-03"></a>

### T49.03 — FCFS, SJF, SRTF and round-robin scheduling

Implement a discrete-event policy model with integer arrival and service times. Tie-break by arrival then task ID; a completion at time t precedes an arrival at t, and dispatch has zero cost in the first model. Turnaround is completion minus arrival; response is first start minus arrival. Shortest remaining time is preemptive, unlike shortest job first.

Implement FCFS, nonpreemptive SJF, SRTF and RR with a configurable positive quantum. Use jobs A=(0,8), B=(1,2), C=(2,1) and derive the complete timeline by hand before executing.

A discriminating experiment exposes: zero quantum; empty workload; simultaneous arrivals; completion at quantum boundary; idle gap; arithmetic overflow. Required evidence: Check service conservation and exact timelines: SRTF completes B at 3, C at 4 and A at 11; explain the tie at 2. Report response, turnaround and waiting time without counting idle time as service.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T49-03](#pr-t49-03).

<a id="t49-04"></a>

### T49.04 — Feedback and proportional-share scheduling

MLFQ infers behavior from CPU consumption; stride allocates proportional service using virtual progress. Neither is a deadline guarantee. Charge CPU use across voluntary yields so a yielding task cannot repeatedly reset its allotment. Represent virtual accounting with checked integers and normalize before wrap.

Add a three-level MLFQ with explicit allotments, periodic boost and yield accounting, then stride scheduling with weights1:2:4. Compare interactive bursts, a CPU hog and a yield-gaming worker.

A discriminating experiment exposes: allotment reset on every yield; starving low queue; zero weight; pass overflow; unfair tie-breaking; sleeping worker receiving unbounded credit. Required evidence: Show the boost prevents the declared starvation case and service converges toward the selected weight ratios over a finite long run. Document transient error and distinguish this teaching policy from Linux EEVDF.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T49-04](#pr-t49-04).

<a id="t49-05"></a>

### T49.05 — Working sets and page-fault observation

Allocated virtual bytes, resident pages and physical I/O are different measurements. First-touch demand-zero faults can consume CPU without disk reads; file-backed misses can trigger readahead or page-cache hits. A working set is tied to a reference window, not merely the allocation size.

Build sequential, strided and randomized page-touch workloads with fixed seeds. Record minor/major faults, RSS, CPU time, elapsed time and the page-size/huge-page configuration before and after each phase.

A discriminating experiment exposes: allocation optimized away; pages never touched; warm cache mislabeled cold; RSS sampled before touch; huge pages changing the unit; background pressure. Required evidence: Explain observed fault classes with a page-reference trace and separate requested bytes, touched pages and resident bytes. Report conditions that prevent a controlled cold-cache experiment.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T49-05](#pr-t49-05).

<a id="t49-06"></a>

### T49.06 — Page replacement from a reference string

A replacement simulator knows logical references, not hardware timing. Use FIFO, LRU, CLOCK and offline optimal with the same frame capacity. CLOCK reference bits approximate recency; optimal needs future knowledge and is an oracle rather than a deployable policy.

Implement the four policies and print each eviction. Use reference string1,2,3,4,1,2,5,1,2,3,4,5 with three and four frames to examine FIFO anomaly.

A discriminating experiment exposes: evicting a free frame; wrong LRU update on hit; CLOCK hand never advancing; capacity zero; using future information in LRU. Required evidence: Independently derive FIFO fault counts 9 and 10 for three and four frames. Verify resident uniqueness and capacity after every step, and explain why more frames need not improve FIFO.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T49-06](#pr-t49-06).


#### Evidence checklist

<a id="t49-07"></a>

### T49.07 — Descriptors and open-file-description lifetimes

A descriptor is a per-process integer referring to an open-file description. dup and inherited descriptors can share an offset, while separate opens ordinarily do not. Closing an integer relinquishes one reference; it does not mean an in-flight operation or a peer descriptor has ended.

Build a descriptor ledger across open, dup, fork, read and close using a temporary file. Demonstrate shared offset updates and independent opens, then enforce close-on-exec for private descriptors.

A discriminating experiment exposes: descriptor-number reuse; double close; leaked pipe writer preventing EOF; assuming dup creates an independent offset; retrying a Linux close after ambiguous failure. Required evidence: Reconcile every descriptor reference and observed file offset. Show pipe EOF only after all writer references close, including inherited copies.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T49-07](#pr-t49-07).

<a id="t49-08"></a>

### T49.08 — Namespaces, readiness and device completion

A namespace changes a resource view; it is not the same mechanism as a cgroup resource budget. Readiness means an operation may make progress now, not that all requested work is complete. Completion needs an operation identity and buffer lifetime extending until its terminal result.

Observe available PID/mount namespace views in a disposable permitted environment and build a poll-driven pipe reader that survives short transfers. Model device submission/completion with generation-checked request IDs.

A discriminating experiment exposes: namespace privileges unavailable; readiness consumed by another reader; stale completion; buffer reused early; EINTR; partial EOF record. Required evidence: Show a readiness race safely handled by retry/error state and reject a stale synthetic completion. Record unavailable namespace operations honestly rather than weakening the isolation claim.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T49-08](#pr-t49-08).

<a id="t49-09"></a>

### T49.09 — CPU and memory budgets with cgroups

CPU quota limits service over a period; it is not a dedicated processor or deterministic response-time guarantee. memory.current includes charged memory under kernel rules and need not equal process RSS. A constrained experiment needs an isolated child group, explicit cleanup and a supervisor outside the tested budget.

Run the same bounded compute/allocation workload without a group, with CPU quota, and with a memory limit in a delegated subtree. Capture cpu.stat, memory.events, pressure observations and workload exits.

A discriminating experiment exposes: no delegation; parent quota dominating child; supervisor inside killed group; conflating throttling with slower instructions; memory pressure unrelated to allocation size. Required evidence: Attribute throughput changes to throttled time where supported, detect allocation/kill outcomes, and preserve exit/status evidence. If delegation is unavailable, close only the model gate.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T49-09](#pr-t49-09).
