<a id="t55-07"></a>

### T55.07 — Epoch reclamation and quiescent states

Epoch schemes delay reuse until every participant that could have seen a retired node passes a quiescent boundary. A stalled participant can retain memory indefinitely. Epoch entry/exit and participant deregistration are part of the safety contract, not optional instrumentation.

Implement a fixed-participant epoch domain for an append/read/remove structure and compare retire-list growth with hazard pointers under a paused reader.

A discriminating experiment exposes: reader accesses after leaving epoch; epoch advanced too early; deregistered active reader ignored; counter wrap; pool exhaustion hidden. Required evidence: Identify the earliest safe reuse point for each retired node and show memory retention under a nonquiescent reader. State that bounded storage can force explicit exhaustion despite algorithmic progress.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T55-07](#pr-t55-07).

<a id="t55-08"></a>

### T55.08 — Read-copy-update as an ownership protocol

RCU readers observe a published immutable version while writers replace it and wait for a grace period before reclamation. Publication, grace-period detection and freeing are separate obligations. A teaching userspace/guest scheme is not automatically equivalent to Linux RCU.

Implement immutable configuration replacement with fixed version slots and a bounded quiescent-state protocol. Keep writer serialization explicit and prevent mutation of published versions.

A discriminating experiment exposes: writer edits published object; grace period ignores preexisting reader; nested read section mishandled; callback frees current version; stalled reader exhausts versions. Required evidence: Show each reader sees a self-consistent version and old storage remains valid through its final reader. Explain the selected grace-period model and its limits.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T55-08](#pr-t55-08).

<a id="t55-09"></a>

### T55.09 — Concurrent histories and linearizability checking

A history records invocation, response, arguments and result for each operation. A linearization must preserve real-time order of nonoverlapping calls and satisfy the sequential object specification. A checker of small histories is a finite oracle, not proof of every possible execution.

Write a bounded backtracking checker for queue histories with distinct operation IDs. Feed generated legal histories and hand-designed lost-item, duplicate-item and ordering violations.

A discriminating experiment exposes: using log order as total execution order; ignoring real-time precedence; pending operation mishandled; duplicate ID; checker accepts empty dequeue while required item exists. Required evidence: Reject the supplied impossible histories and show a witness sequential order for accepted ones. State the history length/state-space limit and retain the smallest counterexample.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T55-09](#pr-t55-09).

<a id="t55-10"></a>

### T55.10 — End-to-end progress and contention audit

Performance comparisons require equal semantics, payloads, allocation policy and shutdown behavior. A lock-free data path that calls a blocking allocator or logger is not an end-to-end lock-free operation. Retry count, tail latency, fairness, cache traffic and memory retention complement throughput.

Compare SPSC, a mutex queue and the reclaimed MPMC queue under uncontended, contended, oversubscribed and paused-participant workloads. Audit all success, failure and reclamation paths.

A discriminating experiment exposes: unequal capacity; benchmarks optimize away work; hidden allocation; only average latency; sanitizer timing used as performance result; stress success advertised as proof. Required evidence: Publish correctness evidence separately from performance data, record uncertainty and classify progress for each complete operation. Explain an observed case where locking performs better.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T55-10](#pr-t55-10).

## Reading guidance

Read only the assigned locator before the related experiment, then return to it after the counterexample. State the source's machine and task-model assumptions next to your own. Historical pseudocode does not authorize undefined C races; Linux, ISO C and a microcontroller memory system are separate contracts. The source/search/reflection ledger is in `research/v3/`; filenames and graph records alone do not qualify as inspected readings.

## Implementation projects

Complete [PR-T55-01](#pr-t55-01), [PR-T55-02](#pr-t55-02), [PR-T55-03](#pr-t55-03), [PR-T55-04](#pr-t55-04), [PR-T55-05](#pr-t55-05), [PR-T55-06](#pr-t55-06), [PR-T55-07](#pr-t55-07), [PR-T55-08](#pr-t55-08), [PR-T55-09](#pr-t55-09), [PR-T55-10](#pr-t55-10) in order. Project manifests distinguish model, host, emulator, cross-build and physical evidence. Later cumulative tests may require later mechanisms; an early milestone is assessed on its own contract and cannot borrow a later reference implementation.

## Mastery gate and feedback

Demonstrate one correct execution and one deliberately wrong variant per mechanism. Explain the first invalid transition, fix its cause, and repeat with an independently chosen input. Review safety, progress, resource lifetime and timing as distinct claims. A stress test supplies observations; bounded exhaustive schedules supply only the stated finite coverage. A deadlocked or unavailable run is not a pass.

## Consolidation and transfer

After seven days rebuild one mechanism from its public contract, change the contention or arrival pattern, and compare the new prediction with the result. After a month integrate two previously separate boundaries. Record surprises, remediation hours and the source passage that changed your reasoning.

## Environment and limits

x86-64 lock-free atomic widths audited in disassembly History/interleaving checker Multicore execution; bounded node pools. Custom target images provide their own startup and required runtime helpers. Compiler-provided type headers and reviewed intrinsics are allowed; linked libc, libgcc, compiler-rt, libatomic, vendor HAL, OpenAMP and pre-existing kernels are excluded. FreeRTOS/Linux comparison programs are explicitly separate builds. Never infer physical WCET, electrical behavior or dual-core cache correctness from QEMU or a hosted model. The final learner record preserves unresolved or unavailable gates.

## Purpose and outcomes

Turn mechanisms into services with explicit process, thread, memory and I/O ownership. Preserve the VM and persistent store implementations; give the store one owner and communicate through bounded requests rather than sharing its internals.

The 12 projects contribute 104 implementation/verification hours. Together with reading (12), assessment (8) and consolidation (8), the provisional module budget is 132 hours. These are planning estimates, not measured learner calibration.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t56-01"></a>

### T56.01 — Process and thread objects as distinct lifetimes

A process owns an address space and handle table; its threads own execution contexts and stacks. Removing the last thread triggers process cleanup only after outstanding kernel references drain. Per-process and per-thread IDs need independent generation checks.

Refactor the existing one-thread process representation into bounded process and thread pools. Preserve old isolation tests and add two threads sharing one process mapping.

A discriminating experiment exposes: process freed while thread runnable; wrong address space selected; thread handle used as process handle; shared kernel stack; count decremented twice. Required evidence: Demonstrate shared user state within one process and isolation across two processes, with complete pool/refcount accounting after all threads exit.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T56-01](#pr-t56-01).

<a id="t56-02"></a>

### T56.02 — Spawn, exit, wait and process reaping

Spawn loads a checked image into a new process; it is distinct from copying the caller address space. Exit publishes status and closes owned resources; wait consumes a child completion according to a single-parent policy. Partial load failure must roll back frames and handles.

Implement bounded spawn/exit/wait using the existing static ELF profile and boot archive. Test parent wait before and after child exit and define orphan handling.

A discriminating experiment exposes: malformed image leaks frames; wait on nonchild; child reaped twice; parent exits first; child handle reused; wait blocks while holding global lock. Required evidence: Run real child programs with distinct exit values and reject foreign/stale waits. Reconcile all resources on load failure and orphan cleanup.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T56-02](#pr-t56-02).

<a id="t56-03"></a>

### T56.03 — Demand-zero faults and frame ownership

An admitted virtual region can begin without a physical page. A not-present user fault within that region allocates and zeroes a frame; a protection fault or invalid address is a different event. Publish the mapping only after initialization, with rollback on allocation failure.

Implement demand-zero for one bounded heap region using the existing frame allocator. Decode fault cause and retain per-process page ledgers.

A discriminating experiment exposes: kernel fault treated as user allocation; stale nonzero data exposed; allocating outside region; racing faults allocate twice; out-of-memory loses existing mapping. Required evidence: Observe real first-touch faults and zero-filled bytes, show invalid accesses terminate the offending process, and verify no frame leaks across exhaustion and exit.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T56-03](#pr-t56-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t56-04"></a>

### T56.04 — Restricted copy-on-write cloning

Restrict COW cloning to a single-threaded process with supported anonymous private pages; reject unsupported shared/device mappings. Mark both mappings read-only, increment frame references and invalidate relevant TLB entries before resuming. A write fault copies only when sharing remains.

Implement the restricted clone and write-fault path with checked frame refcounts and rollback. Test parent and child writing separate values to the same virtual address.

A discriminating experiment exposes: parent remains writable; reference count wrong; old frame freed before shootdown; out-of-memory corrupts original; unsupported multithreaded clone admitted. Required evidence: Demonstrate shared physical frames before writes and distinct contents afterward, including a sole-owner optimization and allocation-failure rollback.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T56-04](#pr-t56-04).

<a id="t56-05"></a>

### T56.05 — Bounded process channels

A channel crosses a process boundary and therefore validates user spans and owns queued copies. Handles name endpoints, not arbitrary shared pointers. Close semantics distinguish peer shutdown, queued data still available and cancellation of blocked operations.

Expose bounded send/receive/close syscalls using generation-checked endpoints. Start with fixed maximum message size and explicit directional rights.

A discriminating experiment exposes: kernel pointer supplied; output crosses unmapped page; oversized payload; endpoint used after close; sender dies with waiter enrolled; message consumed before copy succeeds. Required evidence: Run isolated client/server processes, reject invalid spans without kernel corruption and preserve queued-message accounting through peer exit.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T56-05](#pr-t56-05).

<a id="t56-06"></a>

### T56.06 — Shared-memory objects and explicit synchronization

Shared memory is a separately owned object mapped into admitted processes; mapping it does not synchronize data access. Rights, page lifetime and mapping references must remain explicit. A process exit drops its mappings but must not free storage still mapped elsewhere.

Implement bounded shared-memory create/map/unmap handles and one synchronized producer-consumer protocol. Keep executable mappings out of this teaching profile.

A discriminating experiment exposes: write granted to read-only endpoint; frame freed on first unmap; stale handle; unsynchronized plain-data race; offset/length overflow; mappings overlap protected regions. Required evidence: Show one physical object visible through two virtual mappings with controlled publication, correct rights and final-reference reclamation.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T56-06](#pr-t56-06).

<a id="t56-07"></a>

### T56.07 — Asynchronous block requests and completion ownership

Submission transfers a request buffer to the driver until terminal completion. The kernel may schedule other work while the device owns descriptors. Interrupt arrival is a prompt to consume used-ring state; it is not one completion per interrupt.

Extend the original virtio block path with a bounded outstanding-request pool, generation IDs and wait queues. Preserve descriptor/buffer ownership through success, error and timeout observation.

A discriminating experiment exposes: buffer reused before completion; used index wrap; coalesced interrupt loses completion; stale request ID; device error ignored; timeout frees still-device-owned memory. Required evidence: Run user work while actual block I/O is outstanding and account for all requests/descriptors. Demonstrate that timeout reports uncertainty without unsafe reuse.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T56-07](#pr-t56-07).

<a id="t56-08"></a>

### T56.08 — Read-only boot archive as a file service

Expose the existing bounded boot archive through open/read/seek/close rather than direct archive pointers. Per-open offsets and rights belong to handles. A read may return fewer bytes at EOF; archive data remains immutable and bounds-checked.

Implement a minimal read-only namespace and file operations over validated archive entries. Reuse the existing archive parser and reject writes or unsupported path syntax.

A discriminating experiment exposes: negative/wrapping seek; duplicate names; path traversal accepted; stale file handle; offset shared accidentally between independent opens; read beyond EOF. Required evidence: Read known file hashes through the actual user syscall path and preserve independent offsets. Reject malformed archives before exposing any entries.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T56-08](#pr-t56-08).

<a id="t56-09"></a>

### T56.09 — VM execution as a bounded service

The VM service receives a bounded program/request, verifies it and executes with explicit fuel and object limits. Request identity, caller lifetime and reply ownership are separate from VM internal handles. A service failure must not expose arbitrary kernel state.

Wrap the existing VM in an isolated process service over channels. Add request IDs, bounded program/result messages and a clear cancellation/result-too-large policy.

A discriminating experiment exposes: unverified bytecode; fuel exhaustion crashes server; client exits before reply; oversized result; duplicate request confused with new work; native pointer sent as guest value. Required evidence: Run valid and malformed programs from separate clients, preserve process isolation and return explicit resource errors while other clients progress.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T56-09](#pr-t56-09).

<a id="t56-10"></a>

### T56.10 — Single-owner persistent store service

The existing persistent store retains one mutation owner. Other processes submit bounded commands and never access its page cache or transaction structures directly. A successful reply requiring durability follows the store commit/flush boundary; transport receipt alone is insufficient.

Build a channel-based store service with bounded get/put requests, request IDs and one owner of the block handle. Reuse the existing WAL/checkpoint implementation unchanged behind the adapter.

A discriminating experiment exposes: two writers mutate cache; acknowledgment before durable commit; client retry duplicates nonidempotent effect; queue full loses ownership; store process exits midtransaction. Required evidence: Preserve the store regression suite, show concurrent clients serialized through one owner and correlate durable replies with committed log records.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T56-10](#pr-t56-10).

<a id="t56-11"></a>

### T56.11 — Service restart and reboot recovery

A service crash and a machine reboot have different surviving state. In-flight requests may have uncertain outcomes; a durable operation ID can permit safe deduplication only if stored transactionally with the effect. Restart must revoke stale endpoint generations.

Integrate VM and store clients with supervised restart and the existing disk-recovery path. Persist a known value, terminate/restart the service, then reboot the guest and verify recovery.

A discriminating experiment exposes: stale endpoint still accepted; reply lost after commit; duplicate retry effect; supervisor holds dead process resources; recovery trusts incomplete WAL; fresh disk accidentally used. Required evidence: Recover the committed value after actual reboot, distinguish uncommitted work, and account for every request as completed, rejected or uncertain. Retain disk/image identities and restart traces.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T56-11](#pr-t56-11).

### T56.12 — Physical dual-core application and OS comparison

Transfer the service decomposition to the H745: one core owns acquisition/control and the other owns bounded compute/telemetry. Keep each image freestanding and connect them with the accepted AMP protocol. Compare the same workload structure with the hosted and SMP systems while respecting their different protection and timing properties.

Integrate the accepted dual-core runtime, queues, notifications, cache/DMA rules and peer recovery. Record an end-to-end message ledger, deadline-miss policy and external timing captures.

A discriminating experiment exposes: physical run replaced by host simulation; two peripheral owners; stale epoch accepted; queue overload hidden; mixed clock timestamps; custom firmware links existing OS. Required evidence: Deliver two audited images and actual physical evidence for parallel progress, synchronization, overload and restart. Keep any missing board gate explicitly open while retaining completed build/model evidence.

Develop this mechanism in [PR-T56-12](#pr-t56-12).

## Reading guidance

Read only the assigned locator before the related experiment, then return to it after the counterexample. State the source's machine and task-model assumptions next to your own. Historical pseudocode does not authorize undefined C races; Linux, ISO C and a microcontroller memory system are separate contracts. The source/search/reflection ledger is in `research/v3/`; filenames and graph records alone do not qualify as inspected readings.

## Implementation projects

Begin PR-T56-01 after the early SMP queue milestones, then revisit PR-T53-08 and PR-T53-09 before the COW milestone PR-T56-04. This deliberate cross-module route gives user-thread migration a real process/thread substrate without requiring the later VM/store capstone first.

Complete [PR-T56-01](#pr-t56-01), [PR-T56-02](#pr-t56-02), [PR-T56-03](#pr-t56-03), [PR-T56-04](#pr-t56-04), [PR-T56-05](#pr-t56-05), [PR-T56-06](#pr-t56-06), [PR-T56-07](#pr-t56-07), [PR-T56-08](#pr-t56-08), [PR-T56-09](#pr-t56-09), [PR-T56-10](#pr-t56-10), [PR-T56-11](#pr-t56-11), [PR-T56-12](#pr-t56-12) in order. Project manifests distinguish model, host, emulator, cross-build and physical evidence. Later cumulative tests may require later mechanisms; an early milestone is assessed on its own contract and cannot borrow a later reference implementation.

## Mastery gate and feedback

Demonstrate one correct execution and one deliberately wrong variant per mechanism. Explain the first invalid transition, fix its cause, and repeat with an independently chosen input. Review safety, progress, resource lifetime and timing as distinct claims. A stress test supplies observations; bounded exhaustive schedules supply only the stated finite coverage. A deadlocked or unavailable run is not a pass.

## Consolidation and transfer

After seven days rebuild one mechanism from its public contract, change the contention or arrival pattern, and compare the new prediction with the result. After a month integrate two previously separate boundaries. Record surprises, remediation hours and the source passage that changed your reasoning.

## Environment and limits

Original SMP kernel and isolated user processes Disposable virtio disk image H745 physical endpoint for final transfer. Custom target images provide their own startup and required runtime helpers. Compiler-provided type headers and reviewed intrinsics are allowed; linked libc, libgcc, compiler-rt, libatomic, vendor HAL, OpenAMP and pre-existing kernels are excluded. FreeRTOS/Linux comparison programs are explicitly separate builds. Never infer physical WCET, electrical behavior or dual-core cache correctness from QEMU or a hosted model. The final learner record preserves unresolved or unavailable gates.

# PR-CAP-LINUX-01 — Linux architecture and threat model

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | A |

**Covered topics:** [T20.01](#t20-01), [T22.01](#t22-01), [T35.01](#t35-01).

## Working card

**Build:** Linux architecture and threat model. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Declare the newly exercised boundary and reference existing component evidence.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A changed adapter completion or ownership assumption invalidating an otherwise correct component.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-CAP-LINUX-01 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Specify a bounded telemetry service that reuses P3 and P5, with input source, message processing, output sink and operational limits. Select architecture from at least two alternatives. This is an integration milestone: link the prior component dossier and record only the new work. Apply the profile boundary in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles) and the common review in [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment).

## Inputs and expected results

Use `fixtures/integration/wire.json`. It contains an explicit input and independently recomputed expected model result. Predict the result before inspecting the answer. Synthetic data validates the stated model only; observations from actual binaries, concurrent runs or hardware must be recorded separately. Include one new normal case, one boundary and one failure case specific to this contract.

## Steps

Draw boundaries and ownership transitions, enumerate malformed input, overload, external failure and shutdown threats. Freeze memory, message and descriptor ceilings. Map reusable evidence to the contract and identify the remaining integration tests.

## Failure cases

Reject out-of-contract sizes before access. Preserve ownership and invariants when a backend fails, an operation cannot progress or storage is exhausted. Select applicable failures from the contract above and demonstrate each response. Retain the smallest reproducer and a regression check; unexplained termination or a fabricated successful observation fails the gate.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit architecture decision record, threat/failure model, dependency profile and traceability plan. This milestone adds design integration; existing parser and queue implementation hours are not charged again. Link evidence to the covered topic objectives and state what each artifact establishes. Project hours include implementation and verification; review and later retrieval have separate budgets.

## Hints and recovery

Start from the smallest deterministic fixture and write a state/ownership table. If actual behavior disagrees, separate the model, adapter and environment before editing the core. Consult the linked module's bounded readings and reduce the failure to one boundary transition. Do not resolve an oracle disagreement by changing the expected result without a contract argument.

## Transfer challenge

Change one declared capacity, backend or environment assumption. Predict the surviving invariants and regenerate the affected evidence. Explain the cost of the change and preserve the previous regression. No complete C solution is supplied: the implementation and its defense are learner work.

# PR-CAP-LINUX-03 — Fault and overload campaign

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | A |

**Covered topics:** [T32.07](#t32-07), [T35.06](#t35-06), [T21.04](#t21-04).

## Working card

**Build:** Fault and overload campaign. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Declare the newly exercised boundary and reference existing component evidence.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A changed adapter completion or ownership assumption invalidating an otherwise correct component.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-CAP-LINUX-03 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Challenge the assembled service with allocation, I/O, malformed input and slow-consumer failures while checking capacity and ownership invariants. This is an integration milestone: link the prior component dossier and record only the new work. Apply the profile boundary in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles) and the common review in [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment).

## Inputs and expected results

Use `fixtures/integration/pressure.json`. It contains an explicit input and independently recomputed expected model result. Predict the result before inspecting the answer. Synthetic data validates the stated model only; observations from actual binaries, concurrent runs or hardware must be recorded separately. Include one new normal case, one boundary and one failure case specific to this contract.

## Steps

Inject failures at component boundaries, fuzz the protocol core with bounded campaigns and exercise shutdown races. Preserve minimized regressions. Inspect hardening/dependencies and document which controls actually exist in the chosen build.

## Failure cases

Reject out-of-contract sizes before access. Preserve ownership and invariants when a backend fails, an operation cannot progress or storage is exhausted. Select applicable failures from the contract above and demonstrate each response. Retain the smallest reproducer and a regression check; unexplained termination or a fabricated successful observation fails the gate.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit reproducible campaign commands, findings and fixes, memory/dependency evidence and load data. Test coverage is supporting evidence; it cannot compensate for unexplained lifetime or race defects. Link evidence to the covered topic objectives and state what each artifact establishes. Project hours include implementation and verification; review and later retrieval have separate budgets.

## Hints and recovery

Start from the smallest deterministic fixture and write a state/ownership table. If actual behavior disagrees, separate the model, adapter and environment before editing the core. Consult the linked module's bounded readings and reduce the failure to one boundary transition. Do not resolve an oracle disagreement by changing the expected result without a contract argument.

## Transfer challenge

Change one declared capacity, backend or environment assumption. Predict the surviving invariants and regenerate the affected evidence. Explain the cost of the change and preserve the previous regression. No complete C solution is supplied: the implementation and its defense are learner work.

## Working card

**Build:** Firmware architecture and resource contract. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Declare the newly exercised boundary and reference existing component evidence.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A changed adapter completion or ownership assumption invalidating an otherwise correct component.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-CAP-MCU-01 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Specify a bounded F439 acquisition/command firmware image sharing the Linux protocol core. Define boot, normal work, overload, fault and recovery states. This is an integration milestone: link the prior component dossier and record only the new work. Apply the profile boundary in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles) and the common review in [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment).

## Inputs and expected results

Use `fixtures/integration/irq.json`. It contains an explicit input and independently recomputed expected model result. Predict the result before inspecting the answer. Synthetic data validates the stated model only; observations from actual binaries, concurrent runs or hardware must be recorded separately. Include one new normal case, one boundary and one failure case specific to this contract.

## Steps

Compare superloop/state-machine alternatives and justify the selected contexts. Freeze memory/stack, peripheral timeout, queue and timing contracts. Record board/device/manual revisions and distinguish host/model/physical evidence requirements.

## Failure cases

Reject out-of-contract sizes before access. Preserve ownership and invariants when a backend fails, an operation cannot progress or storage is exhausted. Select applicable failures from the contract above and demonstrate each response. Retain the smallest reproducer and a regression check; unexplained termination or a fabricated successful observation fails the gate.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit architecture decision record, context/ownership diagram, resource ceilings and traceability plan. Existing P3/P4 work is reused; this milestone adds integration decisions and missing tests. Link evidence to the covered topic objectives and state what each artifact establishes. Project hours include implementation and verification; review and later retrieval have separate budgets.

## Hints and recovery

Start from the smallest deterministic fixture and write a state/ownership table. If actual behavior disagrees, separate the model, adapter and environment before editing the core. Consult the linked module's bounded readings and reduce the failure to one boundary transition. Do not resolve an oracle disagreement by changing the expected result without a contract argument.

## Transfer challenge

Change one declared capacity, backend or environment assumption. Predict the surviving invariants and regenerate the affected evidence. Explain the cost of the change and preserve the previous regression. No complete C solution is supplied: the implementation and its defense are learner work.

## Contract

Add documented fault records, watchdog/progress policy and a defensible update/boot handoff design. Implement the safe fault/recovery slice within the existing application; a production bootloader is not required. This is an integration milestone: link the prior component dossier and record only the new work. Apply the profile boundary in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles) and the common review in [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment).

## Inputs and expected results

Use `fixtures/integration/recovery.json`. It contains an explicit input and independently recomputed expected model result. Predict the result before inspecting the answer. Synthetic data validates the stated model only; observations from actual binaries, concurrent runs or hardware must be recorded separately. Include one new normal case, one boundary and one failure case specific to this contract.

## Steps

Use the synthetic slot fixture to explain invalid-image rejection. Inject a selected recoverable peripheral failure and a controlled software fault on the board. Record persistent-state validity, reset reason, ownership cleanup and recovery limits. Discuss authenticity separately from CRC validity.

## Failure cases

Reject out-of-contract sizes before access. Preserve ownership and invariants when a backend fails, an operation cannot progress or storage is exhausted. Select applicable failures from the contract above and demonstrate each response. Retain the smallest reproducer and a regression check; unexplained termination or a fabricated successful observation fails the gate.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit fault decoding, reset/recovery traces, watchdog rationale and update threat model. Power-loss and authenticity claims need evidence beyond the toy slot policy. Never describe selecting a valid record as secure-update certification. Link evidence to the covered topic objectives and state what each artifact establishes. Project hours include implementation and verification; review and later retrieval have separate budgets.

## Hints and recovery

Start from the smallest deterministic fixture and write a state/ownership table. If actual behavior disagrees, separate the model, adapter and environment before editing the core. Consult the linked module's bounded readings and reduce the failure to one boundary transition. Do not resolve an oracle disagreement by changing the expected result without a contract argument.

## Transfer challenge

Change one declared capacity, backend or environment assumption. Predict the surviving invariants and regenerate the affected evidence. Explain the cost of the change and preserve the previous regression. No complete C solution is supplied: the implementation and its defense are learner work.

# PR-P1-01 — Bounded library integration

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Covered topics:** [T14.01](#t14-01), [T14.05](#t14-05), [T16.02](#t16-02), [T18.04](#t18-04).

## Working card

**Build:** Bounded library integration. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Declare the newly exercised boundary and reference existing component evidence.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A changed adapter completion or ownership assumption invalidating an otherwise correct component.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-P1-01 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Assemble the existing vector/ring and arena/pool behind caller-storage interfaces. Freeze capacity, alignment, ownership and error conventions; do not rewrite the prior algorithms. This is an integration milestone: link the prior component dossier and record only the new work. Apply the profile boundary in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles) and the common review in [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment).

## Inputs and expected results

Use `fixtures/integration/queue.json`. It contains an explicit input and independently recomputed expected model result. Predict the result before inspecting the answer. Synthetic data validates the stated model only; observations from actual binaries, concurrent runs or hardware must be recorded separately. Include one new normal case, one boundary and one failure case specific to this contract.

## Steps

Combine two previously tested components in a hosted harness. Fill the queue, reject one extra insertion, remove two values and wrap storage. Allocate aligned records through the declared allocator interface and explain their lifetime across an arena reset.

## Failure cases

Reject out-of-contract sizes before access. Preserve ownership and invariants when a backend fails, an operation cannot progress or storage is exhausted. Select applicable failures from the contract above and demonstrate each response. Retain the smallest reproducer and a regression check; unexplained termination or a fabricated successful observation fails the gate.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit public headers, state-transition traces, invariants and a lifetime diagram. The queue fixture must match without depending on internal index layout; rejected operations preserve state. Show a second backing store with the same contract. Link evidence to the covered topic objectives and state what each artifact establishes. Project hours include implementation and verification; review and later retrieval have separate budgets.

## Hints and recovery

Start from the smallest deterministic fixture and write a state/ownership table. If actual behavior disagrees, separate the model, adapter and environment before editing the core. Consult the linked module's bounded readings and reduce the failure to one boundary transition. Do not resolve an oracle disagreement by changing the expected result without a contract argument.

## Transfer challenge

Change one declared capacity, backend or environment assumption. Predict the surviving invariants and regenerate the affected evidence. Explain the cost of the change and preserve the previous regression. No complete C solution is supplied: the implementation and its defense are learner work.

# PR-P2-01 — Custom entry meets the portable core

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | D |

**Covered topics:** [T09.01](#t09-01), [T10.01](#t10-01), [T11.01](#t11-01).

## Working card

**Build:** Custom entry meets the portable core. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Declare the newly exercised boundary and reference existing component evidence.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A changed adapter completion or ownership assumption invalidating an otherwise correct component.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-P2-01 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Integrate a previously written x86-64 Linux entry/exit adapter with one portable component. Declare stack alignment, entry arguments, selected syscalls and every linked helper. This is an integration milestone: link the prior component dossier and record only the new work. Apply the profile boundary in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles) and the common review in [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment).

## Inputs and expected results

Use `fixtures/integration/binary.json`. It contains an explicit input and independently recomputed expected model result. Predict the result before inspecting the answer. Synthetic data validates the stated model only; observations from actual binaries, concurrent runs or hardware must be recorded separately. Include one new normal case, one boundary and one failure case specific to this contract.

## Steps

Link without the usual startup objects using explicit driver controls. Inspect entry address, load segments, symbols and relocation requirements. Write a bounded diagnostic through your syscall adapter and terminate by the declared exit syscall.

## Failure cases

Reject out-of-contract sizes before access. Preserve ownership and invariants when a backend fails, an operation cannot progress or storage is exhausted. Select applicable failures from the contract above and demonstrate each response. Retain the smallest reproducer and a regression check; unexplained termination or a fabricated successful observation fails the gate.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit link command, map, ELF observations and startup responsibility diagram. The synthetic forbidden-symbol case must reject malloc. The real image audit must explain resolved helpers, not only show an empty undefined-symbol list. Link evidence to the covered topic objectives and state what each artifact establishes. Project hours include implementation and verification; review and later retrieval have separate budgets.

## Hints and recovery

Start from the smallest deterministic fixture and write a state/ownership table. If actual behavior disagrees, separate the model, adapter and environment before editing the core. Consult the linked module's bounded readings and reduce the failure to one boundary transition. Do not resolve an oracle disagreement by changing the expected result without a contract argument.

## Transfer challenge

Change one declared capacity, backend or environment assumption. Predict the surviving invariants and regenerate the affected evidence. Explain the cost of the change and preserve the previous regression. No complete C solution is supplied: the implementation and its defense are learner work.


## Supplied fixtures

- [binary.json](fixtures/integration/binary.json)

```json
{
  "id": "integration-binary",
  "description": "Synthetic symbol closure and partial-write trace, not observed machine ELF",
  "input": {

      "write_adapter",
      "exit_adapter",
      "memcpy_local"
    ],
    "referenced": [
      "write_adapter",
      "exit_adapter",
      "memcpy_local",
      "malloc"
    ],
    "write_request_bytes": 9,
    "write_outcomes": [
      3,
      "EINTR",
      2,
      4
    ]
  },
  "expected": {
    "forbidden": [
      "malloc"
    ],
    "remaining_before_call": [
      9,
      6,
      6,
      4
    ],
    "transferred": 9
  },
  "verification_method": "Set difference and arithmetic trace; actual binary audited separately"
}
```

Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Complete the custom-entry executable's transfer/error contract, including short writes, interruption, zero progress and permanent errors. Keep ABI-specific behavior behind the adapter. This is an integration milestone: link the prior component dossier and record only the new work. Apply the profile boundary in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles) and the common review in [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment).

## Inputs and expected results

Use `fixtures/integration/binary.json`. It contains an explicit input and independently recomputed expected model result. Predict the result before inspecting the answer. Synthetic data validates the stated model only; observations from actual binaries, concurrent runs or hardware must be recorded separately. Include one new normal case, one boundary and one failure case specific to this contract.

## Steps

Feed the supplied deterministic write outcomes through a test adapter, then run the executable with actual Linux syscall tracing. Compare adapter and kernel evidence. Remove one optional helper and document the affected build/dependency proof.

## Failure cases

Reject out-of-contract sizes before access. Preserve ownership and invariants when a backend fails, an operation cannot progress or storage is exhausted. Select applicable failures from the contract above and demonstrate each response. Retain the smallest reproducer and a regression check; unexplained termination or a fabricated successful observation fails the gate.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit the nine-byte transfer trace and syscall/dependency inventory. EINTR retries do not advance the pointer; positive returns do. Zero progress must not cause an unbounded busy loop. Distinguish raw negative syscall results from libc errno conventions. Link evidence to the covered topic objectives and state what each artifact establishes. Project hours include implementation and verification; review and later retrieval have separate budgets.

## Hints and recovery

Start from the smallest deterministic fixture and write a state/ownership table. If actual behavior disagrees, separate the model, adapter and environment before editing the core. Consult the linked module's bounded readings and reduce the failure to one boundary transition. Do not resolve an oracle disagreement by changing the expected result without a contract argument.

## Transfer challenge

Change one declared capacity, backend or environment assumption. Predict the surviving invariants and regenerate the affected evidence. Explain the cost of the change and preserve the previous regression. No complete C solution is supplied: the implementation and its defense are learner work.

## Working card

**Build:** Concurrent ownership and backpressure. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Declare the newly exercised boundary and reference existing component evidence.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A changed adapter completion or ownership assumption invalidating an otherwise correct component.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-P5-01 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Integrate a Linux reader, bounded queue and processing worker using the shared decoder. Each message has one declared owner. Overload uses reject-newest or an explicitly justified alternative. This is an integration milestone: link the prior component dossier and record only the new work. Apply the profile boundary in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles) and the common review in [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment).

## Inputs and expected results

Use `fixtures/integration/pressure.json`. It contains an explicit input and independently recomputed expected model result. Predict the result before inspecting the answer. Synthetic data validates the stated model only; observations from actual binaries, concurrent runs or hardware must be recorded separately. Include one new normal case, one boundary and one failure case specific to this contract.

## Steps

First reproduce the deterministic offer/take/close trace, then implement synchronization around the queue predicate. Use predicate loops for condition waits. Simulate a slow consumer and measure the configured capacity ceiling without silently allocating extra backlog.

## Failure cases

Reject out-of-contract sizes before access. Preserve ownership and invariants when a backend fails, an operation cannot progress or storage is exhausted. Select applicable failures from the contract above and demonstrate each response. Retain the smallest reproducer and a regression check; unexplained termination or a fabricated successful observation fails the gate.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit ownership table, synchronization argument, capacity ledger and concurrent tests. The supplied accepted/rejected/consumed lists must reconcile exactly. A stress pass supplements rather than replaces race and lifetime reasoning. Link evidence to the covered topic objectives and state what each artifact establishes. Project hours include implementation and verification; review and later retrieval have separate budgets.

## Hints and recovery

Start from the smallest deterministic fixture and write a state/ownership table. If actual behavior disagrees, separate the model, adapter and environment before editing the core. Consult the linked module's bounded readings and reduce the failure to one boundary transition. Do not resolve an oracle disagreement by changing the expected result without a contract argument.

## Transfer challenge

Change one declared capacity, backend or environment assumption. Predict the surviving invariants and regenerate the affected evidence. Explain the cost of the change and preserve the previous regression. No complete C solution is supplied: the implementation and its defense are learner work.

## Working card

**Build:** Numerical contract before optimization. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Declare the newly exercised boundary and reference existing component evidence.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A changed adapter completion or ownership assumption invalidating an otherwise correct component.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-P6-01 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Integrate the existing causal FIR or selected computational kernel with a scalar reference and explicit numerical contract. No equivalent library routine may implement the studied core. This is an integration milestone: link the prior component dossier and record only the new work. Apply the profile boundary in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles) and the common review in [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment).

## Inputs and expected results

Use `fixtures/integration/fir.json`. It contains an explicit input and independently recomputed expected model result. Predict the result before inspecting the answer. Synthetic data validates the stated model only; observations from actual binaries, concurrent runs or hardware must be recorded separately. Include one new normal case, one boundary and one failure case specific to this contract.

## Steps

Reproduce exact rational fixture outputs with zero prehistory. Add cancelling, large/small and tail-length cases appropriate to the chosen floating/fixed representation. State absolute and relative tolerance, overflow policy and error measure before benchmarking.

## Failure cases

Reject out-of-contract sizes before access. Preserve ownership and invariants when a backend fails, an operation cannot progress or storage is exhausted. Select applicable failures from the contract above and demonstrate each response. Retain the smallest reproducer and a regression check; unexplained termination or a fabricated successful observation fails the gate.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit scalar implementation, independent oracle rationale, error observations and operation/storage model. Synthetic nanosecond samples teach summary calculation only; they are not measured speed claims. Link evidence to the covered topic objectives and state what each artifact establishes. Project hours include implementation and verification; review and later retrieval have separate budgets.

## Hints and recovery

Start from the smallest deterministic fixture and write a state/ownership table. If actual behavior disagrees, separate the model, adapter and environment before editing the core. Consult the linked module's bounded readings and reduce the failure to one boundary transition. Do not resolve an oracle disagreement by changing the expected result without a contract argument.

## Transfer challenge

Change one declared capacity, backend or environment assumption. Predict the surviving invariants and regenerate the affected evidence. Explain the cost of the change and preserve the previous regression. No complete C solution is supplied: the implementation and its defense are learner work.

# PR-T01-01: Trace, invariant and finite-representation diagnostic

## Contract

Implement a caller-storage prefix-sum routine for at most 16 signed values. Each input and every intermediate prefix must fit the declared result bounds. Return a range failure before any unrepresentable addition, even when cancellation would make the final mathematical sum fit. On every failure leave output storage unchanged; use a fixed local staging array before committing results. Before implementation, give an invariant and termination argument. Independently trace a recursive version on paper; implementation of recursion is optional, but its live-call and space account is required. Include conversion and flag exercises under an explicitly synthetic eight-bit representation, rather than claiming the host has eight-bit bytes.

The declared profile **C** applies to the boundary named here; specify harness versus component dependencies in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). Budget 6 h for implementation and verification together. Start from your own sources and the listed fixtures, with prior modules as prerequisites; no starter repository or solved program is required.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture supplies [3, -1, 4], decimal 173, width 8 and flag mask 12. Expected prefix totals are [3, 2, 6]; the representation is binary 10101101 and hexadecimal ad. The flag table enumerates all four combinations of the two selected bits. Its signed-bound cases use a declared synthetic range -32768..32767: [32767, 1, -1] and [-32768, -1, 1] fail at zero-based index 1 although their final mathematical sums fit; [-32768, 32767, 1] succeeds with prefixes [-32768, -1, 0]. Also test the corresponding INT_MAX and INT_MIN cases for the actual C int type, using <limits.h> rather than assuming its width.

The canonical fixture is `fixtures/language/PR-T01-01.json`. Preserve its supplied fields and add independent cases in your dossier. Run `python tools/verify_language_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to verify the fixture oracle; then test your C component separately.

## Steps

First fill in prediction tables without running code. Implement the iterative component with no external C-library calls; use a hosted harness for printing. Validate the input value and test the next addition against the declared bounds before evaluating it; do not rely on a wider integer type being available. Stage at most 16 prefix results locally and publish them only after complete validation. Add empty and capacity-limit inputs, count operations, and compare a recursive state trace with the iterative trace. Check representability before accepting the synthetic width.

- **T01.01:** Trace a loop and recursive sum on [3, -1, 4]; count additions, iterations and maximum live calls, then state the invariant and decreasing measure. Reject a cancellation case whose intermediate prefix exceeds the declared bounds. Retain a state table, an induction argument, checked-prefix rejection evidence, and separate O(n) work / O(1) iterative / O(n) recursive stack claims. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T01.01.a (Trace loops and recursion using explicit state tables.); T01.01.b (Derive time and auxiliary-space costs for simple implementations.); T01.01.c (State loop invariants and termination conditions before coding.).

- **T01.02:** Convert decimal 173 to binary and hexadecimal, then build a truth table for two flags and compare any/all predicates. Retain conversions checked by reconstruction and a complete truth table including neither, each and both flags. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T01.02.a (Convert between binary, hexadecimal, and decimal representations.); T01.02.b (Relate Boolean expressions to masks and truth tables.); T01.02.c (Distinguish mathematical integers from finite machine representations.).

## Failure cases

Reject a list longer than capacity, an out-of-range input, or an unrepresentable intermediate prefix without changing output storage. Do not dereference an empty range. Never compute an overflowing prefix first and inspect it afterward. A representable final mathematical sum is insufficient: retain the positive and negative cancellation failures as regressions.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit traces, an initialization/preservation/exit proof including representability before every addition, the decreasing measure, complexity accounts and a dependency contract. Show unchanged output sentinels after each cancellation failure and the successful boundary trace. Account for the fixed staging capacity separately from the unbounded-recursion stack model. Each representation result must reconstruct the decimal input. Show any-bit and all-bit predicates differ on a one-bit case.

Record contract, build/dependency evidence, independent cases, minimized failures and the specific evidence file for every linked objective. A passing synthetic oracle does not establish a passing implementation. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the review gate.

## Hints and recovery

Use k as the number already processed, not the next valid index and last processed index interchangeably. Draw recursive activations until the base case; include the base activation in the stated counting convention.

If stuck, separate the violated contract from the observed symptom and reduce the input before changing the implementation. Revisit the linked teaching section and retain the minimized case after repair.

## Transfer challenge

Replace summation with maximum selection, defining the empty case explicitly. Explain which part of the invariant and which storage bound change.

Attempt the changed condition after a delay without copying the prior solution. Explain which invariant, lifetime, resource or dependency claims survive and which must be revised.

# PR-T01-03: Reproducible bounded list tool

## Contract

Build a two-translation-unit list-sum command-line tool with a documented maximum of four decimal integers and a deterministic text protocol. The reusable computation and the effectful parser must be identifiable. Preserve builds and regressions in version control. The tool is deliberately small so that compile, link, startup and runtime failures can be investigated without unrelated application complexity.

The declared profile **A** applies to the boundary named here; specify harness versus component dependencies in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). Budget 6 h for implementation and verification together. Start from your own sources and the listed fixtures, with prior modules as prerequisites; no starter repository or solved program is required.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture defines valid input tokens [2, -5, 9], capacity 4 and signed result bounds -32768..32767. Expected output is status ok, count 3, sum 6. Empty input produces count 0, sum 0. Invalid spelling and excess capacity have distinct errors and no partial result.

The canonical fixture is `fixtures/language/PR-T01-03.json`. Preserve its supplied fields and add independent cases in your dossier. Run `python tools/verify_language_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to verify the fixture oracle; then test your C component separately.

## Steps

Write the contract and test partitions first. Compile both sources to objects and link explicitly. Record source/object/executable/process distinctions. Introduce a missing definition to capture a link failure and an input rejection to capture a runtime response. Commit one minimized regression, fix it, and replay both revisions from clean work directories.

- **T01.04:** Compile one source to an object, link it with a second source, run the executable and sketch one call with parameters, return value and live storage. Retain four saved artifacts or observations and a failure-stage classification for syntax, missing definition, bad entry setup and invalid runtime input. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T01.04.a (Distinguish source files, objects, executables, and running processes.); T01.04.b (Sketch registers, memory, stack frames, and address spaces.); T01.04.c (Separate compile-time, link-time, startup, and runtime failures.).

- **T01.05:** Create a small repository, make one deliberate defect and one fix, and rebuild each revision from a clean directory using explicit C17 flags. Retain a command transcript, two meaningful commits and a clean-checkout replay of the failure and repair. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T01.05.a (Build and run a small program from the shell.); T01.05.b (Preserve reproducible changes and regressions with version control.); T01.05.c (Record compiler versions, commands, inputs, and observed outputs.).

- **T01.06:** Specify a bounded list-sum tool, partition normal/boundary/invalid/empty cases, then preserve one minimized regression when deliberately breaking a limit check. Retain an input partition table, exact status/output contracts and an independently computed expected sum. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T01.06.a (Convert a prose requirement into inputs, outputs, and limits.); T01.06.b (Select normal, boundary, invalid, and empty-input cases.); T01.06.c (Diagnose failures before changing code and retain regression tests.).

## Failure cases

The parser must reject trailing junk, too many tokens, out-of-range values and an unrepresentable intermediate prefix. Check before every addition; a representable final sum after cancellation does not permit an overflowing prefix. Keep user input failures separate from internal invariants. Preserve the first causal error and avoid publishing an accumulated result after rejection.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit the contract, versioned build transcript, process sketch, test table and replay instructions. Another reader must reproduce the good output and the intentionally broken historical revision. Map normal, boundary, invalid and empty cases to stable test identifiers.

Record contract, build/dependency evidence, independent cases, minimized failures and the specific evidence file for every linked objective. A passing synthetic oracle does not establish a passing implementation. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the review gate.

## Hints and recovery

If the shell or compiler is unfamiliar, pause implementation to practice one compile-to-object and one link command. Use an explicit output directory and retain exact arguments rather than relying on shell history.

If stuck, separate the violated contract from the observed symptom and reduce the input before changing the implementation. Revisit the linked teaching section and retain the minimized case after repair.

## Transfer challenge

Make the capacity configurable at build time and demonstrate that the configuration identity follows the binary and tests.

Attempt the changed condition after a delay without copying the prior solution. Explain which invariant, lifetime, resource or dependency claims survive and which must be revised.

# PR-T02-01: Declarator and separate-unit interface catalog

## Contract

Create a small matrix-processing interface and callback dispatcher split across two implementation sources and two consumers. Build a declaration catalog that records identifier grouping, type category, scope, namespace, linkage and storage duration. The component must have complete prototypes and callbacks with exact signatures; pointer casts may not serve as signature adapters.

The declared profile **A** applies to the boundary named here; specify harness versus component dependencies in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). Budget 8 h for implementation and verification together. Start from your own sources and the listed fixtures, with prior modules as prerequisites; no starter repository or solved program is required.

## Inputs and expected results

The synthetic fixture is an object declaration manifest: internal state, external state, block-local temporary and static-duration local cache. Expected categories follow explicitly declared properties. Functions have a separate call/linkage analysis and are not assigned object storage duration. Actual compiler symbol output is collected separately because optimization can remove unused symbols.

The canonical fixture is `fixtures/language/PR-T02-01.json`. Preserve its supplied fields and add independent cases in your dossier. Run `python tools/verify_language_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to verify the fixture oracle; then test your C component separately.

## Steps

Start with pointer-to-row and function-pointer declarations. Compile the public header alone, create two consumers, and inspect each object. Add tag/member/ordinary-name examples and prototype-scope names. Introduce one inconsistent declaration, capture the diagnostic or link limitation, then replace it with a compatible contract.

- **T02.01:** Make a catalog of pointer-to-array, array-of-pointers and function-pointer declarations; annotate declarations versus definitions and rewrite one nested declaration using two typedefs. Retain expression-based explanations, compilable examples and intermediate typedefs that preserve the original type. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T02.01.a (Parse pointer, array, and function declarators systematically.); T02.01.b (Distinguish declarations, definitions, typedef names, and type specifiers.); T02.01.c (Rewrite intricate declarations using readable intermediate typedefs.).

- **T02.02:** Build a matrix of complete/incomplete, object/function, scalar/aggregate examples and compare two declarations of the same external function. Retain a compatibility table and a wrapper-struct experiment that demonstrates stronger semantic separation. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T02.02.a (Distinguish object, function, incomplete, scalar, and aggregate types.); T02.02.b (Identify compatible types across separate declarations.); T02.02.c (Explain the limits of typedef-based semantic type separation.).

- **T02.03:** Trace an identifier through nested blocks, a prototype, a structure tag/member and a label; repair a collision by naming the role. Retain an annotated scope map and negative examples for actual collisions, distinguished from legal but confusing shadowing. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T02.03.a (Trace block, file, function, and prototype scopes.); T02.03.b (Distinguish tag, label, member, and ordinary identifier namespaces.); T02.03.c (Diagnose shadowing and accidental name collisions.).

- **T02.04:** Inspect symbols from two objects and deliberately mismatch a public declaration; record extern, static, register and thread-storage examples under their selected edition. Retain a declaration/linkage/storage-duration table, symbol evidence and a repaired cross-unit mismatch. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T02.04.a (Compare internal linkage, external linkage, and no linkage.); T02.04.b (Analyze extern, static, register, and thread-storage declarations by edition.); T02.04.c (Diagnose inconsistent declarations across translation units.).

- **T02.05:** Pass a row pointer to a matrix function and a context-bearing callback to a dispatcher; state signatures before writing bodies. Retain header compilation, compatible callback calls and a rejected cast-based adaptation with a real wrapper alternative. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T02.05.a (Specify parameter and return types with complete prototypes.); T02.05.b (Compare array-parameter adjustment with actual array objects.); T02.05.c (Audit callback signatures, function-pointer conversions, and call compatibility.).

## Failure cases

Reject a null callback according to the public policy. Do not assume the linker diagnoses every type mismatch. Do not index a matrix through int ** when the representation is an array of rows. Keep deliberate erroneous sources separate from the valid build.

## Acceptance and evidence

Supply the catalog, a namespace/scope map, a symbol comparison and a caller test for each public function. Explain why typedef aliases do not enforce units and show one wrapper-struct alternative. Each of the five linked subtopics needs its own evidence entry.

Record contract, build/dependency evidence, independent cases, minimized failures and the specific evidence file for every linked objective. A passing synthetic oracle does not establish a passing implementation. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the review gate.

## Hints and recovery

Translate each declarator into an expression involving its identifier; introduce typedefs only after that explanation. Use a wrapper function when adapting behavior rather than changing a function pointer’s type.

If stuck, separate the violated contract from the observed symptom and reduce the input before changing the implementation. Revisit the linked teaching section and retain the minimized case after repair.

## Transfer challenge

Add an opaque incomplete type to the API and identify which consumer operations require moving into the implementation.

Attempt the changed condition after a delay without copying the prior solution. Explain which invariant, lifetime, resource or dependency claims survive and which must be revised.

# PR-T02-02: Typed expressions and a two-pass variadic protocol

## Contract

Implement a bounded variadic formatter using a count plus explicit tags. Limit the protocol to promoted int and double arguments; support a sizing pass and a writing pass through va_copy. Separately build a typed-expression and sequencing notebook, replacing ambiguous effectful call-site expressions with explicit steps before they reach the formatter.

The declared profile **A** applies to the boundary named here; specify harness versus component dependencies in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). Budget 8 h for implementation and verification together. Start from your own sources and the listed fixtures, with prior modules as prerequisites; no starter repository or solved program is required.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture supplies an abstract signed value -1 and unsigned comparison width 16. Its converted value is 65535 and its comparison against unsigned 1 is false. This is a synthetic arithmetic model, not a claim that the host unsigned int has 16 bits. Add formatter cases for zero arguments and a promoted float.

The canonical fixture is `fixtures/language/PR-T02-02.json`. Preserve its supplied fields and add independent cases in your dossier. Run `python tools/verify_language_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to verify the fixture oracle; then test your C component separately.

## Steps

Document the tag/count convention, annotate promotions at every call and pair each va_list initialization/copy with va_end. Draw expression trees for arithmetic and conditional operators. Build sequencing graphs for safe and unsafe examples. Run only defined expressions and compare strict-build diagnostics for separate negative cases.

- **T02.06:** Design a tagged/count convention for a statistics formatter, perform two passes using va_copy, and audit every call-site argument after promotion. Retain a promotion ledger, empty-list case, two-pass output and explicit va_start/va_end ownership for each list. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T02.06.a (Apply default argument promotions at variadic call sites.); T02.06.b (Use va_start, va_arg, va_copy, and va_end correctly.); T02.06.c (Specify a reliable argument-type and argument-count convention.).

- **T02.07:** Draw the tree and type each node for arithmetic, conditional and assignment examples; add a range-checked conversion boundary. Retain a typed expression tree and a table showing both accepted conversions and rejected out-of-range values. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T02.07.a (Separate precedence, associativity, and evaluation order.); T02.07.b (Trace integer promotions and usual arithmetic conversions.); T02.07.c (Analyze conditional expressions, assignments, and explicit casts.).

- **T02.08:** List side effects for a nested-call example and replace a conflicting increment/read expression with explicit temporary values. Retain a sequencing graph, classification under the selected edition and a repair whose result no longer depends on argument order. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T02.08.a (Distinguish sequenced, unsequenced, and indeterminately sequenced evaluations.); T02.08.b (Classify conflicting reads and writes under the selected edition.); T02.08.c (Refactor expressions into explicit, reviewable steps.).

## Failure cases

A tag/type mismatch is a caller contract violation that cannot generally be detected by the callee; do not execute it as an ordinary malformed-input case. Insufficient output capacity must report required size and preserve the chosen termination policy.

## Acceptance and evidence

Show identical semantic output from both traversals, exact capacity boundaries and a conversion ledger. Explain an unspecified argument order that remains defined and one unsequenced conflict that does not. Retain the explicit-step repair and a new test using negative and unsigned inputs.

Record contract, build/dependency evidence, independent cases, minimized failures and the specific evidence file for every linked objective. A passing synthetic oracle does not establish a passing implementation. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the review gate.

## Hints and recovery

Keep argument extraction in one switch with the protocol types visible. Separate precedence questions from conversion questions before considering sequencing.

If stuck, separate the violated contract from the observed symptom and reduce the input before changing the implementation. Revisit the linked teaching section and retain the minimized case after repair.

## Transfer challenge

Replace the variadic interface with a tagged-array interface and compare what becomes checkable and what storage the caller must supply.

Attempt the changed condition after a delay without copying the prior solution. Explain which invariant, lifetime, resource or dependency claims survive and which must be revised.

## Contract

Implement a caller-owned record and two views: a read-only pointer/length view and a mutable destination. Use aggregate and designated initialization for records, then expose explicit reset and update operations. The fixture initializes a four-element synthetic aggregate at indices 1 and 3 with 7 and 9. Expected member values are [0, 7, 0, 9]. This describes value initialization only; padding bytes and non-integer representations remain outside its oracle.

The canonical fixture is `fixtures/language/PR-T02-03.json`. Preserve its supplied fields and add independent cases in your dossier. Run `python tools/verify_language_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to verify the fixture oracle; then test your C component separately.

## Steps

Compare static implicit initialization, automatic explicit initialization and later assignment. Draw lifetimes for a file-scope and block-scope compound literal. Compile const-pointer and pointer-to-const examples, including an invalid qualifier-loss conversion. Write a view contract that says who can mutate the underlying storage and when.

For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T02.10.a (Distinguish pointer qualification from pointed-to qualification.); T02.10.b (Design const-correct APIs and inspect qualifier-loss diagnostics.); T02.10.c (Introduce volatile and restrict without treating them as synchronization.).

## Failure cases

Reject destination capacity below the required length without writing. Never return a view into an expired local aggregate. Keep volatile and restrict experiments separate from any concurrency claim, and do not byte-compare structures to establish value equality.

## Acceptance and evidence

Provide member-value checks, a lifetime diagram and header tests for read-only access. Explain why omitted members are initialized while an unrelated uninitialized automatic object is not. The dependency audit applies to the reusable component, including compiler-emitted helpers.
