## Contract

Implement an artifact identity/compatibility report and review the command service against a concrete security/failure checklist. Distinguish digest consistency, signer trust, rollback and reproducibility.

Use dependency profile A under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). Implement the studied mechanism yourself; a mature library may be a separately declared hosted oracle. This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification, with reading/assessment budgeted in the module.

## Inputs and expected results

The supplied fixture `fixtures/embedded/PR-T35-06.json` contains concrete inputs and exact expected fields; use the supplied-fixture download below in the local handbook. Payload abc has a known SHA-256 digest; versions 1,2,3 under minimum 2 have compatibility false, true, true. A matching digest without a trusted signer does not justify authenticity.

Use a mature independent SHA256 implementation and explicit version/trust predicates. No homemade signature algorithm is supplied or required.

## Steps

Record source/dependency/tool/artifact identities and update trust/rollback policy. Review lengths, arithmetic, lifetimes, effects, quotas, isolation, sensitive data and hardening against retained regressions; repair one deliberately flawed boundary and list remaining risks.

First write the public interface, storage/effect limits and expected failure state. Derive at least one supplied value by hand before coding. Implement one normal path, then add each boundary/failure path. Run the independent fixture oracle and your own implementation checks separately; preserve versions, commands, binary identity and raw observations.

## Failure cases

Expose a checksum replaced together with the bytes, an untrusted key, a compatible but uncommitted image, rollback and unsupported threat assumptions.

## Acceptance and evidence

Identity/compatibility fields and review regressions pass. Each reviewed property has concrete evidence or an explicit residual gap; reproducibility is not authenticity or trustworthiness.

Retain an evidence item for each of the three original objectives of every linked topic, including explanation and a check of its own property. Submit the implementation/analysis, input/output replay, dependency/resource ledger and limitations. Expected synthetic values do not substitute for observed tool or physical-target behavior.

## Hints and recovery

Digest agreement answers which bytes match. Authentication additionally needs a justified trust chain and verification procedure.

On a disagreement, minimize the first failing input/event prefix and inspect contract, units and ownership before changing several variables. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted remediation rather than restarting unrelated modules.

## Transfer challenge

Raise the minimum accepted version and show the policy effect without confusing it with a cryptographic signature.

## Contract

Implement the studied mechanism yourself. Existing base work is reused with its original acceptance evidence; this budget covers only the new work described here.

## Inputs and expected results

Put 11, put 22, take, put 33, put 44, put 55, take yield final `[33,44]`; put 55 returns full and preserves `[22,33,44]`. Eight-byte payload slots occupy 24 bytes at offsets 0, 8, 16 before link metadata. The Euclid certificate 1071, 462 ends 21 after three remainder steps. The sorted-but-not-permuted mutation `[2,1]→[1,1]` must be rejected.

## Acceptance and evidence

For .01a submit I/O relation, invariant and Euclid progress derivation; for .01b exact per-primitive counts plus clearly scoped worst/expected/amortized contrasts; for .01c the lost-value first transition. For .02a submit valid indices/offsets and ownership links; .02b paired logical/physical traces, live storage and failure work; .02c an API-level invalidation check after storage-policy change. The supplied states and independent oracle pass, and no copied full implementation is charged as new work.

Keep the evidence items separate for each linked topic's three objectives. Retain the actual input/output replay, build identity, dependency/storage ledger, first counterexample and limits. Deterministic synthetic expectations do not substitute for required executable or device observations.

## Hints and recovery

If equal logical states conceal different costs, annotate each physical read/write or link followed. Payload bytes are not total node bytes. A decreasing Euclid operand proves progress only while the divisor is positive. Start the permutation mutation with two values, where the missing multiplicity is visible.

## Transfer challenge

Keep the same observable trace but change ring capacity to 4. Predict physical offsets and failure point before replay; state which earlier proof obligations change.

- [R-clrs-4](#r-clrs-4): 6.2 Maintaining the heap property. Separate intact child subheaps from the single moving sift-down violation.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T36-02 — Paired original assembly lower-bound kernels

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | C |

**Executable anchors:** algorithms. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/algorithms/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T36](#t36).

**Covered topics:** [T36.03](#t36-03), [T36.04](#t36-04).

## Working card

**Build:** Paired original assembly lower-bound kernels. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Implement lower-bound, stable insertion and heap repair kernels under both target ABIs. Use representation-preserving traces to connect assembly state to the abstract algorithm.

**Changed-condition challenge:** An equal-key or extreme-index case that leaves nominal examples correct while violating the invariant.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T36-02 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Write separate original `.S` files for SysV x86-64 and Cortex-M4 Thumb implementing unsigned 32-bit lower bound. Expose a checked C interface with array pointer, bounded 32-bit length/key and returned index in 0..n. Length 0 performs no load and permits null; otherwise storage is a live sorted uint32_t array. Limit n to a declared address-safe maximum (use n≤1024 for this milestone). Retain the prior C implementation as oracle. Add a separate nested-call ABI probe, not a library search delegation.

This 10-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation belong to the module budget. The concrete original fixture is `fixtures/algorithms/PR-T36-02.json`; run `tools/verify_algorithms_fixtures.py` for its independent narrow oracle, then run your own component checks separately.

Declare the Profile C component boundary and Profile A hosted harness under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles); audit object and final symbols, generated code and callback effects. Implement the studied mechanism yourself. Existing base work is reused with its original acceptance evidence; this budget covers only the new work described here.

## Inputs and expected results

The supplied duplicate/high-bit array returns indices 0, 1, 1, 3, 4 for keys 0, 1, 7, 8, UINT32_MAX. Each supplied interval certificate has three comparisons; empty returns 0. Add a key beyond the last small value, singleton, all-equal and 1024-element cases. Sentinels/guarded bounds are actual harness observations, while fixture counts concern the declared algorithm.

## Steps

Derive the half-open invariant and `lo+(hi-lo)/2` progress. Draw register liveness and each load address before assembly. Use SysV scalar argument registers and AAPCS r0–r3 under the pinned sources; document any wrapper rearrangement. Assemble/disassemble both actual files and execute x86 under Linux plus Thumb on a declared Cortex-M4 ISA emulator or board. Add a probe caller that seeds preserved registers, poisons permitted scratch values and tests nested-call SP alignment/LR preservation. Compare with prior C outputs and trace/count certificates.

## Failure cases

Reject unsorted input or bad extent in the checked wrapper before invoking the unchecked internal kernel. Include n 0/n 1, duplicates, high-bit unsigned keys, signed-branch mutation, loading a[n], wrong scaling and preserved-register corruption. A boundary test must not manufacture undefined C accesses merely to obtain a crash.

## Acceptance and evidence

For .03a submit both authored sources, declarations and captured executions; .03b liveness, signed/unsigned predicates, preserved set and nested-call alignment; .03c sentinel/guard, scratch-poison and callee-save checks with disassembly. For .04a give interval/progress traces; .04b annotate every load width/offset and address bound; .04c compare counts to prior C and supply smallest signedness/off-by-one counterexamples. Cross-compiling alone does not satisfy execution; emulator identity is disclosed.

Keep the evidence items separate for each linked topic's three objectives. Retain the actual input/output replay, build identity, dependency/storage ledger, first counterexample and limits. Deterministic synthetic expectations do not substitute for required executable or device observations.

## Hints and recovery

On x86, 32-bit arithmetic registers zero-extend their 64-bit parent; keep pointer width separate. On Arm, unsigned lower uses the no-borrow interpretation of C. A nested BL overwrites LR, even if the leaf search never did. Before changing instruction sequences, find the first load/interval/preserved register that disagrees.

## Transfer challenge

Retarget one scalar declaration to a different ABI in a separate experiment. State the new argument/stack obligations; keep algorithm and ISA claims distinct.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T36-03 — Tagged stable insertion in assembly

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Executable anchors:** algorithms. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/algorithms/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T36](#t36).

**Covered topics:** [T36.05](#t36-05).

## Working card

**Build:** Tagged stable insertion in assembly. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Implement lower-bound, stable insertion and heap repair kernels under both target ABIs. Use representation-preserving traces to connect assembly state to the abstract algorithm.

**Changed-condition challenge:** An equal-key or extreme-index case that leaves nominal examples correct while violating the invariant.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T36-03 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Write an original bounded insertion kernel in one of the two already exercised assembly ISAs for actual typed records `{uint32_t key; uint32_t tag;}`; n≤32. Sort by unsigned key and preserve initial order of equal tags. Reuse the completed T15 insertion/merge/heap sort artifacts as differential subjects, without reimplementing those full algorithms. Supply prefix-state and comparison/write counters in a separate instrumentation build.

This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation belong to the module budget. The concrete original fixture is `fixtures/algorithms/PR-T36-03.json`; run `tools/verify_algorithms_fixtures.py` for its independent narrow oracle, then run your own component checks separately.

Declare the Profile C component boundary and Profile A hosted harness under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles); audit object and final symbols, generated code and callback effects. Implement the studied mechanism yourself. Existing base work is reused with its original acceptance evidence; this budget covers only the new work described here.

## Inputs and expected results

Tags A..E denote distinct numeric tags in the target harness. Fixture `(3,A),(1,B),(3,C),(2,D),(1,E)` gives B, E, D, A, C, six shift writes, four final placements and nine key comparisons. The merge checkpoint takes left ties before right ties. Sorted/reverse five-key inputs use four/ten comparisons with the declared final-placement convention. Heap-sort evidence is ordering/permutation only, since its prior policy is unstable.

## Steps

Define the pending record, sorted prefix and multiset including the pending value before moving anything. Implement only the bounded kernel, annotate record stride and register pressure, then disassemble/execute it. Emit prefix certificates for the fixture and an equal-key family. Compare each complete result with stable prior C insertion/merge; compare heap sort without requiring tie stability. Count exact moves independently from inversion numbers. Retain build/source provenance so instrumentation and performance versions are distinguishable.

## Failure cases

Test n 0/n 1/32, all equal, largest unsigned keys, capacity 31 for 32 records in the checked API, and a `≥` shift mutation. Whole-record moves must keep key/tag pairs intact. Failure returns before any writes; stable but corrupted multiplicities and sorted but reversed tags both fail acceptance.

## Acceptance and evidence

For .05a submit insertion and merge-prefix reasoning with tag/multiset checks; .05b actual authored assembly, execution and identified prior full-sort reuse; .05c comparison/shift/placement counts for sorted, reverse and duplicate-rich families, with timing in a separate column. Callee-save/sentinel and dependency audits pass as in PR-T36-02. Do not claim a speedup from fewer comparisons alone.

Keep the evidence items separate for each linked topic's three objectives. Retain the actual input/output replay, build identity, dependency/storage ledger, first counterexample and limits. Deterministic synthetic expectations do not substitute for required executable or device observations.

## Hints and recovery

Preserve the pending whole record across shifts. A tie must stop insertion and choose the left head in merge for this policy. Count comparisons at the stopping predecessor, but not a nonexistent predecessor when insertion reaches index 0. If counts differ by one, replay that boundary before altering the algorithm.

## Transfer challenge

Add a descending comparator policy only in a separate interface experiment. Predict which tie rules stay the same and compare observable tag stability.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T36-04 — Moving heap violation in original assembly

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6 h | core | C |

**Executable anchors:** algorithms. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/algorithms/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T36](#t36).

**Covered topics:** [T36.06](#t36-06).

## Working card

**Build:** Moving heap violation in original assembly. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Implement lower-bound, stable insertion and heap repair kernels under both target ABIs. Use representation-preserving traces to connect assembly state to the abstract algorithm.

**Changed-condition challenge:** An equal-key or extreme-index case that leaves nominal examples correct while violating the invariant.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T36-04 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Replace only the sift-down kernel in the completed PR-T14-05 max heap with original assembly in one ISA. Keep its capacity, key multiplicity and API intact; no new heap/container implementation. Kernel precondition: all edges obey heap order except possibly those from the selected p, and both child subtrees are heaps. Equal child keys choose the left child; stop when parent≥selected child. n≤1024 and p<n, with a separate empty-heap no-op wrapper.

This 6-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation belong to the module budget. The concrete original fixture is `fixtures/algorithms/PR-T36-04.json`; run `tools/verify_algorithms_fixtures.py` for its independent narrow oracle, then run your own component checks separately.

Declare the Profile C component boundary and Profile A hosted harness under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles); audit object and final symbols, generated code and callback effects. Implement the studied mechanism yourself. Existing base work is reused with its original acceptance evidence; this budget covers only the new work described here.

## Inputs and expected results

Fixture root replacement `[5,7,8,3,6,2]` follows 0→2 and ends `[8,7,5,3,6,2]`, three comparisons and one swap. A two-level violation follows 0→1→3, four comparisons and two swaps. `[5,5,4]` makes two comparisons and no swap. Counts include sibling and parent comparisons; no-child terminal contributes zero.

## Steps

Freeze the prior heap and swap in a single function boundary. Derive child-index arithmetic under the length bound and draw the moving invariant. Implement/execute the kernel with callee-save and sentinels. Emit snapshots only after complete swaps; independently check intact edges, multiplicities and final order. Reuse prior build/insert/extract tests, adding one-child, equal-child and maximum-length cases. Compute the visited-level height bound separately from measured work.

## Failure cases

Reject p outside the live heap, incorrect n/backing capacity and malformed preconditions through the diagnostic wrapper. Include a right-child-out-of-range mutation, reversed child choice, dropped duplicate and integer child-index wrap reasoning. Reject before mutation where validation applies; the trusted internal kernel requires its documented precondition.

## Acceptance and evidence

For .06a give local precondition and state-path derivation; .06b source/disassembly/execution showing only the kernel replacement and preserved API/tie policy; .06c per-swap independent heap/multiplicity certificates and height/work ledger. Prior full heap acceptance remains referenced. The public oracle validates these narrow certificates, not a provided full C heap.

Keep the evidence items separate for each linked topic's three objectives. Retain the actual input/output replay, build identity, dependency/storage ledger, first counterexample and limits. Deterministic synthetic expectations do not substitute for required executable or device observations.

## Hints and recovery

The violation moves with the displaced old parent. Check child existence before comparing its value; for a leaf there is no comparison. A valid final maximum is not enough: every retained key count must match the original. Repair the smallest one-child case before a large random heap.

## Transfer challenge

Use the same certificate format for a min heap without changing the original max-heap artifact. Identify which predicates reverse and which ownership/bounds facts remain.

# PR-T36-05 — AVL mutation certificates and path costs

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6 h | core | C |

**Executable anchors:** algorithms. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/algorithms/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T36](#t36).

**Covered topics:** [T36.07](#t36-07).

## Working card

**Build:** AVL mutation certificates and path costs. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Implement lower-bound, stable insertion and heap repair kernels under both target ABIs. Use representation-preserving traces to connect assembly state to the abstract algorithm.

**Changed-condition challenge:** An equal-key or extreme-index case that leaves nominal examples correct while violating the invariant.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T36-05 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Add a snapshot/certificate interface to the completed PR-T14-06 AVL tree. Reuse its full insertion/deletion implementation, unique-key reject-duplicate policy and ownership API. Emit stable node IDs, keys, children, parents and cached heights after each complete mutation; null height 0. Build an independent checker that recomputes metadata from reachability rather than trusting the cached heights. Intermediate rotation snapshots are explicitly marked possibly unbalanced.

This 6-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation belong to the module budget. The concrete original fixture is `fixtures/algorithms/PR-T36-05.json`; run `tools/verify_algorithms_fixtures.py` for its independent narrow oracle, then run your own component checks separately.

Declare the Profile C component boundary and Profile A hosted harness under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles); audit object and final symbols, generated code and callback effects. Implement the studied mechanism yourself. Existing base work is reused with its original acceptance evidence; this budget covers only the new work described here.

## Inputs and expected results

The LR fixture 30, 10, 20 ends root 20 with inorder 10, 20, 30 and height 2. Deleting 1 from root 2/left 1/right 4(children 3, 5) ends root 4 with inorder 2, 3, 4, 5 and height 3. Duplicate 20 returns reject/unchanged. A balanced 1, 2, 3 search for 3 takes two key comparisons; the right chain takes three.

## Steps

Freeze prior source, add read-only certificate emission, then derive both rotations by partitioning subtrees. Recompute each node height bottom-up and check parent edges and single reachability. Replay LR and learner-created RL cases, then a deletion with repairs at more than one ancestor from the prior full implementation. Compare the same key set to a bounded unbalanced prior tree; instrument comparisons rather than timing. Inject one stale height/parent into a saved certificate without corrupting a live target pointer.

## Failure cases

Checker rejects duplicate keys, cycles/shared children, unreachable nodes, wrong parent/root, stale heights and unacceptable final balance. Duplicate insertion and absent removal preserve state under the existing policy. Do not perform UB to demonstrate a dangling node; use IDs/generation checks. The simple supplied deletion does not waive the multiple-ancestor path evidence.

## Acceptance and evidence

For .07a submit single/double rotation and complete deletion-path derivations; .07b actual prior-tree instrumentation, recomputed certificates and unchanged duplicate snapshot; .07c balanced/degenerate comparison counts and scope of worst-case depth claims. Original AVL full-build evidence is linked rather than duplicated. The supplied checker/oracle does not implement rotations or deletion for the learner.

Keep the evidence items separate for each linked topic's three objectives. Retain the actual input/output replay, build identity, dependency/storage ledger, first counterexample and limits. Deterministic synthetic expectations do not substitute for required executable or device observations.

## Hints and recovery

Fix child links first, then heights from the lowest changed node upward. In LR, the middle key becomes the subtree root. Equal inorder output can conceal shared/cyclic links; compare reachable IDs before heights. If deletion fails only near the root, inspect where the recorded ancestor walk stopped.

## Transfer challenge

Explain how a red-black policy certificate would differ using the already inspected CLRS properties; do not build another full balanced tree in this budget.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T36-06 — Tombstone probing and byte-span adapters

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Executable anchors:** algorithms. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/algorithms/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T36](#t36).

**Covered topics:** [T36.08](#t36-08).

## Working card

**Build:** Tombstone probing and byte-span adapters. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Implement lower-bound, stable insertion and heap repair kernels under both target ABIs. Use representation-preserving traces to connect assembly state to the abstract algorithm.

**Changed-condition challenge:** An equal-key or extreme-index case that leaves nominal examples correct while violating the invariant.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T36-06 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Write one original bounded assembly lookup kernel over the completed T14 open-addressed table and one small original C naive byte-span matcher with a caller output array. Reuse the prior full table and T15 prefix matcher/preprocessing. For this milestone capacity 8 uses h(k)=k mod 8 and linear steps; lookup visits at most capacity slots, stops at empty, continues past deleted and never mutates. Matcher reports all overlapping offsets; empty pattern matches all n+1 boundaries.

This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation belong to the module budget. The concrete original fixture is `fixtures/algorithms/PR-T36-06.json`; run `tools/verify_algorithms_fixtures.py` for its independent narrow oracle, then run your own component checks separately.

Declare the Profile C component boundary and Profile A hosted harness under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles); audit object and final symbols, generated code and callback effects. Implement the studied mechanism yourself. Existing base work is reused with its original acceptance evidence; this budget covers only the new work described here.

## Inputs and expected results

Key 22 visits 6, 7, 0, 1, 2, 3 and is absent; key 16 hits 0; key 2 hits 2. An absent key in a full eight-slot table returns absent after 8 probes. Byte text 0, 97, 0, 97, 0 with patterns 97, 0 and 0, 97, 0 reports 1, 3 and 0, 2 with six/seven naive comparisons. Empty pattern reports 0..5 without comparisons. Numeric zero is data.

## Steps

Annotate slot layout and stop states from the prior representation; do not cast an unrelated byte array into it. Assemble/disassemble/execute lookup and record visits. Define span lengths, output-capacity preflight and overlap policy before writing the bounded matcher. Compare outputs with the reused prefix matcher and independent slice enumeration. Replay tombstones, wraparound, full-table absence and embedded-zero cases; record probe/comparison counts beside correctness.

## Failure cases

Reject invalid slot states/capacity in a checked wrapper. Test all-deleted tables, zero capacity, pattern longer than text, empty text/pattern, output capacity one short and a tombstone-stop mutation. On output-capacity failure return required count/status and preserve the output buffer; preflight by a read-only count pass or a declared transactional strategy. No strlen/strstr/memcmp delegation.

## Acceptance and evidence

For .08a submit reachability argument, bounded termination and expected-bound assumptions; .08b actual assembly and small original C output API, with prior table/prefix work explicitly reused; .08c independent visit/byte counts and each wrap/full/deleted/zero boundary. Audit ABI, symbols and caller-storage lifetime. A few fast probes cannot establish a probability theorem.

Keep the evidence items separate for each linked topic's three objectives. Retain the actual input/output replay, build identity, dependency/storage ledger, first counterexample and limits. Deterministic synthetic expectations do not substitute for required executable or device observations.

## Hints and recovery

An empty slot and a tombstone have different logical meanings even if both have no current key. Count candidate windows using n−m only after proving m≤n. The empty-pattern output includes the end boundary. If capacity failure writes partial output, move counting/validation before commit.

## Transfer challenge

Replace the fixture hash with the existing table’s real hash in a separate run. Explain which termination invariant survives and which distribution assumptions change.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T36-07 — Graph frontier refinement and checked distances

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Executable anchors:** algorithms. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/algorithms/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T36](#t36).

**Covered topics:** [T36.09](#t36-09).

## Working card

**Build:** Graph frontier refinement and checked distances. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Implement lower-bound, stable insertion and heap repair kernels under both target ABIs. Use representation-preserving traces to connect assembly state to the abstract algorithm.

**Changed-condition challenge:** An equal-key or extreme-index case that leaves nominal examples correct while violating the invariant.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T36-07 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Adapt the completed T15 BFS/weighted solver through the T14 queue/priority heap, adding frontier certificates and an explicit directed graph API for at most 8 vertices/24 edges. Do not rebuild the complete solver or heap. Require nonnegative integer weights, deterministic vertex-ID ties and finite distances 0..65534 with unreachable represented separately. Reject a candidate sum outside that range before committing any public result; preserve the previous output on errors.

This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation belong to the module budget. The concrete original fixture is `fixtures/algorithms/PR-T36-07.json`; run `tools/verify_algorithms_fixtures.py` for its independent narrow oracle, then run your own component checks separately.

Declare the Profile C component boundary and Profile A hosted harness under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles); audit object and final symbols, generated code and callback effects. Implement the studied mechanism yourself. Existing base work is reused with its original acceptance evidence; this budget covers only the new work described here.

## Inputs and expected results

Original A/B/C/D/E graph gives weighted 0, 2, 1, 3, unreachable and hops 0, 1, 1, 2, unreachable. Settlement order is A, C, B, D; predecessors are none, C, A, B, none. The negative-edge reasoning example has true B distance−1 although early settlement says 1. Candidate 65530+10 is a range error, not an unreachable or wrapped result.

## Steps

Identify prior source/functions and retained contracts. Trace BFS layers beside tentative weighted labels and settled membership, recording each improvement. Add a validation/range adapter and snapshot emission; use caller storage and the prior heap ownership policy. For each tiny graph, independently enumerate all simple paths and minimize weight/hops; reconstruct predecessor paths and check every edge sum. Read the historical Problem 2 passage and mark its connected presentation versus this disconnected C API.

## Failure cases

Include isolated source, parallel edges, self-loop, zero-weight ties, no path, negative input and finite-sum overflow. Reject invalid endpoints/counts before work; negative-edge tests are diagnostic counterexamples, not accepted inputs. A predecessor cycle or settling a nonminimum tentative label fails even if one output happens to be correct.

## Acceptance and evidence

For .09a submit distinct layer/tentative/settled traces; .09b adapted queue/heap calls, validation/range/failure evidence and disconnected output; .09c tiny independent path enumeration, predecessor equations and negative/premature-settle counterexamples. Explain why the exponential oracle is restricted to 8 vertices and is not the target algorithm. Link the earlier full implementations and report only new adapter/certificate work.

Keep the evidence items separate for each linked topic's three objectives. Retain the actual input/output replay, build identity, dependency/storage ledger, first counterexample and limits. Deterministic synthetic expectations do not substitute for required executable or device observations.

## Hints and recovery

A BFS queue orders hop layers, not arbitrary weights. In the original trace B must improve after C is processed. Check `weight≤limit−distance` before adding; do not test a wrapped sum. Start disagreement debugging at the first incorrect tentative update or settlement, not the final path string.

## Transfer challenge

Compare a minimum spanning tree question with the same graph’s shortest-path question using the historical Problem 1/Problem 2 distinction; no new spanning-tree implementation is required.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T36-08 — Typed and context interfaces over existing kernels

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T36](#t36).

**Covered topics:** [T36.02](#t36-02), [T36.10](#t36-10).

## Working card

**Build:** Typed and context interfaces over existing kernels. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Implement lower-bound, stable insertion and heap repair kernels under both target ABIs. Use representation-preserving traces to connect assembly state to the abstract algorithm.

**Changed-condition challenge:** An equal-key or extreme-index case that leaves nominal examples correct while violating the invariant.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T36-08 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Expose one completed ordered container through two original C interfaces: a typed value wrapper over real Record storage and a borrowed-pointer collection with explicit comparator context. Integrate one new assembly kernel behind an interface where its preconditions fit. Keep rank-then-id observations equal for valid inputs; keep copy and borrow ownership distinct. Capacity 3; duplicate ID takes precedence over full status. Borrowed rank/id values cannot mutate while stored. No callbacks allocate, retain extra pointers, block or reenter.

This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation belong to the module budget. The concrete original fixture is `fixtures/algorithms/PR-T36-08.json`; run `tools/verify_algorithms_fixtures.py` for its independent narrow oracle, then run your own component checks separately.

Declare the Profile C component boundary and Profile A hosted harness under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles); audit object and final symbols, generated code and callback effects. Implement the studied mechanism yourself. Existing base work is reused with its original acceptance evidence; this budget covers only the new work described here.

## Inputs and expected results

Insert(7, 2), (4, 1), (9, 2) yields ordered(4, 1), (7, 2), (9, 2). Insert 10 returns full unchanged; duplicate 7 returns duplicate unchanged even though full; removing 4 leaves 7, 9. Component frees zero caller objects and retains no borrowed pointers after destroy. Fixture abstract observations apply to both wrappers; internal bytes/layout need not match.

## Steps

Begin with the existing T18 owner/failure/invalidation contract and prior container source. Specify each interface, comparator context, allocation/backing policy and observable errors before writing adapters. Use an actual Record array for typed values and an actual pointer array for borrowed objects; byte arenas must copy in/out or name an implementation-specific firmware contract. Replay supplied and additional capacity/duplicate cases through both interfaces. Change storage through the existing API and use generation/status handles to verify invalidation. Audit object/final symbols and transitive callback effects.

## Failure cases

Include inconsistent comparator, context change while populated, borrowed-record lifetime expiry, mutation of its rank while stored and callback reentry. These are rejected client contracts/diagnostics; never execute dangling-pointer UB. Define failure-atomicity at the adapter boundary, including backing callback failure. Typed copies remain independent of later caller-value changes, whereas borrowed mutation must first remove the object.

## Acceptance and evidence

For .02a give new wrapper offsets/ownership links; .02b compare physical/live/traversal work for the common trace; .02c show defined storage-change invalidation. For .10a submit both interfaces and actual reused-container/assembly integration; .10b ownership/comparator/failure/invalidation contract and copy-versus-pointer example; .10c equal valid observations, separate lifetime evidence and unchanged failures. This is abstraction work over existing full mechanisms.

Keep the evidence items separate for each linked topic's three objectives. Retain the actual input/output replay, build identity, dependency/storage ledger, first counterexample and limits. Deterministic synthetic expectations do not substitute for required executable or device observations.

## Hints and recovery

Hiding a struct does not decide who owns its elements. Treat comparator context as part of the populated structure’s invariant. Duplicate detection precedes capacity rejection under this contract. If a generic adapter needs casts into a declared byte array, revisit the backing contract before optimizing.

## Transfer challenge

Design a borrowed view with no mutation operations and state which invalidation/lifetime obligations it still inherits. Do not broaden the no-call promise to an opaque client callback.

### U-T37-01-01 — Build and inspect: Architectural state and implementation models

**Budget:** 180 minutes inside PR-T37-01. **Evidence scope:** host. **Support:** bounded choice.

Compute signed overflow once from sign relations and once from independently widened range arithmetic. Exhaust every pair and minimize each discrepancy. Create a paired x86/Cortex-M architectural-state table and classify every submitted observation as model, executable ISA or physical measurement. Run one defined unsigned 32-bit target compare as optional corroboration, never an overflowing signed-C test.

Independent arithmetic and bit-slice results agree for every pair.
- Reject operands outside 0..15 or unsupported operations without changing prior output. Include carry-without-overflow, overflow-without-carry, subtraction borrow polarity, negative zero misconception and a deliberately swapped carry/V wire. ## Retained full project contract



# PR-T37-01 — Exhaustive four-bit ALU from Boolean slices

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6 h | core | C |

**Executable anchors:** algorithms. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/algorithms/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T37](#t37).

**Covered topics:** [T37.01](#t37-01), [T37.02](#t37-02).

## Working card

**Build:** Exhaustive four-bit ALU from Boolean slices. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Move from Boolean slices to committed instructions, hazards and cache traces. Compare model predictions with actual architectural evidence without equating simulated cycles to hardware time.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A flushed instruction changing architectural state, or a cache miss being charged as an assumed fixed elapsed time.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T37-01 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Build an original combinational four-bit ALU from Boolean full-adder slices, supporting addition and subtraction via complement-plus-carry 1. Output result, Z, N, carry/no-borrow and signed overflow; label x86 CF separately for subtraction. Model all state and external inputs explicitly. Use unsigned C operations or an original logic-table model inside Profile C; a hosted integer oracle may independently compute modular/range results.

This 6-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation belong to the module budget. The concrete original fixture is `fixtures/algorithms/PR-T37-01.json`; run `tools/verify_algorithms_fixtures.py` for its independent narrow oracle, then run your own component checks separately.

Declare the Profile C component boundary and Profile A hosted harness under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles); audit object and final symbols, generated code and callback effects. Implement the studied mechanism yourself. Existing base work is reused with its original acceptance evidence; this budget covers only the new work described here.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture covers 7+1, 15+1, 8−1, 0−1 and all eight full-adder rows. Exhaust all 256 operand pairs for each operation: addition has 120 carry and 64 overflow pairs; subtraction has 120 borrow and 64 overflow pairs. Four-bit results are not actual x86 register widths; the relationship is in flag semantics. Declare model outputs separately from any 32-bit ISA checks.

## Steps

Derive sum/carry equations from the truth table, compose slices and track carry into/out of the sign bit. Compute signed overflow once from sign relations and once from independently widened range arithmetic. Exhaust every pair and minimize each discrepancy. Create a paired x86/Cortex-M architectural-state table and classify every submitted observation as model, executable ISA or physical measurement. Run one defined unsigned 32-bit target compare as optional corroboration, never an overflowing signed-C test.

## Failure cases

Reject operands outside 0..15 or unsupported operations without changing prior output. Include carry-without-overflow, overflow-without-carry, subtraction borrow polarity, negative zero misconception and a deliberately swapped carry/V wire. Hardware wrap cannot be used to excuse undefined C signed overflow.

## Acceptance and evidence

For .01a define registers/memory/PC/external-input state and show model transitions; .01b separate ISA-visible flags from actual pipeline/cache/board choices; .01c provide evidence-class and assumption table. For .02a give truth-table/equation derivation; .02b exhaustive results/flags and counts; .02c explain Arm no-borrow versus x86 CF and the C semantics boundary. Independent arithmetic and bit-slice results agree for every pair.

Keep the evidence items separate for each linked topic's three objectives. Retain the actual input/output replay, build identity, dependency/storage ledger, first counterexample and limits. Deterministic synthetic expectations do not substitute for required executable or device observations.

## Hints and recovery

Use 7+1 and 15+1 to separate signed overflow from carry. On subtraction, invert the borrow sense when presenting Arm C. Range-check signed interpretations in a wider type; do not use the target’s overflowing signed expression as your oracle.

## Transfer challenge

Change to width 5 and predict range/flag boundaries before exhaustion. Keep the width-independent Boolean derivation and document the new finite state count.

# PR-T37-02 — Real instruction bytes and register/address boundaries

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T37](#t37).

**Covered topics:** [T37.03](#t37-03), [T37.04](#t37-04).

## Working card

**Build:** Real instruction bytes and register/address boundaries. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Move from Boolean slices to committed instructions, hazards and cache traces. Compare model predictions with actual architectural evidence without equating simulated cycles to hardware time.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A flushed instruction changing architectural state, or a cache miss being charged as an assumed fixed elapsed time.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T37-02 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Build a bounded offline annotation/checker for only the inspected x86 REX.W accumulator CMP, JA rel8 and Thumb CMP immediate T1/width discriminator. Reconstruct register writes, endian words and bounded addresses; assemble/disassemble the corresponding actual original snippets. Do not claim a general decoder. Keep a typed/byte-storage permission table without executing invalid C casts.

This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation belong to the module budget. The concrete original fixture is `fixtures/algorithms/PR-T37-02.json`; run `tools/verify_algorithms_fixtures.py` for its independent narrow oracle, then run your own component checks separately.

Declare the Profile C component boundary and Profile A hosted harness under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles); audit object and final symbols, generated code and callback effects. Implement the studied mechanism yourself. Existing base work is reused with its original acceptance evidence; this budget covers only the new work described here.

## Inputs and expected results

The bytes `48 3D FF FF FF FF` encode a 64-bit CMP with sign-extended −1 and length 6 bytes. The separate bytes `77 FE` at `0x1006` branch to `0x1006` when CF=0 and ZF=0. Thumb bytes `05 2A` decode CMP r2, #5, T1, 16-bit. First halfword F000 announces 32-bit Thumb. RAX byte/word writes preserve high bits; EAX 89ABCDEF clears them. Base 1000 hex+3*4+8 yields 1014 hex with end 1018 hex.

## Steps

Hand-annotate each bitfield and signed immediate before implementing the checker. Capture actual source, assembler/disassembler versions and bytes for both architectures. Compare decoded boundaries with the pinned manual and tool output, explaining any syntax differences. Reconstruct the explicit little-endian data and apply bounds before pointer formation. Contrast a real typed pool, byte-copy API and genuine allocated backing with an aligned declared-byte-array cast; separate language permission from hardware access.

## Failure cases

Reject truncated x86 immediates, unsupported opcode/prefix, invalid CMP T1 high bits, a missing second halfword after a 32-bit marker and out-of-extent address. Include wrong next-instruction branch base, wrong signed rel8 and zero-extending every partial register write. Out-of-scope encodings return unsupported, never guessed fields.

## Acceptance and evidence

For .03a submit full-register write states and Thumb contrast; .03b endian/address/extent calculations; .03c separate alignment/reachability/C17 permission evidence and rejected cast. For .04a actual bytes and fields; .04b branch target/width/PC-rule explanation; .04c vendor and disassembly cross-check with deliberate mutation rejection. Static bytes do not establish execution or board behavior.

Keep the evidence items separate for each linked topic's three objectives. Retain the actual input/output replay, build identity, dependency/storage ledger, first counterexample and limits. Deterministic synthetic expectations do not substitute for required executable or device observations.

## Hints and recovery

Thumb instructions are little-endian halfwords here, not a byte-reversed 32-bit word by default. Decode the first-halfword width before advancing. x86 relative targets add displacement to the following instruction. The source locator covers T1 only; do not expand T2 modified immediates from intuition.

## Transfer challenge

Explain what additional vendor passage inspection would be required to add one new encoding. Keep the current decoder’s unsupported response intact.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T37-03 — Clocked toy datapath and commit certificates

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T37](#t37).

**Covered topics:** [T37.01](#t37-01), [T37.05](#t37-05).

## Working card

**Build:** Clocked toy datapath and commit certificates. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Move from Boolean slices to committed instructions, hazards and cache traces. Compare model predictions with actual architectural evidence without equating simulated cycles to hardware time.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A flushed instruction changing architectural state, or a cache miss being charged as an assumed fixed elapsed time.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T37-03 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Implement an original four-register eight-bit machine with 16 byte memory cells, at most 16 program instructions and operations LI, SUB, BNZ, ST, LD, HALT. PC indexes instructions; BNZ has an absolute target index; arithmetic wraps modulo 256. One clock commits one instruction from a complete old-state snapshot. Produce control signals and next-state certificates; it is a pedagogical machine, not a Cortex-M4/x86 emulator.

This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation belong to the module budget. The concrete original fixture is `fixtures/algorithms/PR-T37-03.json`; run `tools/verify_algorithms_fixtures.py` for its independent narrow oracle, then run your own component checks separately.

Declare the Profile C component boundary and Profile A hosted harness under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles); audit object and final symbols, generated code and callback effects. Implement the studied mechanism yourself. Existing base work is reused with its original acceptance evidence; this budget covers only the new work described here.

## Inputs and expected results

The supplied original seven-instruction program loads r1=3/r2=1, loops subtract/branch until r1=0, stores 0 at memory 5, reloads r3 and halts. It commits 11 instructions, with r1 trace 3, 3, 2, 2, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 and final registers 0, 0, 1, 0. No external event arrives in this fixture; any extra event must be injected between commits under an explicit policy.

## Steps

Draw operand muxes, ALU function, register/memory write enables and PC selection. Implement next-state independently of commit, and annotate fetch/decode/operand/execute/update for each event. Preserve old state until all validation succeeds, then commit registers, memory, PC/halt together. Add a maximum-clock budget and output the last accepted state on budget exhaustion. Inspect source for accidental same-step read-after-update and test a source/destination alias case.

## Failure cases

Reject unknown operation, register>3, address>15, out-of-program target and truncated instruction before commit. Budget exhaustion is a nontermination diagnostic, not HALT. A failed decode must preserve all state. Include an intentionally sequentially updated-register mutation to show why simultaneous next-state matters.

## Acceptance and evidence

For .01a give full state/external-input relation and transitions; .01b compare its choices to ISA-visible versus physical implementation choices; .01c label certificate, ISA and physical observations. For .05a submit original model with explicit next/commit; .05b full control/event trace; .05c explain combinational outputs versus stored state and why this is not a faithful commercial datapath. Supplied certificates pass independently of your parser/interpreter.

Keep the evidence items separate for each linked topic's three objectives. Retain the actual input/output replay, build identity, dependency/storage ledger, first counterexample and limits. Deterministic synthetic expectations do not substitute for required executable or device observations.

## Hints and recovery

A computed ALU result is a wire value until commit. Branch decisions read old registers; the previous instruction’s committed result is available only on its next clock. Start with LI and one SUB before introducing the loop. If PCs disagree, check the declared absolute toy target before applying real-ISA PC rules.

## Transfer challenge

Add one external-input event between two commits and state its precedence. Avoid silently adding asynchronous changes inside a transition.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T37-04 — Forwarding, stalls and branch squash schedule

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T37](#t37).

**Covered topics:** [T37.06](#t37-06).

## Working card

**Build:** Forwarding, stalls and branch squash schedule. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Move from Boolean slices to committed instructions, hazards and cache traces. Compare model predictions with actual architectural evidence without equating simulated cycles to hardware time.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A flushed instruction changing architectural state, or a cache miss being charged as an assumed fixed elapsed time.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T37-04 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Build a small original stage-schedule model/checker for declared IF/ID/EX/MEM/WB, single issue, in order. ALU result is available after EX; load after MEM; forwarded values enter next-cycle EX; register-file writes occur before reads in a cycle. A taken branch resolves at EX end, squashes younger IF/ID and refetches target next cycle. Do not label this a physical Cortex-M4/x86 pipeline.

This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation belong to the module budget. The concrete original fixture is `fixtures/algorithms/PR-T37-04.json`; run `tools/verify_algorithms_fixtures.py` for its independent narrow oracle, then run your own component checks separately.

Declare the Profile C component boundary and Profile A hosted harness under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles); audit object and final symbols, generated code and callback effects. Implement the studied mechanism yourself. Existing base work is reused with its original acceptance evidence; this budget covers only the new work described here.

## Inputs and expected results

Fixture I1/I2 dependent ALU, I3 load, I4 load consumer, I5 taken branch, I6 wrong-path work, I7 target retires I1, I2, I3, I4, I5, I7 by cycle 13. I3 MEM 6 requires I4 EX 7. Two younger fetch instances are squashed at 8; target refetch is 9. First four instructions retire by 9 with forwarding/one bubble, versus 14 without forwarding under write-first/read-second register-file order.

## Steps

Draw the stage-by-cycle table and attach a producer availability to every read. Build a bounded scheduler or independent certificate checker, then run the same original stream with/without forwarding. Keep blocked IF/ID slots distinct from empty EX bubbles. On the branch, show which fetched instances are discarded and which instruction identity is later refetched. Count retired instructions separately from fetched/issued instances. Include a parallel explanation of RAW dependence, implementation hazard and C data race.

## Failure cases

Reject a consumer EX before its value is available, duplicate occupancy of a single stage/cycle, advancing a blocked younger instruction, retired squashed work and unsupported branch rules. Include same-cycle MEM 6→EX 6 mutation. Do not count a stalled instruction twice or add a bubble penalty already visible in the schedule.

## Acceptance and evidence

For .06a submit complete RAW/load-use stage table; .06b forwarding/no-forwarding and branch effects with cycle/retirement counts; .06c distinguish dependence/hazard/race with examples and state physical extrapolation limits. The independent oracle validates declared certificates, not an exported commercial CPU simulator. Functional final register equivalence alone does not validate cycle accounting.

Keep the evidence items separate for each linked topic's three objectives. Retain the actual input/output replay, build identity, dependency/storage ledger, first counterexample and limits. Deterministic synthetic expectations do not substitute for required executable or device observations.

## Hints and recovery

Write the producer’s availability edge first. With no forwarding, a following dependent EX waits until the cycle after producer WB; with load forwarding it still waits after MEM. Label I7’s wrong fetch separately from its eventual correct fetch to avoid accidental double retirement.

## Transfer challenge

Move branch resolution to ID under a separately specified model and predict the flush count. State any new operand-availability rule before rerunning.

### U-T37-05-01 — Build and inspect: Memory hierarchy, locality and cache costs

**Budget:** 160 minutes inside PR-T37-05. **Evidence scope:** host. **Support:** bounded choice.

**Requires:** [u-t01-03-03](#u-t01-03-03).

**Imports:** No implicit code dependency.

**New work:**

1. Derive offset/index/tag partitions before coding. Emit cache and shadow state after every reference and explain each category using seen blocks and shadow membership. Design two small original layouts/access orders and compare their normalized address traces under exactly the same geometry. Compute dimensional equations independently from trace hit counting. If optionally measuring host behavior, identify CPU/tool/counters and put observations in a separate column; do not tune fixture geometry to claim the host matches it.
2. Before looking at previous source, predict one boundary transition for Memory hierarchy, locality and cache costs.
3. Produce the smallest independently inspectable implementation or trace for the operation above.

**Check and stop:**

- For .07a submit fields and state/hit trace; .07b AMAT/stall equations and two-layout comparison with units; .07c compulsory/conflict/capacity reasoning and model-versus-measurement boundary. Shadow replacement and capacity are recorded. Correct miss totals with incorrect tags/categories fail acceptance.
- Reject negative/invalid addresses or zero/non-power-of-two geometry in the general wrapper. Include cold start, repeated hits, two conflicting blocks, more than four distinct blocks and an invalid uninitialized-tag mutation. Miss penalty is additional to hit cost under this contract; a total-miss-latency input must be converted explicitly.

**Recall before reopening source:** [recall-t37-07](#recall-t37-07).

This increment uses the observed trace or artifact checks above. Later family gates stay deferred; an empty test selection does not constitute a pass.

**Bounded reading:**

- [R-ENH-PLANTZ-ORGANIZATION-ARM](#r-enh-plantz-organization-arm): Chapter 6 Combinational Logic Circuits — Half Adder, Full Adder, Full Adder from Two Half Adders, Ripple-Carry Addition and Subtraction Circuits, printed 108–114. Derive a four-bit adder/subtractor from Boolean slices; the book uses AArch64, not Cortex-M Thumb.
- [R-ENH-PLANTZ-ORGANIZATION-ARM](#r-enh-plantz-organization-arm): Chapter 7 Sequential Logic Circuits — Flip-Flops, Clocks, D Flip-Flop, printed 136–139. Separate combinational next-state signals from flip-flop state committed at a clock.
- [R-ENH-PLANTZ-ORGANIZATION-ARM](#r-enh-plantz-organization-arm): Chapter 9 Central Processing Unit — Instruction Execution Cycle, printed 170–172. Use fetch/decode/execute as a conceptual model, without importing the book’s implementation as a real Cortex-M datapath.
- [R-ENH-HENNESSY-PATTERSON-6](#r-enh-hennessy-patterson-6): 1.9 Quantitative Principles of Computer Design — Amdahl and The Processor Performance Equation, printed pp.48–54. Check units in CPU-time and Amdahl equations; independently recompute rather than copying inconsistent displayed example numbers.
- [R-ENH-HENNESSY-PATTERSON-6](#r-enh-hennessy-patterson-6): B.2 Cache Performance — AMAT and in-order stall model, printed B-15–B-18. Distinguish AMAT from an explicitly in-order memory-stall estimate.
- [R-ENH-HENNESSY-PATTERSON-6](#r-enh-hennessy-patterson-6): C.2 The Major Hurdle of Pipelining—Pipeline Hazards — hazard classes, RAW and forwarding, printed C-10–C-15. Construct RAW, forwarding and load-use schedules under a declared pipeline model.
- [R-ENH-HENNESSY-PATTERSON-6](#r-enh-hennessy-patterson-6): B.1 Introduction — Q1 block placement, Q2 block identification, Q3 replacement, printedB-7–B-9. Derive block placement, tag identity and replacement rules before simulating a cache.
- [R-ENH-HENNESSY-PATTERSON-6](#r-enh-hennessy-patterson-6): B.3 Six Basic Cache Optimizations — threeC miss categories, printedB-23. Classify misses with compulsory history and a same-capacity fully associative shadow.
- [R-ENH-INTEL-SDM1-093](#r-enh-intel-sdm1-093): 3.4.1.1 General-Purpose Registers in 64-Bit Mode. Explain partial-register preservation versus 32-bit zero extension.
- [R-ENH-INTEL-SDM1-093](#r-enh-intel-sdm1-093): 3.4.3.1 Status Flags. Interpret carry/borrow and signed-overflow flags against the finite arithmetic model.
- [R-ENH-INTEL-SDM1-093](#r-enh-intel-sdm1-093): 3.7.5.1 Specifying an Offset in 64-Bit Mode. Calculate a bounded base/index/scale/displacement address with the selected 64-bit-mode constraints.
- [R-ENH-INTEL-SDM2A-093](#r-enh-intel-sdm2a-093): CMP—Compare Two Operands, printed 3-161–3-162. Decode only the inspected accumulator/immediate CMP forms and their sign extension.
- [R-ENH-INTEL-SDM2A-093](#r-enh-intel-sdm2a-093): Jcc—Jump if Condition Is Met — rel8 predicates and Description, printed 3-499 and 3-502. Compute JA rel8 from the next instruction and the declared unsigned flags.
- [R-ENH-ARMV7M-DDI0403EE](#r-enh-armv7m-ddi0403ee): A5.1 Thumb instruction set encoding — width discriminator and PC reads. Read actual Thumb halfword boundaries and architectural PC rules.
- [R-ENH-ARMV7M-DDI0403EE](#r-enh-armv7m-ddi0403ee): A7.7.27 CMP (immediate) — EncodingT1 and Operation. Decode the visually inspected CMP immediate T1 bitfield only; modified immediates are outside scope.
- [R-ARM-DUI0553B](#r-arm-dui0553b): 3.5.1 ADD, ADC, SUB, SBC, and RSB. Map four-bit model conclusions to documented Arm flag behavior, without conflating hardware wrap with C semantics.
- [R-ARM-DUI0553B](#r-arm-dui0553b): 3.5.5 CMP and CMN. Check compare/no-borrow behavior against the toy arithmetic cases.
- [R-ARM-DUI0553B](#r-arm-dui0553b): 2.3.7 Exception entry and return. Reuse basic exception entry/return evidence and label alignment/FP variants separately.
- [R-ARM-DUI0553B](#r-arm-dui0553b): 2.3.5 Exception priorities. Distinguish priority numbering from a call/return sequence and actual implemented priority bits.
- [R-ST-RM0090-21](#r-st-rm0090-21): 2.1 System architecture — STM32F405/407/415/417 and STM32F42/43 distinctions. Separate F405/407/415/417 from F42/43 memory masters and CCM reachability.
- [R-ST-RM0090-21](#r-st-rm0090-21): 2.1.4 DMA memory bus. Trace DMA memory-master paths to ordinary SRAM rather than guessing from CPU accessibility.
- [R-ST-RM0090-21](#r-st-rm0090-21): 2.3.1 Embedded SRAM. Reuse the accepted embedded-SRAM placement scope for the chosen bank ledger.
- [R-ST-RM0090-21](#r-st-rm0090-21): 2.1.10 BusMatrix. Use round-robin arbitration as documented topology evidence, not a numerical WCET guarantee.
- [R-ST-RM0090-21](#r-st-rm0090-21): 2.1.11 AHB/APB bridges (APB). Explain narrow-write duplication and why register-specific access rules still matter.
- [R-ST-RM0090-21](#r-st-rm0090-21): 2.2 Memory organization. Reconstruct little-endian memory and separate reserved/device regions.
- [R-ENH-AAPCS32-2025Q1](#r-enh-aapcs32-2025q1): The Base Procedure Call Standard — Machine Registers / Core registers. Contrast software-preserved call registers with automatically stacked exception registers.
- [R-ENH-AAPCS32-2025Q1](#r-enh-aapcs32-2025q1): Processes, Memory and the Stack — Stack constraints at a public interface. Check public-call alignment without applying it as a universal exception-frame layout.
- [R-SYS-AMD64-ABI-0-99-6](#r-sys-amd64-abi-0-99-6): 3.2.1 Registers and the Stack Frame. Use one x86 call boundary as a contrast to the synthetic Cortex-M frame.

**Remaining obligations:** mechanism explanation; independent changed-condition evidence; delayed transfer.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T37-05 — Cache tags, miss mechanisms and dimensional costs

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Executable anchors:** algorithms. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/algorithms/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T37](#t37).

**Covered topics:** [T37.07](#t37-07).

## Working card

**Build:** Cache tags, miss mechanisms and dimensional costs. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Move from Boolean slices to committed instructions, hazards and cache traces. Compare model predictions with actual architectural evidence without equating simulated cycles to hardware time.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A flushed instruction changing architectural state, or a cache miss being charged as an assumed fixed elapsed time.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T37-05 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Implement an original bounded trace model for a four-line direct-mapped cache with 16 byte blocks and byte addresses. Add an independent same-capacity fully associative LRU shadow for three-C classification. Keep valid bits/tag identity explicit; no actual memory loads are needed to model a reference. Compute AMAT and a separate declared in-order stall estimate with consistent units.

This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation belong to the module budget. The concrete original fixture is `fixtures/algorithms/PR-T37-05.json`; run `tools/verify_algorithms_fixtures.py` for its independent narrow oracle, then run your own component checks separately.

Declare the Profile C component boundary and Profile A hosted harness under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles); audit object and final symbols, generated code and callback effects. Implement the studied mechanism yourself. Existing base work is reused with its original acceptance evidence; this budget covers only the new work described here.

## Inputs and expected results

Trace 0, 16, 0, 64, 0, 16, 80, 16, 0 yields six misses: four compulsory, two conflict, zero capacity. Trace 0, 16, 32, 48, 64, 0 ends with a capacity miss. Hit 1 ns/additional penalty 30 ns gives AMAT 21 ns for the first trace. Declared 100 instructions, CPI 1.2, 24 references, rate 0.25, penalty 20 cycles gives 240 cycles total and 120 ns at 2 GHz.

## Steps

Derive offset/index/tag partitions before coding. Emit cache and shadow state after every reference and explain each category using seen blocks and shadow membership. Design two small original layouts/access orders and compare their normalized address traces under exactly the same geometry. Compute dimensional equations independently from trace hit counting. If optionally measuring host behavior, identify CPU/tool/counters and put observations in a separate column; do not tune fixture geometry to claim the host matches it.

## Failure cases

Reject negative/invalid addresses or zero/non-power-of-two geometry in the general wrapper. Include cold start, repeated hits, two conflicting blocks, more than four distinct blocks and an invalid uninitialized-tag mutation. Miss penalty is additional to hit cost under this contract; a total-miss-latency input must be converted explicitly.

## Acceptance and evidence

For .07a submit fields and state/hit trace; .07b AMAT/stall equations and two-layout comparison with units; .07c compulsory/conflict/capacity reasoning and model-versus-measurement boundary. Shadow replacement and capacity are recorded. Correct miss totals with incorrect tags/categories fail acceptance.

Keep the evidence items separate for each linked topic's three objectives. Retain the actual input/output replay, build identity, dependency/storage ledger, first counterexample and limits. Deterministic synthetic expectations do not substitute for required executable or device observations.

## Hints and recovery

A repeated block can miss by conflict while the equal-capacity shadow still holds it. The three-C category is evaluated against shadow state before servicing that reference. Normalize addresses to declared blocks; do not confuse array element count with byte offset. Check cycles/seconds conversion before interpreting a large time.

## Transfer challenge

Change associativity to two-way with an explicit replacement rule. Predict which conflict cases disappear and which capacity limitation remains.

## Working card

**Build:** MCU master paths and DMA placement ledger. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Move from Boolean slices to committed instructions, hazards and cache traces. Compare model predictions with actual architectural evidence without equating simulated cycles to hardware time.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A flushed instruction changing architectural state, or a cache miss being charged as an assumed fixed elapsed time.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T37-06 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Reuse the completed T27 target/map and T29 DMA ownership artifacts. Produce an original master/slave reachability graph, annotated linker/map placement and a checked placement/ownership ledger for the exact selected F42/43-class part. No new DMA peripheral driver is required. Fixture base addresses are declared synthetic placement data; verify any actual device addresses against the prior exact target evidence before using hardware.

This 6-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation belong to the module budget. The concrete original fixture is `fixtures/algorithms/PR-T37-06.json`; run `tools/verify_algorithms_fixtures.py` for its independent narrow oracle, then run your own component checks separately.

Implement the studied mechanism yourself. Existing base work is reused with its original acceptance evidence; this budget covers only the new work described here.

## Inputs and expected results

The selected family has 112/16/64 KiB ordinary SRAM and 64 KiB CPU-only CCM. Fixture candidates respectively fail DMA reachability, cross a declared bank, succeed in SRAM3 and overrun its end. Ordinary SRAM totals 192 KiB. Foreground writes while DMA owns the buffer are rejected unchanged. Byte 12 hex and halfword 1234 hex expand to bridge vectors 12121212 hex and 12341234 hex; register-specific access effect remains separately documented.

## Steps

Identify exact part/core/board/document revision, contrasting the earlier F405/407 family without inventing SRAM3 there. Trace CPU and DMA memory-master paths, add linker output section and map/symbol evidence for one reused buffer, then prove allocation extent/alignment/lifetime. Replay give/completion/CPU-access events using the prior ownership protocol. Draw a toy round-robin grant sequence for CPU, DMA2, DMA1 and label its fairness assumptions separately from real burst/clock timing. Annotate APB bridge expansion and the selected peripheral’s access-width rule from existing target work.

## Failure cases

Reject unknown family/revision, CPU-only CCM DMA placement, bank-crossing declared allocation, arithmetic extent overflow and access during DMA ownership. A CPU-accessible or aligned byte array is not thereby a live typed DMA object. Unsupported clocks/peripheral rules are evidence gaps; never test an unverified map by issuing arbitrary MMIO.

## Acceptance and evidence

For .03a retain the prior register-width contrast with this address ledger; .03b calculate endpoints/endian/access bounds; .03c separate C object permission, alignment and reachability. For .08a submit documented master/target graph; .08b actual linker/map placement plus owner/completion protocol; .08c toy arbitration/bridge trace and a list of throughput/electrical claims requiring physical measurement. No emulator-only DMA/latency claim is accepted.

Keep the evidence items separate for each linked topic's three objectives. Retain the actual input/output replay, build identity, dependency/storage ledger, first counterexample and limits. Deterministic synthetic expectations do not substitute for required executable or device observations.

## Hints and recovery

CCM’s address looks like memory but its master connectivity differs. Check the whole buffer, not only its start. Bus reachability does not settle ownership/completion ordering. APB duplicated write data is not permission to use any narrow access on any register.

## Transfer challenge

Move only a CPU-local temporary into CCM and predict linker/map and master-path changes. Keep the DMA buffer in independently verified ordinary SRAM.
