### U-T37-07-01 — Build and inspect: Reset, exceptions and architectural boundaries

**Budget:** 160 minutes inside PR-T37-07. **Evidence scope:** host. **Support:** bounded choice.

**Requires:** [u-t01-03-03](#u-t01-03-03).

**Imports:** No implicit code dependency.

**New work:**

1. Derive vector indices and eight word addresses by hand, then compare with the existing decoder output. Contrast BL/LR and AAPCS-preserved registers against automatically stacked r0–r3, r12, LR, PC, xPSR. Annotate restored state and software prologue obligations; include one original nested-priority trace using the prior target’s verified bits/grouping. Capture a declared emulator or physical-target frame observation and keep it separate from the synthetic ledger. Record boot remapping, stack, FP and padding assumptions explicitly.
2. Before looking at previous source, predict one boundary transition for Reset, exceptions and architectural boundaries.
3. Produce the smallest independently inspectable implementation or trace for the operation above.

**Check and stop:**

- For .09a submit reset/basic-entry/return transitions; .09b call ABI versus exception stacking/priority table; .09c original saved trace checks and emulator/FP/boot limitations. Independent fixture offsets match, and actual reused-tool evidence identifies exact source/binary/environment. A synthetic vector scenario does not verify board boot pins or aliases.
- Reject short frames, unsupported EXC_RETURN, missing Thumb state, guessed FP/padding layout and unknown priority/grouping. Handle malformed reset vector/extent as diagnostic errors, not execution requests. A basic decoder must not infer the complete saved state from eight words or overwrite its previous accepted output on error.

**Recall before reopening source:** [recall-t37-09](#recall-t37-09).

This increment uses the observed trace or artifact checks above. Later family gates stay deferred; an empty test selection does not constitute a pass.

**Bounded reading:**

- [R-ENH-PLANTZ-ORGANIZATION-ARM](#r-enh-plantz-organization-arm): Chapter 6 Combinational Logic Circuits — Half Adder, Full Adder, Full Adder from Two Half Adders, Ripple-Carry Addition and Subtraction Circuits, printed 108–114. Derive a four-bit adder/subtractor from Boolean slices; the book uses AArch64, not Cortex-M Thumb.
- [R-ENH-PLANTZ-ORGANIZATION-ARM](#r-enh-plantz-organization-arm): Chapter 7 Sequential Logic Circuits — Flip-Flops, Clocks, D Flip-Flop, printed 136–139. Separate combinational next-state signals from flip-flop state committed at a clock.
- [R-ENH-PLANTZ-ORGANIZATION-ARM](#r-enh-plantz-organization-arm): Chapter 9 Central Processing Unit — Instruction Execution Cycle, printed 170–172. Use fetch/decode/execute as a conceptual model, without importing the book’s implementation as a real Cortex-M datapath.
- [R-ENH-HENNESSY-PATTERSON-6](#r-enh-hennessy-patterson-6): 1.9 Quantitative Principles of Computer Design — Amdahl and The Processor Performance Equation, printed pp.48–54. Check units in CPU-time and Amdahl equations; independently recompute rather than copying inconsistent displayed example numbers.
- [R-ENH-HENNESSY-PATTERSON-6](#r-enh-hennessy-patterson-6): B.2 Cache Performance — AMAT and in-order stall model, printed B-15–B-18. Distinguish AMAT from an explicitly in-order memory-stall estimate.
- [R-ENH-HENNESSY-PATTERSON-6](#r-enh-hennessy-patterson-6): C.2 The Major Hurdle of Pipelining—Pipeline Hazards — hazard classes, RAW and forwarding, printed C-10–C-15. Construct RAW, forwarding and load-use schedules under a declared pipeline model.
- [R-ENH-HENNESSY-PATTERSON-6](#r-enh-hennessy-patterson-6): B.1 Introduction — Q1 block placement, Q2 block identification, Q3 replacement, printedB-7–B-9. Derive block placement, tag identity and replacement rules before simulating a cache.
- [R-ENH-HENNESSY-PATTERSON-6](#r-enh-hennessy-patterson-6): B.3 Six Basic Cache Optimizations — threeC miss categories, printedB-23. Classify misses with compulsory history and a same-capacity fully associative shadow.
- [R-ENH-INTEL-SDM1-093](#r-enh-intel-sdm1-093): 3.4.1.1 General-Purpose Registers in 64-Bit Mode. Explain partial-register preservation versus 32-bit zero extension.
- [R-ENH-INTEL-SDM1-093](#r-enh-intel-sdm1-093): 3.4.3.1 Status Flags. Interpret carry/borrow and signed-overflow flags against the finite arithmetic model.
- [R-ENH-INTEL-SDM1-093](#r-enh-intel-sdm1-093): 3.7.5.1 Specifying an Offset in 64-Bit Mode. Calculate a bounded base/index/scale/displacement address with the selected 64-bit-mode constraints.
- [R-ENH-INTEL-SDM2A-093](#r-enh-intel-sdm2a-093): CMP—Compare Two Operands, printed 3-161–3-162. Decode only the inspected accumulator/immediate CMP forms and their sign extension.
- [R-ENH-INTEL-SDM2A-093](#r-enh-intel-sdm2a-093): Jcc—Jump if Condition Is Met — rel8 predicates and Description, printed 3-499 and 3-502. Compute JA rel8 from the next instruction and the declared unsigned flags.
- [R-ENH-ARMV7M-DDI0403EE](#r-enh-armv7m-ddi0403ee): A5.1 Thumb instruction set encoding — width discriminator and PC reads. Read actual Thumb halfword boundaries and architectural PC rules.
- [R-ENH-ARMV7M-DDI0403EE](#r-enh-armv7m-ddi0403ee): A7.7.27 CMP (immediate) — EncodingT1 and Operation. Decode the visually inspected CMP immediate T1 bitfield only; modified immediates are outside scope.
- [R-ARM-DUI0553B](#r-arm-dui0553b): 3.5.1 ADD, ADC, SUB, SBC, and RSB. Map four-bit model conclusions to documented Arm flag behavior, without conflating hardware wrap with C semantics.
- [R-ARM-DUI0553B](#r-arm-dui0553b): 3.5.5 CMP and CMN. Check compare/no-borrow behavior against the toy arithmetic cases.
- [R-ARM-DUI0553B](#r-arm-dui0553b): 2.3.7 Exception entry and return. Reuse basic exception entry/return evidence and label alignment/FP variants separately.
- [R-ARM-DUI0553B](#r-arm-dui0553b): 2.3.5 Exception priorities. Distinguish priority numbering from a call/return sequence and actual implemented priority bits.
- [R-ST-RM0090-21](#r-st-rm0090-21): 2.1 System architecture — STM32F405/407/415/417 and STM32F42/43 distinctions. Separate F405/407/415/417 from F42/43 memory masters and CCM reachability.
- [R-ST-RM0090-21](#r-st-rm0090-21): 2.1.4 DMA memory bus. Trace DMA memory-master paths to ordinary SRAM rather than guessing from CPU accessibility.
- [R-ST-RM0090-21](#r-st-rm0090-21): 2.3.1 Embedded SRAM. Reuse the accepted embedded-SRAM placement scope for the chosen bank ledger.
- [R-ST-RM0090-21](#r-st-rm0090-21): 2.1.10 BusMatrix. Use round-robin arbitration as documented topology evidence, not a numerical WCET guarantee.
- [R-ST-RM0090-21](#r-st-rm0090-21): 2.1.11 AHB/APB bridges (APB). Explain narrow-write duplication and why register-specific access rules still matter.
- [R-ST-RM0090-21](#r-st-rm0090-21): 2.2 Memory organization. Reconstruct little-endian memory and separate reserved/device regions.
- [R-ENH-AAPCS32-2025Q1](#r-enh-aapcs32-2025q1): The Base Procedure Call Standard — Machine Registers / Core registers. Contrast software-preserved call registers with automatically stacked exception registers.
- [R-ENH-AAPCS32-2025Q1](#r-enh-aapcs32-2025q1): Processes, Memory and the Stack — Stack constraints at a public interface. Check public-call alignment without applying it as a universal exception-frame layout.
- [R-SYS-AMD64-ABI-0-99-6](#r-sys-amd64-abi-0-99-6): 3.2.1 Registers and the Stack Frame. Use one x86 call boundary as a contrast to the synthetic Cortex-M frame.

**Remaining obligations:** mechanism explanation; independent changed-condition evidence; delayed transfer.

**Objective facets:** [T37.09.a](#t37-09-a), [T37.09.b](#t37-09-b), [T37.09.c](#t37-09-c).

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T37-07 — Call ABI versus reset and exception frame

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Executable anchors:** algorithms. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/algorithms/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T37](#t37).

**Covered topics:** [T37.09](#t37-09).

## Working card

**Build:** Call ABI versus reset and exception frame. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Move from Boolean slices to committed instructions, hazards and cache traces. Compare model predictions with actual architectural evidence without equating simulated cycles to hardware time.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A flushed instruction changing architectural state, or a cache miss being charged as an assumed fixed elapsed time.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T37-07 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Extend the completed T27 startup and T29 frame tools with a call-versus-exception ownership table and an original bounded reset/basic-frame/return trace. Reuse the actual startup/handler implementation; do not rebuild a vector table or exception decoder. ## Inputs and expected results

Declared Flash-vector reset uses MSP 20002000 hex and vector 08000101 hex, entering 08000100 hex. IRQ 5 is exception 21, vector address 08000054 hex. PSP 20001000 hex gives basic frame base 20000FE0 hex; EXC_RETURN FFFFFFFD selects Thread/PSP basic return. Words restore PC 08000200 hex and LR 08000111 hex; lower number 2 has higher urgency than 7 under the scoped priority convention.

## Steps

Derive vector indices and eight word addresses by hand, then compare with the existing decoder output. Contrast BL/LR and AAPCS-preserved registers against automatically stacked r0–r3, r12, LR, PC, xPSR. Annotate restored state and software prologue obligations; include one original nested-priority trace using the prior target’s verified bits/grouping. Capture a declared emulator or physical-target frame observation and keep it separate from the synthetic ledger. Record boot remapping, stack, FP and padding assumptions explicitly.

## Failure cases

Reject short frames, unsupported EXC_RETURN, missing Thumb state, guessed FP/padding layout and unknown priority/grouping. Handle malformed reset vector/extent as diagnostic errors, not execution requests. A basic decoder must not infer the complete saved state from eight words or overwrite its previous accepted output on error.

## Acceptance and evidence

For .09a submit reset/basic-entry/return transitions; .09b call ABI versus exception stacking/priority table; .09c original saved trace checks and emulator/FP/boot limitations. Independent fixture offsets match, and actual reused-tool evidence identifies exact source/binary/environment. A synthetic vector scenario does not verify board boot pins or aliases.

Keep the evidence items separate for each linked topic's three objectives. Retain the actual input/output replay, build identity, dependency/storage ledger, first counterexample and limits. Deterministic synthetic expectations do not substitute for required executable or device observations.

## Hints and recovery

Decode the return variant before selecting the stack pointer and offsets. LR inside the saved frame is different from the handler’s live EXC_RETURN. The hardware basic frame omits r4–r11; software compiler/handler code can preserve them separately. First reconcile those two LRs on disagreement.

## Transfer challenge

Describe the additional inspected specification and capacity checks needed for an FP-extended frame without adding an unverified decoder path.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T38-01 — UART architecture, frame and baud laboratory

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T38](#t38).

**Covered topics:** [T38.01](#t38-01), [T38.02](#t38-02).

## Working card

**Build:** UART architecture, frame and baud laboratory. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Derive frames and transaction states, then measure the relevant electrical behavior. Keep UART/USART, SPI/I2C controllers and RS/CAN transceivers as distinct mechanisms.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A transmitter declaring completion while the final stop bit or bus-turnaround interval is still active.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T38-01 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Reuse the T27 reset/linker and T28 UART adapter. Write an allocation-free character/baud analyzer and a bounded 8N1 target exchange, maximum 16 bytes per request and 32 bytes of RX caller storage. Add 7E1/8E1 to the software frame model; do not silently reuse an 8-bit-with-parity configuration. Results separate byte, parity/framing error, overrun, busy and deadline. Draw the CPU/MMIO/peripheral/transceiver/wire path and document which tested component owns each responsibility.

This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile E under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

PR-T38-01 supplies 42 MHz/115200 baud under both oversampling choices, a 3 Mbaud validity contrast,0xA5 and 0x35 frame patterns, parity/stop corruption and TXE-versus-TC completion observations. The exact rational baud/error fields are the arithmetic oracle; approximate decimal printing is supplementary. The 8N1 0xA5 frame has 10 bits. BRR is 0x16D under OVER8=0 and 0x2D5 under OVER8=1 for the declared clock.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T38-01.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Derive all frame positions and both BRR encodings before programming. Validate divisor and word-length ranges.

2. Implement an explicit byte/error result and bounded wait policy; preserve SR-before-DR status evidence for the chosen F439 receive errors.

3. Replay software fixtures and a synthetic RX-overrun prefix. Keep the older held RDR value distinct from lost later input.

4. Connect only the exact documented board UART routing/logic peer, transmit 16 or fewer known bytes and measure bit/stop timing. Use the existing startup and pin ledger.

5. Audit the profile E image and supply the three architecture receipts: host arithmetic, target operation and physical trace.

## Failure cases

Reject divisor range, unsupported data/parity settings and capacity overflow without publishing partial successful records. A TXE-only release is premature. Record FE/ORE as errors; a baud timeout must not fabricate a received zero byte. A wrong peripheral-clock assumption is a calculation failure even when the peer happens to tolerate it.

## Acceptance and evidence

All fixture bits/encodings/rational values match. Show one actual clock derivation and measured baud discrepancy, final TC after the last stop interval, and exact receive-error handling. Provide separate per-objective evidence for both linked topics. Physical timing is closed only by the captured board/peer route; the software receipt alone is a partial hardware route.

Retain one explicit evidence item for each original objective under every linked topic: explanation, implemented/derived property, observed result and limitation. Submit interface/source, replay, dependency/resource ledger and first-failure analysis. Synthetic, target and physical receipts remain separately identified; equipment acquisition or missing adapter/peer setup is an entry prerequisite, not hidden work inside the hour budget.

## Hints and recovery

Use unsigned shifts with explicit widths. Compute nearest effective divisor first, then encode its mantissa/fraction for the chosen oversampling. Reduce a parity disagreement to one character; reduce a timeout to clock, pin, status sequence and deadline evidence.

If a check disagrees, minimize the first failing prefix and compare units, capture point, state and ownership. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted remediation; repair only the failed objective group.

## Transfer challenge

Change the selected peripheral clock while preserving the character contract; recompute BRR and invalidate stale configuration before the next transfer.

# PR-T38-02 — Synchronous USART clock and sampling laboratory

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T38](#t38).

**Covered topics:** [T38.03](#t38-03).

## Working card

**Build:** Synchronous USART clock and sampling laboratory. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Derive frames and transaction states, then measure the relevant electrical behavior. Keep UART/USART, SPI/I2C controllers and RS/CAN transceivers as distinct mechanisms.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A transmitter declaring completion while the final stop bit or bus-turnaround interval is still active.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T38-02 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Implement the eight-data-bit synchronous-master trace model and one bounded matched CK/TX/RX exchange, at most 8 characters, LBCL enabled for the physical baseline. Reuse the asynchronous USART adapter, but add explicit clock/data configuration and TE/RE-off reconfiguration. Reception must include a declared clock-generating transmit value; no autonomous synchronous receive API is permitted.

This 6-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile E under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture supplies 0x96 under all four CPOL/CPHA combinations, LBCL-on/off contrasts, a clockless receive request and an attempted change with TE active. Data bits are LSB-first. With LBCL on there are 16 data-clock edges and no start/stop clock edges; CPHA selects odd/even capture edges. The fixture does not assert that an LBCL-off trace is compatible with an arbitrary peer.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T38-02.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Draw idle, start, eight data and stop intervals, overlay CK and number edges.

2. Implement the predictor and a configuration validator rejecting changes while TE or RE is enabled.

3. Extend the bounded adapter with transmit-generated clocks and a maximum transfer count/deadline.

4. Use a matched documented peer or declared logic-level receive loopback; capture CK/TX/RX for the LBCL-on baseline. Compare asynchronous and synchronous timing.

5. Replay clockless and live-change failures synthetically; retain peer setup/hold limitations.

## Failure cases

No TX means no receive clock. Mismatched CPHA/CPOL, incompatible last-clock policy and live configuration changes are explicit errors or unclosed peer compatibility. Do not assume USART character/start/stop conventions satisfy a generic SPI target.

## Acceptance and evidence

Correct edge numbers, idle levels, bit order and last-clock policy; no falsely completed clockless receive; one matched bounded physical transfer with source-verified pins. Demonstrate all configuration preconditions and profile E image dependencies.

Retain one explicit evidence item for each original objective under every linked topic: explanation, implemented/derived property, observed result and limitation. Submit interface/source, replay, dependency/resource ledger and first-failure analysis. Synthetic, target and physical receipts remain separately identified; equipment acquisition or missing adapter/peer setup is an entry prerequisite, not hidden work inside the hour budget.

## Hints and recovery

Separate bit order from capture edge and physical clock direction. Start with LBCL-on and one matched mode. A peer disagreement should be reduced to its first capture edge.

If a check disagrees, minimize the first failing prefix and compare units, capture point, state and ownership. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted remediation; repair only the failed objective group.

## Transfer challenge

Describe which additional target framing rules would be required before reusing this clocked character engine for a selected external synchronous device.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T38-03 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Write a caller-storage calculator and at-most 3-controller wired-AND trace model. Inputs are positive bounded integer mV/mA/ns/pF and up to 32 data bits. Use checked 64-bit intermediates or a proved bounded equivalent, integer ceil/floor resistor limits and explicit infeasible status. The physical baseline is a short Standard/Fast-mode bus with known target voltage/sink limits and measured capacitance assumptions; unsupported high-speed modes are excluded.

This 6-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile C under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture uses 3.3 V, VOL0.4 V,3 mA,300 ns,100 pF with 2.2 kΩ/4.7 kΩ choices, then 400 pF. Expected interval is 967..3540 Ω for 100 pF and infeasible for 400 pF. Two streams 101100/101010 lose participation at their first differing dominant bit; identical streams both survive. Common low/high holds are max(4,7)=7 and min(6,3)=3 ticks.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T38-03.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Derive Rp bounds with units and rounding direction; state uncertainty and check products/divisors.

2. Implement the calculator, rejecting empty intervals rather than picking an arbitrary resistor.

3. Implement release-high/pull-low participants, loss logging and wired-AND clock periods. Do not force a losing controller STOP.

4. Measure SDA/SCL low level and rise time on the declared prepared setup, compare scope and decoder views, and label any unknown capacitance estimate.

5. Audit the profile C component object and retain target adaptation separately under E.

## Failure cases

Zero or negative denominators, out-of-envelope inputs, arithmetic overflow, empty resistor interval and non-binary traces fail explicitly. A low pulse on SDA while SCL high is not ordinary data. A push-pull SCL design is rejected unless the inspected single-controller/no-stretch exception is actually declared.

## Acceptance and evidence

All resistor/trace results match the independent exact rational oracle. Show simultaneous identical-prefix arbitration, measured analog levels/rise time and a justified chosen resistor. Logic decoding alone leaves the electrical receipt open.

Retain one explicit evidence item for each original objective under every linked topic: explanation, implemented/derived property, observed result and limitation. Submit interface/source, replay, dependency/resource ledger and first-failure analysis. Synthetic, target and physical receipts remain separately identified; equipment acquisition or missing adapter/peer setup is an entry prerequisite, not hidden work inside the hour budget.

## Hints and recovery

Keep a unit table:0.8473×Ω×pF/1000 gives ns. Never round the minimum downward or maximum upward. Inspect the first lost participant instead of comparing only decoded addresses.

If a check disagrees, minimize the first failing prefix and compare units, capture point, state and ownership. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted remediation; repair only the failed objective group.

## Transfer challenge

Increase estimated capacitance and identify the threshold where the pull-up interval becomes empty; propose a justified change to rate/load rather than guessing a resistor.

# PR-T38-04 — I2C transaction and conditional bus recovery

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T38](#t38).

**Covered topics:** [T38.05](#t38-05).

## Working card

**Build:** I2C transaction and conditional bus recovery. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Derive frames and transaction states, then measure the relevant electrical behavior. Keep UART/USART, SPI/I2C controllers and RS/CAN transceivers as distinct mechanisms.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A transmitter declaring completion while the final stop bit or bus-turnaround interval is still active.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T38-04 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Implement one seven-bit register-byte write followed by repeated START and one-byte read using the reused T28 F439 adapter or a scripted adapter. Caller storage is fixed, one transaction at a time, at most 9 recovery pulses, no automatic unbounded retry. Synthetic target 0x50/register 0x07 returns 0x5A. Results name address_nack, data_nack, arbitration_lost, timeout, reset_required and ok; read output is published only on ok.

This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile C under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

PR-T38-04 supplies successful, address-NACK, data-NACK, lost-arbitration and stretched-clock deadline cases. Address/write and address/read bytes are 0xA0/0xA1. The successful terminal read NACK is expected. Separate line cases cover idle, SDA release after 3 pulses, SDA still low after 9, and SCL not releasable.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T38-04.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Write states and the failure/ownership result of every transition. Separate bus addressing from the synthetic register command.

2. Implement bounded scripted replay and output publication. On the F439 single-byte route apply the inspected ACK-off/ADDR-clear/STOP ordering.

3. Add line observation and the conditional bus-clear action; do not generate clocks when SCL is held low.

4. Replay each failure prefix and prove arbitration loss does not force STOP.

5. Repeat the successful bounded transfer on the declared target, observing SDA/SCL; use synthetic fault injection for conditions that cannot safely/reliably be reproduced physically.

## Failure cases

Fail at the first broken phase; terminal-read NACK is not a data_nack. Lost arbitration releases participation. Timeout returns a diagnosed state, not permission to restart another controller’s transaction. An unreleased line after the bounded recovery requests reset handling and reports failure.

## Acceptance and evidence

Exact fixture statuses, closure actions and publish/no-publish behavior; no infinite waits/retries; successful physical phase trace when closing the board route. Provide explicit evidence for transaction semantics, error distinction and conditional recovery.

Retain one explicit evidence item for each original objective under every linked topic: explanation, implemented/derived property, observed result and limitation. Submit interface/source, replay, dependency/resource ledger and first-failure analysis. Synthetic, target and physical receipts remain separately identified; equipment acquisition or missing adapter/peer setup is an entry prerequisite, not hidden work inside the hour budget.

## Hints and recovery

Use a transaction generation/token so late completion cannot publish into a new request. Keep recovery separate from the original successful transaction. Minimize a failure to the first wrong ACK or line phase.

If a check disagrees, minimize the first failing prefix and compare units, capture point, state and ownership. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted remediation; repair only the failed objective group.

## Transfer challenge

Explain why multi-byte F439 reception needs additional inspected closing/NACK procedures, and keep it outside this milestone rather than extrapolating the single-byte path.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T38-05 — SPI four-mode transaction and ownership laboratory

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T38](#t38).

**Covered topics:** [T38.06](#t38-06).

## Working card

**Build:** SPI four-mode transaction and ownership laboratory. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Derive frames and transaction states, then measure the relevant electrical behavior. Keep UART/USART, SPI/I2C controllers and RS/CAN transceivers as distinct mechanisms.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A transmitter declaring completion while the final stop bit or bus-turnaround interval is still active.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T38-05 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Implement a checked full-duplex eight-bit MSB-first transfer service, maximum 16 bytes, caller-owned TX/RX buffers, one active transaction and explicit timeout/cancel-pending outcomes. Reuse the T28 register adapter and prior ring/ownership abstractions. The selected external target contributes a documented mode/clock/select/dummy-byte contract; the fixture is an original scripted peer, not a claimed sensor command specification.

This 10-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile E under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

0xA6 TX/0x3C RX is traced in all four CPOL/CPHA modes with 16 numbered edges per byte. Final cases include correct drained completion, one missing received byte, BSY still set and cancellation before DMA is confirmed stopped. Mode 0/2 sample odd edges and mode 1/3 even edges.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T38-05.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Draw MOSI/MISO and capture/change edges independently for all modes.

2. Define transfer parameters, lengths, buffer lifetime, status and callback reentry restrictions; reject invalid requests before touching select.

3. Implement one polling path: TXE write, RXNE consume and final TXE/BSY completion. Reuse prior DMA sequencing only for a declared adapter with stop confirmation.

4. Replay timeout, undrained receive and cancelled-in-flight traces; buffer ownership remains with the adapter until completion/confirmed stop.

5. Capture one bounded matched-target transaction, including select setup/hold and final clock. Audit object and image dependencies under the declared E boundary.

## Failure cases

Null/capacity/length/mode rejection, receive overrun, wrong target select policy, BSY timeout, early deselection and buffer reuse while DMA remains active. A request with no meaningful receive payload still needs receive draining. Never change configuration while the selected peripheral transfer is active.

## Acceptance and evidence

Every fixture edge/bit and release decision matches; no solved sensor driver is required. Submit transaction API, per-byte/final trace, resource ledger, cancellation proof and one external capture. Identify which physical target requirements are outside generic SPI.

Retain one explicit evidence item for each original objective under every linked topic: explanation, implemented/derived property, observed result and limitation. Submit interface/source, replay, dependency/resource ledger and first-failure analysis. Synthetic, target and physical receipts remain separately identified; equipment acquisition or missing adapter/peer setup is an entry prerequisite, not hidden work inside the hour budget.

## Hints and recovery

TX-ready, RX-available and wire-idle are separate events. Begin with one-byte polling. Add cancellation only after the normal ownership timeline is explicit; do not let a status return imply hardware stop.

If a check disagrees, minimize the first failing prefix and compare units, capture point, state and ownership. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted remediation; repair only the failed objective group.

## Transfer challenge

Replace the scripted peer with a second documented target whose command/select policy differs while preserving the reusable bus service and its tests.

# PR-T38-06 — RS-232 voltage and DTE/DCE boundary

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T38](#t38).

**Covered topics:** [T38.07](#t38-07).

## Working card

**Build:** RS-232 voltage and DTE/DCE boundary. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Derive frames and transaction states, then measure the relevant electrical behavior. Keep UART/USART, SPI/I2C controllers and RS/CAN transceivers as distinct mechanisms.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A transmitter declaring completion while the final stop bit or bus-turnaround interval is still active.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T38-06 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Reuse the bounded 8N1 UART service to send at most 16 known bytes through a specifically documented 3.3-V MAX3232 circuit and an RS-232 peer or loopback adapter. Use a modest declared rate within guaranteed part/load conditions. Implement a polarity/connection checker, but do not supply an arbitrary generic DB9 pinout: derive the exact selected adapter table with DTE/DCE directions and reference.

This 6-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile E under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture maps logic 1/0 to synthetic−6/+6 V, interprets line samples at/over±3 V and leaves the central region undecided. DTE.TD→DCE.TD and DCE.RD→DTE.RD connections have matching output/input directions; output-to-output and missing-reference examples fail. Synthetic±6 V values are illustrative, not an expected measured MAX3232 amplitude.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T38-06.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Draw logic and RS-232 voltage domains, part supply/capacitor constraints and connector roles.

2. Implement the synthetic polarity/connection checker with undecided input state.

3. Verify the exact prepared circuit and connector mapping before connecting; the line side must reach the transceiver, not an MCU GPIO.

4. Capture logic TX, RS-232 line and returned logic for the known byte sequence; retain rate, cable/load and measured amplitudes.

5. Compare direction mistakes synthetically and audit the reused E firmware.

## Failure cases

Undocumented module substitution, inconsistent DTE/DCE mapping, output-to-output connection, absent reference and voltage outside the selected device envelope. Do not treat the central input-voltage region as guaranteed 0 or 1, or turn a typical maximum rate into a guaranteed one.

## Acceptance and evidence

Exact fixture polarity and connection validity; measured inversion/restoration and correct returned bytes at the declared conditions; source-backed supply/logic/line/connector table. Hardware closure requires the line-voltage observation, not just a TTL UART decode.

Retain one explicit evidence item for each original objective under every linked topic: explanation, implemented/derived property, observed result and limitation. Submit interface/source, replay, dependency/resource ledger and first-failure analysis. Synthetic, target and physical receipts remain separately identified; equipment acquisition or missing adapter/peer setup is an entry prerequisite, not hidden work inside the hour budget.

## Hints and recovery

Use role names and signal directions before pin numbers. If bytes look complemented, inspect line-driver/receiver polarity and pair the logic and analog captures at the same character.

If a check disagrees, minimize the first failing prefix and compare units, capture point, state and ownership. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted remediation; repair only the failed objective group.

## Transfer challenge

Explain and draw the crossed connections needed for a second DTE peer, keeping handshaking excluded unless its exact pins/policy are added.

# PR-T38-07 — RS-422 one-driver two-receiver experiment

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |

**Teaching module:** [T38](#t38).

## Working card

**Build:** RS-422 one-driver two-receiver experiment. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Derive frames and transaction states, then measure the relevant electrical behavior. Keep UART/USART, SPI/I2C controllers and RS/CAN transceivers as distinct mechanisms.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A transmitter declaring completion while the final stop bit or bus-turnaround interval is still active.

Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Construct a short declared one-driver/two-receiver differential path using documented compatible devices, far-end termination and common-mode/reference conditions. Reuse the UART pattern service and at-most 16 bytes. Implement a topology/sign checker; application records and addressing remain outside the electrical experiment. A selected RS-422 component or a separately justified compatible electrical circuit must have its exact transfer/operating data in the equipment ledger.

This 6-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile E under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

The synthetic model declares positive A−B≥200 mV means 1, negative≤−200 mV means 0, and the center is undecided. Two receivers see the same five-bit pattern; a swapped pair complements it and a disconnected receiver has no justified bits. One-driver/two-receiver topology passes, two drivers and the scoped 11-receiver overload do not.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T38-07.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Draw one transmitter and both receiver positions; mark which end terminates, pin sign, reference and device limits.

2. Implement the bounded topology/threshold checker and synthetic swapped/disconnected cases.

3. Measure both receiver outputs for the same known UART pattern on the prepared path. Record cable length, baud and signal/reference envelope.

4. Compare differential and single-ended observations; do not infer all common-mode margins from a decoded byte.

5. Explain how a separate return channel would create full duplex without turning this path into RS-485 multipoint.

## Failure cases

Second active driver is a rejected topology, tested synthetically. Missing/disconnected receiver does not prove a stable zero stream. Reversed labeling, out-of-envelope common mode and assumed maximum-rate/maximum-distance combinations leave the physical gate failed or unclosed.

## Acceptance and evidence

Correct threshold/topology/swapped-pair expectations; both physical receiver traces match the source pattern under declared conditions; clear one-driver versus multipoint explanation and exact device sign/reference ledger.

Retain one explicit evidence item for each original objective under every linked topic: explanation, implemented/derived property, observed result and limitation. Submit interface/source, replay, dependency/resource ledger and first-failure analysis. Synthetic, target and physical receipts remain separately identified; equipment acquisition or missing adapter/peer setup is an entry prerequisite, not hidden work inside the hour budget.

## Hints and recovery

Define the measured differential voltage explicitly. Follow the actual part truth table instead of a generic A/B mnemonic. Begin at a low declared rate and avoid forbidden contention experiments.

If a check disagrees, minimize the first failing prefix and compare units, capture point, state and ownership. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted remediation; repair only the failed objective group.

## Transfer challenge

Add one receiver only after recomputing its input loading and cable/termination implications; explain why this adds no destination-address field.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T38-08 — RS-485 direction-safe reusable byte channel

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | E |

**Executable anchors:** communications. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/communications/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T38](#t38).

**Covered topics:** [T38.09](#t38-09).

## Working card

**Build:** RS-485 direction-safe reusable byte channel. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Derive frames and transaction states, then measure the relevant electrical behavior. Keep UART/USART, SPI/I2C controllers and RS/CAN transceivers as distinct mechanisms.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A transmitter declaring completion while the final stop bit or bus-turnaround interval is still active.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T38-08 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Implement `rs485_byte_channel_v1`: enqueue up to 16TX bytes with a caller token, accept/copy at most 16RX bytes into fixed storage, and emit byte, framing_error, overrun, tx_done, aborted and unavailable events. Return busy/accepted/consumed counts and explicit backpressure. The channel supplies no record delimiter, address or retry protocol. One transaction/driver at a time; callbacks cannot retain borrowed input, allocate or reenter. Reuse the UART adapter and a short two-node THVD1410-class prepared bus; peer scheduling is explicit.

This 10-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile E under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture has two 8N1 bytes at 100 kbaud, DE assert 0,600 ns enabled-receiver startup,200 ns disable and 2 µs guard. Earliest peer start is 202.8 µs; release at 100.6 µs fails while 200.6 µs succeeds. A third synthetic drive interval overlaps the first two and must be flagged. Sixteen 1/8 unit receivers plus modeled bias 2 sum to 4 unit loads. Capacity 2 accepts 17,34 and reports one overflow for 51.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T38-08.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Define IDLE→ENABLING→TX→WAIT_TC→DISABLING→RX_READY states and token/abort ownership. Derive delay rounding for the actual timer.

2. Implement event/capacity handling with final-TC completion and confirmed stop before abort returns ownership.

3. Replay early release, overlap and RX overflow; use synthetic traces for forbidden active-driver overlap.

4. Record actual termination, bias/failsafe, load, reference and transceiver enabled/shutdown mode. Capture DE, UART TX and differential waveform for a scheduled two-node exchange.

5. Export the byte/event header, resource bounds and measured physical receipt to T40; keep application framing outside this channel.

## Failure cases

Premature DE release, simultaneous drivers, shutdown wake delay mistaken for ordinary enable delay, capacity overflow, stale token completion and unconfirmed DMA abort. On unknown device-stop state report unavailable and retain ownership until reset/stop is confirmed. A timeout cannot manufacture tx_done.

## Acceptance and evidence

Exact timing/load/overlap/capacity oracle values; no byte loss hidden by the API; final stop preserved and measured non-overlap on the physical baseline. Supply both software and physical channel receipts and demonstrate token lifetime/backpressure to the T40 consumer. Profile E ledger includes ISR/shared-state and helper dependencies.

Retain one explicit evidence item for each original objective under every linked topic: explanation, implemented/derived property, observed result and limitation. Submit interface/source, replay, dependency/resource ledger and first-failure analysis. Synthetic, target and physical receipts remain separately identified; equipment acquisition or missing adapter/peer setup is an entry prerequisite, not hidden work inside the hour budget.

## Hints and recovery

Round 600 ns to the next timer tick; a 1 µs timer cannot wait 0 ticks. Measure DE against final TC/stop, not against the last data-register write. Separate bias loading from receiver-count arithmetic.

If a check disagrees, minimize the first failing prefix and compare units, capture point, state and ownership. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted remediation; repair only the failed objective group.

## Transfer challenge

Bind T40’s original framing layer to the unchanged byte channel and explain why it must handle delimiters/addressing/retries itself.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T38-09 — Classic CAN codec and bounded bxCAN control

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 12 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T38](#t38).

**Covered topics:** [T38.10](#t38-10), [T38.11](#t38-11).

## Working card

**Build:** Classic CAN codec and bounded bxCAN control. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Derive frames and transaction states, then measure the relevant electrical behavior. Keep UART/USART, SPI/I2C controllers and RS/CAN transceivers as distinct mechanisms.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A transmitter declaring completion while the final stop bit or bus-turnaround interval is still active.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T38-09 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Implement a bounded standard-data classic CAN codec for 0–8 bytes with strict local DLC0–8, an 11/29-bit arbitration-prefix analyzer, and a small mailbox/filter/FIFO model. Reuse the prepared F439 image and implement only one TX mailbox, one mask rule and FIFO0 for the physical baseline; no full general CAN driver, FD, USB or complete fault-confinement state machine. Fixed codec storage is 128 bits plus at most 24 stuff bits; if a bounded output cannot fit, return capacity before publication.

This 12-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile E under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture compares standard remote ID 0x123, extended data sharing base 0x123 and standard data 0x123; standard data wins. Its comparison prefix includes standard IDE0 from the first control-field bit, so standard-remote versus extended is decided by the actual format bit rather than string termination. At 42 MHz, prescaler 6, BS1=11, BS2=2, SJW=1 give 500 kbit/s and sample 6/7. The 0x120/0x7F0 filter accepts 120,123,12F and rejects 130. FIFO10,20,30,40 retains 10,20,30 locked or 10,20,40 unlocked. The original CRC input is the destuffed SOF/header/data for standard ID 0x123 and one byte 0xA5; compare polynomial division with your bounded recurrence.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T38-09.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Draw arbitration fields including standard/extended and data/remote distinctions; use bit-sequence comparisons and explicitly handle identical contenders.

2. Implement the strict standard-data codec, destuff validation and classic CRC check; preserve separate CRC delimiter, ACK and EOF boundaries.

3. Implement the timing/filter/mailbox/FIFO model and reject illegal segment/register values. Make exactly-once receive release visible.

4. Configure one filter/mailbox/FIFO on the prepared board and exchange one known classic frame with a declared peer/transceiver, capturing timing and controller status. Internal loopback is a controller observation, not a physical peer proof.

5. Diagnose supplied arbitration-loss, transmit-error, error-passive and bus-off traces; state recovery exclusions and leave complete transition enforcement to additional inspected scope.

## Failure cases

Identifier/range/capacity rejection, bad stuff/CRC/fixed-form bits, strict-local DLC9–15 exclusion, illegal timing, filter mismatch, mailbox still pending, FIFO overflow and repeated release. Arbitration loss is a retry/participation event, not an error frame. Do not claim link ACK proves application delivery or that automatic bus-off recovery proves network health.

## Acceptance and evidence

Fixture arbitration/timing/mask/FIFO/CRC values, codec round-trip and independent malformed cases; source-backed classic-only capability. Give separate evidence for all six linked objectives: wire semantics, error-state scope, timing, acceptance and ownership. Close the physical receipt only with the declared two-node classic exchange; source analysis and loopback remain separately identified.

Retain one explicit evidence item for each original objective under every linked topic: explanation, implemented/derived property, observed result and limitation. Submit interface/source, replay, dependency/resource ledger and first-failure analysis. Synthetic, target and physical receipts remain separately identified; equipment acquisition or missing adapter/peer setup is an entry prerequisite, not hidden work inside the hour budget.

## Hints and recovery

Compare standard RTR and extended SRR/IDE before lower identifier bits. Keep encoded fields distinct from semantic values minus one. For CRC, inspect the first differing destuffed bit rather than including inserted stuff in the classic input.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T38-10 — ISO CAN FD metadata and external-controller boundary

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Executable anchors:** communications. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/communications/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T38](#t38).

**Covered topics:** [T38.12](#t38-12).

## Working card

**Build:** ISO CAN FD metadata and external-controller boundary. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Derive frames and transaction states, then measure the relevant electrical behavior. Keep UART/USART, SPI/I2C controllers and RS/CAN transceivers as distinct mechanisms.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A transmitter declaring completion while the final stop bit or bus-turnaround interval is still active.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T38-10 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Implement a caller-storage ISO-FD metadata validator, all 16DLC mappings and a declared external-controller SPI/power transaction checker. Valid fixture flags are JSON booleans; raw nonboolean flag values represent malformed input and fail before conversion. The C boundary likewise validates raw 0/1 flag values before conversion. FDF must be true. BRS=false keeps nominal bitrate throughout, BRS=true permits the declared switched data phase; ESI=false denotes active and ESI=true passive transmitter state. Both ESI states and no-BRS FD are valid. Inputs also include payload length≤64, remote flag and controller capability. FD remote requests fail. This core project does not implement a complete FD bitstream, M_CAN driver or physical FD acceptance. Required edition-2 physical closure in PR-T38-11 and PR-T38-12 requires an explicitly inspected exact controller/adapter setup and compatible peer, separately declared equipment and profile E image evidence.

This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile C under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

DLC9,10,11,15 map to 12,16,20,64 bytes. Nine bytes with DLC9 fails. Remote FD and FD sent to classic-only bxCAN fail. CRC width changes after 16 bytes. TCAN4550 supplies VSUP6–24 V and VIO3.135–5.25 V;3.3 V for the whole part fails. Synthetic SPI framing uses a 4-byte command/address/length header and 32-bit data words: two words require 12 bytes total; a 6-byte data tail is incomplete.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T38-10.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Derive the entire DLC map and define separate length, format, capability and storage failure results.

2. Implement the validator and synthetic word-boundary checker; reserve target opcode/address values for the actual inspected controller setup, not this original fixture.

3. Draw arbitration/data bitrate, CRC/stuff-count/fixed-stuff and delay-compensation responsibility boundaries using the inspected ISO/Bosch scope.

4. Inspect the actual TCAN4550 MRAM initialization/32-bit SPI/power obligations and write an F439 external-controller capability/power ledger. Do not provide or copy a full solved controller driver.

5. Document what additional exact setup/measurement would close the required physical FD gate and what the core software receipt already establishes.

## Failure cases

Wrong DLC/payload pair,65-byte overflow, remote FD, unsupported controller, pre-ISO framing assumption, incomplete SPI word and invalid separate supply domains. Larger buffers and FD transceiver labels cannot repair a classic-only frame engine. Do not report physical FD success from a synthetic metadata test.

## Acceptance and evidence

All mappings/validation/CRC-width/capability/power/framing fixture values pass. Explain current ISO versus historical FD scope and show a concrete external-controller design boundary. Core mastery needs the implemented validator and source analysis; full-program hardware mastery needs its own inspected setup, actual compatible peer exchange and receipt.

Retain one explicit evidence item for each original objective under every linked topic: explanation, implemented/derived property, observed result and limitation. Submit interface/source, replay, dependency/resource ledger and first-failure analysis. Synthetic, target and physical receipts remain separately identified; equipment acquisition or missing adapter/peer setup is an entry prerequisite, not hidden work inside the hour budget.

## Hints and recovery

Use a 16-entry checked mapping or derive ranges with explicit bounds; check index before access. Keep BRS disabled semantics distinct from lack of FD capability. Treat a supply-domain diagram as part of the implementation contract.

If a check disagrees, minimize the first failing prefix and compare units, capture point, state and ownership. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted remediation; repair only the failed objective group.

## Transfer challenge

Compare an optional native-FD board with the external SPI route, naming which controller, power, timing and dependency evidence changes without implying either is supplied here.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T38-11 — CAN FD controller bring-up and ownership boundary

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | E |

**Executable anchors:** communications. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/communications/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T38](#t38).

**Covered topics:** [T38.12](#t38-12).

## Contract

Bring up an MCP2518FD external CAN FD controller connected to the existing Cortex-M4 route. Deliver a pin/power/clock ledger, bounded SPI transactions, error propagation and a captured controller identification/loopback transaction. Treat controller initialization and frame storage as a state machine with bounded waits. Keep the prior TCAN4550 synthetic fixture as a comparison; its command framing and supply limits do not describe this controller.

This milestone budgets six hours implementation and four hours verification. Equipment acquisition is an entry prerequisite. Readings are budgeted separately in T38.

## Inputs and expected results

Replay the prior metadata fixture with `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; its mathematical expectations establish only the shared software input contract. Actual electrical values and device responses must come from the recorded configuration and raw measurements. Use the inspected source scope R-V2-COM-MCP2518FD-B for the block/power boundary, then inspect exact implementation passages for the selected board.

## Steps

1. Record exact board revisions, schematic, oscillator and controller/transceiver revisions. Inspect the exact controller SPI, reset, RAM initialization, FIFO and interrupt passages before assigning register values; record their locators in the dossier.
2. Reuse the inspected SPI primitive with explicit chip-select ownership and timeout/error returns. Separate transport errors, device status and CAN errors.
3. Initialize the selected FIFO/RAM arrangement and verify configuration/readback before entering loopback. Capture the actual SPI command and response bytes.
4. Inject a disconnected controller and a deliberately mismatched mode in the isolated setup. Show bounded failure, then restore the known configuration.

## Failure cases

Incorrect supply/logic domains, stale interrupt status, impossible DLC/length, missing peer, wrong timing, buffer exhaustion and a timeout without a documented reset/recovery state. Explain which boundary detects each failure and preserves ownership.

## Acceptance and evidence

A register read returning all ones is not evidence of a valid device. No completion event before chip-select/transaction ownership is released. A valid internal loopback establishes controller-path behavior; it leaves the wire exchange for PR-T38-12. Follow [guide-physical-evidence](#guide-physical-evidence). Preserve source/build identity, setup photograph or schematic, instrument configuration, raw capture, interpretation and a changed-condition repeat. Automated family tests do not close this milestone.

## Hints and recovery

First validate the lowest failed boundary: power and clock, then SPI command/response, controller state, transceiver and peer. Save the first contradictory observation before changing configuration. A known-good peer helps localize a fault but does not replace the learner driver.

## Transfer challenge

Explain the evidence that would need to be repeated after changing the oscillator or transceiver. Repeat one relevant measurement with the changed condition and preserve the earlier result for comparison.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T38-12 — Physical CAN FD dual-rate exchange and recovery

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | E |

**Executable anchors:** communications. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/communications/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T38](#t38).

**Covered topics:** [T38.12](#t38-12).

## Contract

Complete a physical CAN FD exchange between the Cortex-M4 external-controller route and an independent compatible FD peer. Reuse the validated controller boundary from PR-T38-11. Record nominal/data phase rates, transceiver topology, termination, clock assumptions and actual captures. Choose rates supported by every device and the measured wiring; a advertised maximum is not the lab configuration.

This milestone budgets six hours implementation and four hours verification. Equipment acquisition is an entry prerequisite. Readings are budgeted separately in T38.

## Inputs and expected results

Replay the prior metadata fixture with `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; its mathematical expectations establish only the shared software input contract. Actual electrical values and device responses must come from the recorded configuration and raw measurements. Use the inspected source scope R-V2-COM-MCP2518FD-B for the block/power boundary, then inspect exact implementation passages for the selected board.

## Steps

1. Predict valid DLC/payload pairs using PR-T38-10. Send zero, eight, twelve and sixty-four-byte payloads with sequence and end-to-end check fields.
2. Capture both no-BRS and BRS-enabled traffic. Identify arbitration and data phases, acknowledgement, retransmission and the observation point of software timestamps.
3. Exercise missing peer acknowledgement, filter rejection and bounded software queue exhaustion. Record counters, timeout and recovery behavior without using successful metadata validation as a wire-level verdict.
4. Repeat with a changed data-phase rate and a fresh payload generated by the independent peer. Compare intended and observed values and account for capture resolution.

## Failure cases

Incorrect supply/logic domains, stale interrupt status, impossible DLC/length, missing peer, wrong timing, buffer exhaustion and a timeout without a documented reset/recovery state. Explain which boundary detects each failure and preserves ownership.

## Acceptance and evidence

Reject missing ACK, wrong sequence or payload, unbounded retry and absent raw captures. Full closure needs peer receive evidence plus a physical capture and measured configuration; virtual CAN and internal loopback leave this claim not-run. Follow [guide-physical-evidence](#guide-physical-evidence). Preserve source/build identity, setup photograph or schematic, instrument configuration, raw capture, interpretation and a changed-condition repeat. Automated family tests do not close this milestone.

## Hints and recovery

First validate the lowest failed boundary: power and clock, then SPI command/response, controller state, transceiver and peer. Save the first contradictory observation before changing configuration. A known-good peer helps localize a fault but does not replace the learner driver.

## Transfer challenge

Explain the evidence that would need to be repeated after changing the oscillator or transceiver. Repeat one relevant measurement with the changed condition and preserve the earlier result for comparison.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T39-01 — OSI service and encapsulation ledger

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T39](#t39).

**Covered topics:** [T39.01](#t39-01).

## Working card

**Build:** OSI service and encapsulation ledger. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Trace PHY readiness, MAC framing and DMA ownership independently. Validate every length and descriptor transition before exposing a frame to upper layers.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A link reset followed by completion from an earlier descriptor incarnation.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T39-01 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Implement a bounded encapsulation-size and interface-compatibility checker for at most 4 wrappers,8 peer pairs and 8 service connections. The original EDU wrappers are illustrative data, not valid Internet packets. Draw seven OSI responsibilities and their mapping into the later finite Internet endpoint. Declare the difference between a local callable service and the peer protocol bytes; no socket or full network stack is required.

This 6-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile C under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture starts with 12 application bytes and adds 8,20,14 header bytes, producing 20,40,54-byte PDUs. One EDU-LINK peer pair agrees and an EDU-LINK/Ethernet pair does not; a frame service cannot be substituted by an unadapted byte-stream service. Matching names are the declared synthetic compatibility criterion, not a universal protocol negotiation mechanism.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T39-01.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Draw adjacent service and horizontal peer relationships for one original message. Mark SDU/PDU boundaries.

2. Implement checked cumulative sizes and the bounded compatibility checker; reject overflow/capacity.

3. Map OSI purposes to the Internet route, placing dialogue/representation responsibilities without inventing seven wire libraries.

4. Explain why an OS socket client leaves lower layers with its OS while the planned MCU route implements them.

5. Add one case where equal layer numbers still conceal incompatible peer or ownership contracts.

## Failure cases

Header-size overflow, capacity, mismatched peers and wrong local service shape. Do not call the illustrative wrappers UDP/IP/Ethernet merely because some header lengths resemble them. Do not equate all forwarding with IP routing or promise compatibility from equal layer numbers.

## Acceptance and evidence

Exact PDU sizes and declared compatibility values, a complete seven-purpose map and an original SDU/PDU/service/peer explanation. Provide code and explicit evidence for the three linked objectives, including OS-delegation and L2-bridge distinctions.

Retain one explicit evidence item for each original objective under every linked topic: explanation, implemented/derived property, observed result and limitation. Submit interface/source, replay, dependency/resource ledger and first-failure analysis. Synthetic, target and physical receipts remain separately identified; equipment acquisition or missing adapter/peer setup is an entry prerequisite, not hidden work inside the hour budget.

## Hints and recovery

Name what one local caller may assume, then name what the remote peer must decode. Keep byte counting separate from protocol validity.

If a check disagrees, minimize the first failing prefix and compare units, capture point, state and ownership. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted remediation; repair only the failed objective group.

## Transfer challenge

Replace the educational link wrapper with the T39 frame service and identify every shape/ownership agreement still needed before an Internet packet can pass.

# PR-T39-02 — Ethernet media and checked frame boundary

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T39](#t39).

**Covered topics:** [T39.02](#t39-02), [T39.03](#t39-03).

## Working card

**Build:** Ethernet media and checked frame boundary. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Trace PHY readiness, MAC framing and DMA ownership independently. Validate every length and descriptor transition before exposing a frame to upper layers.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A link reset followed by completion from an earlier descriptor incarnation.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T39-02 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Implement an allocation-free untagged Ethernet frame builder/parser: six-byte source/destination, a checked length/type field, payload≤1500, fixed caller capacity 1518 including optional FCS. Local output uses zero pad to 46 payload bytes; the host oracle computes declared reflected CRC32. VLAN, jumbo and the 1501..1535 gap are excluded. Separate buffers with/without FCS and physical preamble/SFD/gap; never place gap bytes in a DMA buffer. Record the prepared 100BASE-TX board/PHY/media path.

This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile C under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

Original fixtures use three payload bytes with EtherType 0x0800 and length 3, requiring 43 pad bytes and 64 frame bytes including FCS. Gap 1520, VLAN 0x8100 and length 2 for a 3-byte payload fail under this local subset. The check string 123456789 has CRC32=0xCBF43926. FCS is calculated over destination through zero pad using declared reflected 0xEDB88320, initial/final complement, then serialized little-endian in this fixture; the target baseline lets MAC generate it.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T39-02.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Draw MAC/RMII/PHY/magnetics/cable boundaries and document exact board/clock/media identities.

2. Implement checked field/length/capacity parsing without casting unaligned network bytes into C structs.

3. Implement the declared CRC arithmetic and compare independent recurrence/zlib results; keep the RFC appendix’s arithmetic purpose distinct from Ethernet normative status.

4. Exercise minimum/maximum/pad/type/gap/tagged cases and distinguish meaningful length from padding.

5. Observe prepared physical link establishment/loss and a selected captured frame; identify whether its capture point exposes FCS/preamble. PHY management details follow PR-T39-04.

## Failure cases

Short header, oversized/overflowing length, capacity, length mismatch, unsupported tag/gap and bad declared FCS. VLAN is excluded, not universally invalid Ethernet. Unknown capture FCS stripping cannot be guessed. A virtual NIC or QEMU run does not prove cable/media/clock behavior.

## Acceptance and evidence

Exact bytes/pad/FCS/length values plus independently reasoned maximum/short-header tests. Submit media/PHY responsibility ledger and actual link/capture observations for the physical route, with FCS visibility explicit. Each of the six linked objectives has its own evidence.

Retain one explicit evidence item for each original objective under every linked topic: explanation, implemented/derived property, observed result and limitation. Submit interface/source, replay, dependency/resource ledger and first-failure analysis. Synthetic, target and physical receipts remain separately identified; equipment acquisition or missing adapter/peer setup is an entry prerequisite, not hidden work inside the hour budget.

## Hints and recovery

Use 14+payload+pad+4 for frame accounting. Compare CRC input bytes at the first mismatch; avoid the suspicious Rev 21 CRC-complement sentence as a derivation. For a length field, upper data excludes pad.

If a check disagrees, minimize the first failing prefix and compare units, capture point, state and ownership. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted remediation; repair only the failed objective group.

## Transfer challenge

Change the MAC stripping policy and update exactly one frame-channel boundary rather than subtracting FCS independently at every layer.

# PR-T39-03 — MAC addressing and bounded learning bridge
