## Working card

**Build:** MAC addressing and bounded learning bridge. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Trace PHY readiness, MAC framing and DMA ownership independently. Validate every length and descriptor transition before exposing a frame to upper layers.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A link reset followed by completion from an earlier descriptor incarnation.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T39-03 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Implement a six-byte MAC classifier and a synthetic three-port, four-entry learning bridge. Table capacity is fixed, expiration is 10 ticks and ingress values are 1..3. Reject group source addresses. Learn/update individual sources, expire before lookup, flood unknown/group destinations to other ports, forward known unicast and filter same-port destinations. This model excludes VLAN, spanning tree, loops and production switch conformance.

This 6-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile C under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

Addresses 02:...:01,01:00:5E:00:00:01,FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF and 00:11:22:33:44:55 exercise local/group/broadcast bits. At time 0 A→B floods; B→A at 1 learns B and forwards to 1; A→B at 2 forwards to 2; A→A at 3 filters; time 12 C→B sees B expired and floods to 1,2. Expiry uses age≥10.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T39-03.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Mark first-octet I/G/U/L and distinguish printed hex order from wire bit order.

2. Implement exact six-byte validation and the fixed table with a declared capacity-failure policy.

3. Replay learning, refresh, same-port filtering and expiration; log table contents and outputs.

4. Add group/broadcast and full-table inputs, rejecting duplicate/conflicting malformed entries without hidden allocation.

5. Compare endpoint filtering and switched capture visibility; explain why promiscuous mode is not a network-wide tap.

## Failure cases

Wrong address length, group source, invalid ingress, nonmonotonic time, table full and stale-entry lookup. Local address does not guarantee uniqueness. Returning an ingress port as a flood destination is a forwarding bug. Bridge forwarding is separate from IP routing.

## Acceptance and evidence

Fixture bit classes and forwarding/expiry outputs plus own group/full-capacity tests. Show first failed invariant, table/resource bound and endpoint filter/capture assumptions. All three topic objectives require evidence.

Retain one explicit evidence item for each original objective under every linked topic: explanation, implemented/derived property, observed result and limitation. Submit interface/source, replay, dependency/resource ledger and first-failure analysis. Synthetic, target and physical receipts remain separately identified; equipment acquisition or missing adapter/peer setup is an entry prerequisite, not hidden work inside the hour budget.

## Hints and recovery

Expire before refreshing the current source and before looking up destination. Separate “unknown” from “known on the ingress port”; both must not use the same output decision.

If a check disagrees, minimize the first failing prefix and compare units, capture point, state and ownership. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted remediation; repair only the failed objective group.

## Transfer challenge

Explain why adding redundant links requires a separate loop-control mechanism rather than extending this fixed-table model by one port.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T39-04 — RMII clock and bounded PHY management

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T39](#t39).

**Covered topics:** [T39.05](#t39-05).

## Working card

**Build:** RMII clock and bounded PHY management. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Trace PHY readiness, MAC framing and DMA ownership independently. Validate every length and descriptor transition before exposing a frame to upper layers.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A link reset followed by completion from an earlier descriptor incarnation.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T39-04 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Implement bounded F439 SMI read/reset/status queries for the inspected LAN8742A route using the matching Rev 8 board Ethernet pin/clock table and actual board-revision receipt. One register access at a time, at most 32PHY addresses for an explicit discovery attempt, finite reset/access/link deadlines. Check PHY IDs, two BSR reads and register 31 negotiated result. Only 10/full or 100/full closes the selected mode-ready gate; half duplex remains decoded but unsupported. Do not transmit with a guessed speed/duplex or edit the MII register while busy.

This 10-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile E under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

At HCLK168 MHz, CR100 divides 102 and PHY0/register 2 read-start is 0x91; busy input forbids writes and 10 MHz HCLK is outside this selected divider scope. PHY IDs are 0007 and C13x. BSR first 20/second 24 distinguishes historic/current link. Register 31=0x1018 indicates 100/full and done;0x1008 indicates 100/half and is excluded. Wrong ID, link-down and incomplete negotiation have distinct fixture results.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T39-04.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Record exact board revision, Ethernet pins/solder bridges, PHY address/ID and 50 MHz reference source. Measure the clock with adequate instrument bandwidth/sampling.

2. Derive PA/MR/CR/MW/MB fields from the actual register scope; require idle before writes, select fields with MB0, then start the read and wait boundedly for completion before consuming data.

3. Implement reset polling and ID masking; unknown/all-ones reads are diagnostic results, not a discovered matching PHY.

4. Read BSR twice, record both values, confirm register 31 done and mode, and configure MAC mode only from a ready result.

5. Capture/record link establishment and removal, MDC rate and timeout prefixes. Export the management result contract for T41.

## Failure cases

Busy no-write, unsupported clock range, absent reference, reset/access timeout, wrong IDs, link down, incomplete negotiation, unknown mode and half-duplex exclusion. A latched-low first read is not alone current link status, and a ready observation is not an everlasting link guarantee. A PHY status fault cannot be inferred solely from a synthetic adapter timeout.

## Acceptance and evidence

Exact fixture command/clock/ID/latch/mode results and explicit timeout tests; actual matching board/PHY status and 50 MHz/MDC observations for physical closure. Record source identities and image audit, and invalidate mode on link change before later sends.

Retain one explicit evidence item for each original objective under every linked topic: explanation, implemented/derived property, observed result and limitation. Submit interface/source, replay, dependency/resource ledger and first-failure analysis. Synthetic, target and physical receipts remain separately identified; equipment acquisition or missing adapter/peer setup is an entry prerequisite, not hidden work inside the hour budget.

## Hints and recovery

Read identity and status before building packets. Reduce an MDIO failure to reference clock, PHY address, divider, busy sequence and source-backed pin path. Preserve first/second latch reads instead of overwriting history.

If a check disagrees, minimize the first failing prefix and compare units, capture point, state and ownership. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted remediation; repair only the failed objective group.

## Transfer challenge

Feed the unchanged ready/link-down management events to T41 and explain which MAC/transmit ownership must be invalidated after a physical link transition.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T39-05 — MAC/DMA reachability and initialization dependencies

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | E |

**Executable anchors:** communications. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/communications/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T39](#t39).

**Covered topics:** [T39.06](#t39-06).

## Working card

**Build:** MAC/DMA reachability and initialization dependencies. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Trace PHY readiness, MAC framing and DMA ownership independently. Validate every length and descriptor transition before exposing a frame to upper layers.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A link reset followed by completion from an earlier descriptor incarnation.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T39-05 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Implement reachable-memory/checked-address and initialization-dependency models, then apply the selected sequence in the reused prepared E image. Declare SRAM interval[0x20000000,0x20030000), CPU-only CCM excluded, aligned fixed normal descriptors and maximum 1536-byte buffers. The local 4-byte alignment rule is a project policy. Assert reset, select RMII under reset/before clocks, enable clocks, complete reset, prepare descriptors, install bases/accepted PHY mode, then start the separately controlled MAC/DMA engines. No full IP/TCP stack is needed.

This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile E under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

0x20000100/64 passes, 0x10000100 fails reachability,0x2002FFF0/32 crosses the end, and 0x20000101 fails local alignment. The good dependency order passes; the bad order selects RMII after clock/reset completion and starts engines before bases/mode. The oracle lists each first-order dependency violation, not a claim of every hardware readiness check.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T39-05.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Derive inclusive start/exclusive end arithmetic and protect addition from overflow. Confirm exact image sections in the link map.

2. Implement the validator and dependency checker; distinguish descriptor policy from generic pointer validity.

3. Write the concrete clock/reset/select/base/mode sequence with bounded readiness/error outcomes using the inspected manual.

4. Establish compiler and DMB/device-order publication contracts; audit generated code and actual object/image dependencies.

5. Run the minimal target initialization and preserve descriptor/base/control observations; failure leaves engines stopped and storage CPU-owned.

## Failure cases

CCM/unreachable or crossing region, overflow, local misalignment, omitted dependencies, wrong reset distinction, unavailable PHY result and reset timeout. A hardware barrier does not cure incorrect address reachability. Never continue starting engines after a failed prerequisite.

## Acceptance and evidence

Exact range/dependency oracle results, correctly placed descriptor/buffer sections and a bounded target initialization receipt. Demonstrate failure leaves a known stopped ownership state. Distinguish hardware ordering, compiler ordering and reachability in the evidence.

Retain one explicit evidence item for each original objective under every linked topic: explanation, implemented/derived property, observed result and limitation. Submit interface/source, replay, dependency/resource ledger and first-failure analysis. Synthetic, target and physical receipts remain separately identified; equipment acquisition or missing adapter/peer setup is an entry prerequisite, not hidden work inside the hour budget.

## Hints and recovery

Validate the last byte/end, not just the starting pointer. Choose RMII while under reset or before clocks. Keep CPU-only CCM and M7 cache recipes out of this F439 path.

If a check disagrees, minimize the first failing prefix and compare units, capture point, state and ownership. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted remediation; repair only the failed objective group.

## Transfer challenge

Move one buffer section to a deliberately invalid region in a separate diagnostic build and show how the validator/map check catches it before device ownership is published.

# PR-T39-06 — Checked Ethernet receive frame channel

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | C |

**Executable anchors:** communications. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/communications/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T39](#t39).

**Covered topics:** [T39.07](#t39-07).

## Working card

**Build:** Checked Ethernet receive frame channel. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Trace PHY readiness, MAC framing and DMA ownership independently. Validate every length and descriptor transition before exposing a frame to upper layers.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A link reset followed by completion from an earlier descriptor incarnation.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T39-06 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Implement normal-descriptor RX validation and `ethernet_frame_channel_v1` receive handoff. At most 2 descriptors per frame and 1536 combined caller bytes; configured CSTF=APCS=0 retains FCS, accepted FL64..1518, publish FL−4 bytes from DA. Require all OWN clear, first FS, last LS, no ES/DE and capacity before publication. The core target baseline can reject multi-descriptor frames; the model still exercises a declared two-descriptor complete chain. A borrowed span/token may be released exactly once, and recycling waits until the consumer releases it.

This 10-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile C under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture has FL64 complete frames with/without a held consumer, DMA-owned, incomplete FS-only, ES/DE, FL100 in capacity 80 and a complete two-descriptor frame. FL64 publishes 60 bytes; incomplete/error/capacity cases publish none. A held successful consumer forbids recycling; returned/failed CPU-owned storage is recyclable under the declared drop policy.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T39-06.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Decode normal RDES0 fields and validity conditions before interpreting FL.

2. Implement validation with no pointer/length publication on failure. Track dropped partial frame state so a later LS-only fragment cannot become a new accepted frame.

3. Implement borrow/release token generation and counters; reject duplicate/stale release and demonstrate consumer backpressure.

4. Bind the reusable C mechanism to the selected E descriptor adapter, retaining separate object/image audits. Observe OWN/status before/after one actual received frame.

5. Export receive span, exact FCS/pad policy, status/drop counters and capacity ownership to T41 without duplicating its future network parser.

## Failure cases

DMA ownership, missing FS/LS, error/truncation, runt/oversized/capacity, duplicate release, stale generation and recycling while borrowed. RX buffer unavailable is explicit suspension/backpressure/drop, not permission to overwrite a live consumer. Do not subtract FCS again downstream.

## Acceptance and evidence

Exact fixture status/length/recycle values plus independently authored token/late-LS/backpressure tests. Every accepted span has proven bounds and exactly-once lifetime. Physical frame/descriptor receipt identifies capture stripping and the selected MAC policy; synthetic correctness alone does not prove wire reception.

Retain one explicit evidence item for each original objective under every linked topic: explanation, implemented/derived property, observed result and limitation. Submit interface/source, replay, dependency/resource ledger and first-failure analysis. Synthetic, target and physical receipts remain separately identified; equipment acquisition or missing adapter/peer setup is an entry prerequisite, not hidden work inside the hour budget.

## Hints and recovery

OWN gates status validity, LS gates final length, and consumer ownership gates recycling. Separate malformed/drop state from temporary lack of completion. Start with one complete descriptor before adding the bounded chain model.

If a check disagrees, minimize the first failing prefix and compare units, capture point, state and ownership. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted remediation; repair only the failed objective group.

## Transfer challenge

Pass an accepted borrowed frame to a synthetic IPv4 consumer that rejects it; show which layer increments which counter and why buffer release still happens once.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A link reset followed by completion from an earlier descriptor incarnation.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T39-07 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Implement a fixed two-descriptor TX publication model and bounded transmit side of `ethernet_frame_channel_v1`. Accept a caller frame beginning DA without preamble/FCS,14..1514 bytes and exact declared capacity; MAC supplies pad/FCS under the selected policy. Copy into fixed internal storage or retain an explicit borrow token until confirmed completion/stop. At most 2 queued slots, one publication at a time. Full ring returns backpressure; no hidden allocation or automatic unbounded retry.

This 10-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile C under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

Successful events prepare tail/head, own tail/head, complete then reuse. Early own-head fails partial_publication; reuse while DMA-owned fails premature_reuse. Error completion and confirmed reset-stop return local ownership but not peer-delivery proof. Payload 3,46,100 requires 43,0,0 pad bytes. The fixture’s completion events imply ownership has actually returned, not merely that an IRQ fired.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T39-07.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Define CPU-prepared, DMA-owned, complete, failed, abort-pending and stopped-generation states.

2. Prepare metadata/buffers and publish tail before first OWN with declared compiler/hardware order.

3. Implement bounded completion, failure/backpressure and stop/reset ownership handling; prevent late-generation completion from ending a new request.

4. Replay publication/reuse failures and add a full-ring plus unconfirmed-stop case.

5. Bind the mechanism to the prepared E adapter for one captured frame and preserve image/map/status evidence, retaining the C component’s separate undefined-symbol audit.

## Failure cases

Capacity/invalid length, partial descriptor publication, full ring, premature reuse, completion without publication, unconfirmed abort and stale completion. On unknown engine state report unavailable/retain ownership; confirmed error completion is not successful wire delivery. An interrupt by itself is insufficient.

## Acceptance and evidence

All publication/reuse/padding fixture values plus own backpressure/generation/stop-confirmation tests. Exact frame policy and first-OWN ordering are visible; every success/error/abort ownership return is justified. Submit target descriptor and external frame observations for hardware closure.

Retain one explicit evidence item for each original objective under every linked topic: explanation, implemented/derived property, observed result and limitation. Submit interface/source, replay, dependency/resource ledger and first-failure analysis. Synthetic, target and physical receipts remain separately identified; equipment acquisition or missing adapter/peer setup is an entry prerequisite, not hidden work inside the hour budget.

## Hints and recovery

Make the first descriptor the final publication point. Keep “queued”, “in flight”, “local completion” and “peer application accepted” as distinct outcomes. On timeout preserve the outstanding token until stop is established.

If a check disagrees, minimize the first failing prefix and compare units, capture point, state and ownership. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted remediation; repair only the failed objective group.

## Transfer challenge

Use the unchanged frame channel for ARP and IPv4 frames and explain why a TCP ACK is a higher-layer event rather than a TX descriptor result.

## Working card

## Contract

Implement a deterministic frame/time/event handoff harness using the already-authored RX/TX mechanisms, at most 2 frames in flight and fixed storage. Add checked one-frame overhead/serialization accounting and capture-clock conversion under a declared offset/uncertainty. Trace one finite HTTP request through ARP/IPv4/TCP/Ethernet responsibilities without implementing the full stack here. T41 owns its finite protocol code; OS sockets can be peers/oracles, not the MCU lower-layer implementation.

This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile C under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

For 32 application bytes with 20-byte TCP/IP headers, IP length 72, Ethernet frame 90 and preamble/gap-accounted 110 byte times give 8800 ns at 100Mbit/s. The zero-data 10Mbit/s contrast still uses a minimum frame. Contract precedence is phy_link, descriptor_available, frame_valid, next_hop, transport, http; multiple downstream failures are attributed first to the earliest failed prerequisite. Timestamp offset 100 µs maps 0,5,20 to 100,105,120;0,20,5 remains nonmonotonic.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T39-08.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Define accepted frame ownership, FCS/padding, time monotonicity and error-event contracts reused by T41.

2. Implement one-frame budget calculations with checked arithmetic; identify excluded processing, propagation, connection/ACK/ARP and response packets.

3. Implement offset/capture validation and first-failure ledger; reject false correlation from unknown clock origin.

4. Drive the existing frame-channel models with a synthetic upper consumer and verify release/backpressure across accepted and rejected packets.

5. Write the concrete HTTP-path namespace/header/validation responsibility trace and a finite endpoint exclusion ledger. Physical receipts correlate actual PHY/descriptor/capture evidence when available.

## Failure cases

Size/rate/clock overflow, zero rate, nonmonotonic timestamps, unknown offset/uncertainty, double-release, unavailable frame storage, invalid frame, missing next hop and downstream protocol failure. Do not count one frame estimate as a whole HTTP exchange or hide general-host reassembly/congestion limitations.

## Acceptance and evidence

Exact budget/failure/timestamp fixture values; own consumer-reject/backpressure and token-generation checks; clear layer-by-layer HTTP-path and finite-subset responsibility/exclusion tables. Each of the six linked objectives has its own measured/derived evidence. Host, target and physical receipts are explicitly distinguished.

Retain one explicit evidence item for each original objective under every linked topic: explanation, implemented/derived property, observed result and limitation. Submit interface/source, replay, dependency/resource ledger and first-failure analysis. Synthetic, target and physical receipts remain separately identified; equipment acquisition or missing adapter/peer setup is an entry prerequisite, not hidden work inside the hour budget.

## Hints and recovery

Start counting at a named boundary. Convert bytes to bits once, and include only the declared one-frame events. Diagnose the earliest failed contract before tuning later-layer timers.

If a check disagrees, minimize the first failing prefix and compare units, capture point, state and ownership. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted remediation; repair only the failed objective group.

# PR-T40-01 — Seven boundary contracts and encapsulation ledger

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T40](#t40).

**Covered topics:** [T40.01](#t40-01).

## Working card

**Build:** Seven boundary contracts and encapsulation ledger. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Give each layer an input contract, peer identity and failure responsibility. Test routing across two physical segments while preventing the relay from acquiring application responsibility.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A valid lower-layer frame carrying an invalid session or application operation.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T40-01 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Produce the executable design boundary for EDU7-v1 before implementing packets. Use the fixed [original wire contract](research/enhancement/networking_contracts.json), rather than choosing new addresses or retry policies. A=17, R=34 and B=51 use two independent segments. R terminates L1/L2 and forwards L3 without decoding presentation/session data. Map application, typed representation, dialogue, bounded reliable message, routed datagram, local frame and physical symbols to their actual responsibility.

Define each layer's submit/receive/tick/completion interface, result and ownership. A synchronous receive span is immutable and borrowed until callback return. Waiting layers copy into bounded private storage. An asynchronous accepted transmit span remains immutable until its specified completion; BUSY consumes nothing. The ledger must identify which completions permit buffer reuse and which establish peer delivery.

## Inputs and expected results

The supplied fixture starts with a conservative L6 service capacity of 80 octets, L5 header 7, L4 payload 24/header 8, L3 header 6 and L2 header 5/CRC 2. The capacity proof gives session storage 87 and fragment capacities 24, 24, 24, 15. Schema 1 cannot actually encode 80 legal octets: its largest canonical record is 1+5*2+(1+2+2+1+16)=33, giving session SDU 40 and fragments 24, 16. The fixture recomputes both bounds. The largest generated network packet is 38 octets and link body 45; generic allowed link payload 40 separately requires body 47 and worst escaped frame 96. Treat storage capacity and accepted syntax as different bounds.

Output a boundary table, nested worked trace and capacity assertions. The fixture's independent arithmetic verifier derives all sizes; your C tests demonstrate that capacities and checked arithmetic enforce them.

## Steps

1. Draw A→R→B and attach three namespaces: local link 1/2, node 17/34/51, ports 7/8.

2. Write a state/lifetime contract for every interface, including upper-delivery rejection and lower BUSY.

3. Derive lengths outward from the 80-octet capacity envelope and the actual 33-octet canonical maximum, then inward from the 40-octet link limit; reconcile all three bounds.

4. Instrument a host pipeline with layer events without yet solving the protocols. Poison borrowed input after return and attempt a forbidden queued reference.

5. Review the trace against X.200 purposes and Peterson/Davie's encapsulation passage. Mark original protocol decisions separately from reference-model definitions.

## Failure cases

Reject an 81-octet presentation record before publication, arithmetic beyond configured capacity, a retained pointer to a borrowed span, and treating R as an application endpoint. A local CRC success may not be reported as session/application success. A BUSY return may not advance or free the sender's buffer.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit the seven service/peer rows, all capacities with units, an exact routed encapsulation trace, and one rejected lifetime trace. Show why Internet protocols do not require one distinct library per OSI layer. For the three topic objectives retain model comparison, nested/address trace and per-boundary ownership/error ledger. This design milestone requires no physical-success claim and does not replace the later implementations.

## Hints and recovery

Start from one record and change one layer at a time. If the length ledger disagrees, label whether a number is SDU, PDU, escaped bytes or physical bit times. If ownership is vague, identify exactly who may write/free each storage slot at one event boundary.

## Transfer challenge

Change only the optional label length. Predict which nested lengths and fragment count change, and which routing/session authority remains unchanged. Do not change the accepted wire contract during the required milestone.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T40.01.a:** Distinguish OSI reference-model responsibilities from a particular protocol suite and Internet architecture.

- **T40.01.b:** Trace an application record through all seven original layer PDUs and both physical segments.

- **T40.01.c:** Specify ownership, capacities, addressing scope and error publication at every service boundary.

# PR-T40-02 — Two-segment RS-485 grant scheduler and measured adapter

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | E |

**Executable anchors:** communications. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/communications/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T40](#t40).

**Covered topics:** [T40.02](#t40-02).

## Working card

**Build:** Two-segment RS-485 grant scheduler and measured adapter. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Give each layer an input contract, peer identity and failure responsibility. Test routing across two physical segments while preventing the relay from acquiring application responsibility.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A valid lower-layer frame carrying an invalid session or application operation.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T40-02 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Reuse the bounded byte-channel work from T38.09 and UART completion from T38.02.c. Adapt it to the declared THVD1400 3.3-V boards and add EDU7-v1's two-segment master-granted schedule. This milestone's new implementation is medium-access scheduling and routed bench integration; do not charge the reused channel implementation again.

Each segment is at most 1 m with termination at both ends and a common reference. RE is low; DE is separately controlled. Assert DE 200 us before data, release only after final TC, then allow a peer after a 200 us guard. Local echo is filtered by transmit ownership. Master link 1 starts a turn each 25 ms: at most one DATA followed by zero-payload POLL; slave link 2 replies once with DATA/EMPTY, starting within 2 ms after complete POLL+guard and completing within 10 ms of its first octet.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture derives ten bits per 8N1 octet, the rounded-up occupancy of 96 octets and legal DE/peer-start events. Its deliberately premature TXE release must fail. Start and completion deadlines are distinct: an on-time reply may legally continue after the start deadline. Host timestamps are injected integer microseconds, never claimed measured waveforms.

Expected outputs include grant state, start/completion timeout counters, echo-filtered peer octets and a waveform index for both actual segments. A missing bench closes software tests only.

## Steps

1. Record board/pins, actual adapter schematic, supply and differential polarity. Check end-to-end termination with power off and explain the approximately 60 ohm parallel result.

2. Reuse the byte/error channel and add per-segment master/slave turn states and finite deadlines. Keep router UARTs independent.

3. Test maximum frame duration, legal EMPTY, no reply, late first byte and legal long reply with virtual time.

4. Measure DE, UART TX and bus differential signal. Correlate TC with the final stop bit; show no driver overlap.

5. Run both segments, then remove/reconnect one cable. Record UART faults/discarded candidates and scheduler recovery without inventing clean bytes.

## Failure cases

An ungranted slave transmission is a counted protocol fault; no overlapping drive is deliberately required to prove rejection. Premature TC assumptions, late start, over 10 ms reply, UART framing/overrun faults and link disconnect produce distinct outcomes. Do not connect an undocumented voltage-domain adapter or substitute RS-232 signals for this differential bus.

## Acceptance and evidence

Retain wiring/termination/part table, two DE/TX/bus captures with settings and timing uncertainty, exact host grant logs, and disconnect/reconnect evidence. The timing oracle checks schedule arithmetic; real measurements close voltage/wiring, final-stop-bit and driver-ownership claims. Demonstrate the three objectives through measured topology, scheduler/TC behavior and an explicit software-versus-physical evidence matrix.

## Hints and recovery

If replies disappear, first compare link grant and DE ownership, then UART errors, then framing; application code cannot repair truncated physical bytes. If a long legal reply is cut off, separate its start deadline from completion deadline. Measure polarity rather than inferring it from a decoder's label.

## Transfer challenge

Run an intentionally slower legal baud as a separate experiment: recalculate the entire turn budget before proceeding. Explain which policy deadlines would need a new contract rather than silently retaining them.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T40.02.a:** Wire and measure the declared 3.3-V transceiver, terminations and two independent half-duplex segments.

- **T40.02.b:** Implement UART transmit-complete, driver-enable guards and master-granted turns without overlapping drivers.

- **T40.02.c:** Separate real physical timing/disconnect evidence from deterministic host octet traces.

# PR-T40-03 — Incremental escaped link framer with independent CRC

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6 h | core | E |

**Executable anchors:** communications. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/communications/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T40](#t40).

**Covered topics:** [T40.03](#t40-03).

## Working card

**Build:** Incremental escaped link framer with independent CRC. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Give each layer an input contract, peer identity and failure responsibility. Test routing across two physical segments while preventing the relay from acquiring application responsibility.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A valid lower-layer frame carrying an invalid session or application operation.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T40-03 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Implement only L2's exact delimiter/escape/header/CRC decoder and encoder above the granted byte channel. Body fields are version 1, kind 0/1/2, local source, local destination, payload length 0..40, payload and big-endian CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE. Encode CRC over the unescaped header/payload, then escape 0x7e/0x7d; delimit with 0x7e. Maximum unescaped body 47 and escaped frame 96 are checked capacities, not allocation suggestions.

Decoder publication occurs only after delimiter, escape, CRC, version, kind, actual length, local destination and grant checks all pass. A POLL/EMPTY has zero payload. A DATA received on the wrong ownership turn does not deliver upward.

## Inputs and expected results

The supplied fixture contains a body with both escape characters, exact encoded wire hex, CRC and known ASCII check vector 123456789→0x29b1. Its negative inputs are isolated candidates for truncated escape, corrupted CRC, foreign destination, impossible declared length, capacity overflow and missing grant. The oracle classifies each isolated candidate; it does not execute a streaming receiver or count callbacks across consecutive candidates.

Create a mandatory learner stream containing an overlong candidate, a resynchronizing delimiter and then a valid frame. Assert exactly one upper callback with only the valid payload. Repeat with truncated escape and foreign traffic preceding a valid frame, and split each stream at every octet boundary.

Your decoder output is an immutable borrowed local SDU plus metadata, or a counted rejection. Splitting input at every octet boundary must produce the same valid payload/event sequence as coalesced input.

## Steps

1. Derive the CRC vector independently on paper for a small prefix, then compare with the supplied finite verifier's polynomial calculation.

2. Design SEARCH/BODY/ESCAPE/DISCARD state and an explicit reset/resynchronization rule for every delimiter.

3. Implement bounded incremental parsing without publishing a partially decoded header or payload.

4. Enumerate every split of the encoded frame and append noise/truncation followed by the valid frame.

5. Integrate grant metadata; serialize one frame on each measured segment and compare the actual unescaped header/CRC with the host expectation.

## Failure cases

Trailing escape, candidate over 47, incorrect CRC/version/kind, mismatch between actual and declared length, foreign addresses and ungranted DATA publish no upper callback. Empty delimiters publish nothing. After DISCARD, the next delimiter permits a fresh candidate; a broken prefix must not poison an indefinitely long stream.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit exact encoder hex, independent CRC witness, exhaustive split table, rejection/resynchronization counters and actual frame capture if bench is available. Show that a valid local frame can still be lost later and that CRC does not authenticate a sender. The objectives' evidence is the parser/encoder contract, bounded recovery traces and scoped delivery/drop observations. Preserve output sentinels and borrowed-span lifetime on rejected input.

## Hints and recovery

Check whether the CRC was computed before or after escaping. If only split input fails, trace the stored escape state rather than changing wire bytes. If noise grows memory, switch to DISCARD with a bounded counter rather than retaining the entire candidate.

## Transfer challenge

Use a payload composed entirely of delimiter/escape octets and recompute the maximum wire size. Explain why worst-case expansion does not double a physical bit error probability into a reliability guarantee.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T40.03.a:** Encode and incrementally validate the exact bounded delimiter/escape/header/CRC frame contract.

- **T40.03.b:** Recover framing after truncation, noise, bad escaping, foreign addresses and overlong input.

- **T40.03.c:** Demonstrate local-link delivery and drop counters without attributing end-to-end reliability to CRC.

# PR-T40-04 — Static two-link router with hop and lifetime oracles

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6 h | core | E |

**Executable anchors:** communications. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/communications/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T40](#t40).

**Covered topics:** [T40.04](#t40-04).

## Working card

**Build:** Static two-link router with hop and lifetime oracles. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Give each layer an input contract, peer identity and failure responsibility. Test routing across two physical segments while preventing the relay from acquiring application responsibility.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A valid lower-layer frame carrying an invalid session or application operation.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T40-04 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Implement L3 forwarding at R and endpoint delivery at A/B. The six-octet header is version 1, network source, destination, hop limit, next protocol 4 and payload length 0..34. A begins hop 4; R forwards only known nonlocal routes with hop>1, preserving end-to-end source/destination/payload and decrementing hop. B locally consumes positive-hop packets addressed to 51. No dynamic routes, broadcast or L3 fragmentation are part of this contract.

Use the exact table: A→51 left/link 2; R→17 left/link 1; R→51 right/link 2; B→17 right/link 1. R owns a bounded private copy while its egress segment is BUSY; the input span is invalid immediately after return. Rebuild egress link header and CRC.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture routes A 17→B 51 via R 34 with hop 4 and a fixed payload. Expected right output retains source 17/destination 51, hop 3, link source 1/destination 2 and identical upper bytes. Additional unknown-route, hop 1, own-origin-loop and bad length/protocol cases produce distinct counted drops with no forward/local delivery.

Output a route decision and changed/preserved field ledger, plus complete rebuilt link bytes from the already-tested L2 encoder. The fixture arithmetic/route oracle does not implement a target router for you.

## Steps

1. Decode the network header with enclosing link bounds before table lookup. Keep ports opaque.

2. Separate local consumption from forwarding; never decrement a hop solely for delivery at B.

3. Copy one accepted egress packet into private storage before returning input ownership. Reject BUSY enqueue without consuming caller state.

4. Poison input storage and delay the other segment's grant; verify egress bytes remain unchanged.

5. Capture the same end-to-end record on both segments and annotate only local addresses, hop and CRC as changed.

## Failure cases

Unknown destination, hop<=1 at a forwarding router, source claiming R in a looped packet, wrong next protocol, actual length mismatch and full egress slot are independent failures. A foreign link address must already have been rejected by L2. An own-origin loop cannot be repaired by merely decrementing hops until zero.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit positive and negative route tables, output wire record, poisoned-input ownership test and measured two-segment relay if available. Explain three address namespaces and why copying a link destination into a network destination is wrong. Evidence for the objectives covers namespaces, exact static forwarding and hop/route/storage failures; every drop leaves session/transport state untouched.

## Hints and recovery

If only delayed egress fails, inspect who owns the input after callback return. If routing works in one direction only, rewrite the left/right local address table explicitly; R has two different link identities. Do not add a default route to make a failing fixture pass.

## Transfer challenge

Predict a hop 2 forward and hop 1 destination delivery, then contrast hop 1 at R. Explain which behavior belongs to the original forwarding contract, rather than assuming an IP router's entire policy was implemented.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T40.04.a:** Keep link next-hop addresses distinct from end-to-end node addresses and service ports.

- **T40.04.b:** Forward between the two segments by the exact static route table while preserving end-to-end fields.

- **T40.04.c:** Predict and verify unknown-route, hop-limit and ownership failures at the intermediate router.

# PR-T40-05 — Stop-and-wait message transport with atomic reassembly

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | E |

**Executable anchors:** communications. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/communications/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T40](#t40).

**Covered topics:** [T40.05](#t40-05).

## Working card

**Build:** Stop-and-wait message transport with atomic reassembly. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Give each layer an input contract, peer identity and failure responsibility. Test routing across two physical segments while preventing the relay from acquiring application responsibility.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A valid lower-layer frame carrying an invalid session or application operation.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T40-05 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Implement L4 over the unreliable routed datagram service. DATA/ACK/PROBE headers carry type, source/destination port, transfer ID, fragment index/count and credit. DATA has 1–24 octets; non-final fragments are exactly 24 and the message is at most 120. Ports 7↔8 select the endpoint service. Keep one outstanding fragment and one bounded reassembly per direction; no partial message reaches L5.

Transfer IDs start at 1 and increase within the session without reuse/wrap. Keep highest-completed ID and one last-completed receipt including final fragment bytes. Re-ACK an identical duplicate final fragment without redelivery; older completed IDs drop. Keep a complete message pending upper consumption with credit zero. Reopen the session before ID wrap.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture has a 25-octet message, repeated first fragment after a lost ACK, a credit-zero pause/probe, credit reopening, final fragment and repeated final fragment. Expected upper bytes appear once only after completion; ACK indices and probe time are exact. Separate failure traces reach retransmissions at 100, 200, 300 ms then fail at 400 ms; blocked credit reaches its independent 500-ms deadline.

Report transfer result, complete delivery bytes/count, matching ACKs, retransmitted bytes/indices, retained/free state and timeout counters. Both failure traces retain unchanged upper output. The supplied oracle derives fragment sizes and abstract event outcomes, not a solved transport stack.

## Steps

1. Spend the first 4 h defining sender/receiver tuple and states, checked fragment arithmetic and matching ACK rules; run a normal 25-octet transfer.

2. Add duplicate receipt and atomic upper publication. A completion callback may refuse consumption, so keep the SDU and advertise no credit.

3. Start clocks only after lower submit accepts transmission; BUSY/grant waiting alone must not consume a retry.

4. In the remaining 6 h, inject lost ACK, wrong ID/index/count, credit pause, reset and final-ACK loss. Advance virtual time exactly through boundaries.

5. Relay on both measured segments and compare application delivery count with frame/retry count. Record which delays come from grants and which from transport timers.

## Failure cases

A mismatched ACK frees nothing. Duplicate accepted data appends nothing. Wrong non-final length, unexpected index/count, total over 120, old completed ID, unsupported port and no capacity are distinct rejects. Credit probes do not restart the blocked deadline. At retry or blocked failure, clear partial state and publish a failure event, never a partial SDU. Session reopen clears old receipts and separates ID incarnations.

## Acceptance and evidence

Retain the sender/receiver state diagram, exact fragment/ACK ledger, injected-clock log, complete upper bytes and failure cleanup witnesses. For all three objectives show checked segmentation/reassembly, match/retry/credit transitions and absence of partial publication/leaks. Capture one dropped-ACK retry on the bench if available. An eventual successful transfer alone cannot replace the timeout/duplicate evidence.

## Hints and recovery

If a repeated byte appears upward, distinguish duplicate fragment append from repeated complete-message publication. If retries fire during BUSY, move the timer origin to accepted transmission. If credit probes prolong blocking forever, retain a separate resource-deadline origin.

## Transfer challenge

Change the message from 25 to 120 octets and predict all five fragment sizes, retained storage and final-ACK behavior. Explain why adopting a byte-stream API would require a different service contract.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T40.05.a:** Segment and atomically reassemble bounded messages using the exact transfer/fragment contract.

- **T40.05.b:** Trace matching acknowledgments, retransmission, duplicates and credit probes with an injected clock.

- **T40.05.c:** Prove that failed or blocked transfers publish no partial message and free their bounded state.

- Nonholder DATA, checkpoint skip/wrap, changed payload at the same checkpoint, stale epoch, incompatible unit/schema and rebooted peer state publish no new effect. Neither checkpoint matching nor an epoch field supplies authentication or durable recovery.

**Build:** Negotiated session, dialogue token and retained-state resume. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Give each layer an input contract, peer identity and failure responsibility. Test routing across two physical segments while preventing the relay from acquiring application responsibility.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A valid lower-layer frame carrying an invalid session or application operation.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T40-06 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Implement L5 independent of L4's transfer IDs. Session headers carry type, nonzero session ID, nonzero epoch and checkpoint. OPEN/OPEN_ACK negotiate schema 1, unit 1 and initial holder A; control records use checkpoint 0. DATA uses the next positive checkpoint per direction. Only the current holder sends DATA. A request transfers the token to B, B responds and transfers it back.

On sending TOKEN, enter TOKEN_PENDING and block new DATA until matching transport completion. Receiver changes holder once on complete TOKEN; repeats are idempotent. A lost ACK can pause progress but cannot permit both endpoints to send. Retained RAM stores committed checkpoint, bytes and response; close/reopen precedes wrap.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture uses a session/epoch, a SET at checkpoint 1, the same DATA again, altered bytes at checkpoint 1, token pending/lost completion, compatible retained resume and peer reboot. Expected effects count is one, the changed duplicate is ERROR, DATA during pending is blocked, retained state resumes and absent state refuses.

Output state/events, token holder, pending flag, per-direction committed checkpoint and application effect count. A successful transport ACK is not by itself compatible negotiation or application authorization.

## Steps

1. Draw negotiation, READY, TOKEN_PENDING, retained-reset, resume-refused and CLOSED transitions.

2. Encode exact OPEN control fields and reject mismatched schema/unit/epoch before DATA delivery.

3. Commit a DATA checkpoint only after accepted upper handling; retain identical bytes and recorded response for duplicate suppression.

4. Lose the token-transfer ACK and attempt DATA at both nodes. Complete/repeat the transfer and prove at most one permission exists.

5. Reset only transport while keeping session RAM, then separately reboot the peer without RAM. Compare RESUME results and cleanup. Correlate session checkpoints with different L4 retry IDs in the log.

## Failure cases

Nonholder DATA, checkpoint skip/wrap, changed payload at the same checkpoint, stale epoch, incompatible unit/schema and rebooted peer state publish no new effect. CLOSE clears session authority; a new epoch cannot inherit an old receipt. An ERROR event may not silently restore token ownership. Neither checkpoint matching nor an epoch field supplies authentication or durable recovery.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit the state diagram and exact OPEN/DATA/TOKEN/RESUME wire fields, lost-ACK token trace, duplicate effect count and retained-versus-reboot evidence. The three objectives require distinct negotiation/dialogue, checkpoint/effect and resumption-limit witnesses. Show where RAM state disappears and explicitly state that an effect surviving a reboot would need a different durable protocol.

## Hints and recovery

If both nodes appear permitted, inspect sender TOKEN_PENDING rather than inventing an extra timeout transfer. If a duplicate changes state, compare checkpoint plus payload and response before applying. If a reboot resumes, identify where the claimed retained state actually came from.

## Transfer challenge

Consider a power loss immediately after applying SET but before any durable record. Explain why this RAM-only design cannot promise durable exactly-once processing; propose requirements without adding an unverified persistence implementation.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T40.06.a:** Negotiate schema/units and enforce explicit dialogue-token ownership independently of transport state.

- **T40.06.b:** Use per-direction checkpoints to suppress repeated application effects after a retained-state resume.

- **T40.06.c:** Distinguish successful RAM-state resume from stale epoch, incompatible negotiation and reboot refusal.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T40-07 — Canonical TLV presentation with strict UTF-8

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | E |

**Executable anchors:** communications. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/communications/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T40](#t40).

**Covered topics:** [T40.07](#t40-07).

## Working card

**Build:** Canonical TLV presentation with strict UTF-8. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Give each layer an input contract, peer identity and failure responsibility. Test routing across two physical segments while preventing the relay from acquiring application responsibility.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A valid lower-layer frame carrying an invalid session or application operation.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T40-07 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Implement L6 schema 1, ascending unique tag/length/value fields and at most 80 octets. Tags 1–5 encode verb u8, request ID big-endian u16, signed big-endian two's-complement centidegrees value, unit u8 and optional UTF-8 label of at most 16 octets. Every record needs verb/request ID; SET and REPLY need value/unit 1. GET need not carry them. ERROR may report retained setpoint/unit 1. Unknown tags are rejected.

Validate all syntax/required fields, exact lengths, integer representation, unit and canonical UTF-8 before publishing a typed record. Use staged output so failure preserves sentinels. Label is display data and never a format string or routing authority.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture encodes SET request 42, value -4000 and unit 1. Its exact presentation wire hex is independently reconstructed; signed bytes are f0 60. Invalid cases include duplicate/out-of-order tag, wrong field length, missing unit, truncated TLV, overlong UTF-8, surrogate encoding and schema mismatch.

Output exact wire bytes or a typed staged value plus deterministic error category. Distinguish representable 12501 from application's disallowed setpoint: L6 can represent it, while L7 rejects its effect.

## Steps

1. Derive the canonical 15-octet SET record by hand; do not copy a native struct.

2. Implement checked encoder capacity and staged decoder with all required-field checks.

3. Decode negative values with unsigned intermediates and explicit representable conversion. Test -32768, 32767 and the application boundaries separately.

4. Validate UTF-8 across each split of a multibyte label; reject overlong, surrogate and >U+10FFFF sequences before publication.

5. Compare outputs with the independent fixture and integrate one encoded record through session/transport without giving presentation access to route/token state.

## Failure cases

Truncation, duplicate/out-of-order or unknown tag, wrong known-field length, missing required tag, invalid unit/schema, label over 16 octets and malformed UTF-8 leave output unchanged. Encoder insufficient capacity writes no partial record under the selected staging contract. A decoded out-of-application-range integer is not silently clamped or applied.

## Acceptance and evidence

Retain exact encode/decode round trips, negative-value derivation, invalid-case sentinels and UTF-8 byte-count/split evidence. For the objectives show representation portability, validated publication and separation of presentation from routing/session/application authority. Measure serialized bytes, not sizeof a host struct. Integrate on the bench only after finite representation tests pass.

## Hints and recovery

If a negative value differs by 65536, inspect signed conversion and byte order. If labels work only unsplit, keep bounded incremental state or decode after complete L6 SDU rather than treating callback boundaries as code points. Do not repair malformed input by replacing characters under a canonical-wire contract.

## Transfer challenge

Replace ASCII label with a legal multibyte label near 16 octets. Predict packet/fragment lengths and explain why the numeric unit remains unchanged even if the display language changes.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T40.07.a:** Convert between local typed values and canonical bounded TLVs without copying native struct layout.

- **T40.07.b:** Validate ordering, uniqueness, signed range, units and UTF-8 before publishing a decoded record.

- **T40.07.c:** Show that presentation encoding changes no routing, transport or application semantic authority.

# PR-T40-08 — Routed SET/GET exchange and physical family closure

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | E |

**Executable anchors:** communications. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/communications/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T40](#t40).

**Covered topics:** [T40.08](#t40-08).

## Working card

**Build:** Routed SET/GET exchange and physical family closure. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Give each layer an input contract, peer identity and failure responsibility. Test routing across two physical segments while preventing the relay from acquiring application responsibility.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A valid lower-layer frame carrying an invalid session or application operation.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T40-08 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Integrate all seven EDU7-v1 layers over the actual two-segment bench. Initial immutable fixture plant value is 1800 centidegrees Celsius and mutable setpoint is 2200. GET returns plant value; successful SET within [-4000, 12500] changes/replies with setpoint. Invalid SET produces ERROR containing retained setpoint/unit 1 and changes nothing. Response request ID matches the request; no physical sensor is implied.

Do not bypass L5 token/checkpoint or L4 duplicate handling to make the application work. Keep application effect count separate from received frame, routed packet and retransmission counts. Host-only success leaves physical acceptance pending.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture applies SET request 42 value -4000, duplicate checkpoint/payload, invalid SET 12501, then GET. Expected setpoint is -4000, plant remains 1800, accepted effects count 1 and response values correlate exactly. It also provides a layered evidence list with no measured physical entries; expected family verdict is pending physical, despite correct software outputs.

Use the earlier exact SET PDU and nested lengths in a correlated trace. Output per-layer event/counter records, application responses, state witnesses and separate software/physical verdicts.

## Steps

1. Execute the integrated host trace through actual layer APIs, including the final-fragment duplicate and retained-session response.

2. Add corrupt/truncated frame, wrong route/hop, lost ACK, credit block, token violation, incompatible OPEN, retained resume, reboot refusal and malformed TLV. Associate each first rejection with its responsible boundary.

3. On hardware capture SET and reverse reply on both segments, annotating link/node/port/request/checkpoint identities and changed hop/CRC.

4. Disconnect/reconnect one segment and repeat after safe recovery; do not turn partial bytes into a successful request.

5. Publish the evidence index and measured uncertainty, then reconstruct one unseen fault and one byte split during review.

## Failure cases

Invalid SET leaves setpoint unchanged; malformed representation publishes no application request; duplicate checkpoint has no second effect. Failed transport never publishes a partial session record. Reboot refuses retained-only resume. Missing DE/bus timing, termination, real relay or disconnect captures cannot be filled by a synthetic event labeled physical.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit exact responses/state/effect count, complete fault matrix, independent host checks and measured waveform/wire records. For the three objectives show application semantics, namespace-correlated routed exchange and independent fault/physical closure. Require actual endpoint build/target execution and original layer code. The supplied verifier's pending-physical result is intentional; replace it only with your separately collected genuine bench evidence, not by editing fixture expected values.

## Hints and recovery

If GET seems to prove unchanged setpoint, remember it returns the separate immutable plant value: use the ERROR retained value plus state witness. If one layer's counter does not match another, loss/retry or forwarding may explain the difference; correlate identities before assuming a bug. Repair the first failed boundary, then repeat one adjacent interaction.

## Transfer challenge

After a delay, reconstruct an invalid SET and lost final ACK without reading the implementation. Add a second application operation only as a new versioned contract with revised typed representation and effect oracles.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T40.08.a:** Implement the exact GET/SET/REPLY semantics and unchanged-state error contract.

- **T40.08.b:** Correlate request IDs, checkpoints, ports, node addresses and link frames in one routed worked trace.

- **T40.08.c:** Collect independent fault oracles and actual physical captures to close the whole educational stack.

# PR-T41-01 — Controlled Ethernet endpoint and ownership ledger

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T41](#t41).

**Covered topics:** [T41.01](#t41-01).

## Working card

**Build:** Controlled Ethernet endpoint and ownership ledger. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Separate sequence arithmetic, stream delivery, timers, flow pressure and HTTP framing. Verify each substate with virtual time and an independent peer before closing physical gates.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A delayed duplicate, sequence wrap or half-close exposing a disagreement between transport and application completion.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T41-01 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Specify the exact F439-LAN8742 same-link profile before implementing its stack. Board IP is 192.0.2.2/24, fixture MAC 02:00:00:00:00:02, peer 192.0.2.1/24, passive TCP 8080. The actual peer MAC is recorded during the cable lab. There is no default route, DHCP, DNS, bridge to the Internet, VLAN or fragmentation/options support. State explicitly that a cooperative-client exchange is not full RFC/IEEE conformance.

Define frame/datagram/segment/stream boundaries and ownership for receive, submit, tick, link change, DMA completion and TCP ACK. Reuse T39's frame-channel design; the new work is the upper packet/stream handoff and finite stack resource plan. A borrowed receive span expires on callback return; queued data needs private owned storage.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture gives an application TCP payload length 3, fixed headers 20/20, Ethernet header 14, minimum pre-FCS frame 60 and FCS 4. Expected IP 43, unpadded frame 57, pad 3 and MAC frame 64 exclude preamble/SFD/interpacket gap. It also budgets six 2048-byte DMA buffers and six 16-byte descriptors.

Output interface/result/lifetime table, nested length diagram, static resource inventory and omitted-requirements matrix. The independent fixture derives arithmetic; actual build map and capacity tests validate placement/bounds.

## Steps

1. Draw MAC/PHY/magnetics/cable and Internet layer ownership without forcing seven one-to-one protocol labels.

2. Define immutable packet spans, complete validation before publication and BUSY without consuming caller bytes.

3. Separate TX DMA buffer reuse from retention of unacknowledged TCP bytes. Design a bounded retransmission copy and 512-byte receive storage.

4. Derive padding and nested length trimming independently, including ARP which has no IP wrapper.

5. Prepare isolated host adapter settings and select independent capture/client tools. Attach actual source revision and board identity to the ledger.

## Failure cases

Do not count Ethernet padding as IP/TCP payload, cast an incomplete header, free retransmission bytes at DMA completion, or call an emulator physical evidence. A second simultaneous connection is refused by the one-connection resource contract. Queue-full/BUSY preserves ownership, and protocol omissions remain visible even after successful HTTP.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit subset/exclusion table, exact boundary lengths and API/resource/ownership ledger. For the objectives demonstrate declared interoperability limits, nested bytes/lifetimes and packet-to-stream semantics. Show at least one rejected borrowed-reference test and a build-map storage plan. No physical claim closes in this design milestone.

## Hints and recovery

Name every length by its starting byte and excluded trailer. If ownership is unclear, compare DMA complete and TCP ACK as two separate events. If an excluded requirement seems optional, consult the actual host/RFC scope before labeling it that way.

## Transfer challenge

Increase HTTP response length beyond MSS 256 and predict segmentation, retained output and padding per packet while preserving the exact response byte stream.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T41.01.a:** Declare the controlled same-link interoperability profile and excluded full-host requirements.

- **T41.01.b:** Trace nested Ethernet/ARP or Ethernet/IPv4/TCP/HTTP lengths and buffer ownership.

- **T41.01.c:** Define byte-span APIs that preserve packet boundaries below TCP and byte-stream continuity above it.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T41-02 — Actual PHY readiness, MDIO deadlines and link incarnation

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T41](#t41).

**Covered topics:** [T41.02](#t41-02).

## Working card

**Build:** Actual PHY readiness, MDIO deadlines and link incarnation. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Separate sequence arithmetic, stream delivery, timers, flow pressure and HTTP framing. Verify each substate with virtual time and an independent peer before closing physical gates.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A delayed duplicate, sequence wrap or half-close exposing a disagreement between transport and application completion.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T41-02 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Reuse T39's bounded MDIO/PHY query interface and record actual NUCLEO-F439ZI MB1137 revision, pins/bridges and fitted LAN8742A. New work is stack readiness and link-incarnation integration, with actual measured reference/link and reset/failure evidence. Configure RMII during documented reset/before ETH clocks; confirm the PHY-generated 50MHz reference and ensure MAC speed/duplex matches the fitted PHY result.

Finite original policies are 10 ms per MDIO transaction,500 ms reset and 5000 ms negotiation. Busy timeout, failed identity, incomplete/down/half-duplex result prevents readiness. Cable loss terminates the old TCP incarnation and retained sends with an abort event.

## Inputs and expected results

Fixture PHY ID 2=0x0007 and ID 3=0xc131 match 0xc130 under 0xfff0. Basic Status first 0x0020 and second 0x0024 report historical down and current up, with negotiation bit 5. Register 31=0x1018 has done bit 12 and speed code 110, hence 100 full. HCLK 180MHz with divider 102 gives the declared MDIO clock calculation. A synthetic reset/busy deadline failure must never set READY.

Outputs include raw identity/status reads, decoded current/historical state, speed/duplex, deadlines, MAC-mode decision and incremented incarnation after a genuine new bring-up.

## Steps

1. Read the exact Rev 8 board Ethernet table and inspected LAN8742A register scope. Compare actual board marking/jumpers; do not assume a newer manual's table was inspected.

2. Implement bounded query/reset/negotiation sequencing around the reused MDIO service. Keep latch-first and current-second samples separately.

3. Decode the four speed/duplex codes and allow only full-duplex readiness; set MAC DM/FES from that result.

4. Measure actual reference clock and link establishment with equipment/settings recorded. Capture MDIO/query logs and independent peer link state.

5. Remove cable, try traffic while down, reconnect and reset the board. Show old transport state is not silently continued.

## Failure cases

Invalid ID, reset never clearing, MDIO busy never clearing, missing clock, negotiation incomplete, half duplex and current down each produce a bounded not-ready result. A low first latch read is not erased from diagnostics by the second current-up read. A query fixture cannot prove a physical clock or cable exists.

## Acceptance and evidence

Retain identity/mode/deadline decode tables, two-read link witness, measured clock/link evidence and old/new incarnation records. For the three objectives show exact physical component boundaries, correct status/timeout readiness and actual board/cable observation separate from mocks. Reuse earlier MDIO evidence by link, then add these integration observations without duplicating T39 hours.

## Hints and recovery

If every register reads 0xffff, inspect management clock, PHY address and physical/reset setup before changing expected IDs. If only first status reads down, consider latch-low semantics. If traffic works only at one speed, verify MAC FES/DM against actual negotiated mode.

## Transfer challenge

Observe a supported 10 full result in a separately declared setup if available; predict the same RMII reference behavior and changed MAC speed setting. Keep half-duplex support as a new contract, not an implicit extension.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T41.02.a:** Locate the F439 MAC, external LAN8742A PHY, RMII clock, magnetics and cable boundaries.

- **T41.02.b:** Read PHY identity, reset/link/negotiation status with exact latch and timeout semantics before marking readiness.

- **T41.02.c:** Measure actual board/link operation and distinguish it from loopback, TAP or mocked-register evidence.
