- [R-PD-GCC-DEBUG-15-2](#r-pd-gcc-debug-15-2): 3.11 Options for Debugging Your Program — opening, -g, -ggdb and -gdwarf. Choose matching debug information and explain what optimization can remove or move before the image investigation.
- [R-PD-GCC-DEBUG-15-2](#r-pd-gcc-debug-15-2): 3.9 Options to Request or Suppress Warnings — -Wall, -Wextra and -Wformat=2. Interpret warning coverage and distinguish silencing the intentional assignment warning from repairing validation.
- [R-PD-DDMIN-ISSTA2000](#r-pd-ddmin-issta2000): Sections 2–3 — Configurations and Tests; Minimality of Test Cases (PDF pp.2–3). Define the same-failure FAIL, PASS and UNRESOLVED replay contract before input reduction.
- [R-PD-DDMIN-ISSTA2000](#r-pd-ddmin-issta2000): Section 4 A Minimizing Algorithm — Figure 1 and reduction rules (PDF pp.3–4). Derive subset/complement trials and independently check the returned 1-minimal certificate.
- [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009): 5.2 Continuing and Stepping — continue, step, next, finish, until, stepi and nexti. Choose source versus instruction stepping to observe the counter guard and first invalid commit.
- [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009): 10.3 Program Variables — selected-frame scope and incomplete or optimized state. Select the correct frame and scope; explain incomplete or optimized-out local state.
- [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009): 5.1.2 Setting Watchpoints — hardware/software limits and watched-object scope. Plan a valid-object watch and a fallback under target width/slot, scope and thread limits.
- [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009): 9.6 Source and Machine Code — info line and disassemble /s, /r, /b. Map a stopped instruction to its source range and inspect the generated branch or call.
- [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009): 18.1 Commands to Specify Files — file, symbol-file and core-file. Pair executable, symbols and core/saved memory while retaining omitted-memory and missing-history limits.
- [R-PD-VIDOVIC-ARM-2026](#r-pd-vidovic-arm-2026): Chapter 5 From Theory to Practice — Crash analysis setup and initial call-stack/locals/status triage, printed pp. 101–104 (PDF pp. 124–127). Critique layered call-stack/locals/status crash triage against the selected platform and UB constraints.
- [R-GRENNING-EMBEDDED-TDD](#r-grenning-embedded-tdd): 5.4 The Embedded TDD Cycle. Allocate host, compiler, evaluation-board, target and integrated evidence without treating one as all others.
- [R-SYS-LINUX-MAN-6-19](#r-sys-linux-man-6-19): read(2) — DESCRIPTION, RETURN VALUE and ERRORS: short reads, EOF, EINTR and EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK. Preserve short-read progress and distinguish EOF, EINTR and would-block histories.
- [R-SYS-LINUX-MAN-6-19](#r-sys-linux-man-6-19): write(2) — RETURN VALUE, ERRORS and NOTES: partial progress, EINTR, EPIPE/SIGPIPE and durability boundary. Preserve partial-write progress and explain EPIPE/SIGPIPE visibility and the durability boundary.
- [R-SYS-LINUX-MAN-6-19](#r-sys-linux-man-6-19): close(2) — NOTES: Dealing with error returns from close() and Linux/POSIX.1-2024 EINTR difference. Diagnose Linux descriptor release/reuse and state the POSIX EINTR portability limit of no retry.
- [R-SYS-POSIX-COND-2024](#r-sys-posix-cond-2024): RATIONALE — Condition Wait Semantics. Explain predicate reevaluation under the same mutex as the causal lost-wakeup repair.
- [R-GCC-INSTRUMENT-152](#r-gcc-instrument-152): -fsanitize=address. Select exercised address-check instrumentation and state its target, runtime and clean-run limits.
- [R-VALGRIND-MEMCHECK](#r-valgrind-memcheck): 4.2.2. Use of uninitialised values. Distinguish initialization from addressability and trace delayed visible use/origin evidence.
- [R-ARM-DUI0553B](#r-arm-dui0553b): 2.4.3 Fault status registers and fault address registers. Decode fault-address validity and retain precise/imprecise and secondary-fault limits.

**Remaining obligations:** mechanism explanation; independent changed-condition evidence; delayed transfer; actual tool/measurement dossier under the assigned conditions.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T44-01 — Evidence-ready warning and logging dossier

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6 h | core | A |

**Executable anchors:** foundations. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/foundations/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T44](#t44).

**Project-specific foundation policy:** Early hosted entry: prerequisite projects supply the initial concepts. Later hardware, process and advanced diagnostic objective cards are assigned at their applicable experiments.

**Covered topics:** [T44.01](#t44-01), [T44.02](#t44-02).

## Working card

**Build:** Evidence-ready warning and logging dossier. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Seal the prediction, establish a same-failure reproducer and choose an observation before editing. Preserve the earliest supported invalid transition and an adjacent case rejecting a symptom-only patch.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A delayed variant with a different root cause but the same visible crash.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T44-01 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Write a learner-owned bounded validation function and diagnostic harness. Investigate a defined assignment-versus-comparison defect; compare assertions/logs enabled and disabled while required validation remains active. Introduce a three-record log and a separate first-cause field here; reuse this artifact in later T21 error handling. This 6-hour milestone includes implementation and verification; module reading, assessment and consolidation are separate. Profile A governs the studied mechanism; hosted diagnostics may be an explicitly declared harness dependency. The learner writes the implementation and intentionally faulty variants. A mature debugger/tool observes it, and the independent static oracle checks only the finite fixture.

Early hosted entry: complete the prerequisite projects in the route. Build the small diagnostic or replay harness here, then carry it into T21/T32 when those later modules need it. The later module is a place to deepen this mechanism, not an additional entry requirement.

## Inputs and expected results

Use `fixtures/debugging_lab/PR-T44-01.json`. Predict admissibility for 0, 1, 4, 5 and the three-record log after four events. The fixture separates retained secondary events from first cause E_INPUT and contains one mismatched image/symbol record. These are static identities/classifications; collect your own warnings and runs. Derive at least one value by hand before consulting the visible expected object. Run `python tools/verify_debugging_fixtures.py` for the independent model certificate and compare your original C separately.

## Steps

1. Write the input/state/effect/failure contract and two pre-run symptom predictions. Retain the original source/image/configuration/environment identities and finite timeout.

2. Compile the faulty function with warnings, predict which parameter value changes, and stop before/after the condition. Fix the relation, then add assert/log toggles and verify the required check in an NDEBUG build.

3. Build the original faulty variant around the supplied fragment/policy, reproduce one failure, and preserve raw observations. Locate the earliest supported invalid transition; record competing hypotheses and a discriminating observation.

4. Reduce the trigger with PASS/same-failure FAIL/UNRESOLVED replay. If already one event, certify that boundary and reduce irrelevant setup rather than manufacture a smaller invalid input.

5. Explain the repair by its invariant, then replay the minimized trigger, adjacent cases and matching build variants. Record remaining unsupported claims and transfer to a changed input/schedule.

```c

/* Intentional defined defect; contract accepts only 1..4. */

static int admissible(unsigned n) {

    if (n = 0u) return 0;

    return n <= 4u;

}

```

## Failure cases

Reject a mismatched image/input, missing finite bound, invalid adapter result, expired watched object, unsupported tool treated as pass, symptom-only patch, or synthetic value presented as an actual C/tool/hardware observation. Undefined behavior has no promised symptom. Preserve the first cause when later logging/cleanup fails. Tool messages may vary by version; compare semantic evidence rather than exact wording.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit the nine-field dossier: contract; predictions; replay identities; actual observation; first-invalid-state evidence; competing hypotheses/test; reduced trigger and tri-state certificate; causal repair/limits; regression matrix and transfer. Address all three a/b/c objectives of each linked topic. The static fixture must pass independently, and the learner C must reproduce its intentionally faulty behavior and repaired contract within the declared scope. An unavailable capability keeps its dependent claim open and uses the stated supported alternative; it cannot be reported as a completed diagnostic or physical result. Assessment distinguishes guided fixture replay from a withheld-variant blind attempt.

## Hints and recovery

External validation must survive NDEBUG. Assertions express internal promises, and their expressions must not perform a required operation. Implement a three-record ring with overwrite-oldest policy and an independent first-cause field: four events retain the last three while the first cause stays E_INPUT. Disable each diagnostic channel independently, then verify no diagnostic-only side effect is evaluated and required validation still runs. Bounded logs can drop events and change timing; retain those limits and compare a release build. A clean warning build or debug-only repair is not a correctness certificate. On disagreement, minimize the first failing prefix, check identities and units, and change one hypothesis-driving variable. Feedback should name the incorrect inference or violated invariant; retry a changed variant instead of repeating unrelated work. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for evidence/feedback policy.

## Transfer challenge

Change the boundary, chunk grammar, optimization, acquisition point, schedule or documented target assumption relevant to this milestone. Predict which evidence survives and which must be recollected. Delay one fresh attempt for at least seven days. A genuinely blind attempt uses a withheld new variant and delayed oracle reveal; a self-authored or visible fixture remains lower-independence practice.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T44-02 — Tri-state minimal reproducer

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | A |

**Executable anchors:** foundations. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/foundations/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T44](#t44).

**Project-specific foundation policy:** Early hosted entry: prerequisite projects supply the initial concepts. Later hardware, process and advanced diagnostic objective cards are assigned at their applicable experiments.

**Covered topics:** [T44.03](#t44-03).

## Working card

**Build:** Tri-state minimal reproducer. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Seal the prediction, establish a same-failure reproducer and choose an observation before editing. Preserve the earliest supported invalid transition and an adjacent case rejecting a symptom-only patch.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A delayed variant with a different root cause but the same visible crash.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T44-02 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Write an original bounded token reducer around a small deterministic replay harness written here. Classify PASS/same-failure FAIL/UNRESOLVED, reduce at most 16 chunks and certify each single deletion. A replay is a fresh call with a reset state and the chosen token sequence. Record PASS when the original defect disappears, FAIL only for the same observed defect, and UNRESOLVED for a timeout, setup failure or different failure. Later T32 projects reuse this harness. This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification; module reading, assessment and consolidation are separate. Profile A governs the studied mechanism; hosted diagnostics may be an explicitly declared harness dependency. The learner writes the implementation and intentionally faulty variants. A mature debugger/tool observes it, and the independent static oracle checks only the finite fixture.

Early hosted entry: complete the prerequisite projects in the route. Build the small diagnostic or replay harness here, then carry it into T21/T32 when those later modules need it. The later module is a place to deepen this mechanism, not an additional entry requirement.

## Inputs and expected results

Use `fixtures/debugging_lab/PR-T44-02.json`. The visible eight-chunk predicate has independent complete triggers 1/7/8 and 2/3; a partial first group without a complete trigger is UNRESOLVED. Candidate 1/7/8 is 1-minimal while the global minimum has size 2. Derive the 88 failing subsets by inclusion-exclusion:32+64−8. It is a model oracle, not a measured reducer transcript. Derive at least one value by hand before consulting the visible expected object. Run `python tools/verify_debugging_fixtures.py` for the independent model certificate and compare your original C separately.

## Steps

1. Write the input/state/effect/failure contract and two pre-run symptom predictions. Retain the original source/image/configuration/environment identities and finite timeout.

2. Write the tri-state test callback before the reducer. Record partition/complement trials, replay identity and bounded work. Check the returned candidate with a separately written exhaustive single-deletion certificate; demonstrate the nonglobal-minimum example.

3. Build the original faulty variant around the supplied fragment/policy, reproduce one failure, and preserve raw observations. Locate the earliest supported invalid transition; record competing hypotheses and a discriminating observation.

4. Reduce the trigger with PASS/same-failure FAIL/UNRESOLVED replay. If already one event, certify that boundary and reduce irrelevant setup rather than manufacture a smaller invalid input.

5. Explain the repair by its invariant, then replay the minimized trigger, adjacent cases and matching build variants. Record remaining unsupported claims and transfer to a changed input/schedule.

The reducer is learner-written. Create a bounded original message/state component with one wrong acceptance transition, then expose only the same-failure test callback to the reducer. The supplied set predicate is a guided certificate experiment; it is not a ready-made causal diagnosis of your component.

## Failure cases

Reject a mismatched image/input, missing finite bound, invalid adapter result, expired watched object, unsupported tool treated as pass, symptom-only patch, or synthetic value presented as an actual C/tool/hardware observation. Undefined behavior has no promised symptom. Preserve the first cause when later logging/cleanup fails. Tool messages may vary by version; compare semantic evidence rather than exact wording.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit the nine-field dossier: contract; predictions; replay identities; actual observation; first-invalid-state evidence; competing hypotheses/test; reduced trigger and tri-state certificate; causal repair/limits; regression matrix and transfer. Address all three a/b/c objectives of each linked topic. The static fixture must pass independently, and the learner C must reproduce its intentionally faulty behavior and repaired contract within the declared scope. An unavailable capability keeps its dependent claim open and uses the stated supported alternative; it cannot be reported as a completed diagnostic or physical result. Assessment distinguishes guided fixture replay from a withheld-variant blind attempt.

## Hints and recovery

The eight-chunk fixture fails when it contains 1, 7, 8 together or 2, 3 together; a partial 1/7/8 group without either complete trigger is unresolved. The candidate 1, 7, 8 fails and all three single deletions are unresolved, so it is 1-minimal. Yet 2, 3 is a smaller failing input. Exhaustive finite enumeration is the independent fixture oracle, distinct from the learner reducer. Check every remaining single deletion and retain the actual replay classification. The reduced input localizes a trigger; inspect the first invalid code transition separately to explain the repair. On disagreement, minimize the first failing prefix, check identities and units, and change one hypothesis-driving variable. Feedback should name the incorrect inference or violated invariant; retry a changed variant instead of repeating unrelated work. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for evidence/feedback policy.

## Transfer challenge

Change the boundary, chunk grammar, optimization, acquisition point, schedule or documented target assumption relevant to this milestone. Predict which evidence survives and which must be recollected. Delay one fresh attempt for at least seven days. A genuinely blind attempt uses a withheld new variant and delayed oracle reveal; a self-authored or visible fixture remains lower-independence practice.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T44-03 — First invalid state with GDB

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | A |

**Executable anchors:** foundations. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/foundations/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T44](#t44).

**Project-specific foundation policy:** Early hosted entry: prerequisite projects supply the initial concepts. Later hardware, process and advanced diagnostic objective cards are assigned at their applicable experiments.

**Covered topics:** [T44.04](#t44-04), [T44.05](#t44-05).

## Working card

**Build:** First invalid state with GDB. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Seal the prediction, establish a same-failure reproducer and choose an observation before editing. Preserve the earliest supported invalid transition and an adjacent case rejecting a symptom-only patch.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A delayed variant with a different root cause but the same visible crash.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T44-03 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Write and diagnose the initialized unsigned admission-counter program. Use source/instruction steps, two frame scopes, a pure conditional breakpoint and a valid-object watch. Reuse the preceding warning/replay harness; the first fault is defined unsigned arithmetic and does not require an out-of-bounds write. This 10-hour milestone includes implementation and verification; module reading, assessment and consolidation are separate. Profile A governs the studied mechanism; hosted diagnostics may be an explicitly declared harness dependency. The learner writes the implementation and intentionally faulty variants. A mature debugger/tool observes it, and the independent static oracle checks only the finite fixture.

Early hosted entry: complete the prerequisite projects in the route. Build the small diagnostic or replay harness here, then carry it into T21/T32 when those later modules need it. The later module is a place to deepen this mechanism, not an additional entry requirement.

## Inputs and expected results

Use `fixtures/debugging_lab/PR-T44-03.json`. Capacity 4 with five acquires then one release gives faulty counts 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 4 and repaired counts 1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 3. Event 5 first violates the invariant. Probe/caller status values 7/2 are synthetic scope examples. Width 8>4 and watches 3>slots 2 require fallback under the declared model. Derive at least one value by hand before consulting the visible expected object. Run `python tools/verify_debugging_fixtures.py` for the independent model certificate and compare your original C separately.

## Steps

1. Write the input/state/effect/failure contract and two pre-run symptom predictions. Retain the original source/image/configuration/environment identities and finite timeout.

2. Stop before the fifth acquire, step through its guard/commit and inspect both frames. Install a watch only on the initialized used object; record actual hardware/software kind or insertion failure and choose a bounded fallback. Compare the stop with the first invalid event, number 5.

3. Build the original faulty variant around the supplied fragment/policy, reproduce one failure, and preserve raw observations. Locate the earliest supported invalid transition; record competing hypotheses and a discriminating observation.

4. Reduce the trigger with PASS/same-failure FAIL/UNRESOLVED replay. If already one event, certify that boundary and reduce irrelevant setup rather than manufacture a smaller invalid input.

5. Explain the repair by its invariant, then replay the minimized trigger, adjacent cases and matching build variants. Record remaining unsupported claims and transfer to a changed input/schedule.

```c

/* Initialize *used=0; no array access occurs here. */

static int try_acquire(unsigned *used, unsigned cap) {

    if (*used > cap) return 0; /* intentional boundary defect */

    ++*used;

    return 1;

}

```

## Failure cases

Reject a mismatched image/input, missing finite bound, invalid adapter result, expired watched object, unsupported tool treated as pass, symptom-only patch, or synthetic value presented as an actual C/tool/hardware observation. Undefined behavior has no promised symptom. Preserve the first cause when later logging/cleanup fails. Tool messages may vary by version; compare semantic evidence rather than exact wording.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit the nine-field dossier: contract; predictions; replay identities; actual observation; first-invalid-state evidence; competing hypotheses/test; reduced trigger and tri-state certificate; causal repair/limits; regression matrix and transfer. Address all three a/b/c objectives of each linked topic. The static fixture must pass independently, and the learner C must reproduce its intentionally faulty behavior and repaired contract within the declared scope. An unavailable capability keeps its dependent claim open and uses the stated supported alternative; it cannot be reported as a completed diagnostic or physical result. Assessment distinguishes guided fixture replay from a withheld-variant blind attempt.

## Hints and recovery

The fixture requests an eight-byte watch on a four-byte-width target and three watches with only two slots. Both exceed its declared geometry; those numbers are a model, not F439 capabilities. Actual hardware availability and insertion/resume errors must be collected. Narrow the watched valid object, use a pure breakpoint, or add a bounded replay log when unsupported. This changes the claim's granularity and perturbation. A watchpoint shows a change, which may occur after the first invalid state; compare it with the contract transition and retain the earliest corroborated violation. Document object lifetime, scope expiry, thread focus, width and slot limits. On disagreement, minimize the first failing prefix, check identities and units, and change one hypothesis-driving variable. Feedback should name the incorrect inference or violated invariant; retry a changed variant instead of repeating unrelated work. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for evidence/feedback policy.

## Transfer challenge

Change the boundary, chunk grammar, optimization, acquisition point, schedule or documented target assumption relevant to this milestone. Predict which evidence survives and which must be recollected. Delay one fresh attempt for at least seven days. A genuinely blind attempt uses a withheld new variant and delayed oracle reveal; a self-authored or visible fixture remains lower-independence practice.

- [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009): 9.6 Source and Machine Code — info line and disassemble /s, /r, /b. Map a stopped instruction to its source range and inspect the generated branch or call.
- [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009): 18.1 Commands to Specify Files — file, symbol-file and core-file. Pair executable, symbols and core/saved memory while retaining omitted-memory and missing-history limits.

- [R-SYS-LINUX-MAN-6-19](#r-sys-linux-man-6-19): write(2) — RETURN VALUE, ERRORS and NOTES: partial progress, EINTR, EPIPE/SIGPIPE and durability boundary. Preserve partial-write progress and explain EPIPE/SIGPIPE visibility and the durability boundary.
- [R-SYS-LINUX-MAN-6-19](#r-sys-linux-man-6-19): close(2) — NOTES: Dealing with error returns from close() and Linux/POSIX.1-2024 EINTR difference. Diagnose Linux descriptor release/reuse and state the POSIX EINTR portability limit of no retry.
- [R-SYS-POSIX-COND-2024](#r-sys-posix-cond-2024): RATIONALE — Condition Wait Semantics. Explain predicate reevaluation under the same mutex as the causal lost-wakeup repair.
- [R-GCC-INSTRUMENT-152](#r-gcc-instrument-152): -fsanitize=address. Select exercised address-check instrumentation and state its target, runtime and clean-run limits.
- [R-VALGRIND-MEMCHECK](#r-valgrind-memcheck): 4.2.2. Use of uninitialised values. Distinguish initialization from addressability and trace delayed visible use/origin evidence.
- [R-ARM-DUI0553B](#r-arm-dui0553b): 2.4.3 Fault status registers and fault address registers. Decode fault-address validity and retain precise/imprecise and secondary-fault limits.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T44-04 — Optimized image and saved-state investigation

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | A |

**Teaching module:** [T44](#t44).

**Required selected project foundations:** [T08.01.a](#t08-01-a), [T08.02.b](#t08-02-b), [T08.04.a](#t08-04-a), [T08.10.a](#t08-10-a). Complete these leaves before this milestone; their work remains in its original module.

**Covered topics:** [T44.06](#t44-06).

## Working card

**Build:** Optimized image and saved-state investigation. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Seal the prediction, establish a same-failure reproducer and choose an observation before editing. Preserve the earliest supported invalid transition and an adjacent case rejecting a symptom-only patch.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A delayed variant with a different root cause but the same visible crash.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T44-04 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Adapt one T08/T36 ABI probe and a learner-owned optimized C function. Match image/symbol/configuration identities, inspect actual disassembly and diagnose a preserved-register or source-mapping discrepancy. A supported core is optional; use an explicitly labelled saved-state alternative if unavailable. This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification; module reading, assessment and consolidation are separate. Profile A governs the studied mechanism; hosted diagnostics may be an explicitly declared harness dependency. The learner writes the implementation and intentionally faulty variants. A mature debugger/tool observes it, and the independent static oracle checks only the finite fixture.

Required selected prelude: `T08.01.a`, `T08.02.b`, `T08.04.a`, `T08.10.a`. Read the corresponding original leaf and reuse its completed artifact or perform that existing budgeted exercise first. These are later milestone requirements, not permission to charge the entire prior module again. PR-T44-01..03 can begin after T03/T07 and the stated small diagnostic/replay preludes; hosted concurrency and firmware skills are needed only for their dependent briefs.

## Inputs and expected results

Use `fixtures/debugging_lab/PR-T44-04.json`. The two toy byte payloads are not real ELF files. Hash each independently and reject a mismatched symbol identity. Synthetic PC 4098 maps to line 42; stack 4104 returns unchanged but preserved register 11 becomes 12. The saved record lacks heap and the optimized local is not materialized. Collect actual image/disassembly/ABI observations separately. Derive at least one value by hand before consulting the visible expected object. Run `python tools/verify_debugging_fixtures.py` for the independent model certificate and compare your original C separately.

## Steps

1. Write the input/state/effect/failure contract and two pre-run symptom predictions. Retain the original source/image/configuration/environment identities and finite timeout.

2. Generate matched debug and production-optimized images. Use info line/disassemble and the chosen ABI probe, then pair a valid saved/core record with its exact image/symbols. Distinguish eliminated values from corrupted values; repair a real boundary defect or reject the unsupported claim.

3. Build the original faulty variant around the supplied fragment/policy, reproduce one failure, and preserve raw observations. Locate the earliest supported invalid transition; record competing hypotheses and a discriminating observation.

4. Reduce the trigger with PASS/same-failure FAIL/UNRESOLVED replay. If already one event, certify that boundary and reduce irrelevant setup rather than manufacture a smaller invalid input.

5. Explain the repair by its invariant, then replay the minimized trigger, adjacent cases and matching build variants. Record remaining unsupported claims and transfer to a changed input/schedule.

Reuse your ABI probe and create a narrowly faulty callee preservation variant in its existing assembly file. In C, create an unused intermediate result and compare its optimized materialization; this example demonstrates source mapping, while the ABI fault supplies a separate causal repair. Do not blame the optimizer for valid elimination.

## Failure cases

Reject a mismatched image/input, missing finite bound, invalid adapter result, expired watched object, unsupported tool treated as pass, symptom-only patch, or synthetic value presented as an actual C/tool/hardware observation. Undefined behavior has no promised symptom. Preserve the first cause when later logging/cleanup fails. Tool messages may vary by version; compare semantic evidence rather than exact wording.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit the nine-field dossier: contract; predictions; replay identities; actual observation; first-invalid-state evidence; competing hypotheses/test; reduced trigger and tri-state certificate; causal repair/limits; regression matrix and transfer. Address all three a/b/c objectives of each linked topic. The static fixture must pass independently, and the learner C must reproduce its intentionally faulty behavior and repaired contract within the declared scope. An unavailable capability keeps its dependent claim open and uses the stated supported alternative; it cannot be reported as a completed diagnostic or physical result. Assessment distinguishes guided fixture replay from a withheld-variant blind attempt.

## Hints and recovery

Reuse a selected ABI probe. Under the inspected historical SysV AMD64 scope, the example entry stack 4104 has the expected 16-byte relation; a changed preserved register 11 → 12 violates the chosen boundary even though the stack returns unchanged. Confirm the actual ABI/build variant before generalizing. A core or saved state needs the matching executable and symbols and can omit memory. The fixture contains registers/text but no heap; unavailable heap state stays open. A core is a stopped snapshot, not the preceding history. If cores are unavailable, compare a valid bounded saved-state record and collect an actual live stop; do not rename the synthetic record a core. On disagreement, minimize the first failing prefix, check identities and units, and change one hypothesis-driving variable. Feedback should name the incorrect inference or violated invariant; retry a changed variant instead of repeating unrelated work. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for evidence/feedback policy.

## Transfer challenge

Change the boundary, chunk grammar, optimization, acquisition point, schedule or documented target assumption relevant to this milestone. Predict which evidence survives and which must be recollected. Delay one fresh attempt for at least seven days. A genuinely blind attempt uses a withheld new variant and delayed oracle reveal; a self-authored or visible fixture remains lower-independence practice.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T44-05 — Memory evidence reconciliation

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | A |

**Executable anchors:** foundations. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/foundations/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T44](#t44).

**Required selected project foundations:** [T16.01.c](#t16-01-c), [T16.11.b](#t16-11-b), [T16.11.c](#t16-11-c), [T32.08.a](#t32-08-a). Complete these leaves before this milestone; their work remains in its original module.

**Covered topics:** [T44.07](#t44-07).

## Working card

**Build:** Memory evidence reconciliation. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Seal the prediction, establish a same-failure reproducer and choose an observation before editing. Preserve the earliest supported invalid transition and an adjacent case rejecting a symptom-only patch.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A delayed variant with a different root cause but the same visible crash.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T44-05 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Adapt isolated existing T03/T16/T32 memory variants in learner-owned C. Diagnose bounds, lifetime, initialization and successful/failed nonzero resize histories, then repair the earliest invalid transition. Reuse the allocator/component and separate dynamic tracks; T45 is optional later deep practice. This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification; module reading, assessment and consolidation are separate. Profile A governs the studied mechanism; hosted diagnostics may be an explicitly declared harness dependency. The learner writes the implementation and intentionally faulty variants. A mature debugger/tool observes it, and the independent static oracle checks only the finite fixture.

Required selected prelude: `T16.01.c`, `T16.11.b`, `T16.11.c`, `T32.08.a`. Read the corresponding original leaf and reuse its completed artifact or perform that existing budgeted exercise first. These are later milestone requirements, not permission to charge the entire prior module again. PR-T44-01..03 can begin after T03/T07 and the stated small diagnostic/replay preludes; hosted concurrency and firmware skills are needed only for their dependent briefs.

## Inputs and expected results

Use `fixtures/debugging_lab/PR-T44-05.json`. The fixture gives five operation histories with first invalid positions 3, 4, 2, 4, null. Failed resize retains valid old ownership/alias; successful resize invalidates the old alias. No crash, return value, sanitizer string or uninitialized value is prescribed. A valid model history is not a clean-tool observation. Derive at least one value by hand before consulting the visible expected object. Run `python tools/verify_debugging_fixtures.py` for the independent model certificate and compare your original C separately.

## Steps

1. Write the input/state/effect/failure contract and two pre-run symptom predictions. Retain the original source/image/configuration/environment identities and finite timeout.

2. Predict the source-level violation without predicting a UB symptom. Run ASan/UBSan and unsanitized Memcheck separately on supported environments, collect reports/silence, identify the first invalid access/lifetime transition, repair it and repeat changed extent/failure cases.

3. Build the original faulty variant around the supplied fragment/policy, reproduce one failure, and preserve raw observations. Locate the earliest supported invalid transition; record competing hypotheses and a discriminating observation.

4. Reduce the trigger with PASS/same-failure FAIL/UNRESOLVED replay. If already one event, certify that boundary and reduce irrelevant setup rather than manufacture a smaller invalid input.

5. Explain the repair by its invariant, then replay the minimized trigger, adjacent cases and matching build variants. Record remaining unsupported claims and transfer to a changed input/schedule.

Write separate small faulty/repaired processes around existing components rather than mix several UB defects into one run. One candidate can read a saved alias after a successful nonzero realloc; another deliberately uses a value before initialization. Keep acquisition failure handling valid so the intended invariant remains identifiable.

## Failure cases

Reject a mismatched image/input, missing finite bound, invalid adapter result, expired watched object, unsupported tool treated as pass, symptom-only patch, or synthetic value presented as an actual C/tool/hardware observation. Undefined behavior has no promised symptom. Preserve the first cause when later logging/cleanup fails. Tool messages may vary by version; compare semantic evidence rather than exact wording.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit the nine-field dossier: contract; predictions; replay identities; actual observation; first-invalid-state evidence; competing hypotheses/test; reduced trigger and tri-state certificate; causal repair/limits; regression matrix and transfer. Address all three a/b/c objectives of each linked topic. The static fixture must pass independently, and the learner C must reproduce its intentionally faulty behavior and repaired contract within the declared scope. An unavailable capability keeps its dependent claim open and uses the stated supported alternative; it cannot be reported as a completed diagnostic or physical result. Assessment distinguishes guided fixture replay from a withheld-variant blind attempt.

## Hints and recovery

Keep the language violation distinct from its observed symptom. A tool might report a later visible use, the process might continue, and a clean run may miss the path. Run separate supported ASan/UBSan and unsanitized Memcheck tracks; use origins where available. ASan alone is not an initialization detector. Record the first invalid source/lifetime transition, each actual tool report or silence, flags and environment. Repair before the invalid transition, verify ownership/failure state, then transfer to a different extent or failure point. An oracle's invalid-event index cannot certify an actual diagnostic or prescribed UB output. On disagreement, minimize the first failing prefix, check identities and units, and change one hypothesis-driving variable. Feedback should name the incorrect inference or violated invariant; retry a changed variant instead of repeating unrelated work. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for evidence/feedback policy.

## Transfer challenge

Change the boundary, chunk grammar, optimization, acquisition point, schedule or documented target assumption relevant to this milestone. Predict which evidence survives and which must be recollected. Delay one fresh attempt for at least seven days. A genuinely blind attempt uses a withheld new variant and delayed oracle reveal; a self-authored or visible fixture remains lower-independence practice.

**Bounded reading:**

- [R-PD-GCC-DEBUG-15-2](#r-pd-gcc-debug-15-2): 3.11 Options for Debugging Your Program — opening, -g, -ggdb and -gdwarf. Choose matching debug information and explain what optimization can remove or move before the image investigation.
- [R-PD-GCC-DEBUG-15-2](#r-pd-gcc-debug-15-2): 3.9 Options to Request or Suppress Warnings — -Wall, -Wextra and -Wformat=2. Interpret warning coverage and distinguish silencing the intentional assignment warning from repairing validation.
- [R-PD-DDMIN-ISSTA2000](#r-pd-ddmin-issta2000): Sections 2–3 — Configurations and Tests; Minimality of Test Cases (PDF pp.2–3). Define the same-failure FAIL, PASS and UNRESOLVED replay contract before input reduction.
- [R-PD-DDMIN-ISSTA2000](#r-pd-ddmin-issta2000): Section 4 A Minimizing Algorithm — Figure 1 and reduction rules (PDF pp.3–4). Derive subset/complement trials and independently check the returned 1-minimal certificate.
- [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009): 5.2 Continuing and Stepping — continue, step, next, finish, until, stepi and nexti. Choose source versus instruction stepping to observe the counter guard and first invalid commit.
- [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009): 10.3 Program Variables — selected-frame scope and incomplete or optimized state. Select the correct frame and scope; explain incomplete or optimized-out local state.
- [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009): 5.1.2 Setting Watchpoints — hardware/software limits and watched-object scope. Plan a valid-object watch and a fallback under target width/slot, scope and thread limits.
- [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009): 9.6 Source and Machine Code — info line and disassemble /s, /r, /b. Map a stopped instruction to its source range and inspect the generated branch or call.
- [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009): 18.1 Commands to Specify Files — file, symbol-file and core-file. Pair executable, symbols and core/saved memory while retaining omitted-memory and missing-history limits.
- [R-PD-VIDOVIC-ARM-2026](#r-pd-vidovic-arm-2026): Chapter 5 From Theory to Practice — Crash analysis setup and initial call-stack/locals/status triage, printed pp. 101–104 (PDF pp. 124–127). Critique layered call-stack/locals/status crash triage against the selected platform and UB constraints.
- [R-GRENNING-EMBEDDED-TDD](#r-grenning-embedded-tdd): 5.4 The Embedded TDD Cycle. Allocate host, compiler, evaluation-board, target and integrated evidence without treating one as all others.
- [R-SYS-LINUX-MAN-6-19](#r-sys-linux-man-6-19): read(2) — DESCRIPTION, RETURN VALUE and ERRORS: short reads, EOF, EINTR and EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK. Preserve short-read progress and distinguish EOF, EINTR and would-block histories.
- [R-SYS-LINUX-MAN-6-19](#r-sys-linux-man-6-19): write(2) — RETURN VALUE, ERRORS and NOTES: partial progress, EINTR, EPIPE/SIGPIPE and durability boundary. Preserve partial-write progress and explain EPIPE/SIGPIPE visibility and the durability boundary.
- [R-SYS-LINUX-MAN-6-19](#r-sys-linux-man-6-19): close(2) — NOTES: Dealing with error returns from close() and Linux/POSIX.1-2024 EINTR difference. Diagnose Linux descriptor release/reuse and state the POSIX EINTR portability limit of no retry.
- [R-SYS-POSIX-COND-2024](#r-sys-posix-cond-2024): RATIONALE — Condition Wait Semantics. Explain predicate reevaluation under the same mutex as the causal lost-wakeup repair.
- [R-GCC-INSTRUMENT-152](#r-gcc-instrument-152): -fsanitize=address. Select exercised address-check instrumentation and state its target, runtime and clean-run limits.
- [R-VALGRIND-MEMCHECK](#r-valgrind-memcheck): 4.2.2. Use of uninitialised values. Distinguish initialization from addressability and trace delayed visible use/origin evidence.
- [R-ARM-DUI0553B](#r-arm-dui0553b): 2.4.3 Fault status registers and fault address registers. Decode fault-address validity and retain precise/imprecise and secondary-fault limits.

**Remaining obligations:** mechanism explanation; independent changed-condition evidence; delayed transfer; actual tool/measurement dossier under the assigned conditions.

**Objective facets:** [T44.08.a](#t44-08-a), [T44.08.b](#t44-08-b), [T44.08.c](#t44-08-c).

# PR-T44-06 — Partial I/O and descriptor autopsy

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | A |

**Executable anchors:** foundations. [Unsolved family scaffold](labs/foundations/README.md). Read its family manifest for tested scope and remaining project obligations.

**Teaching module:** [T44](#t44).

**Required selected project foundations:** [T21.04.b](#t21-04-b), [T24.07.a](#t24-07-a), [T24.07.b](#t24-07-b), [T24.08.b](#t24-08-b), [T24.01.b](#t24-01-b). Complete these leaves before this milestone; their work remains in its original module.

**Covered topics:** [T44.08](#t44-08).

## Working card

**Build:** Partial I/O and descriptor autopsy. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Seal the prediction, establish a same-failure reproducer and choose an observation before editing. Preserve the earliest supported invalid transition and an adjacent case rejecting a symptom-only patch.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A delayed variant with a different root cause but the same visible crash.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T44-06 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Adapt T24 partial-transfer/cursor and descriptor-generation code. Diagnose an intentional offset-reset, errno-overwrite or retry-close defect using injected histories followed by an actual supported learner-process experiment. Keep all resource tests isolated and capped; this close policy is explicitly Linux. This 10-hour milestone includes implementation and verification; module reading, assessment and consolidation are separate. Profile A governs the studied mechanism; hosted diagnostics may be an explicitly declared harness dependency. The learner writes the implementation and intentionally faulty variants. A mature debugger/tool observes it, and the independent static oracle checks only the finite fixture.

Required selected prelude: `T21.04.b`, `T24.07.a`, `T24.07.b`, `T24.08.b`, `T24.01.b`. Read the corresponding original leaf and reuse its completed artifact or perform that existing budgeted exercise first. These are later milestone requirements, not permission to charge the entire prior module again. PR-T44-01..03 can begin after T03/T07 and the stated small diagnostic/replay preludes; hosted concurrency and firmware skills are needed only for their dependent briefs.

## Inputs and expected results

Use `fixtures/debugging_lab/PR-T44-06.json`. Seven output bytes with results 2, EINTR, 2, EAGAIN, 3 retain offsets 2, 2, 4, 4, 7. ENOSPC must survive logging EIO. The Linux reused fd 9 has old/new generations 1/2; retrying close can affect generation 2. A model cap 8 with two base descriptors admits six of seven requests and then EMFILE; it is not a real system-wide exhaustion experiment. Derive at least one value by hand before consulting the visible expected object. Run `python tools/verify_debugging_fixtures.py` for the independent model certificate and compare your original C separately.

## Steps

1. Write the input/state/effect/failure contract and two pre-run symptom predictions. Retain the original source/image/configuration/environment identities and finite timeout.

2. Inject the progress script and show the first offset discrepancy in a faulty `off = n` update. Save errno before logging, trace signal disposition, and diagnose a Linux reused-descriptor retry without actually closing an unrelated FD. Repair ownership/cursors, then collect a real supported short-I/O/EOF/SIGPIPE experiment.

3. Build the original faulty variant around the supplied fragment/policy, reproduce one failure, and preserve raw observations. Locate the earliest supported invalid transition; record competing hypotheses and a discriminating observation.

4. Reduce the trigger with PASS/same-failure FAIL/UNRESOLVED replay. If already one event, certify that boundary and reduce irrelevant setup rather than manufacture a smaller invalid input.

5. Explain the repair by its invariant, then replay the minimized trigger, adjacent cases and matching build variants. Record remaining unsupported claims and transfer to a changed input/schedule.

```c

/* Intentional cursor defect inside a positive-write-result path. */

if (n > 0) off = (size_t)n; /* off should retain prior progress */

```

The surrounding learner code first checks that n does not exceed the remaining span. Use a scripted adapter for this defined cursor defect, then an actual supported OS adapter.

## Failure cases

Reject a mismatched image/input, missing finite bound, invalid adapter result, expired watched object, unsupported tool treated as pass, symptom-only patch, or synthetic value presented as an actual C/tool/hardware observation. Undefined behavior has no promised symptom. Preserve the first cause when later logging/cleanup fails. Tool messages may vary by version; compare semantic evidence rather than exact wording.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit the nine-field dossier: contract; predictions; replay identities; actual observation; first-invalid-state evidence; competing hypotheses/test; reduced trigger and tri-state certificate; causal repair/limits; regression matrix and transfer. Address all three a/b/c objectives of each linked topic. The static fixture must pass independently, and the learner C must reproduce its intentionally faulty behavior and repaired contract within the declared scope. An unavailable capability keeps its dependent claim open and uses the stated supported alternative; it cannot be reported as a completed diagnostic or physical result. Assessment distinguishes guided fixture replay from a withheld-variant blind attempt.

## Hints and recovery

Capture errno immediately after the operation indicates failure, before logging can overwrite it. ENOSPC followed by logging EIO still has original cause ENOSPC. Pthread functions return direct statuses, so that layer does not use this errno rule. EPIPE with default SIGPIPE may terminate before the return is observed; an explicitly handled/ignored signal disposition makes a different experiment. Positive write means local acceptance, not durable storage or peer consumption. On Linux, close releases the descriptor early, so retry after an error can close a reused number/generation. The inspected POSIX.1-2024 EINTR rule differs; label this exercise Linux. Use an injected/capped EMFILE ledger first; any actual exhaustion test is limited to the isolated learner process, at most eight owned records, with cleanup and no system-wide ENFILE campaign. On disagreement, minimize the first failing prefix, check identities and units, and change one hypothesis-driving variable. Feedback should name the incorrect inference or violated invariant; retry a changed variant instead of repeating unrelated work. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for evidence/feedback policy.

## Transfer challenge

Change the boundary, chunk grammar, optimization, acquisition point, schedule or documented target assumption relevant to this milestone. Predict which evidence survives and which must be recollected. Delay one fresh attempt for at least seven days. A genuinely blind attempt uses a withheld new variant and delayed oracle reveal; a self-authored or visible fixture remains lower-independence practice.

**Required selected project foundations:** [T25.03.a](#t25-03-a), [T25.03.b](#t25-03-b), [T25.04.a](#t25-04-a), [T25.04.b](#t25-04-b), [T25.12.c](#t25-12-c). Complete these leaves before this milestone; their work remains in its original module.

## Working card

**Build:** Race, deadlock and lost-wakeup dossier. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Seal the prediction, establish a same-failure reproducer and choose an observation before editing. Preserve the earliest supported invalid transition and an adjacent case rejecting a symptom-only patch.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A delayed variant with a different root cause but the same visible crash.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T44-07 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Reuse one T25 two-thread or condition-wait program and T24 event history. Inject one lock-order, predicate/wakeup or shared-state defect, force a bounded schedule and justify its repair with an ordering/lifetime argument. No new queue or event-loop implementation is charged. This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification; module reading, assessment and consolidation are separate. Profile A governs the studied mechanism; hosted diagnostics may be an explicitly declared harness dependency. The learner writes the implementation and intentionally faulty variants. A mature debugger/tool observes it, and the independent static oracle checks only the finite fixture.

Required selected prelude: `T25.03.a`, `T25.03.b`, `T25.04.a`, `T25.04.b`, `T25.12.c`. Read the corresponding original leaf and reuse its completed artifact or perform that existing budgeted exercise first. These are later milestone requirements, not permission to charge the entire prior module again. PR-T44-01..03 can begin after T03/T07 and the stated small diagnostic/replay preludes; hosted concurrency and firmware skills are needed only for their dependent briefs.

## Inputs and expected results

Use `fixtures/debugging_lab/PR-T44-07.json`. The visible model has cycle A→B→A, conflicting non-atomic W/R without an ordering edge and a check false/set true/signal/wait lost event. The repaired predicate history rechecks true after reacquiring the mutex. There is no promised raced value, detector message or all-schedules result. Derive at least one value by hand before consulting the visible expected object. Run `python tools/verify_debugging_fixtures.py` for the independent model certificate and compare your original C separately.

## Steps

1. Write the input/state/effect/failure contract and two pre-run symptom predictions. Retain the original source/image/configuration/environment identities and finite timeout.

2. Choose one faulty schedule and record its synchronization events before running. Use bounded thread stops or barrier-controlled scheduling, inspect all thread frames and construct the wait/HB graph. Repair the causal lock-order/predicate/publication obligation and exercise at least two different schedules.

3. Build the original faulty variant around the supplied fragment/policy, reproduce one failure, and preserve raw observations. Locate the earliest supported invalid transition; record competing hypotheses and a discriminating observation.

4. Reduce the trigger with PASS/same-failure FAIL/UNRESOLVED replay. If already one event, certify that boundary and reduce irrelevant setup rather than manufacture a smaller invalid input.

5. Explain the repair by its invariant, then replay the minimized trigger, adjacent cases and matching build variants. Record remaining unsupported claims and transfer to a changed input/schedule.

Use the existing T25 predicate-wait program, deliberately move the predicate check outside its mutex-protected wait protocol, and isolate the resulting schedule. A non-atomic data-race variant runs in a separate disposable learner process; its output is not the test oracle.

## Failure cases

Reject a mismatched image/input, missing finite bound, invalid adapter result, expired watched object, unsupported tool treated as pass, symptom-only patch, or synthetic value presented as an actual C/tool/hardware observation. Undefined behavior has no promised symptom. Preserve the first cause when later logging/cleanup fails. Tool messages may vary by version; compare semantic evidence rather than exact wording.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit the nine-field dossier: contract; predictions; replay identities; actual observation; first-invalid-state evidence; competing hypotheses/test; reduced trigger and tri-state certificate; causal repair/limits; regression matrix and transfer. Address all three a/b/c objectives of each linked topic. The static fixture must pass independently, and the learner C must reproduce its intentionally faulty behavior and repaired contract within the declared scope. An unavailable capability keeps its dependent claim open and uses the stated supported alternative; it cannot be reported as a completed diagnostic or physical result. Assessment distinguishes guided fixture replay from a withheld-variant blind attempt.

## Hints and recovery

The lost-wakeup fixture has consumer check false, producer set true/signal, consumer waits. Fixing only the sleep length leaves that window. Reuse T25's predicate-under-the-same-mutex protocol: the wait releases atomically, the producer changes state while holding the mutex, and the consumer rechecks after reacquisition and every wakeup. Save forced schedules, thread identities, direct API statuses and a written ordering/lifetime argument. Supported detector runs and stress add exercised evidence. Halting or logging can hide a race; a detector's silence and one deterministic history do not close all schedules or establish fairness. On disagreement, minimize the first failing prefix, check identities and units, and change one hypothesis-driving variable. Feedback should name the incorrect inference or violated invariant; retry a changed variant instead of repeating unrelated work. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for evidence/feedback policy.

## Transfer challenge

Change the boundary, chunk grammar, optimization, acquisition point, schedule or documented target assumption relevant to this milestone. Predict which evidence survives and which must be recollected. Delay one fresh attempt for at least seven days. A genuinely blind attempt uses a withheld new variant and delayed oracle reveal; a self-authored or visible fixture remains lower-independence practice.

- [R-PD-GCC-DEBUG-15-2](#r-pd-gcc-debug-15-2): 3.9 Options to Request or Suppress Warnings — -Wall, -Wextra and -Wformat=2. Interpret warning coverage and distinguish silencing the intentional assignment warning from repairing validation.
- [R-PD-DDMIN-ISSTA2000](#r-pd-ddmin-issta2000): Sections 2–3 — Configurations and Tests; Minimality of Test Cases (PDF pp.2–3). Define the same-failure FAIL, PASS and UNRESOLVED replay contract before input reduction.
- [R-PD-DDMIN-ISSTA2000](#r-pd-ddmin-issta2000): Section 4 A Minimizing Algorithm — Figure 1 and reduction rules (PDF pp.3–4). Derive subset/complement trials and independently check the returned 1-minimal certificate.
- [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009): 5.2 Continuing and Stepping — continue, step, next, finish, until, stepi and nexti. Choose source versus instruction stepping to observe the counter guard and first invalid commit.
- [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009): 10.3 Program Variables — selected-frame scope and incomplete or optimized state. Select the correct frame and scope; explain incomplete or optimized-out local state.
- [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009): 5.1.2 Setting Watchpoints — hardware/software limits and watched-object scope. Plan a valid-object watch and a fallback under target width/slot, scope and thread limits.
- [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009): 9.6 Source and Machine Code — info line and disassemble /s, /r, /b. Map a stopped instruction to its source range and inspect the generated branch or call.
- [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009): 18.1 Commands to Specify Files — file, symbol-file and core-file. Pair executable, symbols and core/saved memory while retaining omitted-memory and missing-history limits.
- [R-PD-VIDOVIC-ARM-2026](#r-pd-vidovic-arm-2026): Chapter 5 From Theory to Practice — Crash analysis setup and initial call-stack/locals/status triage, printed pp. 101–104 (PDF pp. 124–127). Critique layered call-stack/locals/status crash triage against the selected platform and UB constraints.
- [R-GRENNING-EMBEDDED-TDD](#r-grenning-embedded-tdd): 5.4 The Embedded TDD Cycle. Allocate host, compiler, evaluation-board, target and integrated evidence without treating one as all others.
- [R-SYS-LINUX-MAN-6-19](#r-sys-linux-man-6-19): read(2) — DESCRIPTION, RETURN VALUE and ERRORS: short reads, EOF, EINTR and EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK. Preserve short-read progress and distinguish EOF, EINTR and would-block histories.
- [R-SYS-LINUX-MAN-6-19](#r-sys-linux-man-6-19): write(2) — RETURN VALUE, ERRORS and NOTES: partial progress, EINTR, EPIPE/SIGPIPE and durability boundary. Preserve partial-write progress and explain EPIPE/SIGPIPE visibility and the durability boundary.
- [R-SYS-LINUX-MAN-6-19](#r-sys-linux-man-6-19): close(2) — NOTES: Dealing with error returns from close() and Linux/POSIX.1-2024 EINTR difference. Diagnose Linux descriptor release/reuse and state the POSIX EINTR portability limit of no retry.
- [R-SYS-POSIX-COND-2024](#r-sys-posix-cond-2024): RATIONALE — Condition Wait Semantics. Explain predicate reevaluation under the same mutex as the causal lost-wakeup repair.
- [R-GCC-INSTRUMENT-152](#r-gcc-instrument-152): -fsanitize=address. Select exercised address-check instrumentation and state its target, runtime and clean-run limits.
- [R-VALGRIND-MEMCHECK](#r-valgrind-memcheck): 4.2.2. Use of uninitialised values. Distinguish initialization from addressability and trace delayed visible use/origin evidence.
- [R-ARM-DUI0553B](#r-arm-dui0553b): 2.4.3 Fault status registers and fault address registers. Decode fault-address validity and retain precise/imprecise and secondary-fault limits.

**Remaining obligations:** mechanism explanation; independent changed-condition evidence; delayed transfer; actual tool/measurement dossier under the assigned conditions.

- [R-PD-DDMIN-ISSTA2000](#r-pd-ddmin-issta2000): Sections 2–3 — Configurations and Tests; Minimality of Test Cases (PDF pp.2–3). Define the same-failure FAIL, PASS and UNRESOLVED replay contract before input reduction.
- [R-PD-DDMIN-ISSTA2000](#r-pd-ddmin-issta2000): Section 4 A Minimizing Algorithm — Figure 1 and reduction rules (PDF pp.3–4). Derive subset/complement trials and independently check the returned 1-minimal certificate.
- [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009): 5.2 Continuing and Stepping — continue, step, next, finish, until, stepi and nexti. Choose source versus instruction stepping to observe the counter guard and first invalid commit.
- [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009): 10.3 Program Variables — selected-frame scope and incomplete or optimized state. Select the correct frame and scope; explain incomplete or optimized-out local state.
- [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009): 5.1.2 Setting Watchpoints — hardware/software limits and watched-object scope. Plan a valid-object watch and a fallback under target width/slot, scope and thread limits.
- [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009): 9.6 Source and Machine Code — info line and disassemble /s, /r, /b. Map a stopped instruction to its source range and inspect the generated branch or call.
- [R-PD-GDB-20261009](#r-pd-gdb-20261009): 18.1 Commands to Specify Files — file, symbol-file and core-file. Pair executable, symbols and core/saved memory while retaining omitted-memory and missing-history limits.
- [R-PD-VIDOVIC-ARM-2026](#r-pd-vidovic-arm-2026): Chapter 5 From Theory to Practice — Crash analysis setup and initial call-stack/locals/status triage, printed pp. 101–104 (PDF pp. 124–127). Critique layered call-stack/locals/status crash triage against the selected platform and UB constraints.
- [R-GRENNING-EMBEDDED-TDD](#r-grenning-embedded-tdd): 5.4 The Embedded TDD Cycle. Allocate host, compiler, evaluation-board, target and integrated evidence without treating one as all others.
- [R-SYS-LINUX-MAN-6-19](#r-sys-linux-man-6-19): read(2) — DESCRIPTION, RETURN VALUE and ERRORS: short reads, EOF, EINTR and EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK. Preserve short-read progress and distinguish EOF, EINTR and would-block histories.
- [R-SYS-LINUX-MAN-6-19](#r-sys-linux-man-6-19): write(2) — RETURN VALUE, ERRORS and NOTES: partial progress, EINTR, EPIPE/SIGPIPE and durability boundary. Preserve partial-write progress and explain EPIPE/SIGPIPE visibility and the durability boundary.
- [R-SYS-LINUX-MAN-6-19](#r-sys-linux-man-6-19): close(2) — NOTES: Dealing with error returns from close() and Linux/POSIX.1-2024 EINTR difference. Diagnose Linux descriptor release/reuse and state the POSIX EINTR portability limit of no retry.
- [R-SYS-POSIX-COND-2024](#r-sys-posix-cond-2024): RATIONALE — Condition Wait Semantics. Explain predicate reevaluation under the same mutex as the causal lost-wakeup repair.
- [R-GCC-INSTRUMENT-152](#r-gcc-instrument-152): -fsanitize=address. Select exercised address-check instrumentation and state its target, runtime and clean-run limits.
- [R-VALGRIND-MEMCHECK](#r-valgrind-memcheck): 4.2.2. Use of uninitialised values. Distinguish initialization from addressability and trace delayed visible use/origin evidence.
- [R-ARM-DUI0553B](#r-arm-dui0553b): 2.4.3 Fault status registers and fault address registers. Decode fault-address validity and retain precise/imprecise and secondary-fault limits.

**Remaining obligations:** mechanism explanation; independent changed-condition evidence; delayed transfer; actual tool/measurement dossier under the assigned conditions.

## Retained full project contract



# PR-T44-08 — Reset, HardFault and DMA investigation

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | B |

**Teaching module:** [T44](#t44).

**Required selected project foundations:** [T27.03.a](#t27-03-a), [T27.05.b](#t27-05-b), [T29.01.a](#t29-01-a), [T29.07.a](#t29-07-a), [T31.03.a](#t31-03-a), [T31.05.a](#t31-05-a). Complete these leaves before this milestone; their work remains in its original module.

**Covered topics:** [T44.10](#t44-10).

## Working card

**Build:** Reset, HardFault and DMA investigation. **Evidence:** component dossier. **Start:** predict the supplied case before reading its expected result.

**Engineering question:** Seal the prediction, establish a same-failure reproducer and choose an observation before editing. Preserve the earliest supported invalid transition and an adjacent case rejecting a symptom-only patch.

**Changed-condition challenge:** A delayed variant with a different root cause but the same visible crash.

Use `python -m cmastery init PR-T44-08 <empty-workspace>` to obtain the brief, fixtures and any executable family scaffold. A `not-run` or `unavailable` result leaves the corresponding claim open. Apply the [shared contract cards](#guide-component-contracts), then the project-specific obligations below.

## Contract

Reuse the selected F439 startup, basic fault decoder and ISR/DMA component. Introduce one documented startup-stage or completion-ownership defect in learner-owned code and diagnose competing causes. Static frame/mask results are required; actual emulator/physical evidence retains distinct capabilities and open claims. This 10-hour milestone includes implementation and verification; module reading, assessment and consolidation are separate. Profile B governs the studied mechanism; hosted diagnostics may be an explicitly declared harness dependency. The learner writes the implementation and intentionally faulty variants. A mature debugger/tool observes it, and the independent static oracle checks only the finite fixture.

Required selected prelude: `T27.03.a`, `T27.05.b`, `T29.01.a`, `T29.07.a`, `T31.03.a`, `T31.05.a`. Read the corresponding original leaf and reuse its completed artifact or perform that existing budgeted exercise first. These are later milestone requirements, not permission to charge the entire prior module again. PR-T44-01..03 can begin after T03/T07 and the stated small diagnostic/replay preludes; hosted concurrency and firmware skills are needed only for their dependent briefs.

## Inputs and expected results

Use `fixtures/debugging_lab/PR-T44-08.json`. Manually decode reset 0x08000101, IRQ 3/exception 19/vector 0x0800004C, EXC_RETURN 0xFFFFFFFD, basic frame 0x20000FE0 and stacked PC. Compare precise CFSR 0x8200/BFAR valid against imprecise 0x400 with invalid address. A cancel request leaves DMA ownership unchanged until ack; the third event is premature CPU reuse. The configure-before-enable stage is a declared policy defect. Derive at least one value by hand before consulting the visible expected object. Run `python tools/verify_debugging_fixtures.py` for the independent model certificate and compare your original C separately.

## Steps

1. Write the input/state/effect/failure contract and two pre-run symptom predictions. Retain the original source/image/configuration/environment identities and finite timeout.

2. Verify image, selected board/core, basic-frame assumptions and readable memory before decoding. Reuse startup/fault/DMA artifacts, predict two causes, inspect a safe documented status/trace, and change one stage/ownership transition. Repeat one actual supported target observation or keep the physical claim open with the declared static/emulator alternative.

3. Build the original faulty variant around the supplied fragment/policy, reproduce one failure, and preserve raw observations. Locate the earliest supported invalid transition; record competing hypotheses and a discriminating observation.

4. Reduce the trigger with PASS/same-failure FAIL/UNRESOLVED replay. If already one event, certify that boundary and reduce irrelevant setup rather than manufacture a smaller invalid input.

5. Explain the repair by its invariant, then replay the minimized trigger, adjacent cases and matching build variants. Record remaining unsupported claims and transfer to a changed input/schedule.

In the existing portable DMA state model, intentionally return the buffer to CPU on cancel_request rather than observed stop. Use this deterministic policy defect before any real peripheral experiment. The actual startup/MMIO variant must use the already selected target contract; do not invent a general register address.

## Failure cases

Reject a mismatched image/input, missing finite bound, invalid adapter result, expired watched object, unsupported tool treated as pass, symptom-only patch, or synthetic value presented as an actual C/tool/hardware observation. Undefined behavior has no promised symptom. Preserve the first cause when later logging/cleanup fails. Tool messages may vary by version; compare semantic evidence rather than exact wording.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit the nine-field dossier: contract; predictions; replay identities; actual observation; first-invalid-state evidence; competing hypotheses/test; reduced trigger and tri-state certificate; causal repair/limits; regression matrix and transfer. Address all three a/b/c objectives of each linked topic. The static fixture must pass independently, and the learner C must reproduce its intentionally faulty behavior and repaired contract within the declared scope. An unavailable capability keeps its dependent claim open and uses the stated supported alternative; it cannot be reported as a completed diagnostic or physical result. Assessment distinguishes guided fixture replay from a withheld-variant blind attempt.

## Hints and recovery

CFSR 0x8200 indicates precise BusFault plus BFAR valid; HFSR 0x40000000 records forced escalation. The imprecise 0x400 case has no valid BFAR, so the stale address is not usable evidence and stacked PC is not promised to identify the responsible access. Compare bad startup, peripheral clock/pin sequencing and invalid ownership as competing hypotheses. Do not inspect arbitrary side-effecting MMIO in the debugger. The policy model's configure-before-enable violates its stage invariant; actual peripheral effects require device evidence/measurement. DMA cancellation request leaves ownership with DMA until stop acknowledgment; the third CPU write is invalid even if the core is halted. The selected F439 SRAM/DMA path has no core data-cache maintenance requirement. Static arithmetic, emulator observations and physical fault/electrical observations remain separately labelled. On disagreement, minimize the first failing prefix, check identities and units, and change one hypothesis-driving variable. Feedback should name the incorrect inference or violated invariant; retry a changed variant instead of repeating unrelated work. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for evidence/feedback policy.

## Transfer challenge

Change the boundary, chunk grammar, optimization, acquisition point, schedule or documented target assumption relevant to this milestone. Predict which evidence survives and which must be recollected. Delay one fresh attempt for at least seven days. A genuinely blind attempt uses a withheld new variant and delayed oracle reveal; a self-authored or visible fixture remains lower-independence practice.
